title: provision_vcs_auth must support Azure DevOps end-to-end (PAT provisioning, local+remote members, failure-mode surfacing)
description:
provision_vcs_auth and the fleet-sprint VCS layer (src/tools/provision-vcs-auth.ts, src/services/vcs/*, packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/vcs-module.mjs + vcs-providers/azure-devops.mjs) do not fully support Azure DevOps today. Known gaps: (1) no guided flow for a user to create a PAT and store it as a fleet secret; (2) provision_vcs_auth cannot provision a user's already-working PAT for both local and remote members (local may legitimately be a no-op); (3) ADO auth failure modes (expired PAT, PAT missing required scopes/permissions for a specific operation, malformed org/project/repo URL, etc) do not surface as clean, actionable user-facing guidance -- they degrade or error opaquely today (see earlier field-report finding: provision_vcs_auth preflight could not derive owner/repo from an ADO remote URL and failed outright).

## Context
User requirements verbatim: (1) guide the user to create a PAT and make it a fleet secret variable; (2) allow the user's current working PAT to be usable for both local and remote members (local may end up being a no-op); (3) fleet-sprint must understand and cleanly surface ADO auth failure modes (expired PAT, missing-perms PAT, etc) as clean user actions, not opaque failures; (4) LLM conversations must never be exposed to the raw PAT, given it is a long-lived token -- redaction is a hard requirement, not best-effort; (5) explicitly think through whether a PAT's life can be self-extended, and decide what to do about it; (6) build this modularly via abstractions (existing vcs-providers registry), not ad hoc if/else -- PATs also gate various Azure cloud operations beyond just VCS, so the abstraction should not be VCS-only-shaped. A design/investigation pass by a background Opus agent was requested before implementation -- see that agent's output for the proposed design once available.
acceptance_criteria: User can be guided (docs + tool UX) to create an Azure DevOps PAT and register it as a fleet secret. provision_vcs_auth can provision that PAT for both local and remote members (local may be a documented no-op where not applicable). Distinct ADO auth failure modes (expired PAT, missing-scope PAT, malformed remote URL, revoked PAT) are each classified and surfaced with a specific, actionable user-facing message -- not a generic error. LLM/agent conversations (dispatch prompts, transcripts, logs) never have the raw PAT value exposed at any point -- redaction/scrubbing verified at the lowest applicable layer, not just fleet-sprint's own logging. Design explicitly evaluates (with a documented decision, not left silent) whether a PAT's lifetime can be self-extended/refreshed, and what apra-fleet should do about PAT expiry given ADO PATs are long-lived, non-refreshable-by-default tokens. Implementation is modular: Azure DevOps-specific logic lives behind the existing VCS-provider abstraction (vcs-providers/*.mjs, src/services/vcs/*), not as inline if/else branching in shared code -- and the abstraction is deliberately shaped so it can extend to other Azure PAT-gated capabilities (e.g. Azure cloud operations) later without rework.

title: Propagate sprint FAIL verdict into workflow terminal state and exit code
description:
engine.mjs:157 sets top-level status='success' whenever the workflow module resolves without throwing, even when runner.js deliberately resolves with {status:'failed', verdict:'FAIL'}. A FAIL verdict is never mapped to workflow status, terminalReason, or exit code -- the run reports green while its own Final Review says FAIL.

## Context
Documented verbatim in the 2026-08-04 Fleet Incident Report (Set 2, 'FALSE GREEN') but never filed as a bead. Second live occurrence: ait-gbo sprint on apra-fleet v0.4.0 (sprint_194616.json), still unfixed on main as of this filing. See field-report-ait-gbo-analysis.md section B0.
acceptance_criteria: A run whose result.verdict is FAIL (or result.status is failed) persists top-level status:'failed' (or a distinct completed_failed terminalReason), exits non-zero, and shows red in the supervisor/dashboard. Regression test pins engine.mjs's wf.emit('end') payload for a resolved-but-failed result.

title: [regression][carry-over] Both parts blocked: repo node_modules broken (missing @apralabs workspace links, ajv/smol-toml unresolvable) -- built CLI will not run, 169/185 real-bd suite files fail at 0s with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
description:
Part: 1 (real-bd suite)
Expected: 'node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs --start' (per INTEG-SUITE.md, following the 3a stale-status recovery already covered by apra-fleet-m1n) runs the full @apralabs/apra-fleet-se suite against real bd, with individual test files passing or failing based on actual product behavior; likewise 'npm run test:slow --workspace=@apralabs/apra-fleet-se' should run its two real-time watchdog tests.
Actual: 169/185 files in the main run, and both files in the slow lane, fail immediately (elapsed=0s / ~100-190ms) with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for '@apralabs/apra-fleet-workflow' and, for some files, 'Cannot find package .../node_modules/ajv/index.js'. Inspection shows node_modules/@apralabs does not exist at all (workspace symlinks missing), node_modules/ajv has only dist/ and lib/ subdirs with no package.json/index.js, and node_modules/.bin/vitest is absent. This is a broken/incomplete dependency install in the shared checkout, not 169 individual product regressions -- no test body actually executed. Recovery attempt via 'npm ci' failed: EPERM unlinking node_modules/@rollup/rollup-win32-x64-msvc/rollup.win32-x64-msvc.node ('operation not permitted... file was already in use'), suggesting either a locked file held by another process on this shared machine/checkout or an antivirus/permissions block; a second attempt would only risk degrading the partially-broken install further, so no further self-repair was attempted. File mtimes on the broken ajv dir predate this run's start, so this is pre-existing broken state at session start rather than a live clobber during the run, though a shared-checkout mutual-exclusion gap (see apra-fleet-egc for the analogous smoke-test-sandbox case) remains a plausible contributing cause and should be considered.
Test: node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs --status after --fresh --start: 'discovered=185 done=185 pending=0 failed=169 inflight=0 elapsedWall=93s cumFileTime=113s live=no'. npm run test:slow --workspace=@apralabs/apra-fleet-se: '# tests 2 # pass 0 # fail 2', same ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for @apralabs/apra-fleet-workflow.
Repro: 1) In this checkout run 'ls node_modules/@apralabs' (missing) and 'ls node_modules/ajv' (no package.json). 2) Run 'npm ci' from repo root -- observe EPERM on node_modules/@rollup/rollup-win32-x64-msvc/rollup.win32-x64-msvc.node. 3) Run 'node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs --fresh --start' then '--status' -- observe mass ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND failures at elapsed=0s. Operator action needed: identify/release whatever holds the rollup binary locked (or run npm ci with elevated/administrator permissions on Windows), then re-run 'npm install && npm run build' per the repo's documented prerequisites, then re-run this regression pass's Part 1.
notes:
Escalating to P0: 'node dist/index.js --version' itself fails with the same class of error (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for 'smol-toml' imported from dist/cli/config.js) -- the built CLI cannot run at all in this checkout, not just the test suite. This is a core-path-completely-broken condition per priority rules, and it also blocks Part 2's Setup (node dist/index.js install/status) of this same regression pass.
Part 2 confirmation: ran Setup's 'node dist/index.js install' with sandbox HOME/APRA_FLEET_PORT=18700 -- same ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND ('smol-toml' from dist/cli/config.js) before any sandbox state was created. Did not proceed to Test scenario per the playbook's Setup-verify-failure stop condition. Ran Teardown (node dist/index.js stop errored the same way, harmless since no server had started; rm -rf of the sandbox path succeeded and was verified absent afterward).

title: Dolt recovery Tier 2's server-mode revert is an LLM instruction step, not a guaranteed rollback -- an interrupted dispatch leaves the clone stuck in server mode
description:
Root cause identified for why fleet-win-dev1 ended up in a broken, stuck-in-server-mode local .beads state (the trigger for apra-fleet-ga61's credential-prompt bug being reachable at all in practice).

CHAIN OF EVIDENCE (all within the last 24h, checked live via C:\Users\akhil\.apra-fleet-se\logs\*):
1. Path A (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/dolt-recovery.mjs) fails immediately at its precondition guard every single time it's invoked from runner.js: "recoverDoltConflictPathA requires an injected sql() in opts" (line 220, a separate small bug -- the runner.js call site never wires a sql() function into opts). This throw fires BEFORE step 2 (start ephemeral dolt sql-server) or step 3 (flip metadata.json dolt_mode -> "server") ever run, so Path A itself never touches local state on any of these runs. Confirmed 4 times across 2 sprint logs today (apra-fleet-i8qj-be1014eb...: 3 separate divergence cycles at lines 87/122/157; apra-fleet-ot2z.15_apra-fleet-cmec-3dfb31a5...: 1 cycle at line 51).
2. Path B is explicitly disabled at this call site (enablePathB:false) and its own log line confirms it: "Falling through to Tier 2 without touching any local state."
3. Every one of those cycles escalates to Tier 2 (dolt-recovery-tier2.mjs), which dispatches a REAL LLM AGENT to the affected member (fleet-win-dev1 in all 4 observed cases) armed with the runbook doc packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/dolt-tier2-runbook.md.
4. That runbook's own steps (read directly, 2026-08-12): Step 3 tells the agent to "use `dolt sql-server` against the SAME embedded data dir" (i.e. manually flip the clone into server mode, replicating what Path A does in code) to resolve the conflict via SQL. Step 6 tells the agent to "Flip `.beads/metadata.json` back to `dolt_mode: \"embedded\"` and stop the ephemeral sql-server -- exactly as Path A's own teardown does."
5. UNLIKE Path A's teardown (a genuine code-level `finally` block that runs on every exit path, success or failure, per dolt-recovery.mjs's own module doc: "Reversibility (flip back + teardown on EVERY path, including failure) and zero data loss were both verified"), Tier 2's step-6 revert is just the LAST STEP of a multi-step instruction list an LLM agent is trusted to execute all the way through. There is no code-level guarantee it happens.
6. Direct evidence this gap was hit in practice: the apra-fleet-i8qj sprint log shows the Tier 2 dispatch was "aborted after a confirmed stall" / "exhausted its turn limit (max_turns)" without resolving anything -- meaning the agent could plausibly have already executed step 3 (flip to server mode + start the ephemeral server) before running out of turns, never reaching step 6.
7. Live forensics on fleet-win-dev1 (2026-08-12, this session) found EXACTLY that state: a genuine server-mode Dolt configuration (`.dolt/sql-server.info`, a listener config, dolt_mode effectively stuck in server semantics), plus a SECOND, freshly-dated (today, ~5:44-7:49pm) local Dolt data directory (`.beads/dolt/`) separate from the original `embeddeddolt/` -- consistent with an interrupted/incomplete recovery attempt having partially re-provisioned local state without ever completing its own cleanup.
8. Confirmed as the practical trigger for apra-fleet-ga61 (the credential-prompt-masked-as-'database not found' bug): that bug is dormant in embedded mode (the bd default) and is ONLY reachable when a clone is actually running in server mode with bd's network client needing to authenticate -- which normally never happens unless something (like an interrupted Tier 2 recovery) leaves a clone stuck there.

FIX DIRECTIONS:
- Tier 2's revert-to-embedded step needs a code-level guarantee, not just a runbook instruction the dispatched agent might not reach. Options: (a) wrap the ENTIRE Tier 2 dispatch in an orchestrator-side try/finally that force-flips metadata.json back to embedded and kills any dolt sql-server process regardless of how the agent dispatch ends (success, stall, max_turns, crash) -- mirroring Path A's own guarantee; (b) at minimum, add a supervisor/watchdog-level post-dispatch check that detects "clone left in server mode" and force-reverts it, independent of whether the agent's own step 6 ran.
- Also fix the small, separate, already-identified bug: runner.js's call site to recoverDoltConflictPathA is missing the required sql() opt, so Path A (the SAFE, fully-reversible scripted path) never actually gets a chance to run -- every conflict is needlessly escalated straight past it to the much riskier Tier 2 agent dispatch. Fixing this alone would reduce how often Tier 2 (and its revert-gap) is ever reached.
- Consider whether Tier 2's runbook should be restructured so step 6 happens FIRST relative to whatever risk of interruption exists (e.g. commit to a bounded max-turns budget specifically reserved for teardown, or split into two dispatches: one for the SQL-conflict-resolution work, a second GUARANTEED-to-run cleanup dispatch that only does the revert).
close_reason: Closed by the Dolt settle redesign (commits bc50c72b..c0524454): the LLM Tier 2 dispatch and its runbook are deleted outright, replaced by deterministic settleDoltConflicts() with a real finally-block teardown that never touches metadata.json, plus a supervisor-level orphaned-sql-server sweep as an independent second layer. The 6.5.6e residue assertions in scripts/dolt-settle-integration.mjs (no surviving process, no listening port, no leftover state) passed live on Windows/Linux/macOS, 2026-08-13, exit 0.

comments.author: Akhil Kumar
comments.text:
DESIGN UPDATE (2026-08-12) -- from re-reading the FULL, untruncated Tier 2 dispatch
transcript (fleet-win-dev1, C--akhil-git-apra-fleet 57e01077-3f3f-4922-a198-c23918435ed2.jsonl,
41 Bash tool_use calls, ends on max_turns right after the agent announced step 6).

WHAT THE AGENT ACTUALLY RAN (exact, not paraphrased)

- Started the ephemeral server itself (bd's own `dolt sql-server` was never used):
  `dolt sql-server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 13307 --data-dir .beads/embeddeddolt`
  backgrounded manually, logged to /tmp, no bd involvement.
- Flag-discovery dance (5 failed attempts) before finding the one invocation that
  actually works. Subcommand-level `dolt sql --host ...` fails ("unknown option
  `host'"); top-level flags are required. Final working shape, run from
  `.beads/embeddeddolt/beads` (the nested subdir, not the data-dir root):
    dolt --host 127.0.0.1 --port <PORT> --user root --password "" --no-tls sql -q "USE beads; <SQL>;"
  `--password ""` alone still fails with "TLS requested but server does not
  support TLS" -- `--no-tls` is mandatory. Every query also needs a leading
  `USE beads;` -- omitting it throws "Error 1105: Empty database name."
- SQL sequence matches Path A's steps 4-9 exactly in substance: `SET
  @@dolt_allow_commit_conflicts = 1`, `CALL DOLT_MERGE('origin/main')`, `SELECT *
  FROM dolt_conflicts` (gate: 1 table, 1 row, table=issues), inspected
  dolt_conflicts_issues columns/rows (our_*/their_*/base_* diff), `CALL
  DOLT_CONFLICTS_RESOLVE('--theirs', 'issues')`, `CALL DOLT_COMMIT(...)`, verified
  via dolt_log / dolt_commit_ancestors, then `dolt push origin main` from inside
  .beads/embeddeddolt/beads.
- Teardown that DID happen: killed the manually-spawned server's child PID
  (`kill 29216`) after confirming via `ps aux` the process tree. That is ALL that
  was reversed before max_turns hit.

CRITICAL FINDING -- metadata.json was NEVER touched, and this exposes a deeper gap
than "step 6 didn't run"

No Edit/Write/sed/direct-write tool call targeted metadata.json anywhere in the
41-command transcript. The agent never flipped dolt_mode to "server" at all --
contrary to both Path A's own step 3 and the runbook's step 3/6. Instead it drove
the raw `dolt` CLI straight at the manual server's socket with explicit
--host/--port/--user/--password/--no-tls flags, entirely bypassing bd/metadata.json
routing.

This is only safe because of what `bd dolt status` revealed at step 33: this bd
install runs in **"per-project" mode**, with its OWN separate, already-running
Dolt server (PID 41188, port 62336, data dir `.beads\dolt` -- NOT
`.beads\embeddeddolt`, the dir DEFAULT_EMBEDDED_DATA_DIR/Path A/the runbook all
assume). `.beads/dolt` and `.beads/embeddeddolt` are two DIFFERENT local data
directories. The agent's entire SQL-level fix (conflict resolve + commit + push)
happened against `.beads/embeddeddolt/beads` -- a copy bd's live per-project
server never reads. Direct evidence this caused a real problem: step 32's `bd dolt
pull` (issued immediately after the successful push) FAILED -- "database beads not
found on Dolt server at 127.0.0.1:62336" -- i.e. bd's real, live per-project
server was NOT caught up by the raw-socket fix at all. (It appears to self-heal by
step 33/34, but that recovery is unexplained by anything the agent did -- no bd
dolt pull retry, no bootstrap -- so treat it as unverified, not as proof the two
dirs reconciled.)

So: this specific member was ALREADY in a state where `.beads/dolt` (per-project)
and `.beads/embeddeddolt` (legacy embedded) coexist -- consistent with (and
probably caused by) the earlier interrupted recovery this bead's root-cause chain
already documented (point 7: "a SECOND, freshly-dated local Dolt data directory
.beads/dolt/ separate from the original embeddeddolt/"). Neither dolt-recovery.mjs
nor dolt-recovery-tier2.mjs nor the runbook currently has any concept of
"per-project mode" or a `.beads/dolt` data dir -- grep confirms zero references in
the fleet-sprint package. That is a real gap, independent of the revert-guarantee
bug this bead was originally filed for.

DOES THIS CONVERGE WITH THE PATH A sql()-INJECTION GAP? Partially, not cleanly.

Wiring a live sql()/spawnSqlServer() into runner.js's buildDoltRecoveryLadder()
call (the already-known separate bug, runner.js:1142) is necessary but NOT
sufficient to safely promote this transcript's sequence into a scripted tier.
Path A's code today would spawn its OWN ephemeral server against
DEFAULT_EMBEDDED_DATA_DIR ('.beads/embeddeddolt') and flip metadata.json to point
bd at it -- exactly the step this transcript's agent skipped, and exactly the
data dir that (on this member, right now) is NOT the one bd's live per-project
server actually uses. Injecting sql() naively would risk reproducing the same
"fix looks like it worked, but bd dolt pull still fails" symptom from step 32,
just mechanically instead of by an LLM's luck.

Before Path A's injection can be trusted as the deterministic replacement tier,
add one more precondition step: read `bd dolt status`'s reported data dir/port
(exactly what the transcript did reactively at step 33) and target THAT server/
dir -- either by talking to bd's own already-running per-project server directly
(no ephemeral spawn, no metadata.json flip needed at all -- simpler than Path A's
current design) when one is already up, or falling back to the current
spawn-ephemeral-and-flip dance only in genuine embedded mode. This is a real
design change to Path A, not just "inject the missing opts."

DESIGN DECISION: extend Path A, do not invent a new module

The transcript's SQL sequence is Path A's existing 10-step runbook, not a
different procedure -- the only things it adds are (a) the proven-correct dolt
CLI flag shape (top-level --host/--port/--user root/--password ""/--no-tls, run
from the nested `<dataDir>/beads` subdir, every query prefixed `USE beads;`) and
(b) the per-project-mode awareness gap above. Recommend:
  1. Fix runner.js:1142 to inject real sql()/spawnSqlServer()/allocatePort()/
     readMetadata()/writeMetadata() implementations using the proven flag shape.
  2. Extend dolt-recovery.mjs's spawnSqlServer/sql wiring (or a small precondition
     added ahead of step 2) to detect an already-running bd per-project server via
     `bd dolt status` and use it directly instead of always spawning a new
     ephemeral one against DEFAULT_EMBEDDED_DATA_DIR -- this also simplifies the
     revert story (nothing to spawn/flip/teardown when bd's own server is reused).
  3. No new "dolt-recovery-tier2-scripted.mjs" module -- Path A, once fixed per
     (1)/(2), IS the new deterministic Tier 2.

RENUMBER: current LLM dispatch (Tier 2) becomes Tier 3, last resort only

Rename dolt-recovery-tier2.mjs -> dolt-recovery-tier3.mjs; rename its exports
(buildDoltTier2RunbookPrompt/dispatchDoltTier2Escalation -> ...Tier3...,
DEFAULT_TIER2_RUNBOOK_PATH -> DEFAULT_TIER3_RUNBOOK_PATH) and doc comments
(apra-fleet-eft.9.6 references, "Tier 2" prose) throughout; rename
docs/dolt-tier2-runbook.md -> docs/dolt-tier3-runbook.md and update its own
front-matter/step numbering language ("Tier 2" -> "Tier 3", "Path A/Path B" stay,
add "now Path A (fixed)" as the tier reached before this runbook). Call sites to
update: runner.js:1142 (buildDoltRecoveryLadder options + the sql/spawnSqlServer
injection from item 1/2 above), dolt-sync.mjs's doltPushAfter() (goes through
buildDoltRecoveryLadder already, so likely just the renamed import), and
recoverDoltConflict()'s internal tier label 'tier-2' -> 'tier-3' in
dolt-recovery-tier2(3).mjs plus any log-line/test text asserting on that literal.

Net effect: ladder becomes Path A (scripted, now actually reachable and
per-project-mode-aware) -> Path B (discard-and-rebootstrap fallback, unchanged)
-> Tier 3 (LLM last resort, unchanged code, renamed only) -- with Tier 3's own
step 6 revert-guarantee gap (this bead's original finding) becoming much lower-
risk in practice once Path A actually resolves the common single-row-conflict
case before an LLM is ever dispatched, though the revert-guarantee gap itself is
still unfixed at the Tier 3 level and should remain tracked (fix direction (a)
from the original writeup: wrap the whole Tier 3 dispatch in an orchestrator-side
try/finally, since a runbook instruction step 6 is still not a code guarantee).

comments.author: Akhil Kumar
comments.text:
LIVE VALIDATION (2026-08-12, manual, on fleet-win-dev1): manually re-ran the full ephemeral-sql-server recovery dance end to end (install dolt, start server, connect, list real data, teardown) to prove the exact deterministic steps a fixed Path A should encode. Full write-up: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/dolt-manual-recovery-verified.md.

Key findings relevant to this bead's "capture the LLM's calls into a deterministic script" design:
- Windows process detachment: Start-Process (even with -WindowStyle Hidden/-PassThru) does NOT survive past the invoking SSH session -- the spawned sql-server and its listening port died the instant the launching command ended. schtasks/Register-ScheduledTask also failed live, reproducing apra-fleet-i8qj's exact symptom (LastTaskResult=267011, SCHED_S_TASK_QUEUED -- queued but never run, no interactive logon session). What DOES work, verified live: Invoke-CimMethod -ClassName Win32_Process -MethodName Create, which spawns the process under session 0 (WMI provider host), fully independent of the SSH job object. This is a NEW finding not in the original transcript analysis and should be the detachment mechanism a deterministic Windows recovery script uses.
- The proven-working dolt CLI invocation is even narrower than previously extracted from the LLM transcript: --no-tls must precede --host/--port (order-sensitive), and --user/--password must be OMITTED ENTIRELY (not passed as empty strings) -- passing --user=root explicitly is what triggers the interactive-prompt failure (see apra-fleet-ga61 update). This refines/simplifies the flag set the deterministic script needs to hardcode.
- Confirmed live that .beads/metadata.json never needs to be touched for THIS style of recovery (talking to the raw dolt CLI directly, bypassing bd) -- dolt_mode stayed "embedded" throughout and after. This matches the original Tier-2 transcript's behavior (it also never flipped metadata.json). If a future deterministic script instead routes bd itself through the ephemeral server (Path A's original documented design, which DOES flip dolt_mode to "server"), the revert-to-embedded step must be in a guaranteed finally block, not a discrete step that can be skipped -- this is still the core unfixed gap this bead tracks.

This live validation supports the bead's existing conclusion: every step is mechanical flag/ordering trivia with no judgment calls, confirming it is fully scriptable. The Windows WMI-detachment technique is the one genuinely new implementation detail this validation surfaced beyond what the transcript analysis alone found.

comments.author: Akhil Kumar
comments.text:
CLOSING WITH LIVE EVIDENCE (2026-08-13, branch fix/dolt-settle-recovery,
commits bc50c72b..c0524454; design: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/
dolt-sync-redesign.md).

This bead's gap -- "the revert is an LLM instruction step, not a guaranteed
rollback" -- is closed by deleting the thing that had the gap, then adding two
independent code-level layers in its place:

1. THE LLM TIER IS GONE. dolt-recovery.mjs, dolt-recovery-path-b.mjs,
   dolt-recovery-tier2.mjs and docs/dolt-tier2-runbook.md are deleted
   (commit ed4273ea). There is no agent dispatch anywhere in the conflict path
   any more, so there is no runbook step 6 that can be skipped at max_turns.
   Recovery is now one deterministic function, settleDoltConflicts()
   (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/dolt-settle.mjs), wired at BOTH
   divergence terminals -- push and pull (commit fdb41875); the pull terminal
   previously had no recovery seam at all.
2. TEARDOWN IS A REAL finally. The ephemeral sql-server is spawned and killed
   inside one function, on every exit path including failure, by PID and by a
   port-scoped process sweep. Nothing ever flips .beads/metadata.json --
   dolt_mode stays "embedded" throughout, exactly as the 2026-08-12 live
   validation in this bead recommended, so there is no mode to get stuck in.
3. SECOND LAYER, as fix direction (b) of this bead asked for: a supervisor-level
   sweep (packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/dolt-orphan-sweep.mjs, commit
   bfa27d25) that periodically kills orphaned dolt sql-server processes in
   settle's dedicated port range on every member, independent of whether any
   settle's own teardown ran. Unit-tested in test/supervisor-dolt-orphan-
   sweep.test.mjs.

REGRESSION TEST FOR THIS BEAD, run live: scripts/dolt-settle-integration.mjs
manufactures a genuinely unmergeable conflict in a disposable sandbox DB (never
production .beads), asserts bd dolt pull really fails on it, runs the real
settle, and then asserts NO RESIDUE -- no surviving sql-server process, nothing
listening on the settle port, no leftover sandbox/temp state, dolt_mode still
embedded. One sequential run, exit 0:

  | fleet-win-dev1 (win32) | 2026-08-13 | PASS; dolt 2.2.0 |
  | fleet-lin-dev1 (linux) | 2026-08-13 | PASS; dolt 2.2.0 |
  | fleet-mac (darwin)     | 2026-08-13 | PASS; dolt 2.2.0 |

The renumbering plan in the 2026-08-12 design-update comment (Path A fixed ->
Path B -> Tier 3 LLM last resort) is deliberately NOT what shipped: the whole
ladder was retired instead of renumbered, so no LLM tier remains to guard. The
mechanical flag/ordering trivia that comment catalogued is now encoded directly
in dolt-settle.mjs under a source-text drift guard.

title: bd/Dolt network client fails on Windows in non-interactive sessions: 'database not found' actually masks a credential-prompt failure
description:
Every fleet-sprint dispatched to a Windows fleet member (confirmed on fleet-win-dev1) can hit a deterministic, 100%-reproducible bd/Dolt failure the moment it needs bd dolt push/pull or plain bd list/bd doctor: "Error: failed to open database: database \"beads\" not found on Dolt server at 127.0.0.1:<port>", with the auto-started server's port incrementing on every single retry (confirmed sequence in one incident: 62726 -> 62735 -> 62749 -> 62758 -> ... -> 58820 -> 59066 -> 59272 -> 59325 -> 13307), never stabilizing.

ROOT CAUSE (fully isolated via live debugging on fleet-win-dev1, 2026-08-12):
1. Ruled out: missing/corrupted data. .beads/embeddeddolt/beads/.dolt/noms/ has a complete, healthy chunk store (hundreds of real .darc files, manifest, journal.idx).
2. Ruled out: bd version. Member was on stale bd 1.1.0; upgraded live to 1.1.2 (matching this repo's pin) -- identical failure persisted after upgrade.
3. Ruled out: stale Dolt lock file. noms/LOCK is 0 bytes, dated to the original clone (7/28), not a recent crash artifact.
4. Ruled out: corrupted port-tracking state. .beads/dolt-server.port/.pid are transient (created/deleted per invocation), not stale/corrupt.
5. Ruled out: bd auto-start racing its own fresh server before it's ready. Manually started `dolt sql-server --config config.yaml` in the same directory, waited ~4s for "Server ready. Accepting connections.", then ran `dolt sql -q "show databases"` FROM WITHIN that directory (local/embedded client mode) -- instantly and correctly returned `beads` as an available database. So a fully-warmed, healthy server DOES correctly register the database.
6. Ruled out: bd simply not reusing an already-running server. Pinned dolt.port: 13307 in .beads/config.yaml and kept a pre-warmed server alive on that exact port -- bd's own client THEN correctly connected to that exact port (log confirmed "port X -> 13307 (auto-start)") instead of spinning a new one -- but STILL reported "database not found: beads" against that same server instance that had just been proven healthy via local access one step earlier.
7. ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE: the failure is specific to NETWORK (MySQL-wire-protocol, --host/--port) client connections, not to the server or database state at all. Reproduced directly: `dolt --host 127.0.0.1 --port 13307 --user root sql -q "show databases"` (the same connection mode bd's own client uses) triggers an interactive password prompt ("Enter password:"), which then fails outright in this non-interactive/non-TTY dispatch context with "Failed to parse credentials: The handle is invalid" -- a Windows console-handle bug when a program tries to read a password from stdin with no real console attached (exactly the execution context every fleet-orchestrator-dispatched SSH command runs in). bd's own network client almost certainly hits the identical credential-handling failure internally, but instead of surfacing the real auth/credential error, it gets misreported as the misleading "database not found: beads".

IMPACT: this is NOT specific to one sprint, one branch, or one bead operation -- it will hit ANY bd dolt push/pull/list/doctor/bootstrap call dispatched to ANY Windows fleet member (fleet-win-dev1, fleet-win11) whenever bd's client needs a real network connection to its own auto-started (or even a pre-existing, pinned-port) Dolt server, which is effectively always in this SSH-dispatch execution model. Confirmed as the actual failure behind the 'apra-fleet-ot2z.15,apra-fleet-cmec' sprint's total failure on fleet-win-dev1 (2026-08-12), and structurally identical to the earlier database-not-found failures seen in that same sprint's Dolt recovery-ladder log (Path A/B unavailable, Tier 2 LLM-dispatched recovery exhausted max_turns without ever finding this root cause).

FIX DIRECTIONS (not yet designed in detail):
- Determine whether this is a bd bug, a Dolt (github.com/dolthub/dolt) bug, or purely a Windows non-interactive-stdin credential-prompt handling gap -- may need to be reported/fixed upstream in one of those projects rather than in this repo.
- Local workaround to investigate: does explicitly passing --no-tls / an empty --password flag (rather than relying on an interactive prompt) to bd's underlying dolt client avoid the credential-prompt path entirely? Check whether bd's own dolt-server invocation can be configured (env var, config.yaml key, or bd flag) to use a fixed/empty credential non-interactively so it never attempts to read from a non-existent console.
- Consider whether Windows fleet members' SSH dispatch should allocate a pseudo-console/pty (if the SSH transport supports it) so interactive-style prompts have a real handle to read from, matching how this already gets handled for other interactive-prompt-prone tools in the fleet dispatch layer.
- Until fixed, Windows fleet members cannot reliably run fleet-sprint (or any bd-touching dispatch) -- this should be flagged prominently, not just quietly retried into oblivion by the existing recovery ladder (which has no path that reaches this root cause; Tier 2's LLM-dispatched recovery burned a full max_turns budget without diagnosing it either -- worth teaching that recovery playbook this specific signature: port-incrementing "database not found" loop -> check network-vs-local dolt sql client behavior FIRST before attempting Path A/B/Tier 2).
close_reason: Closed by the Dolt settle redesign (commits bc50c72b..c0524454): bd stays embedded 100% of the time, the old server-mode Path A is deleted, and the single remaining raw-dolt call site (settleDoltConflicts) hardcodes the landmine-safe flag shape (--no-tls first, --user/--password omitted) under a regression test. Verified live on Windows/Linux/macOS by scripts/dolt-settle-integration.mjs (exit 0, 2026-08-13) -- full network-mode SQL recovery over a non-interactive SSH dispatch with no credential prompt. See the closing comment for scope, including the separate bd-side auto-start readiness race that is explicitly NOT claimed fixed here.

comments.author: Akhil Kumar
comments.text:
CORRECTION (2026-08-12, evidence-based, from Tier 2 LLM recovery transcript on fleet-win-dev1: C:\Users\akhil\.claude\projects\C--akhil-git-apra-fleet\57e01077-3f3f-4922-a198-c23918435ed2.jsonl):

Step 7's "ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE" claim needs correction. It asserted that `dolt --host ... --user root sql -q "..."` is "the same connection mode bd's own client uses" and that this triggers an interactive password prompt ("Enter password: Failed to parse credentials: The handle is invalid.") in every non-interactive Windows session -- implying bd's internal network client hits the same failure. That equivalence is FALSE, disproven directly in the SAME non-interactive SSH-dispatched session:

- bd's OWN client calls in that session (`bd dolt pull` at transcript idx 4, `bd dolt show`/`bd dolt status` at idx 25) connected over the network (MySQL wire protocol, same 127.0.0.1:<port>) WITHOUT ever hitting a credential prompt. idx 4 failed with an application-level "database \"beads\" not found on Dolt server at 127.0.0.1:62336" (a real, different bug -- see below). idx 25, against a freshly auto-started server on the same port, reported "Server connection OK". Neither showed "Enter password" or "handle is invalid".
- The credential-prompt failure ("Enter password: Failed to parse credentials: The handle is invalid.") reproduced exactly ONCE in the whole transcript, at idx 34, when the LLM manually typed `dolt --host 127.0.0.1 --port 13307 --user root sql -q ...` WITHOUT `--password ""` and WITHOUT `--no-tls`. Every other manual invocation in the transcript (idx 3, 7, 8, 11, 13, 15, 21, 22, 27, 29-33, 40) that included `--password "" --no-tls` succeeded with normal query results -- including full conflict-resolution SQL (DOLT_MERGE, DOLT_CONFLICTS_RESOLVE, DOLT_COMMIT) run entirely non-interactively over the network in the same SSH-dispatched, non-TTY session ga61 claims can't authenticate.
- One near-miss at idx 15 (password flag only, no `--no-tls`) gave a DIFFERENT error: "TLS requested but server does not support TLS" -- not the credential-prompt error. The credential/handle-invalid error is specific to omitting BOTH flags and letting the raw `dolt` CLI fall back to its own interactive password-prompt code path, which has no console handle to read from in this dispatch context.

REVISED CONCLUSION: this is hypothesis (a), not (b). The "non-interactive Windows sessions can't authenticate to a network-mode Dolt server" framing is WRONG as a blanket claim. What's actually true and narrower: the standalone `dolt` CLI's own interactive credential-prompt fallback (triggered when `--password`/`--no-tls` aren't explicitly supplied) breaks in this context -- a real, fixable, narrow bug, but it only affects manual/ad hoc `dolt` CLI invocations (e.g. by a human or an LLM doing live debugging), NOT bd's own compiled network client, which appears to use a proper non-interactive MySQL driver connection and never hit this failure in the transcript.

Consequently, the original motivating symptom (the port-incrementing "database not found" loop bd itself produces, e.g. idx 4 in this transcript) remains UNEXPLAINED by the credential-prompt theory and needs separate root-causing -- most likely a server-readiness/race condition in bd's auto-start-then-connect sequence (server process up, listening, but the `beads` database not yet registered/loaded when bd's client connects), not a credential/auth issue at all. Note idx 4 and idx 25 both queried port 62336 but at different times/server instances -- first attempt failed "database not found", a later fresh auto-start succeeded -- consistent with a startup race, not an auth failure.

FIX DIRECTIONS UPDATE:
- Drop the "add --no-tls/--password to bd's internal client" fix direction as the primary fix -- bd's internal client already appears to authenticate fine non-interactively (no evidence it ever hit the credential-prompt bug).
- DO fix/document the raw `dolt` CLI usage bug for humans/LLMs doing manual recovery (e.g. dolt-recovery-tier2.mjs runbook instructions, Tier 2 prompts): always pass `--user root --password "" --no-tls` explicitly when using `dolt --host/--port ... sql`, to avoid the interactive prompt fallback. Worth upstreaming to dolthub/dolt too (CLI shouldn't attempt interactive stdin password prompts in non-TTY contexts; should error clearly or default to empty/no-auth like the driver does).
- The real "database not found" auto-start race needs its own investigation: check bd's server-start-then-connect readiness handshake/retry logic (does it wait for "Server ready. Accepting connections." AND for the database to actually be loaded/attached before returning control to the caller?).
- Note: `packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/dolt-sync.mjs` confirms Path A's sql()/spawnSqlServer() runtime is NOT YET injected in production (runner.js has no such runtime) -- Path A currently self-defers to Path B always. The Tier 2 LLM dispatch in this transcript was doing fully manual/ad hoc recovery, not exercising bd's or fleet-sprint's own sql client code at all for the merge/resolve steps (idx 20 onward) -- only for the pull/show/status calls (idx 4, 25) which are bd's real client.

title: [regression][carry-over] Local-member dispatch's clean-env PATH reconstruction cannot find bd/claude installed via nvm -- toy sprint fails immediately with 'bd: not found'
description:
Part: 2 (smoke test)
Expected: 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint --issue gh-toy-4ef --members toy-doer --branch <b> --base main --max-cycles 1 --dispatch-timeout-s 900' runs the toy sprint end to end against the local 'toy-doer' member (registered via 'register-member --type local --path $HOME/toy-repo --llm claude'), reaching the Planner dispatch and eventually closing the canary issue gh-toy-4ef.
Actual: the sprint fails at its very first pre-dispatch step (the D-pull preflight beads-health gate) with: 'DoltSyncError: [Dolt] D-pull failed for member toy-doer: [Command Failed] Exit code 127: Exit code: 127 [stderr] /bin/sh: 1: bd: not found'. The workflow never reaches the Planner. register-member itself already surfaced a related symptom earlier: '[Warnings] claude CLI not found on this machine -- install it before using execute_prompt'.
Root cause (traced): LocalStrategy's clean-env dispatch (src/os/linux.ts getCleanEnv()) rebuilds PATH from scratch via 'env -i HOME=<member/sandbox HOME> USER=... bash -l -c env -0', which sources only /etc/profile and ~/.profile under that (member-scoped) HOME -- never the operator's real, already-resolved PATH. CLI_PATH additionally prepends only "$HOME/.local/bin" (again the member-scoped HOME) before invoking an LLM provider CLI. Neither path includes an nvm-managed Node's per-version bin directory (e.g. /home/<user>/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.2/bin), which is exactly where both 'bd' and 'claude' are actually installed on this host, and which normally only lands on PATH because the operator's own ~/.bashrc sources nvm.sh -- a file that does not exist (and structurally cannot, since the regression-test-playbook's sandbox HOME is deliberately fresh/empty) under the sandboxed/member HOME this exec path reads instead. Reproduced directly: 'env -i HOME=$SANDBOX USER=$USER LOGNAME=$USER SHELL=/bin/bash bash -l -c '\''echo $PATH'\''' prints only /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:/snap/bin -- no nvm path, so neither bd nor claude resolve, matching the sprint's exact 'bd: not found' / register-member's 'claude CLI not found' symptoms.
Test: regression-test-playbook.md Part 2 Test scenario step 4 (fleet-sprint workflow launch), branch HEAD, sandbox at $HOME/temp/.apra-fleet-tests, scratch port 18700, 2026-08-11 regression pass.

comments.author: bella
comments.text:
Root cause: the Claude Code CLI signals a turn-limit termination INCONSISTENTLY across versions/streams -- via the type:result event's subtype='error_max_turns', and/or that event's terminal_reason='max_turns', and/or a distinct standalone transcript event of type='max_turns_reached' (which can precede a bare result event, or be the last event when a hard-timeout kill truncates the stream before any result event). The old parser (src/providers/claude.ts) recorded ONLY obj.terminal_reason on the result event, and both consumers in src/tools/execute-prompt.ts keyed off parsed.terminalReason==='max_turns' alone. A transcript that carried the signal solely via subtype or the standalone event was therefore silently missed and fell through to nonzero_exit, exactly the ekm forensic session that ran 38.5 min to a hard timeout + cold restart.

Fix: (1) added isMaxTurnsSignal(obj) in claude.ts detecting all channels (terminal_reason/subtype/max_turns_reached event/stop_reason); (2) parseResponse now tracks the signal across every transcript event (JSONL, JSON-array, and single-object forms) and normalizes terminalReason to 'max_turns' on the returned result -- including a plain-text fallback path when no result event terminates the stream; (3) added isMaxTurnsResponse(parsed) shared classifier in provider.ts (checks normalized terminalReason OR raw error_max_turns subtype) and routed both execute-prompt.ts classification sites through it. No MCP contract/enum changes -- max_turns_exhausted is the existing reason enum value. tsc green; providers.test.ts 158/158 green with new coverage for subtype-only, standalone-event, array-form, and truncated-stream cases. Pre-existing unrelated failures in workflow.test.ts/eft-41 are an undici/Node webidl incompatibility, present on the base with my changes stashed.

title: [epic] Dispatch-layer reliability: max_turns transcript signal, busy-lock self-heal, AGY output capture
description:
Sprint epic for member fleet-lin-dev1 (branch fix/dispatch-layer-reliability, base chore/integration-binary-fixes-and-auth-selfheal; fresh checkout at /home/akhil/git/apra-fleet-dev1). Makes execute_prompt's terminal-signal handling truthful and self-healing. Anchors: apra-fleet-ekm (P0 -- a max_turns-terminated Claude session was not detected; the dispatch sat dead for 38.5 min until the hard timeout, then cold-restarted: detection lives in src/providers/claude.ts terminal_reason parsing + src/tools/execute-prompt.ts max_turns classification; the runner-side handler is correct, the server signal failed), apra-fleet-idb (stale busy-lock: inFlightAgents entry outlives its process, wedging the member until restart), apra-fleet-qmb (AGY provider returns {} instead of captured response text/session id). HARD CONSTRAINT: no changes to any MCP tool schema, response contract, or reason-enum values -- packages/apra-fleet-client is owned by the concurrent fleet-win-dev1 sprint; if a contract change proves unavoidable, STOP and file a follow-up bead instead. FILE FOOTPRINT (declared for parallel-sprint disjointness -- do NOT touch anything else): src/tools/execute-prompt.ts, src/tools/stop-prompt.ts (only if the lock-release path requires it), src/providers/**, src/services/stall/**, src/services/session-registry.ts, src/services/orphan-recovery.ts, src/utils/prompt-errors.ts, root tests/** (new files + tests/agy-provider.test.ts). Out of bounds: src/services/vcs/**, src/tools/provision-vcs-auth.ts, packages/**, src/index.ts, package.json.


---

VERIFICATION STEPS (added 2026-08-01) -- this epic is an "orphaned parent":
all 6 children closed with a self-reported PASS, code merged directly into
chore/integration-binary-fixes-and-auth-selfheal (no PR: the sprint failed at
gh-pr-create on an unrelated auth issue), but the epic was never
independently verified against its own acceptance criteria.
Model tier: Opus -- P0, three independent anchor bugs, live dispatch-layer
semantics, and a hard file-footprint constraint that only a diff audit can
confirm. Do NOT close on green tests alone.

0. GATE / most important check: all three anchor bugs this epic exists to
   resolve -- apra-fleet-ekm (P0), apra-fleet-idb, apra-fleet-qmb -- are
   still OPEN. Each is "blocked by" a closed child here. Either the anchors
   are genuinely fixed (then they close as part of this verification) or the
   children shipped without resolving them. Resolve this before anything
   else; it is the clearest signal of whether the epic's intent landed.
1. ekm detection (.1): confirm the root cause of the missed max_turns_reached
   transcript signal is DOCUMENTED on the bead (explicit acceptance clause,
   easy to skip). Then confirm in src/providers/claude.ts +
   src/tools/execute-prompt.ts that a max_turns-terminated session ALWAYS
   classifies reason max_turns_exhausted -- including the intermittent shape
   from the ekm forensics, not just the happy-path event.
2. Assert NO new enum values and NO MCP schema/response-contract change (hard
   constraint: packages/apra-fleet-client was owned by the concurrent
   fleet-win-dev1 sprint). Diff the tool schemas and the reason enum against
   the base commit; confirm packages/apra-fleet-client is unchanged by this
   epic.
3. Inactivity watchdog (.2): confirm the mtime cross-check in
   src/services/stall/ terminates a frozen-transcript session within the
   configured window (default ~120s) with a CORRECTLY CLASSIFIED reason --
   not merely "terminated". Confirm the threshold is configurable and
   documented (docs/stall-detector-resilience.md section 7).
4. False-kill safety: confirm a long-running SILENT tool call is not killed.
   The close note says stall fires only when content-timestamp AND mtime
   agree -- verify that conjunction is real in code, since an OR would
   reintroduce false kills. This is the highest-risk regression in the epic.
5. Busy-lock self-heal (.4/.5): exercise the real executePrompt() entry point
   for every findDeadLockPid branch -- remote pid dead (self-heals via SSH
   kill-0), remote pid ALIVE (must stay busy), local pid dead
   (isPidAlive/ESRCH, no SSH round trip), interactive sessionRegistry pid
   dead, and no-pid-still-busy. Confirm release is wired to BOTH child reap
   and client disconnect, not just one.
6. Confirm fleet_status and the dispatch gate never disagree about busyness
   -- assert on both surfaces in the same test, an explicit acceptance
   clause.
7. AGY capture (.6): confirm src/providers/agy.ts parseResponse returns real
   reply text AND the transcript conversation_id (previously hardcoded
   sessionId: undefined) instead of {}. Confirm the fixture
   tests/fixtures/agy-transcript-output.txt is a RECORDED CLI shape, not a
   hand-written one that only matches the parser. No live AGY dispatch.
   Note: docs/provider-matrix.md was deliberately left untouched (outside
   footprint) -- decide whether that is a real doc gap and file a follow-up.
8. File-footprint audit: diff the merge against the declared footprint
   (src/tools/execute-prompt.ts, src/tools/stop-prompt.ts, src/providers/**,
   src/services/stall/**, src/services/session-registry.ts,
   src/services/orphan-recovery.ts, src/utils/prompt-errors.ts, root
   tests/**). Assert NOTHING under src/services/vcs/**,
   src/tools/provision-vcs-auth.ts, packages/**, src/index.ts, or
   package.json was modified.
9. Re-run tsc + the root test suite on the merged branch. The sprint reported
   4 pre-existing undici/webidl failures -- confirm that count and set is
   unchanged, i.e. this epic introduced none of them.

DISPOSITION: anchors ekm/idb/qmb verified fixed and all clauses pass -> close
them and this epic together, with evidence via bd note. Any anchor still
reproducing -> reopen the corresponding child (iuc.1/.2 for ekm, .4 for idb,
.6 for qmb) and keep this epic open. Footprint violation or contract change
found -> P0 finding, file an [integ] bug immediately (it may have raced the
concurrent fleet-win-dev1 sprint).
acceptance_criteria: All child beads closed; a max_turns-terminated session surfaces reason max_turns_exhausted promptly (existing enum value, no new values); a transcript-frozen session is terminated within the configured inactivity window instead of the 3630s ceiling; a busy rejection self-heals stale locks; AGY dispatches return captured text; root test suite + tsc green; no file outside the declared footprint modified.
notes:
Independent integ audit 2026-08-01 (commits 15ec5c94..f0fded83 at merge 017f2175): items 1-5,8,9 PASS with file:line evidence (see apra-fleet-ekm and apra-fleet-idb close reasons); anchor ekm CLOSED, anchor idb CLOSED (residual no-pid gap recorded on the bead); iuc.6 REOPENED (hand-written AGY fixture violates its recorded-shape acceptance) so anchor qmb and this epic stay OPEN. 2026-08-03 (groomer): last child apra-fleet-iuc.6 closed -- src/providers/agy.ts parseResponse() + tests/agy-provider.test.ts land the AGY response/session-id capture fix, verified via fixture-based unit tests only (10/10 passing on chore/integration-binary-fixes-and-auth-selfheal). Do NOT close this epic yet: the fix has never been exercised against a live AGY CLI dispatch, only a recorded transcript fixture, so there is no guarantee it behaves correctly against real agy output shapes/edge cases. Operator instruction: hold this epic open and pick it up for verification during an actual AGY-provider sprint session (a sprint dispatched to an agy member), not a Claude-only session -- only close once a live AGY dispatch has been observed to produce a correctly parsed response/session id.

Triage 2026-08-09 (iuc-agy batch): all three anchors are now closed -- apra-fleet-ekm and apra-fleet-idb were integ-verified 2026-08-01 with file:line evidence (findDeadLockPid five-branch coverage, both release paths), and apra-fleet-qmb + the last open child apra-fleet-iuc.6 are closed today. The single remaining hold ('AGY capture never exercised against a live AGY CLI, only a hand-written fixture') is discharged by PR #383 (feat/agy-output-format-json, merged to main 2026-08-07): AGY now runs with --output-format json and parseResponse reads the native {conversation_id,status,response,usage} envelope as its primary path, pinned by a recorded-envelope integration test, and PR #383 records LIVE dispatch/resumption/unknown-session verification against member fleet-lin-agy. No open apra-fleet-iuc.* children remain. Residual follow-ups carried forward from the 2026-08-01 audit, NOT re-verified here and worth filing separately if still wanted: (a) stall termination still surfaces a generic dispatch_failed rather than a distinct classified stall reason; (b) fleet_status-vs-dispatch-gate agreement is asserted via a writeStatusline proxy rather than a literal fleet_status call; (c) docs/provider-matrix.md was left untouched (was outside the epic's declared file footprint) and may be a real doc gap; (d) apra-fleet-idb's recorded residual: a busy-lock leak occurring BEFORE pid capture has no pid to probe and deliberately stays busy. Closing the epic.

title: [regression][carry-over] sandbox-seed-beads.mjs bd invocation ENOENT on Windows (execFileSync missing shell:true)
description:
Part: 2 (smoke test)
Expected: regression-test-playbook.md's Setup section (Seed the sandbox beads DB step) succeeds on Windows, running 'node scripts/sandbox-seed-beads.mjs --sandbox-root ... --toy-repo ...' to seed the sandbox local beads DB from the toy repo's committed .beads/issues.jsonl.
Actual: the script fails silently with no diagnostic printed to stdout/stderr beyond 'spawnSync bd ENOENT' (script exits 0 despite the failure -- no non-zero exit or error surfaced), because it invokes bd via execFileSync('bd', [...]) without shell:true (or an explicit .cmd extension). On Windows, 'bd' on PATH resolves to a POSIX shell script (no .exe/.cmd wrapper picked up by Node's default execFileSync), so Node cannot exec it directly and every bd call in this script (bd init --from-jsonl, bd dolt push) ENOENTs. This blocks Setup entirely -- the Test scenario can never run because the seeded beads DB (and canary gh-toy-4ef) never materializes.
Test: regression-test-playbook.md Part 2 Setup, 'Seed the sandbox beads DB' step -- 'node scripts/sandbox-seed-beads.mjs --sandbox-root $HOME --toy-repo $TOY_REPO' on Windows (win32, node v22.22.1, git-bash shell).
Repro:
  node -e "const {execFileSync}=require('child_process'); execFileSync('bd',['--version'],{encoding:'utf-8'});"
  -> throws: spawnSync bd ENOENT
  Confirmed working fix pattern: execFileSync('bd', ['--version'], { encoding: 'utf-8', shell: true }) succeeds (prints 'bd version 1.1.0 (8e4e59d39)'); a bare '.cmd' extension swap alone is insufficient (execFileSync('bd.cmd', ...) throws EINVAL without shell:true too).
Also noteworthy: the script's failure is silent (prints only 'spawnSync bd ENOENT' via console.error/log and exits with code 0), so a caller polling exit code alone would not notice Setup did not actually seed anything -- worth hardening exit-code correctness as part of the same fix.
Location: scripts/sandbox-seed-beads.mjs, the two execFileSync('bd', ...) call sites (bd init --from-jsonl, bd dolt push).
close_reason: Triage: duplicate/stale artifact of apra-fleet-2cc, which was closed 2026-07-31 with integ verification that includes a real sandbox-seed-beads.mjs run on this Windows runner (exit 0, real Dolt push) -- the exact scenario 0lf reports. 0lf was filed by the regression runner almost certainly against a stale deployed binary lacking the 2cc.1 fix. Per repo convention: if this recurs on the current deployed binary (v0.4.0_a24eaf or later), REOPEN this bead with the new evidence rather than filing a fresh one.

title: Dispatch layer misses max_turns_reached transcript signal, converts a dead session into a 60-min wasted timeout + cold-restart resume
description: Verified via direct transcript read (apra-fleet-f34.3 streak attempt 1, sprint apra-fleet-xuo, session a5399530 on fleet-win-dev1, 2026-07-30): the agent's own session transcript shows it hit a max_turns_reached event (maxTurns 100, turnCount 101) at 2026-07-31T01:07:46Z. Nothing happened after that line -- the session was dead. But the dispatch was not killed until 01:46:15 by the unrelated 3630s hard-timeout ceiling: 38.5 minutes (63% of the total 60.5-minute "timeout") was pure dead wait on an already-terminated agent. runner.js DOES have correct handling for this exact case (err.details.reason equal to max_turns_exhausted -> resume the SAME session at a higher turn budget, around line 7634) -- it simply never fired here, so the eventual retry was a cold restart in a brand-new session, re-doing all 22 minutes of prior exploration from zero. Notably the SAME condition fired correctly for a different streak (k7b) 60 seconds after it happened in the same sprint run -- so this is an intermittent/racy failure in the max_turns-reached detection path, not a structurally broken mechanism. Fix: make the max_turns_reached detection reliable (investigate why it silently failed to trigger this time), and/or add an inactivity watchdog keyed on transcript mtime so a dead session is caught within 1-2 minutes rather than relying solely on the 60-minute hard ceiling as a backstop. This is the single highest-value fix found in this investigation -- it alone accounts for roughly a third of one Develop-phase round's wall-clock time.
close_reason: Integ-verified 2026-08-01 (independent audit of merged iuc work at 017f2175 on chore/integration-binary-fixes-and-auth-selfheal, NOT the sprint's self-report). Detection: src/providers/claude.ts:33-41 isMaxTurnsSignal() covers all four signal channels (terminal_reason, subtype error_max_turns, type max_turns_reached, stop_reason) and the flag survives JSONL, JSON-array, single-object AND the truncated plain-text fallback (claude.ts:216-224) -- the intermittent shape from this bug's forensics. Both classification sites (src/tools/execute-prompt.ts:139 and :968) route through isMaxTurnsResponse() (provider.ts:60-63). Backstop: stall detector fires at 120s (configurable, docs/stall-detector-resilience.md sec 7) on the content-AND-mtime-stale conjunction (stall-detector.ts:161, false-kill test dead-session-detection-contract.test.ts:190), so even a missed signal can no longer become a 60-min wasted timeout. Root cause documented on iuc.1 (2026-08-01) + commit 15ec5c94. Gates on merged branch: tsc clean; root suite 2867 pass/1 fail (unrelated Windows EBUSY temp-cleanup race in check-sandbox-sync-remote.test.ts); all 7 epic-touched test files 304/304. Residual live-only caveat noted on apra-fleet-iuc: real-CLI end-to-end resume timing not yet observed in a production sprint.

title: Supervisor watchdog never auto-releases a crashed/finished sprint's reservation (check apra-fleet-0j1 first)
description: Note: this may already be tracked as apra-fleet-0j1 (per the 2026-07-30 backlog artifact) -- check bd show apra-fleet-0j1 first and just reopen/comment on it rather than duplicating if so. Watchdog classifies CRASHED/FINISHED continuously (watchdog.mjs) but nothing acts on it -- only a full supervisor restart (reconcile.mjs's startup sweep) or a manual operator force-release (POST /api/reservations/:sprintId/force-release) clears the ledger reservation. Hit live multiple times this session, most recently 2026-07-30 when apra-fleet-fyc's child crashed and had to be recovered by hand. Fix: wire ledger.release() into the watchdog's classification loop, same call reconcile() already makes at startup. See packages/apra-fleet-se/docs/architecture.md "Manual force-release" section (added 2026-07-30) for full mechanism context.
close_reason: Duplicate of apra-fleet-0j1 (hr9's own description says 'check apra-fleet-0j1 first'; 0j1 is the older canonical bead with full acceptance criteria). Implementation tracked under the supervisor-lifecycle sprint epic.

title: Supervisor dashboard page load takes 60-80s+ (near-unusable): per-node bd subprocess spawns instead of one bulk fetch
description:
Reproduced live 2026-07-30: GET / on the supervisor (localhost:8787) took 78.4s wall-clock while GET /api/sprints on the same process answered in 3ms, and both live sprint children's own dashboards (direct child viewer ports) answered in ~100ms. The gap is entirely in the supervisor's own index-page render.

Root cause (verified by reading source, not guessed): backlog.mjs's buildClaimedBy() (line 671-685) re-computes every active sprint's live claimed-scope on EVERY dashboard render by calling expandScope() (scope-overlap.mjs:94-115), which does a breadth-first walk issuing ONE SEPARATE 'bd list --parent <id>' subprocess call PER BEAD NODE, strictly sequentially (no-await-in-loop, one node at a time -- scope-overlap.mjs:103-113). This runs once per active sprint (backlog.mjs buildClaimedBy's Promise.all is only parallel ACROSS sprints, not within one sprint's own BFS walk).

Meanwhile bdListAllBeads()/fetchAllBeadsRaw() (backlog.mjs:93-109), called in the SAME render pass via buildTree()'s Promise.all (backlog.mjs:688-689), already fetches the ENTIRE beads tracker in a single 'bd list --json --limit 0' call. So the render pass pays for both: one cheap bulk fetch AND N expensive sequential per-node subprocess calls for the scope walk that duplicate information already available in-memory from the bulk fetch.

With today's beads tree depth (e.g. epic apra-fleet-xuo: 10 direct children, one of which (k7b) has 4 of its own children; epic apra-fleet-fyc: 5 children) and 2 concurrently active sprints contending for the same embedded-Dolt engine each 'bd' subprocess must open, this is dozens of sequential subprocess spawns per page load, each paying full Windows process-spawn + Dolt-open overhead -- explaining the 60-80s+ observed.

Fix direction (already grounded in existing code, not new invention): buildClaimedBy() should NOT call expandScope()'s subprocess-per-node walker at all. buildTree() (backlog.mjs:688-689) already calls listAllBeads() in the same render pass -- compute each active sprint's live claimed subtree by walking parent-child links IN-MEMORY off that single already-fetched list (the same technique buildBacklogTree() at backlog.mjs:147-195 already uses via its allChildrenOf index), instead of re-querying bd per node. This eliminates the N-subprocess walk entirely, replacing it with zero extra bd calls (reuse the one bulk fetch already happening).

Scope check: expandScope()/bdListChildren() is ALSO used by the launch-time scope-overlap guard (createScopeGuard in scope-overlap.mjs, consulted by POST /api/sprints). That path is lower-frequency (once per launch attempt, not once per page render/poll) and may be lower priority to optimize, or could reuse the same in-memory-walk-off-one-bulk-fetch technique if it also gets slow as the tracker grows -- flag but do not conflate: this bead's scope is the DASHBOARD render path (backlog.mjs buildClaimedBy/buildTree/buildBacklogTasks), not the launch guard.

Acceptance: GET / on the supervisor responds in well under 1s with 2+ active sprints and a beads tree of comparable size/depth to today's (~15-20 nodes per active sprint's claimed subtree). Verify via the same curl -w time_total timing method used to reproduce this.
close_reason: Fixed: buildClaimedBy() in packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/backlog.mjs now computes claimed-scope in-memory (expandScopeInMemory + buildChildIndex) off the already-fetched listAllBeads() result, instead of per-node bd subprocess calls via expandScope(). Committed 6b2684b6 on branch fix/apra-fleet-c4s-dashboard-bulk-fetch, pushed to origin.

title: [test] real concurrent launches engage the HTTP mutex/id-allocator (no silent no-op fallback)
description:
Integration test (integration test folder) proving engagement in a REAL end-to-end launch, which the earlier eft.9.2/9.3 unit tests did not.

What to test:
- Launch two concurrent supervisor-spawned sprints whose scopes both create child beads and both push to Dolt; assert the coordination endpoint actually received acquire/release and id-allocation calls (server-side counter/log assertion), and that both sprints' child ids are distinct and non-colliding.
- Assert the no-op fallback path is NOT taken in either launch (fail the test if the fallback marker/warning appears).
- Repeat the engagement assertion for the supervisor-less CLI topology using the MCP-hosted coordination point.

Acceptance criteria: test fails when --service-url wiring is reverted; passes with both impl tasks landed; no flakiness from fixed sleeps (poll with timeout). ASCII only.
close_reason: Gated the real-bd-only concurrent-launch-engagement suite behind a replay-mode skip (bdMode()==='real'), matching DOLT_SKIP/BD_SKIP precedent, since it was previously failing the default replay suite for lack of committed fixtures that would have made its dolt-mutex assertions vacuous anyway. Also added a >=2 child-id floor per reviewer note.

title: [impl] Host dolt-mutex and id-allocator coordination on the fleet MCP server for supervisor-less launches
description:
Problem: the standalone/detached-binary CLI launch path has no supervisor to reach, so --service-url alone leaves that topology unprotected. cli.mjs already holds a connected mcpClient (used for member_reservation, stop_prompt), so the fleet MCP server is a reachable coordination point.

Work: expose the acquire/release/lease-reclaim surface of src/supervisor/dolt-mutex.mjs and src/supervisor/id-allocator.mjs as fleet MCP tool(s) under src/tools/, preserving FIFO acquire, lease/pid-probe reclaim and token-guarded release semantics; have the runner's mutex/allocator clients use the MCP transport when no supervisor serviceUrl is available. Per CLAUDE.md, packages/apra-fleet-client MUST be updated in the SAME change to wrap the new tool(s).

Acceptance criteria:
- New tool schema(s) registered and reflected in packages/apra-fleet-client in the same commit.
- A standalone-CLI launch acquires the push mutex and allocates child ids through the MCP path; the no-op fallback is only taken when neither supervisor nor MCP coordination is available, and that case logs a warning naming the degradation.
- Unit tests for the new tool handlers; 'npm test' green. ASCII only.
close_reason: Implemented in 0b92604. New fleet MCP tools dolt_push_mutex + child_id_allocator (src/tools/, backed by src/services/sprint-coordination.ts) preserve FIFO acquire, lease/dead-pid reclaim and token-guarded release; acquire is ticketed so a polling waiter keeps its queue position. packages/apra-fleet-client api.mjs wraps both in the same commit. runner.js precedence is now context client -> serviceUrl (supervisor HTTP) -> args.callTool (fleet MCP, verified to reach runSprintCycle as context.args from bin/cli.mjs) -> no-op, and the no-op fallback logs the degradation naming C.2/C.3 and C.4. Tests: tests/sprint-coordination.test.ts (14) + packages/apra-fleet-se/test/mcp-coordination-clients.test.mjs (8); se suite 0 fail, root vitest failures limited to 4 pre-existing Windows EBUSY sandbox-integ tests verified to fail identically without this change. Known non-blocking follow-ups: (a) coordination core is restated in TS because rootDir/allowJs and the workspace dependency direction forbid importing the supervisor .mjs -- a shared coordination workspace package is the right end state; (b) a ticket whose grant is reclaimed by lease/dead-pid expiry leaves a small map entry behind on a long-lived server.

title: [impl] Thread --service-url from supervisor spawner and direct CLI into the sprint runner
description:
Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/spawner.mjs (buildSprintArgv), packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/cli.mjs (buildRunnerArgs ~281 and the engine.executeFile call ~706-729).

Behaviour: buildSprintArgv() adds --service-url pointing at the supervisor's own listening address (the address the supervisor already binds for its HTTP API); cli.mjs accepts --service-url and threads it into the runner args / executeFile options so runner.js (~5013-5052) takes the HTTP-backed dolt-mutex and id-allocator clients instead of the source-3 no-op fallback.

Acceptance criteria:
- grep for serviceUrl now shows it produced by spawner.mjs and consumed by cli.mjs, not only referenced inside runner.js.
- A supervisor-spawned sprint's child command line contains --service-url <supervisor base url>.
- Absent --service-url the behaviour is unchanged (fallback preserved) and no crash.
- Unit test covering buildSprintArgv/buildRunnerArgs argv content added; 'npm test' green. ASCII only.
close_reason: Threaded --service-url from spawner.mjs (createSpawner deps.serviceUrl -> buildSprintArgv) through bin/serve.mjs into cli.mjs (buildOptionsSpec/buildRunnerArgs/executeFile call), which runner.js consumes for the HTTP-backed dolt-mutex/id-allocator clients. Unit tests added in spawner.test.mjs and cli-robustness.test.mjs; targeted node --test run: 51/51 pass. Commit ce178f6.

title: [test] run-id keyed engine run-state across consecutive supervisor sprints
description:
Integration test verifying apra-fleet-k7b.1 (run-id plumbing). Place under the repo integration test folder (packages/apra-fleet-se/test or the designated integration test dir), never inline in src.

What to test:
- buildSprintArgv() (packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/spawner.mjs) emits --run-id <supervisor sprintId> in the child argv.
- bin/cli.mjs consumes --run-id for run-state persistence and falls back to branch name when absent (standalone CLI launch).

title: Wire serviceUrl end-to-end so the dolt-mutex/id-allocator actually engage in real sprint launches (currently dead code)
description:
CORRECTED SCOPE (2026-07-30, superseding this bead's original text): the original framing -- "no lock exists, build one" -- was wrong. A dolt-push mutex (packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/dolt-mutex.mjs, client createHttpDoltPushMutexClient in fleet-sprint/runner.js ~1781-1854, apra-fleet-eft.9.2) AND a global child-id allocator (src/supervisor/id-allocator.mjs, client createHttpChildIdAllocatorClient ~1856-1943, apra-fleet-eft.9.3) already exist and are correctly implemented (FIFO acquire, lease/pid-probe reclaim, token-guarded release).

The real bug: `serviceUrl` -- the one arg that switches these clients from their no-op fallback to the real HTTP-backed path (runner.js ~5013-5052) -- is NEVER passed by either real launch path. Confirmed by direct grep: `serviceUrl` appears nowhere in the repo outside runner.js itself. The supervisor's spawner (packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/spawner.mjs, buildSprintArgv()) has no --service-url flag. The direct-CLI path (packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/cli.mjs, buildRunnerArgs() ~line 281, and the engine.executeFile() call ~706-729) never sets serviceUrl either. So in every real launch today -- supervisor-spawned AND direct-CLI -- both clients silently take the source-3 no-op fallback (runner.js comment: \"a lone sprint has, by definition, no second sprint to conflict with\" -- false for concurrent supervisor-spawned sprints, which is exactly our situation this session).

This means BOTH beads-DB incidents this session (apra-fleet-bnb.1/.2 duplicate filing, apra-fleet-04g.1 id collision) occurred with this \"protection\" silently disengaged the whole time, not merely narrow in scope.

Fix:
1. Wire serviceUrl end-to-end: buildSprintArgv() (spawner.mjs) passes --service-url pointing at the supervisor's own listening address; buildRunnerArgs()/executeFile() (cli.mjs) thread it into the runner's args.
2. For the supervisor-less standalone-CLI launch path (the operator's own `apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint` detached-binary convention, which has no supervisor to reach): host the lock/allocator on the fleet MCP server instead (or in addition) -- cli.mjs already holds a connected mcpClient (used for member_reservation, stop_prompt), so this topology has a reachable coordination point even without a supervisor. This covers both launch topologies; supervisor-hosting alone covers neither today (dead code) and only one after the spawner fix.
3. Add an integration-engagement test that a REAL end-to-end launch (not just runner.js's own unit tests) actually reaches the HTTP endpoint and the no-op fallback is never silently taken when concurrent sprints are live -- the previous eft.9.2/9.3 work shipped modules and unit tests but no integration test proved real launches use them, which is exactly how this went unnoticed.

Note: a dolt-push mutex alone would NOT have prevented the actual apra-fleet-bnb incident (an unmergeable CONTENT conflict from independently-created child ids in separate clones) -- that is the id-allocator's job, not the mutex's. Both need wiring; don't treat the mutex alone as sufficient.

Test: launch two real concurrent sprints (supervisor-spawned) whose scopes share a beads remote; assert both engage the HTTP-backed mutex/allocator (not the no-op fallback) via a log/metric assertion, and that two D-pushes never interleave.
close_reason: Verify-and-close: all 3 children (f34.1-.3) closed -- --service-url wired in spawner.mjs, MCP-hosted dolt-push mutex + child-id allocator shipped for supervisor-less launches, engagement integ-tested (xuo.7).

title: Unify sprint run identity across supervisor and engine so terminations are classified and reported truthfully
description:
The supervisor keys sprints by <issueRoot>-<uuid> but never passes that id to the child: buildSprintArgv() (packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/spawner.mjs) has no run-id flag, and bin/cli.mjs passes sprintId: branchName (~line 682) to the runner, so the engine persists run state at old_runs/<branch>.json (e.g. old_runs/feat/lhf-batch-a.json). The watchdog's hasTerminalState() (src/supervisor/watchdog.mjs) looks for old_runs/<issueRoot>-<uuid>.json, which can never exist, so every ended supervisor-launched sprint is classified CRASHED regardless of outcome.

Evidence (2026-07-30 incident analysis, see ANALYSIS-REPORT.md): incarnations apra-fleet-bnb-de118180 and apra-fleet-04g-1ee6c369 ran 2-3h and ended with orderly recorded reasons (POST_DISPATCH_SYNC_FAILED, SPRINT_STALLED) yet were reported "CRASHED ... no terminal state ever persisted" ~5 min later; branch-keyed state files also let each relaunch overwrite the prior incarnation's record (incarnations apra-fleet-bnb-04a44f65, apra-fleet-04g-3ee3c352 terminal states unrecoverable); the spawner's exit listener discards the exit code it already has in hand. This single misreporting layer manufactured the appearance of "the same error recurring without resolution" when in fact most incarnations were distinct, individually diagnosed issues.

This is a parent/epic; see child tasks for the concrete work breakdown. Complements apra-fleet-jnw (child stdio capture) but does not depend on it.
