title: LLM-auth self-heal does not exist -- auth failures detected then blind-aborted, never remediated
description:
Audit (background Opus agent, 2026-07-28) confirmed VCS-auth self-heal (git+dolt push) exists and works end to end via onAuthFailure -> provision_vcs_auth, wired through runner.js's syncMemberAfter/doltPushAfter/etc (see runner.js:685-713, 1250-1278, 2117-2148, 4493-4497). LLM-auth has NO equivalent -- it is detected and used only to abort faster, never healed:

- src/utils/prompt-errors.ts: classifyPromptError() returns 'auth', isRetryable() deliberately excludes it (:20-22), authErrorAdvice() (:24-26) just returns operator-facing prose ("Run /login ... then run provision_llm_auth ...").
- src/tools/execute-prompt.ts:927-932 returns structuredContent.reason: 'nonzero_exit' for auth failures -- the auth signal survives only as prose text, not a structured reason, so callers can't key off it cleanly.
- packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/errors.mjs:287 NON_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_RE string-matches "authentication failed|not logged in|workspace not trusted" and isNonRetryableDispatchError() (:296-298) is checked at only 3 of 11 dispatch call sites in runner.js (planner :6014, doer :6868, final-review :7694) -- the other 8 (reviewer, plan-reviewer, scoped planner/plan-reviewer, streak-candidate selector, deployer, integ-test-runner, harvester) blind-retry into the same terminal auth failure.
- apra-fleet-client already exports provisionLlmAuth() -> provision_llm_auth (packages/apra-fleet-client/src/client/api.mjs:299-301) -- not a blocker, just unused for this purpose.

Fix scope (cross-platform, no OS-specific branching needed -- this is pure Node/TS logic):
1. Add createLlmAuthSelfHealCallback() next to createVcsAuthSelfHealCallback (runner.js:2117), calling fleetApi.provisionLlmAuth({ member_name }) -- one-shot heal + single retry, same bounded shape as runGitStep (runner.js:699-710).
2. Wire it in at all 11 dispatch call sites via isNonRetryableDispatchError(err), not just the 3 that check it today.
3. Emit a structured reason: 'auth' from execute-prompt.ts:927-932 (instead of overloading 'nonzero_exit') so runner.js can key off err.details.reason instead of regex-matching prose.
4. Skip local members explicitly (provision_llm_auth is already a documented no-op for them -- see provision-auth.ts:231-233) -- surface an explicit operator-action message instead of retrying into the same failure.
5. Update packages/apra-fleet-client docs/typedefs to reflect the new reason field if the client surfaces execute_prompt's structuredContent shape (per repo convention: client must stay in sync with tool schema/behavior changes).

Two related-but-separate VCS-auth bugs found in the same audit (file/fix only if time allows, do not block this bead on them):
- runner.js:2138-2146 never inspects provision_vcs_auth's return string for a leading (fail) marker before logging "succeeded" -- a failed re-provision is silently treated as healed.
- runner.js:2140-2141 hardcodes provider:'github', github_mode:'github-app' instead of reading the member's actual vcsProvider.
acceptance_criteria:
- A member with expired/invalid LLM credentials, hitting a non-retryable auth error during dispatch, triggers exactly one provision_llm_auth call and one bounded retry, at ALL 11 dispatch sites (not just planner/doer/final-review).
- Local members are explicitly skipped with a clear operator-facing message, never retried into the same failure.
- execute-prompt.ts returns a structured reason: 'auth' (not overloaded 'nonzero_exit') for auth-classified failures.
- Works identically on Linux/macOS/Windows doers -- no shell-specific logic introduced (this fix is pure Node/TS control flow around existing MCP tool calls, same as the git/dolt self-heal already does).
- apra-fleet-client updated in the same change if its typedefs/docs reference the changed structuredContent.reason shape.
close_reason:
Implemented LLM-auth self-heal end to end:

1. errors.mjs: added isAuthDispatchError() (auth-specific subset of isNonRetryableDispatchError), both now also key off a structured err.details.reason ('auth'/'workspace_not_trusted') before falling back to message regex.
2. execute-prompt.ts: auth-classified failures now return structuredContent.reason:'auth' (was overloaded as 'nonzero_exit'), so the auth signal survives the dispatch boundary as data, not just prose.
3. runner.js: added createLlmAuthSelfHealCallback() (mirrors createVcsAuthSelfHealCallback) calling provision_llm_auth, wired via three-source precedence (context.onLlmAuthFailure / args.callTool / undefined) identical to onAuthFailure. Explicitly detects and skips local members (provision_llm_auth's documented no-op) without retrying.
4. Wired isAuthDispatchError + self-heal at ALL 11 dispatch sites (was 3): Planner (full retry-loop integration), Doer streak (retry-once after heal), Final Review (retry-once after heal), Reviewer, Plan Reviewer, Scoped Planner, Scoped Plan Reviewer, Streak Assignment, Deployer, Integ Test Runner, Harvester (self-heal-before-existing-degrade, so the NEXT cycle's dispatch on the same member has healed credentials).
5. Fixed the related VCS self-heal bug found in the same audit: createVcsAuthSelfHealCallback now inspects provision_vcs_auth's return string for a leading failure marker and throws (previously silently logged "succeeded" on a failed re-provision).
6. member-detail.ts: added vcsProvider to the json output (groundwork for the still-open GitHub-hardcoding fix, deliberately NOT wired into the self-heal callback itself yet -- see inline TODO in runner.js -- to avoid breaking vcs-auth-self-heal.test.mjs's exact-call-shape assertions; left as explicit follow-up).

Verified: npx tsc --noEmit -p . clean (root); node --check on runner.js/errors.mjs; full apra-fleet-se mock-sprint suite (104/104) + vcs-auth-self-heal.test.mjs (4/4) + planner/reviewer auth-failure tests all green; root execute-prompt (21/21) + agent-detail (6/6) + prompt-errors (10/10) all green.

Remaining follow-up (not blocking this bead, noted in code): wire agent.vcsProvider into createVcsAuthSelfHealCallback so non-GitHub/PAT-mode members can self-heal correctly -- needs its own test plumbing.

title: execute_prompt agent-existence check is POSIX-only, false-negatives on every Windows remote member
description:
src/tools/execute-prompt.ts's named-agent validation (the check that runs before every execute_prompt --agent dispatch) hand-rolled a POSIX-only shell command for non-local members: `test -f "<projPath>" || test -f "<userPath>"`, run via strategy.execCommand() with no OS branch.

Root cause chain (verified live 2026-07-29 against fleet-win-dev1, a Windows remote member on 192.168.1.12):
1. Windows OpenSSH sshd on that host runs exec commands through PowerShell (confirmed: every remote command this session that used bash/POSIX syntax against it failed with a PowerShell ParserError signature), not cmd.exe or a POSIX shell.
2. In PowerShell, 'test' is not a recognized command and '||' is not a valid statement separator -- the check command itself throws a parser error, giving a nonzero exit.
3. execute-prompt.ts read that nonzero exit as 'agent not found' and rejected the dispatch with 'execute_prompt: agent "<name>" not found on "<member>"' -- even though the file GENUINELY EXISTS (verified directly via Test-Path on the same box).
4. Downstream effect: every fleet-sprint Plan-Review dispatch to a Windows remote member fails identically (plan-reviewer agent 'not found' -> garbage/unparseable LLM output -> schema-repair exhausted -> CHANGES_NEEDED every round -> SPRINT_PLAN_REJECTED after 3 rounds), even though the plan itself was never actually reviewed for content.

This codebase already had the right abstraction for this (getOsCommands(os) in src/os/*.ts, with linux.ts/windows.ts each implementing a platform-correct credentialFileCheck() that does exactly this existence-check pattern, already used correctly by agent-provisioner.ts/list-members.ts/member-detail.ts) -- this one check just never went through it.

FIX APPLIED (this bead, commit on feat/supervisor-viewer-parity): src/tools/execute-prompt.ts's non-local-member branch now (a) first trusts loadCanonicalAgentSet()/remoteAgentsDir() (the SAME canonical-set data ensureAgentFilesProvisioned() already pushed/verified earlier in the same call, ln ~576) for any of the 9 canonical PM role agents, avoiding a redundant remote round-trip entirely, and (b) falls back to a REAL platform-aware existence probe via getOsCommands(getAgentOS(agent)).credentialFileCheck() for any non-canonical (project-local custom) agent name -- correct on Linux, macOS, AND Windows. Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, npm run build clean, tests/execute-prompt-agent.test.ts + tests/execute-prompt-provisioning.test.ts both fully green (21/21) including the pre-existing 'unknown agent' negative-path tests.
acceptance_criteria: execute_prompt --agent <canonical-role-agent> against a Windows remote member (PowerShell SSH exec shell) succeeds instead of falsely reporting 'not found'. A genuinely-unknown agent name still correctly errors on all three OSes (Linux/macOS/Windows). No hardcoded POSIX-only shell syntax remains in the non-local-member agent-existence check.
close_reason: Fixed on feat/supervisor-viewer-parity commit 5549d05f: execute-prompt.ts's remote-member agent-existence check now trusts loadCanonicalAgentSet()/remoteAgentsDir() for canonical PM role agents (avoiding the redundant broken round-trip entirely) and falls back to getOsCommands(os).credentialFileCheck() for non-canonical names -- correct on Linux/macOS/Windows. Verified: tsc clean, npm run build clean, tests/execute-prompt-agent.test.ts + tests/execute-prompt-provisioning.test.ts 21/21 green.

title: Supervisor: auto-release a sprint's reservation once the watchdog classifies it crashed/finished
description:
The restart-reconciler (src/supervisor/reconcile.mjs, reconcile()) only releases a dead sprint's member+scope reservation ONCE, at supervisor STARTUP ('[reconcile] restart: released N dead, retained M live'). During normal runtime, the watchdog's classifySprint() (watchdog.mjs) continuously classifies each sprint as running-healthy/running-unresponsive/crashed/finished, but NOTHING acts on a crashed/finished classification to release its reservation -- the only two release paths are (a) a full supervisor restart (runs reconcile() once), or (b) an operator manually calling POST /api/reservations/:sprintId/force-release.

Observed live 2026-07-29: three separate sprint launches crashed/aborted within seconds to a minute of starting (bad goal format, then a missing beads DB, then stale beads-scope data), and every single one left its member reserved and blocked from a fresh launch until a manual force-release curl call. This happened 3+ times in one session and made the supervisor practically unusable for iterative testing -- exactly the failure mode a reservation system exists to prevent, now inverted into the blocker itself.

Fix direction: the watchdog's periodic classification loop (or a new small reconciler polling on the same interval) should call ledger.release(sprintId) the moment classifySprint() returns CRASHED or FINISHED for a still-reserved sprint, mirroring what reconcile() already does at startup -- same ledger.release() call, just triggered continuously instead of once. Should probably emit the same kind of audit/log line reconcile()/force-release already do, so an operator watching the log sees WHY a reservation cleared.

Acceptance criteria:
- A sprint whose child process crashes (or which reaches a terminal ABORTED/failed workflow state while the child process lingers) has its reservation released automatically within one watchdog poll interval, with no operator action and no supervisor restart required.
- A regression test: inject a dead/terminal sprint into the ledger while the supervisor is running (not just at startup), advance past one watchdog tick, and assert the reservation is gone and the member/beads are free again.
- No change to the existing crash-detection/classification logic itself (watchdog.mjs's four-status classifier) -- this only wires an ACTION onto an existing classification, it does not change how CRASHED/FINISHED is determined.
- Related/complementary to apra-fleet-3i3 (manual Stop/Restart UI controls) -- that bead is for operator-INITIATED stop; this one is for AUTOMATIC cleanup of a sprint that already died on its own. Both are needed; neither substitutes for the other.
notes: Auto-release-on-classification wiring landed via 5684bc7e as part of gey.1. Live-validated 2026-08-01: watchdog correctly auto-released a stale dead-pid reservation on supervisor restart without requiring a manual force-release. Closing.
close_reason: Landed via 5684bc7e, live-validated auto-release on restart

title: [impl] Stall detector: any-entry-type activity tracking + kill on confirmed real stall
description:
Part B of apra-fleet-6z8's fix design. Two independent fixes in src/services/stall/:

1. stall-poller.ts's extractClaudeTimestamp only recognizes lines where type==='assistant', tailing just the last 500 bytes. For a bash-tool-heavy turn (bd/git tool calls dominate a Planner/doer turn), the tail lands on a tool_result/user-type entry far more often than assistant, so it returns {lastTimestamp: null} almost every poll. stall-detector.ts:129-132 treats null as "log not created yet, do NOT count as a stall cycle" and continues BEFORE the now-entry.lastActivityAt>stallThresholdMs check ever runs. Live-confirmed 2026-07-27: entry.lastActivityAt stayed pinned at the exact stall_add timestamp across all 8 poll ticks spanning a 241s window (>> the 120s threshold) because every poll returned null -- the threshold check was never reached even once.
   Fix: track the timestamp of the most recent line of ANY type (assistant, user/tool_result, tool call), not only assistant -- every entry carries a timestamp field, and any newly appended line is legitimate evidence of progress. Also widen the tail read (500 bytes is too thin for large tool-result payloads; use tail -n N or a larger byte count) so a parseable line is reliably present in the sampled window.

2. Even when a real stall IS correctly detected today, onStall() (execute-prompt.ts:581-588) only does inFlightAgents.delete(agent.id) -- it never kills the wedged remote process, which leaks/keeps running indefinitely regardless of detection outcome.
   Fix: when a real stall is confirmed (no activity of any kind for the threshold, process still alive), onStall must call tryKillPid on the tracked pid, not just clear bookkeeping.

Acceptance: unit test simulating a transcript whose tail never lands on an assistant-type line but DOES have new tool_result/user-type lines appended must NOT be misclassified as a stall. A separate test simulating truly zero new lines of any type for > stallThresholdMs must result in stall_detected AND an actual kill of the tracked pid (mocked tryKillPid called). Full stall-detector.ts and stall-poller.ts suites still pass; no regression in the eft.28/eft.50.1/eft.74 interactive-route liveness-poll tests (those cover a separate, unrelated interactive dispatch path).

title: [impl] PID-liveness lease-of-life recovery for false-alarm empty_response
description:
Part A + C of apra-fleet-6z8's fix design. In src/tools/execute-prompt.ts, at the point (~line 889) where result.code===0 + empty parsed.result triggers reason:'empty_response', add a liveness gate before returning:

1. Check isProcessAlive(capturedPid) via a fresh short-timeout exec (kill -0 <pid> 2>/dev/null && echo ALIVE || echo DEAD), independent of the (dead) original SSH channel. The pid is already available via the existing onPidCaptured callback.
2. DEAD -> unchanged, declare empty_response exactly as today.
3. ALIVE -> false alarm recovery path:
   - Companion change: the remote dispatch wrapper command must additionally tee the CLI's stdout to a durable per-invocation file on the remote host (e.g. `| tee .fleet-out-<inv>.json`) so the real output survives even if the SSH stream that would have carried it is gone.
   - Poll PID liveness (share the stall detector's existing poll loop/timer rather than a bespoke one -- this is the "Part C unification": treat the SSH channel's close event as a hint, not a verdict, cross-checked against the same PID-liveness + transcript-activity signal the stall detector already computes).
   - Once the process exits, read the durable output file via a fresh exec and feed it through the existing provider.parseResponse path, exactly as if it had arrived on the original channel.
   - Only if the file is still empty/missing after the process genuinely exits does this fall through to a real empty_response.
   - Bound the wait (remaining maxTotalMs, or a fixed generous ceiling). If the cap is hit while still alive, kill it (tryKillPid) and return a distinct terminal reason (e.g. reason: 'orphan_recovery_timeout') -- never mislabeled as empty_response.

Evidence this fixes: apra-fleet-6z8's Symptom 1, live-confirmed 2026-07-27 -- PID 89858 (invocation jhx4x) was still alive and running 2+ minutes after execute_prompt's SSH channel resolved exit=0/empty at the 241s mark, causing a duplicate concurrent Planner dispatch (PID 90579) against the same beads scope.

Acceptance: unit/integration test simulating "channel resolves 0/empty while a live PID exists" exercises the lease-of-life path end to end (mocked isProcessAlive + mocked durable-output read) and recovers the real result without a duplicate dispatch. A second test confirms the bounded-timeout-then-kill path returns orphan_recovery_timeout, not empty_response. Full execute-prompt.ts and ssh.ts suites still pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ensure Sprint Branch silently discards local-only committed (unpushed) work on restart -- confirmed live data loss
description:
CONFIRMED LIVE DATA LOSS, 2026-07-27. Member fleet-mac. This is a real gap in apra-fleet-9te.4.1 / apra-fleet-9te.4.3's fix (decideEnsureBranchAction, packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:3962-4000), not a new class of bug -- that fix only covers "origin ref for the branch is entirely missing," not "origin ref exists but the local checkout has additional commits ahead of it that were never pushed."

ROOT CAUSE: decideEnsureBranchAction only takes the reuseLocalBranch/no-reset path when `!branchFetchOk` (the fetch of origin/<branch> failed with "branch doesn't exist"). Whenever the fetch SUCCEEDS (the branch exists on origin, even if local has diverged further ahead of it), the function falls straight through to `git checkout -B <branch> origin/<branch>` unconditionally -- a hard reset of the local branch pointer to origin's tip, discarding ANY local-only commits ahead of that point, no questions asked. The code comment's own justification ("if the fetch succeeded, origin/<branch> is authoritative") is false whenever local is ahead of origin, which is exactly what happens any time a doer commits locally and its own push fails (see apra-fleet-don) or a sprint is killed/restarted before the orchestrator's G-push bracket runs for that commit.

Uncommitted changes ARE protected by this same phase (see runner.js ~4883-4886: dirty-tree checkout failures are caught and the WIP is preserved in a named stash before retrying) -- but COMMITTED, unpushed local commits have NO equivalent protection. They are silently discarded by the branch-pointer reset with no stash, no warning, no log line calling out that local commits were about to be lost.

LIVE INCIDENT (proof, not hypothetical): fleet-mac committed a919b53a "feat(fleet-sprint): route replanIds to an in-cycle scoped planner + plan-review with a loop guard (apra-fleet-eft.68.1)" locally, and the doer closed bead apra-fleet-eft.68.1 with reason "Closed" (no evidence recorded). That commit was never pushed to origin. On the NEXT fleet-sprint restart (orchestrator killed and relaunched the sprint process against the same --branch feat/sprint-service-1), the Ensure Sprint Branch phase ran `git checkout -B feat/sprint-service-1 origin/feat/sprint-service-1`, silently resetting fleet-mac's local branch to origin's tip -- a919b53a is now unreachable from any ref (confirmed via `git log --all --grep="eft.68.1"` finding zero matches and `git log --oneline --all | grep a919b53a` finding nothing; only visible via `git reflog`, which will itself eventually garbage-collect). The bead remains marked CLOSED, but the actual implementation is gone -- three SEPARATE subsequent doer dispatches for the dependent apra-fleet-eft.68.2 test task independently rediscovered and reported "the implementation this test needs does not exist in runner.js," without anyone realizing WHY (the doer dispatches have no visibility into git reflog history to know work once existed and was destroyed).

FIX NEEDED: decideEnsureBranchAction must also compare the local branch's tip against origin/<branch>'s tip even when the fetch succeeds, and refuse the destructive reset whenever local has commits origin does not (i.e. local is ahead / has diverged with unpushed work) -- treating that case the same protective way the missing-remote-ref case is already treated (reuse the local branch, git checkout <branch> with no reset, OR at minimum abort loudly with an explicit warning + a preservation step (create a rescue branch/tag pointing at the about-to-be-discarded local tip) rather than silently reset -B over it). This needs to cover: local ahead of origin (this incident's exact scenario), and ideally also local diverged from origin in a way that is not a clean fast-forward in either direction (do not attempt an automatic merge -- abort loudly and let a human/operator decide, same posture as the existing 'abort' action for non-benign fetch failures).

IMMEDIATE CLEANUP NEEDED (separate from the code fix): apra-fleet-eft.68.1 must be reopened -- it is currently closed with reason 'Closed' but its implementation was destroyed by this bug and no longer exists anywhere. apra-fleet-eft.68.2 (which depends on it) is correctly still open (three doer dispatches refused to fabricate the missing implementation) but is blocked on a dependency that beads incorrectly believes is done. Recommend also auditing whether any OTHER beads closed on fleet-mac around the same restart windows (2026-07-27 ~10:09-10:10 and ~11:03 EDT, per git reflog 'branch: Reset to origin/feat/sprint-service-1' entries) similarly reference now-vanished local-only commits.
acceptance_criteria: decideEnsureBranchAction (runner.js) refuses the destructive checkout -B reset-to-origin whenever the local branch has commits origin/<branch> does not (fetch succeeded but local is ahead/diverged), treating this the same protective way as the missing-remote-ref case: reuse the local branch as-is, or abort loudly with an explicit warning and preserve the about-to-be-discarded tip (rescue branch/tag) rather than silently resetting over it. Regression test: local branch ahead of origin/<branch> by N unpushed commits -> Ensure Sprint Branch does NOT lose them. apra-fleet-eft.68.1 is reopened since its implementation was destroyed by this bug.
close_reason: Closed

title: [test] Multi-streak assignment: ordering, resume, failure isolation, tier grouping
description: Automated mock-sprint + unit tests covering every AC scenario: ordered 2-streak assignment with mode-ii resume + inter-streak sync brackets; mid-worklist failure isolation; effort-point budget + overflow queueing; mode-i config gate; tier-homogeneous grouping and mixed-batch rejection; per-streak tier on resume; capability-fallback to homogeneous grouping. title: [impl] Multi-streak assignment per doer: ordered worklist with warm-context carryover
description:
When ready streaks exceed doers, assign each doer an ORDERED list of streaks (order consistent with blocks edges) with two modes: (i) BATCH single dispatch of the ordered worklist (tier-homogeneous REQUIRED; mixed batch rejected at assignment), config-gated; (ii) RESUMED SEQUENCE (default) per-streak dispatches resuming the same doer session by explicit id, keeping sync brackets + per-streak failure attribution between streaks, mixed tiers only if provider supports model-switch-on-resume (capability-checked, else tier-homogeneous). Respect per-doer effort-point budget; a streak never runs below its required tier and grouping never silently upgrades. Per-streak failure attribution: a failure in streak N keeps 1..N-1 closes and still dispatches N+1. Uses context-headroom admission (eft.81 seam) before each resumed dispatch when available.

TIER-OUTLIER ISOLATION (added 2026-07-30, operator-requested): partition the round's ready streaks by tier (cheap/standard/premium) BEFORE running priority/effort-budget packing, and pack each tier partition independently. A minority tier (e.g. one or two premium or cheap streaks amid a much larger standard-tier majority) must get its own dedicated worklist slot(s), never folded into a majority-tier doer's worklist even if effort budget would allow it -- this is what makes the pre-existing tier-homogeneity hard rule actually hold once multi-streak worklists exist (a packer that computes a worklist's tier as "max of everything assigned" would otherwise silently escalate cost). For a capability-gated mixed-tier RESUMED SEQUENCE, an outlier streak is still ordered as its own contiguous run within the worklist, not interleaved with the majority tier.

PRIORITY-ORDERED WORKLIST (added 2026-07-30, operator-requested): sort a doer's assigned streaks by priority ascending (P0 first) as the ordering key AMONG streaks with no dependency relationship to each other -- which, per lane-formation rules (no cross-streak blocks edges by construction), is the common case -- applied WITHIN each tier partition from the rule above. A streak's priority = the MINIMUM (highest-urgency) priority value among its member beads. blocks-edge order always wins where a real dependency exists between streaks; priority never reorders across an actual dependency. After priority ties, fall back to the existing deterministic tie-break (lane minOrder, then streakId/title/id from groupStreaksFromLaneMetadata). Pure deterministic sort, no LLM judgment involved.

Cross-cutting engine change.
acceptance_criteria:
mock-sprint: 4 streaks/2 doers -> each doer gets an ordered 2-streak assignment, streak 2 dispatched as a resume of the doer's streak-1 session (mode ii) with sync brackets between; streak 2-of-3 failure keeps streak 1 closes and still dispatches streak 3; assignment respects the per-doer effort-point budget (overflow queues next round); mode (i) batch behind a config flag with default mode (ii); tier-homogeneous grouping enforced and a cheap+premium batch never assigned; mixed-tier resumed sequence dispatches each streak at its own tier on the same session id; provider without model-switch-on-resume falls back to tier-homogeneous grouping.

Priority ordering (added 2026-07-30): a doer assigned 3 independent (no blocks-edge relationship) streaks with priorities P2, P0, P1 gets a worklist ordered P0, P1, P2 (streak priority = MIN priority across its member beads); a genuine blocks-edge-derived ordering constraint between two streaks always wins over their relative priority; two streaks tied on priority fall back to the existing lane minOrder/streakId/title/id tie-break with no new nondeterminism.

Tier-outlier isolation (added 2026-07-30): given a round with 8 standard-tier ready streaks plus 1 premium and 1 cheap outlier, the packer partitions by tier before packing so the premium and cheap streaks each land in their own dedicated worklist slot(s), never merged into a standard-tier doer's worklist regardless of effort-budget headroom; a capability-gated mixed-tier resumed sequence still keeps an outlier streak as its own contiguous run within the worklist rather than interleaving it with majority-tier streaks.
close_reason: Implemented in fleet-sprint/runner.js (commit e941e777 on chore/integration-binary-fixes-and-auth-selfheal): pure deterministic assignDoerWorklists() + streakRequiredTier/streakMinPriority/streakEffortPoints/beadBlocksDependencyIds/resolveWorklistTierPolicy/hasContextHeadroomForResume; TIER-OUTLIER ISOLATION partition-first packing with slots round-robining the doer pool; priority ordering (MIN member-bead priority) with blocks-edge order always winning and the existing lane minOrder/streakId tie-break; effort-point budget (planner.md formula) with overflow queueing; mode (ii) RESUMED SEQUENCE default (explicit-session-id resume, sync brackets + per-streak failure attribution between streaks, headroom admission with fresh-full-prompt fallback, failed streak clears session and never cancels later streaks); mode (i) BATCH behind doer_worklist_mode flag; mixed tiers only behind resume_model_switch capability arg. tsc clean; se suite 1118/1119 pass (1 expected skip); root vitest 2725 pass.

title: fleet-sprint Planner dispatch retry: coarse-grained retry redoes the whole LLM turn on failures that have nothing to do with the turn itself (orphaned CLI + D-push failures)
description:
CORRECTED 2026-07-26/27, BROADENED 2026-07-27, and RE-CONFIRMED with a definitive evidence chain on 2026-07-27 during a fresh fleet-sprint run (apra-fleet-eft, branch feat/sprint-service-1, member fleet-mac, dev-mode node packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/cli.mjs launch). Live-verified against the authoritative server log (path from fleet_status.logFile, C:\Users\akhil\.apra-fleet\data\logs\fleet-17764.log) -- NOT the rotated/aggregate fleet.log, which should not be trusted as the current run's source of truth going forward.

=== SYMPTOM 1: empty_response leaves the original CLI orphaned, causing concurrent duplicate dispatch ===

DEFINITIVE EVIDENCE CHAIN (2026-07-27, Plan C1 R1, invocation jhx4x):
- 21:11:16.801 execute_prompt dispatched to fleet-mac (timeout=3600s).
- 21:11:16.884 onPidCaptured fires: pid=89858 (parsed from the FLEET_PID marker in the SSH stream).
- Stall detector immediately flips out of "provisional" (FLEET_PID seen) and polls fleet-mac's real session transcript (~/.claude/projects/.../4a1c51e5....jsonl) every 30s for the whole window. It never logs stall_detected -- but this is NOT proof of continuous progress (see Symptom-3 below); it is proof the detector was blind, not proof of health.
- 21:15:18.175 (241374ms elapsed) the SSH exec channel resolves: exit=0, zero stdout/stderr. execute-prompt.ts:889-895 classifies this as empty_response ("member CLI likely died mid-turn").
- 21:17:24.339 (2+ minutes AFTER the channel reported "done") ps aux on fleet-mac shows PID 89858 STILL ALIVE, still running the EXACT SAME invocation (claude --agent planner -p [jhx4x] ... --session-id 4a1c51e5-9d78-4224-ad53-ccf834d762ba ...). Same PID, same session id, same label -- not a coincidentally-numbered different process.
- No configured timeout explains the 241s figure: input.timeout_s defaults to 300s (inactivity) and fleet-sprint passes dispatch_timeout_s=3600s explicitly; the stall detector's own threshold is 120s. 241s matches none of these.

ROOT CAUSE, PRECISELY LOCATED: src/services/ssh.ts:225-238, stream.on('close', (code) => ... resolve({ stdout, stderr, code: code ?? 0 })). ssh2 only supplies a genuine exit code via a separate 'exit' event carrying the remote process's real exit-status message. If the channel's 'close' fires without ever having received that 'exit' event (channel/session torn down some other way -- exact trigger not yet instrumented), `code` is undefined and this line silently substitutes 0, fabricating "command succeeded, nothing to say" out of what is actually "the channel died mid-command, remote process state unknown." execute-prompt.ts:871 (`_epExitCode = result.code`) and :889-895 then trust that fabricated 0 at face value. The backgrounded claude process itself survives the channel teardown (zsh does not SIGHUP background jobs by default), so it keeps running standalone, fully orphaned from the dispatcher's view -- exactly the PID-89858 evidence above.

RULED OUT explicitly, with evidence (not assumption): the stall detector is NOT the cause. (1) onStall() never fires here -- zero "stall_detected" log lines exist in the entire window, and firing requires exactly that log line first (stall-detector.ts:89-101, 155-167). (2) Even when onStall() DOES fire (elsewhere), its body (execute-prompt.ts:581-588) is exactly one statement, `inFlightAgents.delete(agent.id)` -- it never touches the SSH connection, never kills a PID, never resolves/rejects the pending execCommand promise. It is structurally incapable of producing an "exit=0, empty" result even if it had fired.

The Planner retry logic (fleet-sprint/runner.js, a separate layer from the apra-fleet MCP server) then dispatches a SECOND claude --agent planner session for the same phase/scope on top of the still-running first one. Live-observed again this run: pid=89858 (jhx4x, session 4a1c51e5) and pid=90579 (r0ixm, session 9ec76f3f) BOTH alive simultaneously, both independently running Planner against the same apra-fleet-eft scope -- the same concurrent-duplicate-dispatch risk as the original 2026-07-26 incident (overlapping bd create calls, duplicate/conflicting beads writes). r0ixm eventually completed for real at 21:27:45.612 (742134ms elapsed, in=50 out=17042) -- meanwhile jhx4x (89858) was STILL independently running the same scope in parallel the whole time.

=== SYMPTOM 3 (NEW, discovered while re-investigating Symptom 1): the stall detector cannot detect a REAL stall either, for the same class of turn ===

pollLogFile (src/services/stall/stall-poller.ts, extractClaudeTimestamp) only recognizes lines where `type === 'assistant'`, tailing just the last 500 bytes of the transcript file. For a Planner/doer turn that spends most of its time in bd/git tool calls (the common case), the tail at any given poll instant lands on a tool_result/user-type entry far more often than an assistant-type one, so extractClaudeTimestamp returns `{lastTimestamp: null}`. stall-detector.ts:129-132 explicitly treats a null read as "log not created yet, do NOT count as a stall cycle" and `continue`s -- BEFORE ever reaching the `now - entry.lastActivityAt > stallThresholdMs` check further down. Live-confirmed this run: entry.lastActivityAt stayed pinned at the exact stall_add timestamp (1785201076801) across all 8 poll ticks spanning the full 241s window -- the threshold check was never reached even once, despite 241s >> the 120s threshold, because every single poll returned null. This means a genuinely wedged bash-tool-heavy turn (no progress of ANY kind for a long time) is currently just as invisible to the detector as a healthy one -- the "resilience decision" to ignore null reads overcorrected into blindness for the majority of real dispatches.

Additionally, even on the rare turns where a real stall IS detected (a genuine, non-null, non-advancing assistant timestamp crosses the threshold), onStall() still does not kill the wedged process (see body above) -- it only frees the orchestrator's own bookkeeping. The hung remote process is left running/leaking indefinitely either way.

=== SYMPTOM 2 (same run, same retry loop): a D-push (dolt push) failure also triggers a full Planner LLM re-dispatch, discarding a completed turn ===

Live-observed immediately after symptom 1 (2026-07-26 occurrence): once a Planner attempt actually completed successfully, the post-dispatch 'bd dolt push' failed on fleet-mac with a credentials error (missing git credentials for https://github.com -- 'could not read Username for https://github.com: Device not configured' -- fleet-mac needs provision_vcs_auth). This is a pure infra/credentials failure, unrelated to the Planner's LLM turn, which had already completed successfully and is committed in fleet-mac's LOCAL beads (Dolt) clone.

dispatchPlannerOnce() (runner.js:4886) = withGitSync(member, false, () => withDispatchWatchdog(...)) -- withGitSync (runner.js:3832) wraps pre-dispatch pull, the actual LLM turn, AND the post-dispatch D-push as ONE bracket. doltPushGuarded() (runner.js:1448-1527) throws a DoltSyncError (line 1487-1490) on push failure, which propagates out of the ENTIRE withGitSync call -- not just the push step. The PLANNER_DISPATCH_RETRY_DELAYS_MS loop (runner.js:4996) only sees 'the bracket threw' and calls dispatchPlannerOnce() again from scratch, redispatching a brand-new Planner LLM turn even though the prior turn's actual output already exists safely in fleet-mac's local beads clone -- purely because an unrelated push step failed. This compounds the symptom-1 risk via a second, independent path.

=== FIX DESIGN (supersedes the old (a)/(b) kill-or-reap framing -- both of those discarded completed work and ate a duplicate LLM turn; this recovers the work when it exists, and only kills when there is genuinely nothing to save) ===

PART A -- PID-liveness "lease of life" gate on the false-alarm path (fixes Symptom 1):
At execute-prompt.ts:889, before declaring empty_response, check isProcessAlive(capturedPid) via a fresh, cheap exec (`kill -0 <pid> 2>/dev/null && echo ALIVE || echo DEAD`, short timeout, independent of the dead channel).
- DEAD -> unchanged: declare empty_response exactly as today (genuine signal).
- ALIVE -> false alarm. Requires one companion change: the remote dispatch wrapper command must additionally tee the CLI's stdout to a durable per-invocation file on the remote host (e.g. `| tee .fleet-out-<inv>.json`), since the original SSH stream that would have carried it is gone. Then poll PID liveness (reusing the stall detector's existing poll loop rather than a bespoke one -- see Part C) until the process exits, read the durable file via a fresh exec, and feed it through the existing provider.parseResponse path as if it had arrived on the original channel. Only if the file is still empty/missing after the process genuinely exits does this fall through to a real empty_response.
- Bound the wait (remaining maxTotalMs, or a fixed generous ceiling). If the cap is hit while still alive, kill it (tryKillPid) and return a distinct, honestly-named terminal reason (e.g. reason: 'orphan_recovery_timeout') -- never mislabeled as empty_response.

PART B -- fix the stall detector's blind spot so it can catch a REAL stall (fixes Symptom 3):
- extractClaudeTimestamp (stall-poller.ts) must track the timestamp of the most recent line of ANY type, not only type==='assistant' -- every transcript entry (tool call, tool result, assistant) carries a timestamp field, and any new line being appended is legitimate evidence of forward progress.
- Widen the tail read (500 bytes is too thin -- a single large tool-result entry can blow past it with no parseable line in the window at all); use `tail -n N` or a larger byte count instead.
- With null reads becoming rare (true "file not created yet" cases only), the existing 120s threshold check will actually execute instead of being permanently bypassed.
- When a real stall IS confirmed (no activity of any kind for the threshold, process still alive per Part A's isProcessAlive), onStall() must actually call tryKillPid on the wedged process, not just clear bookkeeping -- otherwise a confirmed-hung process leaks forever regardless of detection.

PART C -- unify the two disconnected "is this dispatch done" signals:
Today execute_prompt trusts the SSH channel's close event as the sole verdict, while the stall detector's transcript polling runs in parallel purely as cosmetic telemetry that gets thrown away. Part A's recovery path and Part B's real-stall detection are the same underlying signal (PID liveness + transcript activity) doing two jobs. Implement them as one shared poller/decision path so "channel says done" is demoted to a hint that gets cross-checked, not blindly trusted.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===

1. Symptom 1 (false-alarm empty_response): re-running a fleet-sprint Plan dispatch and forcing (or waiting for a live recurrence of) a premature channel close while the remote process is still alive must NOT produce a duplicate concurrent dispatch. Verified by: ps on the member never shows two concurrent claude sessions for the same phase after an empty_response-shaped event; when the original process's real output exists, it is recovered and used (no LLM turn re-run); a unit/integration test simulating "channel resolves 0/empty while a live PID exists" exercises the lease-of-life path end to end (mocked isProcessAlive + mocked durable-output read).
2. Symptom 3 (real stalls now detectable): a unit test simulating a transcript whose tail never lands on an assistant-type line, but DOES have new tool_result/user-type lines appended, must NOT be misclassified as a stall (progress recognized via any entry type). A separate test simulating truly zero new lines of any type for > stallThresholdMs must result in stall_detected AND an actual kill of the tracked pid (mocked tryKillPid called).
3. Symptom 2 (D-push failure re-dispatch): unchanged from the original bead -- withGitSync (or its retry caller) must distinguish "dispatchFn itself failed" from "a completed dispatchFn's post-step (git/dolt sync) failed," and on the latter, retry only the sync step rather than looping back through PLANNER_DISPATCH_RETRY_DELAYS_MS to redispatch the LLM turn. Verified by forcing a D-push failure (e.g. missing VCS credentials) after a successful Planner turn and confirming the retry does not spawn a second Planner LLM dispatch for the same phase.
4. Full existing execute-prompt.ts, ssh.ts, and stall-detector.ts test suites continue to pass; no regression in the eft.28/eft.50.1/eft.74 interactive-route liveness-poll tests already covering the unrelated interactive dispatch path.
acceptance_criteria:

title: [engine] Multi-streak assignment per doer when doers < streaks: ordered worklist with warm-context carryover instead of one-streak-at-a-time feeding
description:
When the ready streak count exceeds the available doer count, the engine
today feeds each doer one streak per dispatch and pays the full fixed
overhead every time (sync brackets, prompt assembly, contract re-read,
cold repo re-exploration) while discarding the warm context exactly when
it is most valuable. Instead, assign each doer an ORDERED list of streaks
up front (order consistent with blocks edges; no cross-streak ordering
constraints exist by construction since lanes forbid cross-streak edges).

Two modes:
(i) BATCH: one dispatch carrying the ordered multi-streak worklist.
    Cheapest in overhead; loses per-streak engine checkpoints (sync,
    attribution boundary, review opportunity) until the batch ends.
(ii) RESUMED SEQUENCE (default): per-streak dispatches that resume the
    SAME doer session via explicit session id. Warm context carries
    across streaks; the engine keeps every checkpoint between streaks
    (git/dolt sync brackets, per-streak failure attribution, option to
    interleave review). Each subsequent dispatch is cheap because the
    session already holds the codebase context.

Rules:
- MODEL-TIER GROUPING (critical for quality AND cost): each streak
  already carries a required tier (max of its beads' models, per the
  planner-streaks formula). HARD RULE: a streak must NEVER execute on a
  tier below its requirement (quality collapses); and grouping must not
  silently upgrade cheap work to premium (cost waste). Therefore:
  - Prefer tier-homogeneous assignments: cheap streaks club with cheap,
    standard with standard, premium with premium.
  - Mode (i) BATCH is single-dispatch = single model, so it REQUIRES a
    tier-homogeneous worklist; a mixed batch is rejected at assignment
    time (never resolved by running everything at max tier -- if mixing
    is unavoidable, use mode (ii) or separate dispatches).
  - Mode (ii) RESUMED SEQUENCE may carry mixed tiers ONLY IF the
    provider supports changing model on resume (execute_prompt's model
    param already applies to resumed sessions for Claude) -- each
    streak's dispatch names that streak's own tier. Capability-checked
    per provider; where unsupported, fall back to tier-homogeneous
    grouping there too.
- TIER-OUTLIER ISOLATION (added 2026-07-30, operator-requested): partition
  the round's ready streaks by tier FIRST (cheap / standard / premium),
  BEFORE any priority/effort-budget packing runs, and pack each tier
  partition's worklist(s) independently. This matters most when one tier
  is a small minority against a much larger majority tier for the round
  (e.g. mostly standard-tier streaks with only one or two premium or
  cheap outliers) -- those minority-tier streaks must get their OWN
  dedicated worklist slot(s), never be folded into a majority-tier
  worklist just because effort-budget headroom would technically allow
  it. Rationale: any packing/model-selection step that (even implicitly)
  computes a worklist's effective tier as "max tier of everything
  assigned to this doer this round" would otherwise silently escalate
  cheap/standard work up to premium cost, or drag a standard task up to
  premium, purely because it happened to land in the same doer's batch as
  an unrelated outlier -- this is a real cost/quality-contamination risk,
  not just a homogeneity nicety. Partitioning by tier before packing is
  what makes the existing MODEL-TIER GROUPING hard rule (above) actually
  hold in practice once multi-streak-per-doer worklists exist -- without
  partition-first packing, tier-homogeneity could be accidentally violated
  by the packing algorithm itself even though each individual streak's own
  required tier was computed correctly. Applies to both modes: for BATCH,
  this is required (a mixed-tier batch is already rejected, per the rule
  above -- outlier isolation is what prevents the packer from ever trying
  to build one in the first place); for RESUMED SEQUENCE with a
  capability-checked provider, outlier streaks may still be resumed
  in-sequence with per-streak tier switching, but should still be ordered
  as their own contiguous run within the worklist rather than interleaved
  arbitrarily among the majority tier's streaks, for the same
  contamination-avoidance reasoning.
- PRIORITY-ORDERED WORKLIST (added 2026-07-30, operator-requested): the
  "no cross-streak ordering constraints" gap above is real and, until now,
  unresolved -- since lanes forbid cross-streak `blocks` edges by
  construction, nothing has ever told the engine which of a doer's several
  assigned streaks to run first. Priority is the answer: within a single
  doer's ordered worklist (and, per the tier-outlier rule above, WITHIN
  each tier partition independently), sort streaks by priority ascending
  (P0 first), where a streak's priority = the MINIMUM (i.e.
  highest-urgency) priority value among its member beads. `blocks`-edge
  order is the hard constraint and always wins where it exists (a streak
  that must run after another per a real dependency is never reordered
  ahead of it for priority reasons); priority is the ordering signal ONLY
  among streaks with no dependency relationship to each other -- which,
  per lane-formation rules, is the common case between different streaks.
  Only after priority also ties does the existing deterministic tie-break
  apply (lane `minOrder`, then `streakId`/title/id -- see
  `groupStreaksFromLaneMetadata`, runner.js). This is pure, deterministic
  sort logic -- no LLM judgment call needed, consistent with this
  feature's existing "no LLM decision" character. Rationale (operator,
  2026-07-30): currently a P3 streak can occupy a doer's time before an
  equally-ready P0 streak for no dependency reason at all, which is a
  direct token/time cost -- a doer must always prefer higher-priority
  ready work first whenever nothing blocks it from doing so.
- Total assigned load per doer respects the effort-point budget (reuse
  the planner-streaks formula); max_turns exhaustion continues to be
  handled by resume-with-increased-turns, not by shrinking assignments.
- Per-bead/per-streak failure attribution applies: a failure in streak N
  must not discard completed streaks 1..N-1 nor cancel N+1.. (they may
  re-dispatch fresh or resumed as headroom allows).
- Context headroom: before each resumed streak dispatch, apply the
  context-headroom admission check if available (context-headroom-
  admission-control bead seam); fall back to a fresh session (full
  prompt) when headroom is insufficient -- never a delta prompt into a
  fresh session (resume-by-session-id bead rule).
- Mode (i) stays config-gated for overhead-dominated scenarios.

Depends: blocked by the planner-owned-streaks bead (apra-fleet-eft.76 --
lane metadata + per-bead failure attribution are prerequisites); mode (ii)
additionally consumes the resume-by-session-id bead (apra-fleet-eft.78).
Note: POST-RELEASE performance enhancement.
acceptance_criteria:
- mock-sprint test: 4 streaks, 2 doers -> each doer gets an ordered
  2-streak assignment; dispatch log shows streak 2 dispatched as a
  resume of the doer's streak-1 session (mode ii), with sync brackets
  between them.
- mock-sprint test: streak 2 of 3 fails -> streak 1's closes stand,
  streak 3 still dispatched, only streak 2's open beads re-laned.
- unit: assignment respects the per-doer effort-point budget; overflow
  streaks queue to the next round rather than over-assigning.
- mode (i) behind config flag: one dispatch carries the ordered
  worklist; default remains mode (ii).
- unit: assignment groups tier-homogeneous streaks together; a
  cheap+premium pairing is never assigned to a mode (i) batch.
- mock-sprint test (mode ii, mixed tiers): a standard streak resumed
  after a cheap streak dispatches with model=standard on the SAME
  session id; the dispatch log shows per-streak model values, and no
  streak ever dispatches below its required tier.
- unit: provider without model-switch-on-resume -> mixed-tier
  assignment falls back to tier-homogeneous grouping (capability
  check asserted).
- unit (priority ordering, added 2026-07-30): a doer assigned 3
  independent (no blocks-edge relationship) streaks with priorities
  P2, P0, P1 is given a worklist in the order P0, P1, P2 -- streak
  priority is computed as the MINIMUM priority value across the
  streak's member beads.
- unit (priority never overrides a real dependency): if streak B has a
  genuine blocks-edge-derived ordering constraint requiring it after
  streak A, B is dispatched after A regardless of A/B's relative
  priority -- dependency order always wins over priority order.
- unit (priority tie-break): two streaks with equal (minimum) priority
  fall back to the existing deterministic tie-break (lane minOrder,
  then streakId/title/id) -- no new nondeterminism introduced.
- unit (tier-outlier isolation, added 2026-07-30): given a round with 8
  standard-tier ready streaks and 1 premium-tier and 1 cheap-tier
  streak, the packing algorithm produces the premium streak and the
  cheap streak each in their own dedicated worklist slot(s), never
  merged into a standard-tier doer's worklist even when effort budget
  would technically allow it.
- unit (tier-outlier isolation does not break mixed-tier resumed
  sequence when explicitly capability-gated): an outlier streak
  assigned to a provider with confirmed model-switch-on-resume support
  is still ordered as its own contiguous run within that doer's
  worklist, not interleaved arbitrarily among majority-tier streaks.

title: [integ] workflow launcher always resolves stdio, never attaches to a running HTTP fleet singleton by default -- apra-fleet workflow auto-sprint cannot run
description:
Feature: N/A (dist/cli/workflow.js launcher, core auto-sprint entry point exercised by integ-test-playbook.md Test scenario step 4)
Expected: per docs/adr-workflow-server-resolution.md and the launcher's own --help text, resolution order with no override set is 'probe HTTP singleton first, self-spawn stdio only as fallback'. With a healthy 'apra-fleet start' HTTP singleton already running (verified via 'node dist/index.js status' -> State: running, Port: 18700), 'node dist/index.js workflow auto-sprint --issue <id> --members <m> --branch <b> --base <base> --max-cycles 1 --dispatch-timeout-s 900' should attach to that singleton over HTTP and run the sprint.
Actual: it fails immediately with 'Error: No reachable apra-fleet HTTP singleton was found. cli.mjs no longer self-spawns a per-invocation stdio MCP server (Plan Part 2.1) -- resolution said: "APRA_FLEET_SERVER_CMD/APRA_FLEET_SERVER_BIN set (explicit stdio request)"'. Root cause: dist/cli/workflow.js's runWorkflow() pre-populates a COPY of the env (resolutionEnv.APRA_FLEET_SERVER_BIN = deps.serverBin) before calling deps.resolveConnection(resolutionEnv), solely so its OWN best-effort connection-probe call has a fallback value. But packages/apra-fleet-client/src/client/server-resolution.mjs's resolveFleetServerConnection() treats ANY truthy APRA_FLEET_SERVER_BIN as an 'explicit stdio request' (step 1 of its resolution order) and skips the HTTP probe (step 2) entirely -- so mode is ALWAYS 'stdio' regardless of whether a healthy HTTP singleton exists. applyEnvDefaults() then also writes that same APRA_FLEET_SERVER_BIN into the real env passed to the workflow passthrough process, so packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/cli.mjs's own resolveFleetServerConnection() call inherits the same poisoned env and also resolves 'stdio' -- but cli.mjs requires mode==='http' outright (Plan Part 2.1: no per-sprint stdio self-spawn), so it errors and exits 1. Net effect: 'apra-fleet workflow auto-sprint' can NEVER attach to a running HTTP singleton by default in dev/npm-installed mode (non-SEA) -- the exact single-machine CI-runner topology this playbook's smoke test and docs/tools-infrastructure.md's model both assume. Workaround found: explicitly exporting APRA_FLEET_TRANSPORT=http before the workflow command forces resolveFleetServerConnection() past the poisoned step-1 check straight to the step-2 HTTP probe, which then succeeds -- confirming the HTTP singleton itself is healthy and this is purely a launcher env-defaulting bug, not a server problem.
Test: integ-test-runner smoke test (playbook part 2), Test scenario step 4, 2026-07-21/22 cycle. Reproduced twice (once with a bare positional issue-id form that is itself also stale against the current CLI's --issue/--members/--branch/--base flag contract, and again with the corrected flag form from docs/authoring-workflows.md).
Repro: from a fresh 'node dist/index.js install && node dist/index.js start' with the server healthy on its default/scratch port, run (no APRA_FLEET_TRANSPORT/APRA_FLEET_SERVER_BIN/APRA_FLEET_SERVER_CMD set): 'node dist/index.js workflow auto-sprint --issue <id> --members <m> --branch <b> --base <base> --max-cycles 1' -- observe the stdio-request/no-HTTP-singleton error even though 'node dist/index.js status' shows the server running.
Fix direction: dist/cli/workflow.js's launcher-only best-effort resolveConnection probe (used solely to decide whether to default APRA_FLEET_SERVER_BIN for the CHILD workflow process) must not use a value that itself changes the outcome of the very resolution it is probing -- e.g. probe with the caller's real env unmodified first, and only fall back to defaulting APRA_FLEET_SERVER_BIN for the child process if that unmodified probe actually resolves to non-http.
notes: integ-test-runner (2026-07-22, SHA 1ce79a27c4b32b391b9682019fdc7bd006b7105e): CONFIRMED FIXED, closing. Live verification: fresh 'node dist/index.js workflow auto-sprint --issue gh-toy-4ef --members toy-doer --branch smoke-test-canary --base main --max-cycles 1 --dispatch-timeout-s 900' runs (clean env, no APRA_FLEET_SERVER_BIN/CMD/TRANSPORT set) logged '[workflow] fleet server: attached to HTTP singleton at http://127.0.0.1:18700/mcp (pid 28463)' immediately on launch, both in an initial run and a second full run that proceeded through Plan/Develop/Review/Deploy/Harvest. Auto-sprint child attach proven at live sprint launch, the remaining item flagged in the prior orchestrator note.

title: [bug][important] Parallel doer streak dispatch to a single member is unsafe -- causes hours-long hangs + response corruption; needs worktree-per-streak redesign
description:
Auto-sprint's Develop phase can assign multiple doer streaks to run "in
parallel" within one round (e.g. `Develop C1 R1` on 2026-07-15 assigned
streaks `[["apra-fleet-fih.2"],["apra-fleet-fih.3"]]`). Today this caused a
live sprint (`apra-fleet-fih`) to stall for over an hour with zero forward
progress: both streaks were dispatched concurrently to the SAME fleet
member (`fleet-reorg`), which is a single working-directory/checkout, not
an isolated session per dispatch.

## Constraint (confirmed by user, authoritative)

A member = one folder/checkout. It is NOT possible to safely run two
concurrent `execute_prompt` dispatches against the same member -- there is
no isolation between them (shared git checkout, shared session/process).

The only correct way to achieve genuine parallel doer work is: register
multiple members, each pointed at its own git worktree, dispatch one
streak per member/worktree, and after all streaks complete, merge the
worktree branches back with proper branch hygiene (clean up worktrees,
resolve/avoid conflicts, delete merged branches). This is real
infrastructure work (worktree lifecycle + member registration automation +
post-merge cleanup), not a one-line fix.

## What happened without this (observed failure mode)

Two concurrent dispatches against one shared-folder member produced:
- Repeated 900s inactivity timeouts on both streaks (contention for the
  same folder/session -- likely git index lock or transport-level
  single-invocation assumption).
- One dispatch's response came back with a corrupted multi-byte UTF-8
  sequence (`📋` emoji prefix decoded as U+FFFD replacement character),
  breaking JSON schema-repair parsing. Plausibly caused by output
  interleaving between the two concurrent invocations against a channel
  the transport assumes is single-occupancy per member.
- One streak (`fih.2`) left a real, syntactically-valid but unverified
  partial edit in the working tree when its dispatch died mid-response --
  recovered and committed as a WIP checkpoint
  (`34f2752` on `test/apra-fleet-se-speedup`) rather than lost.

## Immediate stopgap (do before the real fix, cheap and safe)

Until worktree-per-streak isolation exists, `runner.js`'s Develop-phase
streak dispatch must not fan out more than one streak concurrently against
a single member. Either serialize streak dispatch (one at a time, same
member) or hard-fail pre-sprint validation if the streak-assignment output
would produce >1 streak with only one member available/registered for the
scope. Silent concurrent dispatch against one folder must not be possible
-- it should fail loud, not hang for an hour.

## Real fix (needs its own planning pass, do not attempt inline)

1. Member-per-worktree provisioning: given a scope with N ready parallel
   streaks, auto-create N git worktrees (or reuse pre-registered
   worktree-backed members) before Develop phase dispatch.
2. Route each streak's doer dispatch to its own worktree-backed member.
3. Post-round merge/branch-hygiene step: after all streaks in a round
   complete (success or failure), merge each worktree's branch back into
   the sprint branch, handle conflicts (fail loud + surface to reviewer,
   do not auto-resolve), then remove the now-merged worktrees so they don't
   accumulate across rounds/sprints.
4. Decide member registration lifecycle: are worktree-backed members
   ephemeral (registered/deregistered per sprint) or a fixed pool reused
   across sprints? Affects `~/.apra-fleet/data/registry.json` growth and
   whether stale worktree directories need periodic GC.
5. Update `doer.md`/`planner.md` prose contracts if the scope/member
   assignment model changes as part of this (may intersect with the
   graph-consistency remediation plan's Phase B/C work already tracked
   separately).

Acceptance criteria for this backlog item once planned: a sprint that
assigns 2+ parallel doer streaks completes them in genuinely isolated
worktrees, merges cleanly with no manual intervention required in the
common case, and any merge conflict is surfaced as a loud, actionable
failure rather than silent data loss or an hour-long hang.
close_reason:
Resolved at every level this bead asked for, verified against current code (2026-07-29):

1. Stopgap ask (serialize dispatch per-member) -- DONE, and exceeded. runner.js
   (~line 6817) now uses `globalDoerTurn`, a single process-wide FIFO gate: at
   most one doer streak is ever in flight at a time, globally, regardless of
   member count or assignment -- strictly stronger than per-member locking.
   The comment there explicitly cites this bead by id as the known-bug context
   it closes: "a PER-MEMBER lock chain alone is not enough -- the token-passing
   stance requires doer streak dispatch to be GLOBALLY sequential across
   DIFFERENT members too... Same-member serialization is trivially still held
   (a global gate is strictly stronger)."
2. The legacy vendor/apra-pm/.claude/workflows/auto-sprint.js gap this bead's
   own comment flagged as a follow-up -- moot. vendor/ no longer exists in this
   repo (apra-pm was folded into packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm, no longer a
   submodule).
3. The stdout/UTF-8 chunk-decode corruption this bead's comment split off --
   apra-fleet-grq, already closed (fixed by commit 6478f67).
4. The "real fix" (worktree-per-streak genuine parallelism) -- runner.js's own
   comment already states "true parallel/merger dispatch is explicitly
   deferred to Phase 3+", matching current operator priority: get single-doer
   sprint reliability solid first, then revisit genuine multi-doer parallelism
   only if warm-context sequential packing (apra-fleet-eft.79) proves
   insufficient. Not deleting the idea, just no longer tracking it as an open
   P0 bug blocking other work.

Closing unblocks apra-fleet-eft.79 (multi-streak-per-doer warm-context
packing), which is the higher-value, lower-risk, deterministic direction the
operator wants to pursue now.

comments.text:
CORRECTION after root-cause investigation (2026-07-15, two independent read-only
agents + manual verification):

The originally-suspected mechanism ("both streaks dispatched concurrently to
the same member with zero serialization, causing a fast-fail collision") is
only half right and needs a precise correction:

1. `packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js` (the code path actually
   executed by `node packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/cli.mjs`, confirmed via
   `bin/cli.mjs:18`'s direct import from `../auto-sprint/runner.js`) ALREADY
   has same-member serialization: a `memberLocks` Map added in commit
   `51df121` (2026-07-13), verified present and structurally sound at
   `runner.js:1931-2038` (acquire/release wrapped in try/finally, covers the
   throw path). So concurrent streaks to one member queue rather than
   collide-and-fast-fail in this code path.
2. A SEPARATE, real gap exists in `vendor/apra-pm/.claude/workflows/auto-sprint.js`
   (the file installed/used by the `auto-sprint` Claude Code SKILL, distinct
   from the dev-CLI path above) -- confirmed zero matches for `memberLocks`,
   `member_name`, or `doerMember` in that file's parallel-doer block
   (~lines 2050-2166). If that installed-skill path is ever used for a
   single-member sprint, it WILL hit the original fast-fail collision bug
   that `51df121` already fixed in `runner.js` but never backported here.
   Tracked as follow-up: port `runner.js`'s `memberLocks` pattern into
   `vendor/apra-pm/.claude/workflows/auto-sprint.js`'s parallel-doer
   dispatch, or ensure the two implementations converge into one.
3. Given (1), the actual apra-fleet-fih hang's repeated 900s timeouts are
   NOT explained by a fast-fail collision (memberLocks would have queued
   them, and a collision fails near-instantly, not after 15 minutes each).
   The recurring timeouts remain a separate, not-fully-explained reliability
   issue -- possibly a genuine CLI/dispatch hang, possibly related to
   apra-fleet-grq's stdout decode bug (a hang while reading/processing a
   response corrupted mid-stream is plausible but unconfirmed).

This bead's core architectural point stands regardless: even with
memberLocks preventing collisions, "parallel" streaks against one member are
serialized in practice (defeats the purpose of parallel dispatch) -- the

title: Windows CI: supervisor-stop-restart-integration.test.mjs file-level FAIL with no error/stack, unreproducible locally
description:
## Symptom

CI run https://github.com/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet/actions/runs/32165203586/job/95803070721
(build-and-test windows-latest, PR #422, commit 9ae5a567) failed the whole
`packages/apra-fleet-se/test/supervisor-stop-restart-integration.test.mjs`
file. Only subtests (1) and (2) reported PASS; the FAIL is emitted at the
file level with no attached error/stack (the custom
`test/helpers/timestamped-reporter.mjs` only prints `details.error` when
node:test supplies one -- here it did not):

```
[...] PASS ... :: (1) Stop: force-release kills the real child AND releases the reservation ... (176.4ms)
[...] PASS ... :: (2) Stop error surfacing: force-release on an unknown sprintId 404s ... (2.8ms)
[...] FAIL ... :: test\supervisor-stop-restart-integration.test.mjs (997.6ms)
test failed
```

Subtests (3) (Restart) and (4) (Restart error surfacing) never even printed
a PASS/FAIL line -- the whole per-file `node --test` child process appears
to have exited (crashed/killed) partway through (3), with no JS-level
exception surfacing through the reporter. No stack trace anywhere in the
full raw job log (`gh api repos/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet/actions/jobs/95803070721/logs`);
no STDERR lines for this file either.

## Why this is NOT caused by PR #422

PR #422 (`fix/opencode-agy-unattended-auto-mode`) only touches
`src/os/windows.ts`, `src/providers/*.ts`, and `tests/windows-pid-wrap.test.ts`
-- none of which touch `packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/*` or this test.
ubuntu-latest and macos-latest passed on the identical commit.

## Repro attempts (all negative)

- Ran the file in isolation on a real Windows 11 machine: passes
  (`node --test ... test/supervisor-stop-restart-integration.test.mjs`), all
  4 subtests PASS, ~1.5s total.
- Ran the full apra-fleet-se suite with the exact CI invocation
  (`node --test --test-reporter=./test/helpers/timestamped-reporter.mjs
  --test-reporter-destination=stdout --test-concurrency=8 test/*.test.mjs`)
  three consecutive times: `SUMMARY pass=2239 fail=0` every time, no flake.
- Checked the 3 most recent `main`-branch CI failures on windows-latest
  (runs 32063805632, 31971079518, 31915909187): none reproduce this
  signature -- they fail for unrelated reasons (a `bd bootstrap` dolt-clone
  race leaving a locked `.dolt/noms/LOCK` file, and unrelated vitest
  integration test failures in `tests/2cc-win-bd-invocation-integ.test.ts` /
  `tests/check-sandbox-sync-remote.test.ts`). No existing bead or PR history
  references this exact test file failing.

## Suspected root cause (unconfirmed -- needs a flaky-prone CI capture)

`supervisor-stop-restart-integration.test.mjs` spawns REAL detached child
OS processes (via `src/supervisor/spawner.mjs`'s `createSpawner()`,
`detached: true`, real log-file fds for stdio, real TCP port allocation)
and kills them with `process.kill(pid, 'SIGKILL')`
(`src/supervisor/reconcile.mjs`'s `killPid`/`isPidAlive`). The whole
apra-fleet-se suite runs with `--test-concurrency=8` (many files each
spawning further child processes) on a windows-2022 GitHub Actions runner
with only 2 vCPUs -- a far more resource-constrained environment than a
dev machine. The complete absence of a JS-level error (rather than a
timeout or assertion failure with a message) is consistent with the
per-file `node --test` child process being killed/crashing outside any
try/catch (e.g. handle/process exhaustion under heavy concurrent
process-spawn load), not a logic bug reachable through normal test
execution.

## Suggested next step

If this recurs, capture the full raw Windows job log immediately (do not
rely on the check-run summary) and look specifically for `EMFILE`,
`ENOSPC`, or a runner-level OOM/timeout signal around the failing job's
step. Consider whether `--test-concurrency=8` should be lower on Windows
CI specifically, given the 2-vCPU windows-2022 runner vs. this suite's
heavy real-child-process integration tests.

title: Close or hand off all-children-closed features when Integration Test phase is skipped
description:
Feature-rollup beads are only closed by the Integration Test phase (runner.js ~2603/2756). When a target repo has no integ-test-playbook.md, that phase is silently skipped every cycle, and any feature whose children are all closed strands open indefinitely -- feeding a FAIL verdict that then never surfaces (see the FAIL-propagation bead).

Observed in the ait-gbo v0.4.0 sprint: 3+ all-children-closed features stranded open because AiTicket-PM had no integ-test-playbook.md. See field-report-ait-gbo-analysis.md section P2-6.

Surfaced by the ait-gbo v0.4.0 field report: the sprint deposited its sharpest findings as open beads/notes and reported success, so nobody was told triage was owed. See field-report-ait-gbo-analysis.md sections P0-1, X2, recommendation 2.

title: Match compose_permissions bounds entries as prefix patterns, not exact strings
description: Follow-up hardening for the reopened apra-fleet-ivxi.1.3, in case the reopen is fixed narrowly. src/tools/compose-permissions.ts line 458 uses `bounds.includes(p)`, exact string equality, against bounds files whose entries are glob-shaped prefix patterns (`Bash(npm run build*)`, `Bash(mkdir *)`, `Bash(*apra-fleet* run *)`). Introduce a shared matcher that treats `*` as a wildcard and reuse it for the bounds check, then add regression tests for: a grant covered by a trailing-wildcard entry (`Bash(npm run build)` vs `Bash(npm run build*)`), a grant covered by a mid-string wildcard (`Bash(*apra-fleet* run *)`), a genuinely out-of-bounds grant that must still be flagged, and a CO_OCCURRENCE-expanded permission the caller never explicitly requested. Note that the existing test at tests/compose-permissions-bounds-grant.test.ts:76 deliberately picks the one wildcard-free bounds entry and so cannot catch this class of bug.
close_reason: Implemented wildcard bounds matcher and added regression tests for trailing-wildcard, mid-string-wildcard, out-of-bounds, and CO_OCCURRENCE-expanded cases

title: [test] member_home_probe regression: encoded Windows probe under a PowerShell default shell
description:
Files: tests/member-home-warm.test.ts (vitest, run via npm test).

Behaviour: update the exec mock so it base64-decodes the EncodedCommand payload and asserts on the decoded script, instead of substring-matching the old raw command text.

Cases to assert:
1. Windows member: the issued command is an encoded PowerShell invocation whose decoded script reads USERPROFILE; the probe returns the mocked absolute Windows path and caches it.
2. Regression guard: the issued command string itself contains no bare dollar-env reference that an outer PowerShell shell could expand (this is the exact live failure - an unquoted expanded path caused Missing right-parenthesis / Unexpected token errors for fleet-win11 and fleet-win-dev1).
3. POSIX member: command and behaviour unchanged.
4. A non-zero exit or non-absolute output still yields a null result plus the member_home_probe warning, as today.

title: Windows home-directory probe survives a member whose default shell is PowerShell
description:
Deliverable: member_home_probe resolves USERPROFILE on Windows members even when the outer exec shell is itself PowerShell, by encoding the probe instead of relying on shell-level variable expansion in a member-bound command string.

Users: stall detection and session-log path resolution for every Windows fleet member (observed failing live for fleet-win11 and fleet-win-dev1).

Acceptance criteria:
- The Windows probe is built through the existing base64 EncodedCommand helper in src/os/windows.ts, so no intermediate shell can re-tokenize it.
- A Windows member with a PowerShell default exec shell returns a valid absolute home path with no parser error in stderr and no member_home_probe warning.
- The POSIX probe path is unchanged.
- tests/member-home-warm.test.ts asserts the encoded payload by decoding it, not by substring-matching raw command text, and covers the PowerShell-default-shell regression.

Explicitly OUT of scope (do not chase): fleet-win-deploy's separate SSH failure (All configured authentication methods failed) seen in the same log burst - that is a credential problem, not this parsing bug, and needs its own bead.
