Child beads 69pp.1.1/69pp.1.2 remain open as bead-state lag but the deliverable is committed and verifiably complete.

title: member_home_probe: Windows probe uses unsafe inline powershell -c string, breaks under PowerShell-default SSH shell
description:
src/services/member-home.ts:53-57 (probeCommandFor) built the Windows USERPROFILE probe as a raw inline string:

  powershell -NoProfile -c "[Console]::Out.Write($env:USERPROFILE)"

This assumes the outer shell that runs this command line leaves `$env:USERPROFILE` untouched inside the double quotes so the inner `powershell -c` can expand it itself. On members whose default exec shell is ALSO PowerShell, the outer shell expands `$env:USERPROFILE` during its own tokenization before the inner powershell -c invocation ever sees it, producing the unquoted literal:

  [Console]::Out.Write(C:\Users\akhil)

...which is a PowerShell syntax error (bare path token, not a string). Observed live in production logs for fleet-win11 and fleet-win-dev1 at fleet startup:

  [fleet:warn] member_home_probe home dir probe failed for fleet-win11: code=1 stderr=... Missing ')' in method call ... Unexpected token 'C:\Users\akhil' ...
  [fleet:warn] member_home_probe home dir probe failed for fleet-win-dev1: code=1 stderr=... (same)

Same defect class as apra-fleet-ot2z (relying on shell-level variable expansion in a member-bound command string instead of resolving/encoding it defensively -- see CLAUDE.md's General Principles / regression tests ot2z.2, .5, .7, .9).

FIX APPLIED (branch worktree-fix-member-home-probe-quoting): probeCommandFor now builds the Windows probe via wrapPowerShellEncoded() (src/os/windows.ts), the same base64 -EncodedCommand helper every other Windows-targeting PowerShell invocation in this codebase already uses to avoid re-tokenization by an intermediate shell. Updated tests/member-home-warm.test.ts's mock to decode the -EncodedCommand payload instead of substring-matching the old raw command text. tests/member-home-warm.test.ts (10/10) passes; full suite run pending.

Separately observed in the same log burst (NOT part of this bug, do not conflate): fleet-win-deploy logged "home dir probe errored ... All configured authentication methods failed" -- an SSH auth/credential failure on that specific member, unrelated to the parsing bug above. Needs its own investigation (stale/expired SSH key?) -- not fixed here.
notes: Fix pushed as PR #413 (branch worktree-fix-member-home-probe-quoting): member-home.ts now uses wrapPowerShellEncoded for the Windows probe. 63/63 relevant tests pass. fleet-win-deploy's separate SSH auth failure noted in the description is NOT fixed here -- still needs investigation.
close_reason: integ-test-runner verify-set: ran 'npx vitest run tests/member-home-warm.test.ts' on branch fleet-sprint/ivxi-u1qw-69pp (HEAD 24254da7); confirmed src/services/member-home.ts probeCommandFor uses wrapPowerShellEncoded (no raw $env inline string). 10/10 tests passed, including SF-18 regression guard asserting -EncodedCommand wrapping and no bare $env token. Fix from PR #413 verified present in deployed working tree; defect no longer reproduces.

title: Research: do AGY and OpenCode support project-scoped permission config files at all?
description:
Sub-task of apra-fleet-quv3 (compose_permissions writes to SSH default dir instead of member workFolder on remote members).

Before fixing deliverConfigFile to cd into agent.workFolder for remote members, confirm the premise holds for AGY and OpenCode specifically: do these CLIs actually support a project-local/per-repo permission config file the way Claude Code does (.claude/settings.local.json) and Codex does (.codex/config.toml is user-level though -- verify), or do they only read a single user-level config regardless of cwd?

Currently:
- OpenCode: provider.permissionConfigPaths() returns ['.opencode/settings.json'] (src/providers/opencode.ts) -- relative path, implying project scope is assumed.
- AGY: provider.permissionConfigPaths() returns ['.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json'] (src/providers/agy.ts) -- relative path, implying project scope is assumed.

If either CLI does NOT actually support project-scoped permission files (i.e. it only ever reads a fixed user-level path regardless of cwd), then the "fix" of cd-ing into workFolder before writing would be pointless for that provider -- the real fix would be different (e.g. documenting that grants are inherently user-level for that provider, or finding whatever project-override mechanism it does support, if any).

Deliverable: for each of AGY and OpenCode, state definitively (with doc/source evidence, not assumption) whether a project-scoped permission config path exists, and if so what the correct relative (or absolute-per-project) path and merge semantics are. This determines whether apra-fleet-quv3's fix is a straightforward cd-before-write, or requires per-provider special-casing.

title: compose_permissions writes to SSH default dir instead of member workFolder on remote members
description:
compose_permissions's deliverConfigFile (src/tools/compose-permissions.ts) writes provider permission config files using paths returned by provider.permissionConfigPaths(), which are relative (e.g. Claude: '.claude/settings.local.json'; OpenCode: '.opencode/settings.json'; AGY: '.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json'; Codex: '.codex/config.toml'; Gemini: '.gemini/settings.json' + '.gemini/policies/fleet.toml'; Copilot: '.github/copilot/settings.local.json').

LocalStrategy.execCommand (src/services/strategy.ts:72-77) spawns with cwd: agent.workFolder, so on a LOCAL member the relative path correctly resolves under the registered project folder.

RemoteStrategy.execCommand (src/services/strategy.ts:32-34) delegates to sshExecCommand (src/services/ssh.ts:149-201), which calls client.exec(command, ...) directly over the SSH channel with NO cd/Set-Location into agent.workFolder anywhere in that path. So on a REMOTE (SSH) member, the same relative path resolves wherever the SSH server's default starting directory is -- for Windows OpenSSH that is the user's home profile (%USERPROFILE%), not the member's registered workFolder.

Confirmed live: granting deploy.md permissions to fleet-win-deploy (remote, workFolder C:\akhil\git\apra-fleet-deploy) via compose_permissions landed the permissions ledger at %USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.local.json on the remote host instead of C:\akhil\git\apra-fleet-deploy\.claude\settings.local.json. The equivalent grant to fleet-dev (local, same workFolder pattern) correctly landed at <workFolder>\.claude\settings.local.json.

Impact: for every remote member, compose_permissions silently escalates permissions/config scope from the intended project folder to the member's entire user-level Claude/OpenCode/AGY config -- affecting every project that member ever works in via that home-level config, not just the target project. This is a scope-escalation bug, not just a wrong-path bug.

Fix direction: deliverConfigFile (and detectStacks, which has the same class of relative-path assumption) must anchor all remote commands to agent.workFolder explicitly (cd/Set-Location before mkdir/write/read-back), matching what LocalStrategy gets for free via spawn cwd. Do not rely on the SSH session's default directory.

Also must revisit as part of this bead: verify how the same relative-path delivery mechanism behaves for OpenCode (.opencode/settings.json, src/providers/opencode.ts) and AGY (.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json, src/providers/agy.ts) providers specifically on remote members -- confirm whether they have the same home-dir leak and fix in the same pass, not as a separate follow-up.

title: Decision: extend runner.js for multi-repo, or build a second runner? (recommend: extend + strangler-fig extraction, revisit at Stage 2)
description:
QUESTION (operator, 2026-08-15): should multi-repo support be built by extending the existing
fleet-sprint engine (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js, ~10k lines, monolithic), or by
starting a clean second runner that learns from it?

This decision governs every other child of this epic, so it should be settled before
apra-fleet-74vu.1 starts. Recorded here with the analysis so the reasoning is not lost.
design:
ANALYSIS.

What a rewrite would throw away -- these are the hardened, edge-case-laden invariants the current
runner has accumulated, all of which multi-repo REUSES rather than replaces:
  - git/beads sync brackets and the fast-forward-by-construction invariant (runner.js:7241-7325)
  - dolt push reconcile (dolt-sync.mjs:109-115), deterministic settle (dolt-settle.mjs:1-56), and the
    supervisor-owned dolt_push_mutex
  - the Ensure Sprint Branch safety ladder: adopt-existing-remote-branch, ahead/behind/diverged probes,
    named-stash auto-stash of orphaned WIP (runner.js:5789-5857)
  - worklist packing with tier partitioning and effort budgets (runner.js:3441-3560)
  - the self-heal retry shapes (max-turns resume, trust heal, permissions heal per apra-fleet-u1qw)
  - budget estimation per dispatch (runner.js:7297-7325), viewer state, supervisor reservation
These are the bugs that do not show up in a demo and do show up at hour five of a real sprint. A new
runner restarts that discovery clock at zero.

What the Stage 1 changes actually are, mechanically: substitutions of a scalar for a per-repo lookup.
base scalar -> manifest lookup; global roleMap -> per-repo roleMap with global fallback; globalDoerTurn
-> Map<repoId, chain>; one topology rule -> the same rule per repo group; one PR -> a loop over repos.
None of that is a new execution model. Single-repo is literally the one-entry-manifest case, which is
why every child bead can carry a "single-repo behavior is unchanged" acceptance criterion.

Cost of a second runner: two engines that must both keep working, every fix landing twice or silently
diverging, two sets of playbooks/docs/tests, and a product that has to explain which engine a customer
is on. fleet-sprint is a general product, not an internal script -- forking it doubles the maintenance
surface permanently to buy a one-time cleanliness win.

The real complaint (a 10k-line file is hard to change safely) is a MODULARITY problem, not a multi-repo
problem. Conflating the two means paying for a rewrite and still not knowing whether the new
decomposition is right.

RECOMMENDATION: extend, but pay the modularity tax deliberately as you go -- strangler-fig, not
big-bang. Concretely, each Stage 0/1 bead extracts the seam it touches into its own module with the
runner left as a thin orchestration shell:
  - manifest.mjs (apra-fleet-74vu.1) -- already scoped this way
  - topology.mjs (apra-fleet-74vu.4, from checkMemberTopology runner.js:427-604)
  - branch-ensure.mjs (apra-fleet-74vu.5, from runner.js:5761-5857)
  - assignment.mjs (apra-fleet-74vu.6, streaks + worklists, runner.js:2990-3560)
  - dispatch-gate.mjs (apra-fleet-74vu.7, replacing globalDoerTurn runner.js:7160-7168)
  - publish.mjs (apra-fleet-74vu.10, from runner.js:9204-9283)
Each extraction is covered by the tests that bead already requires, so the refactor is verified by work
you are doing anyway, and runner.js shrinks by exactly the parts multi-repo made complicated.

REVISIT POINT: Stage 2 (apra-fleet-74vu.11) is the genuine architectural break, because it replaces the
single global cycle with concurrent per-repo develop loops -- the global cycle is the runner's central
control-flow assumption. If, after Stage 1 ships, the extracted modules have made the phase pipeline
tractable, Stage 2 is an evolution; if the pipeline is still the bottleneck, THAT is the moment to
consider a new execution core, built on the modules Stage 0/1 already extracted rather than from
scratch.
acceptance_criteria:
- The operator records ACCEPT or REJECT of the recommendation in this bead's notes, with a date.
- If ACCEPTED: each Stage 0/1 bead's design is confirmed to name the module it extracts (the list in
  DESIGN), and no second runner entry point is created anywhere in packages/apra-fleet-se/.
- If REJECTED: this bead is replaced by a scoping bead for the second runner covering, at minimum, how
  the hardened invariants listed in DESIGN are carried over or re-earned, how the two engines are kept
  from diverging, and which engine a customer is routed to.
- The decision is made before apra-fleet-74vu.1 is claimed.

title: Stage 1: per-repo doer turn gates (replace globalDoerTurn) and per-repo doer-side branch pushes
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained).
Today EVERY doer streak turn in fleet-sprint is strictly serialized through a single global promise
chain, globalDoerTurn (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:7160-7168): at most one doer
dispatch is ever in flight for the whole sprint. The stated reason is that concurrent writers would
break the fast-forward-by-construction invariant that the git/beads sync brackets depend on. That
reason is real -- but it is PER BRANCH PER REPO. Two doers working in two DIFFERENT repositories touch
completely disjoint git state, so serializing them buys nothing and costs the entire wall-clock benefit
of multi-repo sprints.

The correct generalization (design doc section 4, "Planning and streaks") is a PER-REPO turn gate: a
Map<repoId, promiseChain>. Serialize within a repo exactly as today; parallelize across repos. Dolt
(beads) writes stay globally serialized through the existing supervisor-owned dolt_push_mutex -- that
is orthogonal machinery that already exists and must NOT be touched.

Second piece of this bead: the sprint's final push currently happens from the orchestrator's own
checkout (runner.js:9231-9239). With N repos the orchestrator must hold zero checkouts, so the push
moves doer-side. This is nearly free: the doer bracket already G-pushes after every streak
(runner.js:7241-7257), so each repo's branch tip is already on its origin.
design:
1) Replace globalDoerTurn (runner.js:7160-7168) with a per-repo gate: a Map<repoId, Promise> where each
   dispatch chains onto the promise for ITS repoId only. Resolve the repoId from the dispatched doer via
   the memberName -> repoId index (from the manifest-driven repo/member resolution bead). Keep the
   existing chaining/error-propagation shape so a rejected turn does not poison other repos' chains --
   a failure in repo A's chain must not block repo B.
2) Preserve the ff-only invariant WITHIN a repo: the sync bracket ordering around each turn is
   unchanged, just scoped per repo. Do not weaken or reorder the git sync brackets.
3) Do NOT change dolt/beads serialization. Beads writes continue to go through the supervisor-owned
   dolt_push_mutex globally, and dolt-sync.mjs / dolt-settle.mjs are untouched by this bead. Two doers
   in different repos may run concurrently in git terms while still queueing behind each other for the
   dolt push -- that is the intended design.
4) Concurrency bound: add an explicit cap on how many repos may have an in-flight doer dispatch at once
   (default: unbounded across repos, but make it a named constant/arg so an operator can throttle
   provider rate limits). Log when a dispatch waits on its repo's gate vs. runs immediately.
5) Move the final push: replace the orchestrator-side push (runner.js:9231-9239) with reliance on each
   repo's doer-side push in the doer bracket (runner.js:7241-7257), plus a per-repo verification step
   that the remote branch tip equals the local tip before PR publication. If a repo's tip is not on the
   remote, dispatch a push on that repo's doer member -- never from the orchestrator.
6) Budget/observability: per-repo spend attribution falls out of per-repo dispatch since the budget
   estimator already prices per dispatch (runner.js:7297-7325); make sure each dispatch's cost record
   carries its repoId, and add a repo lane to the viewer's phase rows.
7) Single-repo compatibility: with a one-entry manifest the Map has one key and behavior is identical
   to today's global chain.
acceptance_criteria:
- globalDoerTurn is gone; a Map<repoId, Promise> gate replaces it, keyed via the memberName -> repoId
  index.
- A mock-sprint test with two repos and one doer each observes the two doer dispatches OVERLAPPING in
  time (both in flight simultaneously); a test with two doers in the SAME repo observes them strictly
  sequential (second starts only after the first completes).
- A doer turn that throws in repo A does not prevent repo B's next turn from running, and A's own chain
  recovers or fails per today's semantics -- covered by a test.
- dolt-sync.mjs, dolt-settle.mjs and the dolt_push_mutex usage are unchanged by this bead (diff review),
  and a test asserts concurrent cross-repo doers still serialize their beads pushes through the mutex.
- A named constant/arg caps concurrent in-flight repos; setting it to 1 reproduces today's fully
  serialized behavior end-to-end.
- Each dispatch's cost/budget record carries its repoId, and the viewer shows a per-repo lane.
- The orchestrator performs no git push in its own working directory: after Develop, each repo's remote
  branch tip equals its local tip, and when a tip is missing from the remote a push is dispatched on
  that repo's doer member -- both asserted by tests.
- Single-repo sprints keep today's serialized behavior; existing doer-serialization tests pass
  unmodified.

title: Stage 1: per-repo roleMaps, repo-pure streaks, and per-repo doer worklist packing
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained).
fleet-sprint groups sprint beads into "streaks" -- sets of beads that must be worked sequentially by
the same doer -- via planner lane metadata (groupStreaksFromLaneMetadata,
packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:3093) with an LLM fallback
(buildStreakAssignmentPrompt, runner.js:2990-3006), validates them in selectStreaks
(runner.js:3026-3063), and packs streaks onto doers with tier partitioning and effort budgets in
assignDoerWorklists (runner.js:3441-3560). Role-to-member mapping is a single global roleMap
(runner.js:2512-2534).

In a multi-repo sprint each repository has its OWN members (one member per repo checkout), so work
must be assigned within a repo, never across. The workspace manifest (Stage 0 sibling bead) carries
per-repo member lists at manifest.repos[repoId].members, and every task bead carries a `repo` metadata
field (the other Stage 0 sibling bead). This bead joins those two facts to the assignment machinery.

The key new invariant: A STREAK NEVER SPANS REPOS. Without it, a single streak could be handed to a
doer whose checkout does not even contain the code the bead refers to.
design:
1) Per-repo roleMaps. Generalize the global roleMap (runner.js:2512-2534) to a per-repo roleMap
   resolved from manifest.repos[repoId].members, with the workspace-level/global map as FALLBACK for
   any role a repo does not define. Expose resolveRole(repoId, role) and route every existing roleMap
   consumer through it.
2) Repo-pure streaks. In selectStreaks validation (runner.js:3026-3063), alongside the existing
   unknown-id and duplicate checks, add: every bead in a streak must carry the same `repo` metadata
   value; a mixed-repo streak is rejected with an error naming the streak and the conflicting repoIds.
   Apply the check to BOTH streak sources -- lane-metadata grouping (runner.js:3093) and the LLM
   fallback -- so a hallucinated cross-repo streak cannot slip through.
3) Streak prompt. Add to buildStreakAssignmentPrompt (runner.js:2990-3006) an explicit instruction that
   streaks must not mix repos, and include each candidate bead's repo value in the rendered bead list
   so the model can obey it.
4) Per-repo packing. In assignDoerWorklists (runner.js:3441-3560), partition streaks by repoId first,
   then run today's existing tier-partition + effort-budget packing WITHIN each repo against that
   repo's doer pool from resolveRole(repoId, 'doer'). Do not change the packing algorithm itself --
   only its input partitioning and the candidate doer pool.
5) Failure modes: a repoId with streaks but no doers in its roleMap (and none in the global fallback)
   is a hard failure at assignment time naming the repoId; a doer that appears in two repos' pools is
   already prevented by manifest validation (one member, one repo) but assert it here too.
6) Single-repo compatibility: with the one-entry manifest all beads carry repo="default", partitioning
   yields one partition, and packing is byte-identical to today.
acceptance_criteria:
- resolveRole(repoId, role) returns the repo's member list when defined and the global roleMap's list
  when the repo omits that role -- both cases tested.
- selectStreaks rejects a streak whose beads carry two different repo values, with an error naming the
  streak and both repoIds; the rejection is tested for BOTH the lane-metadata path and the LLM-fallback
  path.
- The streak assignment prompt contains the "a streak must not span repositories" instruction and each
  candidate bead's repo value -- asserted by a prompt snapshot test.
- assignDoerWorklists on a 2-repo scope assigns every backend streak only to backend doers and every
  frontend streak only to frontend doers; no worklist contains a bead whose repo differs from its
  assigned doer's repo.
- Tier partitioning and effort budgeting produce the same packing decisions within a single repo as
  they do today -- proven by an existing packing test re-run with a one-entry manifest, unmodified.
- A manifest repo that has streaks but no doer in its per-repo roleMap and none in the global fallback
  fails at assignment with an error naming that repoId.
- Existing single-repo streak and worklist tests pass unmodified.

title: Stage 1: per-repo base branches in Ensure Sprint Branch (one branch name, N divergent bases)
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained).
The Ensure Sprint Branch phase (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:5761-5857) runs
`git fetch origin <base>` + `git checkout -B <branch>` on every member in the ensure set using the
SAME validated.baseBranch, because today a sprint has exactly one --base. In a multi-repo sprint the
repos legitimately have different bases -- e.g. backend cuts from `main` while frontend cuts from
`release/2.4`.

The adopted model is Google repo/AOSP semantics: ONE sprint branch NAME (sprint/<topic>) created in
EVERY repo, each cut from ITS OWN manifest-pinned base. The workspace manifest (Stage 0 sibling bead)
supplies manifest.repos[repoId].base. Every PR later targets its own repo's base.

Crucially this is a PARAMETERIZATION, not a rewrite: the existing branch-ensure safety ladder
(adopt-an-existing-remote-branch, ahead/behind/diverged probes, the auto-stash of orphaned WIP at
runner.js:5789-5857) is hardened and stays exactly as it is. Only the value of the base changes, from
one global scalar to a per-repo lookup.
design:
1) In the Ensure Sprint Branch loop (runner.js:5761-5857), which already dispatches per member
   (runner.js:5771-5787), replace the single `validated.baseBranch` with
   manifest.repos[repoOf(member)].base, using the repoId index built by the manifest-driven
   repo/member resolution bead. The branch NAME stays global and identical across repos.
2) Change nothing else in the phase: keep the adopt-existing-remote-branch path, the
   ahead/behind/diverged probes, the auto-stash of orphaned WIP into a named stash, and every existing
   error message. These are hardened behaviors; a regression here is worse than the feature.
3) Base resolution must be per repo everywhere in the phase: the `git fetch origin <base>` must fetch
   that repo's base, and any comparison of the branch against "the base" must compare against that
   repo's base -- grep the phase for baseBranch and confirm no residual global use remains.
4) Record, per repo, the base and the base SHA actually used into the sprint's lockfile/run state
   (the lockfile structure is delivered by the Stage 0 manifest bead). If a repo's resolved base SHA
   differs from the SHA snapshotted in the lockfile at sprint start (i.e. the base moved mid-sprint),
   log a warning naming the repo, both SHAs, and keep the lockfile's original value as the recorded
   "built against" answer.
5) Single-repo compatibility: with the one-entry synthesized manifest, base lookup returns exactly
   today's validated.baseBranch, so single-repo sprints are byte-identical.
6) The --base CLI flag remains supported for single-repo sprints and is ignored (with the explicit log
   line from the Stage 0 manifest bead) when a manifest is supplied.
acceptance_criteria:
- In a 2-repo manifest sprint with backend.base=main and frontend.base=release/2.4, Ensure Sprint
  Branch fetches origin/main on the backend member and origin/release/2.4 on the frontend member, and
  creates the SAME branch name in both -- asserted by a mock-sprint test on the dispatched commands.
- No occurrence of a single global base remains inside runner.js:5761-5857 (grep-level check in the
  test or review notes).
- The existing branch-ensure safety behaviors are preserved and covered by their original tests,
  unmodified: adopting an existing remote branch, ahead/behind/diverged detection, and the named-stash
  auto-stash of orphaned WIP.
- The run state records, per repoId, { base, sha } as actually used by the phase.
- When a repo's base SHA at ensure time differs from the sprint-start lockfile SHA, a warning is
  logged naming the repoId and both SHAs, and the lockfile keeps the original SHA -- covered by a test
  that moves the base between snapshot and ensure.
- A single-repo sprint (no --manifest) produces the identical fetch/checkout command sequence it does
  today; existing Ensure Sprint Branch tests pass unmodified.

title: Stage 1: manifest-driven repo/member resolution and per-repo topology validation (replace the divergent-origin refusal)
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained).
Multi-repo is not merely untested in fleet-sprint today -- it is explicitly REFUSED at the
precondition gate. checkMemberTopology (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:427-540) aborts
the sprint when members report divergent git origin URLs (the refusal is at runner.js:522-531), and
legacy (non---sync) mode is stricter still, requiring identical `git rev-parse HEAD` across all
members (runner.js:552-604).

Stage 1 of the multi-repo plan ("federated workspace") is one fleet MEMBER PER TARGET REPOSITORY: each
repo is checked out only on its own assigned members, and a workspace manifest (a JSON document
declaring repos, their origins, their base branches and which members hold them -- see the Stage 0
manifest bead) tells the runner which member belongs to which repo. This bead is the foundation for
every other Stage 1 piece: it makes the runner think in terms of (repoId -> members) instead of one
global member set, and it converts the divergent-origin refusal from "abort" into "validate against
the manifest".

Repo identity is the ORIGIN URL, not the filesystem path: two machines checking out the same repo at
different paths must resolve to the same repoId. Reverse lookup work_folder -> member is structurally
sound today because two members may never share a working directory on the same device
(docs/architecture.md:19-25, 332-334; workFolder at src/types.ts:23).
design:
1) Build the repo<->member index at launch, from the manifest, using manifest.mjs helpers
   repoOfMember() / membersForRepo() delivered by the Stage 0 manifest bead. Materialize it once into
   the runner's validated state (near the existing arg validation, runner.js:2445-2630) as
   { repoId -> { origin, base, roleMap, members[] } } and { memberName -> repoId }, and have every
   later phase read from it rather than re-deriving membership.
2) Rework checkMemberTopology (runner.js:427-540). Replace the global "all origins must match" rule
   (refusal at runner.js:522-531) with a PER-REPO rule:
   - group members by their manifest repoId;
   - every member in a repo group must report an origin URL that normalizes to that repo's
     manifest.repos[repoId].origin (normalize scheme/host/path so git@host:org/repo.git and
     https://host/org/repo(.git) compare equal, and strip a trailing .git and trailing slash);
   - a member whose actual origin does not match its manifest repo is a HARD FAILURE naming the
     member, the expected origin and the observed origin;
   - members belonging to DIFFERENT repo groups having different origins is now expected and must not
     abort;
   - a member present in --members but absent from the manifest is a hard failure (unassigned member),
     and a manifest member absent from --members is a hard failure (missing checkout) -- both with
     messages naming the member.
3) Legacy identical-HEAD mode (runner.js:552-604): when a manifest with more than one repo is in use,
   this check applies per repo group, never across groups. If legacy mode cannot be made coherent for
   multi-repo, refuse multi-repo in legacy mode with an explicit "multi-repo sprints require --sync
   mode" error rather than silently degrading.
4) Reverse lookup helper. Add memberForWorkFolder(device, workFolder) built on the existing member
   registry, and use it only where a work folder is the known input; repoId resolution itself must go
   through the manifest/origin URL, not the path.
5) Preserve the single-repo path exactly: with the synthesized one-entry manifest (repoId "default"),
   the per-repo rule degenerates to today's global rule and existing topology tests must pass
   unmodified.
6) Observability: emit one preflight log block listing repoId -> members -> resolved origin -> base for
   the whole workspace, so an operator can see the topology the sprint will run with before dispatch.
7) Update packages/apra-fleet-client in the same change if any MCP tool schema shifts (repo convention).
acceptance_criteria:
- The runner exposes a materialized index { repoId -> { origin, base, roleMap, members[] } } and
  { memberName -> repoId } after arg validation; a test asserts both for a 3-repo manifest.
- checkMemberTopology accepts a fleet whose members report THREE different origin URLs when the
  manifest assigns them to three repos -- the old divergent-origin abort (runner.js:522-531) no longer
  fires in that case.
- checkMemberTopology fails, with an error naming member/expected/observed, when a member's actual
  origin does not match its manifest repo's origin.
- Origin normalization tests: git@github.com:acme/backend.git, https://github.com/acme/backend.git and
  https://github.com/acme/backend/ all compare equal; github.com/acme/backend vs github.com/acme/frontend
  compare unequal.
- A member listed in --members but not in the manifest fails preflight naming that member; a member in
  the manifest but not in --members fails preflight naming that member.
- Multi-repo in legacy (non---sync) mode either applies the identical-HEAD check per repo group or
  fails with the exact message "multi-repo sprints require --sync mode" -- one of the two, tested.
- Single-repo sprints (no --manifest) keep today's exact topology behavior; existing topology tests
  pass unmodified.
- Preflight logs one block listing every repoId with its members, resolved origin and base; a test
  asserts each repoId appears once with its member list.

title: Stage 0: decouple the beads Dolt DB onto a dedicated beads remote (orchestrator needs zero code checkouts)
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained).
Beads (this project's issue tracker) stores issues in a local Dolt DB and syncs it through the git ref
refs/dolt/data ON YOUR CODE REPO'S GIT REMOTE (see AGY.md:58 and
packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/dolt-sync.mjs:96-100). Every member's beads clone therefore lives
next to "the" code checkout, and the orchestrator runs all its bd commands from its own checkout
(docs/architecture.md:170-175).

In a multi-repo sprint that assumption breaks badly: with N target repositories there is no single
"the" remote, and naively keeping today's coupling would force the orchestrator machine to clone all N
repos purely for bookkeeping -- exactly what the multi-repo architecture is designed to avoid. The fix
is to point the sprint's beads DB at a DEDICATED beads remote (a beads-only repository, or the
manifest holder repo) so the orchestrator's workspace contains only two things: the workspace manifest
and a code-free .beads clone.

Decision already taken in the design doc (docs/multi-repo-fleet-sprint-strategy.md, section 4 "Dolt /
beads topology"): ONE shared Dolt DB per workspace, NOT per-repo DBs with bd repo add hydration.
Per-repo DBs were considered and rejected because cross-repo links would become second-class
(external:<project>:<capability> targets), the dolt push mutex and settle machinery would have to run
per-DB, and the sprint's single scope query (bd list --parent) would become a federation problem. With
one DB, nothing in dolt-sync/dolt-settle/dolt_push_mutex has to change at all -- each member's beads
clone simply syncs to the beads remote instead of origin, which is per-clone configuration, not an
engine redesign.

This bead is independent of the manifest-schema bead and can be done in parallel with it.
design:
1) bd version reality check FIRST (this is design-doc open question #1 and it gates everything else in
   this bead). The upstream beads project (gastownhall/beads) documents: bd init --remote <url> (the
   Dolt sync remote may be a DIFFERENT git remote than the code repo), beads-only clones, and
   .beads/redirect (several clones sharing one DB). Verify each of these against OUR PINNED bd version
   by actually running them in a scratch directory -- do not trust the upstream docs. Record the
   verified bd version and the exact commands that worked in this bead's notes.
2) Verify dolt-settle compatibility. packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/dolt-settle.mjs:19-21 resolves
   its data dirs via `bd dolt status`; confirm that still resolves correctly for a beads-only clone
   with a non-origin remote, since a code-free workspace is a shape it has never seen.
3) If dedicated remotes are NOT supported by the pin: implement the documented fallback instead --
   host refs/dolt/data on ONE designated "beads home repo" named in the manifest (manifest key
   beadsRemote already carries this; the fallback just means that URL must be one of the code repos).
   Either way the manifest key stays beadsRemote and downstream code is unaffected.
4) Wire the remote through the engine. All dolt traffic goes through one module,
   packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/dolt-sync.mjs:1-131. Today its member probes and push/pull
   brackets assume the beads clone's remote is "origin" alongside the code checkout. Change it to take
   the beads remote from the sprint manifest (manifest.beadsRemote, from the sibling Stage 0 manifest
   bead) and fall back to today's behavior when the manifest has no beadsRemote (single-repo sprints
   must be unchanged). Do NOT change: the first-successful-pusher-wins D-push with one bounded
   reconcile (dolt-sync.mjs:109-115), the deterministic settle (dolt-settle.mjs:1-56), or the
   supervisor-owned dolt_push_mutex serialization -- all three remain correct and global with one DB.
5) Orchestrator beads-only workspace. Document and support an orchestrator whose work folder contains
   the manifest and a .beads clone with NO code checkout, and make the runner's preflight not require a
   git checkout for the orchestrator member when a manifest with beadsRemote is in use. Any bd command
   the orchestrator issues must work from that folder.
6) Bead IDs need no repo scoping (one DB, one prefix). Do not add per-repo ID prefixes.
7) Docs: add a "Beads topology" section to packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/README.md covering
   the dedicated beads remote, the beads-only orchestrator workspace, and the verified bd commands from
   step 1. Update packages/apra-fleet-client in the same change if any MCP tool schema shifts.
acceptance_criteria:
- This bead's notes record: the exact pinned bd version tested, and for each of `bd init --remote
  <url>`, beads-only clone, and .beads/redirect, a verified WORKS / DOES-NOT-WORK result with the exact
  command run.
- `bd dolt status` (as used by dolt-settle.mjs:19-21) resolves data dirs correctly inside a beads-only
  clone with a non-origin remote -- demonstrated by a scripted check, not by inspection.
- dolt-sync.mjs reads the beads remote from manifest.beadsRemote when present and from today's
  origin-derived path when absent; a test asserts a manifest-less (single-repo) sprint still pushes and
  pulls exactly as it does today.
- An end-to-end scenario exists where two members whose checkouts are DIFFERENT repositories both sync
  their beads clones to the same dedicated beads remote, and an issue created on one member is visible
  on the other after a sync bracket.
- The orchestrator can run its full bd command set (bd list --parent, bd create, bd update, bd close,
  bd dolt push) from a work folder that contains only the manifest and .beads -- with no code checkout
  present -- and the sprint preflight does not fail on the missing checkout.
- No changes were made to the D-push reconcile logic (dolt-sync.mjs:109-115), dolt-settle.mjs conflict
  resolution, or the dolt_push_mutex serialization; a diff review confirms these files' logic is
  untouched apart from remote resolution.
- If the pinned bd does NOT support dedicated remotes, the fallback ("beads home repo" named via
  manifest.beadsRemote) is implemented instead and the docs state which path is active.
- packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/README.md has a "Beads topology" section describing the
  above.
notes:
OPERATOR DECISION (2026-08-15, design doc open question #1): beads uses a SEPARATE remote git
repository that has nothing to do with the code repos. This is the design, not a preference -- the
"host refs/dolt/data on one designated code repo" fallback in DESIGN step 3 is now a last-resort
degradation to report and discuss, NOT an equally acceptable outcome. If the pinned bd cannot do
dedicated remotes, surface that as a blocking finding on this bead (and consider a bd upgrade) rather
than quietly implementing the fallback.

title: Stage 0: define the sprint workspace manifest schema and --manifest @file loading (+ base-SHA lockfile)
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained -- do not assume you have read the design doc).
fleet-sprint (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/) today targets exactly ONE git repository per
sprint: --branch and --base are single scalar values and every member is assumed to be a checkout of
the same origin. The multi-repo plan (docs/multi-repo-fleet-sprint-strategy.md, "federated workspace")
replaces "a sprint targets a repo" with "a sprint targets a WORKSPACE MANIFEST" -- a small JSON
document, modelled on Google repo/AOSP manifests, that names every repository in the workspace, pins
each one to its OWN base branch, says which registered fleet members hold each repo's checkout, and
declares the cross-repo dependency graph. The manifest is the spine everything else in Stage 1 reads
(per-repo bases, per-repo roleMaps, merge order, integration build order), so it lands first.

"Stage 0" = additive plumbing with no behavior change for existing single-repo sprints. This bead is
Stage 0's first and most-blocking piece: schema + loader + validation + lockfile. It deliberately does
NOT change dispatch, branching, or PR behavior -- those are Stage 1 children of the same epic.
design:
1) Manifest shape. Create the schema and a documented example. Target shape (derived from the design
   doc section 3 Option D, AMENDED by the operator's 2026-08-15 decision that the deployer is the
   integrator -- there is no all-repos-cloned integration member, so the old `integration` key is
   replaced by `deploy` plus a per-repo `build` declaration):

   {
     "workspace": "acme-shop",
     "beadsRemote": "git@github.com:acme/shop-beads.git",   // SEPARATE beads-only repo, no code in it
     "repos": {
       "backend":  { "origin": "git@github.com:acme/backend.git",  "base": "main",
                     "build": { "command": "npm ci && npm run build", "artifacts": ["dist/**"] },
                     "members": { "doer": ["be-dev1"], "reviewer": ["be-rev"] } },
       "frontend": { "origin": "git@github.com:acme/frontend.git", "base": "release/2.4",
                     "build": { "command": "npm ci && npm run build", "artifacts": ["build/**"] },
                     "members": { "doer": ["fe-dev1"] } },
       "shared":   { "origin": "git@github.com:acme/libs.git",     "base": "main",
                     "build": { "command": "npm ci && npm run build", "artifacts": ["dist/**"] } }
     },
     "graph": { "backend": ["shared"], "frontend": ["shared", "backend"] },
     "deploy": { "member": "deploy-1", "playbook": "deploy.md",
                 "mode": "composed", "artifactsDir": "artifacts" }
   }

   Keys: repos.<repoId> is the repo's stable id used everywhere else (bead metadata, turn gates, PR
   bodies, artifact directories). repos.*.build declares how that repo clean-builds itself in its OWN
   checkout and which artifacts get shipped to the deployer. graph.<repoId> = the repoIds this repo
   DEPENDS ON (edges point at dependencies), used for build order, assembly order and merge-order
   prescription. deploy.member is the member that receives artifacts and assembles/deploys the
   composition under its own work folder (it holds NO source checkout); deploy.mode is
   "composed" | "independent"; deploy.artifactsDir is the subdirectory of the deploy member's work
   folder that receives <repoId>/ artifact trees.

2) Loader + CLI flag. Add --manifest to the fleet-sprint arg contract. Argument parsing/validation
   lives in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js around runner.js:2445-2630 (the same block
   that validates --branch/--base/--members). Accept the "@file" form exactly the way --role-map
   already accepts a file today (args table in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/README.md) --
   reuse that existing file-reading helper. Per the operator's decision on manifest ownership, BOTH
   usages must work: a manifest checked into a holder repo and a manifest passed per launch; the loader
   only ever sees a file path, so this is a documentation/UX requirement plus a test for each usage.
   Put parse/validate logic in a NEW module (e.g. packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/manifest.mjs)
   exporting loadManifest(argValue), validateManifest(obj), repoIds(manifest), topoOrder(manifest),
   repoOfMember(manifest, memberName), membersForRepo(manifest, repoId, role) and
   buildSpec(manifest, repoId). runner.js should only call those exports.

3) Validation rules (all fail fast at launch, before any dispatch, with a message naming the offending
   key):
   - repos must be non-empty; each entry needs a non-empty origin and a non-empty base.
   - every member name in repos.*.members.* and in deploy.member must be a registered fleet member
     (cross-check against the member list the runner resolves for --members).
   - a member may appear under AT MOST ONE repoId (a member is machine+work_folder = one repo
     checkout). deploy.member must NOT appear under any repos.*.members -- the deployer holds artifacts,
     never source.
   - graph keys and values must all be known repoIds; the graph must be acyclic (topoOrder throws
     "manifest graph has a cycle: <path>").
   - if deploy is present, every repo must declare build.command and a non-empty build.artifacts array
     (otherwise the deployer would have nothing to assemble); if deploy is absent, build is optional.
   - deploy.mode must be "composed" or "independent"; deploy.artifactsDir must be a relative path with
     no "..", no absolute prefix and no symlink escape (it names a subtree of the deployer's own work
     folder and must not be able to point outside it).
   - unknown top-level keys and unknown keys inside a repo entry are rejected (typo protection).

4) Single-repo compatibility (the "no behavior change" guarantee). If --manifest is absent, synthesize
   an implicit one-entry manifest in memory: repoId "default", base = validated.baseBranch, members =
   the existing global roleMap (runner.js:2512-2534), empty graph, no deploy entry. Downstream code
   then reads the manifest unconditionally. When --manifest IS supplied, --base is ignored (per-repo
   bases win) and the runner logs one explicit line saying so.

5) Base-SHA lockfile. At sprint start, after topology validation and before Ensure Sprint Branch,
   resolve each repo's base to a concrete SHA (git rev-parse of origin/<base> on one member holding
   that repo -- via the existing per-member command dispatch, NOT from the orchestrator's own checkout;
   the orchestrator must need ZERO code checkouts). Record { repoId: { base, sha, resolvedAt } } into
   the sprint's viewer/run state and expose it for later children (PR bodies embed it). This is the
   vcstool "vcs export --exact" analog: it makes the run replayable and answers "what did we build
   against".

6) Docs + client. Document --manifest, every key, both ownership usages, and the lockfile in
   packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/README.md (args table + a new "Workspace manifest"
   section). If any fleet MCP tool schema in src/tools/* changes, update packages/apra-fleet-client in
   the SAME change (repo convention, mandatory).

7) Do NOT in this bead: change Ensure Sprint Branch, checkMemberTopology, streak/worklist assignment,
   the doer turn gate, the deploy phase, or PR publication. Those are separate children that depend on
   this one.
acceptance_criteria:
- packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/manifest.mjs exists and exports loadManifest, validateManifest,
  repoIds, topoOrder, repoOfMember, membersForRepo, buildSpec.
- A sprint launched with --manifest @<file> parses that file; a sprint launched WITHOUT --manifest
  produces the synthesized one-entry manifest (repoId "default") and behaves identically to today --
  proven by existing single-repo mock-sprint tests passing unmodified.
- Both manifest ownership usages are exercised by tests and documented: a manifest read from a path
  inside a checked-out holder repo, and a manifest passed as an arbitrary per-launch file path.
- An example manifest is checked in (e.g. packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/examples/
  workspace-manifest.example.json) containing every key in DESIGN step 1, including repos.*.build and
  the deploy block.
- Unit tests cover each validation rule and assert the error MESSAGE names the offending key, for:
  empty repos; missing origin; missing base; unregistered member name; the same member under two
  repoIds; deploy.member also listed under a repo; graph value referencing an unknown repoId; a cyclic
  graph (a->b->a); deploy present but a repo missing build.command; deploy present but a repo with an
  empty build.artifacts; deploy.mode not in {composed, independent}; artifactsDir absolute; artifactsDir
  containing ".."; unknown top-level key; unknown key inside a repo entry.
- topoOrder returns dependencies before dependents for {backend:[shared], frontend:[shared,backend]}
  (=> shared, backend, frontend) and throws naming the cycle path for a cyclic graph.
- Launching with both --manifest and --base logs exactly one line stating --base is ignored, and the
  manifest's per-repo bases are used.
- The lockfile is present in run/viewer state with one { base, sha, resolvedAt } per repoId, and a test
  asserts the SHAs came from per-member dispatch (no git rev-parse in the orchestrator's own working
  directory).
- packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/README.md documents --manifest, every manifest key, both
  ownership usages, the --base-ignored rule, and the lockfile.

title: Multi-repo fleet-sprint: federated workspace strategy (manifest + member-per-repo + deployer-assembled integration)
description:
fleet-sprint assumes exactly one target repository per sprint, and that assumption is enforced, not
merely untested: --branch/--base are single values, Ensure Sprint Branch applies one validated
baseBranch to every member (runner.js:5761-5857), checkMemberTopology REFUSES to start when members
report divergent origin URLs (runner.js:427-540, refusal at 522-531), beads sync rides refs/dolt/data
on the code repo's git remote (dolt-sync.mjs:96-100), the orchestrator does its git/PR work from its
own checkout (runner.js:9231-9283), the planner has no repo concept (runner.js:2635-2660), and the
sprint ends in exactly one PR.

Real customers overwhelmingly run polyrepo estates where one logical feature must change several
repos together. "Run one sprint per repo and stitch the PRs yourself" pushes the whole integration
burden onto the customer and is not a sellable answer.

Source design doc: docs/multi-repo-fleet-sprint-strategy.md (full option survey, industry research,
angle-by-angle walkthrough, comparison matrix, staged recommendation). Recommended architecture is
"federated workspace" = Option A (one fleet member per target repository) + Option D (a repo/AOSP-style
workspace manifest supplying per-repo origins, per-repo base pins, per-repo roleMaps, a dependency
graph, and a dedicated beads remote), evolving toward Option E (contract beads + Zuul-style speculative
gating). Option B (dispatches hopping between repo directories) and Option C (git submodules) are
rejected in the doc; C's kernel ("one durable place that names the repo set") is salvaged as the manifest.

This epic covers Stage 0 (manifest + beads decoupling) and Stage 1 (the sellable product feature:
one sprint, N repos, N coordinated PRs, integration-tested together). Stage 2 is a single
forward-looking placeholder child, deliberately not decomposed until Stage 0/1 land and produce
real usage evidence.

fleet-sprint is a GENERAL product: everything built here must be generic multi-repo support, not
"apra-fleet's own repos" support (dogfood-separation principle).
acceptance_criteria:
- Stage 0 children are closed: a workspace manifest schema exists and is accepted via --manifest @file
  (supported both as a checked-in holder-repo file and a per-launch file), a sprint runs with its beads
  DB synced to a SEPARATE beads-only remote repository unrelated to any code repo, and task beads carry
  a repo metadata field the planner stamps.
- Stage 1 children are closed: a single sprint drives N repos via one member (or member set) per repo,
  each repo branching from its own manifest-pinned base, dispatching concurrently across repos while
  staying serialized within a repo, producing one DRAFT PR per repo carrying a shared sprint topic ID,
  cross-links, base-SHA lockfile, prescribed merge order and the joint verdict.
- Integration happens at the DEPLOYER, not via a repo-cloning integration member: each repo's own
  member clean-builds its project in its own checkout, artifacts are transferred to the deployer's
  deployment work folder, and the deployer assembles and deploys the composed artifact in dependency
  order. No member ever holds a second repo's source checkout, and the orchestrator holds none.
- A single-repo sprint launched with no --manifest behaves exactly as it does today (zero regression);
  a one-entry manifest is equivalent to today's single-repo sprint.
- A workspace is reserved in full for the duration of a sprint; two sprints never share a workspace.
- packages/apra-fleet-client is updated in lockstep with any fleet MCP tool schema/behavior change made
  by any child (repo convention -- not optional cleanup).
- The three permission invariants from apra-fleet-ivxi / apra-fleet-u1qw hold across every new surface,
  including the deployer's artifact-assembly surface.
- All seven open questions have recorded operator decisions (see NOTES) and every child bead's design
  matches those decisions rather than the design doc's superseded recommendations.
notes:
OPEN QUESTIONS NEEDING A HUMAN DECISION (doc section 7) -- these are not yet resolved and several of
them gate specific children below; decide them before or during Stage 1 implementation:

1. bd version reality check. Dedicated-remote / beads-only-clone / .beads/redirect are documented
   upstream (gastownhall/beads) but must be verified against OUR pinned bd and against dolt-settle's
   data-dir resolution (dolt-settle.mjs:19-21). Fallback if unsupported: host refs/dolt/data on one
   designated "beads home repo" named in the manifest.
2. Failure isolation policy. If repo X's develop loop fails its cycles, do sibling repos' PRs still
   publish (joint verdict marked FAIL, X's PR missing), or does the sprint hold everything? Doc
   recommends publish-with-honest-verdict. Product call.
3. Who owns the manifest? Checked into a holder repo (auditable, versioned, new repo for the
   customer) vs. passed per launch as a file. Doc recommends supporting both, like --role-map today.
4. Integration member cost. Clone-everything is fine for 2-5 repos; 10+ may need shallow/sparse
   clones or an Nx-style affected-graph subset. Defer until real usage shows the shape.
5. Supervisor reservation semantics. The member-overlap ledger and issue-scope axis need a workspace
   concept. Doc recommends reserving the whole workspace per sprint in v1.
6. Cross-repo verdict in the PR gate. Block per-repo PRs (draft?) until the joint integration verdict
   passes, or always publish with the verdict stated? Interacts with (2).
7. Contract bead artifact format (Stage 2 only). OpenAPI diff vs. pact files vs. published package
   versions -- likely per-stack, needs customer discovery.

SECURITY: any child that touches permission grants for additional repo checkouts must preserve the
invariants established in apra-fleet-ivxi / apra-fleet-u1qw -- a member never self-escalates its own
permissions, the orchestrator grants strictly on a need basis, and the user's absolute restrictions
(NEVER_AUTO_GRANT) are never bypassed.
=== OPERATOR DECISIONS (2026-08-15) -- all seven open questions above are now ANSWERED. Where a
decision conflicts with the recommendation recorded earlier in these notes, THE DECISION WINS. ===

1. BEADS REMOTE: decided. Beads lives in a SEPARATE remote git repository that has nothing to do with
   any code repo. Not "one of the code repos hosts refs/dolt/data" -- a dedicated beads-only repo is
   the design, not a fallback. (apra-fleet-74vu.2 still verifies the pinned bd actually supports it.)
2. FAILURE ISOLATION: decided as recommended -- publish siblings with an honest verdict. If repo X
   fails, X gets no PR and every sibling PR states the joint verdict is FAIL and names X as missing.
   The sprint does not hold all PRs. (apra-fleet-74vu.10)
3. MANIFEST OWNERSHIP: decided as recommended -- support both a checked-in holder-repo manifest and a
   per-launch file, like --role-map does today. (apra-fleet-74vu.1)
4. INTEGRATION TOPOLOGY: DECIDED AGAINST THE DOC'S RECOMMENDATION -- this supersedes the design doc's
   "integration member with a checkout of every repo". Re-cloning all repositories onto one member is
   not sustainable: the disk and time cost grows with the estate and buys nothing we cannot get from
   artifacts. Instead THE DEPLOYER IS THE INTEGRATOR. Each repo's own member does a CLEAN BUILD of its
   own project in its own existing checkout; the resulting artifacts are transferred to the deployer's
   deployment work folder, where the deployer assembles the final composed artifact in dependency
   order. Clean separation: the deployer holds artifacts, never source; no member gains a second
   repo's checkout; integration cost scales with artifact size, not repo count. Reworked into
   apra-fleet-74vu.9 (retitled) and apra-fleet-74vu.8 (rescoped to the deployer role).
5. SUPERVISOR RESERVATION: decided as recommended -- reserve the WHOLE workspace per sprint in v1. No
   sharing of a workspace across concurrent sprints, no disjoint-repo-set sharing. First get one
   sprint working across multiple repos/projects; sharing is not a v1 concern.
6. PR GATE: decided -- consistent with (2). For the first pass every per-repo PR is raised as a DRAFT
   PR. Publication is not blocked on the joint verdict; the draft status plus the stated verdict is
   the gate. (apra-fleet-74vu.10)
7. CONTRACT ARTIFACT FORMAT: decided to defer, as recommended -- it differs per project type and stays
   unexplored until Stage 2 discovery. (apra-fleet-74vu.11)

title: [impl] Decide and implement headless-capable ApraFleet task registration (logon type, trigger, reboot survival)
description:
Decide the fix direction for apra-fleet-i8qj and implement it in registration.

CURRENT CODE (read it, do not trust the bug text): src/services/service-manager/windows.ts register() runs 'schtasks /create /tn ApraFleet /tr <wrapper.bat> /sc onlogon /rl limited /f'. There is NO '/it' flag anywhere -- the 'Logon Mode: Interactive only' state comes from registering WITHOUT /ru//rp, so schtasks defaults to the current user with an interactive-only logon type. Do not go looking for /it to remove.

WORK: evaluate the registration options that make 'schtasks /run' actually fire with zero interactive sessions while preserving reboot survival (AC2 of the parent bug): '/ru SYSTEM' (no password, needs elevation, changes the identity the server runs as -- check that ~/.apra-fleet paths and member config still resolve), '/ru <user> /rp <password>' (stored credentials, requires a secret we may not be able to obtain non-interactively), and/or adding '/sc onstart' as the boot trigger instead of/in addition to '/sc onlogon'. Preserve the existing wrapper .bat mechanism.

FILES: src/services/service-manager/windows.ts (primarily register(); may add a small capability-probe helper). Keep to <=3 files.

DONE / ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. register() now produces a task that can be launched by 'schtasks /run' with no interactive session present, OR -- if no such registration is achievable without credentials/elevation this code can assume -- register() degrades explicitly and the decision is recorded as a bead comment plus a short note handed to the docs task apra-fleet-i8qj.7, making the CLI direct-spawn fallback (apra-fleet-i8qj.4) the shipped behaviour. Either outcome is acceptable; a half-implemented headless registration is not.
2. The chosen direction explicitly addresses parent AC2 (auto-restart after machine reboot) -- either it still holds, or the tradeoff is stated in writing.
3. Elevation/credential requirements are detected and handled, not assumed: if the chosen schtasks invocation fails for lack of privilege, register() must fall back to the current onlogon registration rather than leaving the machine with NO registered task, and must log which mode it landed in.
4. Which mode was used is observable at runtime (e.g. recorded so start()/query() can reason about it, or re-derivable from 'schtasks /query /v').
5. Existing tests in tests/service-manager.test.ts still pass; tsc build passes; ASCII-only source.

comments.author: E2E Tester
comments.text:
DECISION (i8qj.2): headless registration IS achievable, implemented in src/services/service-manager/windows.ts register().

Direction chosen: tiered registration.
1. Primary: 'schtasks /create /tn ApraFleet /tr <wrapper.bat> /sc onstart /ru SYSTEM /rl highest /f'. No stored password needed (SYSTEM takes none), launchable by 'schtasks /run' with zero interactive sessions.
2. Fallback (AC3): if that /create is refused (no elevation), register() retries the historical '/sc onlogon /rl limited' registration, so the machine is never left with NO task, and logs which mode it landed in. If BOTH creates fail but a task already exists (e.g. re-registering a SYSTEM task unelevated), the existing registration is kept and its mode re-derived from 'schtasks /query /fo list /v' Run As User; if neither create landed and no task exists, register() throws instead of returning a false success.

Identity concern checked: running as SYSTEM would otherwise resolve os.homedir() to C:\Windows\System32\config\systemprofile, breaking ~/.apra-fleet (src/paths.ts FLEET_DIR), provider config dirs (src/cli/config.ts) and the credential key ~/.apra-fleet/data/salt. Credentials are NOT DPAPI/user-scoped (src/utils/crypto.ts uses a random AES key file), so pinning the registering user's env into the wrapper .bat is sufficient: the wrapper now emits 'set "USERPROFILE=..."' plus HOMEDRIVE/HOMEPATH/USERNAME/APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA (same session-var set as src/os/windows.ts getCleanEnv), so a SYSTEM-run server uses exactly the files the interactive install wrote.

Parent AC2 (reboot survival): STRENGTHENED, not traded away. '/sc onstart' starts the server at boot with nobody logged in; the old onlogon trigger only fired once a user logged on. In the degraded onlogon fallback the old behaviour (and the old headless limitation) is what you get, and register() says so on stderr.

AC4 observability: mode recorded at ~/.apra-fleet/data/service-registration.json and exposed as readServiceRegistrationMode() (defaults to 'onlogon-interactive' for pre-existing installs); also re-derivable via deriveRegistrationModeFromQuery(). unregister() clears the record. i8qj.3/.4 should branch on these.

NOTE FOR DOCS (apra-fleet-i8qj.7): document that 'apra-fleet start'/install run elevated gives a SYSTEM onstart task that works headless and auto-starts at boot; run unelevated it degrades to the onlogon interactive-only task, which cannot be fired by schtasks /run with no interactive session and only restarts after a user logs on -- the CLI direct-spawn fallback (i8qj.4) covers that case at the cost of reboot auto-restart. Mode is visible in ~/.apra-fleet/data/service-registration.json.

Verification: tsc build passes, tests/service-manager.test.ts 51 tests pass (onlogon assertion retained as the fallback-path contract, new tests for SYSTEM primary path, both-fail-keep-existing, both-fail-no-task throw, USERPROFILE pinning, and readServiceRegistrationMode default). ASCII only.

SITE 2 -- src/tools/remove-member.ts:93: `sed -i '/${escapedKey}/d' ~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, hardcoded POSIX even though `cmds = getOsCommands(getAgentOS(agent))` is in scope and IS used by the adjacent calls at lines 66 and 71. title: fleet-sprint finalizeAbort: PowerShell parse failure on bare $HOME/... path breaks PR lookup on Windows members
description:
Reproduced live on fleet-win-dev1's Sprint 4 (branch feat/viewer-dashboard-polish, sprintId ending e3cb342f...) at the StalledSprintError abort/finalizeAbort step: PR-lookup needs the member's stored VCS credential token, read via a command containing a bare `$HOME/.fleet-git-credential-github` path. On a Windows/PowerShell member this is not variable expansion the way it is in POSIX shells -- PowerShell parsed `$HOME/.fleet-git-credential-github` as `$HOME` followed by a `/` operator expecting a right-hand expression, and errored:

  ParserError: You must provide a value expression following the '/' operator.
  Unexpected token '.fleet-git-credential-github' in expression or statement.

Result: finalizeAbort's PR lookup failed outright and silently degraded to "writing the terminal history record with no PR lookup" -- the sprint's final abort report has no PR link/state even though the branch may have had one.

THIS IS NOT AN ISOLATED CASE. This project has hit bare-$VAR-on-Windows/PowerShell transport issues repeatedly and piecemeal (per session history: bare $variable tokens silently stripped or mis-parsed through the SSH exec transport on Windows members, has bitten multiple different code paths at different times). Requested by the operator: a HOLISTIC audit, not another one-off patch.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Fix the immediate finalizeAbort PR-lookup path so the credential-file read works correctly on both POSIX and Windows/PowerShell members (e.g. resolve $HOME to a concrete path OS-appropriately before building the command, rather than relying on shell-level variable expansion that differs between transports).
2. Grep the ENTIRE codebase (src/, packages/apra-fleet-se/, packages/apra-fleet-workflow/, packages/apra-fleet-client/) for every other place a command string is built containing $HOME, $VAR, or other POSIX-shell-only variable/expansion syntax that gets sent through execute_command/strategy.execCommand to a member -- since agent.os can be 'windows' at any such call site, each one is a latent version of this same bug.
3. For each occurrence found, either (a) resolve the variable to a concrete OS-appropriate path in JS before building the command string (preferred -- matches the pattern already used elsewhere, e.g. path resolution done host-side rather than shell-side), or (b) branch the command construction explicitly on agent.os the way deliverConfigFile() and other os-aware call sites already do.
4. Add a regression test (or extend an existing one) that constructs commands for a synthetic Windows agent and asserts no bare POSIX-only variable syntax appears in the generated command string.
5. Document the pattern/rule in a central place (CLAUDE.md or an internal dev doc) so future command-string construction doesn't reintroduce it: "never rely on shell variable expansion in a command string sent via execute_command; resolve host/path values in JS first, since the target member's shell (PowerShell vs POSIX) is not guaranteed."
notes:
Sweep findings (background agent, read-only grep across src/, apra-fleet-se, apra-fleet-workflow, apra-fleet-client -- packages dirs had zero hits, their command-building is thin/pass-through):

CONFIRMED REAL BUGS (unguarded, reach Windows members):
1. src/tools/monitor-task.ts:35,39,41,47 -- taskDir built as `~/.fleet-tasks/${task_id}` then used in `cat`, `xargs -r kill -0`, `tail -20`. cmds = getOsCommands(getAgentOS(agent)) is computed at line 34 but never actually used for these commands. monitor_task has no OS gate; execute-command.ts's long-running launch only WARNS (doesn't block) on non-linux, so a task can genuinely be started+monitored on Windows. Fix shape: resolve-in-JS via member-home.ts's probeCommandFor (see reference pattern below), or branch cmds for this whole query set.
2. src/tools/remove-member.ts:93 -- `sed -i '/${escapedKey}/d' ~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, hardcoded POSIX despite cmds = getOsCommands(getAgentOS(agent)) already being in scope and used for adjacent calls at lines 66 and 71. remove_member runs against any agent OS. Also wrapped in .catch(() => {}) -- same "hides for a long time" shape as finalizeAbort. Fix shape: branch on agentOs like the adjacent calls already do.

NEEDS HUMAN JUDGMENT (not confirmed bugs, flagged for review):
3. src/cli/watch.ts:426 -- "$HOME/.claude/projects/${f.rtEnc}" then `ls -t | head -1` via execCommand. Gated to !isLocal && provider==='claude' remote members only; not confirmed whether Windows Claude members are excluded upstream of this call. Needs a human check of ctx.agent/isLocal construction before rtEnc is set.
4. src/tools/execute-command.ts:230-236 + src/services/cloud/task-wrapper.ts:34 -- bash wrapper (mkdir -p ~/.fleet-tasks/..., nohup bash ...). Has an explicit runtime warning already (lines 214-216: "bash wrapper designed for Linux... may not support this feature") but isn't blocked. Same root cause as finalizeAbort, but already surfaces a warning rather than failing silently -- lower priority than items 1-2.

ALREADY SAFE (reference patterns to fix the above against):
- src/providers/claude.ts:373-374 -- isWindows ? '$env:USERPROFILE\.claude.json' : '$HOME/.claude.json'
- src/providers/agy.ts:22-23 -- SCRIPTS_UNIX/SCRIPTS_WIN constants selected by OS elsewhere
- src/services/member-home.ts:53-56 -- probeCommandFor(targetOs) branches PowerShell $env:USERPROFILE vs printf '%s' "$HOME" -- BEST reference pattern for the "resolve then interpolate" fix shape, use this for items 1 and 3.

integ-test-runner verification (2026-08-11): On branch fix/compose-permissions-write-noop (commits c99b0199 fix, 722b4122 test), ran `npx vitest run tests/compose-permissions.test.ts tests/compose-permissions-persist.test.ts` -- 2 files, 43/43 tests passed, no failures.

title: [impl] Wire the Clock Skew Check phase into Sprint Setup with a failSoft cross-shell probe and advisory WARNING
description:
File: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js (single file; edits confined to the Sprint Setup block around lines 5552-5760).

Wire a new phase('Clock Skew Check') inside group('Sprint Setup'), immediately AFTER the existing 'Ensure Sprint Branch' member loop, iterating the same dispatched-member set (branchEnsureMembers) sequentially so the command log stays deterministic.

Per member:
1. hubT0 = Date.now().
2. Run the member-side epoch probe through the existing command() helper with { member_name: member, silent: true, failSoft: true, label: `Probe clock on member '<member>'` }. Do NOT introduce hub-side process.platform branching -- the hub's OS says nothing about the member's. Run CLOCK_SKEW_PROBE_POSIX first; if it fails or parseEpochMillis() returns null, retry once with CLOCK_SKEW_PROBE_WINDOWS. This shell-agnostic try/fallback matches the repo convention (runner.js lines 276-282) of not assuming a member shell, and avoids adding member-OS lookup plumbing that runner.js does not have today.
3. hubT1 = Date.now().
4. thresholdMs = clockSkewThresholdMs(process.env); result = evaluateClockSkew({ hubT0, hubT1, memberEpochMs, thresholdMs }).
5. If result.exceeded, log() a single WARNING line that names the member AND the measured skew in ms/seconds and its direction (ahead/behind), and states the operational consequence (stall detection may falsely abort this sprint; resync the member clock). If !result.ok, log() one advisory line that the probe could not be read on that member and skew was not measured.
6. Otherwise log nothing beyond the normal phase bookkeeping.

Acceptance criteria (done when ALL hold):
1. The phase runs once per dispatched member and appears in the sprint log under the Sprint Setup group.
2. ADVISORY ONLY: a failing probe, an unparsable probe, or an over-threshold skew never throws, never aborts, and never marks the sprint failed. Both probe attempts use failSoft: true.
3. The threshold comes from clockSkewThresholdMs(process.env) -- 30000 is never hardcoded.
4. An in-bracket (healthy) member produces no warning and no other behavior change.
5. The warning text contains both the member name and the measured skew value.
6. `npm test` passes; packages/apra-fleet-client is NOT touched (no MCP tool schema change).

Probe-string quoting caveat (read before finalizing the probe strings): review the command-quoting notes at runner.js ~270-290 and ~2050-2075 (base64 argv[1] wrapping; PowerShell/cmd.exe parsing of [ ] and ::) and confirm the chosen probe strings survive that layer unmangled. A mangled probe degrades silently to 'unparsable', which in the log is indistinguishable from a member whose clock simply could not be read -- so the feature would look healthy while measuring nothing.

title: [impl] Add pure evaluateClockSkew() bracket helper + cross-shell epoch probe constants to runner.js
description:
File: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js (single file).

Add an EXPORTED pure helper next to the existing pure decision helper decideEnsureBranchAction() (~line 4551), following the same "pure decision function + thin dispatch call site" convention:

  export function evaluateClockSkew({ hubT0, hubT1, memberEpochMs, thresholdMs })
    -> { ok, skewMs, exceeded, reason }

Behavior:
- memberEpochMs inside [hubT0, hubT1] => skewMs 0, exceeded false.
- memberEpochMs > hubT1 => skewMs = memberEpochMs - hubT1 (member ahead, positive).
- memberEpochMs < hubT0 => skewMs = memberEpochMs - hubT0 (member behind, negative).
- exceeded = Math.abs(skewMs) > thresholdMs.
- Non-finite / NaN / null memberEpochMs (probe failed or emitted unparsable text) => { ok: false, skewMs: null, exceeded: false, reason: 'unparsable' }. NEVER throw: this is advisory-only code.

Also export in the same change:
- CLOCK_SKEW_PROBE_POSIX = 'date +%s%3N'
- CLOCK_SKEW_PROBE_WINDOWS = a PowerShell one-liner printing [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds()
- parseEpochMillis(stdout): trims, takes the first all-digit token, returns null (not NaN, never throws) on anything else -- including the "date: illegal option" / literal "%3N" text a POSIX probe emits on a shell without GNU date.
- clockSkewThresholdMs(env): parseInt(env.STALL_THRESHOLD_MS ?? '120000') / 4, mirroring src/services/stall/stall-detector.ts:96; falls back to 120000/4 on an unparsable value.

Acceptance criteria (done when ALL hold):
1. All four helpers exist in runner.js and are exported.
2. Every helper is pure: no I/O, no Date.now() inside them (the caller supplies hubT0/hubT1), no throwing on bad input.
3. No other runner.js behavior changes in this task -- wiring the phase is the next task in this streak.
4. `npm test` passes.
5. packages/apra-fleet-client is NOT touched: no MCP tool schema changes here, so the CLAUDE.md client-sync rule does not apply.
close_reason: Added pure evaluateClockSkew/parseEpochMillis/clockSkewThresholdMs helpers + probe constants to runner.js; npm test passes (1788/1788).

title: apra-fleet start: Windows scheduled task silently fails with no interactive logon session
description:
On Windows, 'apra-fleet start' (src/cli/start.ts -> WindowsServiceManager in src/services/service-manager/windows.ts) registers a Scheduled Task ('ApraFleet', trigger /sc onlogon, /rl limited i.e. 'Logon Mode: Interactive only') and fires it via 'schtasks /run'. When no interactive console/RDP session exists for the configured user (query user / query session shows no logged-on user -- exactly the normal state of a headless or SSH-managed machine), the task cannot start: schtasks /run returns success but the task body never actually executes. No error is surfaced anywhere -- fleet.log gets no new startup line, port 7523 never opens, and the caller (e.g. 'apra-fleet start' itself, or a deploy runbook invoking it) just times out waiting for the server to come up ('Server did not start in time').

CONFIRMED LIVE on fleet-win-dev1 (2026-08-10, during Sprint 4's Deploy phase): install --force succeeded, stopped the old v0.4.0 server per its documented caution, then 'apra-fleet start' failed with the timeout above. 'schtasks /query /tn ApraFleet /fo list /v' showed the task registered and 'Ready' but Last Run Time frozen at 2026-08-05 (5 days stale -- schtasks /run today never actually fired it). 'query user' confirmed zero interactive sessions on the machine at the time.

This is a real, structural gap, not a one-off: ANY headless/remote-managed Windows fleet member (or any real end user running apra-fleet as a background service on a Windows box with no one at the console -- e.g. a server, a CI runner, a cloud VM) will hit this identically. The immediate operational impact was worked around at the deploy.md runbook level (apra-fleet-<TBD>: deploy.md now launches via 'apra-fleet run --transport http' as a detached child process instead of 'apra-fleet start', which sidesteps the scheduled task entirely) -- but 'apra-fleet start' itself, the documented persistent/survives-reboot entry point for real end users, is still broken for this exact scenario outside of fleet-sprint's own deploy path.

FIX SHAPE (not yet designed in detail): either (a) register the scheduled task so it does not require an interactive session -- e.g. drop the /it (interactive-only) restriction and run under stored credentials or as SYSTEM, so 'schtasks /run' works headless while still preserving the 'survives reboot / auto-restart on logon' property the task exists for; or (b) have WindowsServiceManager.start() detect that no interactive session is available and fall back to spawning 'run --transport http' directly as a detached child process (the same Win32_Process-Create-based mechanism used for the deploy.md workaround), accepting the loss of auto-restart-on-reboot in that fallback case. Whichever direction is chosen, 'apra-fleet start' should also start SURFACING this failure loudly (today it silently times out with a generic message that gives no hint the root cause is 'no interactive session') -- e.g. checkRunningInstance()/query() should distinguish 'task registered but never fired' from other failure modes and say so.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. 'apra-fleet start' on a Windows machine with zero interactive sessions (query user reports none) successfully brings the server up and it stays up, OR fails IMMEDIATELY with a clear, specific error naming the interactive-session requirement as the cause (not a generic multi-minute timeout).
2. Whatever mechanism is chosen still allows the server to auto-restart after a machine reboot (or the tradeoff of not doing so is explicitly documented and accepted).
3. A regression test simulates or documents the no-interactive-session condition and asserts the new behavior (success or fast/clear failure), not the current silent multi-minute timeout.
4. docs/README references to 'apra-fleet start' on Windows note the interactive-session caveat if it remains a real constraint after the fix.

title: Detect hub/member clock skew at sprint setup and surface to operator
description:
Add a Clock Skew Check phase to fleet-sprint's Sprint Setup group (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js, alongside the existing Ensure Sprint Branch phase), one per dispatched member, before real work starts.

Bracket hub-vs-member clock skew the same way this was manually verified during diagnosis: capture hub_t0 = Date.now(), run a member-side probe (Windows: `[DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds()`; POSIX: `date +%s%3N`) via execute_command, capture hub_t1 = Date.now(). Member time should fall within [hub_t0, hub_t1] (plus round-trip slack); skew is how far outside that bracket it lands.

If |skew| > STALL_THRESHOLD_MS / 4 (30s at the current 120s default), log a clear WARNING into the sprint log/dashboard naming the member and the measured skew. Advisory only -- do not hard-abort the sprint, since a member can function for everything except stall detection with a skewed clock.

First cut: log-only inside runner.js, no new/changed MCP tool schema, so packages/apra-fleet-client stays out of scope (per CLAUDE.md's client-sync rule, only needed if a tool schema changes). A broader version surfacing skew in member_detail/register_member output at any time is a separate, later follow-up, not bundled here.

Why this matters: apra-fleet-fleet-win-dev1's stall detector was killing every healthy Planner dispatch as "stalled" -- root-caused via live reproduction to hub/member clock skew of ~215s on fleet-win-dev1 (w32time had never synced, free-running on CMOS clock). lastActivityAt is seeded with the hub's Date.now() but compared against member-produced mtime/content timestamps -- with a 215s skew, that comparison can never succeed, so lastActivityAt never advances and the sprint dies on the first 30s poll tick past the 120s threshold (observed: killed at 130-145s every retry, 3/3 retries). The clock has been manually resynced on fleet-win-dev1 as an immediate unblock (w32tm /config + /resync, verified via the same bracket technique, skew now ~0.4ms), but nothing currently detects this class of failure before a sprint burns retries on it. See apra-fleet's sibling bead for the underlying skew-immune stall-detector fix (long-term correctness fix, not blocking this task).
