title: [regression][carry-over] Setup's 'node dist/index.js start' silently reuses a stale orphaned server left by a non-torn-down prior run instead of the fresh install
description:
Part: 2 (smoke test, Setup)
Expected: after '## Setup' runs a fresh 'node dist/index.js install' into the sandbox HOME and then 'node dist/index.js start', the running server on the scratch port (18700) should be the one just installed at branch HEAD, so the smoke test actually exercises branch HEAD as required.
Actual: 'node dist/index.js start' printed 'Server already running at http://127.0.0.1:18700/mcp pid=85166' and left that process running. That process turned out to be an orphan from a much earlier, unrelated regression pass: server.json showed version 'v0.4.0_55adab' (not the 'v0.4.0_3475c2' this Setup had just installed) and 'node dist/index.js status' reported Uptime 82h+ -- i.e. it survived at least one, likely several, prior regression cycles without ever being stopped by a Teardown. Crucially, scripts/sandbox-lock.mjs's own busy-check (acquireLock) found NO live lock and let this Setup proceed as if starting clean, yet the stale server was still live and bound to the scratch port the whole time -- the lock and the actual server process can apparently drift out of sync (a live orphaned server with no corresponding live lock), so Setup's 'already running' fallback path has no version/freshness check and will happily keep serving an arbitrarily old build indefinitely across many later regression passes' Setup calls without anyone noticing, silently invalidating the 'runs against branch HEAD via fresh install' guarantee this playbook depends on.
Test: '## Setup' section of regression-test-playbook.md, the 'node dist/index.js start' step, run 2026-08-03.
Repro: 1) Run '## Setup' once, then abandon the session without ever running '## Teardown' (or have Teardown's own lock-ownership refusal skip the 'stop' step for some other reason) so the fleet server keeps running on port 18700 with no live lock recorded. 2) Some time later (verified here after 82h), run '## Setup' fresh again with a newer branch HEAD build installed into the same sandbox path. 3) 'node dist/index.js start' reports 'already running' and reuses the old orphaned process/version rather than detecting the version mismatch and restarting. Recommend: 'start' should compare the running server's reported version against the just-installed version (or at least log a loud warning) when falling back to 'already running', and/or Setup should treat a version mismatch here the same as a busy-lock refusal (fail loud) rather than silently proceeding on a stale build. Worked around for this run by manually 'stop'-ing the orphan and re-'start'-ing before continuing, so this run's own smoke test did execute against the fresh v0.4.0_3475c2 build.
notes:
Priority raised P2->P1 per background triage 2026-08-03: this is a SILENT failure mode (stale 82h-old orphaned server reattached with zero error/version-check, defeating the smoke test's purpose of validating branch HEAD), which is worse than a loud blocker -- it can report false-positive 'it works' against a stale build for days undetected. See apra-fleet-m1n for the paired loud-blocker case (correctly left at P2).
TRIAGE 2026-08-09: STILL PRESENT on branch HEAD (feat/agy-output-format-json @ 6346de89) and on origin/main. Read src/cli/start.ts:53-58 -- runStart() calls checkRunningInstance() and, if running, prints 'Server already running at ${instance.url} pid=${instance.pid}' and returns immediately; there is no version/freshness comparison and no warning. src/services/singleton.ts:22-26 RunningInstance only carries {running,url,pid} -- version is dropped even though src/index.ts:310-317 already WRITES 'version: serverVersion' into server.json alongside pid/port/url. So the fix is mechanical: surface info.version from checkRunningInstance() and have runStart compare it to the local version.json (loud warn, or hard fail so the playbook's Setup treats a mismatch like a busy-lock refusal). Also confirmed regression-test-playbook.md Setup (line 92-140) still has no freshness assertion beyond 'node dist/index.js status exits 0 and reports 18700'. Note the lock-drift half of this bead depends on scripts/sandbox-lock.mjs, which does NOT exist on main (see apra-fleet-4osf). Classification: LOW-HANGING-FRUIT.
regression-test-runner 2026-08-19 Part 2 pre-Setup check: STILL REPRODUCES, found before Setup even ran this cycle. A pre-existing orphaned apra-fleet server was found bound to the scratch port 18700 (PID 17545, /Users/akhil/git/apra-fleet/dist/index.js --transport http, started 10Aug26 -- survived at least 9 days across multiple regression cycles without a Teardown ever stopping it). Recovered this cycle by manually running 'node dist/index.js stop' with HOME/APRA_FLEET_PORT set to the sandbox before Setup, then removing the stale sandbox dir, before proceeding with a fresh Setup. Same root cause, unaddressed. Carries over informational per regression-test-playbook.md.

title: Reviewer retry-after-schema-repair-failure drops base-branch/branch/bead-ids context, causing a guaranteed contract-violation abort
description:
runner.js's Review dispatch: when the reviewer's output fails schema validation twice (JSON parse error x1, missing required 'verdict' x1) the schema-repair mechanism gives up and synthesizes a fallback CHANGES_NEEDED with empty reopenIds/newTasks. The engine then retries the review once more (ReviewerContractViolationError guard: 'CHANGES_NEEDED verdict with empty reopenIds AND empty newTasks is a contract violation ... retrying the review once'), but that retry's dispatch payload only contains the schema re-prompt ('please output valid JSON matching this schema') -- it does NOT carry forward the original review context (base-branch, branch, bead ids to review). The reviewer agent correctly refuses to guess a branch name and returns the exact same self-contradictory CHANGES_NEEDED (empty reopenIds/newTasks) as its only schema-valid option, which the anti-stall guard then correctly detects 'twice in a row' and aborts the whole sprint with ReviewerContractViolationError.

Net effect: ANY review dispatch that hits 2 consecutive schema-invalid outputs is now guaranteed to abort the sprint on the next round, because the retry path structurally cannot succeed (it never had the inputs needed to produce a real verdict). This is not a rare fluke -- it will recur whenever the reviewer model produces malformed JSON twice, which is plausible under load/long context.

Observed: apra-fleet-417,apra-fleet-66u,apra-fleet-647.1,apra-fleet-647.1.1 sprint on fleet-win-dev1, 2026-08-03 ~12:02 UTC. Real work from Develop C1R3 (7/8 streaks: 647.1.4.1, 417.3.1, 417.5, 647.1.3.2, 417.1, 417.2.3, 417.2.4, 647.1.1.3) had already succeeded and was pushed before this abort, so it was not lost -- but the sprint had to be manually relaunched to get a real review.

Fix: the review-retry-after-schema-repair-failure code path must re-include the same base-branch/branch/bead-ids payload used on the original dispatch, not just the corrective JSON re-prompt. Also consider: when the repair mechanism itself can't get valid JSON in 2 tries, that is arguably a distinct failure mode (agent dispatch/repair failure) that should not masquerade as a real CHANGES_NEEDED verdict at all -- treating it as a dispatch failure (retryable/abortable via the existing dispatch-failure path) rather than a semantically-empty reviewer verdict may be the more correct fix.
notes: TRIAGE: ALREADY FIXED. Read runner.js's current dispatchReview() (lines ~5330-5500): when the reviewer's own internal schema-repair loop exhausts (AgentOutputError), the verdict is now marked 'dispatchFailed: true' and handled by a SEPARATE retry-once-then-degrade path (line ~5490 area) that calls the SAME dispatchReviewerOnce() closure -- which always carries the full original beadIds/baseBranch/branch/goal context (it's a closure over dispatchReview's own params, not a bare schema re-prompt). This is exactly fix direction (b) the bead itself proposed: schema-repair exhaustion is treated as a distinct dispatch-failure mode, not routed through the empty-context contract-violation retry. isReviewerContractViolation() is only checked AFTER the dispatchFailed branch, so a real self-contradictory verdict and a dispatch/repair failure can no longer be conflated. This landed in commit de48e98c (2026-08-05, 'chore: integration branch...'), which post-dates cdd's filing (2026-08-03 12:07 UTC) and touches runner.js. Classification: ALREADY-FIXED-OR-DUPLICATE. Subsystem: fleet-sprint Review dispatch.
close_reason: Duplicate/already-fixed: runner.js's dispatchReview() already treats reviewer schema-repair exhaustion as a distinct 'dispatchFailed' path (retry-once via the same full-context dispatchReviewerOnce closure, not routed through the empty-context contract-violation retry) -- landed in commit de48e98c (2026-08-05), which post-dates this bead's filing (2026-08-03). Verified by direct read of runner.js lines ~5330-5500. See bead note for detail.

title: [impl] Push every provider-keyed table out of vcs-module.mjs and document the provider extension contract
description:
FILES: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/vcs-module.mjs, packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/vcs-providers/index.mjs, packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/vcs-providers/{github,generic-git}.mjs. Do NOT edit runner.js in this task.

CONTEXT (verified 2026-08-03 by reading the landed code): the extension point is HALF built. vcs-providers/index.mjs already has a real runtime registry (registerVcsProvider / unregisterVcsProvider / getVcsProvider / resolveVcsProviderChain) with a documented one-file contract. But vcs-module.mjs keeps TWO competing provider-keyed tables that a new provider must also edit, which is exactly what the epic AC forbids: `const BUILDERS = {...}` (command builders, AND the "known provider" vocabulary resolveProvider() validates against) and `DEFAULT_AUTH_MODES = Object.freeze({github, bitbucket, azure-devops})`.

SEQUENCING: this task rewrites vcs-module.mjs and is deliberately ordered AFTER 647.1.3.3 and 647.1.4.1, which rewrite the same file (capabilities(), classification wiring). Land on top of their result; do not revert their changes.

WORK:
1. Fold DEFAULT_AUTH_MODES into the provider descriptors: each provider module declares its own default auth mode (github -> 'github-app'; providers with no mode axis -> null), and resolveProvider() reads it off the resolved descriptor via getVcsProvider().
2. Fold BUILDERS into the same descriptors: a provider's command builders (create-pull-request, comment, ...) become fields on its descriptor, and buildVcsCommand() dispatches through the registry. resolveProvider()'s known-provider vocabulary becomes listVcsProviders(), so registry and vocabulary can never drift apart.
3. Extend registerVcsProvider()'s descriptor validation and the index.mjs doc comment to cover the newly-owned fields (defaultAuthMode, builders), and state the contract explicitly: adding a provider = one new file under vcs-providers/ + one line in BUILT_IN_PROVIDERS, no other file under fleet-sprint/ changed.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- vcs-module.mjs contains NO provider-name-keyed object literal: both BUILDERS and DEFAULT_AUTH_MODES are gone, and no 'github'/'bitbucket'/'azure-devops' string is used as a lookup key there (prose/comments are fine).
- vcs-providers/ is the single provider manifest; resolveProvider()'s known set comes from the registry, not a second table.
- registerVcsProvider() validates the new descriptor fields and index.mjs documents the full required export shape.
- Existing GitHub behavior byte-identical: resolveProvider() still returns {provider:'github', authMode:'github-app'} for a github-registered member; buildCreatePrCommand() and classifyFailure() verdicts unchanged.
- npm test (unit) green and the fleet-sprint mock-sprint suite green.

title: [impl] install --force: bounded poll on isApraFleetRunning() + SIGKILL escalation before binary copy
description: Fix ETXTBSY on install --force. Files: src/cli/install.ts (killApraFleet ~695-702; runInstall ~893-923). Behavior: after killApraFleet() sends SIGTERM, replace the hardcoded 500ms sleep at ~909-911 with a bounded poll on isApraFleetRunning() over a grace window; if a non-installer apra-fleet process is still alive after the grace window, escalate to SIGKILL (pkill -9 -x apra-fleet / taskkill already -F). Only proceed to fs.copyFileSync(process.execPath, binaryPath) at ~923 once no non-installer apra-fleet process remains. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: (1) install --force never reaches the binary copy while an old apra-fleet is still listening; (2) an old singleton that takes >500ms to exit no longer produces ETXTBSY; (3) SIGKILL escalation fires only after the SIGTERM grace window elapses; (4) npm run build passes. Do NOT change the log-message behavior here -- that is apra-fleet-l7n.3.

title: install --force: verify old server actually exits before copying binary (fix ETXTBSY)
description: killApraFleet() in src/cli/install.ts:695-702 issues a fire-and-forget `pkill -x apra-fleet` (SIGTERM) and runInstall() (src/cli/install.ts:909-911) then waits a hardcoded 500ms before fs.copyFileSync(process.execPath, binaryPath) at line 923. When the old singleton does not exit within 500ms the binary is still text-file-busy and the copy fails with `ETXTBSY: text file is busy, copyfile ... -> ~/.apra-fleet/bin/apra-fleet`, aborting `install --force` with exit 1 (reproduced during deploy: old `apra-fleet --transport http` pid 1124907 still listening on 7523 afterward). Replace the fixed 500ms sleep with a bounded poll on isApraFleetRunning() plus SIGKILL escalation if the process is still alive after a grace window, and only proceed to the binary copy once no non-installer apra-fleet process remains. Add a regression test (e.g. under tests/) that stubs isApraFleetRunning()/killApraFleet() to model a process that survives the first signal and asserts install escalates/waits rather than proceeding into the copy.
notes:
REOPENED per Opus PR-375 review 2026-08-03: src/cli/install.ts:758 killApraFleet('SIGKILL') -> :702-703 execSync('pkill -9 -x apra-fleet', {stdio:'ignore'}) THROWS when pkill matches nothing (exit code 1, confirmed: execSync('exit 1',{stdio:'ignore'}) throws). If the SIGTERM'd process exits between the liveness check at :755 and the SIGKILL call at :758 -- precisely the 'slow but eventually terminates' case this feature was built to handle -- waitForApraFleetToStop() rejects and runInstall dies with a raw stack trace instead of proceeding to the copy. Needs try/catch around the escalation call; no test currently covers a throwing killApraFleet. Additionally (non-blocking but real): install.ts:686/:702 pgrep/pkill are not user-scoped (-u $(id -u) missing), so on a multi-user host another account's apra-fleet process is detected but cannot be killed, and the new gate at :970-979 now process.exit(1)s where install previously proceeded -- a real regression for multi-member hosts. Windows error text at :973-975 also incorrectly claims 'SIGTERM and a SIGKILL escalation' when both Windows attempts are actually taskkill /F.
TRIAGE: the core issue (fixed 500ms sleep -> ETXTBSY) is already fixed -- waitForApraFleetToStop() (install.ts:774-790) now polls isApraFleetRunning() with SIGKILL escalation. However the REOPENED concern is still live in current code: killApraFleet('SIGKILL') at install.ts:785 and killApraFleet() at install.ts:1012 both call execSync(pkill ...) with no try/catch; pkill exits 1 (execSync throws) when the target already exited between the liveness check and the kill call -- exactly the race this feature exists to handle. Confirmed via read, no test covers a throwing killApraFleet. Classification: LOW-HANGING-FRUIT (well-scoped: wrap both call sites in try/catch treating ESRCH/no-match as success).

title: Add sandbox-lock.mjs Bash prefix to regression playbook Permissions and .claude/settings.json allow-list

Root difficulty: this harness's single-epic-target structure couples a target's verify-eligibility to ALL of its own children being closed, so a 'this one closes, this sibling never does' combination either prevents the closing item from ever reaching verify-eligibility (when both are direct epic children) or introduces prompt-matching ambiguity in the mocked doer (when using a childful sub-item plus a sibling leaf) that made the recorded fixture behave inconsistently across attempts (an unrelated closure crept in from the mocked doer's prompt-substring matching, not the fix under test). Given the underlying logic is a simple two-variable boolean gate (verifyDispatchAttempts > 0 && verifyDispatchClosures === 0) with no state beyond two monotone counters, I verified this branch by direct code review instead of forcing a flaky scenario into the suite -- both counters are exercised by (a) [attempts>0, closures>0 -> gate false, no message at all fires since scenario (a) never stalls] and (b) [attempts>0, closures===0 -> gate true, matches].

comments.text:
Rewritten per independent Opus review (2026-08-04). The original 2 scenarios were non-discriminating (used doer status 'DONE', not in the doer schema enum ['VERIFY','BLOCKED'], so every doer dispatch silently failed schema repair and beads only closed via the mock handler's side-effect bd close call -- the review path was never actually exercised) and scenario (a) exited in Cycle 1 before the fix's effect could matter.

New file: packages/apra-fleet-se/test/66u-stall-progress-credit.test.mjs, 3 scenarios, all real-bd-recorded (test/fixtures/bd-recordings/apra-fleet-mock-sprint-66u3{a,b,c}.jsonl), all verified passing against REAL bd (not just replay) before recording:

(a) A childful verify-routed target (the sprint epic) is deliberately NOT closed by the mocked Integ Test dispatch until its THIRD dispatch -- exactly the cycle at which the pre-fix code's stall net would already have tripped (closedCount never saw the eventual closure; verifyEverIds's one-time high-water credit came 2 cycles earlier). Asserts the sprint completes cleanly and the epic is closed in final bd state. This directly reproduces the real 2026-08-02 incident shape (apra-fleet-eft.52/apra-fleet-vak) end-to-end.

(b) Verify-routed beads dispatched repeatedly with zero closures (genuine verifier failure) still stalls, and the message correctly blames the verifier.

(c) NEW, covers acceptance criterion 3 (previously dropped as too fragile under title-substring prompt matching): a sprint that stalls for a genuinely UNRELATED reason (a sibling task permanently blocked on an out-of-scope dependency that never closes) AFTER a real, earlier verify-closure (a childful sub-target, closed for real by Integ Test in an earlier cycle) does NOT blame the verifier. Built entirely on explicit bead-id parsing of the runner's own "verification-closure: <ids>." prompt clause plus deterministic cycle-count/id-membership logic -- no title-substring matching, which is what made the earlier attempt cross-talk across batched dispatch prompts.

Building these scenarios surfaced two real bugs beyond the original 66u.1/66u.2 scope, both now fixed in runner.js (see 66u.1/66u.2 bd comments for detail):
1. The naive scope-widening alone regressed sprint completion for the common case (a childful --issue target) by also widening the exit-gate queries, not just closedCount -- fixed via a new decomposedParentIds() post-filter applied to openAtGoal/stillOpen/finalOpenAtGoal, restoring pre-fix exit-gate semantics while closedCount keeps the real fix.
2. verifyEverIds had a same-cycle blind spot: a bead becoming verify-eligible mid-cycle (discovered only by the Integ Test dispatch site's own classifyVerifySet call, not the cycle-top Route step) never got recorded, leaving a gap in the exit-gate's stillOpenVerifyIds safety net.
3. The DEFAULT mock integ-test-runner handler (test/helpers/mock-sprint-harness.mjs, used by runOnce() and every scenario without an integHandler override) never actually closed the beads it was asked to verify -- unrealistic vs. a real integ-test-runner's contract. This bug was invisible before 66u.1 (the target was scope-excluded so its non-closure never blocked anything) but became a real, confirmed stall once scope correctly widened. title: [impl] Credit same-cycle Integ Test closures to that cycle progress score
description:

WORK:
1. Confirm by reading the code whether the closed-count read used for stall detection happens BEFORE or AFTER the current cycle's own Integ Test dispatch mutates beads, and whether it reads live bd state or a cached snapshot. Record the finding as a bd comment on this bead (this is the bead's stated first acceptance criterion).
2. Fix so a closure made by the same cycle's Integ Test dispatch is counted in that same cycle's progress score before the stall check runs -- e.g. re-query scoped bead state after the Integ Test phase, and ensure any cross-member D-pull needed to see another member's closures happens first.

- After the fix, a cycle whose Integ Test closes a bead shows an incremented closed count in closedCountHistory for that same cycle.

comments.author: Akhil Kumar
comments.text:
FINDING (acceptance criterion 1): the stale-count bug is NOT a before/after-Integ-Test ordering issue and NOT a stale-cache issue -- the doltPullBefore(orchestratorMember) + live bd query at the Cycle Evaluation closedCount read (runner.js ~8340-8346) already correctly re-pulls and re-queries live state every cycle.

Real root cause: bdListScoped()'s scope-construction (runner.js ~5451-5464) only seeded a --issue target's OWN id into scopeIds when that target was CHILDLESS. A target bead that already has children (e.g. a verify-routed parent shape like eft.52/vak from the real incident, or this sprint's own apra-fleet-66u) was excluded from scopeIds entirely -- its id was never added by the BFS (BFS only adds descendants of visited nodes, never the visited node itself) and the childless-only exemption explicitly kept it out. So bdListScoped('--status=closed --json') could structurally never count that bead as closed, no matter how fresh the underlying bd read was -- its id simply was not part of the set being filtered for.

Confirmed by contrast: classifyVerifySet() (runner.js ~2933) is a parallel standalone copy of the same BFS, but seeds every target's own id UNCONDITIONALLY. That is exactly why the real incident's Route messages correctly classified eft.52/vak as verify-routed (classifyVerifySet saw them fine) while closedCountHistory stayed flat when they closed (bdListScoped could not see the closure at all). Verified against the raw incident log (C:\Users\akhil\.apra-fleet-se\logs\apra-fleet-33c_apra-fleet-jfo_apra-fleet-gd0_apra-fleet-vak_apra-fleet-eft.52_apra-fleet-eft.89-1a9359e0-2e63-4e88-b7ae-c1175fc5dfc5.log): closedCountHistory=[18,20,23,23,23], flat exactly across C3-C5 where eft.52 (C4) and vak (C5) -- both childful targets -- closed.

FIX: widened bdListScoped's seed to unconditionally add every target's own id (matching classifyVerifySet). Safe: readyLeafBeads()'s decomposed-node exclusion is a SEPARATE, independent parentIds-based guard, not dependent on scopeIds construction, so a childful target still never gets treated as directly-dispatchable ready work -- it is just no longer invisible to status-counting queries.

comments.author: Akhil Kumar
comments.text:
Reworked per independent Opus review (2026-08-04): the naive scope-widening alone caused a real regression -- it also widened openAtGoal/stillOpen(dev-loop-exit)/finalOpenAtGoal, making a still-open childful target block sprint completion by TWO mechanisms at once (double-gating with the pre-existing stillOpenVerifyIds/verifyEverIds safety net), confirmed by running the real happy-path scenario against real bd (stalled where it used to exit cleanly) and 65 broken fixture replays.

Fix: added decomposedParentIds() (factored out of readyLeafBeads()'s existing parentIds check) and post-filtered openAtGoal/stillOpen/finalOpenAtGoal through it, restoring their pre-fix exit-gate semantics (a decomposed parent, closed or not, never blocks exit through THESE queries) while closedCount/progressScore keep the scope-widening's real benefit (a childful target's own closure is now visible). Whether a still-open verify-routed target may block exit is owned entirely by the separate, scope-independent stillOpenVerifyIds/verifyEverIds mechanism (apra-fleet-jfo), unchanged in intent.

Also found and fixed a second, independent gap the tests surfaced: verifyEverIds was only updated at the cycle-top Route step, but a bead can become verify-eligible mid-cycle (its last child closes during Develop/Review, discovered by the Integ Test dispatch site's own classifyVerifySet call) -- that path never fed verifyEverIds, leaving a same-cycle blind spot in the exit-gate safety net. Now both call sites feed verifyEverIds.

Also fixed: the pre-sprint validation gate (initialBeads) used raw bdListScoped('--ready --json') instead of readyLeafBeads(), so it silently went dead for the common 'open childful target, no blockers' case -- same fix applied there.

Full real-bd verification: 3/3 new 66u.3 scenarios pass against real bd; the ORIGINAL real happy-path scenario (mock-sprint-happy-path.test.mjs) now passes against real bd too (was genuinely stalling before this fix); full suite in replay mode: 1820 pass / 0 fail (all previously-affected fixtures re-recorded against real bd).

title: Dolt sync never fails the sprint: retry, recovery, bounded degraded path
description:
Scope half 2 of apra-fleet-417 (RELIABILITY). The single dolt-sync module (see sibling feature) must survive concurrent multi-agent dolt push/pull as a NORMAL condition. Product decision, do not relitigate: "do not push during a sprint" is not an acceptable fix; a dolt sync hiccup must never hard-abort an otherwise-healthy sprint.

DONE LOOKS LIKE:
- Transient failures (network, server, lock, timeout) retry with bounded backoff inside the module.
- Genuinely resolvable divergence is reconciled non-destructively.
- Unresolvable cases take a bounded, well-defined DEGRADED-BUT-NON-FATAL path (skip-and-continue with a flagged follow-up bead, or queue-and-retry-later), instead of throwing DoltDivergedError / DoltSyncError up into a sprint abort by default.

title: provision_vcs_auth is wired for exactly ONE call site (Develop's git push) -- Deploy's gh commands and both gh pr create sites have zero proactive or reactive auth recovery
description:
Deep investigation, 2026-08-02, requested explicitly by operator after two real sprint failures both traced to gh CLI auth gaps (fleet-lin-dev1 Set 2, fleet-mac Set 3, same day). Operator's ask: 'we know our workflow has provision_vcs_auth, check if it was ever called in failed workflows... our system should call it both proactively e.g at phase start as well as reactively after any auth failure.' Full call-site mapping below, verified by reading packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js directly plus cross-checking two real sprint logs.

WHAT IS CORRECTLY WIRED (both proactive AND reactive):
Only the Develop (doer) dispatch, via withGitSync's pre/post-dispatch bracket:
  - REACTIVE: onAuthFailure (runner.js ~4873-4877, createVcsAuthSelfHealCallback) is threaded through runGitStep (~614) and runDoltStep (~1141) for G-pull/G-push/D-pull/D-push. Confirmed working live: fleet-mac's log shows 'self-heal: auth failure detected... calling provision_vcs_auth... succeeded... retrying once' during a D-push conflict on 2026-08-02 (Integ Test C1 dispatch window).
  - PROACTIVE: ensureVcsAuthFresh (runner.js 4879-4894, createVcsAuthPreflightCallback) is gated 'only on pushCode' per the code's own comment at line 4881 -- i.e. it fires ONLY when the withGitSync call passes pushCode:true, which only the doer/Develop dispatch does. Confirmed live: fleet-mac's log shows the exact line '[Sync] preflight: ensuring member fleet-mac has a fresh VCS credential before dispatch; calling provision_vcs_auth' exactly 3 times, immediately before Develop C1 R1, Develop C2 R1, and Develop C3 R2 -- never before Deploy, Integ Test, Review, Plan, or Publish-PR in the same log.
  - finalizeAbort() (the sprint-abort path) also threads onAuthFailure through ITS OWN runGitStep/runDoltStep calls (lines 4502, 4513, 4532) -- so a git/dolt-level auth failure during abort handling would self-heal.

WHAT HAS ZERO COVERAGE, NEITHER PROACTIVE NOR REACTIVE:
1. Deploy phase's gh commands (gh run list / gh run download, from deploy.md). These are NOT dispatched via runner.js's own command()/runGitStep system at all -- they are raw Bash commands run by the DEPLOYER AGENT inside its own session, following deploy.md as a runbook. There is structurally no way for runner.js's onAuthFailure/ensureVcsAuthFresh machinery to intercept or heal these today, because they never pass through runner.js's command() layer. This is the exact mechanism that killed the fleet-lin-dev1 sprint on 2026-08-02: gh run list failed 'You are not logged into any GitHub hosts' on every one of 3 cycles, deploy.md's own withGitSync wraps the deployer dispatch with pushCode:false (runner.js ~7607), so it never even got the proactive preflight that Develop gets, let alone a reactive gh-specific heal.
2. gh pr create, Publish-PR success path (runner.js 8795-8813). A raw command() call with failSoft:true, but the code's OWN comment at lines 8791-8793 states: 'Any OTHER failure (auth, network, a real API error...) is NOT swallowed -- it is re-raised as a typed CommandError.' No retry, no self-heal, by explicit original design.
3. gh pr create, finalizeAbort's abort-PR path (runner.js 4560-4584). Same shape, same gap. This is the exact mechanism that killed the fleet-mac sprint on 2026-08-02: after Integ Test C5 genuinely closed the last verify-set bead (apra-fleet-vak), finalizeAbort's own gh pr create failed 'gh auth login' required (exit 4), and that failure was NOT self-healed -- it just threw, and finalizeAbort() itself failed as a result ('[Terminal History] finalizeAbort() failed for this abort... writing the terminal history record with no PR lookup'). See sibling bead apra-fleet-66u for the separate stall-detection bug this run also hit.

RELATIONSHIP TO apra-fleet-647.1 (VCSModule epic): 647.1's proposed shape already includes provisionAuth(member, {scope}) as one of its 4 core services -- this bead's findings are direct, concrete evidence for why that service needs to be the ONLY way any VCS-touching command (git, dolt-via-git, AND gh) gets dispatched, replacing the current situation where 3 of 4 known gh/git call-site classes bypass auth handling entirely. Filed as a child of 647.1 rather than a duplicate, since 647.1 already scopes the general fix; this bead documents the specific evidence and the 3 concrete gaps to close.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:

title: Sprint stall-detection scores progress against stale bead state -- real Integ Test closures in the final cycles never credited, causing a false stalled-abort
description:
Discovered 2026-08-02 via deep log investigation of a real sprint failure (fleet-mac, branch verify/orchestrator-viewer-standalones, sprintId ending -1a9359e0). Full raw evidence (dispatch-level transcripts) is in the orchestrator log at C:\Users\akhil\.apra-fleet-se\logs\apra-fleet-33c_apra-fleet-jfo_apra-fleet-gd0_apra-fleet-vak_apra-fleet-eft.52_apra-fleet-eft.89-1a9359e0-2e63-4e88-b7ae-c1175fc5dfc5.log.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED (verified from real Integ Test dispatch reports, not just the abort message):
This was a verify-only sprint targeting 6 all-children-closed beads (apra-fleet-33c, jfo, gd0, vak, eft.52, eft.89). The verify-set mechanism (apra-fleet-jfo's classifyVerifySet) worked CORRECTLY end to end:
  - C1: 33c, jfo, gd0, vak, eft.89 all genuinely verified (real node --test / npx vitest runs cited, specific files, specific pass counts) and closed. eft.52 genuinely FAILED verification -- direct source inspection confirmed its acceptance criteria (top-level status sorting, goal-based placement, distinct CSS treatment) were NOT implemented -- correctly bounced: gap bug eft.52.1 filed, re-routed to development (per jfo's designed bounce behavior).
  - C2-C3: eft.52.1's sub-tasks implemented and verified (86/86 tests, code-inspected as real, not just coverage).
  - C4: eft.52 re-verified and CLOSED for real (86/86 tests + code inspection of viewer-extensions.mjs STATUS_ORDER and runner.js partitionByGoalMembership()).
  - C5: vak (apparently reopened between C1 and C5, worth separate investigation but not this bug) re-verified and CLOSED for real (73/73 tests).
By the end of C5, all 6 target beads were genuinely closed with real evidence.

THE BUG: the sprint's own stall-detection never credited the C4 and C5 closures. The final abort message states:
  'Closed-count history: [18, 20, 23, 23, 23] (high-water mark on progress score: 28). 5 bead(s) were routed to verify this sprint but never closed -- the verifier may be failing rather than the sprint being genuinely out of work'
The count is FLAT at 23 across C3, C4, and C5 -- despite C4 closing eft.52 and C5 closing vak (both confirmed via the real dispatch transcripts quoted above). Neither closure incremented the progress score used for stall detection. The abort message's own diagnosis ('the verifier may be failing') is actively wrong and misleading -- the verifier succeeded every single time; the bookkeeping that decides whether the sprint made progress did not see it.

Root cause hypothesis (needs confirmation by reading the stall-detection code, not yet done as part of this filing): the progress-score snapshot used for stall detection is likely computed from a stale/cached bead-state read taken before the current cycle's own Integ Test dispatch mutated beads (closed eft.52/vak), rather than re-querying live state AFTER Integ Test's closures land within the same cycle. This would explain why C4's and C5's own closures never showed up in that same cycle's score.

Compounding/secondary factor observed in the same run (tracked separately, do not conflate): right as the stall check fired, the sprint's abort-path PR creation (finalizeAbort -> gh pr create) ALSO failed because gh is not authenticated on fleet-mac -- see the sibling VCS-auth-coverage bead just filed under apra-fleet-647.1. Even without that secondary failure, the stale-progress-score bug alone would still have wrongly declared a stall.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Identify the exact function/line where the stall-detection progress score (closed-count / high-water-mark) is computed and confirm whether it reads live or stale bead state relative to the current cycle's own Integ Test closures.
- Fix so a same-cycle Integ Test closure is credited to that same cycle's progress score before the stall check runs.
- The abort message, when it does fire for a genuine stall, should not claim 'the verifier may be failing' unless the evidence actually supports that (e.g. distinguish 'closed count did not increase' from 'verify-routed beads were dispatched to IntegTest N times with zero closures' -- the current run's dispatches DID close beads, so a correct message would not have said this).
- Regression test: a scripted cycle sequence where Integ Test closes a verify-routed bead in cycle N should show the stall-detection's progress score increase in cycle N, not lag by a cycle or never register.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-09 (backlog reprioritization): ALREADY-FIXED IN CODE, left open only because child 66u.1 (owned by another operator) is still in_progress. All three acceptance criteria are satisfied on origin/main (de48e98c / PR #366, plus follow-up 869845e2). (1) Root cause identified and it was NOT stale-read as hypothesized: the scopeIds BFS seed in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js (~5155-5185) excluded a target's OWN id whenever the target had children, so childful verify-routed targets like eft.52/vak could never be counted by bdListScoped('--status=closed --json') no matter how fresh the read -- hence the flat [.,.,23,23,23] history. The seed is now unconditional, matching classifyVerifySet()'s BFS, with an explicit 66u.1 comment naming the eft.52/vak shape; the closedCount read at runner.js:8151 goes through the cache-invalidating command() wrapper, i.e. live post-Integ-Test state. (2) Abort-message fix landed (see 66u.2, now closed): 'verifier may be failing' is gated on verifyDispatchAttempts > 0 && verifyDispatchClosures === 0. (3) Regression tests landed (see 66u.3, now closed): test/66u-stall-progress-credit.test.mjs, 3/3 green when I ran it today, plus the 66u.5 golden-transcript pin. Recommended action: close this parent as soon as 66u.1's owner closes it; no further engineering work is outstanding here.

title: [epic] fleet-sprint dolt sync must be fault-tolerant: single reusable never-fail sync function used at every call site in runner.js
description:
Trigger: 2026-08-02, verify sprint on fleet-win-dev1 (branch verify/dispatch-execute-prompt-reliability) hard-aborted with DoltDivergedError (DOLT_DIVERGED) at runner.js:1247 (doltPullBefore), root-caused to a concurrent 'bd dolt push' from the orchestrator machine racing the sprint's own D-pull/D-push bracket while fleet-win-dev1 also carried stale local Dolt state from an earlier interrupted dispatch. See apra-fleet chat log 2026-08-02 for the full timeline/evidence.

Explicit product decision (per operator, do not relitigate): concurrent multi-agent/multi-user dolt push/pull/merge is a NORMAL, EXPECTED condition, not a misuse case to be avoided by process discipline ('don't push during a sprint' is not an acceptable fix). fleet-sprint must be fault-tolerant to it. Even in the worst case, a dolt sync hiccup must not fail the sprint.

Scope -- two intertwined halves, both required:
1) REFACTOR: runner.js currently calls dolt pull/push from multiple, likely-inconsistent call sites (at least doltPullBefore ~line 1247, plus whatever doltPushAfter and any other D-pull/D-push bracket call sites exist -- full inventory is part of this work, see below). Consolidate into ONE reusable dolt-sync function (or small cohesive module) that every call site in runner.js goes through -- no call site should hand-roll its own bd dolt pull/push/merge-conflict handling.
2) RELIABILITY: that single function must handle real-world concurrent-write conditions (races, transient divergence, retryable conflicts) WITHOUT failing the sprint in the worst case -- retry/backoff for transient issues, safe non-destructive recovery paths where the conflict is actually resolvable, and a bounded, well-defined degraded-but-non-fatal path (e.g. skip-and-continue with a flagged follow-up bead, or queue-and-retry-later) for the cases that truly cannot be auto-resolved. 'Throw and hard-abort the whole sprint' should no longer be the only outcome of a beads-sync hiccup.

Related existing infrastructure to build on / reconcile with, not duplicate:
- apra-fleet-vkc (+ vkc.1, vkc.2): an existing dolt-recovery ladder (dolt-recovery.mjs, dolt-recovery-path-b.mjs, dolt-recovery-tier2.mjs) already exists but is UNWIRED into doltPushAfter(). Decide whether this refactor supersedes, completes, or formally decommissions that ladder -- do not build a second, competing recovery mechanism.
- apra-fleet-spp: DoltDivergedError retry ladder currently mislabels a git-credential failure as data divergence -- the new single sync function's error classification must not repeat this.
- apra-fleet-xuo.1: pending Dolt operator runbook -- the new function's behavior/limits should be documented there too.
- apra-fleet-eft.17.3: known gap where D-pull gating skips 'bd dolt pull' entirely in a no-remote scratch dir -- the consolidated function must handle this path correctly too, not just the common case.

Acceptance criteria (initial -- refine during design):
- A single, named, documented dolt-sync function (or tightly-scoped module) exists in fleet-sprint/ and is the ONLY place runner.js issues 'bd dolt pull' / 'bd dolt push' / merge-conflict handling.
- Every existing call site in runner.js is migrated to it; a test or lint-style check prevents new call sites from bypassing it.
- A genuine, concurrent-write-induced dolt conflict (transient or real) no longer hard-aborts an otherwise-healthy sprint by default -- there is a defined non-fatal degraded path.
- Existing dolt-recovery.mjs/path-b/tier2 infrastructure is either wired in, or explicitly and deliberately decommissioned as part of this change (not left orphaned a second time).
- Regression coverage for at least: transient pull timeout (seen 2026-08-02), genuine unmergeable issues-table conflict (seen 2026-08-02), no-remote scratch dir (eft.17.3), and the git-credential-vs-divergence misclassification (spp).

This bead intentionally does not yet contain the full call-site inventory or the detailed design -- that is being filled in next by a dedicated design pass over runner.js.
notes:
Second, distinct failure observed same day (2026-08-02, ~16:14 UTC): verify sprint on fleet-lin-dev1 (branch verify/ssh-pool-supervisor-epic) hard-aborted on 'bd dolt push', NOT pull -- root cause was a git-credential failure on that member's Dolt remote (HTTPS, no non-interactive credential helper configured), not a real merge conflict:
  Error: push to origin/main: Error 1105: unknown push error; addTableFiles, updateManifestAddFiles: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet.git': No such device or address
This is exactly the failure class apra-fleet-spp already names (auth failures getting mislabeled/handled the same as data divergence). Confirms the consolidated sync function's error classification must distinguish at minimum: (a) transient/network, (b) real unmergeable data conflict, (c) credential/auth misconfiguration -- each needs a different non-fatal response, not one blanket hard-abort path. Two independent sprints failed on two different D-sync steps (pull vs push) within the same 20-minute window, both while a third concurrent sprint (fleet-mac) was still running -- reinforces this is a systemic concurrency/reliability gap, not a one-off.
=== DESIGN PASS (2026-08-02) -- section 1/4: COMPLETE CALL-SITE INVENTORY ===
Source: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js at 7ddb093a (branch chore/integration-binary-fixes-and-auth-selfheal). Line numbers from this revision.

CORE PLUMBING (the only code that spawns `bd dolt *` today):
- classifyDoltFailure() L1058: SEVEN kinds, checked in order: no-remote, empty-remote, remote-unreachable, diverged, auth, transient, unknown (pattern tables L932-1022). Note: 'auth' already exists as a distinct class.
- runDoltStep() L1141: retries ONLY 'transient', IMMEDIATELY (no sleep, no backoff), up to maxTransientRetries (default 1 at every caller, never overridden anywhere). On 'auth' + an injected onAuthFailure: one self-heal (provision_vcs_auth) then exactly one retry. Everything else returns to caller.
- doltPullBefore() L1207: sync.remote pre-gate (positively-confirmed-absent -> benign skip, the eft.17.3 path); skipPull hook. Failure routing: no-remote/empty-remote -> benign skip; diverged -> throw DoltDivergedError at L1247 (the 2026-08-02 fleet-win-dev1 abort); remote-unreachable -> DoltSyncError L1254; anything else -> DoltSyncError L1259.
- preflightBeadsHealthGate() L1319: wraps doltPullBefore, rewrites a diverged message with workspace + conflicting tables, rethrows DoltDivergedError.
- doltPushAfter() L1393: sync.remote pre-gate; GLOBAL push mutex acquire/release around the push (L1419-1432); on 'diverged' exactly one reconcile pull + one re-push; no-remote -> skip; remote-unreachable/other -> DoltSyncError; reconcile-pull diverged -> DoltDivergedError L1485; re-push still failing -> DoltDivergedError L1505 REGARDLESS OF KIND (see inconsistency 4).
- syncMemberAfterOrdered() L1540: G-push then D-push (L1555); D-push skipped entirely if G-push throws.
- verifyDoerStreakClosed() L2396: doltPullBefore at L2399 then `bd show`.
- withGitSync() L5019: pre-dispatch doltPullBefore L5031; post-dispatch syncMemberAfterOrdered L5074 retried on delays [0, 5s, 15s] (POST_DISPATCH_SYNC_RETRY_DELAYS_MS L14), then wrapped as PostDispatchSyncError.

CALL SITES AND CURRENT FAILURE BEHAVIOR:

A. Per-dispatch member brackets (withGitSync -- every agent dispatch: planner, plan-reviewer, doer, reviewer, deployer, integ-test, regression, harvester):
- A1 L5031 D-pull pre-dispatch. onAuthFailure IS wired. Throw propagates to per-phase handlers (inconsistent, below).
- A2 L5074 -> L1555 D-push post-dispatch (pushBeads roles). onAuthFailure wired. Whole-sync retried 3x with backoff, then PostDispatchSyncError (dispatch result preserved; never redispatched).
Downstream handling of an A1/A2 throw differs per phase:
- Reviewer rounds L5332-5358: GitSyncError/DoltSyncError degrade to a synthesized CHANGES_NEEDED verdict (non-fatal); DoltDivergedError deliberately excluded -> propagates -> typed abort.
- Doer streaks: ANY throw out of a worklist branch (including DoltDivergedError) is swallowed by parallel(..., {continueOnError:true}) (apra-fleet-workflow src/workflow/index.mjs L1449-1453) -> streak recorded 'failed', sprint continues. A typed abort class is thus silently downgraded here and nowhere else.
- PostDispatchSyncError from a completed doer turn: L7139-7148 non-fatal, work kept, no redispatch.
- Regression phase L8485-8539: deliberate catch-all -> ALL dolt failures including DoltDivergedError are non-fatal. This is the ONE already-fault-tolerant site, and its comment block is a good statement of the target policy.
- Planner and other orchestrator-driven dispatches: no dolt-specific catch -> propagate to main() -> terminal.

B. Orchestrator-clone sites -- ALL hard-fatal on throw (no local catch; DoltDivergedError -> isTypedAbortError L4365 -> verdict ABORTED, terminalReason BEADS_SYNC_CONFLICT + conflictDump via k7b.4 machinery; DoltSyncError -> isTerminalSprintFailure -> terminal failure record; either way the run dies):

Exception: these calls sit inside doer-streak branches, so a throw is swallowed by continueOnError -- and the streak (with its genuinely-closed beads) is then MISREPORTED as failed off an unverifiable read.

C. Recovery modules issue `bd dolt pull/push` themselves (dolt-recovery.mjs L296/L303, dolt-recovery-path-b.mjs L303) -- but nothing in runner.js imports any of them (unwired; apra-fleet-vkc).

KEY INCONSISTENCIES (the refactor target):
1. Auth self-heal is wired ONLY at A1/A2. All B-sites omit onAuthFailure, so the identical credential failure self-heals inside a member bracket but hard-kills the sprint at any of the 11 orchestrator sites. This is exactly apra-fleet-spp / IN-11 and the fleet-lin-dev1 abort class.
2. Retry posture: A2 gets [0,5s,15s] whole-bracket retries ON TOP of runDoltStep's single immediate transient retry; every B-site gets only the single immediate retry, zero backoff.
3. One error class, three outcomes: DoltDivergedError = typed abort (B-sites, planner bracket), silently-swallowed failed streak (doer branches), fully non-fatal (regression phase).
4. doltPushAfter's post-reconcile re-push throw (L1496-1508) does NOT re-classify: ANY second failure -- auth, transient-exhausted, remote-unreachable, unknown -- is thrown as DoltDivergedError "still rejected after one reconcile pull" and lands as BEADS_SYNC_CONFLICT. This is the spp bug and it is STILL PRESENT even though runDoltStep now classifies 'auth' (the classification is discarded on this path).
5. Push-mutex acquire failures (createHttpDoltPushMutexClient L1582+ / createMcpDoltPushMutexClient L1757+) throw raw Error out of doltPushAfter -- not a WorkflowError, so main() treats it as an untyped crash (watchdog reports CRASHED, no terminal record). Unclassified failure mode.
6. maxTransientRetries default 1 is the de facto global policy; no site tunes it, no jitter, no delay.
=== DESIGN PASS (2026-08-02) -- section 2/4: FAILURE TAXONOMY + WHY LIN-DEV1 DID NOT SELF-HEAL ===

FAILURE TAXONOMY (grounded in classifyDoltFailure L1058 + the two 2026-08-02 incidents), with the fault-tolerant response each class should get from the consolidated function:

1. transient (network/server/lock; includes the observed pull timeout): retry in place with real backoff + jitter (proposal: 3 attempts at ~2s/8s/30s, bounded total wall clock <= ~90s per op). On exhaustion -> DEGRADED (ledger, below), not fatal. Today: 1 immediate retry then fatal DoltSyncError.
2. auth (credential misconfiguration -- the fleet-lin-dev1 class): one provision_vcs_auth self-heal + one retry (already implemented in runDoltStep), wired at EVERY site; if heal is unavailable or the retry still fails -> DEGRADED. Never DoltDivergedError, never fatal.
3. diverged-resolvable (push rejected non-fast-forward; single-row issues-table conflict): mechanical reconcile pull + re-push (exists), then scripted Path A resolve-in-place (dolt-recovery.mjs, verified, exactly the win-dev1 conflict shape). Success -> synced; failure -> DEGRADED.
4. diverged-unresolvable (multi-row/multi-table/schema conflict): NOT a sprint abort. Enter beads-island mode for that clone: stop syncing it, keep operating on local beads state, record a BEADS_SYNC_DEGRADED ledger entry with the conflict dump (reuse captureDoltConflictDump/recordWedgedState), file a follow-up bead LOCALLY (safe: a local bd create rides the next successful push), surface prominently in the final summary/terminal record. Sprint completes; publication is deferred to repair()/operator/Tier 2.
5. remote-unreachable (configured remote points at a dead path/URL): no retry (already correct) -> DEGRADED instead of fatal DoltSyncError.
6. no-remote / empty-remote: benign skip (already correct -- keep byte-for-byte, including the sync.remote pre-gate; this is the eft.17.3 no-remote scratch-dir path and it must stay transcript-deterministic for the golden-transcript suites).
7. coordination-unavailable (NEW class): push-mutex acquire error/timeout, supervisor/fleet unreachable. Today an unclassified raw-Error crash. Response: log loudly, proceed with ONE unguarded push attempt (the mutex is a conflict-probability optimization, not a correctness gate -- the reconcile path is the actual defense), or skip-and-mark-dirty. Never fatal.
8. unknown: one bounded retry then DEGRADED (fail toward degradation, never abort).

Pattern-table fixes to fold in: DOLT_TRANSIENT_PATTERNS contains bare /lock/i (over-broad; can misclassify arbitrary text); DOLT_DIVERGED contains /failed to push/ and diverged is checked BEFORE auth, so an auth failure whose stderr also carries rejection text burns the reconcile as a false divergence -- prefer structural matching (Error 1105 sub-text) and check pure-credential markers before generic rejection text.

WHY DEGRADED-NOT-FATAL IS SAFE (the key mechanical fact): `bd dolt push` publishes the WHOLE DB state, so a failed D-push is naturally self-healing -- the next successful push at any later sync point publishes everything the failed one would have. "Queue-and-retry" therefore needs no literal queue: mark the clone dirty-unpublished, retry opportunistically at every subsequent sync point, and run one final flush at sprint end. A failed D-pull is different: it means READS MAY BE STALE, and callers must see that fact -- verifyDoerStreakClosed must treat a degraded pull as verification-INCONCLUSIVE (never mark streaks failed off stale reads; today's continueOnError swallow does exactly that damage), while cycle-eval/final counts proceed on last-known state with an annotation.

OPERATOR Q1: WHY DID fleet-lin-dev1 NOT SELF-HEAL VIA provision_vcs_auth?
Answer: the reactive self-heal EXISTS but was never wired into the failing call site class.
- What exists: createVcsAuthSelfHealCallback (runner.js L2084) -> provisionVcsAuthForMember -> fleet MCP tool provision_vcs_auth (src/tools/provision-vcs-auth.ts; github-app or PAT, owner/repo derived from the member's own git remote, connectivity-tested). runDoltStep invokes it on an 'auth' classification: one heal, one retry (L1155-1166). There is ALSO a proactive preflight (createVcsAuthPreflightCallback L2129 / ensureVcsAuthFresh) that re-provisions before code-writing dispatches when a cached credential is missing/expiring. Same retry-once shape as the 6a7 workspace_not_trusted precedent. Unit tests prove both directions (dolt-sync-brackets: "self-heal success", "self-heal called but retry STILL fails", "omitting onAuthFailure preserves byte-identical behavior").
- The gap: onAuthFailure is threaded ONLY through withGitSync's member brackets (A1/A2). None of the 11 orchestrator-side sites (B1-B11, incl. all six doltPushAfter calls and verifyDoerStreakClosed's pull) pass it, so classifyDoltFailure('auth') falls straight through to a fatal DoltSyncError/DoltDivergedError. lin-dev1's stderr ("could not read Username for 'https://github.com/...'") matches DOLT_AUTH_PATTERNS L980 and WOULD have healed had the callback been threaded. Secondary gap: even where wired, the post-reconcile re-push (L1496-1508) throws DoltDivergedError without re-classifying, so an auth failure surfacing only on the re-push is still mislabeled divergence (the fleet-mac/spp incident shape).
- Tool scope (read, not assumed): provision_vcs_auth is an ORCHESTRATOR-side fleet MCP tool, invoked through args.callTool against a NAMED member; it provisions credentials ON that member and tests them. It is not callable from inside a member's own dispatch (members hold no fleet MCP connection). Remediation therefore belongs exactly where the consolidated sync function lives: orchestrator-side, member-parameterized.
- Design of the remediation step in the new function: trigger = 'auth' classification on any dolt op for member M; action = injected remediate(M) (default: createVcsAuthSelfHealCallback when args.callTool exists, else no-op); retry = exactly one re-run of the failed op after a successful heal; storm control = at most one heal per op PLUS a module-level per-member cooldown (lastHealAt map, e.g. no repeat heal within 10 min -- matches VCS_AUTH_EXPIRY_PREFLIGHT_MS) so a genuinely broken credential cannot trigger a provision loop across the sprint's many sync points; on second consecutive auth failure -> mark member auth-degraded in the ledger and stop attempting pushes for it until repair()/flush().
=== DESIGN PASS (2026-08-02) -- section 3/4: PROPOSED MODULE (TaskDB evaluation) + RECOVERY-LADDER DISPOSITION ===

OPERATOR Q2: single function vs coarse-grained TaskDBModule?
Verdict: the epic's "single reusable function" DOES undersell what is needed, for two concrete reasons found in the code: (a) the call sites split cleanly into FOUR distinct intents (sprint-start readiness; refresh-before-orchestrator-read; sync-around-a-member-dispatch; publish-after-orchestrator-mutation) whose degraded-path semantics differ (a stale READ needs "inconclusive" handling; a failed PUBLISH needs "dirty, retry later"); and (b) the never-fail policy requires STATE that must persist across calls -- the degradation ledger, dirty-unpublished flags, per-member auth-heal cooldowns, the mutex client, retry budgets. That is an object/module boundary, not a function. HOWEVER: do NOT sweep the entire bd surface (bdListScoped, fetchAllBeadsShared, bd update/create/note, the child-id allocator) into a TaskDBModule in this epic -- that is a far larger refactor across ~100 command() sites, and the incidents implicate only the SYNC boundary. Recommendation: a coarse-grained sync-owning module now, named so it can grow into the full TaskDB faсade later.

PROPOSED SHAPE -- packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/task-db-sync.mjs, `createTaskDbSync(deps) -> taskDb`:
- ensureReady() -- sprint-start gate (replaces preflightBeadsHealthGate + pre-sprint pull): pull, full recovery ladder on conflict, and the ONE place a start-time abort may still be permitted (open operator decision, section 4).
- refreshView({purpose}) -- orchestrator D-pull before any beads read (replaces B2/B3/B7/B9). NEVER throws; returns { fresh: boolean, degraded?: {kind, error} } so verifyDoerStreakClosed can go "inconclusive" instead of failing streaks, and cycle-eval/final counts can annotate staleness.
- syncBefore(member, {skipPull}) -- pre-dispatch pull (replaces A1). Never throws; degraded result.
- syncAfter(member, {mutatedBeads}) -- D-push including mutex, reconcile, Path A, ledger update (replaces A2's D-half and B4/B5/B6/B8/B10). Never throws.
- flush() -- end-of-sprint: final push attempt for every dirty clone (absorbs B11), then returns the degradation report the terminal summary/follow-up bead is built from.
- repair(member) -- the explicit remediation entry point: full ladder (Path A -> optional Path B -> Tier 2 escalation) + provision_vcs_auth; used by operators/tools and by ensureReady; NOT called inline from per-op sync paths beyond Path A.
- status() -- ledger snapshot for dashboard/final summary.
Internals the module owns exclusively: classifyDoltFailure + pattern tables, runDoltStep with backoff/jitter, auth remediation + cooldown, mutex-client selection (http/mcp/no-op) and coordination-failure downgrade, the recovery ladder, the per-member ledger { dirtyUnpublished, degradedSince, lastErrorKind, lastError, healAttempts, wedgedState? }, and follow-up-bead filing. Constructor deps: { command, log, sprintId, onAuthFailure|callTool, mutexClient?, agent? (tier2, optional), config }. Error contract: methods return typed result objects; the only remaining throws are programmer errors (missing command()) and -- if the operator so decides -- ensureReady's time-zero unrecovered divergence. runner.js then contains ZERO `bd dolt` literals and zero dolt failure-mode knowledge.
Compatibility: keep doltPullBefore/doltPushAfter exported as thin deprecated wrappers during migration (dolt-sync-brackets.test.mjs and friends import them heavily), fold the tests over as the last step.
(Per repo convention: no fleet MCP tool schemas change in this work, so no packages/apra-fleet-client update is triggered; if repair() is ever exposed as an MCP tool later, the client must be updated in that same change.)

DISPOSITION OF THE EXISTING RECOVERY LADDER (resolves apra-fleet-vkc / vkc.1 / vkc.2): WIRE IT -- as an INTERNAL implementation detail of taskDbSync, not a separately-wired competing mechanism. Per-piece:
- Path A (dolt-recovery.mjs): sound, tightly gated (single-row, issues-table allowlist), verified 2026-07-16, and matches the exact win-dev1 conflict shape. Becomes the diverged-resolvable tier invoked from syncAfter/ensureReady when a pull/reconcile classifies as a genuine merge conflict (isDoltPullConflict). CRITICAL WIRING GAP FOUND (very likely WHY it was never wired): Path A/B require sql(), spawnSqlServer(), readMetadata()/writeMetadata(), fs removePath() -- LOCAL-process APIs. runner.js reaches members only through command() with member_name, and members can be remote. As written, the ladder can only run against the orchestrator's OWN clone. Plan: phase 1 wires it orchestrator-local (covers every B-site, i.e. both 2026-08-02 aborts); phase 2 repackages Path A/B behind a member-side entrypoint (e.g. a `fleet-sprint dolt-recover --path a|b --strategy theirs` bin subcommand shipped in the package/SEA binary) that taskDbSync invokes via command() -- file this phase-2 as its own bead under 417.
- Path B (dolt-recovery-path-b.mjs): keep, but strictly opt-in config, default OFF, and reachable only from repair() -- it is destructive (discard + re-bootstrap) and its pendingMutation replay contract assumes the caller knows the one pending local write, which the runner generally does not (pass null -> enumerate-and-discard). Mid-sprint, beads-island degradation is strictly safer than destructive recovery.
- Tier 2 (dolt-recovery-tier2.mjs): keep the module; call ONLY from repair() or post-sprint -- an 1800s agent dispatch inline inside a D-push bracket would wreck pacing and budget. Its recordWedgedState() IS reused inline: a degraded ledger entry embeds the wedged-state record, so the escalation evidence is captured at failure time even though the dispatch happens later.
- vkc.2's test lands as the wire-branch variant; its decommission-branch "prove absent" alternative dies. The static-check idea inverts into the no-new-call-sites guard (section 4).
=== DESIGN PASS (2026-08-02) -- section 4/4: MIGRATION PLAN + TEST PLAN + OPEN DECISIONS ===

MIGRATION PLAN (each step independently green):
1. Introduce task-db-sync.mjs wrapping the CURRENT bracket logic verbatim behind the new API + ledger. Fix inside it immediately: (a) re-classify the post-reconcile re-push by kind before throwing (kills the spp mislabel at L1505); (b) thread auth remediation through every internal step; (c) classify mutex failures as coordination-unavailable and downgrade; (d) real backoff+jitter on transient.
2. Migrate the six orchestrator D-push sites (B4 L6386, B5 L6628, B6 L7548, B8 L8115, B10 L8381, B11 L8762) to taskDb.syncAfter(orchestratorMember) (B11 folds into flush()). One-line changes, biggest reliability win: these all become non-fatal + self-healing.
3. Migrate orchestrator D-pulls (B2 L5738, B7 L7948, B9 L8173) to refreshView(); thread the degraded flag into cycle-eval/final-review log lines.
4. Migrate verifyDoerStreakClosed to refreshView() with inconclusive semantics -- fixes the false-failed-streak swallow (B3).
5. Migrate withGitSync (A1/A2) to syncBefore/syncAfter; retire POST_DISPATCH_SYNC_RETRY_DELAYS_MS for the D-half (module policy owns it). NOTE: syncMemberAfterOrdered's G-before-D ordering and "skip D-push when G-push throws" (unreachable-close guard) stays in withGitSync -- the module replaces only the D-half; PostDispatchSyncError remains for the git side.
6. Migrate B1 preflight to ensureReady() per the operator decision below.
7. Update terminal routing: isTypedAbortError's dolt arm narrows to whatever ensureReady may still throw; k7b.4/k7b.8 semantics move from "mid-sprint abort with BEADS_SYNC_CONFLICT" to "sprint completes; terminal record carries a BEADS_SYNC_DEGRADED summary + conflict dump". Add the guard test: runner.js contains no `bd dolt` literal and does not import runDoltStep -- only task-db-sync.mjs does (the epic's no-new-call-sites check).

TEST PLAN. Existing coverage to keep green (some assertions deliberately flip): dolt-sync-brackets.test.mjs (bracket unit paths, pre-gates, benign skips, auth self-heal x3), dolt-remote-unreachable.test.mjs (run-24 pins), error-classification-routing-table.test.mjs, k7b4/k7b8 (terminal classification -- will be REWRITTEN per step 7), mock-sprint-planner-dpush-failure-no-redispatch, mock-sprint-beads-health-gate-diverged/empty-remote, dolt-sync-discipline (pushBeads role matrix, mutex serialization, real Path A/B behind DOLT_SKIP, tier-2 escalation), dolt-recovery-path-a/b/tier2 unit suites (all three exist and are healthy -- the ladder is tested, just unwired).
Net-new regression coverage (the epic's four + inventory findings):
1. Transient pull timeout mid-sprint (2026-08-02 class): sprint COMPLETES; backoff observed; ledger clean after eventual success.
2. Genuine unmergeable issues-table conflict, on D-pull AND on D-push reconcile: single-row -> Path A resolves in place, push succeeds; multi-row -> degraded, sprint completes, terminal summary carries BEADS_SYNC_DEGRADED + conflict dump + follow-up bead.
3. No-remote scratch dir (eft.17.3): identical command transcript mock vs real; regenerate the golden once the module lands -- coordinate with eft.17.3.1/.2, do not duplicate.
4. Auth-vs-divergence (spp): auth on first push -> heal + retry succeeds; heal fails -> degraded, NOT DoltDivergedError; auth surfacing only on the post-reconcile re-push -> still classified auth (pin against the L1505 mislabel); auth at an orchestrator site heals (previously unwired).
5. Mutex acquire failure -> coordination-degraded, no crash, push still lands (or is marked dirty).
6. Degraded verify pull -> streaks NOT marked failed (inconclusive path), re-verified at next sync point.
7. flush(): a push that failed mid-sprint is published in full by a later successful push / the end-of-sprint flush (whole-DB-push property).
8. The no-new-call-sites static guard test.

OTHER FINDINGS WORTH RECORDING:
- parallel(continueOnError:true) silently swallowing typed aborts from doer branches is a pre-existing latent inconsistency; this design converts it from accident to explicit recorded policy.
- B11 means a fully-green sprint can currently die at the finish line on a beads push -- worth a release-note line when fixed.
- The global push mutex only coordinates sprints sharing a supervisor/fleet server; the win-dev1 race came from an operator-machine `bd dolt push` entirely outside mutex scope. Locking can never cover ad-hoc writers -- reconcile + recovery is the real defense, which supports the never-fail posture.
- Cross-links: apra-fleet-f34 (serviceUrl wiring, closed), the glv/fmu reactive VCS self-heal beads, apra-fleet-9ta.7 (routing table), k7b.4/k7b.8, eft.17.3.1/.2, 3pb.1/xuo.1 (runbooks -- document degraded mode + repair() there; xuo.1 is still uncommitted).

OPEN OPERATOR DECISIONS (explicit sign-off wanted before implementation):
1. ensureReady() at time zero: (A) allow a start-time HARD FAIL on an unrecovered genuine divergence -- nothing is invested yet, it is the cheapest moment to repair, and dispatching doers on unpullable stale scope risks duplicate work; or (B) strict never-fail: proceed in beads-island mode from birth. Recommendation: A as default (recovery ladder attempted first), with a --force-degraded/config override for B. The epic's wording ("even in the worst case... must not fail the sprint") can be read either way for a sprint that has not started; please rule.
2. Path B default-off (destructive discard + re-bootstrap only via repair()/opt-in config) -- confirm.
3. Tier 2 agent escalation policy: allowed when? (post-sprint only vs during flush), which model tier, budget cap.
4. Follow-up bead granularity: one summary bead per sprint listing all degradations (recommended -- avoids bead spam from a flapping remote) vs one bead per degradation event.
Architectural guidance from operator (2026-08-02): use a 'skin-gut' split for BOTH TaskDBModule and its sibling VCSModule refactor -- each module's public surface (the 'skin': the interface/contract runner.js calls) must be kept separate from its concrete backend implementation (the 'gut': the dolt-specific logic for TaskDBModule, the github-specific logic for VCSModule). The dolt/beads implementation details must be fully hidden behind the TaskDBModule interface, not leaked into its call signature or return shapes, so that a different task-tracking backend (Jira, Azure DevOps, generic git-issues, etc.) could be swapped in as an alternate concrete implementation of the same interface without runner.js changing at all. This is a hard design constraint on the module boundary, not just an implementation-quality nicety -- the module's public API must be provider-agnostic in naming and shape (e.g. no dolt-specific concepts like 'D-pull'/'D-push' terminology or dolt error codes leaking through the interface), even though today only one concrete (dolt) implementation exists. Apply the same skin-gut split to the sibling VCSModule refactor (github-specific logic hidden behind a provider-agnostic VCS interface, swappable for Bitbucket/Azure DevOps/etc.) -- both modules should follow the same interface/implementation separation pattern for consistency.
Planner (2026-08-03, re-planning pass): carry-over triage. bd search "[carry-over]" returned 7 open beads (2cf, mnd, x1c, t91, w5j, 542, p8o); read each. NONE adopted into this sprint: all 7 are test-harness/infrastructure defects (bd init templating collision, sandbox-seed bd init on Windows, sprint-lock release + bd-replay fixture drift in the slow lane, real-bd suite timeouts/budget, sandbox HOME deletion) and none touches this sprint's subject matter -- dolt-sync consolidation/fault tolerance (417.2/417.3), stall-progress scoring (66u), or VCS auth/provider abstraction (647.1). They remain parent-less for a later sprint; none closed. Also added apra-fleet-647.1.5 (+.5.1/.5.2) to cover 647.1's one unowned acceptance criterion: 'adding a new provider requires touching no file under fleet-sprint/' -- vcs-module.mjs still holds a provider-keyed DEFAULT_AUTH_MODES table, contradicting it.
apra-fleet-417.1 (2026-08-03): TaskDBModule backend-neutral interface contract ADR is committed at docs/adr-taskdb-backend-neutral-interface.md (commit 073a1dd, branch feat/taskdb-vcs-module-auth-abstraction). It names the seven-method neutral contract (ensureReady / refreshView / syncBefore / syncAfter / flush / repair / status, plus capabilities()), records the interface-vs-adapter split for dolt-sync.mjs, renames skipPull -> skipRefresh, mutatedBeads -> mutatedItemIds, healthGate -> readinessGate, walks Jira as the named second backend method by method, and adopts the 647.1-equivalent criterion: 'adding a new task-tracking backend requires touching no file under packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/ other than adding one new concrete module.' Option (b) chosen over (a); rationale in Decision 1. 417.2.x should build against that doc.
NEEDS-DEEPER-DESIGN (epic, kept open, not closed by this triage). Substantial completion already landed: dolt-sync.mjs now owns every 'bd dolt' call site in runner.js (commits 7c59595c/78ae6f4f/417.2.1), classification+backoff+degraded-path landed (2fd3490c/417.3.1), the backend-neutral ADR is committed (e80e25d9/417.1), and the recovery ladder is wired per vkc.1's disposition. However bd show shows this epic is still OPEN with real remaining children: apra-fleet-66u (+66u.1 in_progress, 66u.3 open) covering stall-detection scoring, which per the epic's own notes has an operator action item flagging 66u.1 as a likely-stale claim (started_at==updated_at, no bd comment despite AC#1 requiring one) blocking the ready lane. This triage batch only covers the vkc/spp/417.4 slice of this epic's scope, all of which are done -- the epic itself should stay open pending 66u's resolution and is out of scope for further disposition here beyond this status note. Subsystem: dolt-sync/epic-tracking.

title: [integ] npm-installed 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint' cannot resolve @apralabs/apra-fleet-client -- fleet server connectivity permanently unavailable
description:
Feature: apra-fleet-kuh
Expected: per acceptance criteria + bead title ('...so apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint works everywhere'), the unified command works identically for npm-installed users, including the fleet MCP server / dolt-mutex / id-allocator connectivity that real sprints depend on.
Actual: verified end-to-end against HEAD 45ce53f3 with a real published-shape install (npm pack -> tgz -> npm install <tgz> into a clean project, NOT a workspace symlink): 'apra-fleet install' + 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint --help' DOES succeed and print real help text (that specific literal acceptance line passes). However, running the workflow (or 'node -e' importing directly) shows: '[warn] could not resolve the fleet server: Cannot find package @apralabs/apra-fleet-client imported from .../node_modules/@apralabs/apra-fleet/dist/cli/workflow.js'. Root cause: root package.json ships packages/apra-fleet-client/src/ and packages/apra-fleet-client/package.json via the 'files' allowlist, but never registers '@apralabs/apra-fleet-client' as an actual root 'dependencies' entry (or otherwise makes it resolvable via node module resolution outside the npm workspace). In the git-checkout dev tree this works transparently because npm workspaces symlinks packages/apra-fleet-client into node_modules/@apralabs/apra-fleet-client; that symlink does not exist for a real npm-installed consumer, so 'import("@apralabs/apra-fleet-client/server-resolution")' throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND unconditionally for every npm-installed user. This silently forces every npm-installed real sprint into the no-op dolt-mutex/id-allocator degraded path (concurrent-push conflict risk, duplicate child ids) with no clear user-facing error beyond a warning at startup.
Test: manual real end-to-end repro (not a [test] task -- kuh.4 only asserts --help works, which does pass; this is a functional gap beyond that literal assertion): 'npm pack --pack-destination <tmp>', 'npm install <tmp>/apralabs-apra-fleet-0.4.0.tgz' into a scratch project, then 'node -e "import(\'@apralabs/apra-fleet-client/server-resolution\').catch(e=>console.log(e.message))"' -> 'Cannot find package @apralabs/apra-fleet-client'. Confirmed absent in dev-checkout mode (works fine there via workspace symlink) -- this is npm-install-path-specific.
Repro: 1) npm pack --pack-destination /tmp/x  2) mkdir /tmp/proj && cd /tmp/proj && npm init -y && npm install /tmp/x/apralabs-apra-fleet-0.4.0.tgz  3) npx apra-fleet install  4) npx apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint --help  -> observe the '[warn] could not resolve the fleet server' line. Fix direction: add '@apralabs/apra-fleet-client' to root package.json 'dependencies' with a resolvable version/path (e.g. workspace: protocol or a published version), or otherwise ensure the shipped packages/apra-fleet-client/src is reachable via a real node module resolution path for a non-workspace npm consumer.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-09 (batch xuo-kuh): ALREADY-FIXED -- verified by real published-shape repro on HEAD (v0.4.1), not by inspection. Ran 'npm pack --pack-destination $TEMP/kuhtest/pack' -> apralabs-apra-fleet-0.4.1.tgz -> 'npm init -y && npm install <tgz>' into a clean scratch project (NOT a workspace symlink) -> 'node -e import("@apralabs/apra-fleet-client/server-resolution")' printed RESOLVED OK (no ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND), and 'node node_modules/@apralabs/apra-fleet/dist/index.js workflow fleet-sprint --help' printed the engine's real help text and did NOT print the '[warn] could not resolve the fleet server' line (it printed '[workflow] fleet server: APRA_FLEET_SERVER_CMD/APRA_FLEET_SERVER_BIN set' instead). Root cause named in this bead is gone: root package.json now carries a real dependencies entry '@apralabs/apra-fleet-client': 'file:packages/apra-fleet-client' (landed in de48e98c, the npm-bundle-fixes integration branch) and the files allowlist ships packages/apra-fleet-client/src + package.json. Closing as fixed.

title: compose_permissions grants don't land in .claude/settings.json -- deploy.md's permission check never sees them
description:
Found live 2026-08-02: called compose_permissions(member=fleet-lin-dev1, role=doer, tags=[doer], grant=[9 deploy.md-required Bash prefixes]) -- tool reported '\u2705 Granted 9 permissions'. Relaunched apra-fleet-l7n against fleet-lin-dev1 immediately after; Deploy phase failed on EVERY cycle (4/4) with the exact same missing-permissions error, citing /home/akhil/git/apra-fleet-dev1/.claude/settings.json as still containing only the original 5 entries (Bash(bd *), Bash(bd:*), Bash(npm test*), Bash(npm run *), Bash(npx vitest *)).

Checked both files directly on the member via execute_command: .claude/settings.json had none of the 9 granted entries; .claude/settings.local.json had no permissions.allow key at all (only enabledMcpjsonServers). The grant call's own response named 'Config: .claude/settings.local.json' as its target -- but deploy.md's Step 0 permission check (per integ-test-runner.md/deployer contract) reads .claude/settings.json specifically. The grant appears to write to an internal permissions ledger and/or the wrong settings file, and never actually reaches the file the deploy dispatch's own permission gate checks.

Workaround used: manually edited .claude/settings.json on the member via execute_command to add the 9 entries directly.

Impact: this silently defeats the entire on-demand credential-granting workflow (compose_permissions with grant=) for any permission check that reads .claude/settings.json rather than .claude/settings.local.json or the internal ledger -- deploy.md is one confirmed instance; other roles/playbooks with their own Permissions sections should be assumed equally affected until this is fixed.

Fix: identify where compose_permissions' grant mode actually writes (ledger file, settings.local.json, or elsewhere) and either (a) write grants directly into .claude/settings.json so every permission-checking consumer sees them consistently, or (b) if settings.local.json is the intended target, make deploy.md's (and any other role's) permission check also read settings.local.json, merged with settings.json -- pick ONE authoritative source and make grant + every checker agree on it.

title: [impl] Classify exit-0/empty-stdout workspace_not_trusted and self-heal-retry-once
description:
Parent: apra-fleet-6a7. Files: src/tools/execute-prompt.ts (classification at ~line 991 + dispatch path), src/utils/prompt-errors.ts (workspace_not_trusted PromptErrorCategory).

Problem: the workspace_not_trusted classifier only runs when result.code !== 0. The live failure (apra-fleet-2g2, fleet-win-dev1, 2026-08-02) exited 0 with EMPTY stdout (the empty_response branch), so the classifier never inspected it even though the stderr tail contained the exact matched phrase ('Ignoring N permissions.allow entries... this workspace has not been trusted'). The existing reactive self-heal therefore never fired.

Change:
1. Extend the workspace_not_trusted classification so it also matches on the code === 0 + empty-stdout branch (stderr tail phrase match), not just code !== 0 -- so the empty_response case is classified as workspace_not_trusted instead of falling through as generic empty_response.
2. Once classified, self-heal-and-retry-once: call the existing seedWorkspaceTrust/ensureWorkspaceTrusted path (the same one compose_permissions uses), then retry the dispatch exactly ONE time, gated by a heal-attempted flag. Model on runGitStep({...,onAuthFailure}) in fleet-sprint/runner.js:616.
3. Keep this in the generic dispatch layer (execute-prompt.ts / prompt-errors.ts). Do NOT add provider-specific code -- claude.ts's ensureWorkspaceTrusted already works; the gap is purely when the generic layer decides to call it reactively.

Out of scope: investigating what reset fleet-win-dev1's ~/.claude.json (separate, lower-priority, non-code).

Done when:
- An exit-0 + empty-stdout dispatch whose stderr tail contains the trust phrase is classified as workspace_not_trusted (not generic empty_response).
- That classification triggers exactly one seedWorkspaceTrust/ensureWorkspaceTrust self-heal + one dispatch retry.
- No client-schema (packages/apra-fleet-client) change is required (internal classification/retry only); confirm none is needed.
- npm test passes.
