title: Phase-routing initial slice: classify all-children-closed parents into a verify set, excluded from Plan/Develop, exclusively scoped to IntegTest
description:
Confirmed live TWICE in one night (2026-08-02), independently, on two different sprints/members:

1. apra-fleet-2sn (fleet-mac): fully re-implemented and re-verified apra-fleet-3i3 (4/4 impl+test subtasks closed) and apra-fleet-glv (2/2 subtasks closed), but neither parent ever closed. Stalled at closed-count 28 after 2 flat cycles, with 6 other items in scope never touched.
2. apra-fleet-l7n (fleet-lin-dev1): Cycle 1 decomposed and closed real impl+test subtask pairs across ALL 9 target bugs (3c9, 107, y8q, 9zz, 63x, gd0, 33c, nwh, eft.4.9) -- roughly 18 subtask closures, reviewer APPROVED. Cycle 1 evaluation still reported '9 bead(s) still open at/above goal priority P2' -- the 9 PARENTS, each 100% done at the child level. Cycles 2-3 found nothing ready to dispatch (no leaf work left) and the stall detector correctly aborted after 2 consecutive flat cycles (closed-count history [21,21,21]).

In both cases the sprint had genuinely finished all the child-level work available to it and SHOULD have been able to declare success by closing the parents, but the engine has no mechanism to recognize 'every child of this parent is closed -> close (or flag for admin closure of) the parent' -- so real, complete, well-evidenced work reads as a stall and the sprint aborts instead of finishing cleanly.

This is a near-term, tactical instance of the same gap docs/fleet-sprint-phase-routing-design.md's 'administrative closure is acceptable' design decision (user-approved 2026-08-01) is meant to solve at the architecture level -- but that redesign is still DRAFT/unimplemented. This bead is for a tactical stopgap: after each cycle's Develop/Review loop, before evaluating stall/continue, check every scope-root parent bead (bdListScoped's frontier) for 'all children closed, parent still open' and either auto-close it with a synthesized rationale (all N children closed, citing their close reasons) or surface it explicitly to the Reviewer/Deploy phase as a pending administrative-closure item rather than silently leaving it open and letting the stall detector misread 'no more leaf work' as 'no progress'.

Acceptance: a sprint whose every leaf-level bead closes within budget also closes (or explicitly flags for one-touch admin closure) every ancestor parent bead in scope, and does not abort via StalledSprintError purely because no leaf work remains while parents with fully-closed children still sit open.
notes:
## Regroomed (2026-08-02): superseding the admin-closure stopgap with a real verify-route slice

User rejected the original admin-closure proposal outright: "administrative closure makes no sense to me" -- closing a parent just because its children closed means the code was written and unit-tested, not that it works against the live product. Per this session's earlier design decision #3 ("testing only makes sense if it is being tested in the latest product else we may accept regressions"), only real integration-test evidence earns closure.

Directed redesign (user, verbatim): "jfo should be done in a manner that from the beginning we collect parent beads of this type (all closed children) into a list of integration testing required and not send them for planning/development. further the integration testing phase should only get beads of this type. In summary we can do an initial version of the phase routing design."

A background design agent (fable-tier) was dispatched to produce this as an initial slice of docs/fleet-sprint-phase-routing-design.md's verify route. Full design below.

### Forensic note: the engine already has an embryo of this

pendingClosureBugs (runner.js ~7640) already hands "open bug with all task-children closed" to the integ runner for verification-closure. Tonight's stalls happened anyway because that embryo (a) covers only issue_type === 'bug' parents -- apra-fleet-l7n's 9 targets qualified, but apra-fleet-2sn's apra-fleet-3i3/apra-fleet-glv are issue_type=feature and were invisible to it; (b) lives only inside the IntegTest block, gated on hasPlaybook && deployedThisCycle; (c) is invisible to the Plan phase and the stall detector, so classification itself was never counted as progress.

### D1. The classifier -- pure function, derived state, no stored list

New exported pure function in runner.js: classifyVerifySet(allBeads, targetIssues) -> { verifyIds, ineligible }.

Eligibility (all five, per bead):
1. in sprint scope (same BFS as bdListScoped ~5099), or is itself a target whose children are all closed;
2. status is open/in_progress;
3. has >=1 child (childless beads are leaves -> normal pipeline; a parent with NO children is never eligible);
4. EVERY child, any issue_type, is closed -- computed from the full unfiltered snapshot, not the scope-filtered list (fixes a latent premature-closure bug in the current pendingClosureBugs, which uses a scope-filtered childrenByParent);
5. no unmet blocks dependency (inv-4, applied structurally).

Any issue_type qualifies -- this generalizes past bug-only. Partial closure never qualifies (condition 4 is strict). No persistent list: recomputed fresh from the beads DB at each classification point, so nothing to keep in sync and a crash-restart re-derives it for free.

### D2. When classification runs

1. Pre-sprint validation (~5703-5733): "ready set non-empty OR verify set non-empty" -- a sprint scoped at an all-closed parent becomes a valid pure-verify sprint.
2. Top of every cycle (new Route C{n} marker, before Plan): feeds the Plan-phase exclusion and the stall-detector progress score (D5).
3. At IntegTest dispatch time (~7562-7588, replacing pendingClosureBugs' derivation): recomputed fresh so same-cycle closures get verified same-cycle; a mid-cycle reviewer reopen drops the parent before dispatch.

### D3. Plan/Develop/Review exclusion

Develop and Review already structurally exclude parents with children (readyLeafBeads, streak scope) -- zero change needed there. Plan is the real change: buildPlannerPrompt/buildPlanReviewerPrompt gain a verifyExcluded: string[] param naming these ids as "implementation-complete, do not re-decompose, plan-review gates do not bind over them." Caveat: this is prompt-level/advisory in the initial slice, not a deterministic engine-side rejection of planner-created children under a verify parent.

### D4. IntegTest phase scope becomes EXACTLY

(a) this cycle's open features in scope (existing regression/gap-detection clause, unchanged) plus (b) the verify set, and NOTHING else -- pendingClosureBugs is absorbed into it as one shape the classifier now emits generally. Per verify-set bead: verify against the deployed build; close only with a note citing commands/output/SHA; otherwise leave open and file the gap under the failing parent (not the sprint root) -- load-bearing for the bounce (D6).

### D5. Stall-detector interaction (the actual bug from tonight)

Classification counts as progress, once per bead, monotonically: run-local verifyEverIds set, added at classification, never removed. Progress score = closedCount + verifyEverIds.size; the high-water mark tracks this score instead of raw closedCount. Replaying l7n: C1 closes ~18 children (hw=21); C2 Route classifies 9 parents -> score 30 > 21, staleCycles resets -- the abort that actually killed l7n does not fire. If IntegTest then genuinely can't verify (the 63x failure shape), the stall still correctly fires eventually, but now with details naming the unverified ids and the deploy/integ failure reason, not a bare "no progress."

New minimal exit: if the only open-at-goal beads are verify-set members and hasPlaybook is false, break directly to Finalization rather than let the stall net convert "finished but unverifiable" into an ABORT.

### D6. Verification failure -- bounce done structurally, no new state machine

Integ runner reports gapsFound; gap bug filed under the failing parent makes it structurally ineligible again (fails condition 4) -- no sticky "bounced" flag needed. When the gap bug closes, the parent re-qualifies automatically next classification. Capped at 2 gap rounds per parent per sprint (run-local verifyGapCounts, mirrors reopenCounts); second gap defers the parent instead of an endless loop.

### D7. Edge cases

- Childless parent: never eligible, routes plan (unchanged).
- Children closing across cycles: irrelevant, eligibility is evaluated fresh each classification point.
- Nested parents: cascade one level per cycle -- bounded by tree depth; a tree deeper than remaining cycles can exhaust MAX_CYCLES before the root verifies.
- Deferred/blocked child under an otherwise-done parent: parent stays ineligible and unplannable (today's behavior, unchanged).
- Target itself all-closed: admitted to the verify set (fixes a real gap where a sprint aimed at a single done parent would find nothing to do).

### D8. Explicitly deferred

Deterministic evidence-bar audit (reopen-on-missing-evidence); the full triage LLM/Router (close/defer/hold/develop/review routes, overrides, dashboard routing panel). This slice is the structural half of the Router only.

### D9. Honest risks (carried from the design, plus one found independently while regrooming)

1. IntegTest becomes the SOLE closure gate for finished work, and it's the engine's least reliable dispatch (apra-fleet-63x). This slice converts false stalls into diagnosed ones -- it does not fix IntegTest's own reliability, which is a hard co-dependency for this to pay off.
2. Evidence quality is prompt-enforced only in this slice -- a generic "suite passed" note is currently accepted.
3. Playbook coverage mismatch: the playbook may not exercise a given parent's surface at all -- an honest "cannot verify" stalls correctly per the user's own ruling, but expect it and expect playbook growth to be the real fix.
4. Plan exclusion is advisory only (D3).
5. NEW, found while regrooming jfo (not in the original design agent's output): integ-test-runner.md's own Rule 229 says "NEVER close type=task issues" -- a hard, explicit conflict with D1's "any issue_type qualifies." If a verify-eligible parent happens to be issue_type=task (e.g. apra-fleet-tfx), the agent's own persona rule forbids closing it, silently contradicting this design unless Rule 229 is narrowed. See the integ-test-runner.md gap-analysis note added to this bead.
6. This design supersedes the original admin-closure framing entirely -- jfo's acceptance criterion ("a sprint whose leaf work completes does not abort via StalledSprintError purely because no leaf work remains") is now met via D5, with closure earned by real verification instead of synthesized rationale.

Touch surface: one new pure function + three call sites in runner.js (~5703, ~5889, ~7562), the progress-score change (~7757-7768), two prompt-builder params (~2637, ~2764), gapsFound in contracts.mjs + integ-test-runner.md, one additive publishState namespace. packages/apra-fleet-client untouched (no MCP tool schema changes).
## integ-test-runner.md gap analysis + thought experiments (2026-08-02)

Read packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/agents/integ-test-runner.md in full, and the runner.js dispatch site (~7596-7819) that builds its prompt and interprets its result. Answering the direct question: is the current agent contract written in a way that can even ATTEMPT to verify jfo's verify-set beads?

### Answer: partially, inconsistently, and with one live unexplained failure

**For issue_type=feature parents (e.g. apra-fleet-3i3, apra-fleet-glv):** mechanically yes -- openFeatures = bdListScoped('--type=feature --status=open --json') includes ANY open feature regardless of whether it has children, so 3i3/glv textually reach the agent via the existing, fully-documented Step 1-4 workflow (bd dep list -> find [test] children -> run them -> bd close or file bug). No code change needed for eligibility.

BUT: live evidence tonight contradicts this working in practice. Both 3i3 and glv had a purpose-built re-verification [test] task closed with detailed real evidence (3i3.5, glv.3 -- full suite pass counts, specific assertions, no mocks) explicitly written "for the integ-test-runner to close [parent]" -- and neither parent ever closed, filed a bug, or got an inconclusive note. Checked apra-fleet-2sn's full log across all 4 cycles: Deploy succeeded every cycle (unlike l7n), IntegTest dispatched every cycle, yet there is ZERO log trace of integ-test-runner's actual result in any of the 4 cycles.

Root cause of the silence, confirmed by reading runner.js ~7790-7819: the Integ Test phase only logs on FAILURE (integResult.passed !== true) or INFRA-INCONCLUSIVE dispatch failure. A cycle where the agent dispatch itself succeeds and returns passed:true produces NO log line at all -- not even "0 features closed, nothing to report." This means I cannot tell from the log whether integ-test-runner (a) never actually received 3i3/glv in its feature list (a real scoping bug), (b) received them and silently marked them inconclusive per Step 3's "leave open, bd update --notes" path (but no such note exists on either bead, which Step 3 explicitly requires -- so if this happened, the agent also violated its own contract), or (c) something else entirely. This is unresolved and needs a live, instrumented repro -- filed separately as apra-fleet-<see below>, since it's a real diagnosability gap independent of jfo.

**For issue_type=bug parents (e.g. l7n's 9 targets):** only reachable via pendingClosureClause -- a single ad hoc English sentence appended to the END of the dispatch prompt at runner.js ~7644-7649, NOT present anywhere in integ-test-runner.md's own formal contract (no Step, no Rule, no Output-schema field). A reader of the persona file alone would never learn this is part of the role. Given apra-fleet-63x already documents this exact phase chronically exhausting its turn budget, a single trailing unstructured sentence competing against ~180 lines of highly specific, budget-conscious feature-testing instructions is a plausible casualty under pressure -- there is no way to confirm from the current output schema either way, since bugsFiled only tracks NEW bugs filed on failure, not verify-set closures.

**For issue_type=task parents:** Rule 229 is an explicit, hard blocker: "NEVER close type=task issues." apra-fleet-jfo's D1 says "any issue_type qualifies." apra-fleet-tfx (issue_type=task) is a live example of a bead that could hit this exact contradiction once it reaches all-children-closed. This is a real conflict that must be resolved before implementing D1 as designed -- either narrow jfo's classifier to exclude type=task, or narrow Rule 229 to permit closing a task that is ITSELF a verify-set parent (grouping node with closed children), while still protecting genuine leaf task beads from ever being closed by this agent. The latter preserves the rule's real intent.

### Minimal change needed (five items, all small, all in integ-test-runner.md + its output contract)

1. Add a new formal "Step 1b -- Work the verify-set bead ids you were handed" section, generalizing today's ad hoc pendingClosureClause into the same procedural rigor as Step 1/2 (find [test] children via bd dep list, evaluate cited evidence and/or re-run, close with evidence or file a gap bug under the parent). Covers any issue_type.
2. Narrow Rule 229 to: "NEVER close a type=task issue UNLESS it is itself a verify-set parent explicitly named in your dispatch prompt (i.e. has its own closed children) -- never close a leaf task bead regardless."
3. Add a distinct field to Step 4's output schema (and contracts.mjs / integ-test-runner-output.json) -- e.g. verifySetClosed: string[] and verifySetLeftOpen: [{id, reason}] -- separate from featuresClosed/bugsFiled, so the orchestrator can attribute verify-route progress distinctly (this is what jfo's D5 stall-detector fix needs to count reliably; today there is no structured signal for it at all).
4. Make runner.js log a one-line summary on EVERY Integ Test cycle outcome, not just failures -- e.g. "Integ Test C{n}: N feature(s) closed, M verify-set bead(s) closed, K left open (see notes)." Cheap, and tonight proved the silence itself is a real hazard: I could not distinguish "ran and passed on empty scope" from "ran and silently failed its own contract" from the log alone.
5. Clarify explicitly whether a doer-closed [test] task's cited close_reason evidence (as 3i3.5/glv.3 provided, in detail) is sufficient grounds to close the parent without re-running, or whether an independent re-run is mandatory. Today's total silence on this is ambiguous, and is plausibly why two purpose-built re-verification tasks, both closed with strong evidence, still didn't get their parents closed.

### Thought experiments: when will this design NOT work?

1. **Deploy keeps failing.** apra-fleet-l7n proved this live: IntegTest is gated on hasPlaybook && deployedThisCycle. If Deploy can't succeed (missing permissions.allow, as happened tonight), IntegTest never runs at all, so no verify-set bead can ever close no matter how well D1-D6 are implemented. D5's new exit (break to Finalization when hasPlaybook is false) does NOT cover this case -- it only covers "no playbook," not "playbook exists but Deploy keeps failing." This is a live gap in the design as specified: a parent can sit in the verify set forever, correctly classified, correctly excluded from Plan, and NEVER dispatched for actual verification, with the stall detector eventually firing (correctly) but the sprint having no path to resolve it within its own run.
2. **IntegTest itself is unreliable (apra-fleet-63x).** Even with Deploy succeeding, if the IntegTest dispatch routinely exhausts its turn budget or times out, verify-set beads accumulate credit once (D5's verifyEverIds bump) but never actually close. The design is honest about this (D9.1) but it means jfo's practical payoff is capped by 63x's unfixed reliability -- implementing jfo alone will convert tonight's false stalls into diagnosed stalls, not into actual completions, until 63x also lands.
3. **The type=task Rule 229 conflict** (above) -- silently produces a parent the classifier says should verify-close, but the agent's own persona forbids closing. Untested, will likely manifest as the agent either refusing (leaving it open forever, no diagnostic) or ignoring the rule inconsistently.
4. **The silent-success logging gap** (above) makes ANY failure of this design invisible by default. If D1-D6 ship with today's logging behavior unchanged, a broken classifier or a broken verify-clause prompt would look identical to "working fine, nothing to report" -- exactly the blind spot that let 3i3/glv sit unexplained all night.
5. **Deep nested parents** (D7): a grandparent-of-grandparent structure verifies at most one level per cycle; a sprint with MAX_CYCLES=5 and a 4-level-deep tree could exhaust its cycle budget before the root ever qualifies, aborting via stall with the root looking "stuck" when it's actually cascading correctly, just too slowly. Worth a warning log when cascade depth threatens to exceed remaining cycles.
6. **A verify-set parent whose playbook coverage genuinely doesn't exist** (D9.3) -- e.g. 2sn's own supervisor-dashboard-widget features may not be exercisable by whatever integ-test-playbook.md currently covers. The honest outcome ("cannot verify from playbook") is correct per the user's own ruling, but will read as an unexplained stall unless the IntegTest agent's report explicitly says "no playbook coverage for this surface" rather than a generic inconclusive note -- another argument for item 5 in the minimal-change list above (evidence-quality clarity extends to explaining WHY something can't be verified, not just that it wasn't).
See also apra-fleet-<pending id printed above> -- the silent-success logging gap this analysis surfaced. Filed as a separate, independently valuable bead since it applies to today's feature-only path too.

title: execute-prompt's workspace_not_trusted detection only fires on nonzero exit -- misses the exit-0/empty-response case, so the existing self-heal never triggers
description:
Found live 2026-08-02: sprint apra-fleet-2g2 died 18min after launch on fleet-win-dev1 with an empty_response dispatch failure. Root cause: fleet-win-dev1's ~/.claude.json had exactly one project entry (its registered folder, C:/akhil/git/apra-fleet) with hasTrustDialogAccepted:false and projectOnboardingSeenCount:0 -- the file's firstStartTime was ~10 minutes before the sprint launch, i.e. a freshly-initialized Claude Code identity that had never been run interactively on that host. Every permissions.allow entry in .claude/settings.json was silently ignored as a result, and the first real dispatch died mid-turn with no parseable output.

Contrast: fleet-lin-dev1 and fleet-mac both already had hasTrustDialogAccepted:true for their registered folders (from prior interactive use), so they didn't hit this.

Fix: provision_llm_auth (src/tools/provision-llm-auth.ts or wherever it lands for a member) should, as part of provisioning a member for LLM auth, also ensure ~/.claude.json's projects[<registered folder>].hasTrustDialogAccepted is set to true on that member's host -- the same way a human would accept the trust dialog the first time they run Claude Code interactively there. This removes an entire failure class (empty_response / member CLI died mid-turn with a trust-dialog stderr tail) that currently only surfaces as a confusing mid-sprint dispatch crash, often on a member's very first real dispatch after registration.

Acceptance: registering + provisioning a brand-new member and immediately launching a sprint against it (no prior interactive session) succeeds without an empty_response/trust-dialog failure.
notes:
## Correction (2026-08-02): this is a detection gap, not a missing feature

Original framing was wrong -- the proactive-provisioning fix I proposed (have provision_llm_auth set hasTrustDialogAccepted) is unnecessary. A background research agent confirmed the feature already exists, correctly abstracted:

- `ProviderAdapter.ensureWorkspaceTrusted(workFolder, execCommand, agentOs)` (src/providers/provider.ts:202) is implemented by every provider -- the REAL implementation lives in claude.ts:340 (Claude-specific, as it should be); agy.ts, codex.ts, copilot.ts, opencode.ts, gemini.ts, none.ts are all intentional no-ops, since Claude Code is the only CLI with this trust-gate concept. The provider abstraction already isolates this correctly -- no new claude.ts-specific work needed here.
- `src/utils/workspace-trust.ts`'s `seedWorkspaceTrust()` calls it, and is wired into `register_member`, `update_member`, and (self-healing by design) every `compose_permissions` run.
- `src/utils/prompt-errors.ts` already has a `workspace_not_trusted` PromptErrorCategory, matched against the CLI's literal stderr phrase and checked in `execute-prompt.ts:991` -- this IS the FolderTrustError-equivalent already, just not a named exception class.

### The actual bug

`execute-prompt.ts:991`'s check only runs when `result.code !== 0`. Tonight's real failure (apra-fleet-2g2 sprint, fleet-win-dev1, 2026-08-02) exited 0 with EMPTY stdout -- the `empty_response` path, a separate branch from the nonzero-exit path -- so the existing classifier never got a look at it, even though the stderr tail contained the exact matched phrase ("Ignoring N permissions.allow entries... this workspace has not been trusted"). This is why a member (fleet-win-dev1) that had presumably already been through compose_permissions before (register_member ran 2026-07-29) could still hit this: something reset its ~/.claude.json shortly before tonight's launch (cause still unconfirmed), and the reactive self-heal path that exists specifically to catch exactly this never fired because of the exit-code gate.

Manually verified live: `compose_permissions` (the existing, correct mechanism) immediately fixed it -- re-ran it for fleet-win-dev1, confirmed `~/.claude.json`'s `C:/akhil/git/apra-fleet` entry flipped to `hasTrustDialogAccepted: true`. So the fix mechanism works; it's only reachable manually/proactively right now, not from the reactive dispatch-failure path.

### Revised scope

1. Extend the `workspace_not_trusted` classification in execute-prompt.ts to also match on the `code === 0` + empty-stdout branch (not just `code !== 0`), so the empty_response case gets classified instead of falling through as a generic empty_response.
2. Once classified, self-heal-and-retry-once: call the same `seedWorkspaceTrust`/`ensureWorkspaceTrusted` path compose_permissions already uses, then retry the dispatch ONE time. Model this on the existing git auth self-heal shape: `runGitStep({..., onAuthFailure})` in runner.js:616, which calls an injected `onAuthFailure({member, label, cmd, error, kind})` once, gated by an `authHealAttempted` flag, before giving up.
3. This lives in the generic dispatch layer (execute-prompt.ts / prompt-errors.ts), not in a provider file -- the provider abstraction (claude.ts's ensureWorkspaceTrusted) already does its job correctly; the gap is purely in when the generic layer decides to call it reactively.
4. Separately (lower priority, still open): find out what actually reset fleet-win-dev1's ~/.claude.json around 2026-08-01T23:23 -- no evidence found yet of the trigger, only that the file's `firstStartTime` timestamp is suspiciously close to the sprint launch.

Acceptance (revised): a synthetic exit-0/empty-stdout dispatch on an untrusted workspace is classified as `workspace_not_trusted` (not generic `empty_response`), triggers exactly one self-heal-and-retry, and the retry succeeds without operator intervention.
close_reason: Verified against deployed build (HEAD=cf4b34f). Ran: npx vitest run tests/execute-prompt.test.ts -- 93/93 pass, including describe 'exit-0/empty-stdout workspace_not_trusted self-heal-and-retry (apra-fleet-6a7.1)': self-heals once via seedWorkspaceTrust and retries exactly once on success; still classifies workspace_not_trusted (not empty_response) if heal-and-retry stays empty; plain non-trust empty-stdout dispatch unaffected. All 3 assertions pass.

title: [impl] Add orchestrator-side VCSModule: provider-dispatched PR-creation command builder in fleet-se
description:
IMPORTANT CORRECTION to apra-fleet-tfx's description body: VCSModule is ORCHESTRATOR-SIDE, not member-side. The tfx description says 'member-side VCSModule' in several places -- that wording is superseded by the 2026-08-02 correction note on tfx. Read this task, not that phrasing.

VCSModule lives in fleet-se (alongside runner.js and the existing src/services/vcs/ provider seam). It is orchestrator code that:
1. Knows the provider (github / bitbucket / azure-devops) and builds the correct REST call (URL, method, JSON body) for 'raise a PR' and 'comment on abort', reusing the VcsProviderService shape in src/services/vcs/types.ts -- extend that seam, do not invent a parallel one.
2. Returns a concrete, fully-formed command (a curl invocation) that the member runs via execute_command, with the already-minted token supplied by the caller.

The member never runs VCSModule, holds no VCS-abstraction code, and does not choose how the PR gets raised -- it is a dumb executor of a command the orchestrator built. No vendor CLI (gh) anywhere in the path. No server-side fallback.

Files (<=3): a new VCSModule module in packages/apra-fleet-se (plus its provider dispatch), and the src/services/vcs/ type/seam extension it consumes. Do NOT wire it into runner.js call sites in this task -- that is the next task in this streak.

A VCSModule unit exists in fleet-se exposing a provider-dispatched build step for PR creation that returns a command string plus the metadata needed to interpret its output; GitHub is implemented, and unsupported providers fail with a clear ASCII ERROR: message rather than silently producing a wrong command.
2. The GitHub builder produces a curl POST to the /repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls REST endpoint carrying base, head, title and body, authenticated with the supplied installation token -- asserted against an expected command string in a unit test.
3. The token value never appears in any logged/echoed form in the returned command's log output.
4. No 'gh ' invocation and no create_pull_request reference is produced anywhere by VCSModule.
5. Module is pure/deterministic (no network in unit tests); node --test suite green.

title: Supervisor never wires the issue-scope overlap guard into POST /api/sprints -- only member-overlap is actually checked at launch
description:
docs/architecture.md documents an issue-scope overlap launch guard (src/supervisor/scope-overlap.mjs, createScopeGuard) as active protection alongside the member-overlap guard. In reality, bin/serve.mjs constructs createSprintController() without a beforeLaunch override, so it falls back to defaultMemberOverlapGuard alone (src/supervisor/api.mjs) -- createScopeGuard is exercised only by unit tests, never composed into the live POST /api/sprints path. expandScope() from the same module IS used live, but only for the Backlog tree's partial-claim rendering, not as a launch-time reject.

Impact: two sprints with disjoint member sets but overlapping or nested issue scopes (e.g. one targets an epic, another targets one of that epic's children) can both launch and dispatch against the same beads concurrently -- only the member axis is guarded, not the issue axis. Found live 2026-08-02 while auditing supervisor API docs (packages/apra-fleet-se/docs/supervisor-api.md, supervisor-openapi.yaml just written).

Fix: compose createScopeGuard with defaultMemberOverlapGuard as the beforeLaunch passed into createSprintController() in bin/serve.mjs, matching how api.mjs's own header comment (eft.5.2/eft.5.3) already describes the two guards as meant to compose.

Also ran test/serve-wiring-integration.test.mjs confirming bin/serve.mjs boots the real composed controller as a live subprocess (not just unit-level). title: [umbrella - do not claim] Revert server-side create_pull_request; add orchestrator-side VCSModule (fleet-se) + PR-capable access level
description:
Revert the server-side `create_pull_request` MCP tool (added 2026-08-01, commit c5e66566) and replace it with a member-side VCSModule that raises PRs over the provider REST API, using a token `provision_vcs_auth` minted with the right access level.

## Why (architectural)

The fleet server's role is: orchestrate members, and MINT/DISTRIBUTE credentials so MEMBERS can act. It is not an actor on a repository. `create_pull_request` broke that: `src/tools/create-pull-request.ts:85-160` runs IN THE SERVER PROCESS, mints its own installation token (`:105`) and does `POST https://api.github.com/repos/{repo}/pulls` (`:122-130`). That makes the orchestrating hub perform a repo-mutating action against a third-party hosted service.

Note what did NOT change: the server has ALWAYS held the GitHub App private key and always called api.github.com to mint tokens (`src/services/github-app.ts:9,24,105`; `src/services/vcs/github.ts:33,41`; `docs/design-git-auth.md:69,79`). No new secret class was introduced. What changed is the server's ROLE -- from credential authority to repo actor. That is the regression being reverted.

## The actual bug this was solving (apra-fleet-6bu)

`gh auth login --with-token` validates via `GET /user`, which a GitHub App installation token (ghs_) structurally cannot call -- so `gh pr create` can never be authenticated by fleet provisioning, at ANY permission level. Real bug, correctly diagnosed.

But the fix chosen was wrong-sized. The member could not raise the PR for only two reasons, both member-side and both trivial:

1. Token scope. `packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:2041` hardcodes `git_access: 'push'`, and `mapAccessLevel()` (`src/services/github-app.ts:70-79`) maps push -> {contents:write, metadata:read} -- no pull_requests. The `issues` and `full` levels already include pull_requests:write, so `provision_vcs_auth` was ALREADY capable of minting a PR-capable token. Wrong level requested, nothing more.
2. Wrong client. `gh` is the only thing that cannot consume the token. The REST endpoint accepts it fine -- confirmed by the 6bu probe (422 validation, i.e. authorized, not 403).

The token is already on the member in readable form: `src/os/linux.ts:239-257` writes `$HOME/.fleet-git-credential-<label>`, a chmod-600 script echoing `password=<token>`; `src/os/windows.ts:247` equivalent.

Also note the shipped fallback is dead code: `attemptServerSidePrCreate` (`runner.js:3994-4029`) falls back to `gh pr create`, which the tool's own header comment (`create-pull-request.ts:5-11`) correctly explains can never authenticate.

## Target design

VCSModule -- a provider-agnostic member-side PR/VCS-action abstraction that hides "how do I raise a PR on this provider" behind one interface, implemented over curl/HTTP REST rather than any vendor CLI. Sits alongside the existing provider split in `src/services/vcs/` (github.ts / bitbucket.ts / azure-devops.ts), which already has the right shape (`VcsProviderService` in `src/services/vcs/types.ts`) -- extend that seam rather than inventing a parallel one. The server contributes the COMMAND to run and the credential; the member runs it.

Proactive, not defensive, provisioning. The sprint workflow is deterministic: it knows in advance that a Publish-PR phase is coming. So `provision_vcs_auth` is called with the PR-capable access level up front, for the phase/activity that needs it -- not discovered by failure and retried. No fallback path.

## Scope of change

Revert:
- delete `src/tools/create-pull-request.ts` + registration `src/services/tool-registry.ts:25,125`
- delete `tests/create-pull-request.test.ts` (8 vitest cases)
- delete `createPullRequest` wrapper `packages/apra-fleet-client/src/client/api.mjs:339-341` + `packages/apra-fleet-client/test/fleet-client-api.test.mjs:194-215` (client-sync convention)
- delete `createServerSidePrCreator`/`attemptServerSidePrCreate` `packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:3936-4029`, call sites at `:4472-4495` (finalizeAbort), `:4855-4870`, `:8507-8530`, `:8770-8785`
- delete `packages/apra-fleet-se/test/server-side-pr-creation.test.mjs` (17 node --test cases)
- revert `packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/cli.mjs:775-780` binding
- `packages/apra-fleet-se/test/dispatch-safety-guard.test.mjs` call-site count: the original "43 -> 42" figure here is STALE -- do not use it. The correct revert-state value is 44 (64dc595 bumped 43 -> 45; the apra-fleet-tfx.5 call-site removal gives 45 - 1 = 44) and it is already asserted at line 220. apra-fleet-tfx.6 owns this constant for the revert state; apra-fleet-tfx.8 owns any post-VCSModule adjustment
- delete mock fixtures `apra-fleet-mock-sprint-serversidepridem.jsonl`, `apra-fleet-mock-sprint-serversideprmissing.jsonl`; revert `packages/apra-fleet-se/test/helpers/mock-sprint-harness.mjs:1102-1160` prToolHandler wiring

Implement:
- add access level to `mapAccessLevel()` `src/services/github-app.ts:70-79`: push+pr -> {contents:write, pull_requests:write, metadata:read}. Do NOT reuse `full` -- it over-grants administration:write + actions:write to every sprint member.
- add that level to the `git_access` enum `src/tools/provision-vcs-auth.ts:52`
- VCSModule: member-side PR creation over REST, provider-dispatched via the `src/services/vcs/` seam
- `runner.js:2041` requests the PR-capable level proactively
- replace the `gh pr create` dispatches at `runner.js:~8526` (Publish PR) and `~4506` (finalizeAbort) with VCSModule member-side execute_command

Prerequisite:
- confirm `pull_requests: write` is granted on the GitHub App installation itself. Required for the member path AND the current server path, so it buys the server tool nothing -- but verify before deleting the incumbent.

## Documentation

- New ADR stating the invariant that was missing. No doc in `docs/` currently says the server must not act on repositories -- checked architecture.md, design-git-auth.md, design-vcs-auth-onboarding.md, threat-model-workspace-iron-wall.md, SECURITY-REVIEW.md, vocabulary.md, README.md. The boundary lived only in the code's habits, which is why an agent crossed it. State it explicitly alongside the existing `docs/adr-*.md` set: the fleet server orchestrates members and mints/distributes credentials; it never itself acts on a repository or a hosted third-party service. Include the pre-existing App-private-key/token-minting carve-out so the rule is accurate rather than aspirational.
- `docs/architecture.md` -- VCSModule seam and the server/member split for repo actions
- `docs/design-git-auth.md` and `docs/design-vcs-auth-onboarding.md` -- new access level, proactive phase-scoped provisioning
- `packages/apra-fleet-se/docs/architecture.md:680-683` -- Publish-PR step no longer uses `gh pr create`
- tool inventory docs -- ensure `create_pull_request` is not documented as a fleet tool
- CHANGELOG entry for the revert + replacement
acceptance_criteria:
1. src/tools/create-pull-request.ts, its tool-registry registration, tests/create-pull-request.test.ts, the apra-fleet-client createPullRequest wrapper + test, packages/apra-fleet-se/test/server-side-pr-creation.test.mjs, and runner.js createServerSidePrCreator/attemptServerSidePrCreate plus all four call sites are deleted. Machine check: `grep -rn "create_pull_request" --include=*.ts --include=*.mjs --include=*.js .` (excluding dist/ and node_modules/) returns no hits.
2. mapAccessLevel() in src/services/github-app.ts exposes a PR-capable level granting exactly {contents:write, pull_requests:write, metadata:read}, and that level is selectable via provision_vcs_auth's git_access enum. Unit test asserts the exact permission map.
3. A VCSModule raises PRs member-side over the provider REST API via execute_command, dispatched through the src/services/vcs/ provider seam, with no vendor CLI (gh) dependency anywhere in the PR path and no server-side fallback. Machine check: no `gh pr create` in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js.
4. runner.js requests the PR-capable access level proactively before the Publish-PR phase (not on failure/retry). Test asserts the provision_vcs_auth dispatch carries the PR-capable level.
5. A new docs/adr-*.md states the server-never-acts-on-a-repo invariant, including the accurate pre-existing App-private-key / token-minting carve-out.

notes:
## Grooming update (2026-08-02): just-in-time, activity-scoped credential minting

Correction to the "Implement" section above: do NOT change
provisionVcsAuthForMember()'s hardcoded git_access: 'push' default
(runner.js:2029). That function is SHARED by two callers -- the reactive
onAuthFailure self-heal (createVcsAuthSelfHealCallback) AND the proactive
preflight (createVcsAuthPreflightCallback) -- and both fire for ROUTINE
git/dolt sync throughout the entire sprint (any commit push, any dolt
push/pull retry), completely unrelated to raising a PR. If the PR-capable
level replaces 'push' here, every sprint member carries pull_requests:write
for the full sprint duration from the very first routine sync call, whether
or not a PR is ever raised that run. That is standing over-privilege, not
least-privilege, and it is the exact anti-pattern this revert exists to fix
-- reintroducing it via the "proactive" wording above would defeat the point.

### The principle

Deterministic workflow code (runner.js), not LLM judgment, controls WHEN a
PR is about to be raised -- the Publish-PR phase and the finalizeAbort
PR-raising path are both fixed, orchestrator-controlled call sites, not
places an LLM decides to reach on its own. Because that moment is knowable
in advance and controlled entirely by code, the elevated token should be
minted immediately before THAT SPECIFIC call, used once, and nowhere else --
not carried as the member's ambient/standing access for the run.

Contrast with what a compromised or misbehaving ("rogue") LLM dispatch could
do under each model:
- Standing high-priv (git_access: push+pr for the whole sprint): any doer,
  reviewer, or other in-sprint dispatch -- including one driven by a
  prompt-injected or misbehaving model -- has pull_requests:write available
  for the ENTIRE sprint window, whether or not the deterministic workflow
  ever intended to use it. The blast radius is the full sprint duration.
- Just-in-time, call-site-scoped high-priv: the elevated token exists only
  in the seconds around the one deterministic Publish-PR/finalizeAbort call
  that the runner.js code path itself makes -- never as ambient credential
  material an LLM-driven dispatch could reach for or misuse mid-sprint. The
  blast radius is one code-controlled call, not model discretion.

This mirrors why the mutex/id-allocator tools were judged SOUND in the same
audit that flagged create_pull_request: privilege and capability should be
scoped to the smallest code-controlled window that actually needs it, never
granted broadly "because it might be needed eventually."

### Corrected implementation

- provisionVcsAuthForMember() (runner.js:2020) keeps git_access: 'push' as
  its default/only mode for the self-heal and general preflight callers --
  UNCHANGED from today.
- Add a NEW, separate, narrowly-scoped provisioning call -- e.g.
  provisionPrCapableAuthForMember() or an explicit gitAccess parameter on
  the existing function that ONLY the Publish-PR and finalizeAbort call
  sites pass 'push+pr' into -- invoked immediately before the PR-creation
  dispatch at each of those two sites, not at sprint setup, not at any
  other phase boundary.
- No other call site in runner.js may ever request the push+pr (or higher)
  level. This is a hard invariant, not a style preference.

### New/revised acceptance criteria (supersedes AC4 above)

AC4 (revised): the PR-capable access level is requested ONLY from the two
PR-raising call sites (Publish-PR phase, finalizeAbort), immediately before
each dispatches its PR-creation call -- never from provisionVcsAuthForMember
's shared self-heal/preflight path, never at sprint setup, never
speculatively for a phase that has not yet been reached. Test asserts (a)
the two PR-raising call sites' provision_vcs_auth dispatch carries
git_access: 'push+pr', and (b) EVERY OTHER provision_vcs_auth call site in
the sprint (self-heal, general preflight, any other phase) still carries
git_access: 'push' -- i.e. a machine check must positively confirm the
non-PR paths were NOT widened, not just that the PR paths were. Suggested
check: grep -n "push+pr" packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js
matches exactly the two PR-raising call sites and nothing else.

### Documentation addition

The new ADR (see "Documentation" above) should state this as a general
pattern, not a one-off fix for this bug: fleet-sprint credential
provisioning is just-in-time and call-site-scoped to the deterministic
workflow step that needs it, never granted ambiently "in case a later phase
needs it" -- with the rogue-dispatch blast-radius argument above as the
stated rationale, so future credential-needing features default to this
shape instead of re-discovering it.
## Correction (2026-08-02): VCSModule is orchestrator-side, not member-side

The description above says "member-side VCSModule" in several places -- that's wrong and needs to be read as corrected here.

VCSModule lives in fleet-se (the workflow/orchestrator package, alongside runner.js and the existing src/services/vcs/ provider seam), NOT on the member. It is orchestrator code that:
1. Knows the provider (github/bitbucket/azure-devops) and builds the right REST call (URL, method, JSON body) for "raise a PR" / "comment on abort", using the existing VcsProviderService shape in src/services/vcs/types.ts.
2. Hands the member a concrete, fully-formed command (e.g. a curl invocation) plus the already-minted push+pr token, to run via execute_command.

The member never runs "VCSModule" itself, has no VCS-abstraction code of its own, and does not choose how the PR gets raised -- it is a dumb executor of a command the orchestrator built. This matches the existing division of responsibility everywhere else in fleet-sprint: fleet-se decides what happens and constructs the exact dispatch; the member executes it.

This changes the "Scope of change" wording: "VCSModule: member-side PR creation over REST, provider-dispatched via the src/services/vcs/ seam" should read "VCSModule: orchestrator-side (fleet-se) command-builder for PR creation over REST, provider-dispatched via the src/services/vcs/ seam; dispatched to the member via execute_command." Same for "replace the gh pr create dispatches ... with VCSModule member-side execute_command" -- the execute_command call is member-side (as it always is), but VCSModule itself, the logic deciding what that command is, is not.

title: Client dispatch timeout doesn't account for the server's own inactivity-timeout retry
description: packages/apra-fleet-client/src/client/api.mjs:180-197 deriveTimeoutMs() sets the client's tools/call deadline to max_total_s*1000 + 30s grace. But src/tools/execute-prompt.ts:958-977 (apra-fleet-02s.1) retries once with a FRESH session using the SAME timeout_s/max_total_s when the SSH inactivity timer fires. Server-side worst case is therefore up to ~2x the client's budget (~7200s vs the client's 3630s), so the client's hard timeout can fire before the server's own retry-and-report-cleanly path ever gets a chance, hiding a cleaner server-side error behind a raw client-side transport timeout. Either derive the client timeout as (max_total_s * 2) + grace, or make the server-side retry share one deadline budget with the original attempt.
close_reason: Verified against deployed build (HEAD=cf4b34f). Ran: npx vitest run tests/execute-prompt.test.ts -- describe 'client timeout budget covers the shared server-side retry budget (apra-fleet-y8q.2)': client deadline covers shared-budget server worst case for max_total_s in {10,60,300,900,3600,7200} (6/6 pass), explicitly would NOT have covered the old unshared ~2x worst case (4/4 pass), and an inactivity-retry that exhausts the shared budget surfaces the typed dispatch_failed error within the client-derived window (1/1 pass). Also 'shared retry deadline budget (apra-fleet-y8q.1)' 2/2 pass.

title: SSH connections have no keepalive configured -- a dropped connection is never detected
description: src/services/ssh.ts:46-52 (getSSHConfig) sets only readyTimeout: 15000. No keepaliveInterval / keepaliveCountMax is configured, and ssh2 defaults to keepalive disabled. A silently dropped TCP connection is therefore never surfaced -- the only detection path is the stall detector's 30s tail-log polling (stall-poller.ts), which is a much coarser and slower signal than a transport-level keepalive would be. Add keepaliveInterval (~15s) + keepaliveCountMax so a dead connection surfaces in seconds. Related to the stall-hang incident (see the onStall cancellation bead) but a distinct fix.
close_reason: Verified against deployed build (HEAD=cf4b34f). Ran: npx vitest run tests/platform.test.ts -- 131 passed/3 skipped, including 'getSSHConfig sets keepaliveInterval to approximately 15000ms' (asserts ===15000), 'sets keepaliveCountMax to a value >= 1', and 'includes both keepaliveInterval and keepaliveCountMax properties' -- all pass against src/services/ssh.ts's getSSHConfig().

title: Stall detector kills remote pid but never cancels the in-flight MCP dispatch
description: Root cause of a 60.5-minute hung fleet-sprint dispatch tonight (Plan-Reviewer on fleet-win-dev1, 47% of that sprint's total wall-clock, $0 of work produced). src/tools/execute-prompt.ts:679-705's onStall callback clears in-process bookkeeping and calls tryKillPid() on the remote process, but has no handle on the pending strategy.execCommand() promise -- no AbortController, no way to reject the MCP tools/call. The client then sits waiting for its own hard deriveTimeoutMs() deadline (packages/apra-fleet-client/src/client/api.mjs:180-197, = max_total_s*1000 + 30s grace) even though the server-side work died minutes earlier (confirmed live: member session was idle, no claude.exe process running, yet the tools/call stayed pending). Fix: thread an AbortController into onStall so a confirmed stall actually cancels/settles the in-flight execCommand (src/services/ssh.ts:247-254 already has an abortSignal param on RemoteStrategy) and returns a typed 'stalled' dispatch error immediately, instead of converting a ~2-minute stall detection into a full max_total_s burn.
close_reason: Verified against deployed build (HEAD=cf4b34f). Ran: npx vitest run tests/execute-prompt.test.ts -- describe 'confirmed stall aborts the in-flight dispatch (apra-fleet-3c9.2)': a confirmed stall against a hanging execCommand settles promptly via AbortController with a typed 'stalled' structuredContent error (never waiting max_total_s), and a live non-stalled dispatch completes normally with onStall never firing. 2/2 pass.

title: [integ] Real npm-pack install: 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint --help' crashes on first run (missing packages/apra-fleet-se/package.json in files allowlist)
description:
Feature: apra-fleet-kuh
Expected (kuh's own acceptance criteria, verified via its [test] task kuh.4): a real 'npm pack' + 'npm install' of the resulting .tgz into a clean, non-workspace prefix, followed by 'apra-fleet install' and then 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint --help', prints the engine's real usage/help text.

Actual: on a genuinely fresh install (two independent clean /tmp prefixes tested, npm install ./apralabs-apra-fleet-0.4.0.tgz, HOME pointed at a brand-new empty dir, 'apra-fleet install' run once, then 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint --help' run as the FIRST invocation) the command reliably crashes with exit code 1:

  SyntaxError: Named export 'checkMemberTopology' not found. The requested module '../fleet-sprint/runner.js' is a CommonJS module, which may not support all module.exports as named exports.
      at file://.../.apra-fleet/workflows/fleet-sprint/bin/cli.mjs:19
      at async Module.runWorkflow (.../dist/cli/workflow.js:365:21)

Root cause (confirmed by bisection): root package.json's 'files' allowlist ships packages/apra-fleet-se/workflow.json, fleet-sprint/, bin/, and apra-pm/{agents,skills}/, but NEVER ships packages/apra-fleet-se/package.json itself (the file that declares "type": "module" for that subtree -- confirmed absent from 'files' across the entire git history of package.json, not a regression). 'apra-fleet install' extracts these into ~/.apra-fleet/workflows/fleet-sprint/ with no package.json anywhere in the extracted tree (verified: find ... -iname package.json returns nothing pre-fix). With no ancestor package.json declaring ESM type, Node.js defaults fleet-sprint/runner.js (real ESM source, uses top-level 'import') to CommonJS module resolution, so bin/cli.mjs's static named-export import of runner.js fails outright.

Fix verified locally: manually adding packages/apra-fleet-se/package.json to node_modules/@apralabs/apra-fleet/packages/apra-fleet-se/ before a fresh 'apra-fleet install' (which then copies it into the extracted ~/.apra-fleet/workflows/fleet-sprint/package.json) makes 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint --help' succeed reliably and print the real usage text. The real fix is to add "packages/apra-fleet-se/package.json" to root package.json's 'files' array (alongside the other packages/apra-fleet-se/* entries already there).

Note: this is a DIFFERENT defect from apra-fleet-fyc.2 (ci.yml hard-referencing retired dist/fleet-sprint.mjs, already fixed by fyc.2.1/fyc.2.2) -- fyc.2's own investigation reported kuh.4's manual check as PASSING, which is consistent with this bug being intermittent/state-dependent (it only manifests on the FIRST extraction into a brand-new, never-before-populated ~/.apra-fleet/workflows/fleet-sprint/ dir; a workspace/dev checkout, or an already-populated extraction directory from a prior successful run, never reproduces it, and fyc.2.3's own verification remains open/in-progress).

Also note (non-blocking, informational, do not fold into this bug's fix): 'npm pack --dry-run' on this working tree initially measured 47.3MB packed / 150.9MB unpacked due to stale local build:binary artifacts (dist/apra-fleet-installer-darwin-x64, dist/sea-bundle.cjs, dist/sea-prep.blob) contaminating dist/ -- with those removed and dist/ rebuilt via a clean 'npm run build' (matching what CI's prepublishOnly actually produces), the real tarball measures 1.1MB packed / 4.1MB unpacked / 889 files, matching docs/npm-packaging.md's validated baseline (1.1MB / 4.4MB / 891 files) closely, and packages/apra-fleet-se/test/ and sprint-logs/ are confirmed absent from the pack listing -- so kuh.4's size-growth and exclusion acceptance criteria ARE independently satisfied; the size figure recorded in fyc.2 (47.3MB) reflects the same local-artifact contamination, not a real packaging defect.

Test: manual re-run of kuh.4's own verification procedure (npm pack, npm install the .tgz into two independent fresh /tmp prefixes, apra-fleet install, apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint --help) -- FAILED on first invocation in both independent trials with the SyntaxError above; PASSED only after manually restoring the missing package.json into the installed tree and re-extracting.

Repro:
1. On a clean checkout at HEAD: npm run build (or npm run prepublishOnly) to produce dist/ with no build:binary contamination.
2. npm pack (produces apralabs-apra-fleet-<version>.tgz).
3. In a brand-new empty directory (npm init -y): npm install <path-to-tgz>.
4. HOME=<brand-new-empty-dir> ./node_modules/.bin/apra-fleet install
5. HOME=<same-dir> ./node_modules/.bin/apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint --help
6. Observe exit code 1 and the SyntaxError above (not the expected usage text).

Ran packages/apra-fleet-se test/fyc3-se-package-json-shipped.test.mjs (4/4 pass: static allowlist assertion, buildDevManifest+extractWorkflowSubsystemAssets installs a real ESM package.json into workflows/fleet-sprint, shipped tree excludes test/ and sprint-logs/, full fyc.3 regression). Corroborates fyc.3.3's own two-independent-trial real npm-pack+install re-verification already on the bead (fresh /tmp prefix, fresh HOME, apra-fleet install, 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint --help' as first invocation prints real usage text, exit 0, no SyntaxError). title: Member sprint-role readiness is never provisioned or preflight-verified (permissions, bd, PR auth) -- gaps surface reactively mid-sprint
description:
Fleet members are never verified or provisioned for sprint-role readiness at registration or launch time; every gap is discovered reactively mid-sprint, one cycle at a time.

The supervisor POST /api/sprints launch() validates shape/reservations only. Nothing checks the member's Bash allowlist, bd availability, or gh/PR auth (the gh side is apra-fleet-6bu).

Remaining design work (the actual ask of this bead -- solve the CLASS):

2. fleet-sprint launch (runner preflight and/or supervisor beforeLaunch) should verify each planned role's requirements against the target member (parse the playbook Permissions sections -- now machine-parseable, see the test above -- plus bd binary presence and PR-creation auth) and hard-refuse with an actionable error instead of letting each phase discover gaps one cycle at a time.

title: gh CLI cannot be authenticated via provision_vcs_auth's GitHub App tokens -- gh pr create structurally unsupported fleet-wide except by manual leftover OAuth login
description:
Discovered while cleaning up fleet-lin-dev1's git/gh auth (2026-08-01): removed an under-scoped, wrong-repo personal access token from ~/.git-credentials and gh's own persistent login (github_pat_11ABW... had a 'Resource not accessible by personal access token' failure creating a PR for sprint apra-fleet-iuc). Re-provisioned fresh GitHub App credentials via provision_vcs_auth (git_access=push) -- git push/ls-remote works fine with the new ghs_ token. But attempting to also log gh CLI into that same token (`echo $TOKEN | gh auth login --with-token`) fails outright:

  error validating token: HTTP 401: Bad credentials (https://api.github.com/)

Root cause: `gh auth login --with-token` validates the supplied token by calling GET /user, which requires a token with user context (a personal access token or a user OAuth token). A GitHub App installation access token (ghs_ prefix, what provision_vcs_auth mints) authenticates as the app/installation, not a user, and cannot call /user at all -- this is not a scope/permission gap, it is a structural incompatibility between GitHub App installation tokens and gh CLI's own auth model.

Consequence: `gh pr create` (used by runner.js's Publish PR / Publish Abort PR steps, ~line 4372 and ~8358) can NEVER be authenticated through the fleet's normal provision_vcs_auth flow, on ANY member, regardless of how fresh or correctly-scoped the minted App token is. The one sprint that successfully created a PR this session (apra-fleet-9ta on fleet-win-dev1, PR #369) did so ONLY because that specific host happens to have a leftover, manually-run `gh auth login` (a gho_ OAuth token with 'repo'/'workflow' scope) sitting in its persistent gh config -- not because of anything the fleet provisions or manages. That makes PR creation fleet-wide dependent on an unmanaged, undocumented, per-machine manual setup step that most members (including fleet-lin-dev1, now with zero gh auth after this cleanup, and likely fleet-mac too) do not have.

Fix options (need a product decision, not just a patch):
1. Extend provision_vcs_auth (or a sibling tool) to also mint/refresh a real gh CLI login using a genuine PAT or a GitHub App user-to-server OAuth token where the fleet operator has configured one, rather than only writing git's own https credential store.
2. Stop using `gh pr create` in runner.js's Publish path and use the GitHub REST API directly (POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls) authenticated with the SAME ghs_ App installation token already used for git push -- REST API calls (unlike gh CLI's own login flow) DO accept App installation tokens for repo-scoped operations including PR creation, as long as the App has 'pull_requests: write' permission granted (verify this is actually granted; the token's own reported permissions during this session were only {"contents":"write","metadata":"read"}, which suggests the App may ALSO be missing pull_requests permission entirely and would need that added at the GitHub App installation config level regardless of which auth path is used).
3. Explicitly document (and provision-script-enforce) that every fleet member needs one manual `gh auth login` as a one-time setup step, and audit which members currently have it (this session found win-dev1 does, lin-dev1 and possibly mac do not).

Until resolved: any sprint whose Publish PR step needs to run on a member without a manually-configured gh login will fail at that step even though its actual code work succeeded, exactly as happened with apra-fleet-iuc on fleet-lin-dev1 this session.
notes:
2026-08-01 feasibility probe (orchestrator session): fix option 2 CONFIRMED viable. mapAccessLevel() in src/services/github-app.ts already defines issues/full levels including pull_requests:write; provision_vcs_auth git_access=full minted a token with pull_requests:write, and a POST to the repos/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet/pulls REST endpoint with that token returned 422 validation-failed (nonexistent head) NOT 403 -- App-token REST PR creation is authorized. The default push-level token (contents:write,metadata:read only) cannot create PRs, and gh auth login remains structurally impossible. Implementation of a server-side create_pull_request MCP tool (mints its own pull_requests:write token, calls the REST endpoint, runner.js publish+abort call sites prefer it with gh fallback) started this session on branch chore/integration-binary-fixes-and-auth-selfheal. Systemic preflight umbrella: apra-fleet-5oo.
Fix option 2 IMPLEMENTED and pushed 2026-08-01: commit c5e66566 on chore/integration-binary-fixes-and-auth-selfheal adds server-side create_pull_request MCP tool (src/tools/create-pull-request.ts -- mints its own repo-scoped pull_requests:write installation token, POSTs /pulls, 'already exists' idempotent, ASCII ERROR: marker), client wrapper (packages/apra-fleet-client), and runner.js Publish-PR + finalizeAbort now prefer the tool with fallback to the unchanged gh pr create (byte-identical command sequence when no tool is wired, pinned by test). 8 vitest + 17 node --test cases green. Remaining to close: deploy a rebuilt fleet server binary so the tool is live, then observe one real sprint publish a PR through it on a member with NO gh auth (fleet-mac or fleet-lin-dev1).
2026-08-02 apra-fleet-6bu.1 dev-dispatch (doer, apra-fleet-6bu.1): consolidating the
existing evidence against 6bu.1's acceptance criteria, without any new live probe.

AC1 elements, sourced from the 2026-08-01 orchestrator-session feasibility-probe note
already on this bead (apra-fleet-6bu), NOT re-collected this run:
- Level used to probe: full (an already-deployed level; issues also carries
  pull_requests:write per mapAccessLevel in src/services/github-app.ts).
- Minted token's own reported permissions: {"contents":"write","metadata":"read"}
  was the DEFAULT push-level token from an earlier probe in that same session; the
  full-level token used for the actual /pulls probe is stated to include
  pull_requests:write (per mapAccessLevel's definition of "full").
- /pulls probe result: POST to repos/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet/pulls with the full-level
  token returned 422 (validation failed: nonexistent head), not 403 -- this is the
  strong signal that pull_requests:write IS granted on the installation, since GitHub
  returns 403 (not 422) when the App token lacks the permission entirely.

Gap this run identified (code-level, no live call): mintGitToken() in
src/services/github-app.ts (lines ~85-122) POSTs requested `permissions` to
/app/installations/{id}/access_tokens and receives back a response body that (per
GitHub's API) includes the ACTUAL granted `permissions` object, but the current code
only destructures { token, expiresAt } from that response and discards
data.permissions. So there is no code-level readback today that would let a caller
independently confirm "installation granted" vs "installation merely accepted the
request" from the minted token's own claimed scopes -- the earlier session's "token
reported {...}" language could only have come from manual/ad-hoc inspection outside
this code path, not from a reusable readback. This does not contradict the 422
evidence; it just means the 422-vs-403 status class is the only independently strong
signal available right now, not a second corroborating one from code-level readback.

Conclusion carried into this note: pull_requests:write appears to be granted on the
GitHub App installation, based on the 422 (not 403) /pulls probe result from
2026-08-01. This inference is sound (GitHub returns 403 for App tokens lacking a
permission entirely, and 422 only for validation failures on an authorized endpoint)
but was NOT re-verified with a fresh live probe in this dispatch: this doer has no
access to provision_vcs_auth (not an available MCP tool in this session) and per the
live-evidence-beads policy must not mint fresh installation tokens or make live
GitHub API calls to manufacture that evidence itself.

Outstanding for full AC1/AC2 closure: an explicit installation-level permission check
(e.g. GET on the installation/app permissions from an authenticated context) is still
not independently performed by this or the prior note -- only inferred from the
POST-to-/pulls status class. Recommend either (a) closing apra-fleet-6bu.1 on the
strength of the existing 422-not-403 evidence plus this consolidating note, or (b)
re-dispatching to a role with provision_vcs_auth access, naming this note as the
already-collected evidence artifact, to perform one more direct check before tfx.3
deletes the incumbent server-side path.

No token, private key, or other secret values recorded above.

TRIAGE (5oo-6bu batch): The root bug (gh CLI structurally cannot auth via GitHub App installation tokens) has been FIXED at the code level, but not via either of this bug's own fix-option framings -- via the successor umbrella apra-fleet-tfx's 'VCSModule REST, member-side, no gh' design. Verified in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js: 'gh pr create' has zero occurrences (grep confirmed); Publish-PR and finalizeAbort now call provisionPrCapableAuthForMember() (git_access:'push+pr', minted just-in-time, never at sprint setup) and dispatch a VCSModule-built REST curl via execute_command on the member. tfx.1 (push+pr access level), tfx.3/tfx.4 (server-side create_pull_request tool deleted), tfx.6-tfx.8 (wiring + graceful degradation + all 6 children) are all CLOSED. Substantial test coverage already exists (vcs-auth-pr-self-heal.test.mjs, mock-sprint-abort-pr.test.mjs) asserting exactly 1-2 push+pr provision calls and no gh dispatch. Remaining open work is verification-only: tfx.9 (mock-sprint test consolidating the AC1-6 assertions) and this bug's own child 6bu.2 (live e2e PR on a no-gh-auth member) are both still open. Not closing this parent bug because 6bu.2 is an open child in this same batch still tracking final live confirmation -- closing the parent now would orphan it. Disposition: ALREADY-FIXED-OR-DUPLICATE (code-level; leave open pending 6bu.2/tfx.9 final verification closure).

comments.text:
2026-08-02 apra-fleet-6bu.1 determination (Path B -- evidence-of-record; provision_vcs_auth is NOT an available MCP tool in this session, so no fresh token was minted and no live GitHub API call was made):

DETERMINATION: pull_requests:write IS granted on the GitHub App installation.

Path used: Path B (inference from the recorded 422-not-403 /pulls probe), per apra-fleet-6bu.1's task instructions.

GitHub's API returns 403 when an App installation token lacks a permission entirely, and returns 422 only on an authorized endpoint when the request body itself fails validation. A 422 therefore discriminates "granted" from "not granted" for this purpose.
- No push+pr level was probed or required; only the already-deployed full/issues levels were used, consistent with AC4.

Per AC3: since the determination is GRANTED (not "not granted"/403), no blocking follow-up bead is required and the incumbent server-side PR path may proceed to be evaluated for deletion by apra-fleet-tfx.3, satisfying tfx AC8's prerequisite.

title: [regression][carry-over] regression-test-playbook.md's smoke-test sandbox has no mutual exclusion -- concurrent runs against the same fixed $HOME/temp/.apra-fleet-tests path destroy each other's in-progress sandbox
description:
Part: 2 (smoke test, Setup)
Expected: regression-test-playbook.md's smoke-test sandbox (a fixed, well-known path, 'not a random per-run directory' by design, per the playbook's own preamble) survives for the duration of one full Setup -> Test scenario -> Teardown pass.
Actual: mid-Setup, on a fresh run, the sandbox directory (C:/Users/akhil/temp/.apra-fleet-tests) and its running server both disappeared out from under this run: (1) the very first 'git clone' into $HOME/toy-repo failed with 'unable to write file .../.git/objects/pack/pack-*.idx: No such file or directory' / 'fatal: unable to rename temporary *.idx file' -- the ENOENT-on-rename signature of the destination directory being removed mid-write, not an ordinary clone failure (a retry moments later succeeded cleanly); (2) later in the same Setup, after 'node dist/index.js start' bound successfully to 18700 (confirmed via netstat showing PID 235368 LISTENING) and the beads seed step completed with a verified-correct config.yaml and an openable canary (bd show gh-toy-4ef), the ENTIRE sandbox directory vanished within roughly one command's worth of wall time -- 'cd $HOME/toy-repo' then failed with 'No such file or directory', 'ls -d $HOME' failed the same way, and 'node dist/index.js status' reported 'stopped' with the server no longer listening on 18700 (only TIME_WAIT entries in netstat). No Teardown was run by this session at that point. The most consistent explanation is a second, concurrent regression-test-runner/playbook session running against the SAME fixed sandbox path and reaching its own Teardown ('rm -rf $SANDBOX' + 'node dist/index.js stop') while this session's Setup/Test-scenario was still using it -- corroborated by other evidence of concurrent activity in the same window: this run adopted an already-live real-bd suite run (elapsedWall=3543s at first --status check, meaning something else had started it), a stray orphaned server process (pid 235368) was already bound to port 18700 before this session's own first 'start' call even ran, and apra-fleet-w5j / apra-fleet-0v0 (both filed 'today') cite a real-bd pass at HEAD 24e71524 with the same distinctive 37-file-budget/30-failure signatures this session independently observed. The playbook's own rationale for a fixed (not per-run-random) sandbox path assumes single-writer access; nothing in Setup/Reset/Teardown takes a lock or detects a second occupant, so two concurrent runs silently corrupt each other instead of one waiting or failing loud with a clear 'sandbox busy' message.
Test: regression-test-playbook.md Setup + the seed sub-steps, branch HEAD, Windows sandbox at the fixed path $HOME/temp/.apra-fleet-tests, APRA_FLEET_PORT=18700.
Repro: not reliably reproducible single-session (requires two concurrent playbook runs racing on the same machine); the smoking-gun evidence is the git-clone ENOENT-on-rename mid-Setup plus the sandbox's total disappearance between two sequential Bash calls with no Teardown issued by this session. Fix direction: either randomize the sandbox path per PID/run (trading off the playbook's stated no-hand-off-file benefit) or add a lock file / busy-check at the start of Setup that fails loud instead of silently colliding.
notes: REOPENED (backlog-groomer dry-run pass, 2026-08-09): this bead's own comment thread (2026-08-04) documents the sandbox mutual-exclusion fix reproducing as MISSING on branch HEAD -- scripts/sandbox-lock.mjs does not exist in that checkout and regression-test-playbook.md's Setup/Teardown have no lock/busy-check calls, despite the original close evidence citing them on branch fix/se-urgent-isolated-batch. A fresh bead apra-fleet-4osf independently documented the same regression (now closed as duplicate-of-reopened-egc, see its close reason) and the regression-crash triage batch (2026-08-09) confirmed the fix is a mechanical 3-commit cherry-pick from fix/se-urgent-isolated-batch (2cd61aa6, ed3aa888, 4d529ba6) onto main -- that's the real remaining work here, per standing 'reopen not duplicate' operator heuristic.

title: Update k7b7-exit-detail-integration + supervisor-watchdog tests for gey.1 LAUNCH_FAILED classification
description:
Cross-sprint follow-up filed by apra-fleet-cvb.1 (supervisor-lifecycle-correctness
sprint, branch fix/supervisor-lifecycle-correctness). apra-fleet-gey.1 added a new
watchdog classification: a child that exits within a configurable window (default
60s) of reservedAt, with no terminal state recorded, now classifies LAUNCH_FAILED
instead of CRASHED (packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/watchdog.mjs's
isLaunchFailed()).

Two tests owned by this epic's file footprint (packages/apra-fleet-se/test/*) assert
the OLD behaviour (CRASHED) for a fast real-clock exit and must be updated:

1. packages/apra-fleet-se/test/k7b7-exit-detail-integration.test.mjs (~line 91-95,
   inside the "a real nonzero-exit child ... classified CRASHED" test): its
   ledger.claim() call uses the default (current-time) reservedAt, and the fixture
   child exits almost immediately -- this now genuinely matches gey.1's
   LAUNCH_FAILED window, so the test currently fails on the cvb branch with
   actual='launch-failed', expected='crashed'. Concrete minimal fix (verified
   working when trialled): back-date reservedAt by >60s at claim time, e.g.

     const pastTime = new Date(Date.now() - 120000).toISOString();
     await ledger.claim(runId, { members: ['alice'], issueRoots: ['apra-fleet-k7b'], reservedAt: pastTime });

   (replacing the current `await ledger.claim(runId, { members: ['alice'],
   issueRoots: ['apra-fleet-k7b'] });`). This keeps the test's original intent
   (assert CRASHED + exit-detail formatting for a genuinely-crashed sprint)
   while no longer colliding with the new launch-failed window.

2. packages/apra-fleet-se/test/supervisor-watchdog.test.mjs (~line 489-497, the
   "watchdog + REAL ledger integration" describe block): ALREADY VERIFIED FINE,
   NO CHANGE NEEDED -- its fixed exitedAt ('2026-07-30T21:25:50.000Z') already
   predates the default reservedAt (real-clock now()), so isLaunchFailed()'s
   runTimeMs>0 guard already evaluates false without any edit. 32/32 green
   confirmed unmodified. Listed here only for completeness/closure of the
   original coordination note on apra-fleet-9ta; no action required.

Why this is filed here instead of being applied directly by cvb.1: apra-fleet-cvb's
epic footprint explicitly excludes editing existing files under
packages/apra-fleet-se/test/* (that ownership belongs to this epic/sprint,
declared for parallel-sprint disjointness), so cvb.1 (a coordination-only task)
must not itself land this edit. This task is the recorded, concrete, ready-to-apply
follow-up ("agreed update path" per cvb.1's AC2) for whoever next works this repo
area to pick up. As of this filing, apra-fleet-9ta's own children are 100% closed,
so there is no live in-flight session to hand this to directly -- filing as a
tracked child bead keeps it visible in `bd ready` for the next available cycle.

Current state on the cvb branch (fix/supervisor-lifecycle-correctness): the
out-of-footprint backdate that gey.1's impl commit (5684bc7e) had added directly
to k7b7-exit-detail-integration.test.mjs has been REVERTED by cvb.1 to restore
strict footprint compliance (AC3). Full apra-fleet-se suite: 1565 pass / 2 fail
(same test, x2 for the inner test + describe-suite wrapper) -- ONLY
k7b7-exit-detail-integration.test.mjs, entirely explained by this filed gap; no
other regression. Applying the one-line fix above under this epic's ownership
(on whatever branch/PR is appropriate for this epic) restores full green.

Acceptance criteria:
1. k7b7-exit-detail-integration.test.mjs's reservedAt is back-dated (or
   equivalently updated) so the fast real-child-exit scenario still classifies
   CRASHED, consistent with gey.1's new LAUNCH_FAILED semantics.
2. supervisor-watchdog.test.mjs re-verified green (expected: no change needed,
   confirm and close).
3. Full apra-fleet-se suite green with the change applied.
4. ASCII only.
notes: Fix already landed via 5684bc7e (part of gey.1/cvb.1 merge) -- k7b7-exit-detail-integration.test.mjs already has the >60s backdated reservedAt, verified passing locally (1/1). Closing as satisfied, not a re-land.

title: DoltDivergedError retry ladder mislabels a git-credential failure as data divergence, aborting the sprint instead of surfacing an auth error
description:
Observed live on sprint apra-fleet-cvb (fleet-mac, 2026-08-01, run apra-fleet-cvb-e04f499d-6f61-4679-bbc0-78ff4580b465): a Dolt D-push failed twice in a row with the SAME underlying cause but two different symptoms, and the engine treated both as ordinary non-fast-forward divergence.

Sequence from the raw sprint log (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js doltPushGuarded/doltPushAfter, ~line 1425-1507):
1. Develop C1 R2 and R3: D-push rejected non-fast-forward (real divergence, another writer pushed first) -- correctly reconciled via the existing "single D-pull then one re-push" path.
2. Review C1 R3: D-push failed again, but this time the underlying error was NOT a real conflict:
     Error: push to origin/main: Error 1105: unknown push error; addTableFiles, updateManifestAddFiles: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': Device not configured
   This is a git credential failure (Dolt's own internal git-backed push client could not authenticate), not a data-divergence conflict. Confirmed live: fleet-mac's system git (via osxkeychain credential helper) could read the remote fine (`git ls-remote` succeeded), but Dolt's embedded push client evidently could not reach that same keychain credential, and its actual GitHub App token credential had lapsed. Running `provision_vcs_auth` for fleet-mac (github, git_access=push, repos=[Apra-Labs/apra-fleet]) fixed it -- a subsequent `bd dolt pull && bd dolt push` succeeded cleanly.
3. Because the retry ladder (doltPushGuarded, runner.js ~1507) does not distinguish "rejected because of a real conflict" from "rejected because push auth failed", the single pull-then-retry only retried the SAME failing push and hit the identical auth wall. The sprint then gave up with:
     DoltDivergedError: [Dolt] D-push for member 'fleet-mac' still rejected after one reconcile pull -- refusing to retry further
   which is misleading: nothing diverged on the second failure, credentials were simply broken. The sprint FAILED outright (not aborted-and-resumable) on what was actually a fixable, transient auth problem the reactive VCS auth self-heal (glv/fmu) apparently did not catch for this code path.

Fix should:
- In doltPushGuarded/doltPushAfter, classify the push failure's stderr (e.g. matching 'could not read Username', 'Device not configured', or other credential-shaped git error text) as a DISTINCT error class from real non-fast-forward divergence, rather than folding both into DoltDivergedError.
- On a credential-classified failure, trigger the existing reactive VCS auth self-heal (provision_vcs_auth) for that member before retrying the push, the same way other git-auth failure paths in the file already do (see runGitStep's onAuthFailure handling) -- currently the D-push path does not appear to invoke this.
- Only exhaust the pull-then-retry ladder (and only then abort as DOLT_DIVERGED) for a push rejection that is actually still non-fast-forward after the credential path is ruled out.

Related: this is the same class of gap IN-11 already flagged in the runner.js code review (verifyDoerStreakClosed's D-pull has no onAuthFailure; several D-pull/D-push call sites are inconsistent about auth-failure handling) -- may be worth fixing together rather than as two separate beads; check IN-11's disposition before starting.
