title: [H] Route sprint publish through VCSModule: pluggable publish, no host-sniffing, no-remote safe
description:
THEME: H (VCS abstraction layer). DEPENDS ON the VCSModule abstraction bead -- do not start until capabilities() exists.

PROBLEM
Three related defects, all in the sprint's publish surface, all dissolved by giving VCSModule a `publish` service instead of letting the runner sniff hosts and shell out to `gh` directly.

EVIDENCE (verbatim, anchored to function/construct -- runner.js is under concurrent comment-only rewrite, so do NOT trust line numbers)

1. HOST-SNIFFING BY LITERAL. runner.js -> isHostedGithubRemote():
     return /^(https?:\/\/([^/@\s]+@)?github\.com\/|git@github\.com:|ssh:\/\/git@github\.com\/)/i.test(url);
   The fail-closed non-hosted branch in the Publish PR step is GOOD and should be preserved in spirit -- it logs "origin remote '...' is not a gh-hostable GitHub remote -- skipping PR creation entirely", closes each target issue directly via `bd close` when the final verdict is PASS, and follows with a doltPushAfter. But:
     - GitHub Enterprise (github.mycorp.com) matches NOTHING, so PRs are silently skipped forever with only a log line, even though `gh pr create` would work there.
     - Every non-GitHub project's only publish artifact is a pushed branch.
   Replace the regex with capabilities().canOpenPullRequest.

2. ABORT PATH NEVER GOT THE FIX. runner.js -> finalizeAbort() calls
     `gh pr create --base "${baseBranch}" --head "${branch}" --title "${prTitle}" --body "${prBody}"`
   with NO isHostedGithubRemote() gate at all -- the fix credited in-comment to apra-fleet-eft.64.1 was applied only to the PASS/FAIL Publish PR step. It does not kill the run (main()'s catch logs "finalizeAbort() failed for this abort (...); writing the terminal history record with no PR lookup"), but every non-GitHub abort burns a guaranteed-failing dispatch and the operator's last log line is a misleading "[Publish Abort PR Failed] gh pr create failed ..." instead of the actual abort cause.

3. NO-REMOTE REPO REPORTS A FALSE ABORT. The Publish PR step opens with
     await command(`git push -u origin ${validated.branch}`, { member_name: orchestratorMember, silent: true, label: ... })
   with NO failSoft. On a local-only git repo -- which legitimately satisfies requirement (1) "uses git" -- this throws CommandError, which `extends WorkflowError` (confirmed in packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/workflow/errors.mjs), so isTypedAbortError() returns true and the run records verdict: 'ABORTED' DESPITE having reached a PASS final verdict. finalizeAbort()'s own `git fetch origin ${baseBranch}` then fails too.
   The prompt layer is already ahead of the engine here -- harvester.md says: "Skip this step if the repo has no remote (local-only transport, git remote prints nothing)".

4. HARDCODED REMOTE NAME. `origin` is a literal at every site: `git fetch origin ${baseBranch}`, `git rev-list --count origin/${baseBranch}..${branch}`, `git remote get-url origin`, `git push -u origin ${branch}`. A project using `upstream` fails. Derive from branch tracking config or accept a --remote arg.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- One publish code path shared by the PASS/FAIL step and finalizeAbort(); neither references `gh` or a host literal directly.
- Default publish behaviour with no PR capability = git push only, sprint still terminates with its TRUE verdict.
- GitHub Enterprise opens PRs.
- GitLab / Azure DevOps push and close target issues cleanly (existing direct-close + doltPushAfter behaviour preserved).
- A repo with NO remote finishes with its true PASS/FAIL verdict, not ABORTED; no push or publish is attempted.
- Remote name is configurable; `origin` is only a fallback default.

Resolves review findings MAJOR-3, MAJOR-4, MAJOR-5, MINOR-11.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-09 (batch 647): READY-AS-IS, but SCOPE IS NOW MUCH SMALLER -- 3 of the 4 listed defects are already fixed by the apra-fleet-647.1 VCSModule epic (now CLOSED), so this bead is unblocked and should be re-read before anyone starts. Verified at source in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js: (1) HOST-SNIFFING -- FIXED: isHostedGithubRemote() no longer exists (grep finds only a comment saying the regexes were deleted and delegated to VCSModule.classifyFailure); the Publish PR step now does vcsCapabilities(originUrl).canOpenPullRequest (~line 9053), which routes through vcs-providers/ descriptors, so GitHub Enterprise/other hosts are a provider-table question, not a literal. (2) ABORT PATH -- FIXED: finalizeAbort() now resolves origin failSoft and applies the SAME capabilities gate (~lines 4406-4418) with an explicit 'cannot open a pull request ... skipping [ABORTED] PR creation; branch is still pushed' log; no bare 'gh pr create' remains anywhere in fleet-sprint (grep for 'gh pr create' -> zero hits in runner.js/vcs-module.mjs/vcs-providers/*). (3) NO-REMOTE FALSE ABORT -- FIXED: the Publish PR push is now failSoft with a bounded POST_DISPATCH_SYNC_RETRY_DELAYS_MS retry loop and, on exhaustion, returns the sprint's TRUE verdict with pushed:false instead of throwing a CommandError into the ABORTED path. STILL OPEN: (4) hardcoded remote name -- 'origin' is still a literal at every site (git fetch origin, git rev-list --count origin/BASE..BRANCH, git remote get-url origin, git push -u origin) in both finalizeAbort() and the Publish step, and bin/cli.mjs has no --remote flag (grep 'remote' in bin/cli.mjs -> zero hits). Also still unmet: the AC 'ONE publish code path shared by the PASS/FAIL step and finalizeAbort()' -- the two sites still duplicate the capability gate and push logic independently; and the non-hosted log line still says the stale 'is not a gh-hostable GitHub remote', which now misdescribes what the capability check actually tests. Remaining work is roughly: extract a shared publish helper, thread a configurable remote (origin as fallback default), and refresh that log string. Suggest downgrading metadata size from M to S. title: [epic] VCSModule (skin-gut): provider-agnostic VCS interface + error taxonomy, hides GitHub-specific logic behind a swappable concrete implementation
description:
THEME: H (VCS abstraction layer).

PROBLEM
The runner parses raw git/gh stderr itself and hardcodes GitHub as the VCS provider. Every new VCS backend (Azure DevOps Git is next in line, then Bitbucket/GitLab) currently means editing regex lists inside runner.js. provision_vcs_auth is a FLEET feature that can and should be extended to other providers; the runner must ask the member registry, not assert. Equally, the typed errors fleet throws across this boundary must not be GitHub-flavoured, and the ability to understand any git error must be delegated to an abstraction layer rather than pattern-matched in the runner's codebase.

EVIDENCE (verbatim, anchored to function/construct -- runner.js is under concurrent comment-only rewrite, so do NOT trust line numbers)

1. Hardcoded provider. runner.js -> provisionVcsAuthForMember():
     // TODO: derive provider/github_mode from the member's persisted
     // vcsProvider instead of hardcoding GitHub App mode.
     provider: 'github', github_mode: 'github-app',
   Shared by BOTH callers: createVcsAuthSelfHealCallback() (REACTIVE, fires on an 'auth' classification) and createVcsAuthPreflightCallback() (PROACTIVE, pre-dispatch, correctly documented "NEVER throws").
   Note the sibling parseOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl() in the same file WAS generalized -- "Deliberately target-agnostic: fleet-sprint develops many different repos, so the `repos` argument passed to provision_vcs_auth must be DERIVED at runtime from the member's own git remote, never hardcoded to a literal repo name." So the repo derivation is clean; only the provider was left behind.

2. Failure classification lives in the runner. runner.js -> `const GIT_AUTH_PATTERNS` and its verbatim twin `const DOLT_AUTH_PATTERNS` (commented "mirrors GIT_AUTH_PATTERNS above. `bd dolt push` shells out to git under the hood"). Consumed by classifyGitFailure() / runGitStep() / runDoltStep().
   Roughly half the list is generic git/OpenSSH text that DOES port:
     /could not read Username for/i, /could not read Password for/i,
     /Authentication failed/i, /Permission denied \(publickey\)/i,
     /terminal prompts disabled/i, /support for password authentication was removed/i
   The rest are GitHub literals:
     /remote: Invalid username or (token|password)/i
     /Bad credentials/i

3. A classification MISS is sprint-fatal, not degraded. classifyGitFailure() falls through to 'unknown' when nothing matches, and runGitStep()'s own contract states: "A diverged (or unknown) failure is returned immediately, never retried." Therefore on:
     - Azure DevOps: TF401019 / transport-dependent auth text
     - GitLab: "HTTP Basic: Access denied"
     - Bitbucket: "Invalid or expired app password"
     - Gitea: "401 Unauthorized"
   a routine token expiry classifies 'unknown' -> NO transient retry, NO one-shot self-heal, immediate GitSyncError/DoltSyncError -> SPRINT ABORT. This is the single highest-value fix in the review.

4. Typed errors must stop being GitHub-flavoured. Anything fleet throws across this boundary should name a provider-neutral condition, with the raw provider text carried as a DETAIL, never as the thing downstream code pattern-matches on.

PROPOSED SHAPE
A VCSModule abstraction providing fixed services over git / gh / az repos / future CLIs:
  - resolveProvider(member) -- from the member registry; NO default, no guessing
  - provisionAuth(member, { scope }) -- wraps provision_vcs_auth using the provider's own mode vocabulary (github-app, PAT, az CLI, etc.)
  - classifyFailure(rawStderr) -> { kind, providerCode, retryable } -- THE ONLY place VCS stderr is ever parsed; per-provider concrete implementations
  - capabilities(remoteUrl) -> { hasRemote, canOpenPullRequest, host } -- replaces host-sniffing (consumed by the publish child bead)
Neutral error kinds: AUTH_EXPIRED, AUTH_DENIED, DIVERGED, TRANSIENT, NO_REMOTE, UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION.
Concrete impls, day one: GitHubVCS (incl. GitHub Enterprise) and GenericGitVCS (push-only fallback, no PR API). Then AzureDevOpsVCS, BitbucketVCS, GitLabVCS.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- runner.js contains ZERO VCS-vendor regexes and ZERO provider literals.
- GIT_AUTH_PATTERNS and DOLT_AUTH_PATTERNS are deleted from runner.js and reborn as per-provider tables inside the module.
- provider/mode for provision_vcs_auth is read from the member registry; if a member has no registered provider, provisioning is SKIPPED (not defaulted to GitHub).
- A member registered with a non-GitHub provider self-heals a simulated auth failure end-to-end in a test.
- Adding a new provider requires touching no file under packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/.
- Typed errors crossing the fleet boundary carry provider-neutral kinds; raw provider text appears only in details.

Resolves review findings BLOCKER-1 and BLOCKER-2.
notes:
Confirmed 2026-08-02 (backlog-groomer research pass) as the sibling epic to apra-fleet-417 (TaskDBModule) in the runner.js dual-componentization effort. Retitled/annotated to explicitly name the same 'skin-gut' pattern now on 417: this bead's public interface (resolveProvider/provisionAuth/classifyFailure/capabilities + neutral error kinds like AUTH_EXPIRED/DIVERGED/TRANSIENT) is the 'skin' that runner.js calls; GitHubVCS is the first concrete 'gut' implementation, with GenericGitVCS/AzureDevOpsVCS/BitbucketVCS/GitLabVCS as swappable follow-on guts behind the same interface -- no github-specific vocabulary should leak through the interface shape. Sequencing: do apra-fleet-417 (TaskDBModule) FIRST -- it already has a complete design pass responding to two live sprint-killing incidents, and cleanly separating the dolt-half of withGitSync() first makes this epic's own git/gh call-site inventory in runner.js easier to scope without re-inventing dolt/git bracket-ordering logic mid-refactor. See also: a real collision risk was found with apra-fleet-tfx.8 (an already-in-flight, narrower thread independently building a 'VCSModule'-shaped REST-dispatch shim for PR creation without depending on this bead) -- tracked separately, see the new reconciliation bead just filed against apra-fleet-647.

Added a blocks edge (tfx.8 blocks 647.1) so this epic's implementation cannot start until tfx.8's landed shim is visible to whoever picks this up.

When implementing 647.1's classifyFailure()/provisionAuth()/capabilities() interface, RECONCILE with tfx.8's already-landed code rather than inventing a second, independent PR-creation path:
- packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js: raiseVcsPrForMember(), provisionPrCapableAuthForMember(), readMemberVcsCredentialToken(), parseVcsCurlOutput() (the just-in-time push+pr credential mint + VCSModule-built curl dispatch for PR creation).
- packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/vcs-module.mjs: buildCreatePrCommand() (the orchestrator-side command builder tfx.8 already wired in).

title: [epic] Certify fleet-sprint as a generic git+beads sprint runner (de-overfit from apra-fleet dogfooding)
description:
fleet-sprint is meant to be a GENERIC autonomous sprint runner for ANY software project satisfying exactly two requirements: (1) it uses git -- explicitly git, NOT GitHub; (2) it uses beads (the bd issue tracker). It is developed by dogfooding on apra-fleet itself.

A read-only product-architecture review (2026-07-31) of the engine (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js, contracts.mjs, bin/cli.mjs), the vendored role prompts (packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/agents/*.md), and the fleet-sprint docs/skills audited that promise. Verdict: NOT handoff-ready today, but closer than expected.

Verified GENERIC and clean (no action needed):
- validateArgs(): no hardcoded member names, no default branch, base_branch is REQUIRED, no apra-fleet issue-prefix. Injection-safe patterns (BRANCH_NAME_PATTERN / ISSUE_ID_PATTERN / GOAL_PATTERN) are content-agnostic.
- bin/cli.mjs: no member/branch/repo defaults. Every 'apra-fleet-*' string is a bead ID in a comment or an npm package name (the engine's own identity).
- Model-tier resolution: FIXED_ROLE_TIER uses 'cheap'|'standard'|'premium' keywords resolved PER MEMBER server-side by resolveModelForTier(). Doc comment is explicit this exists to avoid "a provider-specific model literal being passed verbatim to a member where it means nothing". Genuinely provider-agnostic.
- parseOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl(): handles https, ssh://, and scp-like syntax host-agnostically; documented "Deliberately target-agnostic".
- Beads sync degradation: doltPushAfter() gates on isMemberSyncRemoteConfigured() and returns { skipped: true, reason: 'no-remote' } rather than failing. DOLT_EMPTY_REMOTE_PATTERNS explicitly handles "a sync.remote derived from a bare git-only mirror that Dolt itself has never pushed a branch into".
- Bead-ID handling: allocateChildId() derives from parentId (const prefix = `${parentId}.`); no literal prefix anywhere. Prompts forbid prefix-stripping.
- Prompt language-agnosticism: reviewer.md ("npm run build  # or cargo build, go build, etc.", "adapt to project's build system") and doer.md are correctly generalized. planner.md, plan-reviewer.md, harvester.md, _shared/GRAPH-SEMANTICS.md contain ZERO GitHub, npm, or apra-fleet references.
- node -e on members (probeFileExists, stageCommandBodyMemberSide): requires Node on FLEET MEMBERS, not in the target project's toolchain. Deliberately shell-portable ("inert as syntax in POSIX shells, PowerShell, and cmd.exe alike", base64 single-argv-token). NOT a project-language assumption.
- Playbook ABSENCE handling: probe is failSoft, phases skip non-fatally, all three roles refuse to improvise. This design is right.
- `bd remember` telemetry: NOT used by fleet-sprint at all (only apra-pm/.claude/workflows/auto-sprint.js and skills/pm/cost.md). Non-finding.

Explicitly NOT a finding (owner ruling, 2026-07-31): the apra-fleet instances of deploy.md / integ-test-playbook.md / regression-test-playbook.md at repo root are SUPPOSED to be apra-fleet-specific and are correct as-is. They demonstrate how the system works. There is no canonical playbook shape to converge on -- a project whose deploy needs a second member to flash a device, or whose integ test needs a different-OS host, will legitimately have a different playbook. What is missing is the SECTION CONTRACT documentation and starter templates, tracked separately.

Children of this epic carry the remediation. Priority order: the VCSModule abstraction (and the publish step that depends on it) are the handoff blockers; the rest are documentation and hygiene.

title: watchdog misclassifies a cleanly-finished sprint as 'crashed' -- terminal-state write uses branch name as runId, not sprintId
description:
ROOT CAUSE (found during win-dev1 sprint forensics, 2026-07-31): the workflow
engine's own terminal-state write (packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/viewer/
run-state-paths.mjs) uses whatever `runId` value it was given as the filename
key under <serviceDataDir>/old_runs/<runId>.json (serviceDataDir resolves via
getFleetDataDir() -> ~/.apra-fleet/data, see server-resolution.mjs). Before
apra-fleet-k7b.1 (per-request sprintId minted BEFORE spawn, forwarded into the
child's own argv as --run-id), a relaunch/legacy path can still leave a child
falling back to reusing the BRANCH NAME (e.g. "fix/fleet-sprint-stabilization")
as its internal runId instead of the sprintId the ledger/watchdog/live /state
route all key off of.

Because path.join(oldRunsDir, runId + '.json') does not sanitize slashes, a
branch-name runId containing '/' silently creates a NESTED file
(old_runs/fix/fleet-sprint-stabilization.json) instead of a flat file at the
path the watchdog's hasTerminalState() lookup actually checks
(old_runs/<sprintId>.json). The watchdog's classification in watchdog.mjs is:
once the child PID is gone, status is "finished" iff old_runs/<runId>.json
exists at the expected flat path, else "crashed". Since the real terminal
record exists (status:"success", a full self-assessed FAIL verdict with
detailed reasoning) but at the wrong path, the watchdog reports "crashed" for
a sprint that in fact completed and self-terminated cleanly. This is a lookup-
key bug, not an actual process crash.

Confirmed via direct inspection of ~/.apra-fleet/data/{running,old_runs}/ for
the win-dev1 sprint cross-referenced against watchdog.mjs's WATCHDOG_STATUS
classification logic.

SUGGESTED FIX: either (a) always key terminal-state writes by the ledger's
sprintId (never fall back to branch name) now that k7b.1 mints it pre-spawn
for every launch path including relaunch, or (b) sanitize/reject any runId
containing a path separator before using it as a filename component, or
ideally both -- (a) closes the actual gap, (b) is a defensive backstop against
any other runId-as-filename call site with the same class of bug.
notes: Impl+test landed via 5684bc7e (cvb.3 sanitizeRunIdForFilename backstop + cvb.4 test), confirmed present in run-state-paths.mjs on integration. Closing.

title: [impl] runner.js + integ-test-playbook.md: deterministic children-done/parent-open focus list for Integ Test
description:
Implementation task for apra-fleet-ml4's fix scope. Two coupled changes:

1. runner.js (orchestrator engine, plain code -- no agent dispatch): before
   the Integ Test dispatch step, add a function that queries bd for every
   bead whose direct children are ALL closed, but which is itself still
   open (independent of issue_type). Pass this computed list into the
   integ-test-runner dispatch prompt as an explicit, fixed focus list.
   Empty list is a normal, successful outcome (skip dispatch or report
   zero-in-scope, mirroring integ-test-playbook.md's existing empty-
   feature-list handling).

2. integ-test-playbook.md: rewrite the Procedure section to consume the
   orchestrator-provided focus list directly (same 'test ONLY those, one at
   a time, do not derive the list yourself' pattern already used for
   feature ids) instead of self-deriving scope via
   'bd list --type=feature --status=open'. For each focused parent: verify
   its acceptance criteria against the sprint branch working tree, then
   close it if satisfied, file a new CHILD bead under it (not a new
   top-level bug) if verification finds a real gap/bug, or leave it open
   with a documented reason if inconclusive.

3. packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/agents/integ-test-runner.md: update the
   role description to match -- scope is GIVEN by the orchestrator, never
   self-discovered; 'close a parent once its children are verified', not
   'close a feature'.

Acceptance criteria:
- runner.js has a pure function (unit-testable without a dispatch) that,
  given a bd scope tree snapshot, returns exactly the set of beads with
  100% closed direct children and open status themselves.
- That function's output is what gets passed into the Integ Test dispatch
  prompt -- confirmed by a test asserting the dispatch prompt contains the
  computed list, not a fresh bd query run by the prompt/runner itself.
- integ-test-playbook.md no longer contains 'bd list --type=feature' as a
  scoping mechanism.
- A test sprint scenario with zero type=feature beads but at least one
  fully-child-closed parent bead results in that parent being verified and
  closed (or extended with a new child bead), not a no-op Integ Test pass.
acceptance_criteria: 1) runner.js exposes a pure, unit-tested function returning beads with all-closed children + open self-status. 2) Integ Test dispatch prompt is built from that function's output, not a fresh runner-side bd query. 3) integ-test-playbook.md's Procedure section consumes an orchestrator-provided list, with 'bd list --type=feature' removed as a scoping mechanism. 4) integ-test-runner.md's role description matches (verify-and-close-parent, not close-a-feature). 5) A regression test proves a zero-feature, one-fully-closed-parent scenario results in real verification/closure, not a no-op.

All meaningful implementation work is done under jfo/ml4, which are both already closed. Classification: ALREADY-FIXED-OR-DUPLICATE (duplicate of closed apra-fleet-jfo / apra-fleet-ml4). title: Auto-grant runbook-declared permissions via compose_permissions instead of hand-editing settings.json
description:
Replaces the original one-time settings.json edit (wrong shape -- see notes). deploy.md, integ-test-playbook.md, and regression-test-playbook.md each already carry a `## Permissions` section listing required `Bash(...)` prefixes as bullets. Make that the single source of truth and wire it into compose_permissions instead of hand-maintaining copies in any settings file.

MECHANISM:
compose_permissions already supports a reactive grant mode: `grant: string[]` + `project_folder` (merges into that project's `permissions.json` ledger, then writes `.claude/settings.local.json` -- never `settings.json`, confirmed via claude.ts's `permissionConfigPaths()`).

1. At Sprint Setup, before a member's first Deploy/Integ-Test/Regression-Test dispatch, parse the union of `## Permissions` bullets from whichever playbooks that member's role will run this sprint.
2. Call `compose_permissions(member, grant=[...], grant_reason='<playbook> requirements', project_folder=<repo root>)`.
3. Grants land in the project's `permissions.json` ledger, so they're remembered across relaunches instead of re-granted from scratch every time.

KNOWN RISK -- verify before relying on this: compose_permissions's reactive-grant write path (`deliverConfigFile`'s POSIX branch, a `cat > file << EOF` heredoc sent as one execCommand string) was observed silently no-op'ing on fleet-lin-dev1 this session -- reported "Granted" but settings.local.json's mtime never changed. This design depends on that path actually persisting; add a read-back verification after write so a silent failure surfaces instead of a false "Granted" report.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. deploy.md's Step 0 permission check passes on a member with no manually pre-configured settings.local.json, purely from an automatic Sprint-Setup compose_permissions call.
2. compose_permissions's grant path is verified to actually persist (read the file back after writing, don't trust the write command's exit code alone).
3. settings.json is never touched.
4. Mechanism generalizes to integ-test-playbook.md and regression-test-playbook.md's own Permissions sections, not just deploy.md.
5. Grants persist in the project's permissions.json ledger across sprint relaunches.
notes: Rewritten 2026-08-10: superseded the original settings.json-edit approach per user direction -- one-time commits to the tracked settings.json don't scale and the user's standing rule is settings.json is never touched. New scope wires deploy/integ-test/regression-test playbooks' existing '## Permissions' sections into compose_permissions's reactive grant mode (grant + project_folder), so any project's runbook is self-describing and permissions are approved once per project via the existing permissions.json ledger. Prompted by a live win-dev1 Deploy failure this session traced to a genuinely different root cause (apra-fleet start's Windows scheduled task, see apra-fleet-i8qj / deploy.md's run-not-start fix) -- xuo.12 was not that bug, but the permission-declaration gap it targets is real and still worth fixing properly.

title: Integ Test phase: orchestrator must deterministically feed a 'children-done, parent-open' focus list; type=feature scoping is structurally wrong
description:
CORRECTED root cause (operator clarification, 2026-07-31, superseding the original narrower framing of this bead and consolidating apra-fleet-8qd into it): the workflow's ORIGINAL intent has always been that the Integ Test phase closes parent beads once all their tasks underneath are done -- not that it scopes itself by type=feature. That original intent was never actually implemented; both halves of the mechanism are wrong today:

1. SELECTION -- PLAIN CODE IN THE ORCHESTRATOR ENGINE, NOT AN LLM CALL:
   Before dispatching Integ Test, runner.js itself (the orchestrator's own
   deterministic code, the same layer that already runs bd queries like
   bdListScoped()'s parent-edge BFS walk elsewhere) computes the list of
   'ready for integration testing' parent issues: any bead whose direct
   children are ALL closed/done, but which is ITSELF still open. This is a
   plain bd list/bd show query plus a filter, executed mechanically by the
   engine -- there is NO agent, NO LLM judgment call, and NO prompt involved
   in selection at all. It is NOT integ-test-runner's job to discover this
   list (today's bd list --type=feature --status=open is itself an LLM-
   dispatched agent doing ad-hoc discovery, which is exactly the anti-
   pattern being fixed here), and it is NOT scoped to 'what was touched this
   cycle' -- a parent finished 2 cycles ago and never revisited is exactly
   as in-scope as one finished this cycle. The orchestrator then hands this
   already-computed, fixed list to the dispatched runner explicitly in its
   dispatch prompt: 'focus your integration testing on these issues: [...]'.

2. VERIFICATION -- this is the one and only place an LLM (integ-test-runner)
   is involved:
   For each parent issue in that orchestrator-computed list, integ-test-
   runner does focused testing/verification of that parent's own acceptance
   criteria (now that its children all claim to satisfy it) and then
   decides: (a) close the parent if verification passes, (b) file a new
   child bead under that parent if verification finds a real gap, bug, or
   missing coverage (not a generic new top-level bug), or (c) leave it open
   with a clear reason if verification is inconclusive. This replaces
   integ-test-playbook.md's current 'bd list --type=feature --status=open'
   scoping (see apra-fleet-8qd, now consolidated here) entirely -- that
   query was never the right mechanism; the correct scope was always
   'children done, parent open', independent of issue_type, and computed
   by the engine, not discovered by the agent.

Evidence this has been broken end-to-end (win-dev1 sprint, apra-fleet-xuo,
2026-07-31 forensic analysis):
  - integ-test-runner ran 4 times (cycles C2-C5), closed ZERO features,
    every time -- structurally guaranteed to find nothing under the current
    type=feature query, since this sprint's entire 34-bead scope tree is
    type=task/type=bug.
  - Meanwhile f34, ou7, 2cc, and 3pb each have 100% of their children
    closed and sat open the whole time, completely unexamined by Integ
    Test, because nothing was ever looking for exactly that shape.
  - Real, wasted wall-clock cost: 22-76 real minutes per no-op dispatch.

Fix scope: add a plain deterministic function to runner.js (no agent
dispatch involved) that computes the children-done/parent-open list before
the Integ Test dispatch step, pass that list into the dispatch prompt
explicitly, and rewrite integ-test-playbook.md's Procedure section to
consume that list directly instead of self-deriving scope via bd list
--type=feature. Update integ-test-runner.md's role description to match
(verify parent, close or extend, not 'close a feature'; scope is GIVEN,

title: [integ] check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs resolvesInsideSandbox() mis-resolves file:// URLs with drive letters on Windows, false-FAILs safe sandbox paths
description:

Expected: node scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs <toy-repo> should confirm the Dolt sync.remote, Dolt remote list, and git origin all resolve INSIDE the sandbox root when they genuinely do, printing OK and exiting 0.
Actual: on Windows, after a clean ## Setup run (install/start/clone/seed all succeeded, sandbox-seed-beads.mjs printed '[sandbox-seed] OK'), the checker FAILS both the sync.remote check and the git-origin check even though both values manually verify as inside the sandbox root:
  - sync.remote = file:///C:/Users/akhil/temp/.apra-fleet-tests/.apra-fleet-toy-dolt-remote (config.yaml)
  - git origin  = file:///c/Users/akhil/temp/.apra-fleet-tests/.apra-fleet-toy-origin.git (git remote get-url origin)
  - bd dolt remote list --json origin.url = file://C:/Users/akhil/temp/.apra-fleet-tests/.apra-fleet-toy-dolt-remote
Sandbox root = C:/Users/akhil/temp/.apra-fleet-tests. All three plainly resolve inside it, but the checker reports:
  FAIL: active sync.remote ... resolves outside the sandbox path
  FAIL: git 'origin' remote ... resolves outside the sandbox path
Root cause: resolvesInsideSandbox() (scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs:139-166) strips 'file://' via /^file:\/\/(.*)$/ leaving a leading-slash-prefixed path (e.g. '/C:/Users/...' for the 3-slash Windows form, or '/c/Users/...' for the MSYS/git-bash 3-slash form), then calls path.resolve() on that raw string directly. On Windows, path.resolve('/C:/Users/...') yields 'C:\C:\Users\...' (prepends the current drive root, keeps the leading slash literally), which never matches the real sandbox path -- confirmed live: path.resolve('/C:/Users/akhil/temp/.apra-fleet-tests/.apra-fleet-toy-dolt-remote') -> 'C:\C:\Users\akhil\temp\.apra-fleet-tests\.apra-fleet-toy-dolt-remote'. Same failure mode for the MSYS-style '/c/Users/...' form.
Impact: false-FAILs the sanctioned Setup/Reset verification step on every Windows run, even when the sandbox is correctly isolated -- this is a safety-guard reliability bug (false-fail direction, not a false-pass), but it currently blocks integ-test-runner from ever getting a clean 'OK' from this checker on Windows and forces manual verification as a workaround (as done this cycle).
Test: call resolvesInsideSandbox('file:///C:/Users/akhil/temp/.apra-fleet-tests/.apra-fleet-toy-dolt-remote', 'C:/Users/akhil/temp/.apra-fleet-tests') and assert it returns true; same for the MSYS-style 'file:///c/Users/akhil/temp/.apra-fleet-tests/.apra-fleet-toy-origin.git' form. Fix direction: use fileURLToPath()/pathToFileURL() (node:url) instead of a raw regex-strip + path.resolve() for file:// values, and normalize MSYS-style '/c/...' single-letter-segment paths to 'C:/...' before resolving, mirroring the drive-letter handling already fixed elsewhere in this same defect family (apra-fleet-2cc.2, apra-fleet-xuo.8.1).
Repro: on Windows, run integ-test-playbook.md's ## Setup through the seed step (node scripts/sandbox-seed-beads.mjs ...), then node scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs "$HOME/toy-repo" -- observe FAIL on sync.remote and git-origin checks despite both resolving inside the sandbox root by manual inspection.

title: [integ] f34-concurrent-launch-engagement: real supervisor topology sees 0 reviewer-newTask child beads, HTTP mutex subtest fails
description:
Feature: N/A (real-bd regression suite, part 1 of integ-test-playbook.md)
Expected: two concurrent real sprints dispatched over --service-url should reach the real supervisor and never DEGRADE; at least 2 child beads should be created under the shared parent (one per concurrent sprint's reviewer newTask). Real concurrent launches should also engage the HTTP mutex/id-allocator with no silent no-op fallback (apra-fleet-f34.3).
Actual: 'supervisor-spawned topology (f34.1)' failed: expected at least 2 child beads created under the shared parent, got []. 'apra-fleet-f34.3: real concurrent launches engage the HTTP mutex/id-allocator (no silent no-op fallback)' also failed: 1 subtest failed.
Test: packages/apra-fleet-se real-bd suite, file f34-concurrent-launch-engagement-integration.test.mjs, run via node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs (real bd, not mock). Ran fresh this cycle 2026-07-31 against deployed SHA 4f3e45457c54f3700dbb0843caf660e78aefe973, finishedAt 2026-07-31T07:02:03.054Z, durationMs=476738 (also independently over the 300s single-file budget -- see apra-fleet-eft.17).
Repro: node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs --start; poll --status --wait=45 until complete; inspect f34-concurrent-launch-engagement-integration.test.mjs entry in integ-suite-status.json.
notes: Residual mechanism (diagnosed + reproduced standalone 2026-07-31, apra-fleet-xuo.7.1): the reviewer newTask IS proposed, IS accepted by validateNewTask (SAFE_TEXT_RE allows the '[f34.3] ...' title), and the id-allocator IS engaged over --service-url (the proxy recorded acquire/release/allocate; allocator minted 'tko.1' and 'tko.2'). The loss is one step later, in the bd CLI contract itself: createChildBeadWithAllocatedId() (fleet-sprint/runner.js:2512) issues 'bd create "" --body-file <f> -p <P> --parent <parentId> --id <childId> --silent', and the current bd rejects that combination outright -- 'Error: cannot specify both --id and --parent flags', exit 1. Verbatim from the repro run: '[id-allocator] bd create failed for apra-fleet-bd-init-template-223176-tko.1; released reservation' followed by '[fleet-sprint] newTask bd create FAILED (non-fatal, develop-review) ... falling back to parent-bead notes'. Because persistNewTaskBestEffort degrades instead of throwing, BOTH concurrent sprints finish green while creating zero child beads -- exactly 'got []' at f34-concurrent-launch-engagement-integration.test.mjs:392. The allocator/mutex engagement path is NOT at fault and needs no change; the create command shape is. Confirmed against real bd in a scratch repo: 'bd create --id <parent>.<n> --parent <parent>' errors; 'bd create --id <parent>.<n>' alone succeeds and the child does show up under 'bd list --parent <parent> --json' (dotted-id prefix), but 'bd show' records NO explicit PARENT edge until a follow-up 'bd update <childId> --parent <parentId>' is issued -- which does establish the real edge on a dotted id. Fix: when the allocator grants an explicit childId, drop --parent from the create and re-establish the explicit parent edge with a separate 'bd update <childId> --parent <parentId>' after the allocation is confirmed; keep the single-command '--parent' form unchanged on the null-allocator path (childId null), where bd derives the id itself. Follow-up to the previous note (apra-fleet-xuo.7.1, after the create-command fix landed): with 'bd create --id <parentId>.<seq>' + a separate 'bd update <childId> --parent <parentId>', the reviewer newTasks DO land -- the post-fix real-bd run produced six distinct allocator-minted children (tib.1 .. tib.6) under the shared epic across the two concurrent sprints, with no id collisions, and no 'cannot specify both --id and --parent' error anywhere in the log. The subtest still failed at that point for a SECOND, independent reason in the verification read itself: 'bd list --parent <epic> --json' hides CLOSED beads by default, and a follow-up created in Review C1 R1 is picked up and closed by a later Develop round of the same cycle, so the read saw only the single still-open follow-up ('got [tib.6]'). Adding '--all' alone would have been wrong: setupMinimal()'s own four task children are parented under the same epic but carry FLAT ids, so an unfiltered '--all' count satisfies the '>= 2' floor even on ZERO reviewer newTasks -- precisely the vacuity that floor exists to prevent. The read is therefore '--all' PLUS a filter to the allocator-minted '<parentId>.<seq>' ids only. This strengthens rather than weakens the check: the apra-fleet-04g.1 duplicate-id assertion now examines all six created ids instead of the one that happened to still be open. Verified against real bd in a scratch repo: '--parent'/'--json'/'--all' compose, a closed dotted child appears only under '--all', and the flat-id child appears under both.

title: [integ] ou7.3-sprint-log-integration: nonzero-exit child leaves no traceable log (ledger/history mismatch)
description:
Feature: N/A (real-bd regression suite, part 1 of integ-test-playbook.md)
Expected: a real child process that writes stdout+stderr and exits nonzero should leave a log file on disk, recorded in the ledger and history (apra-fleet-ou7.3: every sprint has a traceable stdout/stderr log reachable from the dashboard).
Actual: assertion 'Expected values to be strictly equal: 0 !== 1' failed in test 'a real child that writes stdout+stderr and exits nonzero leaves a log file on disk, recorded in the ledger and history'; a second subtest 'apra-fleet-ou7.3: every sprint has a traceable stdout/stderr log reachable from the dashboard' then failed at 'failed running after hook' (cascading from the first failure's unclean state).
Test: packages/apra-fleet-se real-bd suite, file ou7.3-sprint-log-integration.test.mjs, run via node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs (real bd, not mock). Ran fresh this cycle 2026-07-31 against deployed SHA 4f3e45457c54f3700dbb0843caf660e78aefe973, finishedAt 2026-07-31T06:54:07.225Z, durationMs=596.
Repro: node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs --start; poll --status --wait=45 until complete; inspect ou7.3-sprint-log-integration.test.mjs entry in integ-suite-status.json.
notes: Residual mechanism (diagnosed + reproduced 2026-07-31, apra-fleet-xuo.6.1): the nonzero-exit path has a ledger/history write-ordering race, not a missing tee. bin/serve.mjs's onChildExit does 'await ledger.recordExit(...)' FIRST and 'await history.record(CHILD_EXITED)' SECOND. Both ledger.mjs and history.mjs commit their in-memory view only AFTER their atomic persist (tmp write + rename), so ledger.get(runId).exitCode becomes observable a whole history persist EARLIER than the CHILD_EXITED event does. Every observer (the ou7.3/k7b7 tests' waitFor, and the dashboard/log-view in production) polls the LEDGER as the readiness signal, then immediately reads history -- so under disk/CPU load the poll wins the race and history.list() still has 0 CHILD_EXITED events: the exact 'Expected values to be strictly equal: 0 !== 1' at ou7.3-sprint-log-integration.test.mjs:131. The log file itself and the ledger logPath are fine; only the history half is late. Reproduced deterministically by injecting a 100ms-delayed writeFile into createHistory in that test: fails with 0 !== 1 every run. The same injection also shows the after-hook cascade: the still-in-flight history persist races the after() 'fsp.rm(dir)' and blows up with ENOENT on sprint-history.json.tmp, because the test never drains ledger.stop()/history.stop() (both are 'await txChain') before deleting the dir. Fix: invert the order so history.record(CHILD_EXITED) completes BEFORE ledger.recordExit() commits -- making 'ledger shows an exitCode' imply 'history already has CHILD_EXITED' for every observer -- and drain ledger/history in the test after-hook with a tolerant rm.

title: Nothing verifies bd-mock recordings against the installed bd version; CI runs replay-only with an unpinned bd
description: Per a 2026-07-31 deep-dive follow-up audit of the Integ Test phase: nothing currently verifies that the bd-mock test recordings (packages/apra-fleet-se/test/fixtures/bd-recordings, 96 recordings, 6,793 recorded bd invocations as of 2026-07-30) still match the behavior of the actually-installed bd binary. The recording mechanism (bd-replay.mjs) mechanically guarantees recordings match what the PRODUCT issues (product-side drift throws loudly via "Recording drift for scenario" on replay) but has NO mechanism to catch TOOL-side drift -- if bd itself changes its output format, JSON shape, id format, or exit codes, replay mode silently serves the stale recorded bytes regardless of what a real bd would actually return. This is explicitly acknowledged in bd-recordings-fidelity.test.mjs's own comments ("Drift against a FUTURE real bd... is caught by running the same tests unmocked -- npm run test:integration -- and fixed by re-recording") but nothing actually runs that unmocked mode anywhere except the per-cycle Integ Test Part 1 phase during a live sprint. Checked: .github/workflows/ci.yml installs @beads/bd UNPINNED (no version pin anywhere in the recordings or workflow) and then runs npm test across workspaces in REPLAY mode only -- grep for test:integration or APRA_FLEET_BD_MOCK across .github/workflows/ returns zero matches. If Part 1 (apra-fleet-040) is gated out of the per-cycle sprint loop without first building a dedicated CI job for this, real-bd-integration testing drops from once-per-cycle to ZERO, not once-per-sprint as intended. Fix: (1) pin the bd version used at recording time and store it alongside the recordings (e.g. capture bd --version output into the fixture metadata); (2) add a check that fails when the installed bd differs from the recorded version; (3) add an actual CI job (scheduled/nightly, or gated to bd version bumps) that runs the real-bd suite (test:integration equivalent) against a pinned bd, so this coverage exists independent of whether/when Part 1 is removed from the per-cycle loop. This is a hard precondition for apra-fleet-040's fix, not independent nice-to-have work -- see apra-fleet-040's amended notes.
notes:
CROSS-REFERENCE 2026-07-31 (integ/regression split, apra-fleet-t4p): the unmocked real-bd lane referenced here no longer lives in the per-cycle Integ Test phase. It is now Part 1 of the new repo-root regression-test-playbook.md, run once per sprint by the new 'regression-test-runner' role via the Regression Test phase (runner.js Finalization group, between Final Review and Harvest; mirrored in apra-pm auto-sprint.js). title: [impl] Use shell-safe bd invocation in sandbox-seed-beads.mjs and check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs
description:
Files: scripts/sandbox-seed-beads.mjs (lines ~113, 123, 127), scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs checkDoltRemoteAbsent() (~line 350).

Root cause: on Windows the global bd resolves to npm's extensionless POSIX shim; execFileSync without { shell: true } uses CreateProcess and cannot exec a shebang script -> 'spawnSync bd ENOENT'.

Fix: route every execFileSync('bd', ...) through a single small cross-platform helper (shell:true, or explicit resolution to bd.cmd on win32) shared by both scripts; keep argument quoting safe (no string concatenation of untrusted values into a shell line).

Acceptance criteria:
- node -e "require('child_process').execFileSync('bd',['--version'])"-equivalent path succeeds on Windows via the helper and still works on Linux/macOS.
- Both scripts complete their bd steps on a Windows runner without ENOENT.
- No hand-run bd init / bd dolt push workaround introduced (run-24 incident guard).
- ASCII only; any shell scripts touched keep LF endings.
close_reason: Review fix: execBdSync no longer routes through { shell: true } on win32 (the actual injection surface, since Node joins bd+args into one unquoted shell command line). Now resolves the npm bd.cmd shim's underlying bin/bd.js script (resolveWindowsBdScript(), parsing the shim's stable double-quoted-path-before-%* pattern) and invokes it directly via execFileSync(process.execPath, [scriptPath, ...args]) -- no shell, no metacharacter reinterpretation possible. Falls back to the old shell:true behavior only if bd.cmd can't be resolved. Verified empirically end-to-end against the real installed bd.cmd (regex extraction + real invocation + an injected '&' arg producing no injected output). execBdAsync (xuo.2, backlog.mjs/scope-overlap.mjs) untouched -- already safe via its own allowlist for its structured-args-only callers. Updated tests/exec-bd.test.ts (16 tests, all pass) covering resolveWindowsBdScript parsing and both execBdSync branches with an injected shell-metacharacter arg, plus a real end-to-end regression check. Corrected the module's own doc comment (previously claimed never-concatenates while shell:true did exactly that) and a stale comment in check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs. Full root vitest suite: 2792/2796 pass, 4 failures are a pre-existing Windows EBUSY temp-dir-cleanup flake in unrelated integ tests, confirmed identical on baseline via git stash. npm run build passes.

title: Windows: execFileSync('bd', ...) without shell:true breaks integ-test setup/verification scripts
description:
Consolidated from two near-duplicate bug reports (apra-fleet-bnb.1/bnb.2) filed by integ-test-runner during this session's Sprint A run, then deleted during beads-DB conflict cleanup without being re-filed elsewhere -- this recreates that lost tracking under one bead, filed top-level (no --parent) per this session's new discipline for ad hoc/decentralized bead creation.

Root cause: on Windows, the globally-installed `bd` command resolves (via `which`/PATH) to npm's generated shim, an extensionless POSIX shell script (paired with bd.cmd/bd.ps1 for native Windows callers, which are NOT what these call sites resolve). Node's child_process.execFileSync(...) without `{ shell: true }` spawns via CreateProcess directly (no shell), which cannot exec a shebang script at all -- it fails with `spawnSync bd ENOENT` even though `bd` works perfectly fine from an interactive shell (bash resolves/execs it) or via execFileSync with shell:true. Verified live: `execFileSync('bd', ['--version'])` -> ENOENT; the identical call with `{ shell: true }` -> succeeds, prints version.

Three known call sites with this exact defect:
1. scripts/sandbox-seed-beads.mjs (lines 113, 123, 127) -- the SOLE sanctioned entry point for beads seeding/rewiring per integ-test-playbook.md (run-24 incident guard prohibits hand-running bd init/bd dolt push as a substitute). This blocks integ-test-runner's Part 2 (smoke test) Setup entirely on Windows -- no lever exists (no --bd-path/env override) and the playbook forbids working around it by hand.
2. scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs's checkDoltRemoteAbsent() (~line 350) -- same defect, would still block Setup verification even if (1) were fixed.
3. scripts/check-toy-doer-credentials.mjs -- a related but distinct Windows path-handling bug in the SAME family (not execFileSync, but also Windows-only): its entrypoint guard `if (import.meta.url === \`file://\${process.argv[1]}\`)` never matches on Windows because import.meta.url uses forward slashes (file:///C:/...) while process.argv[1] uses backslashes, so main() never runs and the script silently exits 0 regardless of provisioning state -- including for the apra-fleet-vak JSON-blob hard-failure check this script is also supposed to enforce.

- Pass `{ shell: true }` (or resolve to the platform-appropriate bd.cmd/bd.ps1 entry point explicitly, or use a cross-platform command-resolution helper) in every execFileSync('bd', ...) call in sandbox-seed-beads.mjs and check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs.
- Fix check-toy-doer-credentials.mjs's guard to use `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href` (node:url) instead of the raw file:// string comparison, so its non-zero exit contract holds on Windows as well as POSIX.

Test:
- node -e "require('child_process').execFileSync('bd',['--version'])" on Windows -> currently ERR spawnSync bd ENOENT; with the fix, succeeds.
- Run integ-test-playbook.md's Setup section on a Windows runner through to sandbox-seed-beads.mjs completing without ENOENT.
- Run check-toy-doer-credentials.mjs against a fleet home whose member has a JSON-blob-provisioned CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN on Windows and confirm a non-zero exit (currently always exits 0 silently).

Keeping closed.

Ran tests/2cc-win-bd-invocation-integ.test.ts directly on this Windows runner (git bash) this cycle: all 5 tests pass, including the win32 execBdSync ENOENT regression check, a real spawned sandbox-seed-beads.mjs run against a scratch sandbox (exit 0, real Dolt push to sandbox-local remote), and check-toy-doer-credentials.mjs child-process exit-code checks for both JSON-blob and healthy-file cases. title: Wire or decommission the existing dolt-recovery ladder (dolt-recovery.mjs / path-b / tier2) -- currently unwired, same failure pattern as the id-allocator/mutex
description:
This repo already contains a scripted Dolt conflict-recovery ladder that nothing in the real runner path ever calls: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/dolt-recovery.mjs (Path A: scripted resolve-in-place for single-row allowlisted conflicts), dolt-recovery-path-b.mjs (re-bootstrap + replay), dolt-recovery-tier2.mjs + docs/dolt-tier2-runbook.md (agent-with-runbook escalation, apra-fleet-eft.9.4/9.5/9.6). Only the test suite (test/dolt-recovery-path-a.test.mjs, -path-b.test.mjs, -tier2.test.mjs) exercises these -- runner.js never imports any of them. doltPushAfter() throws DoltDivergedError today with no recovery attempt at all.

This is the SAME failure pattern discovered this session for the id-allocator/dolt-mutex (apra-fleet-f34): eft.9.x work shipped real modules and unit tests, but the integration wire into the actual runner path was never completed, so it silently does nothing in production. Name the pattern explicitly and check for other unwired eft.9.x deliverables while this is fresh.

Decision needed (this bead is a decision + follow-through, not pure implementation): either (a) wire this ladder into doltPushAfter()'s failure path (attempt Path A -> Path B -> Tier 2 escalation in order before giving up and surfacing BEADS_SYNC_CONFLICT), or (b) if the ladder is stale/superseded by other session-30 work, explicitly decommission it (remove the dead modules, or clearly mark them experimental/unused) rather than leaving working-but-unreachable code that future investigators (like this session) will assume is load-bearing when it isn't.

Cross-reference: this bead's operator-local manual-runbook counterpart (the new "Dolt conflict-resolution runbook" doc from this session's investigation) covers a DIFFERENT scenario than docs/dolt-tier2-runbook.md -- the operator's own local machine clone (embeddeddolt/beads vs embeddeddolt/apra_fleet working-directory naming gotcha, bd's conflict-hiding auto-abort) vs. dolt-tier2-runbook.md's member-clone agent-escalation scenario. Don't parallel-author; cross-link the two docs instead.

Test: if wired, a real D-push hitting a single-row allowlisted conflict is auto-resolved via Path A without human intervention, verified by an integration test that a real (not mocked) doltPushAfter() call reaches dolt-recovery.mjs; if decommissioned, the dead modules are removed or clearly marked and this is documented in the same PR.
notes: ALREADY-FIXED. Parent decision bead for vkc.1/vkc.2, both of which are done and verified (see their notes): the ladder was wired (Path A + Tier 2, Path B deliberately gated off at the runner.js call site) rather than decommissioned, and is now an internal implementation detail of packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/dolt-sync.mjs per apra-fleet-417's design pass ('WIRE IT -- as an INTERNAL implementation detail of taskDbSync'). All associated test suites pass (recovery ladder 39/39, wiring-shape test 14/14). Subsystem: dolt-sync/recovery-ladder.
close_reason: Both children (vkc.1 decision+execution, vkc.2 integration test) closed and verified; ladder wired as internal detail of dolt-sync.mjs.

title: Classify unmergeable beads Dolt conflicts as their own terminal state (BEADS_SYNC_CONFLICT), not generic failure/CRASHED
description:
A D-push bracket that dies on a genuinely unmergeable Dolt conflict (DOLT_DIVERGED, seen live this session as apra-fleet-bnb's POST_DISPATCH_SYNC_FAILED termination) is mostly a cause-chain unwrap, not new plumbing: runner.js (~line 9205) already sets terminalReason from err.code, and the diverged D-push already arrives wrapped as PostDispatchSyncError (errors.mjs ~425-441) with the DOLT_DIVERGED cause preserved. Surface this distinctly as BEADS_SYNC_CONFLICT (once apra-fleet-k7b.2's terminal-state surfacing lands) so the supervisor/dashboard shows "beads sync conflict, needs operator resolution" instead of collapsing it into the same generic CRASHED bucket as every other termination reason.

Cheap, high-value addition: on DOLT_DIVERGED, auto-capture the dolt_conflicts_<table> dump into the sprint's log/diagnostics at failure time (before bd's own safe-abort discards the conflict state) -- this is pure data capture, not resolution, but it means the human resolving it later starts with the actual conflicting rows in hand instead of having to re-run `dolt merge --no-commit` themselves to even see what collided (as this session had to do live, twice).

Depends on apra-fleet-k7b.1/.2 (needs the run-identity/terminal-state plumbing this child sits under).

Test: a sprint whose D-push dies with DOLT_DIVERGED shows terminalReason=BEADS_SYNC_CONFLICT (not CRASHED) in the dashboard/history, with the captured conflict dump attached/linked.
notes: Integration test for this task is apra-fleet-k7b.8 (same streak k7b-conflict). Scope here: implementation plus unit tests only.

comments.author: Akhil Kumar
comments.text:
SEMANTICS REVIEW AFTER THE DOLT SETTLE REDESIGN (2026-08-13) -- no reopen, no
functional change requested. The behavior these beads describe is still correct
and still shipped; only the frequency and the meaning of the terminal have
narrowed, which is worth recording next to the beads that defined it.

On branch fix/dolt-settle-recovery (commits bc50c72b..c0524454) the Path A /
Path B / Tier 2 recovery ladder is deleted and replaced by one deterministic
settleDoltConflicts() (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/dolt-settle.mjs),
wired at both the push and pull divergence terminals. Consequences for this
terminal state:

- The classification itself is unchanged and still load-bearing: runner.js
  maps a DoltDivergedError cause to 'BEADS_SYNC_CONFLICT' rather than the
  generic UNKNOWN bucket, and still captures the conflict dump.
- What reaches it has narrowed sharply. An ordinary resolvable row conflict is
  now settled in place and the sprint continues; the terminal fires only when
  settle itself cannot complete -- an OPERATIONAL failure (no usable dolt
  binary, the ephemeral sql-server will not start, the member is unreachable),
  never on a conflict that is merely unmerged. dolt-sync.mjs logs that
  distinction explicitly ("infra failure, NOT an unresolvable conflict") and
  test/dolt-push-recovery-wiring.test.mjs asserts the original DoltDivergedError
  is surfaced unchanged in that case -- never re-labelled, never escalated to an
  LLM, never retried.
- Naming: 'BEADS_SYNC_CONFLICT' is now slightly imprecise, since the common
  reason it fires is infrastructure rather than an unresolved conflict. Left
  as-is deliberately -- it is a public terminal-reason string consumed by the
  dashboard and by golden transcripts, and the cost of churning it exceeds the
  precision gained. Recorded here so a future reader is not misled by the name.

title: Require machine-checkable dedup evidence before creating a new bead (planner, reviewer, integ-test-runner)
description:
integ-test-runner.md (lines 186-190) already has a narrower version of this instruction ("bd search \"[integ]\"" before filing a bug) and it still produced two near-duplicate bugs (apra-fleet-bnb.1, apra-fleet-bnb.2 -- same root cause, filed 19 seconds apart) this session. A prompt-instruction fix ALONE is not credible given this evidence -- it needs a machine-checkable guarantee, not just more prose.

Fix direction:
1. Broaden and relocate the dedup instruction to every bead-creating role, correctly identified as: planner.md (direct bd create --parent), reviewer.md (proposes newTasks, currently zero dedup language), and integ-test-runner.md (has the narrow existing check). NOT plan-reviewer.md or harvester.md -- verified neither creates beads (plan-reviewer only validates/scores the planner's proposal; harvester is explicitly forbidden from bd create, at most bd note).
2. Instruction wording: \"Before creating a new bead, search existing OPEN items across the ENTIRE backlog (not just the current sprint's scope) for overlap. It is better to refine an existing item's text, or add a child under it, than to create a duplicate.\" Same rule added to CLAUDE.md's Beads section for human-interactive sessions.
3. HARDER GUARANTEE (the actual fix, not just the prompt wording): add a `dedupCheck: {query, candidateIds, verdict}` field to the relevant output schemas (integ-test-runner-output.json, the reviewer's newTasks schema in contracts.mjs) that the orchestrator validates is non-empty/present before accepting a proposed new bead -- forces the search to actually happen and leaves an auditable trail, rather than relying on the persona simply remembering to follow prose instructions under time/token pressure.

This pairs with apra-fleet-n74 (route creation through the orchestrator): once personas PROPOSE rather than directly bd create, the orchestrator is a natural enforcement point for the dedupCheck field before calling createChildBeadWithAllocatedId.

Test: a proposed newTask/bug missing the dedupCheck field is rejected by the orchestrator with a clear repair-retry message (schema validation failure), not silently accepted; a proposal whose dedupCheck.candidateIds includes a real overlapping open bead is either auto-merged into that bead's notes or explicitly flagged for human review rather than created as a new bead.
notes: Triage: confirmed no dedupCheck field anywhere in repo (grep zero hits) and no dedup-instruction language in planner.md/reviewer.md/integ-test-runner.md or CLAUDE.md Beads section (grep zero hits beyond backlog-groomer.md's unrelated 'Deduplication sweep' step). The bnb.1/bnb.2 near-duplicate evidence cited in the description is real motivation for a machine-checkable gate, not prose alone. Blocked by n74 (shares mutex files per planner re-plan notes) -- n74 is itself unblocked/ready, so this chain is live. Classification: READY-AS-IS. Subsystem: bead-creation dedup gate (orchestrator validation).

title: Route integ-test-runner and planner bead creation through the orchestrator's id-allocator instead of direct bd create
description:
Both real beads-DB incidents this session (apra-fleet-bnb.1/.2, apra-fleet-04g.1) came from actors that call `bd create --parent <scope>` directly from their own dispatched Claude Code session: integ-test-runner.md (lines 168-178, bug filing) and planner.md (direct member-side bd create --parent, e.g. lines 49/73/96/127). Neither goes through the orchestrator's own id-allocator-backed bead-creation path (createChildBeadWithAllocatedId, runner.js ~2346-2378), which is the one path built to be collision-safe -- once apra-fleet-f34 actually wires it up end to end.

Do NOT have personas call the supervisor's id-allocator HTTP endpoint directly: integ-test-runner/planner run as dispatched sessions on member machines (possibly remote, e.g. fleet-rev), while the supervisor listens on the operator's host -- nothing hands the persona a reachable URL today, and this is the common case, not an edge case.

Fix direction: mirror the pattern reviewer.md already uses for newTasks (propose via output schema, orchestrator creates). Change integ-test-runner.md's Step 3 and planner.md's direct-create points to RETURN proposed bugs/tasks in their structured output (integ-test-runner already returns bugsFiled -- extend this to be the actual creation mechanism, not just a post-hoc report of an already-direct bd create) instead of running bd create themselves. The orchestrator (runner.js) then creates them through createChildBeadWithAllocatedId, same as the reviewer's newTasks path, gaining the id-allocator's collision-safety for free once apra-fleet-f34 lands.

Do NOT have these personas avoid --parent entirely as a workaround (an earlier draft of this fix considered it) -- sprint scoping is parent-tree-based throughout the codebase (runner.js ~5153 parent-scoped filters, ~5431+ childrenOf maps, pending-closure bug ownership at ~8206-8232, plan-reviewer.md:58's `bd list --parent <scope>`); a flat bug with only a dependency edge would silently vanish from delta-cycle discovery and closure ownership. Parent-tree membership must be preserved; the fix is in WHO calls bd create (orchestrator, not the persona), not in dropping --parent.

Depends on apra-fleet-f34 (the id-allocator must actually be reachable/engaged before routing more creators through it).

Test: integ-test-runner reports a bug via its output schema (no direct bd create in its own session); the orchestrator creates it via createChildBeadWithAllocatedId and it lands with a collision-safe explicit id. Same for a planner-proposed task.
notes: Triage (2mi-n74 batch): verified unimplemented. grep confirms zero dedupCheck usage repo-wide and integ-test-runner.md:229/planner.md:75,107,130,161 still call 'bd create' directly (the exact pattern this bead wants removed). createChildBeadWithAllocatedId exists and is used at runner.js:7667/8328/8610 but only from orchestrator-side paths (reviewer newTasks), not yet wired for integ-test-runner/planner proposals. Blocking dep apra-fleet-f34 is CLOSED (f34.1-.3 landed, serviceUrl wired), so this is unblocked and ready. Design in the description is already thorough (rejects direct id-allocator HTTP calls from personas, preserves --parent/parent-tree scoping). Classification: READY-AS-IS. Subsystem: fleet-sprint/orchestrator bead-creation routing.

title: Supervisor live-view proxy never rewrites the generic on-demand-detail route (task-tree descriptions + activity more... both 404)
description:
The supervisor's live proxy (packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/proxy.mjs) never rewrote the generic /extensions/:extId/detail/:itemId (beads task-tree description expand) or /activities/:id/output (activity "more..." expand) routes, so the child's absolute fetch() calls resolved against the supervisor's own origin instead of re-entering the proxy -- a 404 on every single expand, observed live as "(description unavailable)" and "failed to load (retry?)".

Fixed via rewriteChildHtml() additions plus two new passthrough proxy routes/handlers (handleExtensionDetail, handleActivityOutput) registered in registerLiveRoutes(), with 3 new regression tests in supervisor-proxy.test.mjs (14/14 passing). Fix committed as fcaa92be and already pushed/merged to the integration branch.

Test: see supervisor-proxy.test.mjs's "rewrites the generic extension-detail and activity-output fetch calls" and the two new passthrough-route integration tests.

(Recreated here under a new id: the original apra-fleet-04g.1 was created locally on the operator's machine and independently collided with a pre-existing, earlier-created apra-fleet-04g.1 -- "[integ] Smoke-test Reset leaves prior attempt's toy-app dev server running..." -- on a Dolt merge. That earlier bead is now the canonical apra-fleet-04g.1; this bead preserves the proxy-fix record under its own id. The fix itself was never lost -- only the bead's tracking id changed.)

title: supervisor: tee sprint child stdout/stderr to log files, link from dashboard
description:
packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/spawner.mjs spawns each sprint child with stdio: 'ignore' (spawnSprint(), ~line 214-219) -- the child's own stdout/stderr is discarded entirely, with no log file anywhere on disk. The only observability today is the live SSE viewer (while the sprint is running), sprint-history.json (terminal summary only), and the fleet server's own execute_prompt/execute_command log (truncated previews, and only for dispatch calls -- not the sprint runner process's own console output).

Fix: instead of stdio: 'ignore', open (or create) a per-sprint log file under the SE data dir (e.g. ~/.apra-fleet-se/logs/<sprintId>.log) and pass its fd/stream as stdout+stderr to spawn(), so the full raw child output is captured on disk for the sprint's whole lifetime (including post-crash, which the live SSE view cannot show since the child is gone by the time you look).

Then surface it: add a simple link/route on the supervisor dashboard and per-sprint live view (e.g. GET /sprints/:id/log or similar) that serves that file (tail or full), so a user can click through from the dashboard to see a sprint's raw output/error log -- including for CRASHED sprints where the live viewer is no longer reachable. Nothing fancy: no streaming/tailing UI required beyond what already exists for other views, just a working link.

Keep this scoped: log file management (rotation/cleanup of old sprint logs) is out of scope unless trivial; the acceptance bar is "every sprint (live or crashed) has a traceable stdout/stderr log file, and there's a link from the supervisor dashboard to view it."

(Recreated here: the original apra-fleet-jnw was filed on a machine whose local Dolt clone has an unresolved merge conflict against origin/main and could not be pushed to the shared remote. That local copy still exists but is orphaned/unsynced -- this is the canonical, shared copy going forward.)
close_reason: Verify-and-close: all 3 children (ou7.1-.3) closed -- supervisor stdout/stderr tee + dashboard links shipped.

title: Launch-failure fast path and diagnose-before-relaunch gate in the supervisor
description:
On Jul 29, five sprint incarnations died in 39ms-to-seconds before any dispatch (Arg Contract goal-format error x2, missing member beads DB, "Nothing to do" scope-sync abort x2), yet each left a stuck reservation requiring manual force-release, and each relaunch was manual and blind -- one relaunch (apra-fleet-bnb-e828ded6) re-hit an already-fixed-on-disk bug because it was relaunched against the stale pre-fix supervisor process instead of the restarted one.

Fix direction:
(a) if the child exits within a configurable window (e.g. 60s) with no dispatch recorded, classify launch-failed (a status distinct from CRASHED), auto-release the reservation, and surface the captured stderr tail;
(b) before honoring a relaunch of the same issueRoot, read the prior incarnation's terminal record and refuse/warn when the reason is deterministic and unaddressed -- including anything the engine flagged "must not be retried blindly" (seen in the apra-fleet-bnb-de118180 Dolt-conflict termination) -- and stamp/check the running supervisor's build version so a "fix on disk but not in the running process" mismatch is detected before relaunching against it.

Test: spawn a child that exits 1 in under 1s; assert the reservation is auto-released, the event is recorded as launch-failed with a stderr tail, and a same-root relaunch request returns a warning naming the prior failure reason until explicitly overridden.

Depends on apra-fleet-k7b (needs terminal records findable by run-id, and exit-code capture) and apra-fleet-jnw (stderr tail needs child stdio capture -- degrade gracefully to "no stderr captured" until jnw lands).
notes: planner 2026-07-31 (re-plan): added container-level ordering edge 'gey blocked-by apra-fleet-xuo.6'. Rationale: gey.1 (spawner.mjs/watchdog.mjs + ledger/history record shape, and it CONSUMES the ou7 log tail) contends for the same supervisor spawner-exit log+ledger+history path that xuo.6.1 is repairing. Sequencing at the container level (matching vkc->f34, n74->f34, 2mi->n74, gey->ou7/k7b) keeps lanes 'gey-launch' and 'xuo6-log' separate without a raw cross-lane leaf edge, and avoids the co-lane effort blowout (12 size points x premium 20 = 240 > 200 threshold).
close_reason: integ-test-runner verification-closure: ran packages/apra-fleet-se/test/gey3-launch-failure-relaunch-gate-integration.test.mjs via 'node --test' against the deployed sprint branch working tree (HEAD 45ce53f3). Result: 1/1 pass -- real spawned child exiting 1 in <1s is auto-released and recorded as LAUNCH_FAILED (not CRASHED) with a real stderr tail, relaunch gate returns 409 naming the prior failure. No failures observed; acceptance criteria hold.

title: Record child exit code/signal/time into the ledger on spawner exit
description:
spawner.mjs's child.once('exit') currently only deletes port bookkeeping. Additionally persist {exitCode, signal, at} via the ledger/history so the watchdog can report "exited 1 at 14:25:50" instead of just "pid gone". Independent of the run-id/terminal-state children above -- can land first.

Test: spawn a child that exits nonzero; assert the ledger/history records the exit code and the watchdog line includes it.
notes: Integration test for this task is apra-fleet-k7b.7 (same streak k7b-exit). Scope here: implementation plus unit tests only.
close_reason: spawner.mjs's child.once('exit') now forwards the Node exit event's (code, signal) plus an injectable clock to an optional onChildExit callback keyed by the launch's runId (async-rejection-safe via Promise.resolve().catch()). bin/serve.mjs wires this to ledger.recordExit() (new ledger method, annotates the still-held reservation in place with exitCode/signal/exitedAt, doesn't release it) and history.record(HISTORY_EVENTS.CHILD_EXITED) (new history event kind). ledger/history schemas extended with optional null-defaulted fields (old files still load). watchdog.mjs's new formatExitDetail() builds e.g. 'exited 1 at 2026-07-30T21:25:50.000Z' from the ledger-recorded fields, surfaced via classifySprint()'s new 'detail' field and threaded into defaultRecordTerminalError()'s actual logged TERMINAL ERROR line and persisted terminalReason -- replacing the previous bare 'pid gone'. Unit tests: ledger recordExit (3 new), history CHILD_EXITED (new file, 4 tests), spawner onChildExit incl. throwing-sync and rejecting-async callback safety (6 new), watchdog formatExitDetail (6 new) + classifySprint detail field (5 new) + a REAL-ledger (not fakeLedger) end-to-end integration test proving ledger.list() actually forwards the recorded fields to the watchdog, + a test asserting the ACTUAL emitted log line/persisted terminalReason contain the exit detail verbatim (the bead's literal acceptance sentence). Full targeted sweep across all 13 affected/adjacent test files: 204/204 pass. Documented (not fixed, per advisor review) a narrow claim-after-spawn race for instant child deaths -- noted in the commit message for apra-fleet-k7b.7's integration test. Commit 22e1853.

title: execute_prompt: chunk remote prompt-file writes to avoid Windows CreateProcess command-line ceiling on large (Review-phase) dispatches
description:
Live-reproduced 2026-07-30 on fleet-win-dev1 (Windows remote member,
192.168.1.12): a Review-phase dispatch (embedding full `bd show --json`
output -- description + acceptance criteria -- for 5 beads) never reached
the model as real content. Instead the resumed session received a garbled
"Unable to exec" response, entered a JSON-schema-repair retry loop, and the
lean repair-retry prompt (which relies on conversational memory for the
original task, per apra-fleet-02s.3) collided with the reviewer persona's
own contract of always re-reading `.fleet-task.md` -- so it read only the
repair notice and correctly, but unhelpfully, reported "missing required
review input". The local orchestrator process died shortly after. Net
effect: 3 real, tested, committed doer beads (apra-fleet-3e8, eft.57.2,
eft.81.2 -- all closed via a separate, smaller worklist streak in the SAME
session) got stranded -- code already pushed by the doer's own sync, but
the review never happened and the orchestrator crashed instead of
recovering.

Root cause (traced via fleet-win-dev1's own Claude Code session transcripts
and the local apra-fleet server's fleet.log): `writePromptFile()`
(src/tools/execute-prompt.ts) embeds the ENTIRE prompt content directly into
a single remote exec command line -- for Windows, wrapped in a PowerShell
script that is then UTF-16LE-encoded and base64'd for `-EncodedCommand`
(~2.67x size inflation on top of the raw content). A large Review-phase
prompt (multi-KB, since it inlines full bd show --json for every reviewed
bead) pushes the resulting encoded command line past Windows' CreateProcess
command-line ceiling (32,767 chars) once inflated, causing the remote exec
itself to fail -- surfacing to the model as "Unable to exec ...".

Doer dispatches (small: just branch name + bead ids + a short schema) never
hit this. Only larger dispatches do -- Review is the most exposed since it
inlines full bead detail for potentially several beads at once.

Why this never showed up on fleet-mac: fleet-mac is a POSIX (macOS/bash)
remote member. The POSIX write path (`echo '<b64>' | base64 -d > file`)
uses the SAME whole-content-in-one-command-line pattern, but the real-world
ceiling for a POSIX shell command line (ARG_MAX, typically hundreds of KB to
low MB on macOS/Linux) is roughly 20-60x higher than Windows' effective
~12KB-of-raw-content ceiling after -EncodedCommand's encoding overhead. The
same prompt that broke fleet-win-dev1 sails through untouched on fleet-mac.

FIX APPLIED (this bead, commit on chore/integration-binary-fixes-and-auth-selfheal):
`writePromptFile()` now chunks any remote-member content into bounded
pieces (REMOTE_PROMPT_CHUNK_CHARS = 4000 raw chars/chunk) and writes them
via multiple sequential exec calls instead of one -- Windows: first chunk
via `Set-Content`, subsequent chunks via `Add-Content` (both with
`-NoNewline` so chunks concatenate byte-exact); POSIX: first chunk via `>`,
subsequent chunks via `>>`. Applied on BOTH OS paths (POSIX has far more
headroom today, but shares the same architectural hazard, and
`strategy.execCommand()` has no stdin-based alternative to fall back to).
Prompts under the chunk threshold write in exactly one exec call, same as
before -- zero behavior change for the common case.

Verified: 3 new regression tests in tests/execute-prompt.test.ts (Windows
multi-chunk reconstruction, POSIX multi-chunk reconstruction, small-prompt
single-call no-op-change), all passing. tsc clean. Full root vitest suite
green (2728/34-skip/0-fail, +3 over the pre-fix baseline).

Separately recovered (not part of this bug, but the same incident): the 3
doer beads' commits were already pushed by the sprint's own sync (verified
via `git ls-remote`/`gh api` -- branch feat/lhf-batch-a on GitHub matches
fleet-win-dev1's local HEAD exactly); only the beads-DB closes were stranded
locally on fleet-win-dev1 (bd dolt push after a clean bd dolt pull landed
them in the shared DB).

NOT YET ADDRESSED (follow-up, separate from this fix): the secondary
interaction bug -- a lean schema-repair retry (relying on conversational
memory) colliding with a persona contract that always re-reads
`.fleet-task.md` for its task, causing the retry to look like a
"missing input" review to the model even once resumed context exists. This
fix removes the TRIGGER (oversized prompt causing embed failure), so the
collision should no longer be reachable via this path, but the underlying
design tension (lean-repair-via-resume vs. always-re-read-task-file personas)
is not itself resolved and could resurface via a different large-prompt
timeout/failure mode. Worth a dedicated design pass if it recurs.
close_reason: Fixed on chore/integration-binary-fixes-and-auth-selfheal. writePromptFile() now chunks remote content across bounded Set-Content/Add-Content (Windows) or >/>>  (POSIX) exec calls instead of embedding whole. 3 new regression tests, tsc clean, full vitest suite 2728/34-skip/0-fail.
