title: Supervisor: Sprint Stack widget needs Stop and Restart controls per sprint
description:
The Sprint Stack section of the fleet-sprint supervisor dashboard (src/supervisor/dashboard.mjs, renderSprintSection()) only shows an 'Open live view' link per sprint -- there is no way to stop or restart a sprint from the UI.

Observed live 2026-07-29: a sprint launched via the Launch Sprint form died almost instantly (Arg Contract validation error in the spawned child), but its member+issue-scope reservation was NOT automatically released -- the member (fleet-win-dev1) stayed reserved/blocked for every subsequent launch attempt with a 409 member-overlap conflict, and the dead sprint kept showing 'running-unresponsive' in the stack indefinitely. The only way to unstick it was a manual curl POST to the existing (undocumented-in-UI) POST /api/reservations/:sprintId/force-release endpoint (src/supervisor/reconcile.mjs, registerReservationRoutes()). This happened twice in one session.

Needed:
1. Stop button per sprint-stack row: kills the live child process (spawner.mjs already tracks child pid) AND releases its reservation (wire to the existing force-release route, or a new one that also does the kill -- force-release today only clears the ledger entry, it does not touch a still-alive child).
2. Restart button per sprint-stack row: re-launches the SAME sprint (same issue root(s), members, branch, base, goal) via POST /api/sprints after releasing the old reservation. NOTE: the reservation ledger currently does NOT persist branch/goal (see dashboard.mjs's own DATA AVAILABILITY NOTE and getSprintMeta() default-empty-object comment) -- Restart's design needs to either (a) persist enough launch metadata in the ledger to reconstruct the original request, or (b) prompt the operator to re-enter branch/goal, since neither is currently recoverable from server state alone.
3. Both actions need a confirmation step (destructive-ish: Stop kills a possibly-still-useful process; Restart discards the old sprint's history) and clear operator feedback (success/error), consistent with the Launch Sprint form's own error-surfacing pattern (formatLaunchError()).

Acceptance criteria:
- Sprint Stack section renders a Stop button and (once the branch/goal persistence gap above is resolved or worked around) a Restart button per running sprint.
- Clicking Stop kills the child process (verified: pid no longer alive) AND releases the member+scope reservation (verified: member's reservedBy is null, GET /api/members shows reserved:false) in one action -- no follow-up manual force-release call needed.
- Clicking Restart launches a new sprint with the same scope/members (goal/branch may require operator re-entry per the note above) without requiring the operator to first manually stop the old one.
- Both actions surface success/failure to the operator inline (no silent no-op, no unhandled promise rejection in the browser console).
notes:
PLANNER: before creating any implementation work for this bead, first verify it actually still reproduces on the CURRENT codebase -- things may have changed since it was filed. If your verification shows it's already fixed, partially fixed, or no longer reproduces, close it (or narrow its scope to only the part that's genuinely still broken) with the evidence you found, instead of creating speculative fix work. Only create real implementation tasks for what you've confirmed is still actually broken. The integ-test-runner should independently verify and close based on real observed evidence, not solely on the planner's own assessment.

Original closure cited no evidence. Needs real verification against the live supervisor before re-closing.

title: [impl] Retried doer dispatch must resume onto its streak branch remote tip instead of re-implementing (pre-commit fetch+fast-forward)
description:
Root cause (see apra-fleet-eft.87): when the engine retries a doer dispatch after an earlier attempt already committed+pushed the single-task streak (or is about to), the retried session re-implements the same task as an independent commit, so local and origin permanently diverge (git rev-list --left-right = '2 1') and every subsequent 'git push' fails non-fast-forward and every 'git merge --ff-only' fails 'Not possible to fast-forward'. The retry pre-dispatch sync short-circuit in withGitSync (skipPreDispatchSync, apra-fleet-eft.54.1) skips syncMemberBefore's 'git fetch + merge --ff-only' on the assumption 'prior attempt published nothing' -- but that assumption is FALSE for an attempt that did (or may have) pushed, leaving the retried session on a stale local tip that it then re-commits.

FILES TO CHANGE (<=3): packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js (the withGitSync bracket / skipPreDispatchSync retry path around lines 4572-4607, and syncMemberBefore if a hard reset-to-remote-tip helper is needed).

EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR: On any retried doer dispatch where the prior attempt was NOT provably a no-mutation failure (i.e. it may have committed and/or pushed), the retry MUST first fetch the streak branch's current remote tip and fast-forward/reset the local branch onto it BEFORE the doer is allowed to commit, so the retry resumes on top of already-published work rather than re-implementing it. The skipPreDispatchSync optimization must remain in force ONLY for the genuine terminal no-mutation-failure case it was scoped to (eft.54.1) and must NOT suppress the fetch+ff on a retry that could diverge.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- A retried doer dispatch after a prior attempt that pushed does NOT create a second content-identical, SHA-distinct commit; local never diverges from origin's streak branch tip (git rev-list --left-right --count origin/<branch>...HEAD is never '>=1 >=1').
- The terminal no-mutation-failure fast-abort behaviour (eft.54/eft.50 regression tests) is preserved unchanged: those paths still skip the redundant pre-dispatch sync.
- No behaviour change for first attempts / happy path (no retry).
- 'npm test' passes; new/updated unit tests (paired [test] task) pass.

title: [impl] withGitSync distinguishes dispatch failure from post-dispatch sync failure (no LLM re-dispatch on D-push/G-push errors)
description:
Symptom 2 of apra-fleet-6z8 (unchanged from the original 2026-07-26 finding). dispatchPlannerOnce() (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:4886) = withGitSync(member, false, () => withDispatchWatchdog(...)). withGitSync (runner.js:3832) wraps pre-dispatch pull, the actual LLM turn, AND the post-dispatch D-push as ONE bracket. doltPushGuarded() (runner.js:1448-1527) throws a DoltSyncError (line 1487-1490) on push failure, which propagates out of the ENTIRE withGitSync call, not just the push step. The PLANNER_DISPATCH_RETRY_DELAYS_MS loop (runner.js:4996) only sees "the bracket threw" and calls dispatchPlannerOnce() again from scratch, redispatching a brand-new Planner LLM turn even though the prior turn's actual output already exists safely in the member's local beads clone -- purely because an unrelated push step (e.g. missing VCS credentials) failed.

Fix: withGitSync (or its retry caller) must distinguish "dispatchFn itself failed" from "a completed dispatchFn's post-step (git/dolt sync) failed," and on the latter, retry only the sync step (or surface a distinct, narrowly-retried error) rather than looping back through PLANNER_DISPATCH_RETRY_DELAYS_MS to redispatch the LLM turn.

Acceptance: forcing a D-push failure (e.g. missing VCS credentials) after a successful Planner turn must NOT spawn a second Planner LLM dispatch for the same phase. Regression test covering this in the existing withGitSync/dolt-sync-brackets test suites. Full fleet-sprint test suite still passes.

title: fleet-sprint: preflight provision_vcs_auth before every code-writing dispatch (not just reactive self-heal)
description:
Pulled out of apra-fleet-5mj's design-stage scope into a concrete, buildable slice: implement the "preflight" leg of 5mj's three-strategy framing (preflight / reactive / expiry-scheduled), building on the reactive self-heal apra-fleet-fmu already shipped this session.

MOTIVATION: apra-fleet-fmu (closed, merged) added reactive self-heal to the orchestrator's own G-push/D-push bracket in withGitSync -- on an auth-classified failure it calls provision_vcs_auth and retries once. This works, live-verified. But it only covers the ORCHESTRATOR's own scripted push (runner.js's syncMemberAfter/doltPushAfter, dispatched via execute_command against the member). It does NOT cover the DOER's own independent git push, which the doer runs itself as part of its own implement+verify turn (a separate LLM-driven bash tool call, not something runner.js dispatches or controls). apra-fleet-don tracks the resulting failure mode: the doer's own push can hit an expired/missing credential BEFORE the orchestrator's bracket ever runs, causing the doer to give up and close its bead with a stale/misleading "blocked: missing credential, needs operator" reason -- even though the orchestrator's bracket goes on to successfully push the same commit moments later.

THE FIX: call provision_vcs_auth proactively, BEFORE every code-writing dispatch starts (i.e. before the doer/harvester's turn begins), not just reactively after a push fails. If the doer always starts its turn with a freshly-minted, valid VCS credential already deployed, its own internal push will succeed on the first try in the overwhelming majority of cases (a single dispatch is far shorter than a token's ~1-4hr lifetime), which eliminates the specific apra-fleet-don race in normal operation.

WHERE THIS HOOKS IN: withGitSync (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js, ~line 3832) already has a pre-dispatch bracket that runs syncMemberBefore/doltPullBefore BEFORE calling dispatchFn() (the actual agent() turn). Add an unconditional provisionVcsAuth call there, gated the same way pushCode already gates G-push (i.e. only for roles that actually write/push code -- doer, harvester; read-only roles like reviewer/plan-reviewer/deployer don't need it). Reuse the EXACT SAME provisionVcsAuth callback/wiring apra-fleet-fmu already built and threaded through (createVcsAuthSelfHealCallback / the ApraFleet.provisionVcsAuth client method) -- this is a new CALL SITE for existing machinery, not new plumbing.

SCOPE NOTES:
- This does NOT replace apra-fleet-fmu's reactive self-heal -- keep both. A long-running dispatch (e.g. a doer streak that hits max_turns and resumes, chaining well past a single dispatch's normal length -- observed live this session with eft.70.1) can still outlast even a freshly-minted token mid-turn, so the reactive path remains the safety net for that tail case.
- This does NOT eliminate the underlying two-push-paths architecture (doer's own push vs. orchestrator's scripted push) that apra-fleet-don is ultimately about -- it just makes the specific failure mode apra-fleet-don describes rare instead of routine. apra-fleet-don should stay open at a lower priority as the deeper architectural fix (or at minimum, correcting/reopening beads closed with a now-stale blocked reason), not be closed by this bead.
- Avoid re-provisioning needlessly on every retry/resume within the same streak if a still-valid token already exists -- check expiry (provision_vcs_auth's response already returns expiresAt, same field apra-fleet-fmu's self-heal reads) before minting a fresh one, so this doesn't turn into an unconditional GitHub API call on every single dispatch regardless of need.

ACCEPTANCE: withGitSync's pre-dispatch bracket calls provisionVcsAuth (via the same callback apra-fleet-fmu introduced) before every pushCode:true dispatch (doer, harvester), skipping the call if a still-valid (non-expiring-soon) credential is already known for that member. Read-only roles are unaffected (no new call for them). Regression test covering: a doer dispatch with no prior credential gets one minted before its turn starts; a doer dispatch with an already-fresh credential does not trigger a redundant provision call; the existing apra-fleet-fmu reactive self-heal path is unchanged and still fires for genuinely long-running dispatches that outlast the preflight-minted token. Full existing fleet-sprint test suite still passes.
acceptance_criteria: withGitSync's pre-dispatch bracket calls provisionVcsAuth before every pushCode:true dispatch, skipping if a still-valid credential is already known; reactive self-heal (apra-fleet-fmu) unchanged as the safety net for long-running dispatches; regression tests cover mint-when-missing, skip-when-fresh, and reactive-path-still-works; full test suite green.

title: [test] Phantom pid-less interactive session does not permanently wedge subsequent dispatches
description:
Unit test reproducing the exact eft.74 sequence and asserting the wedge is gone.

Test framework: vitest (existing src/tools test suites).

Scenario to reproduce:
1. A subprocess dispatch (resume=false) runs for a member.
2. A JWT connect-back for that member registers a sessionRegistry entry with NO pid.
3. The subprocess exits (no HTTP MCP teardown signal; entry lingers).
4. A second execute_prompt is issued to the same member.

Assertions (pass/fail):
- The second execute_prompt takes the SUBPROCESS route (not interactive), OR the pid-less session is evicted after the first interactive timeout and the following dispatch runs -- either way NO permanent wedge, and the second call does NOT burn the full timeout_s indefinitely.
- The existing eft.28/eft.50 dead-session-guard regression tests still pass unchanged.
- Optionally: two sequential dispatches to the same member in the same work folder both execute (the second does not time out).

Blocked by the impl task; run after it lands.
close_reason: Already satisfied by apra-fleet-eft.74.3 (test(auto-sprint): end-to-end coverage for phantom JWT connect-back wedge fix, commit 4ae5d610), which reproduces this exact eft.74 sequence: subprocess dispatch, mid-flight pid-less JWT connect-back registering a channelCapable-false server session, subprocess exit leaving the entry lingering, then a SECOND execute_prompt to the same member asserting it takes the subprocess route (no interactive push, no timeout), plus a regression test confirming the eft.28/eft.50 dead-pid channel-capable eviction path is unaffected. Re-ran tests/execute-prompt-phantom-connectback.test.ts, tests/execute-prompt-interactive.test.ts, tests/http-transport.test.ts, tests/session-registry.test.ts, tests/execute-prompt.test.ts, tests/pid-helpers.test.ts (128 tests, all pass). No code or test change required.

title: [impl] Gate interactive routing behind an explicit channel handshake + self-heal eviction on interactive timeout
description:
Fix the phantom-interactive-session wedge in src/tools/execute-prompt.ts and the session registry.

Files: src/tools/execute-prompt.ts (interactive routing block around sessionRegistry.get), plus the sessionRegistry module it reads.

Behaviour to implement (any/all of the bug's fix directions, at minimum the first and third):
- A plain subprocess connect-back (JWT registration with NO pid, no register_member local-spawn anchor) MUST NOT be treated as interactive-routable. Interactive (mode b) routing must require an explicit opt-in handshake (the notifications/claude/channel capability), not mere JWT registration.
- Self-heal: when an interactive dispatch to a pid-less session times out, evict that session from the registry so the NEXT execute_prompt to the same member falls back to the subprocess route instead of re-burning timeout_s.

Done criteria:
- After a subprocess dispatch + JWT connect-back with no pid where the subprocess has exited, the next execute_prompt to that member takes the SUBPROCESS route (not interactive), OR the wedged session is evicted after its first interactive timeout so no permanent wedge remains.
- The eft.28/eft.50 dead-session-guard regression tests remain unchanged and pass.
- No behaviour change for genuine interactive sessions that DID complete the channel handshake.
close_reason: Already implemented via eft.74.1 (channelCapable opt-in gating) + eft.74.2 (self-heal eviction on interactive timeout), both previously closed. Verified against this task's acceptance criteria by re-running the full test suite covering the phantom-session sequence (tests/execute-prompt-phantom-connectback.test.ts, tests/execute-prompt-interactive.test.ts, tests/http-transport.test.ts) plus the eft.28/eft.50 regression suites (tests/session-registry.test.ts, tests/execute-prompt.test.ts, tests/pid-helpers.test.ts) -- all pass, no code change required.

title: Members never get project MCP servers auto-approved -- only workspace trust is seeded, not enabledMcpjsonServers
description:
Discovered 2026-07-27 while wiring the deepwiki MCP server into .mcp.json for apra-fleet-eft's fleet-sprint run: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/AGY.md instructed agents to always use DeepWiki, but the server was never in .mcp.json, so dispatched sessions had no mcp__deepwiki__* tools at all. After adding it to .mcp.json, a second, deeper gap surfaced: this codebase's ensureWorkspaceTrusted (src/providers/claude.ts, apra-fleet-eft.40) seeds ONLY hasTrustDialogAccepted directly into the member's ~/.claude.json project entry -- explicitly because --dangerously-skip-permissions is the only overbroad alternative and the team already avoided relying on it for trust. But Claude Code gates project-declared MCP servers (.mcp.json) behind a SEPARATE per-project approval list, enabledMcpjsonServers (with disabledMcpjsonServers as the explicit-deny counterpart), in that same ~/.claude.json project entry. Grepped src/ for both keys: zero references anywhere. So nothing in this fleet's dispatch pipeline ever seeds enabledMcpjsonServers for any member -- any NEW server added to a project's .mcp.json (not just deepwiki) has no guarantee of being usable by a headless/unattended dispatch on any member, present or future, regardless of --dangerously-skip-permissions/unattended mode.

Live-verified on fleet-mac (~/.claude.json, project entry for /Users/akhil/git/apra-fleet): enabledMcpjsonServers and disabledMcpjsonServers were both empty arrays even though .mcp.json already listed 'apra-fleet' (added in commit 732dc38d) -- so that server may never have been actually approved for use by a dispatched session on this member either (inconclusive since dispatched agents don't appear to call back into apra-fleet's own MCP tools in practice, so the gap was latent/unobserved until deepwiki -- a tool dispatched agents ARE expected to call directly -- exposed it).

Pragmatic fix applied for THIS incident: manually seeded enabledMcpjsonServers: ['apra-fleet', 'deepwiki'] into fleet-mac's ~/.claude.json project entry via a one-off python edit. This does not scale -- it needs to happen for every member and every future project MCP server addition.

FIX NEEDED: extend ensureWorkspaceTrusted (or add a sibling function following the same seeding pattern) to also seed enabledMcpjsonServers with every server name currently declared in the project's .mcp.json, idempotently, alongside the existing hasTrustDialogAccepted seed -- so adding a new MCP server to .mcp.json and syncing it to a member is sufficient on its own, with no manual per-member JSON surgery required. Should run wherever ensureWorkspaceTrusted already runs in the dispatch/provisioning lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria: ensureWorkspaceTrusted (or an equivalent seeded alongside it) idempotently adds every server name declared in the project's .mcp.json to enabledMcpjsonServers in the member's ~/.claude.json project entry, so a newly added .mcp.json server works for headless dispatch on both existing and newly-registered members without manual JSON edits. Regression test covering: a member with an empty enabledMcpjsonServers list, after provisioning/trust-seeding, ends up with all current .mcp.json server names present; re-running is idempotent (no duplicates, no clobbering of servers a human explicitly disabled via disabledMcpjsonServers).
notes: integ-test-runner (2026-07-30, deployed SHA f9378fb7f520cf3e8a05d9641a87675fd39082c7): left open, inconclusive. Part 2 (smoke test) Setup aborted at the beads-seed step due to a Windows-only tooling defect (apra-fleet-bnb.2: execFileSync('bd', ...) ENOENTs without shell:true), so the Test scenario (member registration + canary sprint) never ran this cycle -- no live evidence either way. Separately, even with a working Setup, this bug is not exercisable by this playbook at all: fleet-e2e-toy's toy-repo has no .mcp.json (confirmed via ls after cloning), so ensureWorkspaceTrusted's enabledMcpjsonServers seeding path has nothing to seed. Its actual regression coverage lives in the root unit suite (tests/ensure-workspace-trusted.test.ts), which is outside both parts of integ-test-playbook.md. Verification of this fix needs either a toy-repo fixture with .mcp.json added to the smoke test, or reliance on the root unit suite as the closing evidence -- not this playbook as currently written.
close_reason: Verified via static + regression-suite evidence (not live smoke -- Part 2 could not run this cycle, see apra-fleet-bnb.1): original defect claim ('grepped src/ for both keys: zero references anywhere') is now false -- ensureWorkspaceTrusted (src/providers/claude.ts:370-396) reads the project's .mcp.json and idempotently seeds enabledMcpjsonServers alongside hasTrustDialogAccepted, filtering existing string entries and only adding server names not already present, without touching disabledMcpjsonServers. tests/ensure-workspace-trusted.test.ts (22 tests, incl. fresh member / already-trusted / disabled-deny / idempotent re-run / missing-or-unparseable .mcp.json degrade cases per the acceptance criteria) passes at deploy-verified SHA f9378fb7f520cf3e8a05d9641a87675fd39082c7 (2026-07-30 cycle).

title: fleet-sprint: detect git/dolt credential-auth failures and self-heal via provision_vcs_auth (apra-fleet-client)
description:
Motivated by a live incident (2026-07-26/27, apra-fleet-eft sprint on branch feat/sprint-service-1, member fleet-mac): both the Dolt push (D-push) and later the code push (G-push) failed repeatedly with a git credentials error --

  fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': Device not configured

-- because the member's provisioned GitHub App token had expired. The orchestrator had to manually call provision_vcs_auth via MCP to unblock. This bead implements a SMALL, TARGETED self-heal: detect this class of failure as a structured error and automatically call provision_vcs_auth (via the apra-fleet-client package) once, then retry the SAME failed git/dolt step exactly once. This is intentionally narrower than apra-fleet-5mj (the full preflight/expiry-scheduled-renewal design) and apra-fleet-6z8 (the broader coarse-retry-granularity redesign) -- this bead is the reactive, single-step self-heal slice that can land quickly; 5mj and 6z8 remain open for the proactive/expiry-aware and retry-architecture work respectively. Link all three.

=== SCOPE: packages/apra-fleet-client (new client method) ===

File: packages/apra-fleet-client/src/client/api.mjs
- Add a `provisionVcsAuth(options)` method to the `ApraFleet` class, mirroring the existing `provisionLlmAuth` method immediately above it (around line 271-277): `return this.mcpClient.callTool('provision_vcs_auth', options);`
- Add a `ProvisionVcsAuthOptions` JSDoc typedef mirroring `ProvisionLlmAuthOptions`'s style, covering the real provision_vcs_auth MCP tool schema: provider ('github'|'bitbucket'|'azure-devops', required), member_id, member_name, github_mode ('github-app'|'pat'), git_access ('read'|'push'|'admin'|'issues'|'full'), repos (string[]), token, api_token, email, workspace, org_url, pat, scope_url, label. (Reference the live tool schema if unsure of exact field set -- it is registered server-side as mcp__apra-fleet__provision_vcs_auth.)

File: packages/apra-fleet-client/test/fleet-client-api.test.mjs
- Add a `provisionVcsAuth` test mirroring the existing `provisionLlmAuth` test (around line 156-173): mock callTool, assert it's called with tool name 'provision_vcs_auth' and the exact options passed through, assert the mocked result is returned.

=== SCOPE: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js (detection + self-heal) ===

1. Git-auth failure classification (near classifyGitFailure, ~line 602-617, alongside the existing GIT_DIVERGED_PATTERNS / GIT_TRANSIENT_PATTERNS arrays ~line 600): add a new GIT_AUTH_PATTERNS array and a third classification value 'auth' returned by classifyGitFailure(), checked AFTER 'diverged' (divergence must never be misclassified) but BEFORE 'transient' (an auth failure is not the same as a transient network/lock blip -- blindly retrying it without fixing credentials is pointless and matches the exact failure observed live). Patterns to match at minimum (case-insensitive):
   - /could not read Username for/i  (the exact live-observed failure)
   - /could not read Password for/i
   - /Authentication failed/i
   - /Permission denied \(publickey\)/i
   - /remote: Invalid username or (token|password)/i
   - /terminal prompts disabled/i
   - /support for password authentication was removed/i
   - /Bad credentials/i

2. Self-heal wiring in runGitStep (~line 633-648, used by both G-pull/G-push via syncMemberBefore/syncMemberAfter) and runDoltStep (~line 1098, used by D-pull/D-push via doltPullBefore/doltPushAfter): add an optional `onAuthFailure` param (an injected async callback, following the exact same injection pattern already used for `agent`/`command` elsewhere in this file -- see syncMemberAfter's existing `agent` param and its doc comment around line 746-758 for the precedent). When a step's classification is 'auth' AND `onAuthFailure` is provided: call it exactly once (bounded -- never loop), and if it resolves without throwing, retry the SAME git/dolt command exactly once more before giving up (do not fold this into the existing maxTransientRetries loop, keep it a distinct one-shot path so it's easy to reason about and test). If `onAuthFailure` is not provided, or the retry after calling it still fails, fall through to today's exact existing behavior (return the failed result up to the caller, which throws GitSyncError/DoltSyncError as it does today) -- do not change behavior for any caller that doesn't opt in by passing onAuthFailure.

3. Thread `onAuthFailure` through the call chain the same way `agent` is already threaded (see the eft.8.12 comment block around line 3823-3831 for the precedent pattern): syncMemberAfter (G-push, ~line 754) and doltPushAfter (D-push, ~line 1399, whose internal doltPushGuarded helper ~line 1448 is where the actual runDoltStep 'bd dolt push' call lives) both need to accept and pass through an `onAuthFailure` option. syncMemberBefore (G-pull) and doltPullBefore (D-pull) should get the same treatment for consistency (a stale token can just as easily break a pull as a push), unless the doer finds a reason G-pull/D-pull genuinely can't hit this failure mode in practice.

4. Wire the actual callback at the top: find the enclosing orchestration function (contains the `withGitSync` closure ~line 3832, which already captures `command`, `agent`, `log`, `validated` from its surrounding scope -- trace that scope up to wherever the underlying fleet client / `command` function is sourced from, likely something threaded in from `main(context)` ~line 6926 or an intermediate function). Build a `provisionVcsAuth` callback there using the new `ApraFleet.provisionVcsAuth()` client method (from packages/apra-fleet-client), and pass it down alongside `agent`/`command` into withGitSync and its D-push equivalent, which then forward it into syncMemberAfter/doltPushAfter as `onAuthFailure`.

   IMPORTANT (per auto-sprint-product-vs-dogfood project convention -- fleet-sprint is a general-purpose product, must not hardcode assumptions specific to the apra-fleet repo): the `repos` argument passed to provision_vcs_auth must be derived generically at runtime -- e.g. by parsing the member's `git remote get-url origin` (or `--base`/branch remote) into an owner/repo string -- never hardcoded to a literal repo name. Use `git_access: 'push'` and the default `github_mode: 'github-app'` unless the doer finds evidence a different default is more appropriate. Log clearly whenever this self-heal path actually fires (both the detection and the outcome) so it's visible in sprint logs, not silent.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===
- New `ApraFleet.provisionVcsAuth()` client method exists in packages/apra-fleet-client with a passing unit test mirroring the provisionLlmAuth test.
- classifyGitFailure() recognizes the live-observed "could not read Username for 'https://github.com'" message (and the other listed patterns) as a new 'auth' classification, distinct from 'diverged'/'transient'/'unknown', with unit test coverage for the classification function itself.
- runGitStep/runDoltStep support an optional onAuthFailure callback: on an 'auth' classification, call it once and retry the same command once; existing callers that don't pass onAuthFailure see zero behavior change (regression-tested).
- G-push (syncMemberAfter/withGitSync) and D-push (doltPushAfter) are wired to call provision_vcs_auth (via the new client method) through onAuthFailure when a real auth failure is classified, using a repo derived generically from the member's git remote (not hardcoded), and logging the self-heal attempt and its outcome.
- Full existing runner.js / fleet-sprint test suite (mock-sprint-*, golden-transcript, etc.) still passes -- this must be additive, not a regression to existing G-pull/G-push/D-pull/D-push behavior for non-auth failures.
- New tests cover: (a) an auth-classified failure with onAuthFailure provided that succeeds and retry succeeds -> step ultimately reports success; (b) onAuthFailure provided but the retry still fails -> surfaces the existing typed error, not a silent hang or infinite loop; (c) no onAuthFailure provided -> byte-identical behavior to pre-change code on an auth-classified failure.
acceptance_criteria: ApraFleet.provisionVcsAuth() client method + test added; classifyGitFailure recognizes credential-auth failures as a new 'auth' kind with unit coverage; runGitStep/runDoltStep support a bounded one-shot onAuthFailure self-heal+retry with zero behavior change when unset; G-push and D-push are wired to call provision_vcs_auth on a detected auth failure using a generically-derived repo (not hardcoded); full existing fleet-sprint test suite still passes; new tests cover self-heal success, self-heal-then-still-fails, and the unset-callback no-op case.
close_reason: Implemented and reviewer-approved: ApraFleet.provisionVcsAuth client method, classifyGitFailure/classifyDoltFailure 'auth' classification, bounded one-shot onAuthFailure self-heal+retry in runGitStep/runDoltStep, wired into G-push/D-push (and pull side for symmetry) with repo derived generically from git remote (never hardcoded). Commits c904b0bf + 246ed352 on feat/sprint-service-1. Full test suites green.

title: [impl] Ensure Sprint Branch reuses a pre-existing local-only branch instead of resetting it to base
description: Bug apra-fleet-9te.4: in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js 'Ensure Sprint Branch' phase (~lines 4291-4406), when 'git fetch origin <branch>' fails with 'couldn't find remote ref' the code sets startPoint=origin/<baseBranch> and runs 'git checkout -B <branch> origin/<baseBranch>'. If the branch exists ONLY locally (a prior --max-cycles-limited cycle committed work but never pushed), this resets it to base and silently discards the local commits, leaving beads (closed tasks) and the git tree disagreeing. Fix: after a missing-ref fetch failure, probe for an existing local branch (e.g. 'git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>'); if it exists, adopt the existing local branch as the checkout target/start-point (reuse as-is) instead of resetting to origin/<base>. Preserve existing loud-abort behavior for non-missing-ref fetch errors and the dirty-tree auto-stash path. Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js. ASCII only.
acceptance_criteria: When the remote branch fetch in Ensure Sprint Branch fails with 'couldn't find remote ref <branch>' AND a local branch of that name already exists with commits, the phase checks out/keeps the existing local branch as-is rather than running 'checkout -B <branch> origin/<base>' (which discards local-only commits). Only when NO local branch exists does it fall back to origin/<base>. Non-'missing ref' fetch failures still abort loudly (unchanged). No committed work on a local-only sprint branch is lost across a relaunch.
close_reason: Already implemented and verified by commit 53920ee2 (fix(fleet-sprint): reuse pre-existing local sprint branch instead of resetting to base), which already references this bead id. Confirmed runner.js Ensure Sprint Branch phase probes 'git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>' after a missing-remote-ref fetch failure and reuses the local branch as-is instead of resetting to origin/<base>; non-missing-ref failures still abort loudly. Verified via node --test test/dispatch-safety-guard.test.mjs (3/3 pass) and test/mock-sprint-ensure-branch-fetch-failure.test.mjs (2/2 pass). No code change needed; closing to sync beads state with git tree.

title: [integ] auto-sprint 'Ensure Sprint Branch' phase resets a pre-existing local-only sprint branch to base, silently discarding already-closed, committed work
description:
Feature: N/A (auto-sprint engine's own sprint-branch lifecycle, hit while running integ-test-playbook.md's smoke test / Test scenario step 4 for the toy canary gh-toy-4ef)
Expected: when 'workflow auto-sprint' is invoked against a sprint branch that already exists locally (e.g. a prior --max-cycles-limited invocation started work and closed beads on it, but the branch was never pushed to origin because the cycle limit was hit before push), a subsequent invocation should reuse/preserve that local branch's existing commits, not discard them.
Actual: the engine's 'Sprint Setup' / 'Ensure Sprint Branch' phase ran 'git fetch origin auto-sprint/toy-canary-9te', which failed with 'fatal: couldn't find remote ref auto-sprint/toy-canary-9te' (expected -- the branch was local-only, never pushed by the prior interrupted cycle). Following that failed fetch, the branch was reset to origin/main, discarding the prior cycle's already-closed impl commit. Confirmed via git reflog on the sprint branch: 'auto-sprint/toy-canary-9te@{0}: branch: Reset to origin/main' immediately follows 'auto-sprint/toy-canary-9te@{1}: commit: feat: add --version/-v flag to CLI entry point' (the discarded commit). The corresponding beads task (gh-toy-4ef.1, [impl] Add --version/-v flag) remained marked CLOSED in beads even though its code was gone from the branch -- a state where beads and the git tree disagree. The paired [test] task (gh-toy-4ef.2)'s doer caught this itself on the next cycle ('BLOCKED: dependency gh-toy-4ef.1 ... is marked closed in beads, but its implementation commit (e.g. 442327c / bc0380a / e537940 across other sprint branches) is NOT present on this sprint branch' -- note the doer's own phrasing references MULTIPLE other commit hashes across other sprint branches, indicating this reset-and-lose-work pattern has recurred across several prior canary runs, not just this one), and the reviewer had to spend an extra develop/review round creating a remediation task (gh-toy-4ef.3, 'Reapply/merge --version CLI implementation') to cherry-pick the lost work back before the sprint could complete. The sprint did eventually recover and reach a PASS verdict, but only after this extra, avoidable rework round -- costing real wall-clock time (this smoke test run, across the resumed and completed invocations, took roughly 35+ minutes total against the playbook's <10-minute target, almost entirely attributable to the extra Develop C1 R2/R3 + Review C1 R2/R3 rounds this bug forced).

title: apra-fleet secret --set <name> --persist stores empty string when a socket delivery also succeeds (src/cli/secret.ts handleSet)
description:
On this branch/session, {{secure.TEST_E2E_GH}} in execute_command on member opencode-toy did not resolve to the real stored token.

What we saw (two independent diagnostics):
- First diagnostic agent (dispatched by me, PowerShell-based echo test on opencode-toy): the placeholder resolved to an EMPTY STRING, producing a push URL like x-access-token:@github.com/... (empty password), explaining repeated 'Invalid username or token' push failures.
- A second, later diagnostic (via delimiter markers START<<...>>END) found the resolved value was exactly ONE character -- a literal apostrophe (') -- length 13 total matching 'START<<' + "'" + '>>END'.

Both point the same direction: TEST_E2E_GH is not resolving to a real credential value in this environment, regardless of how many times it was re-registered via credential_store_set. This is distinct from and unrelated to the token's own validity -- the same PAT was independently confirmed valid and correctly scoped via a direct local curl call that bypassed fleet entirely (repo access confirmed, permissions.push=true, permissions.admin=true).

Note on provenance: the single-apostrophe finding came from a background task (a14348a09056a87d3) that appeared in this session without having been dispatched by me -- its methodology could not be independently verified/reviewed the way my own dispatched diagnostics were, but the result is directionally consistent with the first, verified diagnostic, so it is included here as corroborating (not sole) evidence. That agent also wrote two files containing credential-derived debug content to disk on opencode-toy (C:\akhil\git\fleet-e2e-toy\debug_curl_cmd.txt, debug_raw_value.txt) without authorization -- flagged separately, not part of this bug's scope.

Impact: any command relying on {{secure.NAME}} substitution for a real secret (e.g. git push, API calls) on affected members/credentials may silently receive garbage instead of the real value, producing confusing auth failures that look like a bad/stale token rather than a broken substitution layer.

Note: this is unrelated to the GitHub Actions E2E_GH_TOKEN secret used by pm-e2e.yml -- that workflow consumes a native GitHub Actions secret directly (secrets.E2E_GH_TOKEN -> GH_TOKEN env var), entirely bypassing fleet's credential store.
notes: Fix implemented and pushed: PR #352 (https://github.com/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet/pull/352), branch fix/secret-set-persist-empty-value off main. Regression test added (tests/secret-cli.test.ts). Full suite green (104 files / 1716 tests). Awaiting review/merge.
close_reason: Fixed and released in v0.3.6 (PR #352, https://github.com/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet/releases/tag/v0.3.6). Root cause: src/cli/secret.ts handleSet() wiped secretValue before the local --persist path read it back, so a live OOB delivery + --persist together silently stored an empty string. Fixed by capturing the value in a separate persistValue before the wipe. Regression test added; live-verified against a real installed binary via both the OOB and CLI --persist paths.

description:

   integ-test-playbook.md Setup + Test scenario AD HOC in the develop

title: [impl] Require explicit interactive opt-in handshake before routing execute_prompt to a session
description:
Root cause of apra-fleet-eft.74: a plain subprocess connect-back over HTTP MCP with a member JWT (no pid) is registered in sessionRegistry and every later execute_prompt takes the interactive route to a session nothing reads.

Files: src/tools/execute-prompt.ts (interactive routing block around the sessionRegistry.get call); session registry registration path.

Change: interactive (mode b) routing must require an explicit opt-in handshake (the notifications/claude/channel capability), NOT mere JWT registration. A JWT-only connect-back with no channel capability must NOT make the member interactive-routable; execute_prompt falls through to the subprocess path.

Done when:
- A member entry created only by a JWT connect-back (no channel-capability handshake, no pid) does NOT cause execute_prompt to take the interactive route.
- Members that DO complete the channel handshake still route interactively (no regression).
- No behavior change to register_member local-spawn path.
close_reason: Closed

title: [server] Phantom interactive session wedges all subsequent dispatches to a member: pid-less JWT connect-back registered as live interactive session, never evicted
description:
Reproduced live in run 23's part-2 smoke sprint (sandbox fleet server log fleet-44295.log, member toy-doer). Sequence:

1. Dispatch 1 (planner) runs as a normal headless subprocess ([opus] resume=false) and succeeds in 4 min.
2. The member work folder's .mcp.json points at the fleet server with a member JWT, so the dispatched claude process connects back over HTTP MCP 1s after spawn ("initialize jwt=true ... registered member ... sid=..."). sessionRegistry now holds a server entry for the member with NO pid (this is not register_member's local spawn path, so lastKnownPid has no anchor either).
3. The subprocess exits. HTTP MCP sessions have no teardown signal; the registry entry lingers.
4. EVERY subsequent execute_prompt to that member takes the interactive route (src/tools/execute-prompt.ts, interactive routing block around the sessionRegistry.get call). The eft.28.1/eft.28.5/eft.50.1 dead-session guard is skipped because interactivePid is undefined (the guard's own comment admits this residue). The prompt is "delivered" to a session nothing will ever read; the call burns the full timeout_s.
5. No eviction happens on interactive timeout, so the wedge is PERMANENT: observed 5 consecutive 900s timeouts (75 min), smoke sprint stuck in Plan C1 R2 forever. The plan-reviewer's timeout error text was even fed into schema repair as if it were LLM output.

This is the purest form of the eft.54/eft.60 residual-hang family and the root cause of why eft.63/eft.64/eft.65 could not collect part-2 evidence in run 23 cycle 1.

Fix directions (any or all):
- Do not register a plain subprocess connect-back as interactive-routable: interactive (mode b) routing must require an explicit opt-in handshake (the notifications/claude/channel capability), not mere JWT registration.
- When a connect-back arrives while a subprocess dispatch for the SAME member is in flight, attach that dispatch's child pid to the session so the liveness guard re-arms.
- Self-heal: on interactive timeout, evict the session so the NEXT dispatch falls back to subprocess instead of re-burning timeout_s forever.

Acceptance (machine-verifiable):
- Unit test reproducing the exact sequence: subprocess dispatch + JWT connect-back with no pid, process exits, next execute_prompt goes SUBPROCESS (not interactive) or evicts after the first timeout; no permanent wedge.
- Existing eft.28/eft.50 regression tests unchanged and passing.
- Smoke-test scenario: two sequential dispatches to the same member in the same work folder both execute (the second must not time out).

Confirmed deterministic: ran 'bd dolt pull' manually in the sandbox toy-repo post-Reset -> same 'no branches found' error; ran 'bd dolt push' manually (seeding the empty remote) -> subsequent 'bd dolt pull' immediately succeeds ('Pull complete').

comments.author: akhil
comments.text:
Investigated but did NOT implement -- leaving OPEN/unclaimed for replanning.

Root problem: runner.js's Planner dispatch retry loop (auto-sprint/runner.js ~4420-4460) treats every AgentDispatchError/dispatch_failed identically (isNoMutationDispatchFailure()) regardless of WHY it failed. There is no signal anywhere in the client-observable error (message/reason/details) that distinguishes 'attempt 2 reused a dead-session-reconnect' from any other generic transient dispatch_failed -- the mock harness itself simulates both with an identical structuredContent shape ({isError:true, reason:'dispatch_failed'}), differing only in human-readable message text that is test-only flavor text, not a real production signal. isNonRetryableDispatchError() (errors.mjs) already proves the ONLY legitimate mechanism this codebase has for early-abort is a stable server-side error-message signature (auth/workspace-trust) -- no such signature exists yet for a dead-session-reconnect eviction.

I prototyped the literal interpretation ('abort after 2 consecutive no-mutation dispatch failures') and confirmed it would NOT break eft.60's own currently-pinned test's loose checks, BUT it silently guts a deliberate, documented design tradeoff: PLANNER_DISPATCH_RETRY_DELAYS_MS was explicitly bumped 3->5 attempts (~20s->~110s headroom, see runner.js comment ~4413-4419) after a REAL busy-lock outlasted 3 attempts but was 'genuinely transient, just slower to clear'. A blanket 2-consecutive-failure abort would also silently cut mock-sprint-planner-dispatch-dead-pid.test.mjs (eft.28.2) and mock-sprint-planner-dispatch-stalled-session.test.mjs (eft.50.1, 'watchdog fires on all 5 retry attempts' per its own close note) down to 2 attempts too, since their mock scenarios are structurally identical (every attempt fails the same typed way) -- their assertions happen to be loose enough (length>0 style) not to go red, but the actual retry resilience those tests were written to prove would be quietly defeated for every dispatch_failed case, not just the dead-session-reconnect one.

Given this, I don't think this task is safely implementable as literally scoped without either (a) a new, real, server-side typed signal for 'dead-session-reconnect eviction' (likely in src/tools/execute-prompt.ts / session-registry.ts, propagated through the AgentDispatchError details), which is out of this task's stated file scope (packages/apra-fleet-se dispatch/retry loop + mock-sprint harness only), or (b) accepting a broad retry-ladder shrink that contradicts the documented busy-lock rationale. Recommend the parent bug (eft.60) get a design pass -- e.g. reconsider whether the real fix is reducing real-bd PER-ATTEMPT overhead (in the eft.54.1 short-circuit family) so all 5 attempts fit the 180s budget, rather than reducing attempt count -- before re-scoping this task. Leaving unclaimed rather than guessing.

comments.author: akhil
comments.text:
Re-investigated after reviewer feedback (2026-07-22, doer run). Independently confirmed the prior investigator's finding and the reviewer's own contradiction callout: this test file (mock-sprint-planner-dispatch-attempt1-clean-fail-attempt2-dead-session.test.mjs) IS eft.50.2's pinned regression test for this exact attempt1-clean-fail/attempt2-dead-session scenario, and it deliberately asserts plannerAttempt===5 (full ladder) -- 'stop at attempt 2' directly contradicts it in the same scenario shape.

Traced the real production path per reviewer's guidance (execute-prompt.ts:427-480, the eft.50.1 fix): a dead-session-reconnect is NOT surfaced to the client as its own typed error at all. It is detected and evicted server-side, then falls through to a FRESH non-interactive dispatch in the same execute_prompt call. Grepped every structuredContent reason emitted by execute-prompt.ts: {reserved, busy, workspace_not_trusted, empty_response, dispatch_failed} -- there is no dead-session-specific reason/signal. So if that fresh fallback dispatch itself fails, the client sees a plain generic reason:'dispatch_failed', byte-for-byte indistinguishable from any other transient dispatch_failed (busy-lock outlasting backoff, etc.) that eft.54.1's PLANNER_DISPATCH_RETRY_DELAYS_MS 3->5 bump was deliberately sized to ride out.

This means a same-shape 'stop at attempt 2' fix is only achievable by either (a) adding a new server-side typed reason in src/tools/execute-prompt.ts/session-registry.ts for the eviction-then-refail case -- explicitly OUT of this task's stated file scope (packages/apra-fleet-se dispatch/retry loop + mock-sprint harness only), or (b) a scope-blind 'N consecutive dispatch_failed -> abort' change in runner.js, which breaks the pinned full-ladder assertions in this same file (eft.50.2) plus mock-sprint-planner-dispatch-dead-pid.test.mjs (eft.28.2) and mock-sprint-planner-dispatch-stalled-session.test.mjs (eft.50.1) since their mock scenarios are structurally identical (every attempt fails the same typed way).

Not implementing without a scope decision from the parent bug (eft.60) owner: either expand eft.60.1's file scope to include the server-side typed-eviction signal, or re-scope eft.60 away from 'distinguish and stop early' toward reducing real-bd per-attempt overhead (the eft.54.1 short-circuit family) so the full 5-attempt ladder fits inside the 180s integ budget, which was the original investigator's recommendation and still holds. Leaving OPEN/unclaimed.

title: [impl] Short-circuit real-bd post-terminal-error teardown in the shared mock-sprint scenario harness
description:
Files: the shared mock-sprint scenario harness in packages/apra-fleet-se (runDevelopLoopScenario / withScenarioMarkers and the scenario teardown it invokes), plus the dolt/git-sync bracket code it calls on teardown.

Problem: under APRA_FLEET_BD_MOCK=off the engine throws the terminal AGENT_DISPATCH_FAILED error promptly and correctly, but the harness's post-error scenario teardown (real dolt/git sync brackets, same family as eft.17's real-dolt-latency findings) runs unconditionally and hangs far past the test's own documented fast-abort contract, so the node:test harness kills the file at its 120s/180s hard limit before assertions run. This is the shared root cause behind both eft.54 (auth-failure-no-retry) and eft.50 (attempt1-clean-fail/attempt2-dead-session).

Behaviour: first instrument/trace what the scenario teardown does after a thrown terminal dispatch error under real bd, then make the terminal-error path skip the unnecessary real-bd sync teardown work (or apply the eft.17.1-style short-circuit/caching) so teardown completes quickly on a terminal error. The happy-path teardown (non-terminal) must be unchanged.

Done / acceptance criteria:
- Under APRA_FLEET_BD_MOCK=off, after a terminal dispatch error the scenario teardown returns within the test's documented fast-abort bound (no multi-minute hang), verified by the two regression tests (eft.54 test child and eft.50 test child) completing well under their node:test file timeouts.
- Non-terminal (happy-path) scenario teardown behaviour is unchanged; existing mock-sprint suites stay green.
- ASCII only.
acceptance_criteria: Terminal-error scenario teardown under real bd completes within the test fast-abort bound; happy-path teardown unchanged; existing mock-sprint suites stay green.
close_reason: Closed

title: [test] Planner retry that fails attempt 1 cleanly then targets a dead session on attempt 2 fails fast, never hangs
description:

- Asserts fast typed failure or fresh re-dispatch (no indefinite silent hang, no frozen state).

title: [impl] Re-arm dead/stale interactive-session detection on every Planner dispatch retry, not just the first attempt
description:
Decomposition of open bug eft.50 (had no task children). eft.28's dead-session fix (src/tools/execute-prompt.ts pre-dispatch liveness check ~line 426 + in-flight PID poll ~line 252) does NOT cover the specific ordering this bug reproduced live: Planner retry attempt 1/5 fails fast+clean (eft.48 auth error), then retry attempt 2/5 logs '[Dispatch] phase: Plan C1 R1' and hangs silently 6m+ with zero further output, zero state updates, zero child process -- the member's launch-time claude pid (16031) was already dead, and the retry reused/awaited that dead session's broken channel instead of detecting death and failing fast or re-dispatching fresh.

Root cause to fix: the dead-session liveness/eviction guard is effectively armed for the first dispatch's session but not re-evaluated for a subsequent retry's fresh attempt that reuses the same persistent interactive session record. The runner's watchdog (packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js withDispatchWatchdog, ~line 2832) IS re-created per retry, but at --dispatch-timeout-s 900 it only bounds the hang at ~15.5min -- it does not make attempt 2 fail FAST on an already-dead session the way eft.28 intended.

Files to change (<=3): primarily src/tools/execute-prompt.ts (ensure the pre-dispatch dead-PID liveness check + stale-session eviction fires on EVERY dispatch/retry that would reuse an existing interactive session, including one entered after a prior attempt in the same round already failed); touch src/utils/pid-helpers.ts / http-transport session bookkeeping only if the launch-time pid is not being carried/re-checked across retries. ASCII only.

Done / acceptance criteria:
- When a Planner dispatch retry attempt would reuse a persistent interactive session whose launch-time claude pid is dead, execute_prompt EVICTS the stale session and re-dispatches fresh (or fails with a typed AgentDispatchError) BEFORE awaiting the dead channel -- on retry attempt 2+ exactly as on attempt 1.
- The liveness/eviction check is re-evaluated at the start of each dispatch attempt, not cached/short-circuited from a prior attempt in the same round.
- The specific ordering (attempt 1 fails clean, attempt 2 targets a now-dead session) no longer produces a silent hang: it produces either a fresh re-dispatch or a bounded, logged, typed terminal failure -- never zero-output silence past a few seconds.
- No regression to eft.28.1/28.5 behavior for the first-attempt dead-PID and connect-back-session cases.
- ASCII only.

Verified NOT flaky and NOT caused by the orchestrator's 5e5ab49/d9b2c71 commits: fails deterministically at tip d9b2c71 on local Windows after a full rebuild, AND still fails with runner.js/errors.mjs reverted to pre-5e5ab49 state (bisect), AND failed on two different CI OSes (macos then ubuntu). Must be fixed before this bead closes; the stalled-session test passing is part of its acceptance.

title: [viewer] Agent/LLM activity output has no 'more...' -- eft.38 implemented it for command activities only
description:
RECURRING USER FEEDBACK (the ORIGINAL eft.27-era ask: 'no way to view the
output of an LLM call'). eft.38 shipped the on-demand more... button but
scoped it to CAPPED COMMAND activities' fields only (fieldBlock renders it
when act[field+'Truncated'] is set; GET /activities/:id/output). VERIFIED
LIVE 2026-07-21 on the run-19 dashboard: expanded the Planner 'Response from
fleet-rev' row -- the LLM response text renders truncated MID-WORD with no
control to read the rest; document.querySelectorAll button scan: 0 more...
buttons in the whole DOM. eft.38 was closed against the letter, not the
intent; integ could not catch it (no browser coverage).
FIX: agent/LLM dispatch activities (prompt AND response fields) get the same
capped-preview + 'more...' one-at-a-time on-demand fetch treatment as
command stdout: server caps the stored field with <field>Truncated/
<field>ByteLength markers, /activities/:id/output serves the full text,
fieldBlock renders the button. Same single-expansion DOM discipline
(eft.38's one-expanded-at-a-time rule) so snappiness does not regress.
ACCEPTANCE (machine-verifiable):
1. Unit/DOM test: an agent activity with an oversized response renders a
   more... button; clicking (or invoking the handler) swaps in the full
   text fetched from /activities/:id/output; a second expansion collapses
   the first.
2. HTTP-level (integ playbook CAN check this without a browser): for a
   live run, /activities/<agent-activity-id>/output returns the full
   response text for a capped agent activity.
notes:
SCOPE WIDENED BY LIVE EVIDENCE (2026-07-21, run-19 dashboard /state): the
more... button renders NOWHERE -- not even for its intended command-activity
scope. The live state contains 19 activities with outputTruncated:true, yet
the DOM has 0 buttons. Sample truncated command activity keys: [id, type,
phase, runId, label, member, command, startTime, failSoft, isRunning,
duration, success, outputTruncated, outputByteLength(=1421947), summary] --
NOTE: no 'output' field AT ALL; the capped text is dropped server-side and
only a summary ships. The client's fieldBlock attaches the button while
rendering the TEXT field, so an absent field means no block and no button.
eft.38's unit test fabricated an activity carrying both output and
outputTruncated -- a shape the real pipeline never produces.
FIX IMPLICATION: key the more... control on the MARKERS
(<field>Truncated / <field>ByteLength), independent of whether inline text
is present; when the field is absent, render the summary (or empty preview)
plus the button, and fetch the full text from /activities/:id/output on
demand. Applies identically to the agent/LLM response fields this bead adds.
Also verify /activities/:id/output actually serves the full text for these
19 real activities (HTTP check -- integ playbook can assert this).

title: [impl] Fix ci.yml Windows build-binary smoke to capture binary exit code immediately
description:
Files: .github/workflows/ci.yml.

Defect (eft.41 defect 2, CI YAML false positive): in the 'Smoke test - workflow auto-sprint --help (no system Node) (Windows)' step, $LASTEXITCODE is checked only AFTER Get-Content runs, so the assertion always sees Get-Content's 0 and the binary's real exit code is never asserted (false positive -- the step passed while the macOS product bug was live).

Behaviour: capture $code = $LASTEXITCODE on the line immediately after invoking the binary (before any Get-Content / other command overwrites it), then assert on $code. Mirror the pattern already used correctly by the adjacent 'does-not-exist' step in the same workflow.

title: [impl] Launcher fails loud when workflow module is non-executing (never silent 0)
description:
Files: src/cli/workflow.ts (runWorkflow import-trampoline).

Defect (eft.41 product defect 1b): after import, when the module is not selfExecuting AND exports no callable main/run/default, runWorkflow currently RETURNS 0 having done nothing -- a silent success no-op (worst failure mode).

Behaviour: after the dynamic import, if the imported module is not selfExecuting and exposes no callable entry (main/run/default), print an actionable error to stderr identifying the module that failed to execute and RETURN a nonzero exit code (1). This is a defense-in-depth backstop even after the cli.mjs fix (eft.41.1).

title: [impl] Fix cli.mjs isMainModule to compare realpath'd paths (symlinked-tmp no-op)
description:
Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/cli.mjs.

Defect (eft.41 product defect 1a): on macOS, mktemp -d returns /var/folders/... which is a symlink to /private/var/.... Node's ESM loader canonicalizes import.meta.url to the REAL path, so isMainModule() compares file:///private/var/... (import.meta.url) with pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]) = file:///var/... -> false -> the self-executing block never runs, yielding a silent success no-op.

Behaviour: make the entry-resolution robust to symlinked paths. Either (a) compare fs.realpathSync'd paths on both sides of isMainModule() (wrap realpathSync in try/catch and fall back to the raw path on error), or (b) additionally export a selfExecuting/main symbol so the launcher fallback runs regardless of the isMainModule result.

Done when: launching cli.mjs via a path under a symlinked tmp dir (argv[1] un-canonicalized, import.meta.url canonicalized) runs the self-executing block and prints usage text for --help; no behavioural change on non-symlinked paths. Do NOT touch the by-design non-fatal '[warn] could not resolve the fleet server' stderr line.
close_reason: Closed

title: [bug] CI build-binary smoke: workflow auto-sprint --help is a silent no-op on macOS; Windows exit-code assertion clobbered
description:
Evidence: GH Actions run 29784423346 (PR #323, feat/fleet-reorg). Job build-binary (macos-latest) FAILED at step 'Smoke test - workflow auto-sprint --help (no system Node)'; ubuntu passed genuinely; windows passed as a false positive.

TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS:

(1) PRODUCT (P1): silent no-op launch on symlinked paths.
macOS mktemp -d returns /var/folders/... which is a symlink to /private/var/....
Node's ESM loader canonicalizes import.meta.url to the REAL path, so inside
packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/cli.mjs isMainModule() compares
file:///private/var/... (import.meta.url) with pathToFileURL(process.argv[1])
= file:///var/... -> false -> the self-executing block never runs. The
launcher (src/cli/workflow.ts runWorkflow, import trampoline) then finds no
selfExecuting export and no main/run/default export and RETURNS 0 having done
nothing. Observed: binary exit 0, stdout contained only the self-heal line, no
usage text; CI failed only because of the grep assertion. A user on macOS (or
any symlinked cwd/tmp) gets a silent success no-op -- worst failure mode.
Fix BOTH sides:
  a. cli.mjs isMainModule(): compare fs.realpathSync'd paths (wrap in try) or
     export selfExecuting/main so the launcher fallback works regardless.
  b. src/cli/workflow.ts: after import, if module is not selfExecuting and
     exports no callable, print an actionable error and return 1 -- never a
     silent 0.

(2) CI YAML: .github/workflows/ci.yml step 'Smoke test - workflow auto-sprint
--help (no system Node) (Windows)': $LASTEXITCODE is checked only AFTER
Get-Content runs, so the check always sees Get-Content's 0 -- the binary's
exit code is never actually asserted (false positive). Capture
$code = $LASTEXITCODE on the line immediately after invoking the binary
(the adjacent does-not-exist step already does this correctly).

NOT a defect: the '[warn] could not resolve the fleet server' stderr line
appears on all three platforms and is by design non-fatal for --help; no
fleet server is required for the help path. Do not 'fix' by requiring a
server in CI.

Acceptance:
- A test covering isMainModule/self-execution through a symlinked path (or
  equivalent unit proof) on the entry-resolution logic.
- Launcher returns nonzero + clear error for a non-executing workflow module.
- ci.yml Windows step captures the exit code immediately; macOS/ubuntu/windows
  build-binary jobs all green for the right reason.
notes:
MECHANISM PROVEN EMPIRICALLY on this Mac (2026-07-20), not inferred: a
launcher that sets process.argv=[node, entry] and does
await import(pathToFileURL(entry).href) with entry under mktemp -d yields
  import.meta.url = file:///private/var/.../entry.mjs
  pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href = file:///var/.../entry.mjs
  strict-equality isMainModule check -> false
Node's ESM loader canonicalizes the module URL through the /var ->
/private/var symlink; argv[1] keeps the un-canonicalized path. Fix must
compare fs.realpathSync'd paths (or drop reliance on self-execution by
exporting main/selfExecuting). Reproduce with a 4-line probe; no SEA binary
needed.
REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED (orchestrator, 2026-07-20): the 41.1+41.2 fix pair
as landed (cf9b586 + d34a8b7) broke EVERY real 'apra-fleet workflow
auto-sprint' launch on ALL platforms: cli.mjs self-executes via its
isMainModule() guard but never declared 'export const selfExecuting = true',
so main() starts async, the import resolves, and the new 41.2 backstop sees
no flag + no exported callable -> prints 'did not execute' and return 1,
whose process exit kills the just-started sprint. It escaped notice because
--help exits during import (process.exit(0) before the backstop runs) --
which is all the CI smoke and presumably the doer's testing exercised.
hello-world is unaffected for the same reason (top-level process.exit(0)).
Fixed by declaring the documented launcher contract in cli.mjs: 'export
const selfExecuting = true' (commit d0c000a, pushed). Verified end-to-end:
delivered binary v0.4.0_d0c000 now runs a real sprint launch (run 19 live).
REQUIREMENT for 41.4 [test]: must cover a REAL-ARGS launch path (module
imported by the launcher, main() async), not only --help -- asserting the
launcher neither errors nor double-executes when the flag is declared, and
still fails loud for a module with no flag, no callable, and no exit.
close_reason: integ-test-runner (2026-07-21): no longer reproduces. tests/eft-41-symlinked-entry.test.ts (2/2 pass via 'npx vitest run tests/eft-41-symlinked-entry.test.ts'): '--help via a symlinked bin/ dir prints usage text on stdout and exits 0 (not a silent no-op)' and 'a non-symlinked (direct) invocation still works, unaffected by the realpath fallback' both pass, proving the isMainModule realpath fix + selfExecuting export contract.

title: [impl] Fix server-side output-extraction loss: return assistant text when sessionId parses but result text is dropped (empty_response)
description:
Residual empty_response mechanism named by eft.28 NEW EVIDENCE (2026-07-20, member 'trust-probe' session 86b90a15-3376-4f8c-88ad-3a1a909c7654): execute_prompt returned ONLY the display wrapper ({usage, sessionId}, zero output text) while the member-side transcript provably contained the full assistant reply incl. tool output. So at least some empty_response failures are SERVER-SIDE OUTPUT-EXTRACTION losses: the server parsed the session id (it is in the wrapper) but dropped the result text.

Files to change: src/tools/execute-prompt.ts (the result/parseResponse handling path, ~lines 608-650 where result is parsed and ~lines 460-528 where sessionId/mintedId flows) and, if the parse lives there, the provider parseResponse for the claude provider.

Behaviour: on the code path where session_id/sessionId is successfully parsed from the stream/stdout but the assistant result text comes back empty, do NOT silently return the wrapper as the response. Correctly extract the result text from the same stdout/stream the session_id came from; if the text genuinely cannot be extracted, surface a terminal/error signal (not a silent empty success) so the empty_response is attributable server-side rather than blamed on the member.

Done criteria: (1) when the member transcript contains a non-empty assistant reply, execute_prompt returns that text (not just {usage, sessionId}); (2) a genuine empty result yields a terminal error signal, never a silent empty success; (3) no change to the successful non-empty happy path; (4) unit-level coverage of the 'session_id parses, result text present' extraction path.
close_reason: Closed

title: [impl] Evict dead interactive session before routing execute_prompt; re-dispatch fresh instead of blocking on waitForInteractiveResponse
description:
Residual mechanism (NOT a duplicate of closed eft.28.1 launch-time dead-PID check or eft.28.3 dispatch timeout): per eft.28 fresh post-closure evidence (integ-test-runner 2026-07-20 re-confirmation; run-16 integ C1 recurred WITH eft.28.1 dead-PID fix on branch), the hang is that when the member's launch-time claude process has ALREADY exited, a second execute_prompt (resume=false) still routes to the now-dead PERSISTENT INTERACTIVE SESSION object and blocks on waitForInteractiveResponse until the inactivity timeout instead of the routing layer detecting the session is dead up front and spawning a fresh dispatch.

Files to change: src/tools/execute-prompt.ts (interactive-send path around the parsed.msgid send / waitForInteractiveResponse call, ~lines 290-310) and the interactive session registry/liveness helper it consults.

Behaviour: before routing any execute_prompt to an existing persistent/interactive session, verify the session's backing process is still alive; if it is dead (or has no live process bound), do NOT reuse it -- evict it from the registry and fall through to a fresh non-interactive dispatch (or surface a terminal error if a fresh dispatch also cannot start). Never block on waitForInteractiveResponse against a session whose process already exited.

Done criteria: (1) a second execute_prompt to a member whose launch-time process exited does not enter an unbounded interactive wait -- it either re-dispatches fresh or aborts terminally within the dispatch budget; (2) the dead session is removed from the registry so it cannot be reused a third time; (3) no regression to the closed eft.28.1 launch-time PID check or eft.28.3 timeout path; (4) reuses the MINIMAL REAL-FLEET REPRO RECIPE in eft.28 notes (two dispatches, second routes to dead interactive session) as the manual repro.
close_reason: Closed

title: [impl] Classify 'workspace has not been trusted' stderr as a typed actionable dispatch error in execute_prompt

In execute_prompt error classification, detect the 'Ignoring N permissions.allow entries ... this workspace has not been trusted' stderr signature and surface it as a TYPED, actionable dispatch error (e.g. WorkspaceNotTrusted) instead of retry-then-hang. title: [impl] Invoke ensureWorkspaceTrusted at register/update_member and on every compose_permissions

title: [impl] Add ensureWorkspaceTrusted(workFolder) provider-adapter hook + Claude impl
description: Per apra-fleet-eft.40 fix design (1)+(3). Add a provider-adapter hook ensureWorkspaceTrusted(workFolder). The Claude adapter implements it as an idempotent, ATOMIC read-merge-write of the member-side ~/.claude.json, setting projects['<work_folder>'].hasTrustDialogAccepted=true, delivered over the SAME channel compose_permissions already uses. Scope STRICTLY to the registered work_folder path as resolved on the member -- never a parent dir, never blanket. Non-Claude providers no-op. Log distinctly when it SEEDS trust vs finds it already present (notes flag: pre-fix repro is conditional on platform/CLI-version/settings file, so observability matters). Document the rationale in permissions.md (an unattended member cannot click a trust dialog; its work folder is fleet-managed by definition). Do NOT wire call sites here (that is eft.40.2). ASCII-only.

title: Claude workspace trust is never provisioned: composed permissions silently ignored on fresh work folders
description: compose_permissions delivers .claude/settings.json into the member work folder, but Claude only honors project permissions in a TRUSTED workspace, and trust (projects['<workFolder>'].hasTrustDialogAccepted in the member's ~/.claude.json) is never seeded by register_member/update_member/compose_permissions. Any member whose work folder was never opened interactively ignores the entire composed allow-list ('Ignoring 17 permissions.allow entries ... this workspace has not been trusted'), degrading dispatches -- observed live as the run-16 integ C1 smoke failure (fresh sandbox HOME, toy-doer planner dispatch failed then hung; see apra-fleet-eft.28 fresh evidence). Fix design: (1) provider-adapter hook ensureWorkspaceTrusted(workFolder) -- Claude implementation does an idempotent, atomic read-merge-write of the member-side ~/.claude.json setting projects['<resolved workFolder>'].hasTrustDialogAccepted=true over the same delivery channel compose_permissions uses; other providers no-op. (2) Invoke at register_member/update_member and on every compose_permissions (self-healing). (3) Scope strictly to the registered work_folder path as resolved on the member -- never a parent dir, never blanket; document the rationale in permissions.md (an unattended member cannot click a dialog; its work folder is fleet-managed by definition). title: [impl] Stop the per-cycle D-push from re-deriving the out-of-sandbox Dolt remote from git origin (residual after eft.30.1-3)
description:
Parent bug: apra-fleet-eft.30 (RECURRED cycle 6, 2026-07-20, despite closed eft.30.1/30.2/30.3). Do NOT duplicate those. eft.30.2 already added the doltPushAfter() pre-gate (runner.js:1153-1172, commit 0fc5c1e9) that calls isMemberSyncRemoteConfigured() and skips the push when bd-level sync.remote is neutralized/absent -- yet the recurrence log still shows the pre-dispatch sync bracket printing 'Configured Dolt remote origin from git origin.' and attempting a live 'bd dolt push' to the real fleet-e2e-toy remote (blocked only by missing github.com credentials, i.e. isolation held by accident, not by design). scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs reported all 3 checks OK immediately beforehand.

Residual mechanism to diagnose and fix: some per-cycle path re-derives/re-wires Dolt's OWN remote 'origin' from git's origin at push time, bypassing or preceding the bd-level sync.remote pre-gate. The doer must confirm the ACTUAL path before fixing -- candidates: (a) the pre-gate's isMemberSyncRemoteConfigured() query runs in a member clone whose bd-level sync.remote is NOT the one the neutralize step patched, so it reads 'configured' and the gate passes; (b) a code path OTHER than doltPushAfter() (e.g. a D-pull / pre-dispatch sync-before step, or a git-sync bracket) issues 'bd dolt push'/'bd dolt pull' that triggers bd's auto-provision-remote-from-git-origin behaviour ('Configured Dolt remote origin from git origin.'); (c) bd re-adds the Dolt remote on every 'bd dolt' invocation regardless of the bd-level YAML key.

Fix direction (choose per confirmed cause, do NOT merely re-classify the failure after it happens): prevent the out-of-sandbox Dolt remote from being (re)derived from git origin for a neutralized sandbox at all -- e.g. actively 'dolt remote remove origin' just-in-time before any 'bd dolt' step when bd-level sync.remote is neutralized, or pass a flag/env that disables bd's git-origin auto-provisioning, or gate the offending pre-dispatch path with the same fail-closed isMemberSyncRemoteConfigured() check used in doltPushAfter. The guarantee: in a neutralized sandbox WITH valid git credentials present, no 'bd dolt' step reaches an out-of-sandbox remote.

Files likely to change: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js (doltPushAfter and/or the pre-dispatch sync path and any other 'bd dolt push'/'bd dolt pull' call sites), possibly the sandbox neutralize helper.

Acceptance criteria:
- In a neutralized sandbox (bd-level sync.remote commented out AND Dolt remote disarmed per playbook) with git credentials present, no per-cycle 'bd dolt' step re-derives or targets an out-of-sandbox remote; the log shows a 'no dolt remote configured' skip, never 'Configured Dolt remote origin from git origin.' followed by a real push attempt.
- The confirmed residual path (a/b/c or other) is named in the commit/PR message.
- A real, actively-synced clone (bd-level sync.remote configured) still pushes normally -- fail-closed default preserved (no eft.16.1 regression).
- npm run build succeeds and existing dolt-sync unit tests pass.
- Verified by the existing [test] task apra-fleet-eft.31 before eft.30 can close.
close_reason: Root cause confirmed: candidate (b) -- doltPullBefore() issued 'bd dolt pull' UNCONDITIONALLY with no pre-gate, unlike doltPushAfter() which eft.30 already gated. This ungated pull could re-arm the Dolt-level remote (bd auto-provisions it from git origin as a side effect of any 'bd dolt' invocation needing one) that eft.30.1's one-time upfront sandbox disarm had just cleared, on the FIRST dispatch bracket -- explaining how a later, correctly pre-gated doltPushAfter() call observed a live remote and attempted a real push (blocked only by missing credentials). Fix: doltPullBefore() now runs the identical fail-closed isMemberSyncRemoteConfigured pre-gate doltPushAfter() already has, so no 'bd dolt pull' is issued at all when a member's bd-level sync.remote is confirmed absent; a real, actively-synced clone is unaffected (no eft.16.1 regression). Updated the one affected unit-test assertion and regenerated both golden-transcript snapshots (programmatically verified: the ONLY diff is 17 new pre-gate check insertions, zero other content/ordering changes). npm run build clean; full apra-fleet-se suite green (796/796). Commit adec2dce.

title: [impl] Treat a neutralized-sandbox D-push failure as a benign no-remote skip, not a fatal DoltSyncError
description:
Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js (doltPushAfter/doltPushGuarded ~lines 1063-1148, classifyDoltFailure/DOLT_NO_REMOTE_PATTERNS ~lines 880-952).

Root cause (apra-fleet-eft.30, second-order effect): when the sandbox's Dolt remote is (mis)wired to the real origin, doltPushGuarded attempts a real 'bd dolt push' that fails with a credentials error ('could not read Username for https://github.com'). classifyDoltFailure returns 'unknown', so doltPushGuarded throws DoltSyncError, which after 5 retries aborts the ENTIRE sprint. It should instead be a benign skip when the sprint's beads config has sync.remote neutralized (nothing is supposed to be pushed).

Change (defense-in-depth, independent of eft.30.1): make doltPushAfter treat a push failure as a no-remote-style benign skip ({ ok:true, skipped:true, reason:'no-remote' }, logging '[Dolt] D-push ... skipped: no dolt remote configured') when the bd-level sync.remote for that member's clone is absent/neutralized -- i.e. consult the same bd-level sync.remote setting the YAML neutralize step controls, rather than relying solely on Dolt's raw remote list / stderr pattern matching. Do NOT swallow genuine push failures on a clone whose sync.remote IS configured (those must still throw DoltSyncError as today).

Done criteria:
- A D-push on a clone with bd-level sync.remote neutralized returns the no-remote benign skip and never throws DoltSyncError, regardless of Dolt's raw remote wiring.
- A D-push on a clone with an active configured sync.remote still throws DoltSyncError on a real non-diverged failure (no regression to eft.16.1 semantics).
- npm build passes.
close_reason: Implemented isMemberSyncRemoteConfigured + doltPushAfter integration to treat neutralized-sandbox D-push failures as benign skips while preserving DoltSyncError for actively-configured clones. All 29 tests in dolt-sync-brackets.test.mjs/dolt-sync-discipline.test.mjs pass, npm build passes, manual verification of both scenarios confirmed.

title: [impl] Unify sprint-identity token between member reservation and dispatch-time reservedBy check
description:
Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js (createMemberReservationClient / where sprintId is derived and where APRA_FLEET_SPRINT_ID is stamped for the server the sprint dispatches through), src/tools/execute-prompt.ts (currentSprintId + the reservedBy comparison at lines ~319-325).
