title: [integ] Neutralizing sandbox sync.remote in config.yaml does not stop the per-cycle D-push from targeting the real fleet-e2e-toy Dolt remote
description:
Feature: N/A (playbook part 2 -- smoke test sandbox safety, integ-test-playbook.md ## Setup 'Neutralize sandbox sync.remote after any bd bootstrap --yes' + Test scenario step 3)
Expected: after running the playbook's documented neutralize step (commenting out .beads/config.yaml's sync.remote block) following 'bd bootstrap --yes', AND after scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs confirms both 'sync.remote is inert' and '0 commits ahead of origin/main', the per-cycle 'D-push' step that auto-sprint/runner.js's doltPushAfter()/syncMemberAfterOrdered() runs on every dispatch bracket should treat the sandbox as having no dolt remote to push to (runner.js's own doc comment for doltPushAfter describes exactly this: 'a local clone with no configured dolt remote ... has nothing to push -- this is a benign no-op skip, not an error'). This is the mechanism the playbook's Setup section says 'lets Test scenario step 3 rely on skip_dolt_push semantics'.
Actual: despite the neutralize step being performed and scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs passing BOTH checks immediately beforehand, the very first Planner dispatch's D-push step attempted a REAL 'bd dolt push' against origin (git+https://github.com/Apra-Labs/fleet-e2e-toy) and got as far as a live network/auth exchange:
  Error: push to origin/main: Error 1105: unknown push error; addTableFiles, updateManifestAddFiles: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': Device not configured
It was NOT classified/skipped as 'no-remote' -- it only failed because this machine has no git credentials configured for github.com, not because the sandbox correctly recognized the remote as disabled. Root cause: 'bd bootstrap --yes' clones the Dolt database itself from the real remote, which wires Dolt's OWN internal remote config (separate from bd's .beads/config.yaml 'sync.remote' YAML key) to the real 'origin'. The playbook's neutralize step and its verifier (scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs, from apra-fleet-eft.25.1/25.2) only patch/check the YAML key, not Dolt's own remote wiring -- so the isolation guarantee those (closed) issues were supposed to provide is incomplete. In an environment WITH valid git credentials for github.com, this exact sequence would have SUCCEEDED in pushing sandbox test mutations to the real shared fleet-e2e-toy Dolt remote that real users/CI depend on -- the precise hazard eft.25 was filed to prevent. It also has a second-order effect: this failure is not actually a soft/non-fatal condition at the sync-bracket layer (unlike the Harvest-phase 'bd dolt push', which IS explicitly non-fatal and skip_dolt_push-gated) -- doltPushGuarded() throws DoltSyncError on any non-diverged, non-no-remote failure, which after 5 retries (5s/15s/30s/60s backoff) aborted the ENTIRE sprint with terminalReason 'Sprint failed: DoltSyncError' and zero commits landed, even though the toy repo's beads config.yaml had sync.remote correctly neutralized throughout.
Test: run scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs (passes) immediately before invoking 'apra-fleet workflow auto-sprint' in the sandbox; then observe the first dispatch's D-push step in the sprint log -- it should log '[Dolt] D-push for member ... skipped: no dolt remote configured' but instead attempts and fails a real push.
Repro:
1. Setup per playbook incl. bd bootstrap --yes + neutralize sync.remote in $HOME/toy-repo/.beads/config.yaml.
2. node scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs $HOME/toy-repo -- confirm both OK lines.
3. register-member + self-provision a canary task (see apra-fleet-eft.29 repro for exact commands).
4. node dist/index.js workflow auto-sprint -i <canary> -m toy-doer -b integ-smoke-<ts> -B main -c 1
5. Observe the D-push failure in the sprint log ('could not read Username for https://github.com') rather than a 'no dolt remote configured' skip line.
Suggested fix direction: the neutralize step / check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs should also disarm or verify Dolt's own remote config (e.g. 'dolt remote remove origin' in the sandbox toy-repo's beads dolt database after bootstrap, or have doltPushGuarded's 'no-remote' classification consult the same bd-level sync.remote setting the YAML neutralize step controls, not just Dolt's raw remote list).
Full sprint log captured in /tmp/integ-smoke-sprint.log (this run); sprint state at sprint-logs/sprint_141218.json (sprintId 7992d6df-016e-4841-8d82-3b263eab419a). Related but distinct from apra-fleet-eft.25 (which addressed the config.yaml YAML key re-activation but not this deeper Dolt-remote-persistence gap).
notes: integ-test-runner (2026-07-20, cycle 6, feature apra-fleet-eft.11 pass): RECURRED again this cycle despite eft.30.1-3 showing closed. Both the YAML sync.remote neutralize step and the Dolt-level 'bd dolt remote remove origin' neutralize step were run per playbook Setup (and re-run after the fresh bd bootstrap --yes this cycle needed) and both verified clean via scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs (all 3 checks OK, 0 commits ahead of origin/main) immediately before the sprint run. Despite that, the auto-sprint pre-dispatch sync bracket logged 'Configured Dolt remote origin from git origin.' and attempted a live 'bd dolt push' to the real fleet-e2e-toy Dolt remote, failing only on 'could not read Username for https://github.com: Device not configured' (no credentials on this machine) -- not by design. This confirms the D-push step re-derives/re-wires the Dolt remote from git's own origin at push time, ignoring the just-verified neutralized state. Sandbox isolation held only by accident (missing local credentials), same as prior recurrences.
close_reason: Verified 2026-07-20/21: check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs checks 1-3 OK after bootstrap+neutralize; live auto-sprint log confirmed '[Dolt] D-pull/D-push for member toy-doer skipped pre-attempt: bd-level sync.remote neutralized/absent' on every dispatch bracket -- no live push attempt occurred. Residual git-origin-derived risk (not exploitable by any current code path) tracked separately as apra-fleet-eft.39.

title: [impl] Detect dead member claude process in interactive execute_prompt dispatch; never reuse a dead persistent session; enforce dispatch liveness timeout
description:
Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js (dispatch path / interactive execute_prompt handling) and the execute-prompt dispatch layer (packages/apra-fleet-se/src/.../execute-prompt.ts).

Problem (from apra-fleet-eft.28): when a member's launch-time claude process dies before producing a plan (e.g. pid 88175 exit=1 elapsed=1649ms, in=0 out=0), the orchestrator's next '[interactive] timeout=3600s' attempt reuses the ORIGINAL already-dead persistent MCP/elicitation session (pid 87356) instead of detecting the death and spawning a fresh dispatch. From that point the fleet server log records ZERO further lines for 6+ minutes and no watchdog fires. The eft.20.3 watchdog does NOT cover this earlier pre-plan dispatch-hang point.

Behaviour to implement:
- Before reusing a persistent interactive MCP/elicitation session for a dispatch, verify the underlying member claude process is alive (PID liveness). If it is dead, do NOT reuse it: either spawn a fresh dispatch/session or fail fast.
- Add a dispatch-level liveness/no-progress timeout so an [interactive] execute_prompt dispatch cannot hang silently for minutes: when no progress/output occurs within the bound, surface a terminal error (logged AND persisted to sprint state, matching the eft.20.3 surfacing style) instead of hanging.
- The 3600s interactive timeout must not be the only backstop for a member whose process already died before producing output.

Done criteria:
- A dispatch whose target member's claude process has died is either retried on a fresh process or fails with a surfaced, logged+persisted terminal error within the dispatch liveness bound (well under the playbook's <10min budget).
- No code path silently reuses a dead PID's persistent session.
- npm test passes; source is ASCII-only.
close_reason: Closed

title: [impl] Include target issue(s) in bdListScoped scope so a childless leaf sprint target passes pre-sprint validation and reaches Planning
description: File: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js, bdListScoped() (~lines 2698-2745; scope BFS at 2711-2723). title: [integ] auto-sprint pre-sprint validation rejects a childless single-issue sprint target, blocking the smoke test's core path
description:
Feature: N/A (playbook part 2 -- smoke test, integ-test-playbook.md ## Test scenario step 3)
Expected: per integ-test-playbook.md Test scenario step 3-4, running 'apra-fleet workflow auto-sprint -i <canary-id> -m <member> -b <branch> -B main -c 1' against a freshly self-provisioned, childless integ-canary task bead should let the Planner decompose/plan and dispatch work so the canary eventually closes.
Actual: the sprint aborts immediately in the 'Sprint Setup' group ('Ensure Sprint Branch' phase), before the Planner ever runs, with 'Pre-sprint validation failed: No open/in-progress/blocked/deferred beads found for scope --parent <canary-id>. Nothing to do.' Root cause: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js's bdListScoped() (used both for the --ready check and the notDoneBeads fallback at ~line 3222-3255) computes scope as strict DESCENDANTS of targetIssues only (BFS over the parent-child childrenOf map) and never includes the target issue(s) themselves in scopeIds. When the target passed via -i is a leaf bead with zero children (exactly what a fresh self-provisioned canary is, and what any brand-new single-task sprint target would be), scopeIds.size===0 so bdListScoped short-circuits to [] for both the --ready and notDoneBeads queries, and the hard fail at runner.js:3255 fires unconditionally -- before Planning, so the Planner never gets a chance to decompose the leaf into task-type children. This makes it structurally impossible to auto-sprint a single freshly-created leaf issue; only a target that ALREADY has at least one not-done descendant can proceed.

title: [impl] Surface silent doer/orchestrator death after Plan phase: watchdog must log+persist a terminal error instead of exiting quietly
description: The smoke-test run went completely silent: after the doer member session was created (fleet log line at session-registration), the fleet server log showed NO further activity for the rest of the ~10-min run -- no error, no exception, no exit line -- and both the doer member pid and the orchestrator pid were dead afterward with only the plan-approval commits landed. The observable defect to fix here is that a doer sub-session / orchestrator dying mid-Develop produces ZERO diagnostic signal. Add liveness/exit instrumentation so this failure mode is never silent again: (1) the PID-liveness watchdog (from supervisor feature apra-fleet-eft.4) must detect a doer member or orchestrator child that stops making progress / dies and write an explicit terminal error line to the fleet log AND to the sprint state file (e.g. phase-level lastError / a failed status), rather than the run just ending; (2) wrap the doer-dispatch boundary so an unhandled rejection or abrupt process exit during Develop is logged with cause before teardown. This does NOT require fully root-causing the external kill (tracked generically in auto-sprint-2 / auto-sprint-6); it requires making the death observable and recorded. Files: supervisor watchdog + doer-dispatch path under packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint. Cross-reference auto-sprint-2, auto-sprint-6.
acceptance_criteria: When a doer sub-session or orchestrator child dies or stalls mid-Develop, an explicit terminal error is (a) written to the fleet server log and (b) recorded in the sprint state file (failed/lastError), so no run can end after Plan with zero diagnostic signal. A test simulates a doer child that exits/stops responding after the Develop checkpoint and asserts both the log line and the persisted error state are produced.

title: [impl] Fix corrupted sprint state.json write: doubled-quote serialization producing "phase"":"Develop"
description: Locate the per-activity sprint-state writer implemented by feature apra-fleet-eft.2 (continuous running/ -> old_sprints/ state persistence) that produces sprint-logs/.state/<sprint>.state.json. The canary issue gh-toy-53y (and its decomposed child gh-toy-53y.1 with its [impl]/[test] subtasks) remained OPEN the entire time.   ...,"cycle":1,"phase"":"Develop","planApproved":true}

title: auto-sprint: doer.md's blanket issue_type check contradicts the documented structural (has-children) dispatch rule -- causes nondeterministic skip-vs-work outcomes on leaf bug/feature beads
description:
OBSERVED (this sprint run, auto-sprint/eft-service, apra-fleet-eft cycle 1): two doer dispatches, facing the SAME category of bead (a leaf bug-type bead with zero children -- i.e. genuinely workable, not a decomposed grouping parent), made OPPOSITE decisions:

- apra-fleet-eft.6.7 (issue_type=bug, no children): the doer session reasoned past doer.md's literal text, recognized this bead did NOT fall under the "skip non-task" exception since it has no children, implemented the missing regression test, and correctly closed it. Its own notes explicitly flag the ambiguity: "this bead's issue_type is 'bug' (not 'task') and it has no children ... so per the doer contract's Step 1 exception this did not fall under the 'skip non-task beads with children' carve-out ... would flag this bug/task-type distinction to the orchestrator for future bead typing."
- apra-fleet-eft.13 (issue_type=bug, no children -- VERIFIED via `bd show`/`bd list --parent apra-fleet-eft.13` returning zero children, status still open): a different doer dispatch, given a streak of [eft.10, eft.11, eft.12, eft.13], skipped ALL FOUR purely because "issue_type=feature/bug, not task, per `bd show`" -- WITHOUT checking whether any of them actually have children. eft.10/11/12 are legitimately-undecomposed P3 features (correct to skip), but eft.13 is a real, workable P1 bug with a concrete acceptance criterion (the Plan-reviewer's own earlier verdict this same cycle explicitly called it "a leaf bug with a self-contained acceptance criterion requiring a passing regression test") -- it should have been worked, not skipped. It remains open and unclaimed after this cycle.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by reading the actual file, not guessed): `~/.claude/agents/doer.md` itself contains the blanket, type-based rule that caused the second (incorrect) outcome:
  - Step 1 (line ~52-53): "If an assigned id turns out not to be `issue_type=task` (e.g. it is a `bug`/`feature`-typed bead with children, assigned to you in error), skip it, note why in your final report, and do not claim or close it."
  - Line ~122: "Do NOT close features or bugs -- only `issue_type=task` beads."
  - Line ~165: "NEVER close type=feature or type=bug issues"

This directly contradicts the system's own documented dispatch-eligibility semantics (runner.js comments, apra-fleet-xbu.C5, referenced multiple times in this session's other fixes): "a bead that has been decomposed into subtasks ... must never be dispatched to a doer alongside its own subtasks ... This is a STRUCTURAL check (does this ready bead have children in scope?), not an issue_type check -- retyping a bead to change its dispatch eligibility does not work ... A bead can be a leaf `type=task` OR a decomposed `type=bug`/`type=feature` parent; only the has-children structure tells them apart."

So the orchestrator side (runner.js's readyLeafBeads()) already implements the CORRECT structural rule, but doer.md's own written instructions to the LLM doer still describe the WRONG, purely type-based rule -- doer.md's parenthetical "(e.g. it is a bug/feature-typed bead with children...)" gestures at the structural distinction but the actual operative sentence ("If an assigned id turns out not to be issue_type=task ... skip it") and the blanket "NEVER close type=feature or type=bug" reinforce the type-only reading. Different doer sessions resolve this ambiguity differently -- one reads past it to the structural intent (correct), another follows the literal, simpler rule (incorrect) -- producing genuinely nondeterministic dispatch outcomes on the exact same category of bead.

SECONDARY EFFECT (orchestrator bookkeeping): when a doer streak entirely consists of skipped non-task beads (correct or not), the orchestrator currently logs it as "reported status VERIFY but bead(s) still open -- treating streak as FAILED." This conflates "doer correctly determined there was nothing to do" with "doer failed to do assigned work" -- both eft.13's genuine miss and any hypothetical correct all-skip streak look identical in the log as a bare "FAILED" outcome, adding noise and making a real miss (like eft.13) harder to notice/triage after the fact.

FIX DIRECTION (not yet implemented, needs doer.md text revision + possibly an orchestrator classification, not attempted here since doer.md is applied fleet-wide and changing it needs care): rewrite doer.md's Step 1/Step 2/Step 3 exception language to state the STRUCTURAL rule explicitly and primarily ("skip an assigned bead only if `bd show`/`bd list --parent <id>` shows it has children -- i.e. it is a decomposed grouping parent, regardless of its issue_type; a childless bug/feature is a real leaf and must be worked like a task"), removing or clarifying the misleading blanket "NEVER close type=feature or type=bug" line so it doesn't contradict the structural exception it's meant to describe. Separately, consider having the orchestrator distinguish "all-skipped, correctly" from "genuinely failed" streak outcomes in its logging/streak-outcome classification, so a real miss doesn't hide inside undifferentiated "FAILED" noise.
close_reason: Fixed: apra-pm/agents/doer.md:69-99 now implements the has-OPEN-children structural rule the bead demanded; the offending blanket never-close-feature/bug-types language is gone (grep confirms zero hits).

title: auto-sprint: dashboard Sprint tree nests by 'blocks' dependency edges, not 'parent' containment -- grandchildren render as flat top-level rows
description:
OBSERVED (per user's concern: "it is extremely important that the tree should look like a tree and not a flat list"): even after the auto-sprint-3 fix (bdListScoped now correctly includes descendants at any depth in sprintTasks), a level-3 grandchild (e.g. apra-fleet-eft.1.2, child of eft.1 via `--parent`) will show up in the dashboard's "Sprint" section instead of "Backlog" -- but it will NOT render nested/indented under eft.1 in the visual tree.

ROOT CAUSE: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/viewer-extensions.mjs's renderBeadsHtml() builds the tree entirely from `blocks`-type dependency edges (t.dependencies.filter(d => d.type === 'blocks')), explicitly NOT from `parent` (its own comment at line ~176: "Build a dependency tree from `blocks`-type edges, not `parent`"). A bead is nested under whichever bead its `blocks` dependency points at (its "primary blocker"); a bead with NO `blocks` edge to anything renders as a top-level root row regardless of its `--parent`.

Per this project's own GRAPH-SEMANTICS.md convention (referenced in runner.js comments), `parent` (containment: "this task is part of this feature") and `blocks` (work-order dependency: "this must finish before that starts") are deliberately separate, orthogonal edge types -- a task is not expected to have a `blocks` edge to its own parent. So a grandchild that has a `parent` edge to its feature but no `blocks` edge to anything will render as an unindented top-level row in the Sprint section -- visually flat for the containment hierarchy, even though auto-sprint-3 already fixed which SECTION it lands in.

This is the piece of the user's "tree should look like a tree" concern not addressed by auto-sprint-3. Fixing it requires a design decision (not made unilaterally here): (a) switch renderBeadsHtml's nesting to use `parent` instead of/in addition to `blocks`, or (b) render both graphs (containment nesting, with blocks-order called out inline per node), or (c) something else the containment-vs-dependency semantics call for. Needs user/maintainer decision before implementing.
close_reason: integ-test-runner (2026-07-27 cycle, SHA 998b15f344fe2611aad621281d556adb864d1487): defect no longer reproduces. dashboard-tree-grandchild-nesting.test.mjs and viewer-extensions.test.mjs both PASS in this cycle's real-bd part-1 pass (integ-suite-status.json), confirming renderBeadsHtml() now nests the Sprint tree by parent containment (grandchildren render nested, not flat top-level rows).

title: fleet-sprint: planner/plan-reviewer self-query bd --parent directly -- diverges from orchestrator's now-recursive scope
description:
OBSERVED (per user's DRY/componentization concern -- "it should not happen that the viewer tree sees one view of the tree but planner doer etc. see something else"): after fixing auto-sprint-3 (bdListScoped rewritten to a full-project BFS so the orchestrator's dashboard/dispatch scope now correctly includes descendants at any depth), planner.md and plan-reviewer.md still instruct the LLM agent to independently run `bd list --parent <sprint-id> --ready --json` and `bd blocked --parent <sprint-id>` directly via their own Bash access (see planner.md lines ~107-121, plan-reviewer.md lines ~49-53).

`bd list --parent` is and remains single-level only (bd's own CLI, not the orchestrator's JS) -- there is no recursive flag. So when planner/plan-reviewer explore the tree themselves (as opposed to being handed a pre-computed scope as data), they still only see direct children, the exact same limitation bdListScoped had before the auto-sprint-3 fix. This means the orchestrator's dashboard/dispatch view and the planner/plan-reviewer's own self-directed exploration can now diverge on any sprint with 3+ levels of nesting (epic -> feature -> task), which apra-fleet-eft has.

doer.md and reviewer.md are NOT affected the same way -- they only use `bd show <id>` for a specific, already-named bead id (no tree exploration), not `bd list --parent`.

FIX DIRECTION (not yet implemented, needs a design decision): either (a) teach planner.md/plan-reviewer.md to recurse (e.g. instruct them to walk `--parent` transitively, or use `bd list --all` + manual filtering, mirroring the orchestrator's BFS), or (b) have the orchestrator hand the already-computed scope (bdListScoped's result) to these agents as data in their dispatch prompt, removing the need for them to independently query bd for structure at all -- (b) is more DRY and is the direction the user's message leans toward ("all parts of the code get the same view of the beads").
notes: triage 2026-08-09 (autosprint-internals batch): READY-AS-IS / NEEDS-DEEPER-DESIGN (one design call, then small). Still reproduces, re-verified by reading the agent contracts today. NAMING -- stale 'auto-sprint' for fleet-sprint (subject is bdListScoped and the orchestrator's dashboard/dispatch scope, both in fleet-sprint/runner.js -- bdListScoped is live at runner.js:5134). Title corrected. REPRO: planner.md:177-178 still tells the agent to run 'bd blocked --parent <root-id>' and 'bd list --parent <root-id> --ready --type=task --json' itself, and plan-reviewer.md:58 and :76 still do the same ('bd list --parent <scope> --status=open --json'). Confirmed single-level empirically: 'bd list --parent apra-fleet-ak5' returns exactly the 4 direct children, no grandchildren. Meanwhile the orchestrator's bdListScoped does a full BFS (runner.js:5134-5238), so the divergence the bead describes is real and intact. Notably _shared/GRAPH-SEMANTICS.md:33-38 now documents the one-id-per-call limitation and tells agents to merge multiple roots by hand, but never tells them to RECURSE -- so the docs currently entrench the single-level view rather than fixing it. doer.md/reviewer.md remain unaffected as the bead says (bd show <id> only). The fable-model comment's escalation argument still holds. Design decision between (a) recurse in prompts and (b) hand agents the pre-computed bdListScoped scope as prompt data is still unmade; (b) remains the DRY choice and is a modest change. Keeping P1.

comments.author: Bot
comments.text: Independent fable-model review flagged this as more urgent than 'deferred, needs design call' implies: fixing the orchestrator's bdListScoped (auto-sprint-3) WIDENED this divergence rather than just leaving it unchanged -- both orchestrator and planner/plan-reviewer were single-level-wrong before (same wrong answer, no visible split); now only the LLM agents are, meaning the orchestrator can dispatch/track level-3+ tasks the planning agents structurally cannot see in their own bd --parent queries. title: auto-sprint: eft sprint process died silently mid-Develop-phase, no error logged, leaving uncommitted work
description:
OBSERVED: The auto-sprint run for apra-fleet-eft (task b0wm0tejb, launched via bin/cli.mjs --issue apra-fleet-eft --members fleet-reorg --branch auto-sprint/eft-service --base feat/fleet-reorg --viewer-port 18300) stopped partway through Develop Cycle 1 Round 1. Harness reported status "killed" with no user action taken to stop it.

TIMELINE:
1. Sprint Setup + Plan C1 R1 completed normally: plan-reviewer returned verdict APPROVED with full task-tier assignments logged.
2. Develop C1 R1 began: streak assignment computed (14 streaks across eft.1-eft.13 + apra-fleet-ire), first streak [apra-fleet-eft.1.2, apra-fleet-eft.1] dispatched to fleet-reorg.
3. Log ends immediately after that dispatch line -- no error, exception, or shutdown message of any kind. Last log write: 2026-07-17 23:40:08.
4. Two commits DID land on the branch before death (fffc299 "fix(apra-fleet-eft.2.1): make SIGINT test mock honor abort signal", 2062e5a "feat(auto-sprint-eft.1.2): route typed sprint-abort errors through finalizeAbort + terminal history record") -- so real work happened past what the log shows, meaning the log itself stopped updating before the process actually died (or output buffering hid later lines).
5. At kill time: dashboard port 18300 no longer LISTENING, no fleet-se node process alive at OS level, and the working tree was left with uncommitted changes:
   - modified: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/docs/README.md
   - untracked: .tmp-s8-log.txt, .tmp/, test/dispatch-safety-guard.test.mjs

ANALYSIS:
1. No crash signature (no stack trace, no "Error:", no exit-code line) appears anywhere in the captured log -- this looks like the process was terminated externally (SIGTERM/SIGKILL from outside the script), not a script-level fault. I launched it via Bash run_in_background specifically to avoid the "tool-call process group killed on return" failure mode the docs/README.md itself warns about -- worth checking whether that failure mode occurred anyway (e.g. session/job boundary reaping background processes), which would mean the harness-tracked backgrounding does NOT actually protect against it on this platform.
2. The README.md diff left uncommitted is notable: a doer streak (either eft.1.2 or eft.2.1, neither of which is "update the example launch command in this doc") edited the top-of-file example to match this exact session's invocation (issue apra-fleet-eft, branch auto-sprint/eft-service, base feat/fleet-reorg, log path changed to ./sprint-logs/auto-sprint.log). This is scope creep outside the dispatched task's stated acceptance criteria and, combined with auto-sprint-1's finding that this same file steers agents away from the sanctioned Workflow tool, is worth a human looking at directly -- an agent silently keeping this file's example "fresh" to match whatever was last run is a way for the file's instructions to stay perpetually plausible/current-looking regardless of whether they're still correct.
3. Uncommitted work is NOT lost (git status confirms working tree still has it) but is at risk if anything runs git clean/reset before it's triaged. title: Fixed-port test servers in apra-fleet-workflow cause EADDRINUSE cascade -> sprint-wide MCP transport timeout
description:
Root-caused via the fleet-reorg member's actual Claude Code session transcripts (~/.claude/projects/C--akhil-git-apra-fleet-reorg/) after the apra-fleet-eft auto-sprint (branch auto-sprint/eft-service) FAILED: every doer streak from eft.2 onward hit "Transport closed" / "tools/call timed out after 900000ms", retried once, failed again, until the sprint gave up entirely.

TIMELINE:
- Session ee09231b-7afd-48a2-a296-2c49cb88774f: eft.1.1 doer completes cleanly at 2026-07-17T07:39 UTC, commits 7b756ce.
- Session 03816911-3cf2-47cc-99a6-7468a061d9ab (the very next dispatch, eft.2.1 doer): spends the rest of its turn diagnosing an EADDRINUSE-style port conflict on port 18099/18100 -- leftover node.exe processes (observed PIDs 49144, 49260, 29388) from a PRIOR abandoned attempt were still holding those ports. The doer polled with `sleep 20` / `timeout 90 bash -c 'while kill -0 <pid> ...'`, then manually taskkill'd the stale PIDs before it could proceed. This legitimately exceeded the fleet's 900s MCP tools/call timeout even though the CLI session was still alive and working.

ROOT CAUSE (two-fold):
1. packages/apra-fleet-workflow's test suite hardcodes FIXED ports for createDashboardViewer() test servers instead of ephemeral (port: 0):
   - test/apra-fleet-workflow-debounced-writer.test.mjs: 18099, 18100, 18101 (eft.2.1's own feature test)
   - test/apra-fleet-workflow-viewer-lifecycle.test.mjs: 18091-18098
   - test/test-runner.test.mjs: 18080
   - test/manual/e2e-runner.mjs: 18081
   Any two overlapping/retried runs of the same test file collide on the same port.
2. When the fleet's MCP tools/call request times out waiting on a doer turn, runner.js's dispatch-exception retry (apra-fleet-02s.1) spawns a FRESH claude CLI invocation for the same work -- but the PREVIOUS CLI invocation's own backgrounded child processes (e.g. `(node --test ... > /tmp/out.txt 2>&1 &)`, spawned by the doer itself mid-turn) are never killed, since the timeout only tears down the fleet-side transport, not the underlying OS process tree. Those orphans then hold the SAME fixed port for the retry too, so the retry stalls out identically and times out again -- spawning yet more orphans. This is a self-reinforcing cascade, not a transient blip, which is why the sprint never recovered once it started at eft.2 and every subsequent streak failed the same way.

FIX DIRECTION:
- Change every hardcoded createDashboardViewer test port above to `port: 0` (OS-assigned ephemeral) and read the actual bound port back via `server.address().port`, mirroring the NOTE already present at test-runner.test.mjs:196-199 (which deliberately chose a fixed port there for a different, narrower reason -- worth re-checking whether that reasoning still holds once the others are fixed).
- Separately/defense-in-depth: runner.js's dispatch-exception retry path (or execute-prompt.ts's dispatch layer) should make a best-effort attempt to terminate the abandoned CLI invocation's process tree on a transport timeout, not just abandon it -- so a slow-but-alive turn cannot leave orphaned child processes behind for the retry to collide with.
- Add regression coverage: two back-to-back/overlapping runs of the same fixed-port test file (simulating a retry-after-timeout scenario) must not EADDRINUSE.
acceptance_criteria: Every hardcoded createDashboardViewer test-server port in packages/apra-fleet-workflow tests is changed to port:0 (OS-assigned ephemeral) with the actual bound port read back via server.address().port -- covering debounced-writer.test.mjs (18099/18100/18101), viewer-lifecycle.test.mjs (18091-18098), test-runner.test.mjs (18080) and manual/e2e-runner.mjs (18081); the deliberate fixed-port NOTE at test-runner.test.mjs:196-199 is re-evaluated and either kept with a written rationale or converted to ephemeral. The full apra-fleet-workflow suite passes even when the same test file is run twice concurrently/retried, with no EADDRINUSE. Defense-in-depth: the dispatch-exception retry path (runner.js or execute-prompt.ts) makes a best-effort terminate of the previous CLI invocation's OS process tree on a transport timeout so orphaned doer children no longer hold the same port across a retry. npm test passes; source is ASCII-only.
close_reason: integ-test-runner (2026-07-21): no longer reproduces. packages/apra-fleet-workflow/test/apra-fleet-workflow-ephemeral-ports.test.mjs (eft.13.4, 3/3 pass via 'node --test'): back-to-back, overlapping, and 5x-repeated runs of a formerly-fixed-port test file each bind a distinct ephemeral port with no EADDRINUSE even while all old fixed ports 18080-18101 are held by an orphan.

title: Dashboard viewer misclassifies grandchild+ sprint tasks as Backlog (bd list --parent is single-level, unlike --ready)
description:
Found live during the running apra-fleet-eft auto-sprint (dashboard http://localhost:18310, branch auto-sprint/eft-service): every leaf-level task bead (e.g. apra-fleet-eft.1.1, two levels below the epic under feature apra-fleet-eft.1) appears in the dashboard's "Backlog" section instead of nested under "Sprint", even while actively being dispatched, closed, and committed by the running sprint.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via direct bd calls against this repo's real DB):
- `bd list --parent apra-fleet-eft --json` (plain, no --ready) returns ONLY the 12 direct-child features (eft.1..eft.12) -- it does NOT recurse into their own children (the 46 actual task-level leaves).
- `bd list --parent apra-fleet-eft --ready --json` DOES recurse through the full descendant tree (returns leaf tasks like eft.1.2, eft.4.1, eft.3.1, etc. alongside the features) -- so bd's own --parent filter behaves inconsistently depending on whether --ready is also passed.
- packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js's bdListScoped() (~line 1290) and updateDashboard() (~line 1539) call the PLAIN (non---ready) form to build sprintTasks for the dashboard's beads panel. Since leaf tasks are absent from sprintTasks, updateDashboard()'s backlogTasks computation (~line 1575-1580, "everything open/deferred project-wide MINUS sprintIds") then incorrectly captures them as backlog, even though they belong to the sprint and have no relation to any other epic.

SCOPE OF IMPACT: this is a DASHBOARD/VIEWER bug only. Real dispatch/streak-assignment logic already uses --ready-flavored queries elsewhere in runner.js, which DO recurse correctly -- confirmed by the running eft sprint successfully dispatching and closing apra-fleet-eft.1.1 (a grandchild task) in this exact run. No dispatch-scope or sprint-completion logic is affected, only the dashboard's visual Sprint/Backlog split.

FIX DIRECTION: bdListScoped()'s plain (non-ready) call needs to become recursive -- either by unioning bd list --parent <id> --json across every feature-level child returned by the top-level query (walk one extra level), or by finding/using a genuinely recursive bd query if one exists (bd list --help currently shows --parent as single-level-only with no descendant/recursive flag). Whichever fix path is chosen, add regression coverage asserting a 3-level epic->feature->task hierarchy renders its leaf tasks nested under Sprint, not Backlog.
acceptance_criteria: bdListScoped()'s plain (non---ready) call in packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js becomes recursive (union bd list --parent across every feature-level child, or an equivalent genuinely-recursive query) so that leaf task beads two or more levels below the epic appear nested under Sprint in the dashboard, not under Backlog. updateDashboard()'s backlogTasks computation no longer captures in-sprint leaf tasks. A regression test asserts that a 3-level epic->feature->task hierarchy renders its leaf tasks under Sprint (not Backlog). Dispatch-scope and sprint-completion logic remain unchanged. npm test passes; source is ASCII-only.
close_reason: Root-cause fix (bdListScoped recursive BFS) was already merged as commit 7fcebd1a (auto-sprint-3); added the missing regression test asserting a 3-level epic->feature->task hierarchy renders its leaf task under Sprint, not Backlog, in updateDashboard()'s published beads state.

title: [Phase 1] Combined member + issue-scope reservation ledger
description: Plan Part 2.2 + resolved Decisions (reservation authority; member economics). ONE combined ledger owned by the supervisor - reservations: { [sprintId]: { members, issueRoots, childPid, reservedAt } } - claiming both axes in exact lockstep (same launch event claims both, same terminal event releases both; one atomic write, one restart-reconciliation path). Member axis: POST /api/sprints atomically reserves the full member set (union of members + every roleMap value incl. orchestrator) all-or-nothing; overlap returns a conflict naming the other sprint. Issue-scope axis: identity key = root issue id(s) launched with; overlap detection RECOMPUTES the live-expanded subtree (reusing bdListScoped / bd list --parent, not reinvented) for every active sprint at launch-attempt time and intersects with the new request live-expanded scope - never a frozen launch-time snapshot (planners/reviewers grow the subtree mid-run). Any nonzero intersection rejects the ENTIRE launch, naming the conflicting sprint and overlapping bead ids (no partial-launch carve-out - that would require threading an exclude-set through the runner core loop; deferred). Ledger persisted to disk; on supervisor restart, PID-probe reconciliation releases both axes of dead-child reservations and marks the sprint aborted-by-restart. Manual force-release endpoint for wedged states. Known holes surfaced not hidden: (a) service-local ledger is bypassable by a manual bin/cli.mjs run - CONFIRMED acceptable for v1, server-side enforcement is the Phase 3 feature; (b) blocks-edges crossing two disjoint claimed scopes are not detected; (c) pre-Phase-2 the overlap check is best-effort against the service-local synced view - surface a scope-freshness (last synced N minutes ago) indicator. Confirmed member economics: whole-sprint member-per-role reservation even while idle; no role-level hand-off release in v1.
acceptance_criteria: Launching a sprint whose members or live-expanded issue scope overlap any active sprint returns a 409-style rejection naming the conflicting sprint id and the specific overlapping members/bead ids; both axes claim and release atomically on launch and on every terminal path (success, fail, abort, crash-reconciled); ledger survives supervisor restart and PID reconciliation releases dead-child reservations; force-release endpoint works; overlap check demonstrably uses live subtree recomputation (test: a child bead created after launch under a claimed root is still detected); scope-freshness indicator exposed via API; intra-sprint memberLocks behavior unchanged (orthogonal, both stay).
close_reason: Verified via 2026-07-20 real-bd integration run (node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs, 0/74 failures, exitCode=0). Feature's [test] task's dedicated file(s) passed.

title: [Phase 1] Supervisor service: detached child-per-sprint, PID-liveness watchdog, HTTP API
description: Plan Part 2.1 (process model B - recommended and confirmed) + resolved Decision (service restart vs in-flight sprints). A small always-on supervisor process (fleet-se serve) owns the reservation ledger and an HTTP API, and spawns the existing bin/cli.mjs per sprint via spawn({detached: true, stdio: ignore}) with a per-sprint --viewer-port - true independently-surviving orphans; a crashed sprint cannot take down siblings or the service. Status detection per the confirmed design: same-instance exit events are authoritative, but supervisor RESTART is the severance point, so a dedicated liveness watchdog on a short interval PID-probes every ledger-listed sprint and combines with HTTP reachability into exactly four statuses: running-healthy (PID alive, HTTP answering), running-unresponsive (PID alive, HTTP not answering - operator attention, not auto-declared crash), crashed (PID gone, no terminal state persisted), finished (PID gone, terminal state in history). fork()/IPC explicitly rejected. Confirmed: detach-and-PID-readopt on restart is the target; sprints need NOT survive machine restart; journal/replay productization NOT required. HTTP surface: GET /api/members (list_members + reservation overlay), GET /api/backlog, POST /api/sprints (per-request goal - goal is already a per-invocation flag, just forwarded), GET /api/sprints and /api/sprints/:id (live proxied from child /state, else history), POST /api/sprints/:id/stop (proxies child /stop), POST /api/shutdown; service stops only via explicit shutdown/signal.
acceptance_criteria: Supervisor runs indefinitely and only exits on explicit shutdown; sprints launch as detached children of bin/cli.mjs with unique viewer ports; killing the supervisor leaves children running and a restarted supervisor re-adopts them by PID from the persisted ledger; the four statuses are distinguishable in the API and each is exercised by a test (healthy, hung child, killed child, completed child); all listed endpoints implemented with request validation reusing exported validateIssueId/validateBranchName/resolveRoleMap helpers; POST /api/sprints forwards per-request goal into child argv.
close_reason: Verified via 2026-07-20 real-bd integration run (node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs, 0/74 failures, exitCode=0). Feature's [test] task's dedicated file(s) passed.

title: [Phase 0] Continuous per-activity sprint-state persistence (running/ -> old_sprints/)
description: Plan Part 2.3 (Continuous, per-activity persistence + Process-free history file layout) and Part 4 Phase 0. Today the viewer persists sprint state only on end/SIGINT/SIGTERM to sprint-logs/sprint_<HHMMSS>.json - a hard crash (SIGKILL, OOM) loses everything, and HHMMSS keys collide across days. Change: persist on EVERY activity-end, phase, and state event (the same events already driving the SSE broadcast). One file per sprint keyed by sprint id, overwritten in place: live sprint writes running/<sprintId>.json; on completion the file moves to old_sprints/<sprintId>.json, so is-this-sprint-live is a directory-membership check, not a stale field. State file enriched with sprint id, launch args, verdict, PR URL, timestamps, terminal reason. I/O cost mitigated with a debounced writer (coalesce bursts within 200-500ms, always flush before process exit). sprint-logs/ stays exactly as-is (child crash-safety net); old_sprints/ lives under the service data directory, not the repo checkout.
acceptance_criteria: State file is written on every activity/phase/state event via a debounced (200-500ms) writer with flush-on-exit; file is keyed by sprint id and contains args, verdict, PR URL, timestamps, terminal reason; live vs finished is determined by running/ vs old_sprints/ directory membership; a simulated hard-kill mid-sprint loses at most one debounce window of progress (test); existing sprint-logs/ behavior untouched.
close_reason: Verified via 2026-07-20 real-bd integration run (node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs, 0/74 failures, exitCode=0). Feature's [test] task's dedicated file(s) passed.

title: [Phase 0] PR-on-abort: publish Auto-sprint [ABORTED] PR when the branch has commits
description: Plan Part 1.4 + Part 4 Phase 0 + resolved Decision (aborted sprint with zero commits). Today a PR is raised on both PASS and FAIL final verdicts, but sprints that end by THROWING (StalledSprintError, SprintPlanRejectedError, ReviewerContractViolationError, budget-exceeded, pre-sprint validation errors) propagate to the cli.mjs catch block: grace window, exit 1, no branch push, no PR. Fix: catch typed sprint-abort errors in runner.js/cli.mjs and, iff the branch has commits beyond base, push and raise a PR titled Auto-sprint [ABORTED]: <branch> with the failure evidence in the body. Confirmed policy: a zero-commit abort raises NO PR (empty-diff PR is noise) but a history record is always kept either way.
acceptance_criteria: Each typed abort error path, when the sprint branch has >=1 commit beyond base, pushes the branch and creates an idempotent Auto-sprint [ABORTED] PR whose body contains the error evidence; a zero-commit abort creates no PR but still writes a terminal history record; PASS/FAIL finalization behavior unchanged; unit tests cover commits-exist and zero-commit abort paths plus PR idempotency (already-exists swallowed).

title: Fleet-sprint as a service: always-on multi-sprint supervisor
description:
Umbrella epic for the fleet-sprint-as-a-service redesign of packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint: turn the single-shot run-to-completion CLI sprint into an always-on supervisor service running N concurrent sprint child processes with member+issue-scope reservation, a sprint-stack dashboard, and orchestrator-bracketed git+dolt sync.

DESIGN PLAN (source of truth, consolidated single edition 2026-07-16): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/413dd5a5-68f1-4a46-b10f-992dff241d3f
Structure: Part 1 current-state findings (incl. clean dispatch-safety audit of runner.js, 1.6); Part 2 process model (spawn/detached/PID-liveness supervisor, combined member+issue-scope reservation ledger, sprint-stack dashboard, continuous persistence); Part 3 token-passing sync stance, orchestrator-bracketed sync authorship, Dolt conflict handling (verified PoC C.1-C.5, Path A/B recovery, Tier 0/1/2 conflict-escalation ladder for both Dolt and git); Part 4 phasing (Phase 0-3); Part 5 nine resolved architecture decisions.

BUILD ORDER: features carry a [Phase N] prefix per the plan Part 4. Phase 0 = standalone fixes with independent value; Phase 1 = service-ification (no dolt sync, topology guard untouched); Phase 2 = orchestrator-bracketed git+dolt sync (the risky 40 percent); Phase 3 = hardening (server-side reservation, vendored agent-contract updates, deferred crash-resume/merger-agent). Phases are ordering guidance, not hard blocks deps - only genuine prerequisites are noted in feature descriptions (per this repo GRAPH-SEMANTICS lesson: no artificial blocks edges).

CROSS-REFERENCE: apra-fleet-ire (Fleet installer: portable dolt CLI alongside bd) already exists as a standalone task and is a hard prerequisite/component of the Phase 2 Dolt-sync feature (Path A resolve-in-place runbook is unusable without a provisioned dolt binary). It is referenced from that feature, deliberately NOT re-created or reparented here.

Explicitly deferred by the plan (recorded, not scoped): multi-repo-per-project beads remotes; partial-launch scope carve-out; role-level reservation; machine-restart sprint resume; merger-agent/parallel doer streaks.
acceptance_criteria: All child feature beads closed or explicitly deferred with rationale; the service is the single supported user-facing entry point (Decision: CLI fate); Phases 0-1 shipped before Phase 2 sync work lands so new failure modes surface inside a service that can contain, display and record them (plan Part 4).

title: [feature] Inject role-prefixed bd memories (doer-memory-*, reviewer-memory-*, ...) into fleet-sprint dispatches -- operator-extensible prompting without a heavyweight contract-file PR
description:
## Problem

There is currently no way for a repo operator to superimpose extra prose
guidance onto a dispatched role (doer, reviewer, streak-assignment,
integ-test-runner, etc.) without editing that role's prompt contract file
directly (`packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/agents/<role>.md`) -- apra-pm is
no longer a submodule, it is committed directly in this repo, so the path is
now edit-the-file, commit, PR, merge, then rebuild `dist/agents/*.md` before
the change takes effect (no separate upstream repo or submodule-pointer
bump). This is the correct, heavyweight path for stable, designed contract
changes -- but it is far too
slow for a quick, project-specific operator note (e.g. "on this machine,
always double-quote `bd list --status=` filters" or "never busy-wait poll a
backgrounded test command for more than 60s without emitting a status
line") that should take effect on the very next dispatch.

This session hit multiple real examples of exactly this kind of gotcha
(the PowerShell comma-array-mangling bug, the member-is-one-folder
parallel-dispatch constraint, the busy-wait/inactivity-timeout interaction)
-- each would have been directly prevented if a prior sprint's learning had
been immediately available to the next dispatch, with no rebuild cycle.

## Proposed mechanism

Reuse `bd`'s existing memory feature (`bd remember` / `bd memories`,
already used for cross-session operator knowledge -- see `bd prime`'s
"Persistent Memories" block) as the storage and retrieval layer, with a
role-prefixed key convention:

- `bd remember --key doer-memory-<slug> "..."`
- `bd remember --key reviewer-memory-<slug> "..."`
- `bd remember --key planner-memory-<slug> "..."`
- (one prefix per dispatched role/agentType that `runner.js` supports --
  enumerate all: planner, plan-reviewer, doer, reviewer, integ-test-runner,
  deployer, harvester)

Scope: **global**, stored in the project's own beads DB (not
sprint-specific, not bead/item-specific -- confirmed explicitly out of
scope by the repo owner). A memory written today is visible to every
future sprint run against this repo, indefinitely, until updated/removed.

## Integration point

In `packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js`, at each dispatch call
site (the same ones identified for the `max_total_s` ceiling work: Doer,
Reviewer x2, Integ-Test-Runner, plus Planner, Plan-Reviewer, Deployer,
Harvester for completeness), before building the dispatch prompt:

1. Run `bd memories <role>-memory --json` (e.g. `bd memories doer-memory
   --json`) to fetch any matching operator memories for that role.
2. If any are returned, append them to the prompt under a clearly-labeled,
   distinct section (e.g. `## Project-specific operator notes`) so the
   model understands this is supplementary, operator-authored guidance --
   not part of the base agent contract, and not to be confused with
   untrusted agent-output content (no `wrapUntrustedBlock` fencing needed;
   this is operator-authored, trusted content, same trust level as the
   rest of the dispatch prompt).
3. If no memories match, the section is omitted entirely -- no empty
   headers, no behavior change from today for a project that hasn't
   adopted this convention yet.

## Documentation requirement (explicit part of this bead's scope)

This is as important as the code: document the existence of this
extensibility point clearly, so operators actually discover and use it
instead of reaching for the heavyweight contract-file-edit path out of habit.
At minimum:

- Add a section to `packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/docs/README.md`
  (the existing "how to run auto-sprint correctly" doc) explaining the
  `<role>-memory-<slug>` convention, with a concrete example
  (`bd remember --key doer-memory-powershell-quoting "..."`), and stating
  explicitly that this is global/repo-wide, takes effect on the next
  dispatch with no rebuild, and is the preferred path for
  operational/empirical gotchas vs. the direct-edit path for stable
  contract design changes.
- Note the enumerated list of valid role prefixes (must match `runner.js`'s
  actual `agentType` values exactly, or a typo'd key silently never
  matches anything -- consider whether `runner.js` should also emit a
  one-line log/warning listing which memory keys (if any) were actually
  applied to a given dispatch, purely for operator visibility/debugging,
  not enforcement).

## Acceptance criteria

- A `bd remember --key doer-memory-<slug> "..."` memory is visibly
  included in the next Doer dispatch's prompt (verifiable via the sprint
  log's own dispatch-prompt narration, or a direct unit test against the
  prompt-building function).
- No matching memories -> no section appended, no error, no change from
  current behavior.
- All roles enumerated above are covered, not just doer/reviewer.
- `packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/docs/README.md` documents the
  convention with a working example.
- Existing `advanced-mock-runner-test.mjs`/split successor tests still
  pass unmodified (this is additive prompt content, not a change to
  dispatch control flow) -- add new test coverage for the injection
  itself rather than relying on existing tests to incidentally catch it.

## Explicitly out of scope for this bead

- Sprint-specific or bead/item-specific memory scoping (e.g.
  `doer-memory-<bead-id>-<slug>`) -- confirmed not needed right now.
- Any UI/dashboard surface for authoring memories -- `bd remember` on the
  CLI is sufficient.
- Automatic memory *authoring* by the harvester or reviewer roles (a
  separate, related idea discussed the same session -- track as its own
  follow-up bead if pursued, do not conflate with this one, which is only
  about the *retrieval/injection* mechanism for memories a human already
  wrote).
notes: TRIAGE: Confirmed not implemented -- no 'bd memories', role-memory-prefix, or role-prefixed injection logic anywhere in fleet-sprint/runner.js or apra-pm agents/*.md. Spec is unusually complete for an open feature (exact bd remember key convention, exact integration point -- before each of the 8 enumerated dispatch prompt builds, exact doc target packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/docs/README.md, explicit out-of-scope list). P1, and complementary-not-blocking relationship to apra-fleet-tnp (this batch) is correctly self-documented in its own description. No design gaps found; ready to implement as specified.

title: [bug] LocalStrategy.execCommand decodes stdout/stderr per-chunk (data.toString()), corrupting multi-byte UTF-8 split across chunk boundaries (U+FFFD)
description:
ALREADY FIXED -- flagged for review 2026-07-16. Independently verified against current src/services/strategy.ts.

Original claim: LocalStrategy.execCommand decodes stdout (line 141) and stderr (line 161) per-chunk via `data.toString()`, with no persisted multi-byte decode state, corrupting UTF-8 sequences split across chunk boundaries.

Current state (verified 2026-07-16): commit 6478f67 ("fix(strategy): decode stdout/stderr with StringDecoder, not per-chunk toString()") -- commit message says "Fixes apra-fleet-grq" -- already fixes exactly this, and is present on current HEAD.
- Line 5: `import { StringDecoder } from 'node:string_decoder';`
- Lines 145-146: `stdoutDecoder`/`stderrDecoder` instantiated as `new StringDecoder('utf8')`.
- Line 150: stdout uses `stdoutDecoder.write(data)`, not `.toString()`.
- Line 178: stderr uses `stderrDecoder.write(data)`, not `.toString()`.
- Lines 191-192: `stdoutDecoder.end()` / `stderrDecoder.end()` flush any trailing partial multi-byte tail on process close.
- MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES spill path: stdout spill writes the already-decoded `chunk` string; stderr spill writes the raw `data` Buffer directly (byte-oriented) -- both consistent with the bead's own acceptance note that the spill path "can stay byte-oriented if only ever read back as raw bytes".
- A regression test exists: tests/strategy-utf8-chunk-boundary.test.ts, added by 6478f67, forces a real child process to split a 4-byte UTF-8 character across two writes.

Note: the bead's "Scope note" claiming the last commit touching this file was hub-spoke migration (e959d7b) is now STALE -- 6478f67 (this exact fix) is the most recent commit on the file, landed after e959d7b.

RECOMMEND: close this bead as already-fixed rather than feeding it into the sprint. If it should be re-opened, provide fresh evidence (e.g. a live repro AFTER 6478f67) since the current code and its accompanying test both look correct.
close_reason: Already fixed by commit 6478f67 -- verified 2026-07-16 against current src/services/strategy.ts, LocalStrategy.execCommand no longer decodes stdout/stderr per-chunk.

title: [bug] execute_prompt timeouts bypass retry entirely; runner.js conflates dispatch vs schema errors; schema-repair must resume session instead of re-sending full context (wastes tokens)
description:
TRIAGED 2026-07-16: all three findings verified still present in current source; only line numbers have drifted (unrelated commits added lines above these regions since filing).

Follow-up investigation (originally 2026-07-15) after diagnosing apra-fleet-j6i's Final Review timeout/FAIL. THREE distinct, confirmed findings: two are bugs (server-side retry-bypass, client-side error-type conflation), one is a decided fix (schema-repair should use session resume, not fresh self-contained re-asks -- confirmed by user 2026-07-15: "must use resume, else we are wasting tokens").

1) SERVER-SIDE BUG (execute-prompt.ts) -- CONFIRMED, line unchanged: the outer catch block (now verified at execute-prompt.ts:506-508) still sets structuredContent:{isError:true, reason:'dispatch_failed'} for a genuine command timeout/thrown exception, structurally separate from and unreachable from the two retry mechanisms in the preceding try block (stale-session retry, server/overloaded-error retry) -- both of which only fire on a non-throwing nonzero exit, never on a thrown exception. A genuine timeout throws, so it reaches neither retry path -- single-shot, unconditionally-unretried, for every dispatch site system-wide.

2) CLIENT-SIDE BUG (runner.js) -- CONFIRMED, now 6 combined-catch sites (was cited as "at minimum Final Review's, ~line 2201"; verified 2026-07-16 the same `err instanceof AgentOutputError || err instanceof AgentDispatchError` combined-branch pattern exists at runner.js:1249, 1740, 2161, 2218, 2398 (Final Review, was ~2201), and 2462). packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/workflow/index.mjs still correctly types AgentDispatchError vs AgentOutputError distinctly (confirmed: index.mjs's doc comments and throw sites unchanged in intent), but runner.js's catch blocks still discard that distinction, reporting both as "schema-repair exhausted, treating as FAIL" regardless of which actually occurred.

3) DECIDED FIX -- schema-repair must use session resume, not a fresh self-contained re-ask (packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/workflow/index.mjs) -- CONFIRMED, lines verified: repair loop at index.mjs:720 (`for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= maxRepairs; attempt++)`), `isRepair` computed at :728, still dispatches with a STATIC `resume: opts.resume ?? false` at :761 regardless of isRepair. The "F10" self-contained-re-ask rationale comment is still present (now ~:759-761 region). maxRepairs itself computed at :625 (`opts.schemaRetries ?? 2`).

SUGGESTED FIX (full scope, unchanged from original investigation): (1) execute-prompt.ts's outer catch (dispatch exception path) should have its own bounded retry (at minimum one retry with a fresh session, mirroring the existing stale-session-retry pattern) rather than being an unconditional single-shot failure. (2) runner.js's 6 combined-catch sites should branch on the error TYPE (AgentDispatchError vs AgentOutputError) and handle each distinctly -- an AgentDispatchError should trigger a dispatch-retry or a clearly-labeled "infrastructure failure, not a quality failure" outcome, never be conflated with schema-repair exhaustion. (3) switch index.mjs's schema-repair loop to force resume:true when isRepair===true and shrink buildRepairPrompt() to a lean reminder-only message (validation errors + "please respond again with corrected JSON only" -- not re-embedding the full original prompt/invalid output) -- verify session continuity holds specifically across repair rounds before shipping.
close_reason: All 4 sub-tasks (02s.1-02s.4) implemented and tested: (1) execute-prompt.ts outer catch now retries once on a genuine dispatch exception; (2) runner.js's 6 combined-catch sites now distinguish AgentDispatchError vs AgentOutputError in logging; (3) schema-repair re-asks force resume:true and use a lean reminder prompt, per user's 2026-07-15 decision. Verified via node --check, npx tsc --noEmit, and scoped test runs (no full-suite run per 'run sparingly' instruction).

title: Pull-sync: fetch workspace/member/project config from fleet-dashboard into local JSON cache
description:
The core 'reliable storage + easy bootstrap' value-add the product owner asked for. When apra-fleet.exe is SaaS-connected, fetch the caller's workspace(s), and within a selected workspace its members/projects, from fleet-dashboard's real API (GET /v1/workspaces, GET /v1/ws/:id/members, GET /v1/ws/:id/projects per fleet-dashboard/docs/api-contract.md), and cache the result as local JSON extending src/services/registry.ts's existing pattern -- explicitly NOT a local relational database, per the product-owner directive.

Depends on apra-fleet-48p (design) for: what gets cached and where, sync trigger (automatic vs explicit), and conflict/staleness handling.
acceptance_criteria: A SaaS-connected apra-fleet.exe instance can pull its workspace's member/project list from fleet-dashboard and have it reflected in local commands (e.g. list_members) without requiring any local Postgres/SQL. Standalone (non-SaaS) operation is provably unaffected -- existing local-only tests pass unmodified. Tests use fleet-dashboard's real documented response shapes, not hub-service's retiring shapes.
notes: Cross-repo prerequisite (per AGREED docs/bootstrap-sync-design-proposal.md): do not start until fleet-dashboard builds GET /v1/ws/:id/bootstrap (filed as fleet-dashboard-1il in their tracker -- does not exist yet). Pull-sync fetches from this endpoint, not from session-only list routes.
close_reason: Implemented src/services/cloud-sync.ts: fetches fleet-dashboard's GET /v1/ws/:id/bootstrap (fleet-dashboard-1il, now shipped) with the stored member JWT, caches to sibling cloud-cache.json (registry.json untouched -- different concept). On-demand sync (no polling daemon), fail-open on network/5xx/429 to last-synced cache, distinct credential-expired state on 401 (never silently falls back). Wired into list_members: [cloud] section (compact) / cloud field (json), invisible in standalone mode. 9 new/updated tests, full suite 2146/2146 passing, tsc clean. Commit fdaae75 on feat/pull-sync-fleet-dashboard.

description:

title: Design: bootstrap/sync contract, sync policy, and enrollment auth flow against fleet-dashboard
description:
Precedes all implementation work in this epic. Design questions that need explicit answers before code is written, since guessing wrong here means redoing downstream work:

1. Sync direction and conflict resolution: is it pull-only (cloud is authoritative, local registry.json is a read-through cache), push-only (local registrations get mirrored up, cloud never overwrites local), or bidirectional reconcile (and if so, what wins on conflict -- last-write-wins by timestamp, cloud-always-wins, or explicit user prompt)?
2. Sync trigger: automatic the moment a device is SaaS-connected (every registry read/write also touches the network), or an explicit opt-in action per workspace/member/project (e.g. 'apra-fleet sync' command, or only new registrations get pushed, existing local-only agents stay local-only until explicitly migrated)?
3. Enrollment/auth: today's 'apra-fleet join <token>' (src/cli/join.ts) exchanges a token for a machine JWT against apra-fleet-reorg's OWN hub-service (POST /join/exchange). Under the new architecture this must point at fleet-dashboard's real API instead. fleet-dashboard's docs/api-contract.md does not currently document an enrollment-token flow at all (see docs/api-contract-reconciliation.md item 22, recommended CONTRACT ADAPTS to add one) -- this is a cross-repo dependency, not something apra-fleet-reorg can finish alone. Design what apra-fleet-reorg's client-side shape should be given the contract's EXISTING member-registration endpoint (POST /v1/ws/:id/members issues a JWT once) as a fallback if the enrollment-token section never lands, vs. waiting for it.
4. What exactly gets cached locally as JSON, and where: extend src/services/registry.ts's existing registry.json shape, or a new sibling file (e.g. cloud-workspace-cache.json)? Must not introduce a local relational DB per the product-owner directive.
5. Failure/offline behavior: if fleet-dashboard is unreachable, does apra-fleet.exe fail closed (block local operations pending sync) or fail open (operate on stale local cache, retry sync later)? Given 'today's standalone mode must keep working,' fail-open matching standalone behavior is the likely answer, but state it explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: A short design doc (docs/) answering all 5 questions above, reviewed before any of this epic's other children start implementation. Explicitly confirms zero impact on standalone (no-cloud) operation as a design constraint, not just an aspiration.
close_reason: AGREED via docs/cross-repo-design-protocol.md's autonomous negotiation loop -- 2 rounds, both spawned as fresh agents scoped to fleet-dashboard's real code, zero human relay needed since both repos are local to this machine. Round 1 found the original plan was unimplementable (member JWTs have zero read access in fleet-dashboard's real API) plus a real security bug in fleet-dashboard's own code (filed as fleet-dashboard-anw). Round 2 confirmed the revised resolution (dedicated GET /v1/ws/:id/bootstrap endpoint; member registration stays human-session-only, permanently) with zero open objections. Full record: docs/bootstrap-sync-design-proposal.md (Status: AGREED) and fleet-dashboard's docs/bootstrap-sync-design-response.md (both rounds).

title: [EPIC] SaaS bootstrap/sync integration (apra-fleet.exe <-> fleet-dashboard) + hub-service retirement
description:
Follow-on to the hub-spoke migration (apra-fleet-us9, closed) and the API contract reconciliation (docs/api-contract-reconciliation.md). Product-owner directive (2026-07-05): fleet-dashboard is the ONLY true persistence layer for workspace/project/member/secret configuration; apra-fleet.exe must never reimplement that persistence, even for a self-hosted story. Cross-checked against fleet-dashboard's own docs/architecture.md, which confirms this as their real, tested architecture (DynamoDB-backed, OAuth+session-cookie auth already built, iron-wall workspace isolation already tested).

User's explicit scoping decision (2026-07-05), reconciling this with today's working product: (1) today's standalone apra-fleet.exe (local registry.json, LocalStrategy, RemoteStrategy/SSH) continues to work exactly as-is, zero regression, SSH is NOT deprecated or gated behind anything -- it remains a permanent first-class execution transport, not a migration target. (2) The cloud/SaaS value-add is specifically: (a) easy bootstrap of workspaces/members/projects via a web UI instead of local-only CLI setup, and (b) reliable, durable storage of that configuration off fragile developer devices -- NOT replacing SSH-based execution with a relay. (3) src/hub-service/ (the Postgres-backed hub built this session) is retired to REFERENCE-ONLY status -- valuable as a working proof of the wire-protocol/security-isolation semantics, but fleet-dashboard is the real production tier-3 implementation going forward; hub-service is not deployed or extended further. (4) Relay/NAT-traversal command execution (the envelope/SSE system) is explicitly DEFERRED -- fleet-dashboard's own bidirectional WebSocket relay is 'designed, not yet built' per their architecture.md, so no urgent need to build or maintain a competing apra-fleet-reorg-side relay right now. Focus is the bootstrap/sync integration first.
acceptance_criteria: apra-fleet.exe gains an opt-in SaaS-connected mode that can bootstrap workspace/member/project config from fleet-dashboard and keep local registry.json durably synced, while standalone (no-cloud) operation is provably unchanged (existing test suite for local/SSH paths continues to pass with zero modification). src/hub-service/ is clearly marked reference-only in its own docs and the project's top-level docs, with no further production feature work landing there.

title: register_member must verify apra-fleet is installed/running on the remote member, auto-install from GitHub releases if not
description:
register_member should check whether apra-fleet is actually installed and running on the target remote member. If it is not, it should attempt to install it automatically by downloading the appropriate SEA binary from GitHub releases (matching the member's OS/arch), rather than silently leaving the member without it.

This is needed so remote members can use KB (kb_capture/kb_query/etc.) and code-intelligence (code_graph/code_impact/code_query/etc.) features, which depend on apra-fleet being present and running on that member -- today a remote member can be registered and dispatched to without apra-fleet ever being installed there, silently losing access to these features.

Blocks apra-fleet-93pt: tool-granular gating of the 'apra-fleet' MCP server (instead of disabling it wholesale) only has anything to gate if apra-fleet is actually installed and running on the member in the first place.

Must honour the target member's OS: apra-fleet installers/release assets differ per platform (Windows/macOS/Linux, and arch within each) -- never assume the orchestrator's own OS/arch when picking which release asset to download, resolve it from the member's own registered OS (same convention as getAgentOS/getOsCommands elsewhere in this codebase).

Must also keep the remote member's apra-fleet version in sync with the orchestrator's own version -- not just a one-time install-if-missing check, but an ongoing check (e.g. at register_member/update_member, or periodically) that upgrades a remote member running an older apra-fleet version to match the orchestrator, so version drift between the hub and its members does not silently break protocol/API compatibility. Discoverability: e.g. fleet_status should be able to surface which members are running a version older than the orchestrator's own, so drift is visible even before an upgrade attempt runs.
acceptance_criteria:
1. register_member (or a step it triggers) detects whether apra-fleet is installed and its MCP server is running on the target remote member.
2. If not installed, it downloads the correct GitHub release asset for the member's OWN registered OS/arch (never the orchestrator's) and installs it, then verifies it started successfully.
3. If not running but installed, it starts it (consistent with existing start/run conventions elsewhere in the codebase).
4. A remote member registered without apra-fleet pre-installed ends up with working KB/code-intelligence tool access after registration, verified by a test.
5. A remote member running an older apra-fleet version than the orchestrator gets upgraded to match, verified by a test (install-if-missing and version-sync are both covered, not just the missing case).
6. fleet_status surfaces which members are running a version older than the orchestrator's own, so drift is visible independent of whether an auto-upgrade has run.
7. Failure to install/start/upgrade is surfaced clearly (non-fatal to registration itself, but the member's KB/code-intel limitation is reported), not silently swallowed.

title: fleet-sprint: auto-resume past LLM usage exhaustion with a slow probe loop, distinct from needs-relogin
description:
When a dispatch fails because the member's LLM usage/quota window is exhausted (subscription plan window or rate limit -- distinct from an auth/login failure), fleet-sprint should not just surface the failure and stop. It should:

1. Recognize the "usage exhausted" error class specifically (as opposed to auth/login failure, which is a different remediation path already handled by the existing onLlmAuthFailure self-heal in runner.js).
2. Where the provider/CLI exposes a reset time for the usage window, use it to schedule the next check. Otherwise, fall back to a slow polling loop (e.g. every 15 min) that sends a minimal/cheap "hello" prompt to test whether usage has recovered.
3. Keep retrying in this slow loop until the cheap prompt succeeds, then resume normal dispatch -- this should be a permanent, reusable utility any future fleet-sprint (or other workflow) can call, not a one-off patch.
4. Separately detect the "needs re-login" case (the member's session/OAuth token is actually invalid, not just rate-limited) -- this cannot self-heal via polling and needs a human action.
5. Surface BOTH conditions (usage-exhausted-waiting vs needs-relogin) as a banner at the top of the workflow/supervisor viewer, so a human watching the dashboard immediately sees which of the two is blocking progress, without having to dig through logs.

Originating discussion (paraphrased): the point about continuing beyond token/usage exhaustion is simple to implement in fleet-sprint -- recognize the error, either compute when prompts will work again or just retry a cheap test prompt periodically, and since this is a workflow it's straightforward to add as a permanent utility for any future workflow implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A dispatch failure classified as usage-exhausted (not auth/login) triggers a slow polling loop (provider-reported reset time if available, else a fixed interval e.g. 15 min) that sends a minimal test prompt, and resumes normal dispatch automatically once it succeeds -- with a test proving this end-to-end on a mocked exhausted-then-recovered provider response.
2. Usage-exhausted is classified distinctly from needs-relogin (auth failure) -- a test proves the classifier does not conflate the two error shapes.
3. The needs-relogin case does NOT enter the slow-retry loop -- it surfaces immediately as requiring human action, consistent with the existing onLlmAuthFailure self-heal path.
4. The workflow/supervisor viewer shows a banner at the top of the page when either condition is active, distinguishing "waiting for usage to reset" from "needs re-login," backed by a test asserting the banner renders for each state and clears once resolved.
5. The polling utility is implemented as a reusable function (not embedded one-off logic) so a future workflow can invoke it without re-implementing the same loop.

description:

## Context
Rationale from the user: Gemini is replaced by AGY and there is no need to maintain and keep Gemini alive. Surfaced during the PR #422 review (opencode/agy unattended-mode fix), where Gemini was noted as having the same unhandled-auto gap as opencode/agy did before that fix -- rather than patch it, remove Gemini entirely.

Gemini provider support is entirely removed AND zero references to the GEMINI PROVIDER remain anywhere in the repo -- including historical/archival material (docs/stabilization-log.md-style writeups, CHANGELOG entries, RECOVERY.md-style incident docs, old design docs) as well as current-facing files.

CRITICAL, READ FIRST: src/providers/agy.ts is NOT a Gemini-adjacent file to clean up -- it is AGY's (Antigravity's) own provider, and it legitimately contains the literal substring "gemini" throughout: its OS-level config/credential paths (~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/..., ~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json, ~/.gemini/google_accounts.json), its underlying model ids (gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-3.5-flash-lite), and user-facing tier labels ("Gemini 3.5 Flash (Medium)"). This is because Antigravity is built on Google's Gemini stack and inherits its config namespace -- NOT because AGY reuses code from src/providers/gemini.ts. These strings in agy.ts (and any AGY docs/tests describing AGY's own .gemini paths or model ids) must NOT be touched. title: Azure DevOps create-pull-request builder
description:
PR creation is deliberately unimplemented for Azure DevOps (vcs-providers/azure-devops.mjs: builders: null). provision_vcs_auth also cannot derive owner/repo from an Azure DevOps remote URL shape (https://dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>/_git/<repo>) and fails outright rather than degrading cleanly.

title: [impl] Add the permissions-composer role contract and its fixed cheap model tier
description:

Contract content: tools limited to Read and the fleet compose_permissions tool - it cannot perform deploy or test work and cannot hand-edit settings files. Input: the calling phase name and its member/project folder. Job: read that phase's runbook (deploy.md, integ-test-playbook.md or regression-test-playbook.md) Permissions section, extract the exact Bash prefixes it declares, and call compose_permissions with grant set to exactly those prefixes plus project_folder, grant_reason and role set to the calling phase's role. It must not request anything beyond what the runbook names, must not attempt to route around a NEVER_AUTO_GRANT rejection, and must report such a rejection as a terminal failure. It runs orchestrator-side only, never as a member-dispatched role.

Lane note (for reviewers): this task is the HEAD of streak u1qw-heal, which is streakOrder-banded to run AFTER lane ivxi-bounds. ivxi-bounds occupies orders 3-5 (max open order 5); u1qw-heal occupies 11-13 (min open order 11). Because lanes sort across each other by minimum streakOrder, min(u1qw-heal)=11 > max(ivxi-bounds)=5 carries the ordering purely as lane sequencing - there is NO blocks edge between open members of the two lanes, and none must be re-added (the previously present apra-fleet-ivxi.1.5 -> apra-fleet-u1qw.2.1 edge was removed for exactly this reason). The one remaining incoming dependency, apra-fleet-u1qw.1.2, is already CLOSED and so is not an open cross-lane edge. The ordering is in any case an ordering of convenience, not a compile-time coupling: this task only adds a new markdown contract file and one FIXED_ROLE_TIER line, and touches no code that ivxi-bounds edits.

Lane membership here is forced, not chosen - this task and apra-fleet-u1qw.2.2 both edit runner.js (FIXED_ROLE_TIER at line 104 vs the dispatch sites near 7974/8164), a mutex resource that must not be split across streaks.

description:

- permissions-composer reads the calling phase's runbook Permissions section and requests exactly the prefixes named there - no more, no less; it must not widen to whatever the role bounds would allow.
- Grants inside the calling role's bounds land silently; grants outside bounds still unblock the phase but are ledger-flagged outOfBounds (depends on apra-fleet-ivxi).
- A NEVER_AUTO_GRANT rejection is a real terminal failure surfaced honestly - no retry loop, no bypass.
