description:
Deliverable: compose_permissions gains a per-role bounds concept so a grant that is outside the calling role's expected scope is recorded distinctly in the permissions.json ledger, while behavior for in-bounds and role-less grants is unchanged.

Users: the orchestrator (fleet-sprint runner) and the permissions-composer role (apra-fleet-u1qw), which relies on this bounds check for its safety property.

Acceptance criteria (from apra-fleet-ivxi):
- Grant matching the calling role's bounds profile lands in the ledger exactly as today (no outOfBounds field).
- Grant outside the role's bounds is still granted but the ledger entry carries outOfBounds true and requestedByRole.
- Grant with no role specified behaves exactly as today (fully backward compatible).
- NEVER_AUTO_GRANT (sudo, su, env, printenv, nc, nmap) still hard-rejects regardless of bounds; bounds never loosen the denylist.
- Old permissions.json ledgers (entries without outOfBounds) still load without error.
- skills/fleet/permissions.md documents the bounds file format and the outOfBounds flag.
- Unit tests cover in-bounds, out-of-bounds, no-role, and NEVER_AUTO_GRANT-under-permissive-bounds.

Security invariants (non-negotiable, per bead notes): a member must never be able to escalate its own permissions (bounds files must not be member-readable/editable levers); the orchestrator grants strictly on a need basis from the blocked operation's runbook, never broad standing grants; user-set absolute restrictions (NEVER_AUTO_GRANT) can never be overridden from below.
close_reason: integ-test-runner: verified against deployed build. Ran 'npx vitest run tests/compose-permissions-bounds-matrix.test.ts' -- 5/5 passed (in-bounds, out-of-bounds, no-role, NEVER_AUTO_GRANT-under-permissive-bounds, old-shape ledger replay). Also confirmed skills/fleet/permissions.md documents the bounds file format and outOfBounds flag (lines 72-114). All acceptance criteria hold.

title: Stage 1: PR-per-repo publication with sprint topic ID, sibling cross-links, base-SHA lockfile and prescribed merge order
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained).
A fleet-sprint ends by pushing one branch and opening exactly ONE pull request: the push runs as a
command on the orchestrator member's checkout and the PR is created via VCSModule.capabilities()
(packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:9204-9283, PR creation at 9267-9283).

A multi-repo sprint must instead open ONE PR PER REPO -- this is what every multi-repo AI harness does
(Cursor's cloud agents advertise "one prompt can produce three pull requests in three repos"). True
atomic cross-repo merge does not exist on GitHub (merge queues are per-repo), so the honest offer is
ORDERED, coordinated merges -- and that is exactly the gap competitors still have: Cursor users
explicitly complain there is no merge ordering across the PRs it opens.

So each PR must carry: a generated SPRINT TOPIC ID shared by all sibling PRs (Gerrit topic semantics;
Gerrit's documented failure mode is topic-name COLLISIONS, so the ID must be generated and namespaced,
never free text), cross-links to every sibling PR, the base-SHA lockfile (what each repo was built
against), the prescribed merge order derived from the manifest dependency graph (dependencies first),
and the joint integration verdict.

PR creation itself needs no checkout -- it is already a REST call built orchestrator-side -- so with
per-repo origin URLs from the manifest the orchestrator still holds zero code checkouts.
design:
1) Generate the sprint topic ID once at sprint start: namespaced and collision-proof, e.g.
   "fs-<workspaceName>-<sprintId-or-short-uuid>". Never derive it from free-text user input. Store it in
   run state and reuse it for every PR.
2) Replace the single publish path (runner.js:9204-9283) with a loop over manifest.repos. For each
   repoId: verify the remote branch tip (the doer-side push bead guarantees the tip is already on
   origin; if not, dispatch a push on that repo's doer member -- never from the orchestrator), then open
   a PR via the existing VCSModule.capabilities() REST path using that repo's origin from the manifest,
   with head = the shared sprint branch name and base = manifest.repos[repoId].base.
3) PR title carries the topic ID. PR body must contain, in a stable machine-parseable block:
   - the sprint topic ID;
   - links to every sibling PR (fill these in with a second pass after all PRs exist, since the first
     PR cannot know the later URLs);
   - this repo's base branch AND the base SHA from the sprint lockfile ("built against");
   - the prescribed merge order: the manifest graph's topological order restricted to the repos that
     actually have PRs, dependencies first, rendered as a numbered list with this repo's position
     highlighted;
   - the per-repo verdict and the joint integration verdict;
   - an explicit "merge all or none" operator note, stating that atomic cross-repo merge is not
     available and the order above must be followed.
4) Failure isolation (design doc open question #2 -- CONFIRM THE DECISION WITH THE OPERATOR BEFORE
   IMPLEMENTING, and record the decision in this bead's notes). Recommended default: publish siblings
   with an honest verdict -- if repo X's develop loop failed, X gets no PR and every sibling PR states
   that the joint verdict is FAIL and that X is missing. The alternative is holding all PRs. Whichever
   is chosen must be implemented explicitly, not left implicit.
5) Related open question #6: whether a per-repo PR should be opened as a DRAFT until the joint verdict
   passes. Same rule -- decide with the operator, record the decision, implement it explicitly.
6) Single-repo compatibility: with the one-entry manifest, exactly one PR is opened as today, with the
   extra body block degrading to a single-repo form (topic ID + lockfile, no sibling links, trivial
   merge order).
7) Update packages/apra-fleet-client in the same change if any MCP tool schema shifts (repo convention).
acceptance_criteria:
- A 3-repo sprint opens exactly 3 PRs, one per repoId, each as a DRAFT PR, with head = the shared
  sprint branch name and base = that repo's manifest base -- asserted against a mocked VCS module
  (including the draft flag on every create call).
- The orchestrator opens the PRs with no code checkout of any target repo (test asserts no
  clone/fetch in the orchestrator's working directory during publish).
- All sibling PR titles contain the identical generated topic ID; the ID matches the namespaced
  pattern (e.g. ^fs-[a-z0-9-]+-[a-z0-9]+$) and is not derived from free-text input -- tested.
- Each PR body contains a machine-parseable block with: the topic ID; a link to every OTHER PR in the
  set (verified after the second pass, so the first-created PR also has all links); this repo's base
  branch and the lockfile base SHA; a numbered merge order equal to the manifest graph's topological
  order restricted to repos with PRs, dependencies first; the per-repo verdict; the joint verdict; and
  the "merge all or none" note.
- For graph {backend:[shared], frontend:[shared,backend]}, every PR body's merge order reads
  shared, backend, frontend.
- FAILURE ISOLATION (decided): a sprint where repo X failed still publishes every sibling PR; X has no
  PR; every sibling body states joint verdict FAIL and names X as missing -- covered by a test.
- A single-repo sprint opens exactly one draft PR, with the degraded body block (topic ID + lockfile,
  no sibling links); existing publish tests pass with only the body-block and draft-flag additions.
notes:
OPERATOR DECISIONS (2026-08-15) -- design doc open questions #2 and #6 are now ANSWERED. Implement
these; do not re-open them during implementation.

#2 FAILURE ISOLATION: publish siblings with an honest verdict. If repo X's develop loop failed, X gets
NO PR, every sibling PR still publishes, and every sibling PR body states that the joint verdict is
FAIL and names X as the missing repo. The sprint does NOT hold all PRs.

#6 PR GATE: for the first pass, every per-repo PR is raised as a DRAFT PR. PR creation is not blocked
on the joint verdict -- draft status plus the stated verdict is the gate, and a human promotes the set
out of draft when satisfied. This is consistent with #2: publish, but honestly and non-mergeably.

title: Stage 1: deployer-assembled integration -- per-repo clean builds, artifact transfer, graph-ordered assembly in the deploy work folder
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained). NOTE: this bead SUPERSEDES the design doc's integration proposal. The doc
(docs/multi-repo-fleet-sprint-strategy.md, section 4 "Integration phase") recommended a dedicated
integration member holding a checkout of EVERY repo. The operator rejected that on 2026-08-15:
re-cloning all repositories onto one member is not sustainable -- disk and time cost grow with the
estate, and it buys nothing that artifacts do not already give us. Implement what is written HERE, not
what the doc's section 4 says.

The problem is real even so. In a single-repo sprint, "deploy" and "integ test" act on one repo's
branch. Once a sprint changes N repositories together, the only meaningful test is of the COMBINED
system -- and no member holds it, since each member checks out exactly one repo.

DECIDED DESIGN: THE DEPLOYER IS THE INTEGRATOR.
- Each repo's OWN member performs a CLEAN BUILD of its own project, in its own existing checkout, at
  the sprint branch tip. No new checkouts anywhere.
- The declared build artifacts are transferred to the DEPLOYER member's deployment work folder.
- The deployer assembles the final composed artifact under that work folder, in the manifest dependency
  graph's topological order, then deploys it; integ-test then runs against the deployed composition.
- Clean separation: the deployer holds ARTIFACTS, never source. No member ever gains a second repo's
  checkout. The orchestrator holds nothing. Integration cost scales with artifact size, not repo count.

Consequence to be explicit about: the doc's "workspace review pass on the composite source workspace"
is REMOVED, because no composite source tree exists any more. The joint verdict is instead computed
from the per-repo review verdicts plus the composed deploy result plus the composed integ-test result.
Deeper cross-repo interface review is deferred to Stage 2 contract beads (apra-fleet-74vu.11) rather
than faked by cloning source somewhere.

Per-repo review stays exactly as today (runner.js:5550-5604, each repo's reviewer against its own
diff); per-repo unit tests stay per-repo in Develop/Review; regression test stays informational
(runner.js:4082-4084).
design:
1) Manifest wiring. Consume the deploy/build keys added by apra-fleet-74vu.1:
   deploy: { member, playbook, mode: "composed"|"independent", artifactsDir } and, per repo,
   build: { command, artifacts: [glob, ...] }. If a multi-repo manifest declares no deploy member,
   skip the phase with a prominent warning (do not hard-fail early adopters) and mark the joint verdict
   as NOT_EVALUATED. Single-repo sprints keep today's deploy path unchanged.
2) Per-repo clean build. For each repoId in topoOrder(manifest) (dependencies first: for graph
   {backend:[shared], frontend:[shared,backend]} that is shared, backend, frontend), dispatch the
   repo's declared build.command on THAT repo's own member, in its own checkout, at the sprint branch
   tip. "Clean" means the build starts from a clean tree state and a removed/ignored previous build
   output directory -- define this precisely and make it deterministic; the point of the clean build is
   that the artifact is reproducible from the branch tip alone.
3) Artifact transfer. Collect each repo's declared build.artifacts globs and transfer them to the
   deployer member at <deploy work folder>/<artifactsDir>/<repoId>/, using the fleet file-transport MCP
   tools (send_files / receive_files) rather than any bespoke copy path. Record per-repo artifact
   manifest entries (file list + sizes + a content hash) in run state so the composition is auditable
   and reproducible. Fail the phase, naming the repoId, if a declared artifact glob matches nothing.
4) Assembly + deploy. On the deployer, run the manifest's deploy playbook to assemble the composed
   artifact from <artifactsDir>/* in topological order and deploy it. Honour deploy.mode: "composed" =
   assemble and deploy the whole system (docker compose / helm / equivalent) and point integ-test at
   it; "independent" = deploy each repo's artifact in graph order. Contract gating between independent
   deploys is Stage 2, not this bead.
5) Phase ordering. This runs per cycle after Review, as part of / immediately before Deploy. Today's
   per-cycle Integ Test phase (runner.js:8046-8121) then targets the DEPLOYED COMPOSITION rather than a
   single repo's deploy. Deploy failure still skips integ-test (today's shape, runner.js:8029), applied
   per composition.
6) Failure -> beads. Each build, assembly, deploy or integ-test failure files an [integ] bead stamped
   with the `repo` metadata of the repo the dependency graph blames (the owning repo of the failing
   build/test; when ambiguous, the repo lowest in topological order among those involved). Reuse the
   existing [integ] filing helper. These feed the next cycle exactly like today's integ-test bugs.
7) Joint verdict. Compute it from per-repo review verdicts + composed deploy result + composed
   integ-test result, and store it in run state for the PR publisher (apra-fleet-74vu.10) to embed.
   Do NOT introduce a composite-source review pass.
8) Permissions: the deployer's grants for build-artifact receipt and assembly come from
   apra-fleet-74vu.8. Do not compose ad hoc permissions here, and never let a member request its own
   grants (invariant from apra-fleet-ivxi / apra-fleet-u1qw).
9) Observability: log per repo the build duration and artifact size, and the total composed artifact
   size, so the real cost shape of integration is measurable (this is the metric that justified
   rejecting the clone-everything design).
acceptance_criteria:
- No member and no orchestrator ever obtains a checkout of a repository it did not already hold: a test
  over a 3-repo manifest asserts zero clone/checkout commands were dispatched for the deploy phase.
- Each repo's build runs on that repo's own member, in its own checkout, at the sprint branch tip, and
  the builds are dispatched in topoOrder -- for {backend:[shared], frontend:[shared,backend]} the
  observed order is shared, backend, frontend.
- The build is clean: a test asserts the previous build output directory is removed (or the documented
  clean mechanism runs) before build.command executes.
- Declared artifacts land at <deploy work folder>/<artifactsDir>/<repoId>/ on the deployer, transferred
  via the fleet send_files/receive_files tools (asserted against a mocked transport), and run state
  records the per-repo artifact file list, sizes and content hash.
- A declared artifact glob matching no files fails the phase with an error naming the repoId and the
  glob.
- The deployer assembles and deploys from the artifacts directory only; a test asserts no source tree
  exists under the deploy work folder.
- deploy.mode "composed" deploys the assembled system and integ-test targets it; "independent" deploys
  each repo's artifact in graph order -- both paths tested.
- Deploy failure still skips integ-test (runner.js:8029 behavior), now per composition.
- A failing composed integ-test files an [integ] bead whose repo metadata equals the blamed repoId,
  via the existing filing helper, and that bead appears in the next cycle's scope.
- A joint verdict is stored in run state, derived from per-repo verdicts + composed deploy + composed
  integ-test; no composite-source review pass exists anywhere in the implementation.
- The per-repo reviewer flow (runner.js:5550-5604) is untouched (diff review).
- A multi-repo manifest with no deploy member skips the phase with a warning and a NOT_EVALUATED joint
  verdict -- tested.
- Single-repo sprints keep today's deploy/integ-test behavior; existing cycle tests pass unmodified.
- Per-repo build duration, per-repo artifact size and total composed artifact size are logged.

title: Stage 1: deployer permissions for multi-repo artifact assembly (bounds-deployer, artifact receipt dir, no self-escalation)
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained). This bead was originally scoped to an "integration member" holding a checkout
of every repo. That design was rejected by the operator on 2026-08-15 (see the epic's DECISIONS notes):
the deployer is the integrator, and it receives BUILD ARTIFACTS rather than source. This bead is
rescoped accordingly, and is now considerably smaller -- there is no composite source workspace to
trust, and no union-of-every-stack permission surface.

Fleet permissions are per-work-folder by construction: compose_permissions detects the stack from the
member's work_folder, writes .claude/settings.local.json THERE, keeps a per-project permissions.json
ledger, and Claude workspace trust is seeded strictly to that exact folder -- an untrusted folder
SILENTLY DROPS every composed allow (skills/fleet/permissions.md:5-44, 80-128).

The member-per-repo model composes with this cleanly and that is a large part of why it was chosen:
each repo's members keep grants scoped to their own repo's work folder, ledger and stack profiles, so
adding repositories to a workspace never widens any existing member's permissions. (It is also why the
rejected "one member hops between repo directories" option was rejected: a doer that cd's into a
sibling repo is an unprovisioned, untrusted, unledgered agent there.)

What actually needs permission work in Stage 1 is therefore narrow:
  (a) the deployer needs to RECEIVE artifacts into its deployment work folder and ASSEMBLE/deploy them;
  (b) each repo's own member needs its declared clean-build command to be grantable in its own folder.

SECURITY INVARIANTS -- established in apra-fleet-ivxi (per-role bounds files + outOfBounds ledger
flagging) and apra-fleet-u1qw (orchestrator-side permissions-composer self-heal). Do not re-derive
them; read those beads and comply:
  1. A member NEVER self-escalates its own permissions (structurally guaranteed because
     composePermissionConfig disables the fleet MCP server on every composed member -- this bead must
     not weaken that in any way).
  2. The orchestrator grants strictly on a NEED BASIS -- exactly what the blocked operation's runbook
     documents, never a broad standing grant "to be safe". A bounds file is a scope definition for
     flagging, never a pre-grant list.
  3. The user's ABSOLUTE restrictions (NEVER_AUTO_GRANT) are never bypassed, for the deployer as for
     any other role.
design:
1) Read apra-fleet-ivxi and apra-fleet-u1qw first. ivxi already introduces a bounds file per role,
   including bounds-deployer.json. This bead EXTENDS that existing file for multi-repo assembly -- it
   does not create a parallel mechanism and does not add a new "integration" role.
2) Extend skills/fleet/profiles/bounds-deployer.json (ivxi's format) with the prefixes a multi-repo
   deployer legitimately needs: receiving files into <work folder>/<artifactsDir>, unpacking/assembling
   artifacts, and the composition/deploy tooling the manifest's deploy playbook uses (e.g. docker
   compose, helm, make, the workspace package manager). Scope every path-bearing prefix to the
   deployer's OWN work folder -- the deployer must have no grant that reaches into any repo member's
   checkout.
3) Per-repo build grants. Each repo member's declared build.command (manifest key from
   apra-fleet-74vu.1) runs in that member's own folder under its own stack profile. Verify the existing
   doer bounds cover ordinary build commands; if a repo's build command is out of bounds it is still
   granted but ledger-flagged outOfBounds per ivxi -- do not special-case it silently.
4) Trust seeding. The deployer's work folder is an ordinary single member work folder (no composite
   workspace now), so today's trust seeding applies unchanged -- confirm it covers the artifactsDir
   subtree created at runtime, since an untrusted path silently drops composed allows.
5) Isolation checks. Confirm and test that composing permissions for repo A's member never writes into
   repo B's folder or ledger, that the deployer's ledger is separate from every repo member's ledger,
   and that adding a repo to the manifest changes no existing member's composed settings.
6) Self-escalation guard. Assert the deployer's composed config still has the fleet MCP server
   DISABLED; all its grants are composed orchestrator-side (the load-bearing property from u1qw).
7) NEVER_AUTO_GRANT stays an absolute hard-stop for the deployer regardless of bounds -- a rejection
   surfaces as a real terminal failure, never a silent bypass.
8) Document the multi-repo deployer surface (artifact receipt + assembly) in
   skills/fleet/permissions.md alongside the existing bounds documentation.
acceptance_criteria:
- skills/fleet/profiles/bounds-deployer.json (ivxi's format and loader) covers artifact receipt into
  the deployer's artifactsDir, artifact assembly, and the manifest deploy playbook's composition
  tooling. No new "integration" role or bounds file is introduced.
- Every path-bearing prefix in bounds-deployer.json is scoped to the deployer's own work folder; a test
  asserts no deployer grant path resolves inside any repo member's checkout.
- Composing permissions for the deployer writes only to <deploy work folder>/.claude/
  settings.local.json and the deployer project's permissions.json ledger -- a test asserts no repo
  member's settings or ledger file was modified.
- Workspace trust covers the deployer work folder including the runtime-created artifactsDir subtree;
  a test asserts an artifact written under artifactsDir is readable by the deployer's composed config.
- A test asserts the deployer's composed config disables the fleet MCP server (no self-escalation).
- A test asserts adding a new repo entry to the manifest changes NO existing member's composed
  settings.local.json or ledger.
- A repo build command outside the doer role's bounds is still granted but ledger-flagged
  outOfBounds: true with requestedByRole set (apra-fleet-ivxi semantics) -- tested.
- A NEVER_AUTO_GRANT-listed permission requested for the deployer is hard-rejected and produces a
  terminal failure -- tested.
- skills/fleet/permissions.md documents the multi-repo deployer artifact-receipt/assembly surface.

title: Stage 0: add repo metadata to task beads and teach the planner the workspace
description:
CONTEXT (self-contained).
fleet-sprint's planner phase turns sprint goals into a bead DAG. Its prompt contract carries target
issues, goal, requirements text and per-task model-tier metadata (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/
runner.js:2635-2660), but it has NO concept of a repository -- the only occurrence of "repository" in
all of runner.js is incidental prose in a doer resume nudge (runner.js:7376-7377).

For multi-repo sprints, every task bead must say WHICH repository it belongs to, because that is what
later determines which member executes it, which branch it lands on and which PR it appears in. The
chosen mechanism (design doc section 4, "Dolt / beads topology" and "Planning and streaks") is a `repo`
metadata field on the bead -- exactly parallel to the model-tier metadata the planner already stamps
today -- carrying a repoId from the workspace manifest (the manifest is a JSON document declaring the
sprint's repositories, their base branches and their members; see the sibling Stage 0 manifest bead).

Hard rule from the design: a TASK bead lives in exactly ONE repo. Only features/epics may span repos,
and the planner must decompose those into per-repo children. This mirrors GitHub's own published
guidance for their single-repo coding agent (decompose into repo-scoped tasks around a shared contract).

Stage 0 scope: get the metadata and the planner prompt right. CONSUMING repo metadata at dispatch time
(streak purity, per-repo worklists, per-repo turn gates) is Stage 1 and lives in sibling beads.
design:
1) Bead metadata field. Stamp `repo: "<repoId>"` on task beads, using the same mechanism the planner
   already uses for the model-tier field (runner.js:2645-2651 -- follow that code path exactly rather
   than inventing a second metadata channel). repoId values must be keys of manifest.repos.
2) Planner prompt. Extend the planner prompt built around runner.js:2635-2660 with a WORKSPACE section
   rendered from the manifest: for each repoId, its one-line purpose/origin, plus the dependency graph
   (manifest.graph, where graph.<repo> lists the repos that repo depends on). Add explicit instructions:
   (a) stamp `repo` on EVERY task bead; (b) a task bead belongs to exactly one repo -- if work spans
   repos, create a feature/epic parent and per-repo task children; (c) express cross-repo ordering as
   ordinary same-DB `blocks` dependency edges between those per-repo children (one shared Dolt DB means
   cross-repo edges are plain edges, not external: references). Contract beads are a Stage 2 concept --
   do not mention or require them here.
3) Validation after planning. Where the runner validates the planner's output, add a check that every
   task-type bead in sprint scope carries a `repo` value that is a known repoId. For a single-repo
   sprint (synthesized one-entry manifest, repoId "default") the value is auto-filled rather than
   required from the planner, so single-repo behavior is unchanged.
4) Backfill/repair path. Beads created before this change, or created by a human without the field,
   must not hard-fail a multi-repo sprint: log a clear warning listing the unstamped bead IDs and
   fail the sprint at the precondition gate with a message telling the operator to set the repo field
   (fail fast is correct here -- silently guessing a repo would dispatch work into the wrong checkout).
5) Docs: document the `repo` bead metadata field and the planner workspace section in
   packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/README.md. Update packages/apra-fleet-client in the same
   change if any MCP tool schema shifts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Task beads created by the planner in a manifest sprint carry a `repo` metadata value equal to a key
  of manifest.repos; a test inspects created beads and asserts this for every task bead.
- The planner prompt contains a workspace section listing each repoId and the dependency graph -- a
  test snapshots the built prompt for a 3-repo manifest and asserts each repoId and each graph edge
  appears in it.
- The planner prompt instructs (verifiable by string assertions in the same snapshot test): stamp repo
  on every task bead; one repo per task bead; cross-repo ordering via `blocks` edges between per-repo
  children of a shared feature/epic.
- A planner output containing a task bead with no `repo`, or with a repoId not in the manifest, is
  rejected at the post-plan validation step with an error naming the offending bead ID and the invalid
  value.
- In a single-repo sprint (no --manifest), task beads are auto-stamped repo="default" and no planner
  prompt change is visible in the single-repo snapshot test -- existing single-repo planner tests pass
  unmodified.
- A multi-repo sprint whose pre-existing scope beads lack the repo field fails at the precondition gate
  with a message listing every unstamped bead ID (it does not guess a repo and does not silently run).
- packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/README.md documents the repo bead metadata field and the
  one-repo-per-task-bead rule.

title: permissions-composer: generic bounded self-heal role for Deploy/IntegTest/RegTest permission gaps
description: Sprint apra-fleet-i8qj/xj7v/5ti7 (branch fleet-sprint/win-headless-service-start) wasted 4 of 5 cycles because fleet-win-deploy's checkout had no .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json (both are gitignored and per-checkout by design -- see .gitignore:28 and agents/deployer.md's own doc comment), so deploy.md's Step 0 permission check blocked Deploy (and cascaded to skip Integration Test) every cycle until an operator manually ran compose_permissions. There is exactly one auto-compose call in the whole codebase today (register-member.ts:418-437, role=doer hardcoded, runs ONCE at registration) and it could not have helped anyway -- no built-in profile (base-dev, base-reviewer, tag-devops, tag-gpu) contains deploy.md's required Bash prefixes, since those live only in deploy.md's own Permissions section. Root cause and design discussion: this sprint's run log at http://localhost:8787/sprints/apra-fleet-i8qj%2Capra-fleet-xj7v%2Capra-fleet-5ti7-23d3d921-8cca-4bb2-9798-9588679fdacb/log. This bead adds a self-heal path: a small, GENERIC, safety-conscious role that any phase (deployer, integ-test-runner, regression-test-runner, or a future one) can call to resolve a permission gap -- explicitly scoped to PROTECT the system from over-broad grants, not just to unblock whichever phase called it. Depends on apra-fleet-ivxi (per-role bounds + out-of-bounds ledger flagging) since permissions-composer's whole safety property rests on checking requests against those bounds.
design: 1) Structured failure signal (coordinator-approved, do first): extend the deployer/integ-test-runner/regression-test-runner output schemas with a blockedReason field (e.g. blockedReason: 'missing_permissions') instead of prose-matching notes text, so the runner.js heal-trigger check is exact, not string-sniffing. 2) New role agents/permissions-composer.md -- tools: [Read, mcp__apra-fleet__compose_permissions] only (cannot do deploy/test work itself, cannot hand-edit settings files). Model tier: cheap (add permissionsComposer: 'cheap' to FIXED_ROLE_TIER in runner.js next to streakAssignment). Its job: read the calling phase's runbook (deploy.md / integ-test-playbook.md / regression-test-playbook.md, whichever the caller names) Permissions section, extract the exact requested Bash prefixes, and call compose_permissions(grant: [...], project_folder, grant_reason, role: <calling phase's role>) for the target member -- relying on apra-fleet-ivxi's per-role bounds check to flag anything outside that role's expected scope in the ledger, rather than reimplementing bounds logic itself. It must NOT attempt to route around a NEVER_AUTO_GRANT rejection -- a hard rejection from compose_permissions is a real, terminal failure it reports honestly, not something to retry/paper over. 3) Wiring in runner.js: generalize the existing deployer failure branch (runner.js ~8025-8029, where deployResult.deployed === true is checked) into a shared helper usable by the deployer, integ-test-runner, and regression-test-runner dispatch sites -- on blockedReason === 'missing_permissions', dispatch permissions-composer once, then retry the original phase dispatch once (mirror the existing max-turns-resume shape immediately above that block, and the trustHealAttempted single-retry pattern in execute-prompt.ts:1240-1256). It must also satisfy invariant 2 by construction: it reads the calling phase's runbook Permissions section and requests EXACTLY those prefixes (already the filed design) -- do not let implementation drift toward "grant everything the bounds file allows" as a shortcut; request only what the specific blocked operation needs. Invariant 3 (NEVER_AUTO_GRANT as an absolute, un-loosenable floor) already holds via ivxi's design step 4 and must not be bypassed by this bead's heal-retry loop -- a NEVER_AUTO_GRANT rejection stays a real, terminal failure (already an explicit AC).

title: compose_permissions: per-role permission bounds and out-of-bounds ledger flagging
description: Today compose_permissions has only a global NEVER_AUTO_GRANT denylist (sudo, su, env, printenv, nc, nmap) plus static base-dev/base-reviewer/tag-<name>.json profiles -- there is no notion of a per-role reasonable/expected permission scope, and every grant lands identically in the permissions.json ledger's granted[] array with no distinction between a routine, expected grant and a novel, out-of-policy one that unblocked a caller. This bead adds that missing bounds concept, as prep for apra-fleet permissions-composer (see the sibling bead) which needs to check requests against it.
design: 1) Add a per-role bounds definition, e.g. skills/fleet/profiles/bounds-<role>.json (deployer, integ-test-runner, regression-test-runner, doer, reviewer, ...), each listing prefix patterns considered in-scope for that role -- analogous shape to the existing tag-<name>.json profiles, loaded by a new loadBounds(role) helper in compose-permissions.ts. 2) Extend the Ledger interface's granted[] entry shape from {permission, reason, date} to {permission, reason, date, outOfBounds?: true, requestedByRole?: string} (backward compatible -- old entries without the new fields still load fine per loadLedger's existing raw.granted ?? [] fallback). 3) In the grant path (around compose-permissions.ts:424-433), when a role is known for the request, check each granted permission against that role's bounds file; permissions outside bounds get outOfBounds: true recorded in the ledger entry. In-bounds grants land exactly as they do today (no behavior change). 4) NEVER_AUTO_GRANT stays an absolute hard-stop regardless of any role's bounds -- bounds only widen what is silently grantable within a role, never override the denylist. 5) Document the new bounds file format and out-of-bounds ledger flag in skills/fleet/permissions.md (which already documents the ledger and NEVER_AUTO_GRANT) and in agents/schemas or wherever compose_permissions' own tool description lives.
acceptance_criteria: - A grant request whose permission matches an entry in the calling role's bounds-<role>.json is recorded in permissions.json ledger exactly as today (no outOfBounds field, or outOfBounds omitted/false). - A grant request outside that role's bounds is still granted (this tool does not block delivery) but its ledger entry carries outOfBounds: true and requestedByRole set. - A grant request with no role specified behaves exactly as today (fully backward compatible, no bounds check applied). - NEVER_AUTO_GRANT continues to hard-reject regardless of bounds. - Existing permissions.json ledger files (old shape, no outOfBounds field) still load without error. - skills/fleet/permissions.md documents the bounds file format and the ledger's new outOfBounds flag. - Unit tests cover: in-bounds grant (no flag), out-of-bounds grant (flag set), no-role grant (unchanged legacy path), NEVER_AUTO_GRANT still rejected even when role bounds would otherwise allow it.
notes:
SECURITY INVARIANTS (user directive, 2026-08-15 -- non-negotiable, apply to every design/implementation in this area, not just this bead):

1. A member must NEVER be able to escalate its own permissions. Already structurally true (composePermissionConfig() disables the fleet MCP server on every composed member -- see u1qw's correction note) -- this bead must not weaken that in any way (e.g. bounds files must not become something a member can read/edit to widen its own ceiling).
2. The orchestrator is an EXECUTOR of user will, not an independent grantor: it must request/compose strictly what the blocked operation's own runbook documents as needed (need basis), never a broad standing grant "to be safe." Bounds files (this bead's deliverable) exist to make "in-scope for this role" checkable, not to become a new source of over-broad default grants.
3. The user must be able to set ABSOLUTE restrictions nothing below can override. NEVER_AUTO_GRANT already does this (hardcoded sudo/su/env/printenv/nc/nmap, unconditional hard-stop regardless of role bounds -- design step 4 already preserves this). Gap: it is code-hardcoded only, not user-configurable. Consider (during implementation, not necessarily blocking this bead's AC) whether the user should be able to extend this denylist via a config file the code loads at startup, additive to (never replacing) the hardcoded floor.

These three invariants are the acceptance bar for the whole permissions-composer effort (this bead + apra-fleet-u1qw): the user has flagged that earlier formulations of this design got this wrong more than once, and considers getting it right the most important remaining gap before fleet-sprint is a mature, user-ready product. Origin: these ideas existed and matured over many iterations in the old apra-pm skill implementation and were lost when fleet-sprint was split out of it -- rebuild them cleanly, don't re-derive from scratch and risk losing them again.

title: Reviewer creates its own beads directly and returns newTaskIds, not title/description text -- retire orchestrator-mediated newTask creation and the child-id allocator
description:
Context: dogfooding fleet-sprint on fix/dolt-settle-recovery (sprint
apra-fleet-i8qj/apra-fleet-xj7v/apra-fleet-5ti7) surfaced that reviewer is the
ONLY beads-creating role that does not call `bd create` itself. planner,
integ-test-runner, and regression-test-runner all create beads directly and
return ids; reviewer instead returns `newTasks: [{title, description,
priority}]` JSON, which the ORCHESTRATOR (runner.js) turns into beads on its
behalf. This was originally done to centralize id-minting through
childIdAllocator/computeChildFloor and avoid concurrent-sprint child-id
collisions on dot-suffixed ids (e.g. two sprints both computing "abc.9" as
the next free slot). Depends on apra-fleet-vepq (UUID-based child ids), which
removes the reason that centralization was needed in the first place.

This bead is the full redesign, not just the id-scheme prerequisite:

a) Reviewer creates its own beads directly -- stop returning title/description
   text to the orchestrator. reviewer.md currently states "NEVER mutate beads
   directly -- no bd update, bd close, bd create, bd reopen" (Rules section)
   specifically for this reason; that prohibition is lifted for bead CREATION
   only (reopen/close semantics are a separate question, out of scope here).
   reviewer already has Bash tool access (frontmatter: `tools: [Read, Grep,
   Glob, Bash, Write]`), so this is a prompt/contract change, not a
   capability change. Mirror the "search for duplicates before creating"
   convention integ-test-runner.md/regression-test-runner.md already use.

b) Schema + downstream code: newTasks -> newTaskIds.
   - reviewer-output.json: replace `newTasks: [{title, description,
     priority}]` with `newTaskIds: string[]`. Drop the `title` field's
     `pattern`/`description` (the SAFE_TEXT_RE character-allowlist) entirely
     from this schema -- title never crosses the JSON boundary anymore, so
     the whole reason for that allowlist (safe shell interpolation by the
     orchestrator) goes away for this path.
   - reviewer.md Step 5 output-fields section: update the `newTasks`
     description accordingly.
   - runner.js: THREE call sites currently consume `verdict.newTasks` and
     must change to instead validate `verdict.newTaskIds` (confirm each id
     exists via `bd show`, was actually created this dispatch not
     hallucinated/reused, and is parented under the expected scope):
       1. Develop/Review loop, ~line 7854-7914
       2. Re-review, ~line 8519-8567
       3. Final Review, ~line 8809-8855
   - Retire the machinery that only existed to make orchestrator-side
     creation safe for LLM-authored titles: `sanitizeNewTaskTitle()`,
     `validateNewTask()`'s title branch (`SAFE_TEXT_RE` check), the whole
     rejected-newTask fallback path (`persistRejectedNewTaskToParentNotes`,
     `trackRejectedNewTaskForResurfacing`, `clearResubmittedNewTask`, and the
     `pendingRejectedNewTasks` resurfacing-into-next-planning-prompt logic).
     None of it is needed once reviewer creates the bead itself with full
     control over its own title/description.

c) Failure handling -- extend the pattern that already exists, don't invent
   a new one. `dispatchReview()` (runner.js ~line 5549-5710) already:
     - resumes the SAME session on max_turns exhaustion
       (`dispatchReviewerResume()`, "Continue your review exactly where you
       left off in this same session... Finish evaluating the remaining
       acceptance criteria and return your final verdict now"), and
     - on genuine dispatch failure (schema-repair exhausted, transport error,
       auth error, sync error) already synthesizes
       `{verdict: 'CHANGES_NEEDED', dispatchFailed: true}` -- NEVER treated
       as APPROVED.
   Add the missing piece: if reviewer stalls/fails midway through creating
   its own newTasks, the resume prompt must tell it to `bd search` for
   duplicates of what it may have already created before continuing (same
   dedup convention as (a)), so a resumed dispatch doesn't double-file. If
   resume also fails, the existing `dispatchFailed -> CHANGES_NEEDED`
   synthesis already covers "never treat an incomplete/failed round as
   APPROVED" -- confirm this holds when the failure happens mid-bead-creation
   too, not just mid-verdict-formation.

d) Remove the child-id allocator. `childIdAllocator` / `computeChildFloor` /
   `createChildBeadWithAllocatedId` (runner.js) exist ONLY to make
   orchestrator-mediated creation collision-safe under the old dot-suffix
   scheme. Once beads use UUID-based ids (apra-fleet-vepq) there is no
   collision to coordinate against, so: remove this allocator machinery
   entirely, and reviewer (like planner/integ-test-runner/regression-test-
   runner) always creates its own bead via a plain `bd create --id <uuid>
   --parent <target-parent> ...` -- no orchestrator involvement, no special
   case for reviewer.

e) Fix every test that breaks. This area has heavy existing coverage that
   hard-codes the current title/description contract and must be rewritten,
   not just patched, including (non-exhaustive, grep `newTask`/`reviewer` in
   test/ for the full set):
     - test/newtasks-validation.test.mjs
     - test/rejected-newtask-resurface.test.mjs
     - test/newtask-body-file-roundtrip.test.mjs
     - test/newtask-body-member-side-transport.test.mjs
     - test/19o3-newtask-allowlist-resurface-integration.test.mjs
     - test/mock-sprint-finalization-pr-injection.test.mjs
     - test/golden-transcript.test.mjs / golden-transcript-3bead.test.mjs
       and their fixtures/bd-recordings/*.jsonl that encode reviewer
       returning title/description (any fixture whose reviewer verdict JSON
       carries newTasks with title/description needs updating to
       newTaskIds).
     - test/runner-role-input-contract.test.mjs
   Expect this to be the largest line-count item in the change even though
   it's the least design-risky.

Acceptance criteria:
- reviewer.md and reviewer-output.json updated per (a)/(b); reviewer no
  longer forbidden from `bd create`, newTasks field removed, newTaskIds
  added.
- All three runner.js call sites (Develop/Review, Re-review, Final Review)
  consume newTaskIds and validate returned ids instead of creating beads.
- sanitizeNewTaskTitle/validateNewTask's title branch and the rejected-
  newTask resurfacing stack are removed (or clearly justified if any part
  must stay).
- childIdAllocator/computeChildFloor/createChildBeadWithAllocatedId removed;
  reviewer's bead creation goes through the same plain `bd create --parent`
  path as planner/integ-test-runner/regression-test-runner, using the
  UUID-based id scheme from apra-fleet-vepq.
- Resume-on-failure prompt for reviewer includes a dedup-before-continuing
  instruction; a dispatch failure at any point in this flow still resolves
  to CHANGES_NEEDED, never APPROVED (verified by a test exercising a
  simulated mid-creation failure).
- Full test suite green; every test/fixture that encoded the old
  title/description newTasks contract is updated to the new id-based one.

Out of scope (tracked separately, not part of this bead): the finding that
in-cycle reopens (`bd update <id> --status=open`, Develop/Review and
Re-review loops) do not persist the reviewer's reason to the bead's own
notes the way Final Review's reopen does via `--append-notes` -- a related
but distinct beads.md "beads holds all task state" gap.

title: Replace dot-suffixed child bead ids with UUID-based ids to remove the central allocator bottleneck
description:
Context: this came out of dogfooding fleet-sprint on fix/dolt-settle-recovery
(sprint apra-fleet-i8qj/apra-fleet-xj7v/apra-fleet-5ti7), while investigating
why reviewer's newTasks field carries full title/description/priority JSON
instead of just bead ids, unlike planner/integ-test-runner/regression-test-runner
which all call bd create directly and return only ids.

Current design and why it exists:
reviewer is the one role that does NOT call bd create itself. Instead it
returns newTasks as {title, description, priority} JSON, and the ORCHESTRATOR
(runner.js) creates the bead on its behalf via createChildBeadWithAllocatedId,
which mints the child id through an in-process childIdAllocator + computeChildFloor
before calling bd create --parent <id>. This exists specifically to stop two
CONCURRENT sprints creating children under the SAME parent bead from computing
the same next dot-suffixed child number (e.g. two sprints both computing
"abc.9" as the next free slot and colliding). Routing bead creation through the
orchestrator's allocator was the fix for that collision risk -- which is why
reviewer's output carries full title/description/priority text instead of an id:
there was no id yet for it to return.

The asymmetry this creates:
planner, integ-test-runner, and regression-test-runner all call bd create
directly (see apra-pm/agents/planner.md, integ-test-runner.md Step 3,
regression-test-runner.md Step 3) with NO equivalent allocator coordination.
regression-test-runner sidesteps the collision risk by filing beads
standalone/parent-less by design (see its Step 3 "Why parent-less is the point"
section) -- no parent means no shared dot-numbering slot to collide on. But
integ-test-runner creates children directly under `--parent=<scope id>` with a
plain bd create and NO allocator -- meaning it has the SAME latent
concurrent-child-id-collision exposure the allocator was built to prevent for
reviewer, just never examined or protected. Only reviewer pays the
structured-JSON-instead-of-id tax; the risk the tax is paying for is not
actually mitigated fleet-wide.

Proposed fix: stop using dot-suffixed sequential child ids (abc.9, abc.10)
for follow-up/child beads created by any of these roles. Instead:
1. Create the new bead with a globally-unique, non-sequential id (UUID or
   equivalent random suffix) -- bd create already supports this today via
   `bd create --id <explicit-id> ...` (confirmed: `bd create --help` lists
   `--id string  Explicit issue ID (e.g., 'bd-42' for partitioning)`), so no
   new bd capability is required, only a different id-generation strategy at
   the call site (pass a UUID instead of leaving id derivation to the
   dot-suffix default).
2. Wire the parent-child (grouping) edge AFTER creation, via the SAME
   `--parent <parent-id>` flag (or `bd dep add` per the parent-child vs
   blocks distinction in agents/_shared/GRAPH-SEMANTICS.md), rather than
   relying on bd to derive the next sequential dot-suffix under that parent.

Why this is a real fix, not just a workaround: a UUID-keyed id has
astronomically low collision probability regardless of how many sprints/roles
create children under the same parent concurrently, so it removes the NEED
for a central allocator entirely. That means:
- reviewer's newTasks could be redesigned to create beads directly and return
  bead ids (see companion redesign discussion in this same session) without
  reintroducing the collision risk the current centralization exists to
  prevent -- removing the last blocker on that redesign.
- integ-test-runner's already-latent, currently-unprotected collision
  exposure goes away too, for free, without adding allocator coordination to
  it.
- Every bead-creating role (planner, doer follow-ups, reviewer,
  integ-test-runner, regression-test-runner) can converge on ONE consistent
  pattern: create directly, with a collision-safe id, return the id. No role
  needs special-cased orchestrator-mediated creation for id-safety reasons.

Scope note: this is infrastructure/id-scheme work, not sprint-scoped feature
work -- it should be picked up alongside the larger reviewer-direct-creation
refactor (see companion notes: reviewer.md/reviewer-output.json/runner.js
newTasks -> newTaskIds redesign, and the observation that in-cycle reopens
via `bd update <id> --status=open` do not persist the reviewer's reason to
the bead itself, unlike Final Review's reopen path which does via
--append-notes) rather than as an isolated one-off change, since the id-scheme
change is what unblocks that refactor's concurrency-safety question.

Acceptance criteria:
- Decide and document the new id-generation strategy (UUID vs other
  collision-resistant scheme) for follow-up/child beads created by any
  fleet-sprint role.
- childIdAllocator / computeChildFloor (runner.js) and their dot-suffix
  sequencing logic are either removed or clearly scoped down to only the
  cases that still need them (if any remain).
- reviewer, integ-test-runner, regression-test-runner, and planner all
  create follow-up/child beads through the same id-generation path (no
  role-specific exception for collision-safety reasons).
- A concurrency test (two simulated concurrent sprints creating children
  under the same parent) demonstrates no id collision under the new scheme.

title: Sprint progress-bar widgets: disagreeing unlabeled counters + bar scrolls out of view
description:
Three related UX/correctness bugs in the fleet-sprint progress-reporting widgets, all found live while dogfooding the i8qj/xj7v/5ti7 proof sprint -- screenshots showed 10/15, 8/18, 0/7, 0/9 for what a user reasonably assumes is 'the same number' on the same sprint at the same moment.

1) Sprint's own dashboard, Tasks tab (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/viewer-extensions.mjs): renderProgressBarHtml's bar (e.g. '10/15', apra-fleet-x8r) is closed/required over sprintTasks ONLY, filtered by goalMax and decomposedParentIds. Directly below it, the separate 'eft.90' counter (viewer-extensions.mjs ~line 670-674, comment: 'a persistent M/N item count at the top of the panel') is openBeadCount/totalBeadCount over sprintTasks.concat(backlogTasks), with NO goal/parent filtering. Different denominator (15 vs 18: required-to-close vs everything-including-backlog) AND inverted numerator polarity (closed vs open) -- two independently-shipped widgets stacked with zero label distinguishing them, guaranteed to disagree by design, not a computation bug in either one individually.

2) Supervisor dashboard, Sprint Stack card (src/supervisor/dashboard.mjs ~line 658-677): 'Claimed scope: N bead(s)' is the RAW unfiltered size of the full live subtree under the sprint's issueRoots (beadCount = scope.size). The progress bar's own M/N a few lines above it is computeSprintProgress() run on the SAME scope but goal+decomposedParentIds-filtered. Same species of bug as (1): two different definitions of 'how many beads', unlabeled, shown adjacent. Compounded by scope legitimately GROWING over a sprint's life as planners add children mid-run (expandScope is live, not stale) -- so the raw number also changes cycle to cycle (observed 0/9 early, 0/7 later), which is correct/by-design for that number alone but, again unlabeled, reads as a bug.

3) Layout: on the sprint's own dashboard, the Tasks tab's fixed panel-header (packages/apra-fleet-workflow-rendered markup, panel-header div containing just the text 'Tasks') is a SEPARATE sibling element from the scrollable #extension-beads container the progress bar is injected into (viewer-extensions.mjs's renderBeadsPanel(): container.innerHTML = renderProgressBarHtml(progress) + renderBeadsHtml(...), where container = #extension-beads, which has overflow-y: auto). The progress bar is therefore the first item INSIDE the scrollable region, not pinned in the header row next to 'Tasks' -- scrolling down through a long task list scrolls the progress bar out of view entirely.

## Context
Filed 2026-08-13 during the i8qj/xj7v/5ti7 dogfood sprint (fleet-sprint/win-headless-service-start). User's own words: 'make me feel which 4th grader has written this code' -- root cause in both counter-disagreement cases is not a math bug, it is two independently-authored, unlabeled widgets measuring genuinely different things (or growing over time) placed adjacent to each other with no distinguishing context.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The two counters on the sprint's own Tasks tab either show the SAME definition (pick one: closed/required, goal+parent-filtered, sprint-only -- matches the actual completion gate) with the second one removed as redundant, OR both are kept but each gets an explicit, visible label naming exactly what it counts (e.g. 'Required: 10/15' and 'All tasks (incl. backlog): 10 open / 18 total') so they never again read as a disagreement. 2) The supervisor Sprint Stack card's 'Claimed scope: N' and its progress bar's M/N are each explicitly labeled with what they count (e.g. 'N total in scope' vs 'M/N2 required, goal-filtered'), so a growing raw scope count over a sprint's lifetime is legible as expected behavior, not a glitch. 3) The Tasks-tab progress bar (whichever single widget survives from item 1) is moved into the fixed panel-header row, next to the 'Tasks' label, so it remains visible regardless of scroll position in the task list below it. 4) Covered by tests: existing viewer-extensions.test.mjs / x8r-sprint-progress-bar.test.mjs coverage updated to assert on the new labeled output; a DOM-level or snapshot check confirms the progress widget renders inside panel-header, not inside the scrollable #extension-beads container.

title: [impl] Hidden-window detached launch helper for Windows (SW_HIDE via Win32_Process Create)
description:
Add ONE standardized helper for launching a detached, console-window-free background process on Windows, so no session ever again hand-rolls an Invoke-CimMethod incantation.

SCOPE BOUNDARY (important): this task owns WINDOW VISIBILITY and the detached-launch mechanism only. It does NOT touch, redesign, or replace the ApraFleet scheduled-task registration -- parent AC1's "preferred: a real Windows service registration" clause is owned by apra-fleet-i8qj.2 under a different sprint goal. Do not edit src/services/service-manager/windows.ts register()/start(), and do not edit src/cli/start.ts (owned by apra-fleet-i8qj.4). If i8qj.4 later wants this helper, it will import it.

FILES: src/os/windows.ts (new exported helper, next to wrapPowerShellEncoded) plus at most one types/index touch. Max 3 files; no call-site rewiring in this task.

BEHAVIOUR:
- Export a helper such as launchDetachedHidden({ command, args, cwd, logFile, title }) returning the created PID, or a structured failure, built on Win32_Process Create with a STARTUPINFO carrying dwFlags=STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW and wShowWindow=SW_HIDE (0), so the child gets NO visible console window.
- Build the PowerShell through wrapPowerShellEncoded -- never a bare interpolated string. The ad hoc attempts that motivated this bug died from cmd.exe quote stripping; encoded-command wrapping is the documented cure.
- Resolve every path in JavaScript before building the command; no $HOME, ~, or backtick expansion in the command string (CLAUDE.md rule; apra-fleet-ot2z precedent).
- Redirect stdout and stderr to the caller-supplied log file so a hidden process is still observable.
- The launched process must survive the parent process / SSH channel exiting.

PRIMARY vs FALLBACK (decide here; do not build both): hidden launch is the primary behaviour. Parent AC3's explicit-window-title path is the SANCTIONED FALLBACK only -- implement it as a single title option applied when the caller explicitly opts out of hiding, or when SW_HIDE is unavailable, producing an unambiguous title such as "Apra Fleet MCP Server -- do not close". A visible window must never be the default.

DONE / ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. A single exported helper exists in src/os/windows.ts and emits an encoded-command PowerShell invocation of Win32_Process Create with STARTUPINFO wShowWindow=SW_HIDE.
2. It returns the child PID on success and a structured, non-throwing failure with the raw PowerShell stderr preserved on failure -- callers can branch and nothing is silently swallowed.
3. stdout/stderr land in the caller-specified log file; the launched process outlives its launcher.
4. The visible-window path exists only as an explicit opt-out and sets an unambiguous console title.
5. No changes to scheduled-task registration, src/cli/start.ts, or any non-Windows path.
6. tsc build passes, npm test passes, ASCII-only source per repo convention.

Emitted via wrapPowerShellEncoded; decoded script tokens for 5ti7.3 to assert: $SW_HIDE = 0, New-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_ProcessStartup -ClientOnly -Property @{ ShowWindow = $SW_HIDE; CreateFlags = $CREATE_NO_WINDOW }, Invoke-CimMethod -ClassName Win32_Process -MethodName Create, FLEET_LAUNCH_PID:. WMI has no dwFlags property: ShowWindow maps to STARTUPINFO.wShowWindow and implies STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW (documented in JSDoc). NOTE for 5ti7.2: returned PID is the cmd.exe /c wrapper that owns the child (needed for > log 2>&1 redirection); it exits with the child and taskkill /F /T kills the tree. Failures are structured (ok:false with stderr + parsed Create ReturnValue), never thrown. Visible window is explicit opt-out only (showWindow:true -> ShowWindow=1 + Title default 'Apra Fleet MCP Server -- do not close'). Build + full test suite green (fail=0).

title: Windows detached launch leaves visible console windows for apra-fleet run and the fleet-sprint supervisor
description:
Every session that deploys/relaunches apra-fleet on Windows (deploy.md's WMI Win32_Process.Create technique) ends up inventing its own ad-hoc launch incantation, and none of them suppress the console window. Result: 2 persistent black cmd.exe windows on the user's desktop -- one for 'apra-fleet run --transport http' (MCP server, port 7523) and one for the fleet-sprint supervisor ('node bin/serve.mjs', port 8787) -- neither of which the user has any use for, and which look alarming/unfamiliar ('never seen that for fleet supervisor'). A normally-registered 'apra-fleet start' scheduled task does not show a window; the manual WMI-detach fallback (used when start's scheduled-task registration fails with Access Denied, which deploy.md says is expected on this machine) currently does.

## Context
Filed 2026-08-13 after redeploying fix/dolt-settle-recovery: killed a stale supervisor + relaunched both server and supervisor via ad hoc Invoke-CimMethod Win32_Process.Create calls (first two attempts silently died from an unrelated cmd.exe quote-stripping bug, third attempt worked but left visible windows). User flagged this as a recurring pattern across sessions, not a one-off, and wants it fixed generally, not just muted this once.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Both the MCP server and the fleet-sprint supervisor can be launched detached on Windows via a single, standardized helper (not hand-rolled per-session PowerShell) with NO visible console window -- e.g. WMI Win32_Process.Create with STARTUPINFO wShowWindow=SW_HIDE / dwFlags STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW, or CreateProcess with CREATE_NO_WINDOW, or (preferred if feasible) a real Windows service registration that doesn't require an interactive logon session at all, replacing the scheduled-task approach that fails with Access Denied. 2) deploy.md is updated to document/use this single helper instead of leaving the exact launch mechanics to be improvised each time. 3) Last-resort fallback if truly hidden launch cannot be made reliable: each window's title is set explicitly and unambiguously (e.g. 'Apra Fleet MCP Server -- do not close' / 'Apra Fleet Sprint Supervisor -- do not close') via the process's console-title API or a leading 'title ...' in the wrapping cmd, so a user who does see them can immediately identify what they are and that closing them kills the service. 4) Verified live on a real Windows machine, not just code review.

The root package.json test script is 'vitest run', and vitest.config.ts include is ['tests/**/*.test.ts', 'packages/*/tests/**/*.test.ts']. The fleet-sprint runner's suites live in packages/apra-fleet-se/test/ as .test.mjs files run by node --test via that workspace's own test script, so they are silently excluded from the repo-level gate. A reviewer or CI job running root npm test gets a green result that never exercised runner.js at all -- two review rounds in a row have had to invoke mock-sprint-abort-pr.test.mjs, vcs-auth-pr-self-heal.test.mjs, mock-sprint-windows-vcs-credential.test.mjs and resolve-member-os-cache.test.mjs by hand to satisfy the acceptance criteria of apra-fleet-ot2z.1 and apra-fleet-ot2z.2. Pre-existing, not caused by fix/cross-shell-home-var.

Fix: chain the workspace suite into the root test script (for example: vitest run, then npm test -w @apralabs/apra-fleet-se) or add an explicit CI step. Separately, address the SprintLockHeldError flakiness that suite shows under --test-concurrency=8 whenever any real sprint holds a lock: roughly 20-23 tests across 19o3-newtask-allowlist-resurface-integration, 66u-stall-progress-credit, budget-live, develop-review-loop-exit-logging, doer-global-sequencing, error-classification-routing-table, final-review-auth-self-heal, git-sync-brackets and golden-transcript-3bead fail purely on lock contention, which makes the suite unusable as a gate until it is fixed (options: per-test unique sprint branch names, or serialising the lock-acquiring scenarios).
close_reason: Chained apra-fleet-se node --test suite into root npm test (package.json); isolated mock-sprint scenarios' sprint-lock dir (mock-sprint-harness.mjs runDevelopLoopScenario + 3 standalone scenario files) from the real machine-global lock dir to eliminate SprintLockHeldError flakiness under --test-concurrency=8. Full workspace suite: 2030 pass, 0 fail. Root build passes.

title: resolveMemberOs: cache only successful member_detail OS resolutions, not the 'linux' fallback
description: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js resolveMemberOs (~lines 1725-1748) writes memberOsCache.set(member, os) on BOTH the success and the catch path. Because member_detail performs a live connectivity check, a single transient failure (member briefly asleep, flaky SSH, MCP hiccup) permanently pins that member to the 'linux' fallback for the whole runner process -- including the auth-retry credential read at runner.js:1984, whose entire purpose is to recover. On a Windows member that means the POSIX $HOME string (the exact apra-fleet-ot2z bug) is re-emitted for the rest of the sprint, with the failure surfacing only as the generic credential-read error. Fix: cache only when member_detail actually yielded an `os`; on the fallback path return 'linux' without caching so the next call re-probes. Add a unit test that stubs fleetApi.memberDetail to reject once and then resolve os='windows', asserting the second call builds the Windows -EncodedCommand form (clearMemberOsCache is already exported as the test seam).
close_reason: Fixed: resolveMemberOs now caches only successful member_detail-derived OS, not the linux fallback; added unit test.

title: Make wrapPowerShellEncoded surface non-terminating PowerShell failures as a non-zero exit code
description: src/os/windows.ts:15-18 wrapPowerShellEncoded() emits `powershell -EncodedCommand <b64>`, which exits 0 unless a terminating error occurs. Non-terminating failures (Set-Content access-denied, Remove-Item failure, a cmdlet erroring with default $ErrorActionPreference='Continue') write to stderr but still return exit code 0, so callers that check the exit code cannot see them. This now affects every site ot2z.10 routed through the helper: remove-member.ts:95-103's new authorized_keys cleanup warning (it fires correctly on POSIX, where sed exits 2 on a missing file, but can stay silent on Windows), strategy.ts:52 deleteFiles, monitor-task.ts:46/50/54, and windows.ts's writeTextFile/credentialFileWrite/readRemoteJson/hashFilesRecursive. Fix in the helper so all call sites benefit: prepend `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` and wrap the script body in try/catch { Write-Error $_; exit 1 }, then re-check the sites that intentionally tolerate missing paths (deleteFiles uses -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue and must keep exiting 0) so no false failures are introduced. Add a unit test asserting the wrapped script for a failing cmdlet yields a non-zero exit path.
close_reason: Implemented $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' + try/catch{exit 1} + explicit exit 0 in wrapPowerShellEncoded; verified deleteFiles' SilentlyContinue tolerance still exits 0; added unit + live-PowerShell tests; tsc build and full targeted test suite pass

title: Wrap Windows member-bound commands in an explicit powershell -EncodedCommand instead of relying on the member's default sshd shell
description: src/tools/monitor-task.ts:41-53 and src/tools/remove-member.ts:92-94 send raw PowerShell one-liners over strategy.execCommand with no explicit shell wrapper, while src/services/strategy.ts:50-52 (deleteFiles) and src/services/stall/stall-poller.ts:112 both wrap explicitly (powershell -EncodedCommand / powershell -c). The unwrapped form works only if the Windows member's sshd default shell is PowerShell; on a cmd.exe default it silently produces garbage. Normalise Windows command construction onto a single explicit wrapper helper (e.g. reuse the -EncodedCommand pattern in src/os/windows.ts:164/204/216) so the convention added in CLAUDE.md ('wrap PowerShell commands explicitly rather than assuming the member's shell') is actually satisfied at these call sites.
close_reason: Wrapped monitor-task.ts, remove-member.ts, and strategy.ts deleteFiles Windows PowerShell one-liners in an explicit powershell -EncodedCommand via new wrapPowerShellEncoded() helper in windows.ts; build + full vitest suite pass.

title: [impl] Document the 'no shell variable expansion in member-bound command strings' rule in CLAUDE.md and resync agent docs
description:
Covers UPDATED ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 6 in apra-fleet-ot2z's notes. Source material is the root bug's OWN NOTES (the completed opus-traced sweep: confirmed sites, already-safe reference patterns) -- there is no separate audit bead; do not go looking for one.

FILES: CLAUDE.md (Conventions section), then regenerate AGENTS.md and AGY.md via `node scripts/sync-agent-docs.mjs`. Do NOT create a new .md doc (new docs need user review; CLAUDE.md is already the source of truth for the generated agent docs).

WORK: Add a tight Conventions bullet (one or two bullets, not an essay) stating the rule, worded to match the actual defect class:
  - The failure is NOT "a $VAR appears in a command" -- PowerShell resolves $HOME fine. It is relying on POSIX-shell path expansion in a string sent to a member whose shell may be PowerShell or cmd, where `$HOME/.foo` parses as $HOME followed by a `/` operator and errors out.
  - Rule: never build a member-bound command (execute_command / strategy.execCommand / fleet-sprint's command()) by pasting a shell variable into a path -- no `$VAR/...`, no `~/...`, no backticks, no `$( )`. agent.os can be 'windows' at ANY call site.
  - Instead resolve host/path values in JS first (reference pattern: src/services/member-home.ts:40-56 probeCommandFor) or branch construction on agent OS (src/providers/claude.ts:373-374, src/os/*). Where a command must be PowerShell, wrap it explicitly (powershell -EncodedCommand, as src/os/windows.ts does) rather than assuming the member's default shell.
  - A POSIX-only feature must HARD-FAIL or be OS-gated with a surfaced error -- an advisory warning that never gates is a false success, not a mitigation (see the long_running case fixed in apra-fleet-ot2z.4).
  - Cite apra-fleet-ot2z as the originating incident and name the regression tests that enforce this (apra-fleet-ot2z.2, .5, .7, .9) as the enforcement mechanism.
ASCII only (repo rule).

DISPATCH NOTE: this task is independently dispatchable at ANY point in the sprint, including before the fixes land. Cite apra-fleet-ot2z.2/.5/.7/.9 by id as the intended enforcement mechanism; do NOT verify those beads exist, that their test files are present, or that their tests pass -- that is each of those beads' own work. The rule text comes from the root bug's notes, which are already complete.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- CLAUDE.md contains the rule under Conventions, ASCII-only, and its wording does not forbid legitimate PowerShell `$env:*` / automatic-variable usage (e.g. `Join-Path $HOME 'x'`) -- only expansion-pasted paths.
- The advisory-warning-is-not-a-gate point is stated explicitly.
- `node scripts/sync-agent-docs.mjs` has been run and the regenerated AGENTS.md / AGY.md are included in the same change (no hand-editing of generated shared sections).
- No new .md file is created.

title: Align computeSprintProgress required count with the completion gate's required set
description: apra-fleet-x8r.1 shipped computeSprintProgress() with required = sprintTasks.length (every bead in the bdListScoped('') scope). runner.js's real completion gate (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js around line 8134) computes openAtGoal = bdListScoped('--status=<NOT_DONE_STATUSES> --priority-max=<goalMax>') MINUS decomposedParentIds(), i.e. below-goal beads and decomposed parents are not part of the required-to-close set that gates sprint exit. Consequence: on a sprint whose scope contains below-goal-priority beads or decomposed parents, the new progress bar can never reach N/N even when the sprint legitimately completes, which is the opposite of the widget's stated purpose ('how much of this sprint's required work is actually done'). Plumb the sprint's goalMax and the decomposed-parent id set through to the viewer payload alongside sprintTasks and have computeSprintProgress filter on them, rather than re-deriving either client-side. Add unit coverage for a scope containing a below-goal bead and a decomposed parent reaching N/N.

title: Make stall detector immune to hub/member clock skew
description:
src/services/stall/stall-detector.ts compares member-produced signals (mtime, content timestamp) directly against a hub-seeded lastActivityAt baseline (src/tools/execute-prompt.ts:694 seeds it with the hub's Date.now()). When the member's clock is skewed from the hub's by more than STALL_THRESHOLD_MS (120s default), that comparison can never succeed in the direction that matters, so lastActivityAt never advances and the detector kills genuinely healthy, actively-working sessions on the very first poll tick past the threshold.

Root-caused via live reproduction on fleet-win-dev1 (see apra-fleet-lgz0's description for the full incident): the member's w32time had never synced (free-running on CMOS clock, ~215s behind hub). Every one of 3 consecutive Planner-dispatch retries was killed with lastActivityAt bit-for-bit identical to its own stall_add timestamp -- i.e. the signal never advanced even once, despite the real session transcript growing to 100-200KB of fresh content each time. Disproved alternative theories live: reader commands (Get-Item/Get-Content) correctly track a file under active concurrent write (tested with AutoFlush=true/false StreamWriter, FileStream+Flush, File::AppendAllText variants); Claude Code 2.1.220 writes its transcript incrementally, not batched (smooth timestamp spread across session, gaps p50 <1s).

Fix shape (not yet implemented):
- Extend StallEntry (stall-detector.ts) with lastSignal: { contentTs: number | null; mtimeMs: number | null } | null -- member-clock values, compared only against the entry's own previously-stored member-clock values, never against the hub-clock lastActivityAt.
- Replace the cross-clock comparisons (currently ~lines 200-202 and ~224-229: `mtimeMs > entry.lastActivityAt`, `ts > entry.lastActivityAt`) with change detection: if this poll's member-side signal differs from lastSignal, that is progress -> stamp lastActivityAt = Date.now() (hub clock, unchanged) and update lastSignal.
- First poll after stall_add seeds lastSignal only -- must count as neither progress nor a stall-eligible tick, to avoid an off-by-one false-something on the very first observation.
- Apply the same treatment to the provisional path (pollDirectoryActivity's mtime-only check, currently ~lines 102-109).
- Threshold arithmetic itself (Date.now() - lastActivityAt > stallThresholdMs) stays pure hub-clock, unchanged -- only the "did anything change" signal moves to member-clock-only comparison.
- This also fixes the converse, currently-live hole: a member clock running AHEAD of the hub currently makes any wedged session on that member look permanently alive (mtime/content always "newer" than the hub baseline), so the detector can never kill it.

Secondary, separate scope (do not bundle into this bead): probe and persist clock offset at member registration/dispatch time, surface via member_detail/register_member -- if that lands, packages/apra-fleet-client must be updated in the same change per CLAUDE.md (tool schema change). Tracked separately from this bead's core fix.

Also fix along the way: pollDirectoryActivity (stall-poller.ts:120) uses Get-ChildItem directory enumeration, which live-reproduction showed serves ~30s-stale cached directory entries vs a direct Get-Item -LiteralPath on the same file at the same instant (Windows does not always flush directory-entry metadata on WriteFile without FlushFileBuffers). Re-stat the winning candidate via Get-Item -LiteralPath after picking the newest by enumeration. 30s of lag against a 120s threshold is material even though it did not cause this specific incident.

Verification requirement (do not repeat the mistake made twice while diagnosing this): every fix claim during this investigation that was verified only against already-closed, static files, or without an intentionally-skewed clock, turned out to be incomplete or address the wrong function. The fix here must be verified with a new test that specifically asserts the detector does NOT kill a session when member-clock signals are offset from the hub by more than STALL_THRESHOLD_MS in EITHER direction (member behind and member ahead), in addition to the existing mocked-timestamp regression suite (tests/stall-poller.test.ts, stall-detector.test.ts, stall-no-signal-false-kill.test.ts, stall-any-entry-activity-and-kill.test.ts) staying green. Given this touches core polling logic shared by every provider (Claude/Gemini/AGY) and platform (Windows/POSIX), treat as medium-risk, not a quick patch.

title: Stall poller kills copilot/codex/none dispatches past 120s (resolveSessionLogDir returns null)
description:
For copilot, codex, and none providers, resolveSessionLogDir() returns null, so pollDirectoryMtimeMs always returns null for their dispatches. Combined with the unconditional provisional-baseline stall check in stall-detector.ts (fires at STALL_THRESHOLD_MS, default 120s), any dispatch on these providers that legitimately runs longer than 120s gets onStall fired, its remote pid killed, and the dispatch aborted with a false stalled error -- even though it was making real progress.

This is the same failure shape PR #383's MF-5 had for AGY before it was fixed (AGY's directory-scan depth bound didn't reach the real transcript path, so pollDirectoryMtimeMs always returned null and 120s+ AGY dispatches were false-stalled and killed). Confirmed during round-4 review of PR #383 that this is pre-existing on main, not introduced by that PR, and affects a different provider set (copilot/codex/none) via the same underlying mechanism -- no directory-mtime fallback exists for providers whose resolveSessionLogDir returns null.

Fix direction: either give these providers a working resolveSessionLogDir so the directory-mtime fallback can function, or make the provisional-baseline stall check aware that no fallback signal exists for the provider and use a longer/different timeout policy instead of assuming activity absence == stall.

## Context
Discovered incidentally during PR #383 (feat/agy-output-format-json) round-4 re-review while tracing the AGY stall-detection fix (MF-5). See PR comment: https://github.com/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet/pull/383#issuecomment-5213248907
close_reason: Fixed in feat/agy-output-format-json commit 36c52bcd (PR #383). Verified independently by mutation testing: codex/copilot/none dispatches no longer false-killed on the baseline stall timeout when no reliable signal exists. See PR #383 round-5 review comment and github.com/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet/issues/390.

title: Make golden-transcript integ-test-runner mock's verify-id regex dot-tolerant
description: packages/apra-fleet-se/test/golden-transcript.test.mjs:402 and packages/apra-fleet-se/test/golden-transcript-3bead.test.mjs:352 parse runner.js's verifyClause with /await verification-closure: ([^.]+)\./. Because [^.]+ stops at the first '.', a verify-routed bead id containing a dot (the project's standard decomposed-child form, e.g. apra-fleet-eft.52) is truncated to its parent prefix and the mock would issue `bd close` against the WRONG bead. No scenario in these two files currently generates a dotted verify id, so nothing fails today - but the sibling `doer` handler in the same file (golden-transcript.test.mjs:296) uses a dot-tolerant `(.+)` capture, so this commit introduced an inconsistency that will bite the first scenario that makes a decomposed child verify-eligible. Fix: anchor the capture on the clause terminator rather than the first dot (e.g. match up to '. For each,' or use a non-greedy capture with an explicit trailing-sentence anchor), and add a mock-harness unit test that feeds a prompt naming a dotted id (apra-fleet-xyz.1) and asserts exactly that id is closed.
close_reason: Fixed dot-truncating verify-id regex in golden-transcript.test.mjs and golden-transcript-3bead.test.mjs via shared extractVerifyIds() helper; added unit test asserting dotted verify ids are preserved. Commit 79e49e8.
