description:
Fix apra-fleet-ta3 in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js (syncMemberAfter, ~lines 903-1010) (+ CHANGELOG.md entry). Observed live: doer streak closed fine, then '[Sync] G-push pull-rebase for member fleet-lin-dev1 failed: fatal: couldn't find remote ref fix/dispatch-stall-reliability' (runner.js ~line 992).

Diagnose first, then fix -- a suppression-only patch is NOT acceptable:
(a) Control only reaches the pull-rebase at line 938 when the initial 'git push <remote> <branch>' at ~line 919 was classified push.kind === 'diverged' (line 927). But a first push of a locally-created branch to an origin that does not have it should CREATE the branch, not fail. The doer must determine why runGitStep classified that push failure as 'diverged' when the remote ref was absent (read runGitStep's classifier), and fix the real cause -- e.g. the push failing because no upstream is configured and/or the classifier mapping that message to 'diverged'.
(b) Add a missing-remote-ref guard in the rebase path mirroring the EXISTING benign-skip already used by syncMemberBefore at ~line 800 (/couldn't find remote ref/i): if origin has no such branch there is nothing to rebase against, so skip the rebase and proceed to a real push that creates the branch. Factor the regex into one shared predicate used by both syncMemberBefore and syncMemberAfter rather than duplicating it.

Acceptance criteria:
- On a branch that exists locally but NOT on origin, syncMemberAfter completes with { ok: true, pushed: true } and the branch is created on the remote -- 'missing ref no longer throws' alone does NOT satisfy this; the push must succeed.
- The root cause of the 'diverged' classification for an absent remote ref is identified and addressed (in runGitStep's classification and/or the push command), and documented in a code comment at the fix site.
- Genuine non-fast-forward divergence (remote branch EXISTS and has diverged) still takes the existing one-bounded-pull-rebase path and still raises GitDivergedError when it remains rejected -- no weakening of the single-writer invariant.
- Tier 2 conflict-ladder behavior is unchanged.
- The 'couldn't find remote ref' predicate exists in exactly one place and is used by both bracket halves.
- npm test passes.

Note on criterion (a): if the actual control path to the pull-rebase turns out to differ from the hypothesis above, criterion (a) is satisfied by documenting the REAL path that produced the failure and fixing it wherever it lands -- the requirement is a diagnosed root cause, not this specific hypothesis.
Note on tests: also confirm packages/apra-fleet-se/test/mock-sprint-publish-push-failure.test.mjs (existing syncMemberAfter coverage) still passes; if it only runs in a slow/real-bd lane, run that lane for it explicitly.
close_reason: Diagnosed root cause (generic git push-rejection trailer text misclassifies a never-pushed branch's push as 'diverged'); added shared isMissingRemoteRefError() predicate used by both syncMemberBefore and syncMemberAfter; guarded the pull-rebase path to skip conflict-ladder machinery and retry the push directly when the remote ref is absent, creating the branch. Genuine divergence/Tier2 paths unchanged. npm test passes (only pre-existing unrelated golden-transcript drift fails).

title: [test] bdListScoped survives a transient bd timeout and still fails loud when retries are exhausted
description:
Unit test for apra-fleet-23j.1. Add tests in packages/apra-fleet-se/test/ (new file, e.g. 23j-bdlist-transient-retry.test.mjs, following the style of the existing 66u-stall-progress-credit.test.mjs which already exercises bdListScoped/scope-resolution with an injected command()).

What to test (vitest, injected fake command() -- no real bd, no network):
1. Transient-then-success: fake command() returns 'Command timed out after 120000ms of inactivity' on attempt 1 and valid bd JSON on attempt 2. Assert the call resolves with the parsed beads and that command() was invoked exactly twice.
2. Retries exhausted: fake command() always returns the transient text. Assert the call rejects, and that command() was invoked exactly the configured max attempts (no more) -- i.e. the failure is still fatal and bounded.
3. 'Failed to execute command on <member>' text is classified transient the same way as the timeout text.
4. Non-transient garbage output (e.g. 'not json at all') rejects on the FIRST attempt with the [bd JSON Parse Error] message and issues NO retry.
5. Regression guard: the retry path never substitutes an empty array for a failed scope query.

Acceptance criteria:
- All 5 cases present and passing via npm test (or the package's vitest invocation).
- Tests use injected fakes only; runtime under ~10s; no sleep-based flakiness (retry backoff must be injectable/short-circuited in tests).
- Test fails if the retry wrapper from 23j.1 is reverted.
6. Coverage of 23j.3: assert the converted call sites (the bd show / children lookups) also retry on the transient shape -- at minimum one test driving a bd-show-style call through the shared wrapper.

This task runs LAST in its streak (after 23j.1 and 23j.3), so the tests must be written against the fully-converted call sites.

title: [impl] Bounded retry + transient-error classification for bdListScoped's bd list calls
description:
Fix apra-fleet-23j: runner.js bdListScoped() (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js) feeds raw execute_command output straight into parseBdJson() with no retry, so a transient member-side bd/dolt slowness ('Command timed out after 120000ms of inactivity' / 'Failed to execute command on <member>') makes parseBdJson throw, the throw escapes runSprintCycle, and the whole sprint run dies.

Files to change (2): packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js (+ CHANGELOG.md entry).

Work:
1. Add an exported transient-bd-failure classifier (e.g. isTransientBdCommandFailure(raw)) matching the two observed non-JSON shapes: /Command timed out after \d+ms/i and /Failed to execute command on/i. Non-JSON output that does NOT match stays fatal immediately (no retry) -- garbage JSON is a real bug, not a transient.
2. Add a small bounded-retry wrapper used by BOTH bd-list call sites inside bdListScoped's closure: fetchAllBeadsShared() (~line 5065, 'bd list --all --limit 0 --json') and the filter query (~line 5152). 2-3 total attempts with backoff (e.g. 2s, 5s), logging each retry in the existing [Sync]/log style, mirroring updateDashboard's degrade-and-continue tone.
3. Do NOT change updateDashboard's existing non-fatal dashboard behavior, and do NOT convert exhausted retries into a silent empty list -- after the final attempt the error still propagates (scope resolution must never silently report 'no beads in scope').

Acceptance criteria:
- A bd list call whose first (and optionally second) attempt returns the timeout/'Failed to execute command on' text and whose next attempt returns valid JSON resolves successfully with the parsed beads, and the retry is logged.
- A bd list call that returns that transient text on EVERY attempt still throws (fatal), after exactly the configured number of attempts -- no infinite retry.
- Non-transient unparseable output throws on the FIRST attempt with the existing [bd JSON Parse Error] message; no retries are issued.
- Both call sites inside bdListScoped go through the wrapper (no remaining bare command()+parseBdJson pair in that closure).
- npm test passes.
close_reason: Implemented isTransientBdCommandFailure + bdListWithRetry wrapper for both bd-list call sites in bdListScoped; npm test passes (only pre-existing unrelated golden-transcript drift fails).

title: [regression][carry-over] Smoke-test toy sprint's Deploy phase fails EADDRINUSE on port 3001 when a prior interrupted run's toy dev server was never stopped
description:
Part: 2 (smoke test)
Expected: regression-test-playbook.md's Test scenario step 4 (apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint --max-cycles 1 against canary gh-toy-4ef) runs Deploy successfully, so Integration Test can attempt the canary; step 5's assertion (canary issue gh-toy-4ef closed, branch has a commit, ./tool --version prints 'fleet-e2e-toy v1.0.0' and exits 0) is met.
Actual: the toy sprint's Deploy C1 phase failed: 'npm run start:test' errored with EADDRINUSE on port 3001 because a stale toy-app dev server process (PID 93536, ts-node) survived from an earlier interrupted smoke-test attempt on the same fixed sandbox path (~/temp/.apra-fleet-tests). Deploy correctly refused to kill/reuse the pre-existing process (not its job) and stopped; Integration Test was skipped this cycle. Combined with the Develop/Review round cap (3) being reached within the single max-cycles:1 budget, the test child gh-toy-4ef.2 (Jest coverage for --version) never closed, so the canary epic gh-toy-4ef itself was left OPEN and the sprint's own Final Review verdict was FAIL. The underlying --version feature implementation (gh-toy-4ef.1) is correct and verified working directly (node dist/index.js --version -> 'fleet-e2e-toy v1.0.0', exit 0), so this is a smoke-harness robustness gap, not a product code defect in the deployed --version feature itself.
Root cause: regression-test-playbook.md's ## Setup section (fresh HOME wipe + reinstall) does not kill stray processes still bound to the toy app's dev-server port 3001 -- only ## Reset does that bounded lsof-kill-poll loop (apra-fleet-04g.7). If a previous attempt's Setup ran and its toy dev server was never torn down (e.g. this exact session resumed a partially-completed Setup/Test-scenario across a schema-validation retry without an intervening Reset/Teardown), the next Test scenario's Deploy inherits the stray port binding.
Test: apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint -i gh-toy-4ef -m toy-doer -b auto-sprint/regression-smoke -B main --max-cycles 1 --dispatch-timeout-s 900 (branch fix/runner-dolt-push-reliability @ 349e6743). Deploy C1 log: 'Deploy FAILED this cycle (C1): ... EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3001 ... PID 93536 ... Skipping Integration Test phase.' Final verdict: FAIL, canary gh-toy-4ef left open, sprint branch pushed with commits (e6a2d1a feat: add --version/-v flag, plus docs).
Repro: leave a toy-repo 'npm run start:test' (PORT=3001) process running from a prior attempt, then run ## Setup (fresh HOME/sandbox, no explicit port-3001 kill) followed by Test scenario step 4 -- Deploy's start:test step collides with the stray process.
Fix suggestion: either (a) add the same bounded lsof-kill-poll loop from ## Reset to the end of ## Teardown (so a torn-down run can never leave the port bound for the next Setup), and/or (b) add it to ## Setup itself as a defensive pre-check before the sandbox is (re)provisioned.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-08-09: STILL PRESENT on branch HEAD and origin/main; no fix commit exists ('git log --all --oneline -i --grep=cgc5' -> no matches). Read regression-test-playbook.md directly: the bounded lsof-kill-poll loop for port 3001 exists ONLY in '## Reset' (lines 204-235: 'PIDS=$(lsof -ti tcp:3001 ...)' with a 5s retry and a loud failure message). '## Setup' (lines 92-140) is just install/start/git clone/git config with no port-3001 pre-check, and '## Teardown' (lines 253-266) is only 'node dist/index.js stop' + 'rm -rf $SANDBOX' -- it never kills the toy app's dev server, so an interrupted or torn-down run can still leave PORT=3001 bound for the next Setup exactly as described. Did not re-run the toy sprint (expensive, and the repro needs a stray ts-node dev server). Fix is a copy-paste of the existing Reset block into Teardown (and defensively into Setup), a docs/playbook-only change with zero product-code risk. Classification: LOW-HANGING-FRUIT.
regression-test-runner 2026-08-19 Part 2 pre-Setup check: STILL REPRODUCES. Found a stray toy-app dev server bound to port 3001 (PIDs 24660/24661, ts-node under /Users/akhil/temp/.apra-fleet-tests/toy-repo, started 10Aug26) left over from a prior interrupted/non-torn-down attempt on the same fixed sandbox path. Recovered this cycle using the Reset section's own documented kill loop (lsof -ti tcp:3001 | xargs kill -9, bounded deadline) before Setup, then removed the stale sandbox dir. Same root cause, unaddressed. Carries over informational per regression-test-playbook.md.

title: [test] clean-pack size guard rejects an oversized package and accepts a small one
description:
Verification for apra-fleet-yj1.1/yj1.2 (and for the threshold-flag parsing hardening closed as apra-fleet-0v0.2/0v0.3, commit c1aff2b). Add tests/check-pack-size.test.ts (vitest), mirroring the existing tests/check-integ-suite-budget.test.ts pattern for script-level tests.

WHAT TO TEST (all against JSON fixtures / direct function calls, no npm invocation):

1. unpackedSize just above the 10000000 threshold -> non-zero exit / thrown failure, message contains the actual byte count and '::error::'.
2. unpackedSize just below the threshold -> success, no error emitted.
3. Regression guard for the original bug: a fixture whose human-readable notice would scrape to '4' but whose real unpackedSize exceeds the threshold MUST be rejected (this is the case the old grep arithmetic silently passed).
4. Malformed / empty / missing-unpackedSize JSON -> loud failure, not a silent pass.
5. Threshold flag equals form: parseThresholdArg(['--threshold=5000000']) returns 5000000, i.e. the equals spelling is honored and does NOT silently fall back to DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_BYTES (10000000). Assert the space-separated form ['--threshold','5000000'] still returns 5000000, and that an absent flag returns undefined so the env/default fallback still applies.
6. Explicitly-supplied unparseable or non-positive threshold ('--threshold abc', '--threshold=abc', '--threshold=0', '--threshold=-1') fails loudly: the parse throws / the script exits 1 with an '::error::' line naming the bad value, rather than silently running the guard at the default threshold.
Plus a source-literal assertion that .github/workflows/ci.yml no longer contains the 'grep -oE .[0-9]+.' PACK_BYTES arithmetic and does invoke check-pack-size.mjs.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:

- New test file with the four size/JSON logic cases, the two threshold-flag parsing cases (5 and 6), and the ci.yml wiring assertion; all pass via npm test.
- Tests import the parsing/threshold functions directly (or run the script with fixture input); they must not shell out to npm pack.
- Case 3 fails if the implementation reverts to scraping the human-readable notice.
- Case 5 fails if parseThresholdArg is reverted to recognising only the space-separated form; case 6 fails if an explicitly supplied bad value silently falls back to the default.
- ASCII only.
close_reason: Extended tests/check-pack-size.test.ts (33 tests, all passing) covering: checkPackSize threshold rejection/acceptance with byte count and ::error:: in message; regression fixture whose human notice scrapes to '4' but real unpackedSize exceeds threshold; malformed/empty/missing-unpackedSize JSON loud failures; parseThresholdArg (newly exported) equals-form/space-form/absent-flag cases; explicit bad --threshold values failing loudly both via direct calls and actual script child-process runs (exit 1, ::error:: naming the bad value); and source-literal ci.yml assertions (no grep -oE PACK_BYTES arithmetic, invokes check-pack-size.mjs). title: [impl] Scope install's running-process guard to the install target instead of OS-global process name
description:
Root-cause fix for apra-fleet-1aw: 'apra-fleet install' refuses to run whenever ANY apra-fleet process exists on the machine, even when the install is fully isolated by HOME/USERPROFILE/APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR (the shape used by ci.yml's 'Pack + install into a clean temp prefix (fleet-sprint smoke test)' step). That makes the step unreplayable locally on any dev box or self-hosted runner that already runs an apra-fleet server.

DESIGN (decided - do not re-open):
- Do NOT change isApraFleetRunning() itself. Four other call sites depend on its current OS-global semantics: src/cli/install.ts:751/755/760 (waitForApraFleetToStop) and :972 (post-kill recheck), and src/cli/uninstall.ts:303.
- Add a scoped pre-check used ONLY at the guard site (src/cli/install.ts around line 954). The guard must refuse ONLY when the running server is actually relevant to THIS install, i.e. either:
  (a) a live instance is recorded for the resolved data dir (server.json under APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR / homedir .apra-fleet/data - reuse the existing checkRunningInstance()/isPidAlive() machinery in src/services/singleton.ts rather than reimplementing pid liveness), OR
  (b) the running server's executable resides under the install prefix being written. This second condition is mandatory: the guard exists partly to prevent ETXTBSY on fs.copyFileSync when overwriting a binary that is currently open (see the comment above waitForApraFleetToStop). A data-dir-only check would silently let an install overwrite a live binary for a dev who overrides only APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR.
- If the scoped check says 'not relevant to this install', proceed with the install and print a one-line informational note naming the unrelated running server, instead of exiting 1.
- --force semantics are unchanged when the guard does fire.

FILES: src/cli/install.ts, plus at most one small helper module (new file or src/services/singleton.ts). Max 3 files.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- With an apra-fleet server running under the default HOME/data dir, an install run with an isolated HOME + APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR + install prefix completes successfully (exit 0) without --force and without killing the running server.
- With a live server recorded in the SAME APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR the install targets, the guard still fires with the existing 'apra-fleet is currently running' error and exit 1.
- With a running server whose executable is under the install prefix being written, the guard still fires even when the data dirs differ.
- isApraFleetRunning() keeps its current exported signature and global semantics; uninstall.ts behaviour is unchanged.
- npm run build and npm test pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: [test] mrj: createChildBeadWithAllocatedId creates with --id only, links parent via separate bd update
description:
[test] Verify apra-fleet-mrj fix: createChildBeadWithAllocatedId no longer sends --id and --parent together to bd create. On the allocator-granted explicit-id path it issues the create with --id ONLY, then records the parent edge with a SEPARATE bd update <id> --parent <parent>, and the created bead id equals the allocated childId. On the null-allocator path it uses --parent (no --id).

The fix has landed in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js (createChildBeadWithAllocatedId: parentageFlags = grant.childId ? --id <childId> : --parent <parentId>; explicit-id path follows with bd update <childId> --parent <parentId>). This task pins that behavior so the bug can be closed.

Confirm the suite asserts ALL of: (a) the explicit-id create carries --id <childId> and does NOT include --parent; (b) a separate follow-up command bd update <childId> --parent <parentId> records the parent edge; (c) the returned childId equals the allocator-granted id; (d) the null-allocator path uses --parent and returns childId null.

Both dispatches showed the same failure shape: the AGY provider stages the prompt as a .fleet-task.md file and instructs the model to 'read it, then execute', but the model looks for that file in /home/akhil/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch instead of the member's actual work folder (/home/akhil/git/fleet-lin-agy). list_dir on scratch returns empty, view_file on scratch/.fleet-task.md 404s, and the model falls back to 'find /home/akhil -name .fleet-task.md' -- the transcript ends there (search results not yet surfaced) rather than ever producing a direct reply to the prompt. Confirmed reproducible across two separate dispatches (cheap and standard tier), both fresh sessions (resume: false).

Likely root cause: src/providers/agy.ts writes/stages .fleet-task.md relative to the wrong base path (member work_folder vs the CLI's own scratch dir), or the invocation cwd passed to the agy CLI does not match where the file is staged.

Needs an AGY member to develop and test against -- this cannot be diagnosed or verified from a Claude-only session. fleet-lin-agy (registered 2026-08-03) is available for this.

Related: apra-fleet-qmb / apra-fleet-iuc.6 (AGY response/session-id capture) -- both need a live AGY dispatch to validate against real CLI output; this staging bug blocks getting a clean live transcript to validate against, so it may need to be fixed first.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh execute_prompt dispatch to an agy member (resume:false, no prior session) produces a direct reply to a simple non-tool-requiring prompt without the model needing to search for or failing to find .fleet-task.md; verified via a live dispatch (not a fixture), evidence includes the actual response transcript.
notes: Triage 2026-08-09 (iuc-agy batch): root cause fixed the day after this was filed. src/providers/agy.ts buildPromptCommand staged the task file with a RELATIVE instruction ('Your task is described in .fleet-task.md in the current directory'), which the AGY model resolved against its own scratch dir (~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch) rather than the member work folder. Commit de48e98c (2026-08-05, merged to main via #366) changed it to an absolute POSIX path: normalizedFolder = folder.replace(/\/g,'/'); fullPromptPath = path.posix.join(normalizedFolder, promptFile); instruction = 'Your task is described in <fullPromptPath>. Read that file first...' -- and the command still cds into the escaped work folder first. Pinned by tests/integration/agy-integration.test.ts: expect(cmd).toContain('Your task is described in /home/user/workspace/.fleet-task.md'). Live acceptance is also met by proxy: PR #383 (merged 2026-08-07) records live verification of a fresh dispatch plus context resumption against member fleet-lin-agy -- a fresh dispatch could not have produced a real reply if the model still could not find the task file. Closing as fixed; if a future live AGY dispatch reproduces the scratch-dir search, reopen THIS bead with the new transcript rather than filing a duplicate.
close_reason: Fixed by de48e98c (2026-08-05): the AGY prompt instruction now embeds the absolute /<work_folder>/.fleet-task.md path instead of a bare relative filename; pinned by tests/integration/agy-integration.test.ts and corroborated by PR #383's live fresh-dispatch verification on fleet-lin-agy.

title: [feature] Guarantee bd prime context reaches every fleet-sprint dispatched session (verify SessionStart hook or have agents call bd prime)
description:
## Problem

bd remember / bd prime is the intended channel for durable, cross-role operator knowledge (bd prime prints the "Persistent Memories" section). But its delivery to fleet-sprint dispatched roles is entirely convention-based today:

- runner.js never runs bd prime and never injects memories into dispatch prompts (verified: zero references in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js).
- Delivery relies solely on the target repo carrying a Claude Code SessionStart hook running bd prime (as this repo's checked-in .claude/settings.json does, and as packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/.claude/settings.json ships with 'bd prime --hook-json').
- A target repo missing that hook silently loses ALL persistent-memory context for every dispatched role -- no warning, no failure, just quieter agents. Non-Claude providers have no equivalent hook at all.

## Proposed fix (either or both; simple lift)

Option A (preferred, deterministic): add a preflight check to fleet-sprint's setup phase -- alongside the existing deploy.md / integ-test-playbook.md / regression-test-playbook.md existence checks -- that verifies the target repo's .claude/settings.json registers a SessionStart hook invoking bd prime. Emit a loud warning (or fail, behind a flag) naming the missing hook and the exact JSON to add. Zero prompt/token cost.

Option B (fallback / non-Claude providers): make dispatched agents always run bd prime themselves -- either a line in each role contract (packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/agents/*.md: "run bd prime before Step 1") or a standard preamble line the runner prepends to every dispatch prompt. Costs tokens per dispatch but works on providers without SessionStart hooks.

Recommendation: implement A as the gate, and B's prompt-preamble form only for members whose provider lacks hook support.

## Relationship to existing work

Complementary to apra-fleet-5fi (engine-side injection of role-prefixed doer-memory-*/reviewer-memory-* entries into dispatch prompts). 5fi filters and injects role-scoped memories; THIS bead guarantees the baseline bd prime context (all memories + workflow context) reaches sessions at all. If 5fi lands first, this bead still matters for the non-injected context bd prime carries and for repos/providers outside 5fi's injection path.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A sprint launched against a repo WITHOUT the bd prime SessionStart hook surfaces a clearly-worded warning (or a gated failure) in the setup phase output and on the dashboard, naming .claude/settings.json and the exact hook JSON to add.
2. A sprint launched against a repo WITH the hook produces no such warning.
3. If Option B is implemented: at least one dispatched role's transcript for a hook-less repo shows bd prime output present in-session (machine-checkable via the per-sprint log).
4. Unit test coverage for the preflight check (hook present / absent / malformed settings.json).
5. Doc update: the fleet-sprint docs README notes the hook as a recommended target-repo prerequisite.
notes: TRIAGE: Confirmed not implemented -- zero 'bd prime' or SessionStart-hook references in fleet-sprint/runner.js. The proposed Option A (preflight check) fits an existing, directly analogous pattern already in runner.js: probeFileExists('deploy.md')/'integ-test-playbook.md' checks at the setup phase (~line 7727-7728) that warn/log on absence rather than fail -- the bd-prime-hook check would read target repo's .claude/settings.json for a SessionStart hook the same way. Option B (prompt preamble) is a smaller independent fallback. Complementary to apra-fleet-5fi (also this batch) per its own description -- 5fi injects role-scoped memories, this guarantees baseline bd-prime context reaches sessions at all; neither blocks the other. Ready to implement, Option A first.

title: Cover createMemberVcsProviderResolver directly (cache-once, fail-closed, unregistered member)
description: apra-fleet-417.7 added createMemberVcsProviderResolver (runner.js ~line 1859) but every test for the provider threading injects a hand-rolled resolveMemberProvider, so the real resolver has zero direct coverage. Add unit tests with a stubbed callTool that assert: (a) the resolved provider is cached per member -- a second git failure for the same member issues no second VCSModule.resolveProvider lookup; (b) when resolveProvider throws (fleet unreachable, unregistered member with its typed 'ERROR:' response) the resolver returns undefined, logs, and caches the undefined so it is not re-queried; (c) the returned callback never throws. title: [regression][carry-over] run-integ-suites.mjs Part 1 blocked: stale integ-suite-status.json references retired/renamed test files, fail-loud with no non-destructive recovery
description:
Part: 1 (real-bd suite)
Expected: 'node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs --status' at the start of a fresh regression pass either reports a clean starting state or lets the runner safely resume/start the real-bd suite run per INTEG-SUITE.md steps 1-2.
Actual: --status exits 2 (fail-loud) with: 'status file integ-suite-status.json records results for files that no longer exist: dispatch-watchdog-timer-ref.test.mjs, mock-sprint-finalization-git-push-failure.test.mjs, part2-sha-freshness.test.mjs, predicted-context-split.test.mjs, mock-sprint-planner-dispatch-dead-pid.test.mjs, mock-sprint-planner-dispatch-stalled-session.test.mjs. The test directory changed mid-pass; use --fresh to start a new pass.' The leftover integ-suite-status.json (gitignored local state, timestamped 2026-07-31, from an earlier session/sprint) still names test files that have since been renamed/retired in packages/apra-fleet-se/test (per checkStale() in scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs). Per INTEG-SUITE.md step 1 and the script's own 'This is a fail-loud condition: file a bug bead, do not continue' message, this blocks running the real-bd suite for this regression pass entirely -- the only documented recovery is --fresh, which INTEG-SUITE.md explicitly reserves for a brand-new measured pass and the fail() helper's own boilerplate tells the operator not to self-heal past this without filing a bug first.
Test: node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs --status (step 1 of INTEG-SUITE.md) -- exit code 2, output above.
Repro: 1) Have an integ-suite-status.json at repo root recorded against an older packages/apra-fleet-se/test file set. 2) Rename/retire one or more *.test.mjs files in that directory (as happened here, e.g. mock-sprint-planner-dispatch-dead-pid.test.mjs retired per its own header comment). 3) Run 'node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs --status' -- checkStale() fails loud for ANY historical result naming a file no longer on disk, with no non-destructive way to reconcile an intentional/blessed rename short of --fresh (which discards all prior timing/result history). Consider: a --fresh invoked automatically only for the stale-file case (not corrupt JSON), or a --prune-stale mode that drops only the missing-file entries and keeps everything else, so a routine test-file rename between regression passes does not require filing a bug + always paying for a brand-new full timed pass.

Classification: READY-AS-IS (well-scoped script UX bug: add a --prune-stale mode or auto --fresh-on-stale-only). Subsystem: scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs.

Same root cause, unaddressed. Recovering via --fresh per the script's own message to proceed with this pass's Part 1 run.

title: Fix activeChannels leak paths in src/services/ssh.ts
description: src/services/ssh.ts:154-175: activeChannels is incremented before the Promise executor but released only via settle(), so a synchronous throw from client.exec() leaks the counter and makes the pool entry permanently unreapable (idle timer keeps re-arming). Also releaseChannel() re-resolves pool.get(key) and can decrement a newer entry it never incremented if the connection closed and a new entry was created for the same key in between -- can let a live channel be reaped. Capture the entry reference once and release it via a finally-equivalent path. From Opus PR-375 review, 2026-08-03.
notes: TRIAGE: confirmed still unfixed by reading src/services/ssh.ts:149-176. (1) poolEntry.activeChannels+=1 happens at line 169 right before client.exec() at line 234, but the intervening code runs inside a bare 'new Promise((resolve,reject)=>{...})' executor with no try/catch -- a synchronous throw from client.exec() would reject the promise (JS Promise-executor semantics) without ever calling settle()/releaseChannel(), permanently leaking the counter. (2) releaseChannel() (line 171-176) re-resolves pool.get(key) fresh instead of using the poolEntry reference captured at line 168, so if the connection closed and a new pool entry was created for the same key in between, release decrements the wrong (newer) entry's counter, exactly as described. Classification: LOW-HANGING-FRUIT -- fix is scoped (wrap client.exec in try/catch routed to settle(); capture and reuse poolEntry ref in releaseChannel).

title: install --force: scope pgrep/pkill to the current user
description: src/cli/install.ts:686 (pgrep -x apra-fleet) and :702 (pkill) match other users' processes. Combined with the new hard exit(1) at :970-979, install --force/update becomes unusable on a host where multiple fleet member accounts each run their own apra-fleet. Add -u "$(id -u)" to both pgrep and pkill, and add a test. From Opus PR-375 review, 2026-08-03.
acceptance_criteria: pgrep/pkill in the install --force stop path are scoped to the current user (e.g. pgrep -u $UID / pkill -u), never matching other users' apra-fleet processes. A same-named process owned by another user is NOT signalled. Change confined to the install --force path (src/cli/install.ts); existing single-user behaviour preserved.
notes:
Cross-reference: apra-fleet-fyc.2.5 found the same defect independently (isApraFleetRunning machine-wide guard, discovered via fyc.2.3's npm-publish install-gate test run). Fix once, close both.
TRIAGE: confirmed still unfixed -- grepped install.ts for '-u' scoping on pgrep/pkill (isApraFleetRunning:713, killApraFleet:729-730): none present, both remain machine-wide. The bead's own cross-reference note claiming fyc.2.5 fixed the same defect is INACCURATE: read commit 4cf0f369 (apra-fleet-fyc.2.5.1) directly -- it added classifyRunningServer()-based data-dir/install-prefix root scoping (addresses false-positive blocking across unrelated installs, apra-fleet-1aw) plus a --skip-running-check opt-out. It does not touch pgrep/pkill's OS-user scope at all; a same-user multi-install false-positive (fyc.2.5's target) is a different bug from a multi-account host where user B's process is detected but user A cannot kill it (this bead's target). Do not close as a dup of fyc.2.5. Classification: LOW-HANGING-FRUIT -- add '-u 197609' to both pgrep -x and pkill -x/-9 invocations plus a regression test.

title: bdListScoped() crashes the whole sprint on a transient bd-command timeout instead of retrying/degrading
description:
runner.js bdListScoped() (~line 5411, called from runSprintCycle ~7819) shells out 'bd list --all --limit 0 --json' to the dispatched member via execute_command and feeds the raw output straight into parseBdJson() (line 129) with no retry and no timeout-classification guard. When the member-side bd/dolt call is transiently slow or lock-contended (observed: 'Command timed out after 120000ms of inactivity' against a healthy, idle member -- bd responded normally seconds later), parseBdJson throws on the non-JSON 'Failed to execute command on ...' error text, and that throw is NOT caught -- it propagates out of runSprintCycle and crashes the entire WorkflowEngine execution ('Sprint failed'), losing all further progress for the run.

Contrast: the SAME bd-list-based dashboard refresh (updateDashboard's sprint-tree panel) hits the identical error and logs it as '(non-fatal, will retry next update)' -- i.e. the engine already has a proven graceful-degradation pattern for this exact failure, it's just not applied to the bdListScoped() call site used for real scope-resolution logic.

Observed: apra-fleet-417,apra-fleet-66u,apra-fleet-647.1,apra-fleet-647.1.1 sprint on fleet-win-dev1, 2026-08-03 ~09:00 UTC, crashed at the start of Review C1R1 after Develop C1R1 had already closed 3 real beads (417.2.1, 647.1.3.1, 647.1.1.1) -- that progress survived only because Dolt had already been pushed; a crash before push would have lost it outright.

Fix: give bdListScoped() (and any other non-dashboard bd-list call site sharing this pattern) a bounded retry (e.g. 2-3 attempts with backoff) on the 'Command timed out'/'Failed to execute command on' shape before treating it as fatal, mirroring updateDashboard's existing degrade-and-continue handling. Related to the broader class of health-check/diagnostic calls that assume success and crash ungracefully -- see apra-fleet-jmv, apra-fleet-ta3.
notes: TRIAGE: Real fix already written and committed -- 4904f1d7 'fix(fleet-sprint): bounded retry for transient bd-list failures in bdListScoped' + a4853b31 'extend transient bd-command retry to remaining call sites' (adds isTransientBdCommandFailure/bdListWithRetry, applied at bdListScoped's call sites) plus full unit coverage (96f6a039, eb37531b, f239cc75) -- all on origin/fix/runner-sync-ref-resilience, merge-base c8c92d6f (2026-08-04), never merged, no open PR (gh pr list empty). Current main/this-branch runner.js has NO bdListWithRetry/isTransientBdCommandFailure -- bug is still live here. Action: cherry-pick or PR the existing branch rather than re-implementing. Labeled low-hanging-fruit (fix exists, just needs landing).

title: [bug] G-push pull-rebase fails with 'couldn't find remote ref' when the sprint branch hasn't been pushed to origin yet
description:
Found live 2026-08-03: Set 3 sprint (l7n cluster, fleet-lin-dev1, branch fix/dispatch-stall-reliability), Develop C1 R1, doer streak [apra-fleet-0v0.1].

Doer dispatch completed and closed apra-fleet-0v0.1 successfully, but the post-dispatch G-push failed:
  [Sync] G-push pull-rebase for member 'fleet-lin-dev1' failed: [Command Failed] Exit code 1: Exit code: 1
  [stderr]
  fatal: couldn't find remote ref fix/dispatch-stall-reliability

Root cause (likely): the pull-rebase step assumes origin already has the sprint branch, but on a fresh sprint the branch is only created locally by branch-ensure and doesn't get pushed to origin until the FIRST successful git push -- so any pull-rebase attempted before that first push has nothing to rebase against. This mirrors the same class of bug as apra-fleet-jmv (finalizeAbort's git rev-list crashing on a nonexistent ref) -- multiple call sites in runner.js assume a sprint branch exists on origin without checking first.

Fix: before pull-rebase, check whether origin/<branch> exists (git ls-remote or fetch + rev-parse --verify); if not, skip the rebase (nothing to rebase against) and proceed straight to push. Likely worth doing together with apra-fleet-jmv and the broader apra-fleet-417/647.1 VCS/dolt-sync call-site consolidation, since this is exactly the class of "does the ref exist before I operate on it" gap that refactor is meant to close.

Evidence: sprint log at C:\Users\akhil\.apra-fleet-se\logs\apra-fleet-l7n_apra-fleet-3c9_apra-fleet-6a7_apra-fleet-y8q_apra-fleet-63x_apra-fleet-107_apra-fleet-9zz-f43c9bac-e540-46e8-a8b6-611e12280070.log

Current main/this-branch runner.js's G-push pull-rebase path (~line 941-999) still has no isMissingRemoteRefError guard -- bug is still live here. Action: land the existing branch/commit rather than re-implementing. Labeled low-hanging-fruit.

title: [impl] Stall-abort message must match the evidence, not assert the verifier is failing
description:
FILES: packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js -- the stalled-sprint abort message builder (around the `Closed-bead count history (per cycle evaluation)` / `High-water-mark closed count` lines, currently ~4390-4425).

WORK: Distinguish two different facts in the abort message instead of conflating them:
- "closed count did not increase across N cycles" (progress fact), versus
- "verify-routed beads were dispatched to Integ Test N times and produced ZERO closures" (verifier fact).
Only emit the "the verifier may be failing" wording when the second condition actually holds. When Integ Test dispatches DID close beads, say so explicitly and list the unclosed verify-set ids without editorializing.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Message text is derived from counters that separate dispatch-with-closures from dispatch-without-closures.
- In the bead's real scenario (dispatches closed beads), the message does not claim the verifier may be failing.
- Message stays ASCII-only.
- `npm test` green.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-09 (backlog reprioritization): ALREADY-FIXED. The abort-message split landed on origin/main via de48e98c (integration branch, PR #366) and is present in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js today: verifyDispatchAttempts/verifyDispatchClosures counters are declared at runner.js:6004-6014 with an explicit apra-fleet-66u.2 comment, incremented at runner.js:8156-8168 against live scoped closed-state (closedIdsNow), and the abort builder at runner.js:8198-8222 only emits the 'verifier may be failing' wording when (verifyDispatchAttempts > 0 && verifyDispatchClosures === 0); otherwise it emits the neutral 'N verify-routed bead(s) remain unclosed: <ids>'. It also now lists only STILL-open verify ids rather than the monotone verifyEverIds set, fixing the incident wording that named 33c/jfo/gd0 as never-closed. ASCII-only, message text verified by reading. Covered by packages/apra-fleet-se/test/66u-stall-progress-credit.test.mjs cases (b) and (c), which I ran green (3/3 pass, node --test, 9.6s). Closing as fixed.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Akhil Kumar
comments.text:
Implemented: the abort message now derives verifySuffix from two things instead of blindly dumping verifyEverIds (runner.js Cycle Evaluation, near the StalledSprintError throw):

1. Only the STILL-open verify-routed beads are named (a live check against fetchAllBeadsShared(), same pattern as the existing stillOpenVerifyIds check a bit further down) -- verifyEverIds is monotone and never drops a closed id, so dumping it directly named beads that had closed cycles earlier as 'never closed'. This is the exact wording bug that shipped in the real 2026-08-02 incident: it named apra-fleet-33c/jfo/gd0 as 'never closed' when all three had closed back in Cycle 1.

2. The 'the verifier may be failing' wording is now gated on two new per-sprint counters, verifyDispatchAttempts and verifyDispatchClosures (tracked once per cycle, right after the closedCount read, reusing the already-fetched snapshot -- no extra bd call): only emitted when Integ Test was actually handed a non-empty verify set at least once AND never once closed anything it was asked to verify. When some closures did happen but others remain open, the message now reads '<N> verify-routed bead(s) remain unclosed: <ids>.' without the verifier-blame editorializing.

Regression coverage: packages/apra-fleet-se/test/66u-stall-progress-credit.test.mjs, scenario (b) ('verify-routed beads dispatched repeatedly with zero closures triggers a real stall whose message correctly blames the verifier') exercises the TRUE branch end-to-end via the mock-sprint harness (real bd, recorded fixture). Scenario (a) exercises the no-stall path where the message never fires at all. The FALSE branch (closures occurred, stall for an unrelated reason, message must not blame the verifier) was attempted as a third e2e scenario and dropped as too fragile to keep reliable within this harness's single-epic-target structure -- see 66u.3's comment for the full reasoning; that branch is covered by direct code review of the boolean gate instead.

comments.author: Akhil Kumar
comments.text:
Reworked per independent Opus review (2026-08-04): the verifyDispatchAttempts/verifyDispatchClosures counters (and the pre-existing stillOpenVerifyIds/finalUnclosedVerifyIds checks from apra-fleet-jfo) read fetchAllBeadsShared()'s cached snapshot, which is NOT refreshed by a bdListScoped() call and can be stale by a full cycle in a topology with no dolt sync remote (doltPullBefore/After are both benign no-ops there) -- the integ runner's own bd close happens inside an agent() dispatch, never through the cache-invalidating command() wrapper. Confirmed this made the new counters' freshness claim false exactly as the reviewer predicted.

Fix: all verify-closure freshness checks (the new counters' closedThisDispatch check, the abort message's stillOpenVerifyIdsForAbort, the exit-gate's stillOpenVerifyIds, and Final Review's finalUnclosedVerifyIds) now read a single fresh bd list --status=closed --json per check-site (reusing the SAME already-fresh read that feeds closedCount where possible) instead of the cache. This also strengthens the pre-existing jfo mechanism, not just the new 66u.2 code.

See apra-fleet-66u.1's comment for the related exit-gate scope-filtering fix and the mid-cycle verifyEverIds gap this also surfaced and fixed.

title: [bug] finalizeAbort's abort-diff diagnostic crashes when the sprint branch was never created (git rev-list on nonexistent ref)
description:
Found live 2026-08-03: Set A sprint (apra-fleet-417/66u/647.1/647.1.1 on fleet-win-dev1, branch feat/taskdb-vcs-module-auth-abstraction) aborted at the Beads Health preflight gate before branch-ensure ever ran, so the sprint branch was never created locally or pushed to origin.

finalizeAbort()'s abort-path diagnostics then tried to compute a commit-count diff for the abort record:
  git rev-list --count origin/<base>..<branch>
This failed with "fatal: ambiguous argument ... unknown revision or path not in the working tree" since <branch> doesn't exist anywhere yet. The error was caught and logged ("[Terminal History] finalizeAbort() failed for this abort ... writing the terminal history record with no PR lookup"), so the sprint still terminated cleanly overall -- this is non-blocking, diagnostic-only breakage, not a sprint-killing bug.

Fix: before running the rev-list, check whether <branch> exists locally (or was ever created), and skip/zero the commit-count diagnostic gracefully (commitCount: 0 or null) rather than letting the git command throw. Likely near the same finalizeAbort() code path apra-fleet-tfx.8/647.1.1 already touch (Publish/Abort PR wiring), so worth sequencing alongside that work rather than as a fully separate task.

Evidence: sprint log at C:\Users\akhil\.apra-fleet-se\logs\apra-fleet-417_apra-fleet-66u_apra-fleet-647.1_apra-fleet-647.1.1-6bca3037-64f9-43c7-a37b-4a7c58a84e95.log
notes: TRIAGE: Confirmed still open and unaddressed, including on the sibling origin/fix/runner-sync-ref-resilience branch which fixed the closely-related ta3/23j bugs but does NOT touch finalizeAbort's rev-list path. Current code (runner.js ~4358-4379): finalizeAbort always runs 'git fetch origin <baseBranch>' then 'git rev-list --count origin/<baseBranch>..<branch>' and throws CommandError on failure (caught non-fatally by the outer abort-catch site today, per bug's own report, so this is diagnostic-only breakage, not sprint-killing). No guard exists for <branch> never having been created locally. Straightforward fix, same technique ta3's isMissingRemoteRefError/branch-exists check already demonstrates -- check local branch existence (or catch 'unknown revision') before the rev-list and return commitCount:0/null gracefully. Labeled low-hanging-fruit.

title: TaskDBModule needs an explicit second-backend interface contract, mirroring 647.1's day-one multi-provider VCS scoping
description:
Found by backlog-groomer research pass, 2026-08-02; narrowed by the operator 2026-08-03; acceptance criteria repaired by a scoped replan 2026-08-03 after a reviewer flagged them as unsatisfiable as written.

BACKGROUND

apra-fleet-647.1 (VCSModule) scopes multi-provider support from day one -- GitHubVCS and GenericGitVCS as concrete implementations at launch, AzureDevOpsVCS/BitbucketVCS/GitLabVCS as named follow-ons, with an explicit acceptance criterion that 'adding a new provider requires touching no file under packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/'.

apra-fleet-417 (TaskDBModule) originally had no equivalent. That asymmetry has since been closed: commit 073a1dd landed docs/adr-taskdb-backend-neutral-interface.md, which records (Decision 2) the backend-neutral TaskDBModule vocabulary -- ensureReady / refreshView / syncBefore / syncAfter / flush / repair / status plus capabilities() -- (Decision 3) a method-by-method walk-through of Jira and generic-git-issues as candidate second backends, and (Decision 4) the 647.1-equivalent extensibility criterion: 'adding a new task-tracking backend requires touching no file under packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/ other than adding one new concrete module.'

REMAINING DELTA (this is the whole of the work left on this bead)

Per the operator note of 2026-08-03, the second-backend question was narrowed from the generic Jira/Azure-Boards/generic-git-issues framing to one concrete research question: evaluate Azure DevOps Boards, driven through the az CLI (az boards work-item create/show/update, az boards query), as the candidate second concrete TaskDBModule backend. This is a RESEARCH/feasibility spike -- interface fit, auth model, rate limits, and whether Azure Boards can be expressed without leaking Azure-specific vocabulary through the skin-gut interface. It is NOT an implementation task: do not build a stub backend, and do not write production code.

Do NOT re-derive the contract that the ADR already records. The job is to test that landed contract against Azure Boards and to confirm or amend it.

FILES: none -- this task modifies no file in the repository. Deliverables are recorded ON this bead (apra-fleet-417.1) via 'bd update --design' (use --append-notes if you add notes; never --notes, which replaces the operator's directive). Do not edit runner.js, do not edit any file under packages/apra-fleet-se/, do not edit docs/adr-taskdb-backend-neutral-interface.md, and do not edit the parent epic apra-fleet-417.

See the ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA field of this bead for the definition of done.
design:
RESEARCH SPIKE RESULT -- Azure DevOps Boards (via az CLI) as the SECOND concrete
TaskDBModule backend. Design-only; no code, no stub, no file changed.

== 2. EVIDENCE BASIS (stated first so every claim below is read against it) ==
Findings are derived from the DOCUMENTED az CLI command surface from model
knowledge (az devops extension: `az boards work-item create|show|update|delete`,
`az boards work-item relation add|remove|show`, `az boards query --wiql`,
`az boards area/iteration project list`, `az devops login`, `az devops configure
--defaults organization= project=`), plus DIRECT READS of this repository for the
auth half: src/tools/provision-vcs-auth.ts and src/services/vcs/azure-devops.ts.
NO live az trial was run: `az --version` in this environment returns
"az: command not found", and no Azure DevOps tenant is available. Per AC item 2 a
live trial is optional; the findings stand on the documented surface alone. No
numeric rate-limit constant is asserted below, because none can be cited from a
live source here.

== 1(a) INTERFACE FIT -- the seven methods + capabilities(), one line each ==
Contract under test: docs/adr-taskdb-backend-neutral-interface.md Decision 2.

1. ensureReady() -> one cheap authenticated probe, `az boards query --org <org>
   --project <proj> --wiql "SELECT [System.Id] FROM workitems"` (or `az devops
   project show`); ready:true, else degraded.kind 'auth' (TF400813 / login
   required), 'no-store' (TF200016 project does not exist), 'store-unreachable'
   (DNS/5xx). No local view to reconcile. Fully expressible.
2. refreshView({purpose}) -> no-op returning {fresh:true}: every read is a live
   REST call behind az, so the view is never stale; may return
   degraded.kind:'transient' on 429/5xx. May invalidate a local id cache.
   Fully expressible.
3. syncBefore(worker,{skipRefresh,readinessGate}) -> no-op returning {ok:true};
   there is no per-worker clone to freshen. skipRefresh is honored trivially;
   readinessGate reduces to the cached ensureReady() verdict. Fully expressible.
4. syncAfter(worker,{mutatedItemIds}) -> the substantive method: one `az boards
   work-item update --id <id> --fields ...` per id (and `az boards work-item
   create` for ids new this cycle). CANNOT EXPRESS (two gaps): (i) there is NO
   batch/transactional command -- publication is per-item and non-atomic, so a
   cycle can end half-published; (ii) `az boards work-item update` exposes no
   revision/ETag/if-match option, so the ADR's "one bounded reconcile" degrades
   to re-read via `az boards work-item show` + re-apply, i.e. last-writer-wins,
   with no way to detect that a concurrent writer won. Retry on transient with
   backoff; on auth, re-provision once and retry.
5. flush() -> retry only the ids still marked unpublished in the per-item
   ledger. There is NO whole-state publish, so a later success does not carry
   earlier failures -- this backend is exactly the case mutatedItemIds and
   capabilities().wholeStatePublish were added for. Fully expressible.
6. repair(worker) -> credential re-provision (redeploy the PAT, see 1(b)) plus a
   connectivity retest. CANNOT EXPRESS: there is no recovery-ladder / Path-B
   re-clone analogue, because there is no local wedged state to unwedge; repair
   is auth-only and never returns an escalation dump.
7. status(worker) -> ledger snapshot plus last known reachability; issues no az
   command and never throws. Fully expressible.
8. capabilities() -> declared descriptor for an AzureBoardsTaskDB:
   { wholeStatePublish: false,
     supportsRepair: 'auth-only',
     supportsCoordinationLock: false,
     kinds: ['transient','auth','store-unreachable','no-store','unknown'] }
   Justification against the ADR's eight-kind taxonomy: 'conflict-resolvable'
   and 'conflict-unresolvable' are UNREACHABLE (a remote-first store has no
   divergence and no merge); 'coordination-unavailable' is unreachable because
   the backend is never asked to take a lock (see supportsCoordinationLock
   below); 'no-store' IS reachable and is kept, unlike the ADR's Jira row --
   az reports a missing org/project distinctly (TF200016) and conflating that
   with 'store-unreachable' would make a permanent misconfiguration look
   retryable. supportsCoordinationLock:false because Azure Boards offers no
   server-side lock primitive comparable to the Dolt push mutex; serialization,
   if wanted, is the orchestrator's job, not the backend's.

== 1(b) AUTH MODEL ==
Three candidates. RECOMMENDED: PAT.
- PAT (recommend): az reads it from AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT, or interactively via
  `az devops login --organization <org_url>` (PAT on stdin). Non-interactive,
  scopeable to Work Items (read/write), revocable, and it is ALREADY a
  first-class credential in this repo: src/tools/provision-vcs-auth.ts:45
  accepts provider 'azure-devops', :62/:85 take org_url + pat (with
  {{secure.NAME}} resolution from the credential store, :100), and an OOB
  prompt at :123-128 when the pat is absent.
- az login (interactive AAD / device code): unusable unattended for fleet
  members; refresh depends on a browser-backed token cache.
- Service principal (`az login --service-principal`) with the SP added to the
  Azure DevOps org: the correct long-run answer for CI-grade identity, but it
  needs tenant-side setup that provision-style handling does not model today.
FLOW THROUGH PROVISION-STYLE HANDLING -- and the ONE REAL GAP:
src/services/vcs/azure-devops.ts:19 currently deploys the PAT via
`gitCredentialHelperWrite('dev.azure.com', '', pat, label, scopeUrl)` -- that is
a GIT credential, consumed by git over https to dev.azure.com. The az CLI does
NOT read the git credential helper; it wants AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT (or the
`az devops login` token cache). So the credential PLUMBING is already there and
the secret is already stored and revocable, but an AzureBoardsTaskDB adapter
needs the same stored PAT surfaced a second way (env var injected into the az
child process, or an `az devops login` step in ensureReady()). That is an
adapter-local concern -- it changes no interface method -- but it is real work
and must not be assumed free because 'azure-devops' already appears in
provision_vcs_auth.

== 1(c) RATE LIMITS / THROTTLING for per-cycle sprint sync ==
Mechanism (documented behavior; no numeric constant asserted here): Azure DevOps
Services applies per-organization/per-identity consumption limits measured in
throughput units, first by INJECTING DELAY into responses and then, past the
threshold, by returning HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header; rate-limit state is
also advertised on normal responses via X-RateLimit-* style headers. Two
consequences specific to this design: (1) az surfaces neither Retry-After nor
the rate-limit headers to the caller -- an adapter shelling out to az sees only
a nonzero exit and stderr text, so backoff must be a fixed exponential schedule
classified as 'transient', not a Retry-After-honoring one; (2) the per-item,
process-per-call shape of syncAfter (one az invocation per mutated id, each a
full CLI start plus auth) makes throttling MORE likely per unit of work than a
batched REST client would, so a large cycle should be chunked and paced. For
realistic per-cycle sprint volumes (tens of mutated items) throttling is
unlikely to bind; the risk is a bulk backfill or a repair storm, not steady
state.

== 1(d) VOCABULARY LEAKAGE ==
Verdict: Azure-specific vocabulary can be kept OUT of the interface, and the
exact place it pushes against it is nameable.
- The seven methods are SYNC-LIFECYCLE ONLY; none of them is item CRUD. For the
  Dolt adapter `bd` performs the writes and the module merely publishes. An
  az-CLI adapter IS the writer, so it must supply, at write time: work-item type
  (`--type`, mandatory on `az boards work-item create`), area and iteration path
  (`--area` / `--iteration`), and a target state for transitions
  (`--state`, constrained by the project's process state model).
- The pressure point is therefore syncAfter(worker,{mutatedItemIds}): ids alone
  do not carry enough information to write an Azure work item. This does NOT
  require a signature change and MUST NOT get one -- the fix is adapter-owned
  CONSTRUCTION-TIME configuration (organization, project, default work-item
  type, area/iteration path, and a task-state -> Azure-state map), exactly as
  the Dolt adapter takes remote/branch configuration. Adding
  `workItemType`/`areaPath` to any interface parameter would be the leak, and is
  rejected here.
- Second, smaller point: Azure work-item ids are org-global integers while the
  current backend's ids are strings. mutatedItemIds must stay typed as OPAQUE
  strings; the integer mapping is adapter-local ledger state.
- No other leak found: the failure taxonomy, capabilities() and the remaining
  six methods are expressible without naming Azure.

== 3. GO / NO-GO ==
GO -- Azure DevOps Boards is a suitable backend #2. Single strongest reason: it
is the cheapest FALSIFIABLE second backend available to this repo, because the
credential half already exists as a first-class provider (provision-vcs-auth.ts
'azure-devops' + services/vcs/azure-devops.ts) while its physics are the exact
opposite of Dolt's (remote-first, per-item, no whole-state publish, no merge),
so implementing it actually exercises the neutral seam instead of re-confirming
Dolt's shape. (Strongest counterweight, recorded honestly: no atomic or
optimistic-concurrency write primitive in `az boards work-item update`, so
syncAfter's bounded reconcile is last-writer-wins -- acceptable for a
single-orchestrator sprint, and it must be written down in the adapter, not
papered over.)

== 4. CONTRACT CONFIRM-OR-AMEND ==
The ADR's Decision 2 / 3 / 4 contract does NOT hold entirely unchanged for an
AzureBoardsTaskDB: it holds subject to ONE amendment, required by this spike's
capabilities() descriptor in 1(a).
- WHERE: Decision 2, the capabilities() paragraph (adr-taskdb-backend-neutral-
  interface.md lines 90-92), which describes "the booleans wholeStatePublish,
  supportsRepair, supportsCoordinationLock". An AzureBoardsTaskDB cannot declare
  supportsRepair as a boolean: its repair() is credential-only (no recovery
  ladder, nothing local to unwedge), which is neither true nor false. Decision
  3's own Jira row already declares supportsRepair:'auth-only', so Decision 2's
  wording is inconsistent with Decision 3 today, and Azure is the second
  backend that needs the third value -- evidence the tri-state is structural,
  not a one-off.
- REPLACEMENT WORDING for that clause: "...plus the booleans wholeStatePublish
  and supportsCoordinationLock, and supportsRepair, which is one of true (full
  recovery ladder), false (no remediation) or 'auth-only' (credential
  re-provisioning and a connectivity retest only, with no local state to
  unwedge)."
- Decision 4's criterion SURVIVES this amendment unchanged: "adding a new
  task-tracking backend requires touching no file under
  packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/ other than adding one new concrete
  module." The amendment widens the value domain of one descriptor field that
  each backend module declares about itself; it adds no dispatch point, no
  runner.js literal, and no shared file a new backend would have to edit beyond
  the one manifest line Decision 4 already allows.
- No method name and no parameter name changes are needed. In particular the
  three Decision 2 renames (skipRefresh, mutatedItemIds, readinessGate) are all
  CONFIRMED by this spike: mutatedItemIds is load-bearing for Azure exactly as
  predicted for Jira, and skipRefresh/readinessGate are honored trivially by a
  remote-first backend.
- Because the recommendation is GO, no alternate candidate backend is required
  by AC item 4; the ADR's existing secondary candidate (generic git-issues)
  stands unchanged.

== 5. POINTER ==
Interface contract of record: docs/adr-taskdb-backend-neutral-interface.md
(Decision 2 = the seven methods + capabilities(); Decision 3 = the Jira /
generic-git-issues walk-through this spike parallels for Azure Boards;
Decision 4 = the extensibility criterion and the task-db-backends/ registry
shape). 417.2.x should follow that ADR plus the amendment in item 4 above.

== 6. NO CODE, NO FILE CHANGES ==
This spike modified no file in the repository -- not runner.js, not anything
under packages/apra-fleet-se/, and not the ADR itself. All deliverables are on
apra-fleet-417.1. The parent epic apra-fleet-417 was not edited.

title: [impl] Compose createScopeGuard into the live POST /api/sprints beforeLaunch guard
description:
The issue-scope overlap guard (packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/scope-overlap.mjs createScopeGuard, returning { checkLaunch, formatScopeConflict }) is documented in docs/architecture.md as an active launch guard but is never wired live: bin/serve.mjs (~L240-L246) constructs createSprintController() WITHOUT a beforeLaunch override, so it falls back to defaultMemberOverlapGuard alone (packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/api.mjs L140/L306). Only the member axis is guarded; two sprints with disjoint members but overlapping/nested issue scopes can both launch against the same beads.

Fix: in bin/serve.mjs, build a composed beforeLaunch and pass it as deps.beforeLaunch into createSprintController(). The composed guard must run BOTH: (1) the existing defaultMemberOverlapGuard(ledger, listMembers) fn (member axis), and (2) createScopeGuard({ ledger }).checkLaunch(issueRoots) (issue axis) -- beforeLaunch is invoked as beforeLaunch({ members, issueRoots }); call checkLaunch with issueRoots and, when result.ok is false, throw an Error whose message is formatScopeConflict(result.conflicts) so the launch rejects with the same shape the member guard uses. Reuse the same ledger already passed to the controller. Order: preserve member-guard behavior; either guard failing rejects the launch. This matches api.mjs's own header comment (eft.5.2/eft.5.3) describing the two guards as meant to compose. Update packages/apra-fleet-client if any request/response surface changes (none expected -- internal wiring).

Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/serve.mjs (compose + inject beforeLaunch); import createScopeGuard from src/supervisor/scope-overlap.mjs.

DONE / ACCEPTANCE:
- createSprintController() in bin/serve.mjs is constructed with an injected beforeLaunch that composes defaultMemberOverlapGuard AND createScopeGuard's checkLaunch over the same ledger.
- A POST /api/sprints whose issueRoots overlap or nest with an already-active sprint's live-expanded scope is rejected (even when member sets are disjoint), with a message from formatScopeConflict naming the conflicting sprint(s) and overlapping bead ids.
- Member-overlap rejection behavior is unchanged; a launch that overlaps on neither axis still succeeds.
- Existing supervisor api / scope-overlap unit suites still pass.
close_reason: Round-3 review addressed: extracted the beforeLaunch member+scope guard composition into an exported composeBeforeLaunch() in bin/serve.mjs (behavior unchanged) and added 3 regression tests in supervisor-skeleton.test.mjs proving disjoint-member/overlapping-scope rejection (409 field=issue), member-axis-first ordering (scope guard never runs once member guard rejects), and pass-through when neither axis overlaps. title: Supervisor POST /api/sprints/:id/stop returns 500/ECONNREFUSED for a terminal-but-lingering sprint child
description: Reproduced twice independently this session (apra-fleet-vak's dead-child scenario, and apra-fleet-fyc-e9cfc4b6-... just now): when a sprint child has already reached a terminal state (FAILED/plan-rejected) and is in its post-terminal dashboard-linger window (process still alive, but its embedded HTTP dashboard server on the viewer port -e.g. 8082- has already closed), calling POST /api/sprints/:id/stop tries to proxy/signal the child via that port and gets ECONNREFUSED, surfacing as a raw 500 to the caller instead of a clean 'already terminal, nothing to stop' response. Supervisor's own log: '[supervisor] request POST /api/sprints/<id>/stop failed: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8082'. Separately, GET /api/sprints/:id also threw a generic {"error":"internal supervisor error"} for the same sprint in this window (worth checking if it is the same root cause or a distinct one -- both were observed on a supervisor process that turned out to be running STALE code, ~11.5h old, predating today's cvb/ed4 merges, so re-verify against a freshly-restarted supervisor before concluding this is unfixed by ed4's retry work). Fix direction: the stop handler should check watchdog-classified terminal status (or PID liveness + last-known-terminal history record) BEFORE attempting to proxy the port, and return a clean no-op success/'already terminal' response rather than shelling out to a port that may legitimately already be closed in this window.
notes: CONFIRMED still reproduces on a freshly-restarted supervisor (uptime seconds, not hours) running today's latest merged code -- rules out staleness as the explanation. GET /api/sprints/:id and POST .../stop both return {"error":"internal supervisor error"} for a sprint that has reached a terminal state (this time GitDivergedError) and is in its 300s post-terminal dashboard-linger window. Confirms the fix needs to check watchdog-classified terminal status before touching the child's viewer port, not assume the supervisor process being 'fresh' avoids it.

title: [test] ed4: atomic-rename persist retries transient EPERM/EBUSY and never drops an audit event
description:
Verification for apra-fleet-ed4 (depends on ed4.1). Deterministic unit test -- no real sleeps, no real Windows needed -- exercising the EPERM/EBUSY retry via dependency injection.

New test file (follow the epic naming convention): packages/apra-fleet-se/test/ed4-atomic-rename-retry.test.mjs. Do NOT edit existing test files, test/helpers/, or test/fixtures/.

What to test (inject a fake deps.fs whose rename() is a stub, plus injected retry timing so no real backoff sleeps occur):
1. Transient recovery: rename() throws {code:'EPERM'} on the first N-1 attempts then resolves; assert persist() ultimately succeeds, the on-disk (in-memory fake) content is the fully-written document, and the audit event is NOT lost. Assert rename was called N times.
2. Same assertion for {code:'EBUSY'}.
3. Non-transient error passthrough: rename() throws {code:'ENOSPC'} (or any non EPERM/EBUSY); assert persist() rejects immediately with that error and does NOT retry (rename called exactly once).
4. Exhaustion: rename() always throws EPERM; assert persist() rejects after the bounded number of attempts (last error re-thrown), and rename call count equals the configured bound.
5. Happy path unchanged: rename() succeeds first try -> exactly 1 rename call, no delay.
Cover both createHistory (history.mjs) and the ledger.mjs persist path (or the shared helper if ed4.1 factored one) so both callers are proven.

title: [impl] ed4: bounded EPERM/EBUSY retry around atomic tmp-write+rename in supervisor persistence
description:
Fix apra-fleet-ed4: on Windows, fs.rename() in the tmp-write-then-rename atomic-replace pattern can fail with EPERM/EBUSY when the destination file is momentarily locked/open by another process, silently dropping a durable audit event (observed live 2026-08-01 on a watchdog history.record(AUTO_RELEASED)).

Files to change (all within the cvb footprint packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/**):
- packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/history.mjs: wrap the fs.rename(tmpPath, filePath) step in persist() (~line 137) with a bounded retry.
- packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/ledger.mjs: apply the identical retry to persist()'s fs.rename (~line 362) -- same tmp-write-then-rename gap.
- Prefer factoring a single tiny shared helper (e.g. renameWithRetry(fs, tmp, dst, opts)) rather than duplicating the loop; keep it inside supervisor/** (a new small module under src/supervisor/ is acceptable). Max 3 files.

Behaviour:
- Retry ONLY on err.code === 'EPERM' || err.code === 'EBUSY' (transient Windows locking). Re-throw immediately on any other error code.
- Bounded: a few attempts (e.g. up to 5) with a small backoff (e.g. ~10ms escalating). After the final attempt, re-throw the last error so a genuinely stuck rename still surfaces.
- Retry timing must be injectable/overridable so tests need no real sleeps (e.g. accept a sleep fn or attempt/delay opts via the injected deps).
- fs.rename must remain injectable exactly as today (deps.fs.rename) so the retry is unit-testable.

Also do the declared sweep: confirm ledger.mjs is the only OTHER supervisor tmp-write+rename path; note (in the bead/commit, not by editing out-of-footprint files) if packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/viewer persistState paths share the gap so a follow-up can be filed -- do NOT edit files outside the cvb footprint.

Acceptance criteria:
- history.mjs and ledger.mjs persist() rename steps retry on EPERM/EBUSY and succeed once the lock clears; non-EPERM/EBUSY errors are NOT retried and propagate unchanged.
- Retry count is bounded and the last error re-throws after exhaustion.
- No behavioural change on POSIX / when rename succeeds first try (same number of rename calls: exactly 1).
- npm run build passes; ASCII only.
