title: history.mjs atomic-rename persist can EPERM on Windows, silently dropping an audit event
description:
Observed live on supervisor restart (2026-08-01, after merging apra-fleet-cvb.1/.2/.3/.4 + gey.1's watchdog auto-release fix, apra-fleet-0j1):

  [watchdog] auto-released reservation for 'apra-fleet-cvb-e04f499d-6f61-4679-bbc0-78ff4580b465' (status=finished, exited 1 at ...)
  [error] [watchdog] history.record(AUTO_RELEASED) failed for 'apra-fleet-cvb-...': Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename 'C:\Users\akhil\.apra-fleet-se\sprint-history.json.tmp' -> 'C:\Users\akhil\.apra-fleet-se\sprint-history.json'
    at async Object.rename (node:internal/fs/promises:781:10)
    at async persist (file:///C:/akhil/git/apra-fleet/packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/history.mjs:137:9)

The auto-release itself succeeded (the reservation was correctly cleared -- confirmed via GET /api/members immediately after), but the durable AUTO_RELEASED audit event failed to persist because the tmp-write-then-rename pattern in history.mjs's persist() hit EPERM on Windows. This is a known Windows quirk: fs.rename() (and the underlying MoveFileEx) can fail with EPERM/EBUSY if the destination file is open/locked by another process at the moment of rename (e.g. something still had a read handle on sprint-history.json), which is far more common on Windows than POSIX since Windows enforces mandatory file locking by default.

Impact: this is not data corruption (the tmp file write itself presumably succeeded, only the rename failed) but it means an operator-facing history/audit trail can silently lose an entry on Windows specifically, with only a console.error and no retry -- worth confirming whether persist() retries on EPERM/EBUSY or gives up on the first attempt (a quick read of history.mjs's persist() suggests it does not retry).

Fix: add a short bounded retry (a few attempts with a small backoff) around the rename step specifically for EPERM/EBUSY on Windows, since these are frequently transient (the locking process releases its handle within milliseconds). This is the same class of Windows-specific file-handling gap already seen elsewhere in this codebase (see apra-fleet-2cc's shell:true / execFileSync Windows issues) -- worth a broad sweep for any other tmp-write-then-rename persistence path in the supervisor (ledger.mjs, run-state-paths.mjs) that might have the identical gap, not just history.mjs.
close_reason: integ-test-runner: re-verified on branch fix/supervisor-lifecycle-correctness-2 @ 70268838. Ran packages/apra-fleet-se/test/ed4-atomic-rename-retry.test.mjs directly (node --test): 10/10 pass, covering both history.mjs createHistory() and ledger.mjs createLedger() persist() rename paths -- transient EPERM recovery, transient EBUSY recovery, non-transient ENOSPC passthrough (1 call, no retry), bounded exhaustion (last error re-thrown), and unchanged happy path (1 call, no delay). Also ran the full apra-fleet-se suite (npm test): 1716 pass / 2 fail, both failures confined to test/serve-wiring-integration.test.mjs, a pre-existing unrelated flaky dashboard-render timing issue already tracked under apra-fleet-ryk (P3) -- no history.mjs/ledger.mjs persist failures anywhere in the run. Defect no longer reproduces; closing.

title: Document the beads conventions fleet-sprint requires beyond stock bd
description:
A stock `bd` install does NOT satisfy what fleet-sprint requires. Every convention below is a planner-authored layer on top of stock beads, and all of them are currently IMPLICIT -- discoverable only by reading runner.js and the vendored role prompts. A third-party project cannot comply with an undocumented contract.

REQUIRED CONVENTIONS TO DOCUMENT

1. Per-bead model tier: --metadata '{"model":"cheap|standard|premium"}' on EVERY task. plan-reviewer.md returns CHANGES_NEEDED without it -- buildPlanReviewerPrompt() instructs the reviewer to reject a plan "as missing model metadata". These three keywords are the fixed vocabulary; they resolve per-member server-side.

2. Lane / streak metadata: --metadata '{"streak":"<lane-id>","streakOrder":<n>}'. The engine reads b.metadata.streak for DETERMINISTIC streak grouping; its doc comment notes "A partly-laned plan counts as 'no lane metadata'", in which case the engine silently degrades to the LLM-based streakAssignment path. Ordering is "within a lane by numeric streakOrder".

3. Size buckets S/M/L with the fixed effort formula (S=1 / M=2 / L=4 multiplied by cheap=1 / standard=10 / premium=20, threshold 200). Hardcoded in planner.md / plan-reviewer.md prompt text, not parameterized.

4. Title tags the engine and roles match on: [impl], [test], [integ], and "[regression][carry-over]" (the engine even tells operators to re-check with: bd search "[carry-over]").

5. issue_type vocabulary task | feature | bug, with a hard dispatch rule: buildPlannerPrompt() states "Doers can only claim issue_type=task beads" and requires any open bug-type bead in scope to be decomposed into task children "including a [test] task where the fix is testable". The engine also derives pendingClosureBugs client-side by filtering b.issue_type === 'bug' && b.status === 'open' with all children closed.

6. Priority format P0-P4, and the sprint goal band as 'P1' | 'P1/P2' | 'P1/P2/P3' (GOAL_PATTERN; default 'P1/P2'). The reviewer prompt uses the band to defer below-goal work: "Features/beads BELOW the goal priority ... are DEFERRED BY DESIGN".

7. Sprint scope is resolved PARENT-CHILD ONLY. blocks/blocked-by edges do not define scope. A blocks edge between a parent and its own child deadlocks the sprint -- the engine detects this specific case and offers `bd dep remove` fixes.

8. .beads/ must live at the ORCHESTRATOR's repo root, not inside a track worktree.

NON-FINDING (record so it is not re-investigated): `bd remember` telemetry key patterns are NOT used by fleet-sprint at all. Grep across the package finds them only in apra-pm/.claude/workflows/auto-sprint.js and apra-pm/skills/pm/cost.md.

DELIVERABLE
A "beads project contract" doc under packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/ that a third-party project can follow, plus a pointer to it from the fleet-sprint README/skill.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Each convention above is documented with the exact bd command that satisfies it.
- Where the engine DEGRADES rather than fails (e.g. missing streak metadata -> LLM grouping), the doc says so.
- A reader can bootstrap a compliant beads DB for a fresh project without reading runner.js.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-09 (batch 647): LOW-HANGING-FRUIT -- pure documentation, zero code change, no design decision outstanding, and the bead already contains the researched content; it is close to a write-up of its own description. Nothing is implemented: no beads-contract doc exists under packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/ (only coach-role-design, dolt-tier2-runbook, fleet-sprint-diagram, README, stabilization-log) and fleet-sprint/docs/README.md covers only invocation/arguments/preconditions. Spot-verified the load-bearing claims at source so the author can trust them: convention 1 -- runner.js:2733 and :2753 still have plan-reviewer rejecting beads 'as missing model metadata'; convention 2 -- runner.js:2894 still carries the doc comment 'A partly-laned plan counts as "no lane metadata"' and :2917/:2935 read b.metadata.streak for deterministic grouping; convention 5 -- runner.js:2651 still states verbatim 'Doers can only claim issue_type=task beads'; the recorded NON-FINDING also still holds, grep -rn 'bd remember' over packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/ returns zero hits. ONE CORRECTION for the author: convention 5's second half is stale -- the client-side pendingClosureBugs derivation described in the bead was replaced (runner.js:7853, 'apra-fleet-jfo: replaces the old bug-only pendingClosureBugs'), so the doc must describe the CURRENT verify-set behaviour rather than the bug-only filter, and should be re-read at that call site before writing. Labelling low-hanging-fruit. No 'auto-sprint' misnaming: the two 'auto-sprint' strings in this bead are the real path packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/.claude/workflows/auto-sprint.js (confirmed to exist) and apra-pm/skills/pm/cost.md, both correct as literal file references.

title: De-apra-fy the regression role contract and regressionReport schema
description:
Distinct from the playbook-documentation bead: this is ENGINE and CONTRACT structure, not documentation. apra-fleet's own product and test vocabulary are baked into a role contract and an output schema as if they were generic structure.

EVIDENCE (verbatim)

1. apra-pm/agents/regression-test-runner.md embeds apra-fleet's literal CLI health check as if it were what a Setup verify step IS:
     "the Setup verify step (node dist/index.js status reporting the server up on the scratch port)"
   `node dist/index.js status` is apra-fleet's own command. No other project has it.

2. The same file's role description asserts apra-fleet's test structure as THE shape of a regression pass:
     "the real-bd functional suite plus the toy-sprint smoke test"
   and its steps are named accordingly:
     "## Step 1 -- Run Part 1: the real-bd suite"
     "## Step 2 -- Run Part 2: the sandbox smoke test"
     "Run the playbook's real-bd suite section (the heading naming the product's ...)"

3. It is not just prose -- the two-part split is baked into the CONTRACT:
   - fleet-sprint/contracts.mjs: the regressionReport schema REQUIRES suitePassed and smokePassed.
   - runner.js -> buildAnalysisText() emits:
       `Regression pass: ... (real-bd suite: ${...}, smoke test: ${...}).`
   - runner.js's regression error handlers construct fallbacks of the same shape, e.g.
       regressionResult = { passed: false, suitePassed: false, smokePassed: false, bugsFiled: [], summary: ... }
   A project whose regression pass is not two-part must therefore LIE in its schema fields.

DECISION REQUIRED (pick one, then implement):
  (a) Generalize: replace suitePassed/smokePassed with `parts: [{ name, passed }]` in the regressionReport schema, in buildAnalysisText()'s rendering, and in every fallback construction; strip the apra-fleet literals from regression-test-runner.md and describe the parts abstractly.
  (b) Keep two parts as a HARD project contract -- but then say so explicitly in the playbook-seam contract doc (sibling bead), and still strip `node dist/index.js status` from the role prompt.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- regression-test-runner.md contains no apra-fleet-specific command or product noun.
- Whichever option is chosen, the regressionReport schema and the playbook-seam contract doc agree with each other.
- The apra-fleet regression-test-playbook.md at repo root still passes unchanged in substance (it may be re-headed if option (a) renames sections).

Resolves the structural half of review finding MAJOR-7.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-09 (batch 647): NEEDS-DEEPER-DESIGN -- not blocked on evidence (all of it re-verified as still true today) but on the owner's (a)-vs-(b) ruling, which a doer cannot make because it changes a versioned output contract. Re-verified: fleet-sprint/contracts.mjs:523-536 still declares suitePassed/smokePassed as boolean properties AND lists both in required: ['passed','suitePassed','smokePassed','bugsFiled','summary']; runner.js:3986-3987 still renders 'real-bd suite: ... , smoke test: ...' in buildAnalysisText(); and all four regression fallback constructions (runner.js:8836, 8839, 8847, 8850) still hardcode { suitePassed:false, smokePassed:false }, with 8792 logging '(suite: ..., smoke: ...)'. apra-pm/agents/regression-test-runner.md is unchanged too: line 3 frontmatter description still says 'the real-bd functional suite plus the toy-sprint smoke test', line 112 still names apra-fleet's own CLI health check ('node dist/index.js status' reporting the server up), and Steps 1/2 at lines 84/103 are still titled after the two apra-fleet parts. Practical suggestion for whoever schedules this: the two halves are separable and only ONE half needs the ruling. Stripping 'node dist/index.js status' from the role prompt and describing the Setup verify step abstractly is required under BOTH option (a) and option (b) and is a genuinely small, unambiguous change -- consider splitting it into a child bead that can ship immediately, leaving the schema question (parts:[{name,passed}] vs a documented hard two-part contract, plus its OUTPUT_SCHEMA_MAJOR implications and the regression-test-playbook.md re-heading) as the part that waits on the decision. Also worth deciding jointly with apra-fleet-647.3, since option (b) explicitly discharges its obligation into 647.3's playbook-seam contract doc. No 'auto-sprint' naming issue in this bead's text.

title: Document the playbook seam contract (required sections, discovery, absence) and ship starter templates
description:
SCOPE NOTE (owner ruling, 2026-07-31): this is NOT about making the apra-fleet playbooks generic. deploy.md / integ-test-playbook.md / regression-test-playbook.md at this repo's root are SUPPOSED to be apra-fleet-specific and are correct as-is -- they demonstrate how the system works. Every type of project will have a different playbook; some will need other members to deploy the software or to test it. What is missing is (a) the SECTION CONTRACT the roles hard-require, and (b) starter templates so a third-party project can get going.

PROBLEM 1 -- REQUIRED HEADINGS ARE LOAD-BEARING LITERAL STRINGS, DOCUMENTED NOWHERE.
The vendored role prompts read specific `##` headings out of the playbooks. Verbatim:
  apra-pm/agents/deployer.md:
    "Read `deploy.md`. Look for a `## Permissions` section. If found, verify each"
    "1. Read `deploy.md` -- understand the Deploy, Smoke test, and CI sections"
    "2. Execute every command in the `## Deploy` section in order"
    "3. Run the command in `## Smoke test`"
  apra-pm/agents/integ-test-runner.md:
    "Read `integ-test-playbook.md`. Look for a `## Permissions` section. If found,"
  apra-pm/agents/regression-test-runner.md:
    "Read `regression-test-playbook.md`. Look for a `## Permissions` section. If"
    "Bring the sandbox up with the playbook's `## Setup` section, run the playbook's `## Test scenario` inside it, then ALWAYS run `## Teardown`"
    "Confirm the playbook's `## Teardown` has run"
A third-party author has no way to learn that `## Teardown` is a load-bearing string.

PROBLEM 2 -- DISCOVERY PATH IS UNDOCUMENTED.
runner.js -> probeFileExists() dispatches
  `node -e "console.log(require('fs').existsSync('${filename}') ? 'found' : 'not found')"`
called as probeFileExists('deploy.md'), probeFileExists('integ-test-playbook.md'), probeFileExists('regression-test-playbook.md') -- BARE filenames resolved against whatever cwd the member dispatch lands in. The engine never states the contract. The only hint anywhere is one hedged sentence in apra-pm/skills/pm/sprint.md: "present in the worktree (or repo root / docs/)" -- three alternatives, no precedence. Pick one, document it, and consider an ordered search path (./ then docs/).

PROBLEM 3 -- ABSENCE SEMANTICS ARE UNDOCUMENTED (but already correct; document as a FEATURE).
The probe is failSoft, so it can never kill a sprint. Phases skip with e.g.
  "Skipping Deploy Phase (no deploy.md found, or the probe itself failed -- see prior log line)"
  "Skipping Integration Test Phase (no playbook found, or the probe itself failed -- see prior log line)"
  "Skipping Regression Test Phase (no regression-test-playbook.md found, or the probe itself failed -- see prior log line)"
and the roles refuse to improvise (deployer.md: "do not improvise deploy steps that are not written down in the runbook").

PROBLEM 4 -- AN ENTIRE ROLE AND PLAYBOOK ARE ABSENT FROM THE ROLE ROSTER.
regression-test-runner and regression-test-playbook.md appear in NO role roster: absent from packages/apra-fleet-se/docs/overview.md, docs/architecture.md, and every SKILL doc. An undocumented ninth role.

DELIVERABLES
- A playbook-seam contract doc under packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/ specifying, per playbook: required headings, optional headings, which role consumes each, discovery path and precedence, and absence semantics.
- Starter TEMPLATES (skeleton headings, empty bodies) a project copies and fills in -- plus an explicit note that a playbook may legitimately dispatch OTHER MEMBERS (e.g. a device flasher, a different-OS test host).
- Add regression-test-runner and regression-test-playbook.md to the role rosters in docs/overview.md and docs/architecture.md.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Every `##` heading a role reads is listed in the contract doc, and the doc is the source cited by the role prompts.
- Templates exist for all three playbooks and a fresh project using them passes each phase's probe.
- A reader can determine, without reading runner.js, where to put a playbook and what happens if they omit one.
- Role rosters name all dispatched roles.

Resolves review finding MAJOR-6 (revised per owner ruling) and the docs half of MAJOR-7.

title: integ-test-runner is a structural no-op when a sprint's scope has zero type=feature beads
description:
Found via forensic analysis of the win-dev1 sprint (apra-fleet-xuo, 2026-07-31): integ-test-runner ran 4 times across cycles C2-C5 (22-76 min each -- real wall-clock cost) and closed ZERO features every single time, not because of any bug in its own logic but because this sprint's entire scope tree (all 34 beads under apra-fleet-xuo) is type=task or type=bug -- there are no type=feature beads anywhere in scope. integ-test-playbook.md's procedure scopes itself via 'bd list --type=feature --status=open', so with no features present it is structurally guaranteed to find nothing, every cycle, for the life of the sprint.
Expected: either (a) the planner/orchestrator recognizes a sprint has zero features in scope and skips dispatching integ-test-runner for it (saving the real per-cycle wall-clock cost -- 22 to 76 minutes observed here), or (b) integ-test-runner's mandate is broadened to also verify/close completed type=task work under some criteria, if that is the intended coverage gap this sprint fell into.
Actual: integ-test-runner is dispatched and burns real time every cycle regardless, producing a predictable no-op result.
Impact: pure wasted wall-clock/cost on a task/bug-only sprint -- reference apra-fleet-63x (integ-test-runner routinely burns 15-85min per dispatch) for related cost concerns.

description:

2. The single-sprint viewer's extension area (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/viewer-extensions.mjs) -- one bar for the sprint currently being viewed.

title: [test] check-watchdog-isolation.mjs entrypoint guard runs main() as a spawned CLI on Windows
description:
Pins the fix from apra-fleet-xuo.10 so the silent-pass regression cannot return.

WHAT TO TEST: spawn scripts/check-watchdog-isolation.mjs as a real CLI child process (node <script> ...), as tests/check-sandbox-sync-remote-integ.test.ts does for the analogous xuo.8 fix -- do NOT import the module, since importing bypasses the very guard under test.

TEST LOCATION: tests/check-watchdog-isolation-integ.test.ts (repo convention: script CLI/integration specs live under tests/ with the -integ.test.ts suffix, e.g. check-sandbox-sync-remote-integ.test.ts, check-toy-doer-credentials.test.ts). Framework: vitest, run via npm test.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. A spawned invocation of the script produces non-empty stdout/stderr proving main() ran -- asserting on output presence, not just exit code, since the defect was 'prints nothing and exits 0'.
2. The exit contract holds both ways: exit 0 only on a genuine PASS path, and NONZERO on the failure path (drive the script into a failing/invalid-argument condition and assert the nonzero code). A silent exit 0 for an arbitrary argument must FAIL the test.
3. The test fails against the pre-fix guard (file-colon-slash-slash string comparison) and passes against the pathToFileURL guard -- state in the test how that was confirmed.
4. Windows-path safe: no assumptions about forward-slash-only paths; ASCII only; the suite leaves no stray files/handles behind (cleanup verified).
5. npm test stays green overall.

title: [impl] Fix check-watchdog-isolation.mjs entrypoint guard to use pathToFileURL
description:
SOURCE (not new scope): this item is recorded verbatim in apra-fleet-xuo's own NOTES as a reviewer-proposed newTask from cycle 3 that was REJECTED only by the title safe-character allowlist bug since fixed by apra-fleet-19o.1; apra-fleet-19o.2 exists precisely to resurface such items into the next planning dispatch. Dedup check performed: bd search 'watchdog-isolation' (status all) returns no issues; bd search 'entrypoint guard' returns only the closed xuo.8.x / 2cc.x beads for OTHER scripts. Defect re-verified live at scripts/check-watchdog-isolation.mjs:161.

DEFECT: line 161 uses if (import.meta.url === file-colon-slash-slash + process.argv[1]), which never matches on Windows (argv[1] is a native path, so the built string has two slashes vs import.meta.url's three). main() therefore never runs: the script prints nothing and exits 0 for ANY argument -- the same silent-pass defect apra-fleet-xuo.8 was filed for. Independently verified during review that this is the ONLY remaining offender across scripts/ (grep of process.argv[1] confirms every other script already uses the pathToFileURL form).

FILES: scripts/check-watchdog-isolation.mjs (single file).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. The file imports { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url' and the guard reads exactly: process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href -- matching the shipped fix in scripts/check-toy-doer-credentials.mjs:772 and scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs:576.
2. Running 'node scripts/check-watchdog-isolation.mjs' on Windows actually executes main() (it produces output) instead of exiting 0 silently.
3. PASS CONDITION, not a note: after the guard starts firing, run the vitest suites that cover this script and confirm they stay GREEN. Lesson from apra-fleet-xuo.8.1: once the guard is fixed, main() runs for the first time, which on Windows can leave file handles open in whatever sandbox it touches and break a test's cleanup. Do not assume the one-line change is inert; if a suite breaks, fixing that fallout is part of THIS task.
4. ASCII only; no unrelated refactors.
close_reason: Fixed pathToFileURL entrypoint guard; verified main() executes on Windows; full vitest suite green (199 files, 2812 tests passed).

title: Integ Test Part 2 pass/fail rests entirely on agent self-report; no machine-checkable artifact, unreliable on empty-response/timeout, never confirmed on Windows
description: Per a 2026-07-31 deep-dive follow-up audit of the Integ Test phase's Part 2 (the real toy-app smoke-test sprint): Part 2 HAS been confirmed to complete and pass, repeatedly (verified across historical run logs -- mac1.json, lhf-batch-b.json, sprint_121333.json -- plus a hand-run confirmation documented in docs/eft64-harvest-non-hosted-remote-smoke-evidence.md), correcting an earlier, thinner reading. However every PASS verdict found rests ENTIRELY on the integ-test-runner agent's own self-reported JSON -- there is no independent, machine-checkable artifact backing it. The engine's only automated check is that a deployedSha is present (validates freshness, not correctness; part2-sha-freshness.test.mjs pins only this). No run log captures the actual --version stdout, a bd show gh-toy-4ef status transcript, or the toy-repo's real commit SHA as a structured, independently-verified field. The self-report channel is also demonstrably unreliable: roughly 6 of ~20 historical Integ Test dispatches returned null/empty (max_turns exhaustion, empty_response, or a 60-minute inactivity timeout), and at least one PASS verdict arrived via a 19-second schema-repair retry dispatch that nonetheless claimed a fresh, complete end-to-end Part 2 run -- a claim with no way to be independently verified true. Additionally: Part 2 has never been confirmed to pass on Windows (the only Windows dispatch found died at spawnSync bd ENOENT before reaching Part 2; every confirmed pass is on fleet-mac or fleet-rev), and integ-test-playbook.md's Reset section is hard-bash/lsof-based, not Windows-portable. Fix: have the runner emit captured --version stdout, the bd show gh-toy-4ef status line, and the sprint branch's head SHA as structured, engine-validated fields (the same treatment deployedSha already gets under eft.55) rather than trusting free-text agent narrative alone.
notes:
CROSS-REFERENCE 2026-07-31 (integ/regression split, apra-fleet-t4p): Part 2 moved out of the per-cycle Integ Test phase into regression-test-playbook.md, run once per sprint by the new 'regression-test-runner' role. PARTIALLY ADDRESSED: the new agents/schemas/regression-test-runner-output.json declares an optional structured 'smokeEvidence' object with three fields intended to be exactly the machine-checkable artifact this bead asks for -- versionStdout (verbatim stdout of the toy CLI --version on the sprint branch), canaryStatus (the status from bd show gh-toy-4ef), and toyRepoHeadSha (the toy repo head SHA after the toy sprint) -- alongside separate suitePassed/smokePassed booleans instead of one blended 'passed'. NOT YET ADDRESSED, still the open work here: (a) nothing in the engine VALIDATES smokeEvidence -- the fields are requested and carried, but a report omitting them or filling them with plausible fiction is still accepted, so the pass verdict still ultimately rests on self-report; (b) the deployedSha freshness check that was the only automated check is now RETIRED for this path (validatePart2Evidence has no engine call site; the regression phase provisions its own sandbox and has no deploy target to attest against), so there is currently LESS automated checking than before, not more; (c) Windows confirmation is unchanged/unconfirmed. Note also the phase is soft-fail by design and never gates the sprint, so a silently-degraded Part 2 is now even less likely to be noticed -- which raises, not lowers, the priority of making the evidence machine-checked.
TRIAGE: Confirmed via contracts.mjs (line ~465) and test/regression-phase-never-gates.test.mjs: validatePart2Evidence/extractPart2Sha were deliberately REMOVED as consumer-less dead code during the integ/regression split, and a regression test now actively guards against re-adding either without an engine call site. smokeEvidence IS present as an optional structured field in agents/schemas/regression-test-runner-output.json and regression-test-runner.md, but nothing validates/enforces it -- pass verdicts still rest on self-report. This matches the bead's own notes exactly; the remaining gap (wiring real engine-side validation for a sandbox with no deploy target to attest against, plus Windows confirmation) requires actual design work, not a quick fix. Classification: NEEDS-DEEPER-DESIGN. Subsystem: regression-test-runner / Part 2 evidence.

title: fleet-sprint viewer: duration formatting (h/m/s) inconsistent -- closed/parent activities show raw seconds instead of formatted duration

The currently-running activity (e.g. the live "Develop R1 C3" row) correctly shows a human-readable h/m/s duration, but previously-closed parent/activity rows instead show a raw seconds value (e.g. "6390s"), causing visual inconsistency and making completed-phase durations harder to read at a glance. However this split is INTENTIONAL, not accidental: the eft.45.1 comment at line ~633-645 explicitly says formatTime's decimal form 'is reserved for the completed-duration label' and deliberately chose formatUptime only for the live-tick case. The identical split also exists in the phase-header duration code (eft.53.2, same file ~417-441) with matching test assertions (viewer-phase-duration-dom.test.mjs) that lock in '5.0s'/'42.0s' decimal output for completed phases. Still low-hanging-fruit given the small blast radius, but flagging the design-intent tension for whoever picks it up.

title: Integ Test phase part 1 (129-file real-bd suite) runs every cycle for ~55min and has never caught a product regression -- gate to once-per-sprint or CI
description: Assess-first: verify this is still true before implementing -- re-check the last few completed Integ Test runs' filed bugs. Per an independent audit of integ-test-runner (2026-07-30, read integ-test-playbook.md + packages/apra-fleet-se/apra-pm/agents/integ-test-runner.md + 4 completed historical sprint runs -- lhf-batch-a, lhf-batch-b, mac1 C4/C5, plus live apra-fleet-fyc): Part 1 (scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs, 129 real-bd files, APRA_FLEET_BD_MOCK=off) takes ~55 minutes wall-clock per cycle (3353s/3377s observed vs. INTEG-SUITE.md's stated ~7min expectation) but its ~10 filed [integ] bugs across all read runs are almost entirely ABOUT the suite itself (timeouts, concurrency contention, a test mocking the wrong field) rather than product regressions -- contrast with Part 2 (the real toy-sprint smoke test) and the install/launcher bugs, which caught 4 real P0s nothing else would have. Fix direction: run Part 1 once per sprint (or move it to CI) rather than once per develop/review cycle, recovering most of the phase's per-cycle cost without losing its (currently near-zero) marginal per-cycle signal.
notes:
AMENDED 2026-07-31 after a rigorous follow-up audit (operator pushed back hard on the original framing -- correctly). Original justification below was partly wrong and is corrected here; the fix DIRECTION survives but is now three-tier, not a flat "cut it."

Corrections to the original claim:
- "Has never caught a product regression" is FALSE as stated. apra-fleet-eft.16 (29/74 files failing on a real runner.js doltPullBefore() defect) and apra-fleet-eft.17.3 (still open -- a real, currently-live mode-dependent divergence the bead itself documents as "passes in mock mode, fails in real mode") are both genuine product findings from Part 1 that mock mode structurally cannot produce (mock mode synthesizes dolt-sync brackets as clean no-ops, per bd-replay.mjs).
- Accurate framing: Part 1's MARGINAL value over the mocked run is narrow (the project's own test/TEST-VALUE-ANALYSIS.md measured the mocked suite at ~95-98% of full protection, and that 95-98% figure is why bd-replay.mjs was built on 2026-07-17) -- but that narrow slice (real bd-CLI integration behavior) is currently tested NOWHERE else. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs replay-only with an UNPINNED bd install -- zero real-mode coverage exists outside this per-cycle phase today.
- Part 2 (the toy smoke-test sprint) is credited elsewhere with "4 P0s" -- the real number from the closed-bead record is closer to 20 (eft.19/20/24/28/29/30/47/48/50/51/61/63/64/65/82/84/86/87, 04g.1/04g.4, 9te.3/9te.4). This makes reclaiming Part 1's per-cycle time budget to protect Part 2 a STRONGER argument, not a weaker one -- Part 2 is where almost all the real yield is.

Corrected fix direction (three-tier, not a flat cut):
1. Full 129-file suite in MOCK mode every cycle (already effectively free, this is just npm test).
2. A ~14-file verb-covering REAL-bd lane every cycle: analysis of 6,793 recorded bd invocations found they collapse to only 38 distinct bd command shapes, and a cost-weighted set-cover of ~14 scenario files covers all 38 shapes using only ~17.5% of the real-bd work (~1,188 of 6,793 calls). This preserves ~100% of bd-shape-drift detection at a fraction of the 55-minute cost. Needs re-measurement against a fresh integ-suite-status.json (none currently exists on disk -- see the P1 recordings-drift bead) before finalizing the exact file list.
3. The full 129-file suite in REAL mode once per sprint, AND/OR a new nightly/scheduled CI job -- NOT "or move it to CI" as originally worded, since no such CI job currently exists (grep for test:integration/APRA_FLEET_BD_MOCK across .github/workflows/ returns zero matches). Building that job (with a PINNED bd version, see the companion P1 bead) is a hard precondition for removing Part 1 from the per-cycle loop, not an optional alternative -- without it, gating Part 1 takes real-bd testing from once-per-cycle to zero, not once-per-sprint.

See also (filed alongside this amendment): a new P1 bead on bd-recordings staleness/CI real-mode coverage, and a new P2 bead on Part 2's pass/fail currently resting entirely on agent self-report with no machine-checkable artifact.
RE-SCOPED 2026-07-31 by the integ/regression split (apra-fleet-t4p, branch worktree-agent-a2ebeb95110de8719). The CADENCE half of this bead is now DONE: Part 1 (the real-bd suite) no longer runs per cycle. It moved, together with Part 2 (the toy-sprint smoke test), out of integ-test-playbook.md into the new repo-root regression-test-playbook.md, owned by the new once-per-sprint 'regression-test-runner' role and dispatched by a new Regression Test phase in the Finalization group (runner.js, between Final Review and Harvest; mirrored in apra-pm's auto-sprint.js between the final-review gate and Harvest). The per-cycle Integ Test phase is now feature closure only.

REMAINING WORK for this bead, narrowed: Part 1's FILE SELECTION inside the new playbook. Even at once-per-sprint cadence the suite is ~55 minutes of wall clock and a large share of its historical [integ] bugs are about the suite itself (timeouts, concurrency contention) rather than product regressions. Decide which of the 129 real-bd files genuinely need the real bd CLI vs. which are adequately covered by replay mode, and shrink/split accordingly. Do NOT re-litigate cadence -- that is settled.
TRIAGE: Notes already narrowed scope (integ/regression split, apra-fleet-t4p) -- cadence is settled (Part 1 now runs once/sprint via regression-test-runner, not per-cycle). Remaining work is purely file-selection research: which of the 129 real-bd files need the real bd CLI vs. adequately covered by mock/replay. No further code verification possible without running the analysis described (cost-weighted set-cover over 6793 recorded bd invocations). Classification: NEEDS-RESEARCH-ONLY. Subsystem: integ/regression-test-runner.

title: createChildBeadWithAllocatedId: bd create fails combining --id and --parent flags
description: Discovered while verifying apra-fleet-f34.3: fleet-sprint/runner.js's createChildBeadWithAllocatedId() (line ~2511) always issues 'bd create ... --parent <parentId> --id <allocatedChildId>' when the id-allocator grants a childId. Against the currently installed bd CLI this errors with 'cannot specify both --id and --parent flags', so the create fails, the allocator reservation is released (non-fatal, degrades to parent-bead notes per persistNewTaskBestEffort), and the allocated id is never actually applied to the created bead. Reproduced live in packages/apra-fleet-se/test/f34-concurrent-launch-engagement-integration.test.mjs (both topologies) -- search its captured stderr for 'cannot specify both --id and --parent flags'. Needs investigation: either bd's CLI contract changed (parent-implies-generated-id now, and --id should not be sent when --parent is present) or bd needs a flag-combination fix. Acceptance: real 'bd create <title> --parent <id> --id <childId>' succeeds and the created bead's id equals the allocated childId.
notes: TRIAGE: Already fixed in current code. createChildBeadWithAllocatedId() (runner.js ~2148-2200) never combines --id and --parent: 'const parentageFlags = grant.childId ? --id ${grant.childId} : --parent ${parentId};' (line 2166) -- explicit-id path uses --id alone then a separate 'bd update <id> --parent <parentId>' call (2183-2187) to link the parent edge afterward, exactly matching this bead's acceptance criteria intent (avoid the bd CLI's --id+--parent conflict). No open-code evidence of the reported error remains; f34-concurrent-launch-engagement-integration.test.mjs (referenced in the bug) exercises this path. Closing as already-fixed.
close_reason: Already fixed: createChildBeadWithAllocatedId never combines --id+--parent (parentageFlags ternary + separate bd update --parent link); see note.

title: sprint-coordination: reclaimed acquire tickets leave map entries behind on the long-lived fleet server
description: Self-reported by the doer in apra-fleet-f34.2's close reason and not otherwise tracked: in src/services/sprint-coordination.ts, a ticket whose grant is later reclaimed by lease expiry or dead-pid probe leaves a small entry behind in the server-side ticket map. Because the fleet MCP server is always-on (unlike a per-sprint supervisor), these entries accumulate monotonically over the server's lifetime -- a slow unbounded-growth leak rather than a correctness bug. Fix: drop the ticket entry when its grant is reclaimed (and/or sweep tickets whose underlying grant no longer exists during the existing lease sweep). Add a unit test asserting the ticket map returns to its prior size after a lease/dead-pid reclaim. The separate 'extract a shared coordination workspace package so the mutex/allocator core is not restated in TypeScript' follow-up is claimed tracked elsewhere in the same close reason and is deliberately NOT duplicated here.
close_reason: Fixed ticket map leak on grant reclaim (lease expiry + dead-pid); added unit tests asserting ticketCount() returns to prior size for both paths. Committed 463eb4f.

title: Harden the other pre-existing shell:true bd invocations (backlog.mjs, scope-overlap.mjs)
description: Surfaced while reviewing apra-fleet-2cc.1. The same unquoted-argv-through-shell issue exists in pre-existing code outside this sprint's scope: packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/backlog.mjs (execFileAsync('bd', ['list','--json','--limit','0'], { shell: true })) and src/supervisor/scope-overlap.mjs (execFileAsync('bd', ['list','--parent', parentId, '--json','--limit','0'], { shell: true })). scope-overlap.mjs is the more exposed of the two because parentId is an interpolated bead id rather than a literal. Node does not quote array args when shell:true, so a metacharacter (&, ;, $, parens) in an interpolated value reaches the shell. Fix consistently with whatever approach apra-fleet-2cc.1 lands on (win32 shim resolution without shell:true, or explicit quoting), ideally by routing these through the same shared helper.
close_reason: Routed backlog.mjs and scope-overlap.mjs through new execBdAsync() shared helper with allowlist arg validation; verified with unit tests + live bd invocation

title: [impl] Write docs/dolt-operator-conflict-runbook.md and cross-link the tier2 runbook
description:
New file: docs/dolt-operator-conflict-runbook.md (operator-local scenario), plus a cross-link edit in docs/dolt-tier2-runbook.md.

Content - the exact procedure used live on 2026-07-30 (verified safe twice, no data loss):
1. 'bd dolt pull' failing with 'merge conflicts ... merge aborted and working set restored' is SAFE, not destructive.
2. Find the embedded-Dolt working directory via .beads/metadata.json dolt_database (GOTCHA: .beads/embeddeddolt/beads vs .beads/embeddeddolt/apra_fleet differ per clone - check, do not assume).
3. Set a throwaway local dolt identity (dolt config --local --add user.email/name) for raw dolt CLI use.
4. 'dolt merge origin/main --no-commit' to reproduce the conflict without bd's auto-abort hiding it.
5. Inspect: select table, num_conflicts from dolt_conflicts; then select * from dolt_conflicts_<table>.
6. Resolve per table with 'dolt conflicts resolve --ours|--theirs <table>' where picking a side wholesale is genuinely safe; for a real content collision (two DIFFERENT issues claiming one id) the LOSING side's content must be recreated under a fresh id with a cross-reference note, never silently discarded.
7. 'dolt add -A && dolt commit && dolt push origin main'.
8. Verify every beads clone pulls cleanly afterwards.
Also state when this doc applies vs docs/dolt-tier2-runbook.md (member-clone agent escalation).

Acceptance criteria:
- Doc exists with all eight steps and the embedded-Dolt path gotcha spelled out.
- Bidirectional cross-links between the two runbooks with a one-line 'use this one when...' each.
- ASCII only; per repo policy the new doc is surfaced for user review before being committed.
close_reason: Wrote docs/dolt-operator-conflict-runbook.md (new file, all 8 steps transcribed with the embedded-Dolt path gotcha spelled out via reading dolt_database from .beads/metadata.json, never hardcoding a directory name) and added a reciprocal cross-link in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/docs/dolt-tier2-runbook.md (the bead's stated path 'docs/dolt-tier2-runbook.md' turned out to be that file's actual repo-root-relative location per DEFAULT_TIER2_RUNBOOK_PATH in dolt-recovery-tier2.mjs, not literally at docs/ -- verified before writing). Both docs have a one-line 'use this one when...' trigger pointing at each other (operator = you, own clone, raw dolt CLI; tier2 = dispatched agent, member clone, automated escalation after Path A/B fail), and relative markdown links verified to resolve on disk in both directions. title: Write operator-local Dolt conflict-resolution runbook (distinct scenario from docs/dolt-tier2-runbook.md)
description:
docs/dolt-tier2-runbook.md already exists but covers a different scenario: agent-driven escalation on a MEMBER's clone (part of the dolt-recovery-tier2.mjs ladder, apra-fleet-vkc). This bead is for the OPERATOR-LOCAL scenario this session actually lived through twice: a human/orchestrating Claude Code session's own local bd clone hits a Dolt merge conflict (child_counters/dependencies/issues) that bd's own `bd dolt pull` safely aborts and restores but does not resolve.

Document the exact working procedure used live this session (verified safe, no data loss both times):
1. `bd dolt pull` fails with "merge conflicts in <tables> require operator resolution; merge aborted and working set restored" -- this is safe, not destructive.
2. Find the actual embedded-Dolt working directory -- NOTE THE GOTCHA: this differs per clone's own .beads/metadata.json `dolt_database` config (e.g. .beads/embeddeddolt/beads/ vs .beads/embeddeddolt/apra_fleet/ -- check metadata.json first, don't assume).
3. Set a throwaway local dolt identity if needed (`dolt config --local --add user.email/name`) -- bd's own embedded dolt calls don't need this but the raw `dolt` CLI does.
4. `dolt merge origin/main --no-commit` to reproduce the conflict without bd's auto-abort hiding it.
5. Inspect `dolt sql -q "select \`table\`, num_conflicts from dolt_conflicts"` then `select * from dolt_conflicts_<table>` for each conflicted table to see the actual base/ours/theirs rows.
6. Resolve per-table: `dolt conflicts resolve --ours|--theirs <table>` for conflicts that are genuinely fine to pick one side wholesale (audit-only fields, or one side is simply newer/canonical); for a real content collision (two DIFFERENT issues claiming the same id), theirs/ours picks one issue's content for that id -- the LOSING side's content must be manually recreated under a fresh id afterward (bd create, closed with cross-reference note) rather than silently discarded.
7. `dolt add -A && dolt commit -m "..." && dolt push origin main` to conclude.
8. Verify all 3 (or however many) beads clones pull cleanly afterward.

Cross-link docs/dolt-tier2-runbook.md and note when each applies (member-clone agent escalation vs. operator-local manual resolution).

Test: doc review only -- no automated test; acceptance is that a future operator hitting this can follow the doc without re-deriving the embedded-Dolt path gotcha or the raw dolt CLI commands from scratch.

title: [impl] Make member env-var OAuth provisioning JSON-aware (extract accessToken)
description:
Root-cause fix for apra-fleet-vak (currently worked around by hand-seeding a second bare-token secret in integ-test-playbook runs).

FILES: src/cli/auth.ts only.

WHAT: provisionEnvVarForMember() (src/cli/auth.ts ~line 255) calls encryptPassword(token) on the raw resolved secret, so a secret stored as a full claudeAiOauth JSON object ({accessToken, expiresAt, scopes, ...}) lands verbatim as encryptedEnvVars.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and every dispatch to that member fails with 'Authentication failed ... Run /login'.

Add a NEW small exported helper (e.g. export function extractBearerTokenFromSecret(secret: string): string) in src/cli/auth.ts and call it on the resolved secret before encryptPassword:
- if secret.trim() starts with '{' and JSON.parses to an object with a string accessToken -> return that accessToken (trimmed)
- otherwise return the secret unchanged (verbatim pass-through; no trimming surprises for bare tokens beyond whitespace)
- nested shape tolerance: also accept { claudeAiOauth: { accessToken } } since that is the on-disk credentials-file shape.

DO NOT reuse parseClaudeOAuthSecret() for this: it returns an OBJECT and SYNTHESIZES expiresAt/scopes for bare tokens, which is correct for the credentials-FILE path and wrong for an env var. Leave parseClaudeOAuthSecret and the credentials-file path completely unchanged.

Export the helper so a unit test can call it directly. Keep the existing console output/behaviour otherwise; do not change auth.ts's non-ASCII glyphs here (out of scope, tracked separately).

DONE CRITERIA: npm run build passes; provisioning a member from a JSON-object secret stores only the bare accessToken; provisioning from a bare token is byte-identical to today's behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: src/cli/auth.ts exports a token-extraction helper used by provisionEnvVarForMember such that: a full claudeAiOauth JSON object secret (and a { claudeAiOauth: { accessToken } } wrapper) yields ONLY the bare accessToken stored in encryptedEnvVars.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; a bare token string is stored unchanged; a non-JSON string starting with '{' or invalid JSON falls back to verbatim pass-through without throwing. parseClaudeOAuthSecret and the credentials-file write path are unmodified. npm run build clean.

title: Unify fleet-sprint entry point for npm-installed users -- ship packages/apra-fleet-se so 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint' works everywhere
description:
BACKGROUND -- three user types, only two have a working command surface today:

1. Internal/dev users (git clone): run either 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint ...'
   or 'node packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/cli.mjs ...' directly. Both resolve to the
   same source files (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js) because
   src/cli/install.ts's buildDevManifest() finds packages/apra-fleet-se on disk
   and copies it into ~/.apra-fleet/workflows/fleet-sprint/ via collectPackageTree().
2. npm-installed users ('npm install -g @apralabs/apra-fleet' or a local project
   dependency, NOT the SEA binary): root package.json's "files" field
   (line 29-36) ships ONLY dist/, hooks/, two script files, skills/, version.json.
   packages/ is NOT in the tarball. packages/apra-fleet-se/package.json is
   itself "private": true (line 5), so it can never be a real npm dependency
   either. Consequence: buildDevManifest()'s fs.existsSync() checks for
   packages/apra-fleet-se all fail, so workflowRuntime/agentSchemas/
   builtinWorkflows all come back undefined, hasWorkflowAssets() returns
   false, and 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint' hard-fails with (workflow.ts:366-374):
     "this apra-fleet binary was built without the workflow subsystem assets
     ... Rebuild the binary ('npm run build:binary') or reinstall a current
     release ('apra-fleet update')"
   This message is actively wrong for this audience -- it assumes source/SEA
   build tooling they don't have, and never mentions the one thing that DOES
   work for them today: the bare 'fleet-sprint' command.
3. Non-dev users (pre-built SEA binary + 'apra-fleet install'): scripts/gen-sea-config.mjs
   ALSO collectPackageTree()s the raw packages/apra-fleet-se source tree into the
   SEA-embedded builtinWorkflows asset (gen-sea-config.mjs:190-191) -- same
   mechanism as dev mode, just SEA-asset-backed instead of disk-backed. Works fine.

WHAT KJ'S BRANCH (kj/fix-apra-fleet-se, 3 commits, currently unmerged, ahead 3 /
behind 1 vs main) ALREADY DOES -- it fixes the ONE code path that is the sole
lifeline for user type 2 today: the root package's own separate npm bin entry
  package.json:22-25:  "bin": { "apra-fleet": "dist/index.js", "fleet-sprint": "dist/fleet-sprint.mjs" }
built by 'npm run build:se' -> scripts/bundle-se.mjs (an esbuild bundle of
packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js + its .mjs siblings), which runs
automatically as part of "prepublishOnly" on every real npm publish. Its 3 commits:
  - 533fee23 fix(bundle): give the ESM fleet-sprint bundle a real require for
    CJS deps -- dist/fleet-sprint.mjs died on EVERY invocation with
    "Dynamic require of 'node:assert' is not supported" (undici, pulled in via
    apra-fleet-client's transport, is CJS; esbuild's ESM require-shim throws on
    anything it can't resolve statically). Fix: inject a real createRequire-backed
    require via a banner. Added a smoke test that actually spawns the built bundle.
  - db7367fa fix(bundle): ship every runner sibling, not a hand-maintained subset --
    bundle-se.mjs hand-listed 3 sibling .mjs files (contracts.mjs, errors.mjs,
    viewer-extensions.mjs) to copy next to the bundle (runner.js is deliberately
    never bundled, read from disk as text by the engine); that list had gone
    stale (conflict-ladder.mjs, sprint-lock.mjs were missing), so the binary
    died with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on its first real sprint. Fix: scan the
    directory instead of naming files; added a static check walking the
    runner's transitive relative imports.
  - 2cc52680 test(install): guard the dev manifest against a stale apra-pm path --
    regression test only, no live bug (main already has correct paths); guards
    buildDevManifest() against a single stale hardcoded path silently disabling
    the ENTIRE workflow install with a false success + exit 0.
  These 3 commits are real, necessary fixes for user type 2's ONLY current
  path -- kj was not testing the wrong thing. They should still be merged
  regardless of what this bead decides, since user type 2 needs SOME working
  path in the meantime.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD IS ABOUT: rather than accepting a permanently-forked
command surface (git-clone/SEA users type 'apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint',
npm users type the bare 'fleet-sprint' command, forever, as two different
supported UX paths depending on install method), unify on ONE command
('apra-fleet workflow fleet-sprint ...') for all three user types, and retire
the separate bundled dist/fleet-sprint.mjs bin entry entirely once that's done.

Measured cost of unification (2026-07-29, working tree measurements):

title: [integ] Reviewer newTask with non-ASCII punctuation (em-dash) silently blocks canary closure instead of being sanitized
description:
Feature: N/A (playbook Part 2 smoke test, integ-test-playbook.md ## Test scenario step 5)
Deploy-verified SHA under test: bb192071276ddaf2c6aa367df5336728c0199f0d (v0.4.0_bb1920)

Expected: per integ-test-playbook.md ## Test scenario step 5, after the canary sprint (workflow fleet-sprint -i gh-toy-4ef -m toy-doer --max-cycles 1) runs, the canary issue gh-toy-4ef (and its children) should end up closed once the deliverable is verifiably complete.

Actual: The canary's actual deliverable (--version/-v flag) was implemented correctly and verified functionally (node ./tool --version and -v both print 'fleet-e2e-toy v1.0.0' and exit 0 on the sprint branch integ-smoke-20260729042813b; tests/cli.test.ts has 4 passing cases). However the final Review verdict was FAIL and gh-toy-4ef / gh-toy-4ef.2 were left OPEN, because the reviewer's own follow-up newTask (title: 'Verify and close remaining open P1 version-flag beads (gh-toy-4ef.2 and parent gh-toy-4ef)') was rejected by validateNewTask()'s SAFE_DESCRIPTION_RE (/^[\t\n\r\x20-\x7E]+$/, runner.js:3426) because its description contained a non-ASCII em-dash character ('—'). Per runner.js's fail-closed design (apra-fleet-eft.56/eft.73 lineage) the rejection is non-fatal and the raw finding is appended verbatim to gh-toy-4ef's notes via appendRejectedFindingToParentNotes() -- so nothing is silently lost -- but with --max-cycles 1 there is no further cycle to act on that note, so the sprint (and this smoke-test pass) ends with the canary still open despite the underlying work being functionally complete.

Test: integ-test-playbook.md ## Test scenario step 5, this cycle's run (branch integ-smoke-20260729042813b, run id integ-smoke-20260729042813b). Final result.verdict='FAIL', result.notes explicitly says the deliverable/tests/lint/build all pass but 'gh-toy-4ef.2 ... and its parent gh-toy-4ef ... are still OPEN' due to the rejected newTask. gh-toy-4ef's own bd notes contain the verbatim rejected finding: rejectionReason 'description fails ASCII-printable validation /^[\t\n\r\x20-\x7E]+$/ (or is empty): ...' (the offending description used a Unicode em-dash '—' in two places).

Repro: run a canary/toy sprint where the reviewer's follow-up newTask description happens to contain a Unicode em-dash (or any other char outside \t\n\r\x20-\x7E) -- common LLM output style. validateNewTask() rejects the whole task outright instead of sanitizing just the offending characters, so the actionable follow-up (closing already-satisfied beads) never gets filed as a bead and, in a single-cycle run, is never acted on.

Suggested fix: SAFE_DESCRIPTION_RE already exists specifically to be permissive (multi-line ASCII-printable) unlike SAFE_TEXT_RE (title) which still needs the tighter shell-safety allowlist. Since description is only ever written via --body-file (never shell-interpolated, per the eft.56.1/eft.73.1 hardening comment above SAFE_DESCRIPTION_RE), there is no injection reason to reject it outright for a handful of common non-ASCII punctuation (em/en dash, curly quotes, ellipsis) that LLM reviewers routinely emit. Consider normalizing those specific characters to ASCII equivalents (em/en dash -> '--', curly quotes -> straight quotes, ellipsis -> '...') before validation, the same 'sanitize instead of reject' approach already used for the finalVerdict PR body/title text a few hundred lines below in this same file, rather than dropping the whole newTask (with its downstream fail-closed/notes-fallback machinery) over cosmetic punctuation.

Fix landed via commits 5791ab8e/afbfdc8b with regression coverage via 1cdf7aaa/2144ffe1 (test asserts the exact 04g.2 repro string -- em-dash + curly quotes + ellipsis -- now passes validateNewTask with correct ASCII substitution), both merged into current HEAD via de48e98c. description:

Final Review verdict: FAIL -- gh-toy-4ef and both P1 children (.1, .2) remain OPEN, 0 beads closed, no CLI implementation landed (diff vs main only touched .beads/config.yaml and CLAUDE.md).

This is very likely purely environmental contamination, not a regression in the SHA under test: an earlier, genuinely fresh run in this same session (before any Reset/retry churn) fully PASSED against the toy CLI feature, and the abandoned branch 'b' attempt under this SAME SHA had already gotten as far as the doer successfully implementing the --version flag (commit 'feat: add --version/-v flag to CLI entrypoint') before being wiped by Reset -- so the underlying product code is not obviously broken. The failure only reproduces when a prior attempt's background dev-server process survives a Reset into the next attempt.

Deploy phase output: 'Deploy FAILED this cycle (C1): ... npm run start:test ... exited immediately with: Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3001 ... unrelated pre-existing node/ts-node process (pid 42492, already running ~9m37s before this attempt, not started by this deploy run) was already bound to port 3001'. title: Launch Sprint form: auto-generate a branch name when left blank
description:
src/supervisor/launch-form.mjs's buildLaunchRequestBody() currently requires an explicit branch name -- an empty/whitespace-only value is a hard client-side validation error ('Branch name is required.', line ~99). Operators launching a quick one-off sprint (e.g. today's low-hanging-fruit batches) have to invent a branch name every time, which is friction for no real benefit in the common case.

Fix: when the branch field is left blank, auto-generate one instead of erroring, using the convention 'fleet-sprint/<doer>-<3 random alphanumerics>' -- e.g. 'fleet-sprint/fleet-win-dev1-a7k'. <doer> is the (first, if multiple) selected member name; the 3-char suffix avoids collisions across repeated launches against the same member without the operator having to think about it. An explicitly-typed branch name is always honored verbatim (this is a fallback for the empty case only, never an override).

Acceptance criteria:
- buildLaunchRequestBody() with an empty/whitespace branch and at least one member does NOT return a client-side error; it fills in a generated 'fleet-sprint/<doer>-<3 random alphanumerics>' branch name in the returned body.
- The random suffix is drawn from [a-z0-9] (or similar), exactly 3 characters, alphanumeric only (matches this repo's branch-naming convention and the existing ARG_CONTRACT-style branch validation elsewhere in the codebase).
- An operator-supplied branch name is never overridden -- generation only kicks in when the field is genuinely empty.
- Unit test coverage: blank branch -> a body with a well-formed generated branch name matching the expected pattern; non-blank branch -> passed through unchanged.
notes: Confirmed still a hard error: packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/launch-form.mjs:106-109 -- buildLaunchRequestBody() trims opts.branch and returns {ok:false, error:'Branch name is required.'} on empty/whitespace, no auto-generation path exists. Fix is small and precisely scoped by the bead itself (generate 'fleet-sprint/<doer>-<3 random alphanumerics>' only when branch is blank, never override an explicit value) with concrete acceptance criteria and clear unit-test shape (function is already unit-tested standalone per the file's own doc comment, 'TESTABLE WITHOUT A DOM'). title: Allow llm_provider=none via update_member; reject execute_prompt-family tools cleanly for it
description:
User-reported gap (2026-07-28), found while trying to mark member 'spark' llm:none after its claude CLI turned out not to be on PATH.

PART A -- update_member cannot set llm_provider to 'none':
src/tools/register-member.ts:50 already includes 'none' in its llm_provider enum ("Use 'none' for a plain command executor with no LLM at all"), so a member CAN be registered fresh with llm_provider:none. But src/tools/update-member.ts:49 has a narrower enum -- z.enum(['claude', 'gemini', 'codex', 'copilot', 'agy', 'opencode']) -- missing 'none'. An already-registered member (like spark) can never be converted to llm:none after the fact; only a brand-new registration can set it. Add 'none' to update-member.ts's llm_provider enum, matching register-member.ts's existing allowed set and description.

PART B -- execute_prompt-family tools should reject 'none' members cleanly, not throw deep in NoneProvider -- applies REGARDLESS of whether the member reached llm:none via register_member (already supported) or update_member (Part A):
src/providers/none.ts implements a deliberate fail-loud NoneProvider "so a caller that forgets the 'none' check fails loudly" -- but that's a safety net, not a good user-facing error. execute-prompt.ts ALREADY does this correctly (line 468-470): checks agent.llmProvider === 'none' up front, before entering any busy state, and returns a clean, actionable message ('... has no LLM provider (llm_provider: \"none\") -- it is a plain command executor. Use execute_command instead.') instead of letting NoneProvider throw deeper. register-member.ts itself is also already correct on this front (isNoLlm check at line 321 skips version/auth verification during registration).

The following tools call getProvider(agent.llmProvider) with NO equivalent guard, and will hit NoneProvider's throw-loud methods instead of a clean rejection for a llm:none member -- this is a property of the TOOL, not of how the member got its llm:none value, so it must be verified for members from BOTH entry points:
- src/tools/stop-prompt.ts -- no llmProvider==='none' check at all (only an unrelated 'none' string used for pid-missing logging).
- src/tools/provision-auth.ts:241 -- const provider = getProvider(agent.llmProvider); called with no guard (this is provision_llm_auth).
- src/tools/update-agent-cli.ts:28 -- const provider = getProvider(agent.llmProvider); called with no guard (this is update_llm_cli).

Add the same early, clean-message guard execute-prompt.ts already has to each of these three tools, before any provider/CLI logic runs. Audit for any other execute_prompt-family tool with the same gap while implementing (grep getProvider( callers across src/tools/).

PART C -- keep packages/apra-fleet-client in sync with this change:
packages/apra-fleet-client/src/client/api.mjs's UpdateMemberOptions/RegisterMemberOptions typedefs (~lines 83, 101) type llm_provider as a loose {string}, not a literal union, so 'none' already passes through the client mechanically with no code change required. Still: (1) confirm this explicitly with a client-side test (updateMember/registerMember with llm_provider:'none' round-trips through the mocked callTool exactly like every other provider value, mirroring the existing provisionVcsAuth/provisionLlmAuth test pattern in packages/apra-fleet-client/test/fleet-client-api.test.mjs), and (2) update the JSDoc comment on both typedefs to mention 'none' as a valid value alongside the others, so the client's own documentation doesn't silently drift from the server's actual accepted enum. This is required by CLAUDE.md's apra-fleet-client sync policy, not optional cleanup.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- update_member can set llm_provider to 'none' on an already-registered member; member_detail reflects it afterward.
- stop_prompt, provision_llm_auth, and update_llm_cli each return a clean, actionable rejection message (not a raw NoneProvider exception/stack trace) when called against a member with llm_provider:'none' -- tested for a member that reached llm:none via register_member AND for one that reached it via update_member, confirming no behavioral difference between the two entry points. title: [viewer] Task tree: filter by Type/Status/Pri/Model column headers, server-side (not just UI)
description:
User-reported usability gap (2026-07-28): the fleet-sprint dashboard's beads/task tree (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/viewer-extensions.mjs, renderBeadsHtml()) has grown large enough that it's hard to visually locate "open"/"in progress" items in the rendered tree table. The table's rightmost four column headers -- ID/Title/Type/Status/Pri/Model (viewer-extensions.mjs:434-435, badges rendered via typeBadge/statusBadgeForNode/priorityBadge/modelBadge) -- should double as clickable filter controls for Type, Status, Priority, and Model.

REQUIREMENTS (verbatim from the report):
1. Clicking a column header (Type/Status/Pri/Model) filters the tree to that value; the currently active filter(s) must be clearly visible to the user (e.g. a highlighted header + an explicit "filtering by: X" indicator, not just an implied state).
2. This must NOT be UI-only (i.e. not just hide/show rows via client-side CSS/JS on data already fetched). The filter needs to reach the actual endpoint/computation that produces the task tree data, so an active filter can reduce the payload/traffic sent to the browser, not just what's rendered from an already-fetched full data set.

ARCHITECTURE NOTE (relevant to the fix, found while scoping this): renderBeadsHtml (viewer-extensions.mjs:92) is exported as SOURCE and re-embedded via .toString() into a browser-side <script> (viewer-extensions.mjs:598), and is invoked CLIENT-SIDE on every state poll against already-delivered data (viewer-extensions.mjs:726, `container.innerHTML = renderBeadsHtml(lastBeadsData.sprintTasks || [], lastBeadsData.backlogTasks || [], ...)`). Today the FULL sprintTasks/backlogTasks arrays are already sent to the browser on every poll regardless of what's rendered -- a naive client-only filter would satisfy requirement 1 but not requirement 2. sprintTasks/backlogTasks are populated server-side in fleet-sprint/runner.js (see the state-shape comment around runner.js:5417-5421, "sprintTasks: everything under this sprint's target scope (re-fetched...)" / "backlogTasks: open/deferred beads project-wide that are NOT already...") -- that's where a filter parameter would need to actually narrow the `bd list` query/result set, not just the render step.

SCOPE: 
- UI: clickable Type/Status/Pri/Model headers, visible active-filter state (multi-select or single-select TBD by whoever implements -- note in the bead which was chosen), a clear way to clear the filter.
- API/state layer: thread the active filter through to wherever sprintTasks/backlogTasks get computed/queried (runner.js) so an active filter can actually reduce what's fetched/sent, not just what's displayed. Consider a query-param or websocket-message-shaped filter spec so the client can express it and the server can act on it.
- Preserve existing tree/nesting semantics (parent-containment hierarchy, backlog-vs-sprint sectioning, collapse/expand) -- filtering narrows WHICH rows appear, it should not change HOW they're nested/sectioned.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (draft, refine during implementation):
- Clicking a Type/Status/Pri/Model header value filters the tree to matching rows; the active filter is visibly indicated in the UI at all times while active.
- With a filter active, the network payload for the next state poll is measurably smaller than the unfiltered payload for the same underlying data set (proves server-side narrowing occurred, not just client-side hiding).
- Clearing the filter returns to the full, unfiltered tree.
- Existing tree nesting/section tests (dashboard-tree-grandchild-nesting.test.mjs, viewer-extensions.test.mjs, and friends) continue to pass unmodified for the no-filter-active case.
- New tests cover: filter-active payload is narrower than unfiltered; filtered tree still nests correctly (a filtered-out parent with a filtered-in child does not orphan/misrender that child); clearing the filter restores full state.
notes: Verified genuinely unimplemented (no filter state, no column-header click handlers, no server-side filter param found in viewer-extensions.mjs or runner.js's sprintTasks/backlogTasks construction) and its blocker apra-fleet-eft.70 is now CLOSED (integ-verified 2026-08-01), so it is technically unblocked. However this is NOT low-hanging fruit: the bead's own acceptance criteria require (1) new client filter UI + visible active-filter indicator, (2) a new filter spec threaded through the client poll into runner.js's bd-list query construction so payload size measurably shrinks (not just client-side hiding), (3) preserving existing tree/section/nesting semantics under a filtered view, and (4) new tests for narrower-payload + no-orphaned-children + clear-filter, all while leaving existing nesting tests green. That is a real client+server design/protocol change (new filter wire format, query-param semantics on the state poll), not a mechanical polish fix. Classifying needs-deeper-design; did not label low-hanging-fruit.

title: [integ] auth --oauth --member stores a JSON credential blob verbatim as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN when the secret was seeded from a full claudeAiOauth object
description:
Discovered while running the eft.74.8 live smoke retest (integ-test-playbook.md Setup + direct execute_prompt dispatch to a sandbox local member).

integ-test-playbook.md step 3a computes $SECRET from the runner's real ~/.claude/.credentials.json as a JSON object ({accessToken, expiresAt, scopes, ...}, refresh token deliberately stripped) whenever that file exists, and step 3a stores that same $SECRET into the persistent secret store (apra-fleet secret --set ... --persist). Step 3b then reuses the same secure.<name> reference for BOTH:
  (a) the bonus credentials-FILE write (apra-fleet auth --oauth --llm claude secure.<name>), which correctly JSON-aware-unwraps the object via parseClaudeOAuthSecret() in src/cli/auth.ts, and
  (b) the PRIMARY member env-var provisioning (apra-fleet auth --oauth --member <name> secure.<name>), whose provisionEnvVarForMember() in src/cli/auth.ts does NOT unwrap -- it calls encryptPassword(token) on the raw resolved string and stores it verbatim as encryptedEnvVars.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.

Effect: whenever the runner's real credentials.json exists (the common case, not an edge case), the member's CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN env var ends up holding a JSON blob instead of a bare access token. LocalStrategy's clean-env dispatch (env -i ... bash -l -c 'export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=<blob> && claude ...') then fails every dispatch to that member with 'Authentication failed on "<member>". Run /login to refresh your credentials...' -- reproduced live: both of two sequential execute_prompt dispatches to a freshly-registered sandbox member failed in ~4.4s with exit=1 until the member was re-provisioned from the bare $CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN env var instead.

scripts/check-toy-doer-credentials.mjs does not catch this: it only checks that encryptedEnvVars.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is non-empty (not that it is bare-token-shaped), so this class of misprovisioning currently passes the playbook's own verification step and only surfaces as a live dispatch auth failure.

Suggested remediation (either or both):
1. Make provisionEnvVarForMember() in src/cli/auth.ts JSON-aware like parseClaudeOAuthSecret() -- if the resolved secret parses as a JSON object with an accessToken field, extract just that field before encrypting/storing as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.
2. Or: have integ-test-playbook.md's step 3a compute two distinct secrets -- the full claudeAiOauth object for the credentials-file bonus write, and a second bare-token secret (accessToken only) for step 3b's member env-var provisioning -- so each consumer gets the shape it actually needs.

Acceptance: a member provisioned via 'apra-fleet auth --oauth --member <name> secure.<ref>' where <ref>'s stored secret is a full claudeAiOauth JSON object authenticates successfully on the next dispatch (no 'Authentication failed' / no raw JSON landing in encryptedEnvVars.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN). scripts/check-toy-doer-credentials.mjs is extended to flag a JSON-shaped env-var value as a hard failure, not just non-empty.
notes: integ-test-runner (2026-07-30, deployed SHA f9378fb7f520cf3e8a05d9641a87675fd39082c7): left open, inconclusive. Part 2 (smoke test) Setup aborted at the beads-seed step due to a Windows-only tooling defect (apra-fleet-bnb.2: execFileSync('bd', ...) ENOENTs without shell:true), before member registration/credential provisioning/Planner dispatch (steps 1/3/4) could run -- no live auth evidence either way this cycle. Additionally note for whoever retries: this bug's own verification script, scripts/check-toy-doer-credentials.mjs, is itself non-functional on Windows (import.meta.url vs backslash argv[1] guard never matches, so main() never runs and it silently exits 0 regardless of provisioning state -- also captured in apra-fleet-bnb.2) -- so even a successful Setup on this platform would not have produced trustworthy automated evidence for vak without that guard fixed first. src/cli/auth.ts's provisionEnvVarForMember() JSON-unwrap fix (287403b) and the checker's hard-fail addition (884fa12) are both present in the deployed SHA per source read, but that is not a substitute for an actual dispatch-level repro/non-repro.
close_reason: integ-test-runner (2026-08-02, working-tree SHA 8231db2c, no dispatch-level sandbox available under the current per-feature integ-test-playbook.md, which explicitly excludes sandbox lifecycle/live-dispatch testing -- that only lives in regression-test-playbook.md/regression-test-runner): verified per apra-fleet-vak's own [test] task (apra-fleet-vak.3). Ran 'npx vitest run tests/auth-oauth-secret.test.ts tests/check-toy-doer-credentials.test.ts' -- 73/73 tests passed (0 failed), covering: full claudeAiOauth JSON object -> bare accessToken extraction, { claudeAiOauth: { accessToken } } wrapper unwrap, bare-token passthrough, malformed-JSON passthrough without throw, parseClaudeOAuthSecret regression guard unchanged, and the checker's hard-fail on JSON-shaped encryptedEnvVars.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / bare-token pass / plaintext-unavailable indeterminate outcomes. Confirmed by source read that the fix is present in the working tree: src/cli/auth.ts:299-314 (JSON-aware accessToken extraction used by provisionEnvVarForMember) and scripts/check-toy-doer-credentials.mjs:213-269 (hard-fail status for JSON-shaped decrypted plaintext, citing apra-fleet-vak). 'npm run build' also green (tsc, no errors). Defect no longer reproduces per the repo-local test evidence available to this playbook; closing. Note: the separate Windows-only tooling defect referenced in the prior inconclusive note (apra-fleet-bnb.2) is a distinct issue and not blocking this bug's own acceptance criteria.
