title: fleet-sprint: build provision_vcs_auth / provision_llm_auth into the orchestration loop for ruggedization
description:
Motivated by a live incident (2026-07-27, apra-fleet-eft sprint on branch feat/sprint-service-1, member fleet-mac): the Planner's Dolt push failed mid-sprint with "could not read Username for https://github.com: Device not configured" -- fleet-mac simply had no VCS credentials provisioned. The sprint had to be manually paused (in effect) while the orchestrator ran provision_vcs_auth by hand to unblock it. Separately, provision_llm_auth is a known manual recovery step today whenever a member's LLM session goes stale/unauthenticated (see fleet-sprint-cli skill precondition #4 and the local-member-auth-expiry-recovery memory).

CORE ASK: fleet-sprint should not assume it is always launched on a machine, or against members, that already have live VCS and LLM credentials wired up. Today both provision_vcs_auth and provision_llm_auth are external, manual, human-triggered MCP tool calls the orchestrator happens to run when something breaks -- they are NOT part of fleet-sprint's own orchestration loop, so a credential gap surfaces only as an opaque mid-run dispatch failure (empty_response, dolt push auth error, etc.) rather than being proactively checked/repaired.

RUGGEDIZE ALSO MEANS EXPIRY-AWARE JUST-IN-TIME RENEWAL, not only reactive repair after a failure. Observed directly in this incident: the GitHub App token minted by provision_vcs_auth for fleet-mac carries a short (~1hr) expiry. A long-running multi-cycle fleet-sprint (max-cycles default 5, potentially hours) will walk right off the end of that token's lifetime and hit the exact same auth failure again later in the same run if nothing tracks expiry. So this needs a proactive path, not just a reactive one: fleet-sprint (or the underlying sync/dispatch layer) should know each provisioned credential's expiry (VCS token expiresAt is already returned by provision_vcs_auth; LLM session/OAuth tokens have their own refresh windows) and trigger re-provisioning BEFORE expiry -- comfortably ahead of the deadline, not at first failure -- so a long sprint never has to fail-and-retry its way into discovering a credential lapsed.

DESIGN GUIDANCE FROM USER (2026-07-27), narrowing the two credential kinds asymmetrically:

- provision_vcs_auth is the EASY side: it mints short-lived tokens directly from GitHub (via the configured GitHub App), so it can be called directly, headlessly, by the orchestration loop itself -- no human-in-the-loop secret material needed, just wiring fleet-sprint to call it proactively/on-schedule.

- provision_llm_auth is the HARD side and needs its own design: it should support two modes --
  (1) an explicit API key from the right LLM provider, supplied as a fleet secure-variable NAME on the CLI (i.e. a {{secure.NAME}}-style reference resolved from the credential store, per the existing fleet-secure-placeholder-quoting contract used elsewhere), or
  (2) "oauth" (the default), meaning: reuse/derive the member's LLM auth from the ORCHESTRATOR's own OAuth session/credentials, rather than requiring each remote member to have independently completed its own interactive OAuth login.
  Design needs to work out how mode (2) concretely propagates orchestrator-side OAuth material to a remote member without a human re-running an interactive login there.

- SCOPE NARROWING: this whole LLM-auth-ruggedization problem is mostly a NON-issue for the local-only member scenario, since a local member already shares/reuses the orchestrator's own host OAuth session directly. It matters primarily -- arguably only -- for the REMOTE member scenario, where the member's LLM CLI runs on a separate machine with its own (or no) OAuth session. Design and prioritization should focus there, not spend effort ruggedizing the local case which is already fine.

NEEDS DESIGN THINKING, not a quick fix. Open questions to resolve before implementation:

1. Preflight vs. reactive vs. expiry-scheduled: three overlapping strategies now in scope -- (a) an upfront preflight check for every --members target (alongside fleet-sprint-cli's existing "is this member registered"/"topology compatible" checks), (b) reactive self-heal on auth-shaped dispatch failures (distinct from generic empty_response/dolt errors), and (c) proactive just-in-time renewal scheduled off each credential's known/tracked expiry so it never lapses mid-run in the first place. VCS side: straightforward, since provision_vcs_auth can be called directly/headlessly on a schedule. LLM side: depends on resolving the oauth-passthrough design below first.

2. Expiry tracking: where does fleet-sprint learn a credential's expiry and when to renew? provision_vcs_auth already returns expiresAt -- something needs to persist that per-member (sprint run state? a per-member credential-status side-table?) and compute a renew-before deadline (e.g. renew at 80% of lifetime, or N minutes before expiry) rather than waiting for expiry itself. For LLM auth, expiry tracking differs by mode: an explicit API-key secure-variable presumably doesn't expire the way OAuth does; the oauth-passthrough mode's expiry semantics depend entirely on how orchestrator-OAuth-reuse is implemented (item 3 below).

3. LLM oauth-passthrough mechanism (the crux of the hard side): work out concretely how "reuse the orchestrator's own OAuth creds" propagates to a remote member -- token forwarding, a short-lived derived/delegated credential, or something else -- without ever requiring a human to interactively log in on the remote member. Must also define fallback behavior when the orchestrator's own OAuth session itself is the thing that's stale (can't delegate from a session that's already invalid).

4. Blast radius / safety: provisioned GitHub App tokens are short-lived (observed ~1hr expiry in this incident) and scoped (repos + access level) -- any automatic re-provisioning or renewal inside the orchestration loop must not silently escalate scope/access beyond what a human would have explicitly granted, and should log/report every renewal (proactive or reactive) so this isn't a silent credential-rotation surprise. A renewal-scheduling loop also needs its own failure mode thought through (what happens if the just-in-time renewal itself fails -- does it fall back to the reactive self-heal path, or escalate to a human?). Same applies to LLM oauth-passthrough: propagated credentials must not grant a remote member broader access than the orchestrator itself has.

5. Where in the fleet-sprint code this hooks in: likely candidates are the same withGitSync bracket / Dolt sync layer implicated in apra-fleet-6z8 (coarse retry granularity), and/or a new preflight phase alongside "Ensure Sprint Branch" in Sprint Setup, plus some kind of lightweight background/periodic check for the expiry-scheduled renewal path (long sprints already have a dispatch loop that could carry this, vs. needing a genuinely separate timer). Consider whether this should be a generic fleet-sprint capability or a shared capability all apra-fleet-se workflows (auto-sprint, fleet-sprint) can use, given both use members with the same VCS/LLM auth dependencies.

ACCEPTANCE (design-stage): a written design covering (a) preflight vs. reactive vs. expiry-scheduled strategy for both VCS and LLM auth, noting VCS is the straightforward headless case; (b) how credential expiry is tracked and renew-before deadlines are computed for each; (c) the concrete LLM auth design: explicit secure-variable API key mode plus an oauth-passthrough mode that reuses the orchestrator's own OAuth session for remote members without an interactive login there, scoped explicitly to the remote-member case (local members are out of scope, already fine); (d) safety constraints preventing silent scope escalation on auto-reprovisioned/renewed VCS tokens or delegated LLM credentials, plus the renewal-failure fallback path; (e) where this hooks into fleet-sprint's existing phases/withGitSync bracket. Implementation follows as a separate pass once the design is reviewed.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewed design doc/plan exists answering: the combined preflight/reactive/expiry-scheduled strategy for both VCS (straightforward, headless via provision_vcs_auth) and LLM auth (harder: explicit secure-variable API key mode vs. an oauth-passthrough mode reusing orchestrator OAuth for remote members, scoped to the remote-member case since local is already fine); how credential expiry is tracked and renew-before deadlines are computed for each; safety constraints preventing silent scope escalation plus the renewal-failure fallback path; and where this hooks into fleet-sprint's existing phases/withGitSync bracket. Implementation work is scoped and split into follow-up tasks once the design is approved.
notes: Triage 2026-08-09 (iuc-agy batch): unchanged and correctly scoped as design-stage. Confirmed nothing has landed: fleet-sprint has no preflight or expiry-scheduled credential phase, and provision_vcs_auth / provision_llm_auth remain external human-triggered MCP tool calls (src/tools/provision-auth.ts is still a plain per-call tool with no scheduler or expiry tracker on the fleet side, and its getProvider call at :241 is itself the subject of apra-fleet-0s6). The crux named in the bead -- how to propagate orchestrator-side OAuth material to a REMOTE member without an interactive login there -- is still an open question with no chosen mechanism, and the local-member case is genuinely already fine (see the local-member-auth-expiry-recovery precedent: local members reuse the host OAuth session). Also note the interaction with the newly-added expiry-adjacent surface: nothing today persists provision_vcs_auth's returned expiresAt per member, so the ~1hr GitHub App token walk-off that motivated this bead would still recur on a long multi-cycle sprint. Classification: NEEDS-DEEPER-DESIGN -- acceptance is explicitly 'a reviewed design doc', so this should be sequenced as a design task with a human review gate, and its implementation split out afterwards; it is not sprintable as-is by a doer agent. P2 is defensible but it is the largest and least tractable item in this batch -- if the reprioritization wants throughput, put 0s6 and tvbk ahead of it.

title: Watchdog tick has no reentrancy guard -- overlapping classifyAll runs can race on recordedCrashes/state-file writes
description: watchdog.mjs sets a setInterval (5s, watchdog.mjs:438) that calls classifyAll for every tracked sprint. classifyAll does a blocking spawnSync WMIC/PowerShell cmdline read per sprint on Windows (watchdog.mjs:151-152) plus a ~1.5s HTTP liveness probe per sprint. acceptance_criteria: classifyAll invocations from the interval are serialized (e.g. an in-flight flag/promise guard skips or queues a tick that arrives while the previous one is still running) so recordedCrashes and state-file writes cannot interleave across overlapping ticks. title: Naming collision: 'auto-sprint' means two unrelated things (Claude Workflow-tool skill vs apra-fleet CLI workflow) -- agents conflate them

   <name> --base <name>` CLI invocation (via the SEA binary or bin/cli.mjs),
   documented in packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/docs/README.md. This is
   the actual sprint engine (runner.js), unrelated to the Claude Code
   Workflow tool despite the identical name.

An agent reflexively pulled up the auto-sprint-args skill (meant for #1) when
asked to launch #2, and nearly built a launch command using the wrong
argument shape (issues array vs --issue/--members/--branch/--base flags).
See auto-sprint-1 (open, related) for the adjacent README-contradiction bug
about how to launch #2 safely.

FIX: rename or clearly disambiguate one of the two systems in all
user-facing/skill-facing verbiage (e.g. the Claude-Code-internal one could be
renamed away from "auto-sprint" entirely, or the skill description and the
apra-fleet-se README should each explicitly warn "not to be confused with
Claude Code's own \"auto-sprint\" Workflow-tool skill / apra-fleet's product
workflow of the same name" with a one-line pointer to the other).
close_reason: Root cause resolved: the naming collision no longer exists now that the CLI product workflow is genuinely renamed to fleet-sprint (apra-fleet-wkg.1, verified complete), leaving Claude Code's native /auto-sprint skill as the sole holder of that name by explicit design.

title: [engine] Planner-owned streaks: high-cohesion lane metadata at plan time, deterministic grouping, per-bead failure attribution
description:
Today streak formation happens at develop time via an LLM dispatch that receives BARE BEAD IDS ONLY (buildStreakAssignmentPrompt forbids investigation), so high cohesion is impossible by construction: the assigner cannot know two beads touch the same module or the same mutual-exclusion resource. Run 23 C1 R1 assigned 10 singleton streaks (10x exploration overhead) and split two beads that both bump the same vendor submodule pointer into separate streaks (silent-overwrite hazard). A streak today is also effectively an unordered bag with all-or-nothing failure semantics.

Definition (contract): a streak is an ORDERED list of task beads one doer session works start-to-finish; order consistent with blocks edges; members share working context (same component/module/files of the target project - high cohesion); no cross-streak blocks edges between open members and no two streaks touching the same mutual-exclusion resource (e.g. a submodule pointer, a version field, a committed fixture) - low coupling. impl+[test] pairs co-streak by default (the test author inherits the implementer's warm context).

Changes:
1. Planner (planner.md contract, TARGET-PROJECT-AGNOSTIC wording): emit streak lane metadata per task (streak: <lane>, streakOrder: <n>) via the same bd metadata channel as model. Planner does the splitting math: effort points = (sum of size points: S=1, M=2, L=4) x (max model weight in lane: cheap=1, standard=10, premium=20 - mirrors real per-token cost ratios, so effort points approximate dollar cost). Over a threshold constant -> split at a blocks-edge boundary, never splitting mutex-resource members apart. NOTE: the formula doubles as cost control - the engine already prices a mixed streak at its max tier, so clubbing cheap chores into a premium lane upgrades their execution cost; the formula penalizes exactly that.
2. Plan-reviewer (plan-reviewer.md): new criterion - every task has lane metadata; lanes are cohesive (members' named files/component overlap); no cross-lane edges among open members; mutex resources co-laned; every lane's effort points under the threshold.
3. Engine (runner.js): group each develop round deterministically from lane metadata intersected with the current ready/open set, ordered by streakOrder within blocks-edge constraints. The runtime Streak-Assignment LLM dispatch is retired to a FALLBACK used only when tasks lack lane metadata (back-compat with old plans).
4. Per-bead failure attribution (PREREQUISITE for bigger streaks): when a streak reports, close what verifiably closed, mark FAILED only the beads still open, and re-lane only those. Never discard completed work because a sibling was refused.
5. NO hard size cap: max_turns exhaustion is already handled by resume-with-increased-turns; only effort points split a lane. The formula is an explicit placeholder seam for predicted context size (see the follow-up P3 bead).

Acceptance (machine-verifiable):
- planner.md/plan-reviewer.md updated with generic vocabulary (no apra-fleet-specific names); plan-reviewer output flags a lane violation as CHANGES_NEEDED with the criterion number.
- mock-sprint test: a plan with lane metadata produces the exact deterministic streak grouping (no Streak Assignment dispatch in the command log); a plan WITHOUT lane metadata falls back to the LLM assignment path unchanged.
- mock-sprint test: a 3-bead streak whose doer closes 2 and refuses 1 results in the 2 staying closed, only the 1 re-dispatched next round, with an attribution log line.
- unit test for the effort-point split: S+M+L premium lane over threshold splits at a blocks boundary; mutex-resource members are never separated (submodule-pointer scenario pinned).
- golden transcript updated deliberately; dispatch-safety-guard count changes accounted for (one dispatch site removed/downgraded).

description (observed run 21 C1, 2026-07-22):

title: [integ] Smoke test: Harvest/PR-creation dispatch fails 'gh auth login' required -- canary never closes even after a fully APPROVED-quality sprint
description:
Feature: N/A (playbook part 2 -- smoke test, integ-test-playbook.md Test scenario step 4-5, Harvest phase)
Expected: per integ-test-playbook.md Test scenario step 5, after a successful sprint cycle the canary issue (gh-toy-4ef) should end up closed and the sprint branch should carry a commit; a real, fully-working end-to-end smoke-test pass should reach that closed state.
Actual: this cycle (SHA 1ce79a27c4b32b391b9682019fdc7bd006b7105e), a live auto-sprint run against the toy sandbox got all the way through Plan -> Develop -> Review -> Deploy -> Integ Test -> Final Review with real Planner/Doer/Reviewer dispatches all succeeding (gh-toy-4ef.1 and gh-toy-4ef.2 both implemented, tested, and closed; 33/33 tests passing) -- but the Harvest C1 phase then fails outright: '[Command Failed] Exit code 4 ... To get started with GitHub CLI, please run: gh auth login. Alternatively, populate the GH_TOKEN environment variable...'. Sprint ends FAILED and gh-toy-4ef (the parent feature/canary) is left OPEN -- never closed -- because closure is gated on the Harvest/PR step succeeding, and nothing in integ-test-playbook.md's Setup ever provisions gh CLI auth or GH_TOKEN in the sandbox HOME.
Root cause: integ-test-playbook.md's Setup/Reset sections wire the toy repo's git 'origin' to a sandbox-local bare mirror (by design, for isolation) but never configure any GitHub-hosting credential (gh auth login / GH_TOKEN) for that sandbox HOME, and the Harvest phase's PR-creation step has no fallback for a git remote with no hosting API behind it. Every real smoke-test run that reaches Harvest against this playbook's sandbox will hit this deterministically, so the canary can never reach 'closed' via the documented flow -- only the sub-tasks (gh-toy-4ef.1/.2) get closed via bd close during Develop, not the parent feature.
Test: live auto-sprint run, 2026-07-22 cycle, SHA 1ce79a27c4b32b391b9682019fdc7bd006b7105e; node dist/index.js workflow auto-sprint --issue gh-toy-4ef --members toy-doer --branch smoke-test-canary --base main --max-cycles 1 --dispatch-timeout-s 900 against a freshly Reset sandbox.
Repro: complete Setup/Reset per the playbook (no gh auth ever provisioned), run the workflow auto-sprint command above through to a clean Reviewer APPROVED verdict, observe Harvest C1 fail with the gh-auth error and gh-toy-4ef remain open.
Fix direction: either (a) the playbook's Setup should provision a throwaway/local gh auth or GH_TOKEN for the sandbox (if such a token is available in the runner's environment), or (b) the Harvest phase should detect a non-hosted (plain file://) git remote and skip PR creation, closing the canary directly instead of gating closure on a PR that can never be opened, or (c) the playbook's own Test scenario step 5 assertion should be relaxed/clarified for sandbox runs where PR hosting is unavailable by design.

title: [refactor] Add 4th model tier 'best' above premium -- cross-cutting tier-enum expansion (apra-fleet + apra-pm)
description:

  defaults remain unchanged. Existing 3-tier metadata everywhere stays valid.

title: [integ] Setup's documented clone step leaves git origin pointing at real fleet-e2e-toy, permanently failing check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs's 4th check
description:
Feature: N/A (playbook part 2 -- smoke test sandbox safety, integ-test-playbook.md ## Setup + its Neutralize/Verify subsection)
Expected: integ-test-playbook.md ## Setup's Verify step says scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs 'exits 0 (OK lines) when all three hold' after the documented neutralize sequence (YAML sed patch + bd dolt remote remove). Running it after those exact documented steps should report all-clean, since the playbook frames this as the gate before proceeding to any auto-sprint run.
Actual: the script (extended by apra-fleet-eft.31, closed) now runs a 4th check, checkGitOriginNotHazard, that asserts the sandbox clone's OWN 'git remote get-url origin' does not point at the hazard remote. But integ-test-playbook.md ## Setup's own documented step is 'git clone https://github.com/Apra-Labs/fleet-e2e-toy "$HOME/toy-repo"' -- which by definition sets git origin to that exact URL -- and neither ## Setup nor the Neutralize subsection includes any step to rewrite/unset the clone's git origin. Consequently checkGitOriginNotHazard FAILS every single time immediately after following the playbook's Setup steps verbatim, with no documented remediation in the playbook to make it pass. Reproduced this cycle: after 'bd bootstrap --yes' + the YAML sed patch + 'bd dolt remote remove origin' (all three original checks report OK), the script still exits 1 solely on check 4: 'FAIL: git origin remote in .../toy-repo is https://github.com/Apra-Labs/fleet-e2e-toy -- points at fleet-e2e-toy, so any future bd dolt invocation that auto-provisions a Dolt remote from git origin (apra-fleet-eft.30/eft.35) would re-wire straight back to the real remote even if the checks above currently report clean.'
Assessed current risk: LOW in practice right now -- apra-fleet-eft.35 (closed) already made doltPullBefore()/doltPushAfter() fail-closed on isMemberSyncRemoteConfigured (the bd-level sync.remote key, confirmed inert this run via check 1), so no 'bd dolt pull/push' should fire at all in this sandbox regardless of what git origin points to. Check 4 is a defense-in-depth guard against a hypothetical future regression re-opening a path that bypasses that pre-gate, not a currently-live exploit. Proceeded with this cycle's smoke test on that basis, watching for any 'Configured Dolt remote origin from git origin' or live push log line as a signal to treat as an eft.30/35 recurrence.
Test: node scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs "$HOME/toy-repo" immediately after the documented ## Setup + Neutralize sequence -- exits 1, only the 4th line is FAIL, other three are OK.
Repro: 1) Fresh sandbox per playbook ## Setup (install, start, git clone fleet-e2e-toy). 2) bd bootstrap --yes in $HOME/toy-repo. 3) Run the documented sed YAML patch + bd dolt remote remove origin. 4) node scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs "$HOME/toy-repo" -- exits 1 on checkGitOriginNotHazard every time, since step 1's git clone is what set origin in the first place and no step ever changes it back.
Fix direction: either (a) add a documented ## Setup or Neutralize step that rewrites/removes the sandbox clone's git origin (e.g. 'git remote set-url origin file:///dev/null' or 'git remote remove origin') and re-run the verify script after it, or (b) relax checkGitOriginNotHazard to treat a clone's own origin as expected/inert once checks 1-3 hold (its purpose per apra-fleet-eft.31 is catching a re-provisioned Dolt remote deriving from origin, not the git origin's mere existence).
close_reason: integ-test-runner (2026-07-21): no longer reproduces. Ran node scripts/check-sandbox-sync-remote.mjs $HOME/toy-repo immediately after this cycle's full documented ## Setup Neutralize sequence (YAML sed patch, bd dolt remote remove, git remote set-url origin file:///dev/null/neutralized-sandbox-origin per eft.31): all 4 checks report OK, including 'git origin remote ... does not reference fleet-e2e-toy'. Note: the origin-neutralize step itself now breaks the sprint engine's own 'git fetch origin' -- filed separately as apra-fleet-eft.47, a distinct downstream consequence, not this bug's verify-script defect.

title: Viewer unusable on large sprints: full-state polling blocks the main thread for tens of seconds
description: Measured first-hand against a live 449-activity sprint (viewer on :18300, about 3h uptime, Chrome). GET /state returns a 116 MB payload per poll (2.8s transfer); the page then JSON-parses and re-renders it on the main thread. PerformanceObserver longtask (buffered) recorded a 49634 ms long task plus a 4199 ms one; an expand click measured 0 ms in the handler but 9009 ms click-to-paint; steady-state 250 ms interval drift spikes to about 750 ms. User-visible effect: Chrome page-is-unresponsive dialog every 2-3 expand clicks -- the viewer is effectively unusable for large sprints. Payload anatomy: 679 strings of 200+ chars total 110 MB, of which only 25 MB is unique -- 85 MB (73 percent) is pure duplication, e.g. one 202-char string repeated 63 times: the same bead descriptions and command outputs are embedded again and again by every bd command activity. The existing mitigations (400 ms poll coalescing, data-rendered render-once guard, flex min-height scroll chain) are confirmed present in the served page and insufficient: they reduce render frequency, not the O(entire-history) cost of each render. Fix direction (user-specified): (1) lean list state -- activities and referenced beads carry only id, title, updatedAt and short summaries; descriptions and transcripts are NEVER embedded in list state (90 percent of use cases never open them); (2) on-demand description endpoint (GET /beads/:id/description or equivalent) fetched only when the user expands; (3) browser-side cache in localStorage keyed by bead id, validated with the last-modified/updatedAt timestamp carried in the lean list state -- dip into the cache first, refetch only when the timestamp changed; append-only payloads like agent transcripts may use content-hash keys; (4) server-side dedup for any remaining repeated strings (send each unique string once with references); (5) if any large parse remains, fetch+parse in a Web Worker. Keep everything target-agnostic and sprint-size-agnostic.
acceptance_criteria: Against a sprint with 500+ activities: 1. expand-click-to-paint under 200 ms; 2. no main-thread long task over 500 ms during steady-state polling (PerformanceObserver longtask evidence in the closing note); 3. recurring poll payload under 1 MB regardless of sprint length; 4. descriptions load on demand and repeat views hit the localStorage cache (verified by a second expand causing no network request when updatedAt is unchanged, and a refetch after the bead is updated); 5. no page-is-unresponsive dialog across a 50-expand-click session; 6. regression test pins the list-state endpoint to summary-only shape (no description/transcript fields).
notes:
MEASURED ROOT CAUSE REFINEMENT (live 188 MB /state payload dissected in-browser): the median activity event is 1 KB -- normal. The bloat is concentrated in 130 command-activity events of about 1.3 MB EACH (164 MB of the 188 MB total): every one is the complete captured stdout of bd list --all --limit 0 --json (a full project-wide beads dump with all descriptions and acceptance criteria), which the engine runs repeatedly in its scoping/sync brackets and the viewer stores verbatim in state. Prioritize accordingly: (a) cap captured command output stored in activity state -- keep a head plus tail excerpt and total byte count, with the full output available only via an on-demand endpoint -- this removes the 164 MB structurally regardless of which command is chatty; (b) generic string dedup helps less than expected here because successive dumps differ slightly as beads change; (c) the related engine-side waste of running bd list --all --limit 0 repeatedly is tracked as apra-fleet-eft.15 -- fixing the query frequency there compounds with the output cap here. The lean list-state work (eft.27.1) and localStorage/on-demand description work remain valid; this note redirects the largest remaining byte source.
USER FEEDBACK (2026-07-20, live on the eft.27.1 lean viewer during run 16): (1) KEEP THE SNAPPINESS -- the lightweight fast experience of the lean viewer is loved and is the top constraint; no fix may regress it. (2) Detail viewing gap: there is currently NO way to view full descriptions / LLM call output in the viewer. Required UX: ONLY the lowest-level widget (an individual activity item) gets a 'more...' button that loads FULL detail for that ONE item on demand (via the on-demand endpoints); header/title ellipses must NOT be expandable -- truncated titles stay truncated. One item expanded at a time. (3) Scroll problem NOT fixed: the scrollability crisis is still present in the lean viewer and still needs a real fix.
MINOR BUG (user-observed via Save button, 2026-07-20): the viewer's Save/download exports globalState which still carries the top-level _strings dedup table (114 entries in the observed file) even though every $ref was already resolved inline -- the table is pure duplicated dead weight in the saved workflow-state.json and misleads readers into thinking the file is interned. Fix: strip _strings from the resolved state after resolveStringRefs() in poll() (or exclude it in saveState()) in packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/viewer/index.mjs.

title: Reservation interop gap: workflow/cli-launched sprints are invisible to the supervisor
description: Server-side member reservation (eft.10.1-.3) is enforced one-directionally. Direction A works: a supervisor-launched sprint reserves its members (ledger drives server reserve/release via member_reservation), and execute-prompt.ts rejects any dispatch to a member whose reservedBy names a different sprint (currentSprintId from APRA_FLEET_SPRINT_ID stamped by the supervisor spawner into the per-sprint server env), so a workflow-launched sprint (currentSprintId undefined) cannot dispatch to a supervisor-reserved member. Direction B is a gap with two holes. Hole 1: a sprint launched directly via apra-fleet workflow auto-sprint (or bin/cli.mjs) never reserves its members server-side -- neither cli.mjs nor auto-sprint/runner.js calls member_reservation at sprint start or release at sprint end (the only reserve/release logic there is the bead id-allocator, unrelated). Hole 2: the supervisor launch overlap guard (defaultMemberOverlapGuard in packages/apra-fleet-se/src/supervisor/api.mjs) consults only its own ledger.list(), never the fleet server reservedBy field, so even a reservation made by other means is not seen at launch validation. Net effect: while a workflow-launched sprint runs on member M, POST /api/sprints with members including M is accepted (no 409) and two sprints interleave dispatches on M -- the unsafe concurrent-sprint case apra-fleet-qv1 describes; the per-member busy-lock only prevents moment-to-moment dispatch overlap, not cross-sprint interleaving. Fix direction: (1) runner.js reserves every sprint member server-side at sprint start (sprint id = the same identity used for the dolt-mutex/allocator) and releases in the finally path including abort; (2) defaultMemberOverlapGuard additionally reads the server member records (list_members reservedBy) and rejects a launch overlapping ANY server-side reservation, naming the owning sprint id; (3) the supervisor /api/members reservation overlay shows server-side reservations too. All surfaces stay target-agnostic: sprint id is opaque, no assumptions about which repo the sprint develops.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A sprint launched via apra-fleet workflow auto-sprint (and via bin/cli.mjs directly) reserves each members entry server-side at startup and releases on every exit path (success, stall-abort, SIGINT); unit tests cover the reserve/release bracket. 2. With such a sprint holding member M, POST /api/sprints whose member union includes M returns 409 naming the owning sprint id; unit test covers ledger-empty-but-server-reserved. 3. GET /api/members shows the server-side reservation for M. 4. Release on abnormal exit (killed child) is verified via lease expiry or watchdog force-release and documented.
close_reason: Verified 2026-07-20/21: reservation-interop-e2e.test.mjs (eft.26.3, exercising the eft.26.1+eft.26.2 fix pair end to end) passed clean in playbook part 1's 85/85 real-bd suite.

title: (BUG) First-run onboarding banner corrupts JSON tool responses on the very first MCP call after fresh install
description:
Discovered during apra-fleet-eft.22 (undici bundling re-verification) end-to-end smoke of a fresh dev-mode install.

Repro: fresh sandbox HOME, 'node dist/index.js install' + 'start', 'register-member' via the CLI (src/cli/register-member.ts calls tools/register-member.ts directly, bypassing the MCP tool-registry wrapTool() onboarding path entirely), then run 'node dist/index.js workflow auto-sprint ...'. auto-sprint's cli.mjs (packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/cli.mjs ~line 524) calls fleetApi.listMembers({format:'json'}) as its first-ever MCP tool call against this server session, then does JSON.parse(listRes.content[0].text) assuming content[0] is the raw JSON payload.

Root cause: src/services/tool-registry.ts wrapTool()'s getOnboardingPreamble() (line ~59) calls getFirstRunPreamble() and returns the banner UNCONDITIONALLY when !bannerShown, before checking isJson -- see the isJson check only guards getWelcomeBackPreamble(), not the first-run banner. So on a truly fresh server, the first MCP tool call to ANY active tool (including JSON-typed ones like list_members) gets a content[0] block of '<apra-fleet-display>...banner...</apra-fleet-display>' prepended ahead of the actual JSON text, breaking any machine caller that assumes content[0] is the JSON payload. Client-visible symptom: 'Error: Failed to list fleet members: Unexpected token '<', "<apra-flee"... is not valid JSON', and the sprint aborts before Sprint Setup.

Impact: because register-member is CLI-only and bypasses the banner-consuming tool-registry path, list_members via auto-sprint's cli.mjs is typically the literal first MCP tool call after a fresh install in the real 'install -> register-member -> auto-sprint' flow, so this reproduces on essentially every very first auto-sprint launch on a fresh install (bannerShown is persisted after the first call, so retries/subsequent runs do not repro).

Fix direction: getOnboardingPreamble() should only return the first-run banner for non-JSON-response tool calls (move the isJson check above the getFirstRunPreamble() call, matching the existing isJson guard on getWelcomeBackPreamble()), OR cli.mjs's JSON-consuming call sites should scan content[] for the block without an <apra-fleet-display> wrapper instead of assuming content[0].

Not part of apra-fleet-eft.22/eft.19 scope (those are specifically about undici module resolution, which is independently confirmed fixed -- see eft.22 close notes). Filing separately per the acceptance-criteria instruction to report concrete issues found without folding them into the undici verification.
close_reason: Fixed: moved isJson check above getFirstRunPreamble() in getOnboardingPreamble() (src/services/tool-registry.ts), matching the existing getWelcomeBackPreamble() guard. Banner is now deferred (not lost) until the next non-JSON active-tool call, so a JSON-typed tool's content[0] is never corrupted on the first call after a fresh install. Updated tests/onboarding.test.ts and tests/onboarding-smoke.mjs which had encoded the old JSON-bypass behavior (from commit 75d36972 / PR #101) as expected; added a regression test asserting a JSON-typed tool's first-ever call on a fresh server returns parseable, unprefixed content[0]. Full vitest suite: 2361 passed / 12 skipped. Build clean.

title: [impl] Fix integ-test-playbook.md Teardown tilde no-op: capture absolute sandbox path before reassigning HOME
description: In integ-test-playbook.md the Teardown block (around lines 153-157) exports HOME=~/temp/.apra-fleet-tests and then runs rm -rf ~/temp/.apra-fleet-tests. title: [integ] integ-test-playbook.md Teardown: 'rm -rf ~/temp/.apra-fleet-tests' silently no-ops because HOME was already overridden to that same path earlier in the block
description:
Feature: integ-test-playbook.md ## Teardown section (not a product feature -- filing as [integ] since it is a real, reproducible defect discovered while running the playbook)
Expected: Teardown 'stops the server and deletes the sandbox entirely, so no state accumulates or drifts from a fresh install between runs' (playbook's own stated purpose).
Actual: The Teardown block is:
  export HOME=~/temp/.apra-fleet-tests
  export USERPROFILE="$HOME"
  export APRA_FLEET_PORT=18700
  node dist/index.js stop
  rm -rf ~/temp/.apra-fleet-tests
Because HOME is reassigned to the sandbox path on line 1, bash's tilde expansion on the LAST line now resolves '~' using the NEW (already-overridden) $HOME, not the real user home. So 'rm -rf ~/temp/.apra-fleet-tests' actually targets $REAL_HOME/temp/.apra-fleet-tests/temp/.apra-fleet-tests, which does not exist. rm -rf on a nonexistent path exits 0 and prints nothing, so the failure is completely silent -- the command 'succeeds' while leaving the real sandbox directory ($REAL_HOME/temp/.apra-fleet-tests) fully intact on disk. Same class of issue would also affect USERPROFILE-based tilde expansion on Windows if PowerShell/cmd similarly re-resolved after the reassignment (not verified on this run -- this run is macOS/zsh).
Test: Ran integ-test-playbook.md Setup, Test scenario, and Teardown verbatim during a smoke-test pass. After running the Teardown block exactly as written (copy-paste), $HOME/temp/.apra-fleet-tests still existed on disk with the full sandbox (.apra-fleet, .beads, .claude, .dolt, toy-repo, etc.) untouched, even though 'node dist/index.js stop' correctly stopped the server and the shell reported no error.
Repro:
1. In a fresh shell: export HOME=~/temp/.apra-fleet-tests (some path that does not yet exist is fine)
2. rm -rf ~/temp/.apra-fleet-tests
3. Observe this targets $HOME/temp/.apra-fleet-tests (i.e. .../temp/.apra-fleet-tests/temp/.apra-fleet-tests using the reassigned HOME), not the original real-$HOME/temp/.apra-fleet-tests -- confirm via 'echo ~/temp/.apra-fleet-tests' after the export to see the resolved path change.
Workaround used this run: deleted the sandbox with an explicit absolute path (/Users/<user>/temp/.apra-fleet-tests) instead of the tilde form, so the sandbox WAS actually removed before returning results -- but the playbook's own copy-paste block does not self-correct this, so every future run following it verbatim will silently accumulate/reuse a stale sandbox directory unless the runner notices independently.
Suggested fix direction (not applied -- do not modify integ-test-playbook.md per runner contract; a maintainer should update it): compute/store the absolute sandbox path in a variable BEFORE reassigning HOME (e.g. SANDBOX="$HOME/temp/.apra-fleet-tests" as the very first line, then 'rm -rf "$SANDBOX"' at the end), or use $USERPROFILE/$REAL_HOME captured pre-export, in both ## Teardown and anywhere else in the file that exports HOME and later re-uses a tilde path in the same block.
close_reason: Fix verified: current integ-test-playbook.md Teardown already uses the SANDBOX="$HOME/temp/.apra-fleet-tests" pattern (captured before HOME reassignment) as suggested. Re-ran Teardown verbatim this cycle (2026-07-20): rm -rf "$SANDBOX" correctly removed the sandbox (confirmed via ls exiting 'No such file or directory' afterward), no stale directory left behind.

title: [bug] execute_prompt busy-lock leaks: fleet_status idle but dispatch rejected with reason busy
description:
Observed twice on fleet server v0.3.5_8a1ef3 (log fleet-26772.log):
- 2026-07-19: fleet-dev held a busy lock ~20 min while idle (frozen token counts, no live process); during the apra-fleet-0ei hotfix track.
- 2026-07-20: two consecutive execute_prompt dispatches to fleet-dev returned {isError:true, reason:busy} while fleet_status reported the member idle (last session ~10h old).
Both times stop_prompt cleared it and reported 'no active session was running', proving the lock was stale, not a live prompt.

Likely cause: the in-flight dispatch lock (inFlightAgents or equivalent) is not released on some abandoned/killed dispatch path (client disconnect, process reap race).

Acceptance criteria:
- Lock release is tied to child-process reap AND client disconnect (no path leaves a lock with no live process).
- Add a TTL or liveness check: a busy rejection must verify the locked session has a live process; if not, self-heal (release + allow dispatch) and log a warning.
- fleet_status and the dispatch gate must agree: a member reported idle can never be rejected as busy.
- Regression test simulating an orphaned lock.
close_reason: Integ-verified 2026-08-01 (independent audit of merged iuc work). findDeadLockPid (src/tools/execute-prompt.ts:322-352) covers all five branches, each driven through the REAL executePrompt() entry point by tests: remote pid dead self-heals via fresh SSH kill-0 probe (execute-prompt-idb-busy-lock.test.ts:68), remote pid alive stays busy (:174), local pid dead via isPidAlive/ESRCH with no SSH round trip (:108), interactive sessionRegistry pid dead (:136), no-pid-still-busy (:212). Lock release is wired to BOTH child reap (execute-prompt.ts:1193-1196 finally) and client disconnect (abortHandler + MCP disconnect cleanup test execute-prompt.test.ts:1122/1140). Busyness-surface agreement asserted at execute-prompt-idb-busy-lock.test.ts:244-303 (dispatch gate outcome + statusline idle record in the same test; noted caveat: uses writeStatusline as the second surface, not a literal fleet_status call). RESIDUAL GAP recorded: a busy-lock leak that occurs BEFORE pid capture leaves no pid to probe, and the no-pid branch deliberately stays busy -- if the original wedge ever recurs in that exact shape, reopen THIS bead with the new forensics rather than filing a duplicate.

title: fleet-sprint: budget-aware streak sizing and review scheduling (predict per-task cost, negotiate streak length vs review frequency against a cost budget)
description:
IDEA (from project owner, solidified via background fable-model design pass, then revised to integrate the review-yield angle -- not yet implemented, not yet sized into a real DAG):

Sprint cost is primarily driven by streak count and review count. Smaller streaks -> more streaks -> more reviews; reviews are overhead (a countermeasure against doer/planner errors), so given a limited cost budget, longer streaks + fewer reviews could reduce cost -- IF per-task cost can be predicted well enough to negotiate the tradeoff deliberately, rather than just degrading quality blindly. Second, owner-added angle: a review only earns its cost when it says CHANGES_NEEDED; a review that returns APPROVED-with-nothing-wrong is pure overhead. The historical CHANGES_NEEDED ratio ("review yield") is therefore a direct empirical measure of whether a given doer/model/bucket combination is over- or under-reviewed -- and because apra-fleet runs doers across heterogeneous providers (Claude, OpenCode, Antigravity/agy) at very different capability/cost tiers, yield-driven review tuning doubles as an automatic quality-equalizer across those providers, not just a cost lever.

=== Solidified proposal (rev 2: review-yield integrated as a first-class signal) ===

1. PREDICTION FROM EXISTING DATA: two companion metrics, both derived from the same instrumentation.

1a. COST PREDICTION: `bd remember` already persists per-task/role/model token usage (e.g. "apra-fleet-04a.3 claude-sonnet-4-6 tokens: input=85000 output=8000"). Group historical entries by (role, model tier, complexity bucket S/M/L from plan-reviewer's taskAssignments); predict a task at its group's median cost (token distributions are right-skewed by retry/CHANGES_NEEDED loops -- use median not mean), with p80 used for budget-feasibility checks. Hierarchical fallback when a group is thin: (role,tier,bucket) -> (role,tier) -> (role) -> hardcoded prior. A full regression model is NOT justified given sample sizes and mostly-categorical variance drivers.

1b. REVIEW YIELD (new, co-equal metric): for every review dispatched, record the verdict outcome and track yield = fraction of reviews producing CHANGES_NEEDED (or otherwise causing a reopen), grouped by the DOER's (provider/model, tier, bucket) -- keyed to the doer, not the reviewer, because yield measures the doer's error rate as seen through review, which is exactly the quantity review frequency should be calibrated against. Same hierarchical fallback as 1a, with a deliberately conservative prior (assume moderate-to-high yield, i.e. "reviews are useful") for thin groups so a new/unproven doer model starts fully reviewed and must EARN reduced coverage through accumulated APPROVED verdicts. Yield is the empirical signal that drives review frequency (section 3); cost pressure (section 2) remains a separate, combinable signal. If 8/10 reviews of a given group historically return APPROVED with nothing wrong, that group's review cadence is demonstrably over-provisioned relative to its actual error rate -- independent of any budget concern.

New instrumentation needed (serves both 1a and 1b): (a) normalize `bd remember` entries into a machine-parseable convention (e.g. `cost/<bead>/<role>` key with a JSON value: provider, model, tier, bucket, tokens, review-round-count) instead of today's free text; (b) record per-review outcome records (e.g. `review/<bead>/<n>`: doer provider/model/tier/bucket, verdict, whether it caused a reopen, reviewer tier/cost) -- review-round-count and reopen probability fall out of this and also feed the cost predictor, since CHANGES_NEEDED loops multiply cost.

2. NEGOTIATION MECHANISM -- two independent levers, applied together:

2a. BUDGET PRESSURE (cost lever, as before): at the start of each Develop phase, compute `predicted_remaining` (sum of median doer cost for ready/open tasks + predicted review cost under current policy + fixed per-cycle overhead) and `pressure = predicted_remaining / budget.remaining()` (the budget object/remaining() already exists per apra-fleet-unw2.8/N10). Three regimes: pressure <= 0.8 -> no budget-driven change; 0.8-1.3 -> economy mode (hint the streak-assignment prompt to prefer fewer/longer streaks capped at K tasks, shift review granularity toward per-streak); pressure > 1.3 -> infeasible, do NOT silently degrade further -- descope (defer lowest-priority ready leaves via the harvester's existing deferral mechanism) or halt with a budget report. Recompute every cycle so early actuals relax/tighten the policy.

2b. YIELD-DRIVEN REVIEW RATE (quality-calibration lever, new -- active even at zero budget pressure): each (doer provider/model, tier, bucket) group carries a target review rate derived from its historical yield. Sustained low yield (e.g. <20% CHANGES_NEEDED over a minimum sample, say n>=10 reviews) is evidence of over-provisioned review for that group and justifies reducing its review frequency on quality-efficiency grounds alone; high yield (e.g. >50%) justifies per-task review plus tighter mid-streak checkpoints (section 3) regardless of budget slack. Guardrails: never drop a group's sampling rate below a floor (e.g. p >= 0.15) so yield statistics keep refreshing and a degrading model gets re-detected; any reopen or post-sprint bug attributed to an under-reviewed group immediately snaps that group back to full review until yield re-earns the reduction (fast-down on bad news, slow-up on good news).

Interaction rule: pressure-driven cuts must be yield-aware, not uniform. Under budget pressure, review reductions come FIRST and DEEPEST from low-yield groups (where reviews are statistically least likely to catch anything); high-yield groups keep or even gain review coverage under pressure, because cutting exactly where reviews fire most is how quality degrades blindly -- the failure mode this whole proposal exists to avoid. If pressure demands cuts beyond what low-yield groups can absorb, that is a descope/halt signal (the pressure > 1.3 branch), not a license to cut high-yield review.

3. RISK-WEIGHTED REVIEW SCHEDULING -- do not compound levers naively: the naive version (longer streaks AND fewer reviews) doubles down on the same failure mode (streak-length risk is exactly what review exists to catch). Mechanism: allocate review coverage per-streak proportional to predicted risk, where historical review yield for the streak's doer group is now a first-class input to the risk score alongside streak length, bucket sizes, historical reopen rate, and cross-streak file overlap. A long/heavy streak or any streak run by a high-yield (error-prone) doer group always gets fully reviewed; a short/cheap streak run by a sustained-low-yield doer group can be sampled (reviewed with probability p, bounded below per 2b's floor). Mid-streak checkpoints every N tasks inside long streaks remain (a cheap-tier "sanity" pass over the doer's existing VERIFY checkpoint output: build passes, diff touches expected files, commit-per-task discipline held) at ~10% of full review cost, bounding context-degradation blast radius to N tasks -- and N itself tightens for high-yield doer groups. Hard floors: final-review/integration phases are never skipped regardless of mode or yield; the per-group sampling floor of 2b always applies.

3b. CROSS-MODEL QUALITY BALANCING (apra-fleet differentiator): because apra-fleet dispatches doers across providers -- premium Claude tiers, cheaper OpenCode-hosted models, Antigravity/agy -- the same yield-driven mechanism automatically equalizes output quality across radically different doer cost/capability profiles with zero provider-specific hand-tuning. Concretely: a cheap-tier OpenCode doer will empirically show high review yield and elevated reopen rates, so the mechanism holds it at high review frequency and tight checkpoint spacing (self-correcting: its total cost = cheap doer + heavy review, which may still beat premium-doer + light review); a premium Claude doer with sustained near-100% APPROVED yield earns progressively lighter review over time. Both ends of the spectrum are handled by one policy reading one statistic. This also makes the cost predictor's economics honest: the true cost of running a task on a cheap model INCLUDES its yield-implied review and reopen overhead, so the system can eventually compare "cheap doer + heavy review" vs "expensive doer + light review" as total-cost alternatives per bucket -- a natural future extension (doer-model selection by total predicted cost at equal quality), explicitly out of scope for this epic but enabled by this data.

4. VALIDATION BEFORE DEFAULT-ON: backtest first at zero cost, for BOTH metrics -- (a) cost: replay past sprints' recorded costs against the predictor, report per-group MAPE and fraction of tasks under the p80 bound (target >=80%); (b) yield: replay past sprints' review verdicts, report per-group yield estimates with confidence intervals and check stability (does a group's yield in the first half of history predict its second half? flag groups too thin or too noisy to act on). Stop here if either predictor is bad; in particular, do not activate lever 2b for any group whose yield estimate is unstable. Then A/B on the fleet-e2e-toy harness: matched sprints (same seed backlog), optimization off vs on with budget set to ~70% of the unconstrained run's actual spend; where feasible, include at least one heterogeneous-doer configuration (mixed Claude + OpenCode doers) to exercise the cross-model balancing path of 3b. Measure total spend, review count and per-group yield, reopen count, reviewer CHANGES_NEEDED rate, post-sprint bug count (integ-test-runner), final-review verdicts. Acceptance: >=20% cost reduction with reopen/bug rate increase bounded by an agreed epsilon, AND no under-reviewed group's bug contribution exceeding its full-review baseline by more than epsilon. Ship behind a flag (--budget-optimize), default OFF, with both the pressure computation and per-group yield table printed even when off ("shadow mode") so predictions accumulate credibility before being trusted.

5. SCOPE/SIZING: not small. Four touchpoints -- (a) a new cost-and-yield history module (parse/normalize bd remember entries, compute per-group cost stats AND per-group review-yield stats with the fallback chain and stability checks) -- contained and independently testable, modestly larger than the cost-only version; (b) a memory-format convention change plus every token-usage-recording call site, now also including per-review outcome recording at every review-verdict-handling site; (c) runner.js Develop-phase changes: pressure computation, yield-aware review-rate policy (2b) and its guardrails, streak-prompt hint, review-dispatch gating, mid-streak checkpoint -- the risky part, since runner.js is already ~2000+ lines with careful fallback semantics that must survive (e.g. the one-bead-per-streak fallback), and 2b's snap-back-on-reopen path adds state that must be robust; (d) the validation harness runs themselves, including the mixed-provider A/B leg. Estimate: one epic, 5-7 tasks, mostly M/L bucket. RECOMMENDED FIRST SLICE (shippable with zero behavior change): the history module (cost + yield) + shadow-mode reporting of both the pressure number and the per-group yield table, with no actual streak/review-policy changes yet -- lets prediction accuracy AND yield stability get validated in production before any decision logic depends on either, and starts accumulating the per-provider yield history that 3b's cross-model balancing needs on day one.

title: fleet-sprint: run3 (fleet-rev) failed cleanly at Plan phase -- fleet-rev missing all .claude/agents/*.md role definitions
description:
OBSERVED: run3 (task b1fggpgwn), same branch/issue as run1/run2 but with --members fleet-rev instead of fleet-reorg, failed at the very first Plan phase. Root cause was immediately visible and fully logged (unlike run1/run2's silent deaths -- see below for why that contrast matters):

  [Workflow Log] Planner: execute_prompt: agent "planner" not found on "fleet-rev".
  Expected at:
    /Users/akhil/git/apra-fleet/.claude/agents/planner.md
    ~/.claude/agents/planner.md

This repeated for 3 planning rounds (schema-repair exhausted each time since the "planner" dispatch itself never ran), then SprintPlanRejectedError correctly aborted cycle 1 rather than proceeding with an unapproved plan. cli.mjs's own try/catch handled it cleanly: full stack trace logged, "Sprint failed:", dashboard kept alive for the 300s grace window, orchestrator exited via its own process.exit(process.exitCode||1) -- a normal, fully-visible failure path.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR auto-sprint-4/-6: this is the first time in three runs we've seen cli.mjs's OWN error-handling machinery actually fire and produce output. Runs 1 and 2 (fleet-reorg) never printed anything like "Sprint failed:" or a stack trace before going silent -- confirming that whatever killed those runs was NOT a caught application-level failure (that code path clearly works and is verbose when it does fire). This strengthens the external-kill hypothesis in auto-sprint-4 rather than weakening it.

ROOT CAUSE: fleet-rev is a newly-onboarded remote member (its beads workspace was itself only just bootstrapped this session, see prior work) that never received the auto-sprint role-agent definitions (planner.md, plan-reviewer.md, doer.md, reviewer.md, harvester.md, deployer.md, integ-test-runner.md, ci-watcher.md, plus _shared/ and schemas/ support dirs) that fleet-reorg has via the shared Windows-user home directory (C:\Users\akhil\.claude\agents\). fleet-rev's home directory is a separate machine (192.168.1.13) with none of these.

FIX APPLIED: packaged C:\Users\akhil\.claude\agents\ into a tarball, transferred via the apra-fleet MCP `send_files` tool to fleet-rev's work-folder root, then dispatched a background agent to extract it into fleet-rev's repo-local `.claude/agents/` (the first of the two lookup paths execute_prompt checks) via `execute_command`. Retry pending confirmation the extraction succeeded.

SECONDARY (non-fatal) ISSUE ALSO SEEN: `finalizeAbort()`'s git diff during the abort path failed with "fatal: ambiguous argument 'feat/fleet-reorg..auto-sprint/eft-service': unknown revision or path not in the working tree" -- fleet-rev's local checkout likely doesn't have both branches fetched/known yet. This was handled gracefully (fell back to writing terminal history with no PR lookup) but is worth fixing properly: the sprint's branch-ensure phase should guarantee both --base and --branch are resolvable refs on the dispatched member before any git diff against them is attempted.
notes: triage 2026-08-09 (autosprint-internals batch): ALREADY-FIXED. NAMING -- stale 'auto-sprint' for fleet-sprint (cli.mjs, SprintPlanRejectedError, --members, finalizeAbort; bead namespace predates the 2026-07-26 rename 058160e7). PRIMARY issue was never an app bug: member fleet-rev had simply never been provisioned with the role-agent .md definitions, and the bead itself records the remediation applied in-session (agents tarball shipped via send_files, extracted into fleet-rev's repo-local .claude/agents/). One-off environment gap, not reproducible from the code. SECONDARY issue -- finalizeAbort()'s git diff failing on 'ambiguous argument <base>..<branch>: unknown revision' because the member had not fetched both refs -- IS now fixed in code and verified by read: finalizeAbort() performs 'git fetch origin <baseBranch>' before its diff (fleet-sprint/runner.js:4359, with an explicit '[Abort Finalize Failed] git fetch ... failed' guard at :4365), and the branch-ensure path fetches BOTH refs up front ('git fetch origin <baseBranch> --quiet' :5567 and 'git fetch origin <branch> --quiet' :5583) -- exactly the fix this bead asked for. Its remaining diagnostic value (evidence that cli.mjs's error path is verbose when it fires, strengthening auto-sprint-4's external-kill hypothesis) is already recorded in auto-sprint-4's own notes. Closing as fixed.
close_reason: Triage 2026-08-09: primary cause was a one-off member-provisioning gap on fleet-rev, remediated in-session (agents shipped via send_files) -- not a code defect. The secondary, genuinely-code-level issue (finalizeAbort git diff against unfetched refs) is fixed and verified live: finalizeAbort git-fetches the base ref before diffing (fleet-sprint/runner.js:4359-4365) and the branch-ensure path fetches both --base and --branch up front (:5567, :5583). No residual work.

title: auto-sprint: docs/README.md instructs bypassing the sanctioned Workflow tool via disowned background process
description:
OBSERVED: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/docs/README.md (apra-fleet-reorg repo) instructs agents to launch sprints via a raw `node bin/cli.mjs ... &` + `disown` background process, and explicitly tells agents NOT to use Claude Code's Workflow tool, claiming `Workflow({name:"auto-sprint"})` "fails immediately with Error: require is not defined, before any sprint phase runs."

ANALYSIS:
1. This claim is false or at least misleading: a legitimate `auto-sprint` skill IS registered and invocable in this session (Skill tool), and it resolves to `Workflow({ name: "auto-sprint", args: {...} })` -- which is the documented, sanctioned path. I confirmed this via the skill's own instructions.
2. The README's prescribed pattern (raw detached process + disown, explicitly justified as "so it survives the tool call's process group being killed") matches the exact anti-pattern this project's root CLAUDE.md warns against: "Do not author a wrapper script, alternate binary, or other workaround whose purpose is to bypass the block, even if the underlying operation is judged safe" (citing the 2026-07-02 scripts/recovery.sh incident in RECOVERY.md).
3. User (akhil) reviewed this concern, explicitly authorized trusting the README ("the old auto-sprint is being retired as it is locked into claude"), and later explicitly instructed running the literal command from README line 14 for apra-fleet-eft.
4. Compromise taken: launched via Bash `run_in_background` (harness-tracked, stoppable, notifies on exit) rather than shell `&`+`disown`, achieving the same practical effect (survives this tool call) without deliberately evading session tracking.
5. OPEN QUESTION for a human to resolve: is this README genuinely current project guidance reflecting a real migration away from Workflow-locked auto-sprint, or is it a stale/planted doc that should be corrected/removed now that the Workflow-based auto-sprint skill demonstrably works? Recommend verifying with whoever authored the README before more agents/sessions read and act on it.
close_reason: No longer reproduces: fleet-sprint/docs/README.md (post-rename) no longer claims Workflow({name:auto-sprint}) fails immediately or instructs bypassing the Workflow tool. It now gives factual backgrounding guidance (nohup/disown, PowerShell Start-Process) for a genuinely long-running process, which is legitimate advice, not the anti-pattern this bead flagged.

title: [impl] Path B: discard-and-re-bootstrap fallback with mutation replay and Windows gotchas
description:
Files: the dolt-recovery module (Path B branch).

Implement the verified Path B fallback: rm .beads/embeddeddolt, .beads/metadata.json, .beads/backup (KEEP config.yaml with sync.remote), then BD_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 bd bootstrap --yes, then replay the one pending mutation. Handle the two verified Windows gotchas: (1) broken git+C:/ URL derivation when sync.remote is absent -- hence keeping config.yaml; (2) a leftover empty DB makes the retry fail until embeddeddolt is removed. This accepts discarding the loser clone's other unsynced local state, which is kept small by design (one streak worth of writes) -- log exactly what was discarded.
acceptance_criteria: Path B recovers a wedged clone end-to-end (test) and replays the pending mutation so it is not lost; config.yaml with sync.remote is preserved (asserted) while embeddeddolt/metadata.json/backup are removed; both Windows gotchas are covered by tests or explicit guards; the discarded local state is enumerated in the log rather than silently dropped.

title: [impl] Path A: scripted resolve-in-place dolt conflict recovery behind two deterministic gates
description:
Files: new src/supervisor/ or auto-sprint/ dolt-recovery module (orchestrator script, NO agent dispatch).

Implement the VERIFIED (2026-07-16) 10-step Path A runbook from plan 3.4, exactly: detect via bd dolt pull exit code/error text; start dolt sql-server --data-dir .beads/embeddeddolt on an ephemeral loopback port, externally managed (bd dolt start uses the wrong dir -- GH#2438); flip metadata.json to dolt_mode server; re-open the aborted merge with SET @@dolt_allow_commit_conflicts = 1; CALL dolt_merge(origin/main) (the step upstream docs omit); SELECT * FROM dolt_conflicts as the gate; CALL dolt_conflicts_resolve with the REQUIRED table-name arg; dolt_commit; pull+push; teardown and flip back to embedded (reversibility was verified, zero data loss). Gate the whole procedure on TWO deterministic checks: (1) the conflicting table is issues (or an explicitly extended allowlist) AND (2) a plain single-row conflict shape. HARD PREREQUISITE: apra-fleet-ire provides the portable dolt CLI -- this runbook is unusable without it.
acceptance_criteria: Path A runs end-to-end as a command()-driven procedure with zero agent dispatch against a deliberately wedged test clone, passing both gates, with zero data loss and both sides history present in dolt_log; metadata.json is flipped back to embedded and the sql-server torn down even on failure (reversibility asserted); the dolt_merge step and the table-name arg to dolt_conflicts_resolve are present; a multi-row or non-issues-table conflict does NOT proceed (gate rejects it).

title: [impl] Globally-coordinated child-id allocator for shared-parent bead creation
description:
Files: new src/supervisor/ id-allocator module + the runner.js bead-creation path.

PoC-confirmed constraint C.4: concurrent child creation under a shared parent produces genuine child-id collisions; allocation must be sequential per parent. Implement a globally-coordinated allocator (supervisor-owned, same authority as the push mutex) for any scope where two sprints can create children under a shared parent, so that two sprints never mint the same child id.
acceptance_criteria: A test recreating the C.4 concurrent same-parent creation scenario produces zero id collisions; allocation is sequential per parent and concurrent across different parents (not one global lock for everything); allocator state survives supervisor restart; a child that dies mid-allocation does not leak or reserve a permanent gap that breaks later allocation.
close_reason: Globally-coordinated per-parent child-id allocator implemented in src/supervisor/id-allocator.mjs, wired into the supervisor over HTTP; supervisor-id-allocator.test.mjs covers C.4 zero-collision concurrency, independent concurrent parents, restart persistence, dead-pid/lease-expiry reclamation, floor seeding, and the null-client seam; verified passing (15 tests).

title: [impl] Service-side global dolt push mutex serializing all cross-sprint dolt writes
description:
Files: new src/supervisor/ dolt-mutex module + an API for children to acquire/release; runner.js call sites in the D-push bracket.

PoC-confirmed constraint C.2: ANY concurrent write to the same row hard-conflicts (row-level, NOT cell-level, in bd 1.1.0 embedded mode -- the disjoint-field re-test refuted the upstream cell-level claim), and C.3: one unresolved conflict wedges the ENTIRE clone sync. Therefore this mutex is a LOAD-BEARING v1 requirement, not a fallback: all cross-sprint dolt writes serialize through the supervisor. Needs a lease/timeout so a crashed child cannot wedge the mutex forever, and release on every terminal path.
acceptance_criteria: Two concurrent sprints never execute a dolt push at the same time (test with two children asserts non-overlapping push windows); the mutex is released on success, failure, and child crash (lease expiry test); a crashed holder does not wedge the mutex permanently; acquisition is fair enough to avoid starvation (FIFO); the mutex lives in the supervisor, not per-child.

title: [impl] D-pull/D-push bracket helpers and 3.3 table insertion points (incl. D-pull before the post-streak bd show read)

Conflict policy is first-successful-pusher-wins with ours/theirs fixed mechanically by which clone resolves -- never per-conflict judgment.

title: [impl] Tier 1 scripted git conflict detection and clean-state restore
description:
Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js sync helpers.

Plan 3.4 git ladder, script-first posture. Tier 0 prevention is exclusive per-sprint branch ownership + rebase-before-push + sequential streaks (covered by sibling tasks). This task implements Tier 1 SCRIPTED detection: read the git pull --rebase exit code, detect unmerged paths via git status --porcelain, and run git rebase --abort to restore a clean state before raising the typed diverged error. Tier 2 (agent-with-runbook dispatch) is reserved ONLY for semantically overlapping edits to the same lines that a fixed ours/theirs policy structurally cannot arbitrate -- do not dispatch an agent for anything a script can decide.
acceptance_criteria: A rebase conflict is detected from the exit code plus porcelain unmerged paths; git rebase --abort restores a clean working tree (asserted: porcelain empty afterwards) before the typed diverged error propagates; no agent is dispatched at Tier 1; the escalation point to Tier 2 is a single documented, testable branch.

Plan 3.3: for synced mode, checkMemberTopology stops requiring identical HEADs across members (that requirement is what forces a shared workspace). New precondition: every member reports the same git remote get-url origin value AND passes a working bd dolt pull probe. Legacy shared-workspace mode keeps the same-HEAD check unchanged. Mode selection must be explicit, not inferred silently.
acceptance_criteria: In synced mode, members with different HEADs but the same origin URL and a passing dolt probe are accepted; a member with a divergent origin URL or a failing dolt probe is rejected with a message naming the member and the failed precondition; legacy mode still enforces same-HEAD (regression test); both modes covered by tests; every probe command passes an explicit member_name.

title: [impl] G-push before D-push ordering for code-writing roles; G-push failure skips D-push and fails the streak
description:
Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js (doer and harvester post-dispatch paths).

Plan 3.3 push ordering: for code-writing roles (doer, harvester ONLY), G-push MUST succeed BEFORE D-push. If G-push cannot be resolved, D-push MUST NOT run -- the streak is recorded failed with the explicit log message about not advertising an unreachable close (closing a bead in dolt while the code that justifies it is unpushed is the exact failure this prevents).
acceptance_criteria: For doer/harvester, D-push is never invoked unless G-push succeeded first (test injects a G-push failure and asserts zero D-push calls); on G-push failure the streak is recorded failed with the explicit not-advertising-an-unreachable-close log message; non-code-writing roles are unaffected by this ordering rule.

title: [impl] Make doer streak dispatch globally sequential across members
description:
Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js (memberLocks, around lines 1966-1978).

Today only SAME-member streaks serialize via memberLocks. The token-passing stance requires doer streak dispatch to be GLOBALLY sequential across different members too -- confirmed required even for just two sequential heterogeneous members (x86 + ARM64 hand-off), because concurrent writers break the fast-forward-by-construction invariant. Replace the per-member lock chain with a global sequencing gate for doer streaks. Merger-agent / parallel streaks are explicitly deferred to Phase 3+ -- do not build toward them here. Related known-bug context: apra-fleet-qv1.
acceptance_criteria: Two doer streaks assigned to DIFFERENT members execute strictly one-after-another (test asserts non-overlapping dispatch windows); same-member serialization still holds; the global gate is released on every terminal path including thrown/failed streaks (no deadlock on failure -- explicit test); no parallel/merger path is introduced.

title: [impl] syncMemberBefore/syncMemberAfter helpers: G-pull ff-only, G-push with bounded pull-rebase-retry, typed errors
description:
Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js (new exported helpers), packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/errors.mjs (new typed errors).

Plan Part 3.1/3.3. Stance: single-writer token passing -- the writer pushes, then the next reader pulls, so every intra-sprint git merge is fast-forward BY CONSTRUCTION. A non-FF is a hard TYPED error, never auto-resolved. Implement syncMemberBefore(member) = G-pull (fetch + merge --ff-only) and syncMemberAfter(member, { pushCode }) = G-push (push with ONE bounded pull-rebase-retry). Both issue git via command(..., { member_name }) -- orchestrator-bracketed authorship (3.2): agents never run sync themselves. Every bracket needs failSoft-with-retry semantics that DISTINGUISH transient-retry (network/lock) from diverged-abort (non-FF, unmerged paths) -- this is risk 2 in the plan; a diverged state must never be retried blindly.
acceptance_criteria: syncMemberBefore/syncMemberAfter are exported from runner.js and issue every git command via command() with an explicit member_name; G-pull uses merge --ff-only and a non-FF result raises a distinct typed error (not a generic failure); G-push retries pull-rebase at most once, then raises a typed diverged error; transient failures (network/lock) are retried, divergence failures are never retried (test asserts the two classifications separately); new error types extend WorkflowError and carry the member and git output.

title: [impl] Replace per-sprint StdioTransport with shared fleet-server attach over streamable HTTP in cli.mjs
description:
Files: packages/apra-fleet-se/bin/cli.mjs (StdioTransport import line 10; construction ~line 451; resolveFleetServerConnection already present at ~line 61/15 for exactly this purpose).

title: [Phase 2] Dolt sync discipline: D-pull/D-push brackets, global push mutex, child-id allocator, Path A/B conflict recovery
description: Plan Part 3.3 (dolt columns), Part 3.4 (verified PoC findings C.1-C.5, escalation ladder, verified Path A runbook, Path B fallback), Part 4 Phase 2. HARD PREREQUISITE: apra-fleet-ire (Fleet installer: portable dolt CLI alongside bd) - the Path A resolve-in-place runbook is unusable in production without the provisioned dolt binary; do not duplicate that bead, it already tracks the installer work. PoC-confirmed constraints this feature must respect (C.1-C.5): disjoint-issue edits merge cleanly; ANY concurrent write to the same row hard-conflicts (row-level, NOT cell-level, in bd 1.1.0 embedded mode - disjoint-field re-test refuted the upstream cell-level claim); one unresolved conflict wedges the clone ENTIRE sync; concurrent child creation under a shared parent produces genuine child-id collisions (sequential-per-parent allocation). Therefore two LOAD-BEARING v1 requirements, not fallbacks: (a) a service-side GLOBAL push mutex serializing all cross-sprint dolt writes through the supervisor; (b) a globally-coordinated child-id allocator for any scope where two sprints can create children under a shared parent. Brackets per 3.3 table: D-pull before every dispatch that reads beads; planner D-push after; orchestrator D-pull after every doer D-push and BEFORE the bd show verification read (the single most divergence-sensitive read - without it every remote doer streak is falsely FAILED); orchestrator D-push after applying reopens/new tasks; integ-test-runner D-push only (never touches code, no git push); D-pull before cycle-eval/final-review counts; harvester D-push after. Conflict policy: first-successful-pusher-wins, ours/theirs fixed mechanically by which clone resolves - never per-conflict judgment. Path A (primary, VERIFIED 2026-07-16): the 10-step scripted resolve-in-place runbook - detect via bd dolt pull exit/error text; dolt sql-server --data-dir .beads/embeddeddolt on an ephemeral loopback port (externally-managed; bd dolt start uses the wrong dir, GH#2438); flip metadata.json to dolt_mode server; re-open the aborted merge with SET @@dolt_allow_commit_conflicts = 1; CALL dolt_merge(origin/main) (the step upstream docs omit); SELECT * FROM dolt_conflicts as the gate; CALL dolt_conflicts_resolve with the REQUIRED table-name arg; dolt_commit; pull+push; teardown and flip back to embedded (reversibility verified, zero data loss). Runs as orchestrator script with NO agent dispatch, gated by two deterministic checks: conflicting table is issues (or explicitly extended) AND a plain single-row conflict shape. Path B (fallback, verified): discard-and-re-bootstrap - rm .beads/embeddeddolt .beads/metadata.json .beads/backup (keep config.yaml with sync.remote), BD_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 bd bootstrap --yes, replay the one pending mutation; handle the two Windows gotchas (broken git+C:/ URL derivation when sync.remote absent; leftover empty DB makes retry fail until embeddeddolt removed); accepts discarding the loser other unsynced local state - kept small by design (one streak worth of writes). Tier 2 real agent dispatch ONLY when a gate fails or a scripted step returns unrecognized output. Adopt upstream per-bead work-claiming (bd update --claim, bd ready --assignee) inside the brackets as a third cheap prevention layer.
acceptance_criteria: All 3.3 dolt brackets implemented incl. orchestrator D-pull before the post-streak bd show verification (test: remote doer close is not falsely FAILED); all cross-sprint D-push/D-pull serialize through the supervisor mutex (test: two concurrent sprints never race a push); child-id allocator prevents the C.4 collision scenario (test recreates concurrent same-parent creation); Path A implemented as a command()-driven procedure passing both deterministic gates, exercised end-to-end against a deliberately wedged test clone with zero data loss (both-sides history present in dolt_log); Path B implemented and exercised on a wedged clone incl. mutation replay; unrecognized output or failed gate escalates to Tier 2 (recorded, runbook-documented) instead of proceeding blind; prerequisite apra-fleet-ire referenced and completed before this ships.
