title: [Phase 2] Orchestrator-bracketed git sync: per-dispatch brackets, sequential streaks, topology-guard replacement, git conflict ladder
description: Plan Parts 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, the git side of 3.4, Part 4 Phase 2, resolved Decisions (sync-command authorship; sequential streaks). Stance (3.1): single-writer token passing - hand-off = writer pushes then next reader pulls, so every intra-sprint git merge is fast-forward by construction; a non-FF is a hard TYPED error, never auto-resolved. Confirmed: multi-member doer streak dispatch becomes GLOBALLY sequential (today only same-member streaks are serialized via memberLocks); required even for two sequential heterogeneous members (x86 + ARM64 hand-off); merger-agent/parallel streaks explicitly deferred to Phase 3+. Authorship (3.2, confirmed): orchestrator-bracketed - runner.js issues sync deterministically via command(..., {member_name}) around every dispatch; agents do NOT run sync themselves. Implementation (3.3): one shared syncMemberBefore(member) / syncMemberAfter(member, {pushCode}) pair wrapping EVERY dispatch - planner, plan-reviewer, doer, reviewer, deployer, integ-test-runner, harvester - no phase-based exemptions (a deployer on a stale checkout is as damaging as a stale reviewer diff), per the 3.3 insertion-point table (G-pull = fetch + ff-only merge; G-push = push with one bounded pull-rebase-retry). Push ordering: for code-writing roles (doer, harvester only) G-push must succeed BEFORE D-push; if G-push cannot be resolved, D-push must NOT run - streak recorded failed with the explicit log message about not advertising an unreachable close. Topology guard: checkMemberTopology stops requiring identical HEADs for synced mode - new precondition is same git remote get-url origin + a working bd dolt pull probe per member; same-HEAD stays for legacy shared-workspace mode. Git conflict ladder (3.4): Tier 0 prevention (exclusive per-sprint branch ownership, rebase-before-push, sequential streaks); Tier 1 scripted detection (git pull --rebase exit code, unmerged paths in git status --porcelain, git rebase --abort to restore clean state); Tier 2 agent-with-runbook dispatch ONLY for semantically overlapping edits to the same lines that a fixed ours/theirs policy structurally cannot arbitrate - script-first posture confirmed. Scope (Decision, shared beads remote / MVP model): 1 sprint -> 1 repo -> that repo remote; multi-repo-per-project sprints explicitly out of scope. Every sync bracket needs failSoft-with-retry semantics distinguishing transient-retry from diverged-abort (risk #2 in the plan).
acceptance_criteria: syncMemberBefore/After helpers exist and wrap all seven dispatch types per the 3.3 table (test asserts coverage); doer streaks across different members run strictly sequentially; non-fast-forward pull and out-of-turn writes surface as typed fail-fast errors; G-push-fails => D-push skipped and streak marked failed (tested); topology guard accepts same-origin+dolt-probe synced mode and still enforces same-HEAD legacy mode; Tier 1 git detection and abort path covered by tests; retry logic distinguishes transient from divergence failures; no vendored agent .md file gains sync commands under this feature.

title: [test] installer installs a portable, working dolt CLI and degrades gracefully
description:

title: Fleet installer: install and verify a portable dolt CLI alongside bd
description:
src/cli/install.ts (~line 1040, the 'Beads install step') currently installs only @beads/bd via npm global install, with no dolt binary install. PoC (2026-07-16, dolt-poc-v2, run on Windows) confirmed that having a real dolt binary available (portable download, no admin/system install needed -- dolt v2.2.0 windows-amd64.zip, ~40MB download, single ~123MB static exe, no dependencies) and spinning up a temporary 'dolt sql-server' pointed directly at bd's existing '.beads/embeddeddolt' data dir (no migration needed) unlocks the documented dolt_conflicts / dolt_conflicts_resolve resolve-in-place path for Dolt merge conflicts -- which is otherwise completely blocked in bd's embedded mode ('bd sql'/'bd doctor' both hard-refuse). Measured footprint: ~73MB idle RSS, ~1.6s startup, single configurable port (default 3306), no system-wide footprint -- cheap enough to install unconditionally and spin up on-demand only when a conflict is actually detected (no persistent daemon required).

PLATFORM SCOPE (explicit, 2026-07-16): the PoC above was run on Windows only, but the fleet installer runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux members (see list_members: this repo's own fleet has windows/linux/macos members registered). The install step being added here MUST resolve and install the correct dolt release asset for whichever platform/arch the installer is running on -- windows-amd64.zip, linux-amd64.tar.gz, darwin-amd64.tar.gz, darwin-arm64.tar.gz -- not just the Windows asset. Do not hardcode or special-case Windows only.

Add a fleet-installer step (mirroring the existing Beads install step's already-installed-check pattern) that downloads/extracts the platform-appropriate dolt binary to a per-install location (e.g. alongside the existing BIN_DIR, not system PATH) and verifies it via 'dolt version', then smoke-tests that a real 'dolt sql-server' can start against a scratch data dir and accept a connection -- on whichever platform the installer runs on. See the auto-sprint-service design plan (https://claude.ai/code/artifact/413dd5a5-68f1-4a46-b10f-992dff241d3f, Part 3.4) for the full verified PoC findings and the exact conflict-resolution command ritual this unlocks (that PoC's command ritual and footprint numbers are Windows-measured; the same commands are expected to be portable via dolt's own cross-platform sql-server/bd sql interface, but were not independently re-measured on macOS/Linux).

title: auto-sprint: permanently-failed doer streaks still get sent into Review with no actual work to review
description:
Confirmed live during apra-fleet-7pm sprint (2026-07-14): Develop C1 R2 had both streaks ([apra-fleet-7pm.5] and [apra-fleet-7pm.7]) exhaust their retry-once and end with outcome:'failed' (both dispatch attempts hit the 300s inactivity timeout -- see apra-fleet-aw8). Log: 'Develop C1 R2 streak outcomes: [{beadIds:[apra-fleet-7pm.5],outcome:failed},{beadIds:[apra-fleet-7pm.7],outcome:failed}]', immediately followed by '--- Phase: Review C1 R2 ---' dispatching against those same bead ids.

Root cause: runner.js:1802 assignedBeadIds = streakOutcomes.flatMap((o) => o.beadIds) has no filter on o.outcome -- every streak's bead ids feed into the Review evidence-gathering (bd show + reviewer dispatch) regardless of whether the streak actually succeeded, failed with a real doer report, or (this case) failed with NO doer ever having successfully run at all.

Consequence: the Reviewer (premium tier, per FIXED_ROLE_TIER.reviewer) gets dispatched to 'review the work just done' for beads that have zero actual new work -- no commits, no diff, nothing changed from before the round started. Best case this wastes a premium-tier review call producing a CHANGES_NEEDED verdict that just re-states 'nothing was done' (functionally a no-op, just an expensive one); worst case it produces a confusing/incorrect verdict since the reviewer's prompt and contract assume real work happened.

Recommendation: filter streakOutcomes to only include outcome !== 'failed' bead ids in assignedBeadIds sent to Review; permanently-failed streaks' beads should just remain in their current (still-ready, never-closed) state and naturally get picked up again by the next Develop round's 'bd list --ready' scan -- no review dispatch needed for beads nothing happened to. Related to apra-fleet-aw8 (root cause of WHY streaks fail) but distinct -- this is about what the orchestrator does AFTER a streak is already known to have failed with no work product.

Confirms permanently-failed streak beadIds are excluded from Review dispatch; the original 'Review with no actual work' defect no longer reproduces.

title: fleet-sprint: doer-dispatch retry after inactivity timeout should escalate timeout + carry forward killed-attempt context (not blind resume)
description:
Distilled from live analysis during the apra-fleet-7pm sprint run (2026-07-13), triggered by a real timeout+retry observed live on streak apra-fleet-7pm.3 ('Command timed out after 300000ms of inactivity' -> retried once -> succeeded).

CURRENT STATE:
- runner.js:1730-1750 dispatchDoer() retry: on failure, calls the IDENTICAL dispatchDoer() a second time -- same prompt, same (default) timeout_s, no resume flag override. No escalation of any kind.
- execute-prompt.ts:164/353: timeout_s defaults to a flat 300s (5 min) applied uniformly across every role -- planner/reviewer analysis calls AND doer streaks doing full impl+test+commit work share the same default.
- Confirmed already-solid: strategy.ts:112-118 does a proper tree-kill (killTree() before child.kill('SIGKILL')) on inactivity timeout before the retry starts -- no orphan-process/PID-collision risk from this mechanism (this was the concern behind the historical apra-fleet-kwx incident; already handled correctly here).
- Confirmed via code: retry does NOT use session resume. packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/workflow/index.mjs:761 explicitly defaults resume: opts.resume ?? false (F10 / apra-fleet-unw.3, deliberate -- keeps workflow-authored prompts self-contained/deterministic), and dispatchDoer() never overrides opts.resume, so every retry is a fresh session with zero memory of the killed attempt; all partial work from the killed attempt is silently discarded and fully redone.

GAPS / RECOMMENDATIONS (user-reviewed 2026-07-13):
1. Escalate timeout_s on retry, linearly, e.g. 300s -> 600s -> 900s (5/10/15 min) rather than reusing the identical value on every attempt. Stay in timeout_s (seconds) throughout -- do NOT introduce a raw-ms public option; the codebase's existing public-facing config surface (timeout_s) is already seconds-based and should stay that way (internal strategy.ts setTimeout calls are fine in ms, that's Node's native timer API, not a public knob).
2. Role-specific default timeout_s: doer streaks run full impl+test+commit cycles, categorically heavier than planner/reviewer analysis calls, but share the same global 300s default. Consider a higher default specifically for doer-role dispatches (e.g. 900s).
3. DO NOT simply flip retries to resume:true. The killed attempt was hard SIGKILL'd mid-work (tree-killed after inactivity), not gracefully stopped -- its working directory / git state could be genuinely inconsistent (mid-file-edit, half-finished git operation). Blindly resuming a session whose process was just hard-killed risks the resumed conversation's understanding diverging from actual on-disk state -- this is the same risk category flagged in this project's own git-loss-incident-2026-07-02 memory ('timeout != process death', orphaned/half-finished git operations from overlapping dispatch). SAFER alternative that still achieves 'continue where we left off': have the retry prompt explicitly embed a git status/git diff snapshot of what the killed attempt left behind, so the fresh (self-contained, resume:false) session can see and account for partial work -- consistent with the existing design pattern already used for schema-repair re-asks (buildRepairPrompt in index.mjs embeds prior context directly in prompt text rather than relying on resume:true).
4. No telemetry/visibility today for 'timed out twice in a row' vs any other unrecoverable dispatch error -- both collapse into the same generic dispatchError -> streak marked 'failed' path (runner.js:1756-1766). If the SAME failure reason (inactivity timeout specifically) fires on both the original and retry, that's a strong signal the timeout is mis-sized for this task class, but nothing currently tags/surfaces that distinctly, making it hard to tell 'timeout needs tuning' from 'genuinely broken task' without reading raw logs.

Separate, smaller open question raised alongside this: should the rarely-used opts.timeoutMs (client-side MCP request-timeout override, AgentOptions field, distinct from the inactivity timeout_s) also be converted from ms to seconds for consistency? Not yet decided -- flagged for whoever picks this up to ask/decide, low priority, does not block items 1-4 above.
notes:
SCOPE BROADENED (2026-07-13, confirmed live): the same no-escalation gap applies beyond doer streaks. dispatchReview() (runner.js:1134-1188) has its OWN 2-attempt retry loop with a smart contract-violation check (a CHANGES_NEEDED verdict with empty reopenIds AND empty newTasks is recognized as meaningless and auto-retried, throwing ReviewerContractViolationError only if it repeats) -- this is better-designed than the doer path, observed live working correctly after a real 300s inactivity timeout on the Reviewer. But its retry (runner.js:1139) reuses the identical default timeout_s with no escalation, same gap as the doer path. plan-reviewer (~runner.js:1513) and Final Review (~runner.js:2113) likely share the same pattern -- not yet individually confirmed. Recommend the timeout_s escalation fix (item 1 in this issue) be applied at a shared/common dispatch-retry layer if one gets introduced, rather than doer-only, so all 4 retry sites (doer, reviewer, plan-reviewer, final-review) benefit uniformly.
triage 2026-08-09 (autosprint-internals batch): STALE-LOW-VALUE, largely superseded. NAMING -- 'auto-sprint' here is STALE for fleet-sprint, proven directly: this bead's own partial fix, commit c0bfa6c8 'fix(auto-sprint): bump doer/reviewer dispatch timeout to 900s (apra-fleet-aw8)', patched packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js, the directory later renamed to fleet-sprint/ by 058160e7. Title corrected. Re-checked the 4 gaps against current fleet-sprint/runner.js (~8.4k lines): (2) role-specific timeout -- SUPERSEDED, there is now a single DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_S applied as both timeout_s and max_total_s, default 3600s (12x the 300s that motivated this bead) and operator-configurable via the dispatch_timeout_s arg (runner.js:2397-2408, validated >=60). (4) telemetry -- largely addressed by withDispatchWatchdog (runner.js:4506-4533), which emits a distinct labelled '[dispatch-watchdog] ... produced no result within Ns' message per stalled attempt. (3) killed-attempt context -- addressed by a different and better mechanism than proposed: the retry path now reasons explicitly about what the prior attempt left behind (skipPreDispatchSync / resumeOntoRemoteTip, runner.js:772-819, 4974-5001, 7318), and max_turns escalation on retry exists (6997-7006). (1) linear timeout_s escalation across retries -- the ONLY item still genuinely unimplemented, and with a 3600s default its value is now marginal. Lowered P2 -> P4; residual scope is item 1 alone.
Re-prioritized P4->P2 (2026-08-17): the engine-side analog of this bead's timeout/retry gap is now confirmed live in a real field sprint. ait-gbo v0.4.0's 120s transcript-frozen stall detector killed 3 healthy dispatches after ~23min of visible progress (indistinguishable from a hang under the flat threshold); one of them (Harvest) was never retried, so the sprint shipped with no harvest report at all. Extend scope: declared per-dispatch expected duration, stall/inactivity threshold scaling, and retry coverage specifically for stall-killed Final Review and Harvest phases. See field-report-ait-gbo-analysis.md section P1-4, recommendation 5.

title: auto-sprint: Streak Assignment mis-costed at premium tier; long-term should be deterministic JS, not an LLM call
description:
Distilled from live analysis during the apra-fleet-7pm sprint run (2026-07-13).

CURRENT STATE: packages/apra-fleet-se/auto-sprint/runner.js:1627-1636 dispatches a dedicated LLM call ('Streak Assignment') every Develop round (up to 3x per cycle) to group ready beads into parallel-safe work streaks. It reuses agentType:'planner' and FIXED_ROLE_TIER.planner = 'premium' (runner.js:94-101) purely by code-reuse convenience, not because the task needs premium reasoning.

WHY IT'S SEPARATE FROM THE INITIAL PLANNER CALL (cannot simply be merged): the initial planner call builds the DAG once per Plan phase; Streak Assignment runs once per Develop round against whatever beads are CURRENTLY ready (bd list --ready), which changes as prior-round work completes -- that input doesn't exist at initial-planning time. Temporally separate steps, not mergeable into one call.

WHY IT COULD IN PRINCIPLE BE PURE JS (no LLM): bd's own dependency graph ('blocks' edges) already guarantees ordering-safety for the ready set -- a bead only becomes ready once its blockers close, so ready beads are already DAG-safe to run in any order/parallel from a pure-ordering standpoint. What Streak Assignment actually decides beyond that is FILE-COLLISION risk between formally-independent ready beads. That's a deterministic set-overlap (union-find) problem IF beads carried structured file-touch metadata.

WHY IT CAN'T BE PURE JS TODAY: no structured/validated file-touch field exists on beads. 11 of 13 tasks in this exact epic (apra-fleet-7pm) happen to include a free-text 'Files: ...' line in their prose description, but 2 (.7, .11) don't, and grep of vendor/apra-pm/agents/planner.md shows ZERO mentions of any 'Files:' convention -- it's not documented, schema-validated, or guaranteed present/well-formed. A JS parser scraping this would be brittle (though would degrade safely to 'own streak' for tasks missing the line, not corrupt anything).

TWO-PART RECOMMENDATION:
1. Quick low-risk win: add a distinct FIXED_ROLE_TIER['streak-assignment'] = 'standard' (or 'cheap') instead of reusing .planner's 'premium' tier. selectStreaks() (runner.js:606) already has a robust, always-correct fallback (one-bead-per-streak) whenever LLM output is invalid, so correctness isn't gated on premium-quality output -- low risk to downgrade.
2. Real structural fix: have the planner agent emit a validated 'touches: [file paths]' field as real bead metadata (not prose) when creating each task. Once that exists, Streak Assignment becomes pure deterministic JS (union-find over file-set intersection) -- eliminates the LLM call entirely (not just cheapens it), zero latency, more reliable than an LLM guess. Larger change: touches planner.md's task-authoring contract, beads schema/metadata, and runner.js's streak-assignment code path.
close_reason: Subsumed by apra-fleet-eft.76, which retires the runtime Streak-Assignment LLM dispatch entirely (planner-owned lane metadata at plan time) -- goes further than this bead's own two-part recommendation (tier downgrade, then deterministic JS via file-touch metadata).

title: Improve opencode auth error classification in execute_prompt
description: When execute_prompt fails on an opencode member due to auth (missing API key, expired OAuth token, wrong model access), the error currently falls through to 'unknown' category with no actionable message. Need to: 1) Experiment with what real auth error output looks like from opencode for each provider (Google, OpenCode Go, Ollama). 2) Add specific regex patterns to classifyError() in opencode.ts that match those outputs and return 'auth'. 3) Ensure the error message surfaced to the user includes the actual error text and a hint on how to fix (e.g. run opencode auth login, set GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY, etc). Requires manual testing with an intentionally broken auth state on opencode-toy to capture real error output.
notes: Triage 2026-08-09 (iuc-agy batch): still valid, still unimplemented. src/providers/opencode.ts classifyError() (~lines 64-68) matches only 'command not found'/'is not recognized' -> unknown, 'connection refused|ECONNREFUSED' -> server, 'timeout|ETIMEDOUT' -> server, 'rate limit|429' -> overloaded, then falls through to 'unknown'. There is no auth-shaped pattern at all, so a missing API key / expired OAuth / no model access still surfaces as an unactionable 'unknown'. Blocking factor is unchanged and is the whole cost of the bead: step 1 requires capturing REAL opencode auth-failure output for each backend (Google, OpenCode Go, Ollama) by deliberately breaking auth on an opencode member -- the regexes cannot be written responsibly from guesswork, and guessed patterns are exactly how a misclassification bug gets shipped. Classification: NEEDS-RESEARCH-ONLY. The implementation once the strings are in hand is ~10 lines plus tests. Suggest scheduling it alongside any session that already has an opencode member available (e.g. opencode-toy), and attaching the captured stderr to this bead as the deliverable of the research half.

title: Stage 2 (placeholder): contract beads and Zuul-style speculative gating for federated sprints
description:
FORWARD-LOOKING PLACEHOLDER -- deliberately not decomposed yet. Do not start this before Stage 0 and
Stage 1 have landed and produced real usage evidence; the design doc is explicit that Stage 2's shape
should be informed by which cross-repo failures ACTUALLY occur in practice.

CONTEXT (self-contained). Stage 1 delivers one sprint driving N repos through one global cycle: per-repo
members, per-repo bases, per-repo dispatch, an integration phase on a composite member, and one PR per
repo with a prescribed merge order. Stage 2 ("Option E: contract-first federated sprints", design doc
section 3) is the mature end-state that scales past that:

- CONTRACT BEADS: machine-checkable interface artifacts (OpenAPI diff, schema migration, published
  package version, pact file) that every cross-repo dependency edge must flow through. Frontend work
  that needs a backend endpoint is blocks-linked to the backend's CONTRACT bead, not to the backend's
  implementation beads.
- PER-REPO DEVELOP LOOPS running concurrently and independently, gated only by contract beads, instead
  of one global cycle -- so a 10-repo workspace does not make every repo wait on every other repo's
  cycle boundary.
- FAILURE ISOLATION by construction: one repo's FAIL no longer aborts the others; its dependents'
  contract beads simply stay unproven and their PRs say so.
- Pact-style `can-i-deploy` gates between per-repo deploys in the manifest's "independent" deploy mode.
- Zuul-style SPECULATIVE ASSEMBLY: check out every repo's sprint branch together, build, and run
  cross-repo tests before any PR publishes -- Stage 1's integration phase is the first, simpler version
  of this.
- A verdict model that is per-repo AND joint.

Open question carried from the design doc (#7): the contract bead ARTIFACT FORMAT (OpenAPI diff vs pact
files vs published package versions) is likely per-stack and needs customer discovery before committing.

Full context: docs/multi-repo-fleet-sprint-strategy.md sections 3 (Option E), 4 and 6.
design:
Not designed yet, by intent. Before decomposing this bead:
1) Collect evidence from real Stage 1 sprints: which cross-repo failures actually occurred, at which
   phase, and whether an explicit interface artifact would have caught them earlier.
2) Do customer discovery on contract artifact format per stack (open question #7).
3) Then split this placeholder into implementable children, expected to be roughly: contract bead type
   and semantics; planner discipline for emitting contract beads; per-repo concurrent develop loops
   replacing the global cycle; can-i-deploy gating between independent per-repo deploys; the
   per-repo-plus-joint verdict model.
acceptance_criteria:
- This bead is not started while any Stage 0 or Stage 1 sibling remains open.
- Before any implementation work begins, this bead is replaced by concrete child beads (contract bead

title: Document that the CI sandbox cannot discriminate hidden versus visible window launches
description: The automation shell runs in a non-interactive Windows session, so Win32_Process.Create attaches created processes to the Services session regardless of the ShowWindow value; both hidden and visible launches report MainWindowHandle 0 and Window Title N/A. Capture this limitation in docs/windows-detached-launch.md (or docs/test-inventory.md) next to the live-test entry so future agents do not mistake a passing no-visible-window assertion in CI for real verification, and so the interactive-session requirement is discoverable without re-deriving it.
notes: The window-station/session constraint this issue asks to document (a non-interactive session cannot discriminate a hidden launch from a visible one, because Win32_Process.Create attaches the child to the caller's own session) is now written up in docs/windows-detached-launch.md under 'Known limitation, not yet closed out', item 1. That doc also states the sanctioned follow-up: proving the positive-control discriminator requires a real interactive Windows logon (RDP or physical console), which is tracked separately (apra-fleet-i8qj.19 / apra-fleet-5ti7.4). If this issue's sole ask was the documentation, it is satisfied by that section; leaving open only if a different artifact (e.g. inline code comment) was also expected.

for the showWindow:true opt-out path. src/cli/launch-fleet-supervisor-windows.ts
never passes a title option, so if the supervisor's launch ever used the

either call site today), it would incorrectly present the MCP server's

Supervisor -- do not close".

(2) tests 2a and 2b end with expect(true).toBe(true) after an await of 100ms; the real assertion there is structural (the unhandled error event would crash the runner), so replace the vacuous expectation with a comment or an explicit process-level unhandled-rejection/exception check.

title: win32 detectStacks marker filter is case-insensitive while the STACK_MAP lookup is case-sensitive
description: In src/tools/compose-permissions.ts detectStacks(), the Windows branch filters Get-ChildItem -Name output with @(<markers>) -contains $_. PowerShell's -contains is case-insensitive, so a file literally named Package.json or CARGO.TOML passes the filter, but the caller then does STACK_MAP[file] with the on-disk casing, which misses, and the stack is silently dropped. Net effect is a silently missed stack rather than a wrong one, so severity is low, but the two halves should agree: either normalize the filename before the STACK_MAP lookup or make the PowerShell filter case-sensitive with -ccontains. Add a case-variant marker case to the win32 suite in tests/compose-permissions.test.ts.

title: Surface the Windows service registration mode in apra-fleet status
description:
Re-submitted from a rejected newTask proposal (cycle 4 rejection: the title contained backticks and failed the safe-character allowlist; the previous description also stated no decided outcome or acceptance criteria). Both defects are corrected here: the title is plain ASCII-safe, and the work below is DECIDED, not conditional.

BACKGROUND: docs/transport-and-service-mode.md previously told users to run 'apra-fleet status' to see whether the ApraFleet scheduled task is registered SYSTEM/onstart or onlogon-interactive, but src/cli/status.ts only prints 'Service: installed (enabled|disabled)'. readServiceRegistrationMode() (src/services/service-manager/windows.ts) has no consumer outside its own module and tests/service-manager.test.ts. apra-fleet-i8qj.7's rework resolved the doc side by dropping the 'apra-fleet status' clause and keeping the service-registration.json path, which is accurate today. DONE / ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:

1. On win32 only, runStatus() prints the Windows scheduled-task registration mode obtained from readServiceRegistrationMode() (e.g. 'Registration: SYSTEM/onstart' vs 'Registration: onlogon-interactive'), and prints the ServiceStatus.registeredButNeverFired flag when it is set (flag added by apra-fleet-i8qj.3).
2. Non-win32 status output is byte-for-byte unchanged; a missing or unreadable registration record degrades to a clear 'Registration: unknown' line rather than throwing or aborting status.
3. docs/transport-and-service-mode.md restores the 'apra-fleet status' wording for discovering the registration mode, keeping the service-registration.json path as the secondary/manual route. Do not edit deploy.md (owned solely by apra-fleet-5ti7.5).
4. Unit test added to the existing status CLI test file asserting: win32 path prints the mode for each of the mode values readServiceRegistrationMode() can return; the never-fired flag is surfaced; the non-win32 path prints no registration line. The test must fail against the pre-change status.ts.
5. tsc build passes, npm test passes, ASCII-only. Surface the changed markdown for user review rather than committing it silently.

title: Windows long_running task.log loses stderr from a FAILING native command
description:
Documented, accepted tradeoff from PR #405 (fix/cross-shell-home-var)'s new
Windows long_running support (generateTaskWrapperWindows in
src/services/cloud/task-wrapper.ts). To avoid a worse bug (Windows PowerShell
reclassifying a SUCCESSFUL native command's stderr as a terminating error
under $ErrorActionPreference="Stop", which would false-fail exit-0 commands
like git/npm/curl that log warnings to stderr), stream 2 (Error) is
deliberately left unredirected -- only streams 1/3/4/5/6 go to task.log.

Side effect: a FAILING native command's stderr is also lost (it throws
nothing under PowerShell, so the catch block's exception-detail capture
never fires either). Linux's `2>&1` wrapper has no such gap -- on Windows,
debugging a failed long_running task currently has less diagnostic
information available than on Linux.

Not blocking (confirmed nothing downstream depends on task.log containing
this data), but worth closing the gap -- e.g. by exploring the child-process
exit-status approach originally proposed during review (spawn the wrapped
command in a child PowerShell/cmd process and capture its output streams
independently of the wrapper's own $ErrorActionPreference scoping), or some
other mechanism that doesn't reintroduce the false-failure bug this
tradeoff was chosen to avoid.

title: Sprint progress bar and beads tree disagree on below-goal beads admitted by the blocks-edge exception

title: formatTime(NaN) renders 'NaNs' in the workflow viewer
description: apra-fleet-4wr.1 replaced formatTime's `if (!ms) return '-'` guard with `if (ms === null || ms === undefined) return '-'` in packages/apra-fleet-workflow/src/viewer/index.mjs (line ~241). This is correct and intentional for the zero case (0 must render '0s', not '-'), but it also means a NaN input now renders the literal string 'NaNs' where it previously rendered '-'. Reachable at index.mjs:469, which computes new Date(phase.phaseEndedAt).getTime() - new Date(phase.phaseStartedAt).getTime() guarded only on phaseEndedAt: a frozen phase carrying an end timestamp but no/invalid start timestamp yields NaN. Add a Number.isFinite(ms) check that returns the '-' placeholder, plus a unit test pinning formatTime(NaN) === '-' alongside the existing 0/negative/sub-second cases.

title: Scenario END markers report PASS even when the scenario failed
description: apra-fleet-20i.1.4.1 added '=== END scenario: <tag> (PASS/FAIL) ===' markers in packages/apra-fleet-se/test/helpers/mock-sprint-harness.mjs. In runRejectedPlanScenario() the `passed = true` assignment sits after the inner try/catch that swallows the run error into the returned `error` value, so the marker prints PASS for every completed run regardless of outcome; runOnce()/runDevelopLoopScenario() have the same weakness for failures surfaced via a returned error rather than a throw. The FAIL branch is therefore effectively dead for those paths, which undercuts the marker's value when scenarios interleave in CI output. Either set `passed` from the actual scenario outcome (e.g. error === undefined and the caller's assertions), or move the marker emission to the caller so it reflects the test's real verdict. Add a test asserting a deliberately failing scenario emits (FAIL).
close_reason: Fixed passed-verdict logic in mock-sprint-harness.mjs: runRejectedPlanScenario sets passed=Boolean(error) (rejection is its success contract), runDevelopLoopScenario sets passed=(error===null) (generic harness, real outcome); runOnce audited/unchanged (no swallow). Added mock-sprint-scenario-marker-verdict.test.mjs pinning (FAIL) for a deliberately-erroring scenario and (PASS) for the rejected-plan scenario, with recorded bd fixtures. title: AGY stall detection: a guessed home dir with stale files can license a false-positive kill
description:
SF-20 from PR #383's review history (github.com/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet/issues/390, resolved via 36c52bcd/1f41d218/78892e3d). The username-convention fallback (used only when the real home-dir probe fails or hasn't run yet) upgrades to signalAvailable: true as soon as it finds ANY mtime under the guessed provider log directory, including a stale one older than dispatch start. If the guessed home happens to be wrong but the full guessed provider-specific directory tree (e.g. .gemini/antigravity-cli/brain) happens to exist with only old files, lastActivityAt never advances and the baseline stall-kill fires -- a false positive.

This is narrow: it requires a wrong username guess to coincidentally produce an identical provider-specific directory structure, which is unlikely in practice, and SF-18's proactive home-dir warming (registration + startup sweep) has already made the username-fallback state rare (the probe now succeeds and caches the real value in most cases). Already covered by an explicit test pinning the current tradeoff (tests/stall-no-signal-false-kill.test.ts).

Fix direction (not yet designed): distinguish a guessed-and-verified directory (files found, but never cross-checked against a known-good marker) from a probed-and-confirmed one, or require the guessed directory to be re-validated against a second independent signal before being trusted as authoritative.

## Context
Surfaced during PR #383 (feat/agy-output-format-json) round-5 review of the #390 home-dir/stall-detection fix. See PR comment: https://github.com/Apra-Labs/apra-fleet/pull/383#issuecomment-5219469441
notes: Triage 2026-08-09 (iuc-agy batch): mechanism CONFIRMED in code, and the bead's own risk framing holds. src/services/member-home.ts:106 homeDirFromUsername + the two fallback returns (:167-169, :195-197) tag a guess with source:'username-fallback'; src/services/stall/stall-poller.ts returns {mtimeMs, signalAvailable:true} (:110) as soon as ANY mtime is found under the guessed provider log dir, with no comparison against dispatch start, and src/services/stall/stall-detector.ts:119/:138 consumes that as authoritative signal. So a wrong-but-structurally-identical guessed tree containing only stale files does let the baseline stall-kill fire. Preconditions make it very narrow: SF-18's proactive home-dir warming (1f41d218, registration + startup sweep) means the probe usually succeeds and caches the real home, so the username-fallback state is now rare, and the miss additionally requires the wrong user's machine to carry an identical provider-specific tree (e.g. .gemini/antigravity-cli/brain). Current tradeoff is already pinned by tests/stall-no-signal-false-kill.test.ts. No fix is designed -- the suggested direction (distinguish guessed-but-unverified from probed-and-confirmed, or require a second independent signal before trusting a guessed dir) is a real design decision in the stall-detector trust model, not a patch. Classification: NEEDS-DEEPER-DESIGN; P3 remains correct -- do not promote ahead of pdwh's much likelier siblings.

title: Generalize playbook-declared-permissions -> ledger sync for any fleet-sprint project (not just apra-fleet)
description:
apra-fleet-fccm seeded THIS repo's own permissions.json by hand-parsing three
apra-fleet-specific playbook filenames (deploy.md, integ-test-playbook.md,
regression-test-playbook.md) with a one-off script + a drift-guard test that
hardcodes those three filenames. That only works because apra-fleet dogfoods
fleet-sprint on itself and happens to use those exact filenames. It does NOT
generalize to any other project that adopts fleet-sprint -- a fresh project
would need someone to manually author its own permissions.json by hand, with
no tooling support, and no drift guard unless it copy-pastes and re-adapts
apra-fleet-fccm's test.

Per fleet-sprint-product-vs-dogfood policy (fleet-sprint is a general
product; apra-fleet-specific structure must not leak into the engine/prompts;
target-specific fixes go target-side), the fix here needs to be something a
project author invokes generically -- e.g. a CLI/skill command that:
  1. Discovers whatever playbook files a project actually has declaring
     `## Permissions` sections (not a hardcoded 3-file list -- could be a
     glob, a manifest, or convention-based discovery of playbook files these
     projects author for deployer/integ-test-runner/regression-test-runner
     roles).
  2. Parses/extracts declared Bash(...) (and possibly other tool) permission
     strings the same way apra-fleet-fccm's parser does.
  3. Seeds/updates that PROJECT's own root permissions.json ledger.
  4. Optionally scaffolds a project-local drift-guard test (or provides a
     reusable, importable drift-guard helper/library function so projects
     don't each hand-roll the parsing regex apra-fleet-fccm wrote twice).

Explicitly still out of scope / needs its own design decision (do not fold
into this bead without separate discussion, see docs/auto-sprint-permission-
diff-safety-block.md for why): whether fleet-sprint's runner.js or
register_member should ever auto-invoke this at sprint-launch or
member-registration time. That auto-delivery question is a DIFFERENT,
deliberately-deferred concern (self-grant-by-the-engine risk) from "give
project authors a reusable tool to seed their own ledger by hand/CI."

Prior art to reuse rather than re-derive: the parsing logic in
tests/permissions-ledger-drift.test.ts (extractDeclaredPermissions) and the
seeding done ad hoc for apra-fleet-fccm -- both currently apra-fleet-specific
and need to move to a general, target-agnostic location (likely
packages/apra-fleet-se or a shared script/skill) before any other project can
use them.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-09 (batch 647): NEEDS-DEEPER-DESIGN, and the bead's factual premise is now STALE -- it must be re-grounded before anyone starts. title: Make check-pack-size.mjs accept the threshold flag equals form
description: Refiled -- this task was rejected by the orchestrator's title validator last round because the original title contained an equals sign, which is outside the safe-character allowlist. title: [impl] Scope install's running-process guard to the install target so isolated-prefix installs are not falsely blocked
description:
Files (1-2): src/cli/install.ts (guard block ~L892-912, isApraFleetRunning ~L673-693, usage/help text ~L739/L757). Optionally the killApraFleet path if it needs the same scoping hook.

PROBLEM: The pre-install guard at ~L893 fires when '(isSea() || isNpmGlobalInstall()) && isApraFleetRunning()'. isApraFleetRunning() is machine-wide ('pgrep -x apra-fleet', ~L686) -- it blocks even when the new install targets a fully isolated HOME/prefix (e.g. a throwaway FAKEHOME used by fyc.2's clean-temp-prefix CI smoke step) that shares no filesystem path with the already-running instance. WHAT TO CHANGE:
1. Make the guard block ONLY when the new install would actually collide with the running instance's own install/binary path. 3. Preserve the existing behavior when the install DOES target the running instance's own root: still block (with the same message) unless --force, which still stops it.

Keep changes focused; do NOT alter unrelated install steps. Update packages/apra-fleet-client if any tool schema is touched (it is not expected to be here). ASCII only.

title: install running-process guard (isApraFleetRunning) is machine-wide, not scoped to the install target -- false positive under concurrent dispatch / shared hosts
description:
src/cli/install.ts's pre-install guard ('Error: apra-fleet is currently running. Stop the server before installing.') fires whenever (isSea() || isNpmGlobalInstall()) && isApraFleetRunning() is true. isApraFleetRunning() is a machine-wide 'pgrep -x apra-fleet' (see install.ts ~line 673-693) -- it does not check whether the already-running instance's binary/install path has anything to do with the NEW install's target directory.

This means the guard trips even when the new install is fully isolated (e.g. a temp HOME/prefix used by an npm-publish CI smoke test, per apra-fleet-fyc.2's 'Pack + install into a clean temp prefix' ci.yml step) and would never actually conflict with the already-running instance's files. On a real single-purpose CI runner this rarely surfaces (nothing else is running apra-fleet there), but on a shared dev host or any environment with concurrent apra-fleet dispatch/orchestration already running persistently, it produces a hard false-positive block with no way to opt out short of --force (which kills the unrelated live process machine-wide -- unacceptable when that process is, e.g., an active FleetView/orchestrator server backing other concurrent work).

Observed while executing apra-fleet-fyc.2.3's clean-temp-prefix install step: a real, unrelated, already-running apra-fleet --transport http service (launchd-managed, cwd = this repo, logging to ~/.apra-fleet/data/fleet.log) caused 'apra-fleet install --skill none --workflows all --transport stdio' (targeting a throwaway FAKEHOME) to refuse with exit 1, even though the two installs share no filesystem path.

Suggested fix: scope the guard to the actual conflict it's trying to prevent -- e.g. compare the running process's own binary path (ps/lsof) or its resolved install-root against the NEW install's target root, and only block when they'd actually collide. Alternatively, add an explicit opt-out (e.g. --skip-running-check, or auto-skip when HOME/APRA_FLEET_DATA_DIR clearly differs from the running instance's) for isolated-prefix installs.
acceptance_criteria: Installing to a demonstrably separate/isolated HOME or install prefix succeeds even when an unrelated apra-fleet process is running elsewhere on the host; the guard still blocks when the new install would actually collide with (overwrite) the running instance's own binary/install path.
notes: Cross-reference: this is the same underlying defect as apra-fleet-l7n.4 (install.ts pgrep/pkill not scoped to the current user, found independently via Opus PR-375 review). Fix once, close both.
close_reason: integ-test-runner: verified against deployed build (HEAD 3475c225, branch fix/se-urgent-isolated-batch). Ran: npx vitest run tests/install-running-guard.test.ts tests/install-force.test.ts -> 2 files, 27 tests, all pass, incl. 'isolated-prefix install with unrelated server running proceeds without exit(1)', same-root still blocks + --force stops it, --skip-running-check bypass, and unresolvable-root/cross-platform (macOS/Windows) cases. Guard now scopes to install target root; feature behaves as specified. Closing.

title: Clean-pack guard's 10MB size check is a no-op (parses human-readable unpacked size wrong)
description:
Found while running apra-fleet-fyc.2.3's live verification of the npm-publish
gating sequence.

.github/workflows/ci.yml 'Clean-pack guard' step computes:
  PACK_BYTES=$(npm pack --dry-run 2>&1 | grep 'unpacked size' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1)
  if [ -n "$PACK_BYTES" ] && [ "$PACK_BYTES" -gt 10000000 ]; then ...

npm prints unpacked size in human-readable form, e.g.:
  npm notice unpacked size: 4.1 MB

grep -oE '[0-9]+' on that line yields just the mantissa's integer part (e.g.
"4"), never the actual byte count. The -gt 10000000 comparison can therefore
never fire regardless of actual tarball size -- confirmed locally: current
measured unpacked size is 4.1 MB and PACK_BYTES evaluates to 4.

The stale-artifact regex check (.exe/sea-prep.blob/sea-bundle.cjs) in the same
step works correctly; only the byte-threshold arithmetic is broken.

Fix: parse npm pack's JSON output (npm pack --dry-run --json) for an accurate
byte count instead of scraping the human-readable notice line.

Not currently blocking anything -- 4.1 MB is genuinely under 10MB -- but the
guard would silently pass an oversized package.
notes: ALREADY-FIXED-OR-DUPLICATE. Verified: children apra-fleet-yj1.1/.2/.3 are all CLOSED, and .github/workflows/ci.yml's Clean-pack guard step (line ~702) now calls 'node scripts/check-pack-size.mjs' instead of the broken grep-based PACK_BYTES arithmetic described in this bug. scripts/check-pack-size.mjs (read directly) parses 'npm pack --dry-run --json' for a real unpackedSize byte count, exactly the fix this bead requested. The parent bead itself was left open despite all subtask work landing -- closing as fixed by its own children.
close_reason: Fixed by children yj1.1 (check-pack-size.mjs added), yj1.2 (ci.yml wired to it), yj1.3 (regression test) -- all closed. Verified ci.yml no longer uses the broken grep-based byte parse; check-pack-size.mjs correctly reads npm pack --dry-run --json.

title: [regression][carry-over] node dist/index.js status misreports 'stopped' right after a real 'start' because the sandbox HOME was deleted out from under the running server mid-Setup (root cause: concurrent playbook run on the shared fixed sandbox path, not a start/status race)

The subsequent second 'start' then correctly saw no live state, assumed nothing running, and fell back to port 62076 because 18700 was still physically held by the orphaned first process -- again explained by the concurrent deletion, not by 'start' failing to detect its own sibling.

title: Sync fail-safe silently treats a bd command timeout as configured, masking member unresponsiveness
description:
Observed in sprint apra-fleet-cvb-e04f499d-6f61-4679-bbc0-78ff4580b465, Sprint Setup phase, log lines 21-22:

[Workflow Log] [Dolt] could not parse 'bd config get sync.remote --json' output for member 'fleet-mac' (fail-safe: treating as configured): Unexpected token 'F', "Failed to "... is not valid JSON
[Workflow Log] updateDashboard: failed to refresh sprint-tree panel (non-fatal, will retry next update): [bd JSON Parse Error] Failed to parse JSON output from 'bd list --all --limit 0 --json': Unexpected token 'F', "Failed to "... is not valid JSON. Raw output snippet: "Failed to execute command on \"fleet-mac\": Command timed out after 120000ms of inactivity"

The 'could not parse ... JSON' fail-safe path is designed for cosmetic/format issues in bd's stdout, but here the actual underlying cause was a real command timeout: 'bd config get sync.remote --json' never returned because the command hung for 120s of inactivity on member 'fleet-mac' before the transport gave up. The fail-safe swallowed this and reported 'treating as configured' -- i.e. a genuine member-responsiveness failure at sprint startup is indistinguishable, from the log/behavior, from a merely-malformed-but-harmless JSON response, and the sprint proceeded as if sync.remote were confirmed configured.

This happened right at Sprint Setup, before the first dispatch, and (per this run) did not recur, but the fail-safe as written cannot tell a genuine bd-unresponsive-member condition from cosmetic JSON noise -- worth distinguishing 'exit/timeout error surfaced as command output' from 'command succeeded but printed odd JSON' so a real hung-member condition is surfaced/retried rather than silently defaulted to the optimistic branch.

File: search packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js for the 'could not parse' / 'fail-safe: treating as configured' log message and the 'bd list --all --limit 0 --json' dashboard refresh parse path (updateDashboard).
notes: TRIAGE: Confirmed live in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/dolt-sync.mjs's isMemberSyncRemoteConfigured() (lines ~195-222, not runner.js as the bead's own file pointer suggested -- code has moved/been extracted since filing). The fail-safe still conflates three distinct failure modes (command() throw, failSoft error result, and JSON parse failure) into one 'treating as configured' path with no differentiation of a real timeout-shaped error message from cosmetic JSON noise, exactly as described. Fix is small: pattern-match res.error/err.message for timeout-like text before falling into the generic fail-safe log line, to surface a distinct warning. Classification: LOW-HANGING-FRUIT. Subsystem: fleet-sprint dolt-sync / member responsiveness.

title: newTask title allowlist rejects benign shell-safe chars like = losing real findings to notes-only fallback
description:
Observed in sprint apra-fleet-cvb-e04f499d-6f61-4679-bbc0-78ff4580b465 (Review C1 R1), log lines 159-160:

[Workflow Log] Reviewer newTasks: REJECTED (not sent to bd create) -- title fails safe-character allowlist /^[A-Za-z0-9 .,:;!?()'_/\[\]-]+$/ (or is empty): "Stabilize flaky serve-wiring-integration 'GET /' dashboard-render test under --test-concurrency=8"

Root cause: SAFE_TEXT_RE in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:3642 (/^[A-Za-z0-9 .,:;!?()'_/\[\]-]+$/) rejects the title solely because of the '=' in "--test-concurrency=8". Per the file's own design comment (runner.js:3620-3641), the actual shell-injection vectors that must stay excluded are backtick, $, double-quote, and backslash -- '=' has no special meaning inside a double-quoted bd create "..." command in POSIX or Windows shells and is not a documented hazard. apra-fleet-19o.1 already loosened this same regex once (added '[' and ']') for exactly this class of false-rejection, but '=' (and likely '&', '%', '#', '+', all called out as description-only-safe in the runner.js:3640 comment) were left off the title allowlist.

Impact: apra-fleet-19o.2's resurfacing mechanism keeps the finding from vanishing (it lands verbatim in the parent bead's notes, as seen here), but it does NOT become a real, plannable bd bead unless/until a later Plan-phase dispatch resubmits it with a corrected title -- and this sprint terminated (DoltDivergedError, apra-fleet-spp) before reaching another Plan phase, so the finding (a real flaky-test bug in serve-wiring-integration.test.mjs) is currently sitting only in apra-fleet-cvb's notes field, not tracked as its own bead.

Fix direction: extend SAFE_TEXT_RE to allow '=' (and audit the other characters the runner.js:3640 comment already documents as safe-for-description-but-currently-title-unsafe) while keeping backtick/$/"/backslash excluded, mirroring the apra-fleet-19o.1 precedent (test both newly-accepted and still-rejected titles).
notes: LOW-HANGING-FRUIT. Verified live: SAFE_TEXT_RE at packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js:3619 is still /^[A-Za-z0-9 .,:;!?()'_/\[\]-]+$/ -- '=' is not in the allowlist, confirming the bug reproduces today. No later fix landed: searched apra-fleet-xuo's full 24-child tree (the epic that did fix related newTask-allowlist issues, e.g. apra-fleet-19o added '[' and ']') and found no child addressing '='. The file's own adjacent comment (runner.js:3617-3623) already documents '=','&','+','%','#','$' as description-safe-but-title-unsafe, giving a ready-made list to extend SAFE_TEXT_RE from, mirroring the apra-fleet-19o.1 precedent this bead cites (loosen regex, add tests for newly-accepted and still-rejected titles). Clear, small, well-precedented fix.

title: [integ] Smoke-test canary sprint blows the 10-min time budget (~24 min actual): per-phase dispatch overhead, not Planner scope expansion

title: Harden durable-stdout-tee mechanism: agy dependency, FLEET_PID identity, discard-on-timeout
description:
Consolidates three separate follow-ups filed after apra-fleet-6z8.1's review into one bead -- they're all small observations about the same new mechanism (the durable stdout tee added to src/os/linux.ts for orphan recovery) and belong together, not as three standalone beads. (apra-fleet-8hb, the POSIX 'set -o pipefail' shell-compatibility bug, stays separate -- that one is an actual correctness bug, not a hardening note.)

1. AGY provider dependency is incidental, not designed: agy.ts's buildPromptCommand ends with '...; node <agy-transcript-reader> ...', so 'A ; B | tee' attaches the tee to the transcript reader only, not the agy CLI. It happens to work because agy's parseResponse consumes the FLEET_TRANSCRIPT_START/END block that script emits, but nothing pins this relationship. Add an explicit test or comment documenting the dependency.

2. FLEET_PID now names the wrapper shell instead of the CLI process on the teed path: 'set -o pipefail; ... | tee' defeats the shell's exec-optimization of '{ cmd; } & _fleet_pid=$!', so the recorded pid is the parent shell, not the CLI (previously it was the CLI itself -- e.g. apra-fleet-6z8's own forensic evidence used pid 89858 = claude --agent planner directly). Functionally safe (kill -0 liveness still tracks the pipeline; killPid recursively walks pgrep -P and kills the descendant tree), but blunts the forensic ps-aux evidence chain that diagnosed 6z8 in the first place. Consider recovering the CLI's own pid via a second FLEET_CLI_PID marker for diagnostics.

3. Orphan recovery discards a possibly-already-written durable output file on timeout-kill: execute-prompt.ts's maxWaitMs = max(maxTotalMs - elapsed, 0); when the budget is already exhausted this is 0, so recoverOrphanedDispatch kills the live pid on the first loop iteration and returns orphan_recovery_timeout WITHOUT ever reading the durable output file -- a result that may already be fully written to disk at that moment is discarded. Read the durable file once after the kill (best-effort) before returning the timeout reason.

All three are small, same-file/same-mechanism, non-blocking. Reasonable to pick up in one sitting.
notes: TRIAGE: Verified all three sub-items against src/os/linux.ts and src/tools/execute-prompt.ts. (1) AGY dependency: the ';'-chained 'A ; B | tee' relationship to agy-transcript-reader.js is confirmed live in agy.ts and still undocumented as a pinned relationship. (2) FLEET_CLI_PID: grepped src/ for 'FLEET_CLI_PID' -- zero matches, still unimplemented; only FLEET_PID (naming the wrapper shell) exists. (3) execute-prompt.ts lines ~1197-1213: on orphan_recovery_timeout the function returns immediately without ever reading the durable output file that may already be fully written -- confirmed still discarding it, matching the bead exactly. Sibling bug apra-fleet-8hb.1 (pipefail POSIX guard) is already closed/fixed separately and correctly excluded from this bead's scope. All three items are small, same-file, well-scoped, and still open. Classification: LOW-HANGING-FRUIT. Subsystem: durable stdout tee / orphan recovery.

description: Non-blocking follow-up from apra-fleet-6z8.2 review. stall-poller.ts's new RAW_TIMESTAMP_RE fallback (used when zero lines in the tail parse as whole JSON) takes the LAST \"timestamp\":\"...\" occurrence anywhere in the raw tail text, including one embedded inside a tool_result's CONTENT (e.g. a bd/JSON payload the agent just read/printed). title: [integ] Real-bd suite: 3 files fail under --test-concurrency=8 (timeout) but pass cleanly standalone -- contention-induced false negatives
description:
Feature: N/A (packages/apra-fleet-se real-bd suite, part 1 of integ-test-playbook.md, node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs)
Expected: every file in the full concurrent real-bd pass (--test-concurrency=8) either genuinely passes or genuinely fails on its own merits, independent of how many other real-bd-heavy files happen to be running concurrently.
Actual: this cycle's full pass (deploy-verified SHA 998b15f344fe2611aad621281d556adb864d1487, run via 'node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs --fresh; --start; --status' per INTEG-SUITE.md) recorded 3 failures at --test-concurrency=8:
  - bd-init-templating.test.mjs: 'test timed out after 60000ms' at elapsed=93s.
  - mock-sprint-planner-auth-failure-no-retry.test.mjs: 'Expected an immediate abort (single attempt), took 114166ms' (its own 60000ms fast-abort bound).
  - serve-wiring-integration.test.mjs: 'GET / returns 200 ... request timeout' (its internal 5000ms HTTP client timeout).
All 3 were re-run standalone immediately after (APRA_FLEET_BD_MOCK=off node --test <file>, no concurrent real-bd load) and PASSED CLEANLY, well inside their respective budgets: bd-init-templating.test.mjs in 21.7s (budget 60s), mock-sprint-planner-auth-failure-no-retry.test.mjs in 26.8s (budget 60s, 1 Planner attempt as expected, no retries), serve-wiring-integration.test.mjs in 3.6s total (its GET / step alone took 3.1s, under the 5s client timeout it breached only when contended). None of the 3 represent a functional regression -- correctness is fine; the concurrent run simply starves individual dispatches/HTTP round-trips of CPU/IO past their fixed timeout budgets when 7-8 other real-bd-heavy files (golden-transcript*, budget-live, mock-sprint-happy-path, etc.) are running at the same time. This is the same resource-contention pattern already tracked at apra-fleet-eft.17 (28-34+ files exceeding the 300s single-file duration budget under this same concurrency=8 load) -- eft.17 documents the DURATION-budget symptom; this bug documents the sharper, correctness-adjacent symptom of the same root cause: fixed, tight timeout budgets inside individual tests (60s/5s) can flip a PASS into a hard FAIL purely from contention, producing a false-negative regression signal in the concurrent run.
Test: node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs full 114-file real-bd pass (elapsedWall=3353s); standalone reruns of each of the 3 named files immediately after, all green.
Repro: run the full real-bd suite at --test-concurrency=8 under load comparable to this cycle's run (8 real-bd-heavy files in flight simultaneously); observe one or more of the 3 named files exceed their internal fixed timeout; re-run the same file alone (no concurrent load) and observe it passes well inside budget.
Fix direction (not performed here per role boundaries): either (a) give these 3 tests a contention-aware/scaled timeout (e.g. derive from --test-concurrency or a documented headroom multiplier) instead of a fixed wall-clock bound, or (b) address the underlying eft.17 contention/throughput issue so no individual file is starved this close to its budget in the first place. Whichever lands should re-verify these exact 3 files pass consistently at full concurrency, not just standalone.
notes: integ-test-runner 2026-07-31 (SHA 55adab25 cycle) re-run: STILL REPRODUCES under the fresh 131-file --test-concurrency=8 pass -- serve-wiring-integration.test.mjs failed ('GET / ... timed out waiting for GET / to render the dashboard', elapsed=46s.). Standalone rerun immediately after (APRA_FLEET_BD_MOCK=off node --test packages/apra-fleet-se/test/serve-wiring-integration.test.mjs) PASSED cleanly in 3.1s (GET / returned in 2.6ms). Same contention-induced false-negative pattern as previously documented; no functional regression, no new bug filed. Part-1 summary this cycle: elapsedWall=4044s, cumFileTime=27271s, 131/131 discovered files completed, 1 failed (this bug).
close_reason: Verified fixed this cycle (deploy-verified SHA bd4681cdd646e19f30ab03fff73127d9e4eeb33e): full concurrent real-bd pass (node scripts/run-integ-suites.mjs, --test-concurrency=8 default, 119/119 files) recorded 0 failures. All 3 previously-contended files passed cleanly at full concurrency this time: bd-init-templating.test.mjs (durationMs=95317, well under 60s*contention budget), mock-sprint-planner-auth-failure-no-retry.test.mjs (durationMs=113893), serve-wiring-integration.test.mjs (durationMs=10956, its GET / step nowhere near the 5s client timeout). No longer reproduces even under the same concurrency load that triggered it previously. See integ-suite-status.json for the recorded per-file results.

title: Doer's own git push (separate from orchestrator G-push bracket) has no self-heal, closes beads with stale/misleading BLOCKED reasons
description:
Observed 2026-07-27 during a live apra-fleet-eft fleet-sprint run on fleet-mac, immediately after apra-fleet-fmu (git/dolt credential-auth self-heal) landed and was confirmed working at the orchestrator level.

The doer's own workflow does an independent 'git push origin <branch>' as part of its own implement+verify step, SEPARATE from the orchestrator's G-push bracket (withGitSync/syncMemberAfter in packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint/runner.js) that fmu's onAuthFailure self-heal is wired into. Live sequence for streak apra-fleet-eft.69.1:

1. Doer implements the task, commits locally as 598a56d2, then tries its own 'git push origin feat/sprint-service-1' as part of its verify step. At this point in time fleet-mac has no valid VCS credential yet (fresh sprint instance, nothing provisioned since restart), so the push fails: 'could not read Username for https://github.com: Device not configured'.
2. The doer has no self-heal of its own -- it just gives up, closes the bead with reason 'blocked: missing secret/credential for git push ... operator needs to supply credentials', and reports status BLOCKED, even though the actual implementation is complete, tested (987/987), and committed locally.
3. Moments later, the ORCHESTRATOR's own G-push bracket (which DOES have fmu's self-heal) runs for the same streak, hits the identical auth failure, correctly calls provision_vcs_auth, and its retry succeeds -- 598a56d2 (the SAME commit the doer already made) lands on origin/feat/sprint-service-1 successfully.
4. Nobody goes back and corrects the bead: apra-fleet-eft.69.1 remains CLOSED with the stale, now-FALSE close reason claiming the work is still blocked on missing credentials and needs operator intervention -- when the commit is in fact already published on origin. Verified live: bd show apra-fleet-eft.69.1 on fleet-mac still shows the stale blocked reason even though 'git branch -r --contains 598a56d2' confirms origin/feat/sprint-service-1 has it.

This is misleading for anyone reading bead history/close reasons later (looks like unresolved operator action is needed when it is not), and will likely recur for every other streak in a fresh sprint's first cycle (16 streaks were queued in this same Develop C1 R1 round), since each doer's OWN push attempt races ahead of the orchestrator's self-healing bracket and has no visibility into whether the orchestrator ultimately succeeds afterward.

FIX DIRECTIONS (needs design, more than one viable approach):
(a) Have the doer's own internal verify-step git push ALSO benefit from the same onAuthFailure self-heal path fmu introduced (i.e. share the auth-classification + provision_vcs_auth retry logic between the doer's direct push and the orchestrator's G-push bracket), so a doer never gives up on a merely-transient/self-healable credential gap.
(b) Simpler alternative: have the doer NOT attempt its own git push at all as part of verify -- rely entirely on the orchestrator's G-push bracket (which already runs after every doer dispatch) to publish the work, so there is only ONE push path and ONE place self-heal needs to live. This may be the more surgical fix if the doer's own push was only ever meant as a local save-point / was redundant with the orchestrator's bracket to begin with -- needs confirming against the doer's actual contract/prompt (packages/apra-fleet-se/fleet-sprint or the pm doer skill/prompt) to see whether the doer is EXPECTED to push itself or if that is incidental/unintended duplication.
(c) At minimum (even if (a)/(b) are not done): when the orchestrator's G-push bracket succeeds for a streak whose bead(s) were already closed BLOCKED by the doer's own failed push attempt, reopen/correct the bead's close reason to reflect that the work actually published successfully -- so stale false-BLOCKED reasons never persist in beads history.
acceptance_criteria: No bead is left closed with a stale/false 'blocked: missing credential' reason once the commit it describes has actually been successfully pushed to origin by the orchestrator's G-push bracket. Either the doer's own push path gains the same self-heal fmu gave the orchestrator's G-push bracket, the doer stops attempting its own redundant push (relying solely on the orchestrator's bracket), or the orchestrator corrects/reopens-and-recloses affected beads with an accurate reason after its own successful push. Regression test covering: doer's own push fails on a self-healable auth error, orchestrator's later G-push succeeds for the same commit -- the bead's final state accurately reflects that the work is published, not blocked.
notes:
Downgraded 2026-07-27: apra-fleet-glv (preflight provision_vcs_auth before every code-writing dispatch) will make this failure mode rare instead of routine, since the doer will almost always start its turn with an already-fresh credential. This bead stays open for the deeper architectural point (two independent push paths, and correcting/reopening beads closed with a stale blocked reason) but is no longer urgent once glv lands.
TRIAGE: Bead's own blocking dependency, apra-fleet-glv (preflight provision_vcs_auth before every code-writing dispatch), is now CLOSED (verified 2026-08-02, 67/67 tests pass) -- confirmed via bd show. Per the bead's own 2026-07-27 downgrade note, this was expected to make the described race 'rare instead of routine' once glv landed, which it now has. The deeper architectural point (two independent push paths; stale BLOCKED close reasons not auto-corrected) is still technically unaddressed in code, but re-validating actual current frequency/impact now that glv has shipped is the right next step before investing in a fix. Classification: NEEDS-RESEARCH-ONLY. Subsystem: fleet-sprint doer git push / self-heal.

title: [impl] Context-headroom admission control in execute_prompt
description: execute_prompt gains optional expected_context_tokens (number) or size bucket (S/M/L -> configured token estimates). Track per-session cumulative tokens (input+output, keyed by session id) and each model's context window; headroom = window - cumulative - safety_margin. If demand > headroom, reject with structured {reason:'insufficient_context_headroom', detail:{demand,headroom,window}} and NO LLM call. If demand fits but lands inside the safety margin, allow but attach a structured warning. No declared demand -> current behavior unchanged (warning-only mode via config). Up to 3 files + schema.

title: [server] Context-headroom admission control: callers declare estimated context demand; execute_prompt rejects dispatches that would land dangerously close to compaction
description:
A dispatch that lands in a session with too little context headroom gets
compacted mid-task -- prior context (the very thing a resumed delta
prompt depends on) is summarized away, and quality collapses silently.
Make demand vs headroom an explicit admission check:

- Caller side: execute_prompt gains an optional expected_context_tokens
  (number) or size bucket (S/M/L -> configured token estimates). The
  auto-sprint engine supplies it from the task's size metadata.
- Server side: track per-session cumulative tokens (input+output already
  parsed per dispatch, keyed by session id) and know each model's context
  window. headroom = window - cumulative - safety_margin.
- If demand > headroom: reject with a structured error (reason:
  "insufficient_context_headroom", detail: {demand, headroom, window})
  WITHOUT invoking the LLM. Caller decides: fresh session, smaller task,
  or split.
- If demand fits but lands inside the safety margin: allow, but attach a
  structured warning so orchestrators can prefer a fresh session next
  round.
- No declared demand: current behavior unchanged (no admission check);
  warning-only mode available via config.
acceptance_criteria:
- unit: resumed session with high cumulative tokens + L-size demand is
  rejected with insufficient_context_headroom and no spawn occurs.
- unit: same demand against a fresh session passes; near-margin pass
  attaches the structured warning.
- unit: omitted demand -> no check, no warning (back-compat pinned).
- engine test: dispatch carries expected_context_tokens derived from the
  task's S/M/L metadata.

title: [server] Usage/budget awareness in execute_prompt: surface warnings as a subscription window or dollar budget nears exhaustion
description:
Fleet dispatches burn either subscription quota (OAuth members: plan
windows / weekly caps) or metered dollars (API-key members). Today a
member silently runs until the provider hard-fails mid-sprint (the
observed failure mode: auth/limit errors surfacing as opaque dispatch
failures deep inside a run). execute_prompt should surface pressure
BEFORE exhaustion:

- PRIMARY SOURCE (per user direction): provider-native usage/quota
  APIs/SDKs, NOT fleet-side self-metering. Self-metering drifts: it
  misses cache-pricing nuances, provider-side retries, and any usage the
  same account burns OUTSIDE fleet. Per provider, discover and use the
  official endpoint: e.g. Anthropic's usage/cost Admin API for API-key
  members and the subscription quota/reset signals the Claude CLI itself
  exposes for OAuth members; OpenAI usage API for Codex; equivalents per
  provider adapter. This is an adapter-layer capability (getUsage()),
  capability-flagged per provider -- exactly like every other
  provider-specific feature.
- FALLBACK ONLY: where a provider exposes no usage API, degrade to
  fleet-side accumulation from dispatch-result token counts (priced via
  get_member_model_pricing), clearly labeled source: "estimated" in the
  structured output so callers can tell measured from guessed.
- Allow a configured budget: dollars/day or tokens/window per member or
  workspace (config file; optional). Budgets compare against the
  provider-reported numbers when available.
- First step of implementation is a short survey doc (mirroring
  docs/interactive-injection-provider-survey.md) recording each
  provider's usage-API reality with [OK]/[DOC]/[TBD]/[FAIL] confidence,
  before any code.
- When usage crosses a warning band (e.g. 80%) every execute_prompt
  result carries a structured warning (structuredContent.usage:
  {spent, budget, fraction, scope}) in ADDITION to the normal result --
  orchestrators can then de-prioritize, downshift model tiers, or pause.
- Optional hard threshold (e.g. 100%): reject NEW dispatches with a
  structured error (reason: "budget_exhausted") without invoking the LLM;
  never kill an in-flight session.
- Subscription-plan members without a priceable meter: warn from
  provider-side signals where available (rate-limit/quota error sniffing,
  reset-window headers) -- best-effort, clearly labeled source.
acceptance_criteria:
- unit: crossing the warning band adds the structured usage block to the
  next result; below band there is none.
- unit: hard threshold rejects with budget_exhausted and no spawn occurs.
- unit: provider adapter getUsage() is the source when the capability is
  present (asserted via mock adapter); fallback estimation path engages
  ONLY when the capability is absent, and its structured output carries
  source: "estimated" vs source: "provider".
- survey doc exists with a per-provider usage-API row and confidence
  marker before adapter code lands.

title: [server+engine] resume-by-session-id in execute_prompt (schema-first) + per-role round resume in auto-sprint
description:
Part 1 (fleet server, small):
- Widen execute_prompt input: resume: boolean | string (z.union). true keeps
  today's behavior (resume the member's stored last session); a string means
  "resume exactly this session id". The provider layer already supports this
  (agent.sessionId -> buildResumeFlag/buildSessionIdFlag in
  src/providers/claude.ts); the handler just prefers the caller-supplied id
  over agent.sessionId.
- Promote the "session: <id>" text footer into the structured result
  (structuredContent.sessionId) per the schemas-are-the-contract rule.
  Keep the footer for back-compat.
- SEMANTICS SPLIT on session-not-found (CRITICAL): explicit session-id
  resume means the caller ASSERTS the prompt depends on that session's
  prior context. If the id cannot be resumed (unknown, expired, provider
  rejects it), this is a TERMINAL ERROR: return it to the caller WITHOUT
  making any LLM call. Do NOT apply the existing automatic
  stale-session-recovery fallback (retry fresh) to explicit-id calls --
  a context-dependent delta prompt executed in a blank session is
  meaningless at best and destructively wrong at worst. The transparent
  retry-fresh recovery remains ONLY for resume=true (best-effort mode,
  where prompts must be self-contained). Error shape: structured
  (isError + reason: "session_not_found"), so orchestrators can decide
  deliberately (rebuild context and re-dispatch fresh with a FULL prompt,
  or abort) instead of getting a silent wrong-context response.

Part 2 (auto-sprint engine, depends on part 1):
- Record each dispatch's returned sessionId per (role, cycle). Within the
  SAME cycle and phase, resume the same role's session across rounds by
  passing its session id explicitly:
  planner R1 -> R2 -> R3 (apply reviewer deltas in a warm session),
  reviewer R1 -> R2 -> R3 (structurally enforces prior-round verdict
  consistency -- the run-21 goalpost-moving failure class),
  doer retry rounds (warm codebase context for feedback fixes).
- Guards: NEVER resume across cycles (re-plans want fresh eyes); fall back
  to a fresh session when the prior round ended in error/timeout state or
  the resumed session nears its context ceiling; degrade gracefully on
  providers without resume support (Copilot none, Codex partial) --
  capability-checked, not provider-name-checked.
- Rationale: a fresh plan round re-derives everything (contract re-read,
  bd list dumps) to apply a one-line reviewer fix; resumed rounds are
  cache-priced and turn-cheap. Est. 30-60% cost cut on plan phases, plus
  the reviewer-consistency quality win.
acceptance_criteria:
- execute_prompt accepts resume as boolean or session-id string; unit test
  proves a string id resumes THAT session even when the member's stored
  last session is a different one.
- structuredContent.sessionId present in the tool result; schema updated;
  footer unchanged.
- mock-sprint test: planner R2 dispatch carries resume=<planner R1 session
  id> (not true/false), reviewer R2 carries the reviewer R1 id; cross-cycle
  plan dispatches carry resume=false.
- mock-sprint test: prior round ends in dispatch error -> next round uses a
  fresh session (no resume id).
- unit test: explicit session-id resume with an unknown/expired id returns
  a structured session_not_found error and NO LLM invocation occurs (spawn
  layer never called); resume=true with a stale stored session still does
  the transparent retry-fresh recovery (existing behavior pinned).
- engine test: on session_not_found the engine does NOT re-send the delta
  prompt; it rebuilds a self-contained full prompt for a fresh session (or
  fails the round explicitly), asserted via the dispatched prompt content.

title: [perf] Engine/viewer hammer beads with repeated full-DB fetches (bd list --all --limit 0 --json)
description:
description (user-dictated 2026-07-22):

The engine/viewer issue "bd list --all --limit 0 --json" repeatedly, some
calls back-to-back. Two independent problems:
1) Frequency: full refetches fire far too often (including sequentially,
   which looks naive - no caching/coalescing between adjacent call sites).
2) Scope: each call pulls EVERY issue in the DB. The beads DB only grows
   (it is shared, append-heavy, cross-sprint), so full-table pulls are a
   growing pain: cost scales with total history, not with the active sprint.

Fix direction: audit all bd list call sites; coalesce adjacent calls behind
a short-lived cache/single snapshot per phase step; scope queries (--parent
<epic>, status filters, --since/incremental if bd supports it) so cost
scales with the active subtree, not the whole DB.

acceptance (machine-verifiable):
- A mock-sprint run's command log shows no two identical full-list fetches
  within one phase step (coalesced), and steady-state fetches are scoped
  (no --all --limit 0 on the hot path; or documented why a full fetch is
  genuinely needed at the specific remaining sites).
- Add a command-count/shape tripwire (dispatch-safety-guard style) so
  regression back to full-DB polling fails CI.

title: [engine] doer can push a dangling vendor submodule pin (unpushed SHA) undetected
description:

Every fresh clone / CI run / deploy of the branch would fail 'git submodule update' with 'not our ref'. The orchestrator happened to be watching and repaired the pin (e21e3cc -> pushed apra-pm commit 7b467a09); nothing in the engine caught it.

Fix: the engine's post-doer commit validation (or the doer contract + a runner-side guard) must reject any commit that changes a gitlink (mode 160000) entry to a SHA that is not reachable on the submodule's configured remote (git ls-remote / git fetch <sha> probe), failing the streak with an actionable message instead of pushing a dangling pin.

title: [build] CI build-binary logs are full of false-positive warnings that mask real ones
description: User feedback (2026-07-21, first fully-green CI run 29869270095): the linux/macos build-binary job logs read as broken despite succeeding, because of KNOWN-BENIGN warnings -- (1) postject repeats warning: Can't find string offset for section name '.note.100' ~10x per linux build (upstream noise against Node 22 ELF sections; injection succeeds); (2) the macOS 'Stripping macOS codesign...' step reads like a failure though it is a required, intentional step (postject cannot inject into a signed binary); (3) setup-action deprecation warnings (punycode, url.parse, Node 20) from GitHub's own actions. False positives train contributors to ignore warnings, so real ones get skimmed past. Fix: filter postject stderr to drop ONLY the exact known-benign patterns (keep everything else verbatim, fail if postject exits nonzero); reword the codesign step to state it is expected ('codesign stripped by design: postject requires an unsigned binary; re-signed ad-hoc after injection'); pin/upgrade the deprecated setup actions where upstream fixes exist. The filter must be an explicit allowlist of benign patterns with a comment linking the upstream issue -- never a blanket 2>/dev/null.
acceptance_criteria: Machine-verifiable: (1) a clean build-binary run's log contains ZERO occurrences of the .note string-offset warning and zero unexplained 'Stripping' lines (the reworded line states it is expected); (2) the postject wrapper script has a unit test proving a NON-allowlisted stderr line passes through verbatim and a nonzero postject exit still fails the build; (3) grep of the workflow yaml shows no bare 2>/dev/null on the postject invocation.

The build-binary job exists at .github/workflows/ci.yml:188 (not renamed). Real CI log read per parent's acceptance: green run 30707838901 (2026-08-01) tail shows clean postject lines, no .note warnings, reworded codesign line. tests/package-sea-postject.test.ts (10 tests, passing in that run) covers benign-drop, verbatim pass-through, and nonzero-exit failure.

description: User request (2026-07-21), phase-level sibling of apra-fleet-eft.45 (which covers per-activity elapsed ticking). title: [integ] viewer-perf-regression-e2e: on-demand description fetch/cache test mocks wrong wire field ('description' instead of 'text'), 3 subtests fail
description:
